records.title: Biosynthesis-Integrated Editing of Bacterial Cellulose Enables Sequence-Programmable Biointerfaces
records.abstract: Abstract  Structural polysaccharides self-assemble into densely packed fibrils, providing a molecular foundation for the hierarchical organization and mechanical integrity of biological materials. However, the same interchain interactions that stabilize these structures severely restrict chemical accessibility, making molecular editing after assembly a formidable challenge. Here, we integrate regiochemical editing into bacterial cellulose biosynthesis using azido-glucose analogues substituted at C2, C3, or C6. The resulting cellulose materials exhibit regioisomer-dependent differences in crystallinity, fibrillar organization, and mechanical properties, while precursor feeding further modulates crystallinity. The incorporated azide groups remain chemically accessible after assembly, enabling DNA conjugation and rolling-circle amplification to construct sequence-programmable aptamer interfaces. By varying the aptamer sequence, the same cellulose platform can be reprogrammed for either selective cell capture and release or HGF-mimetic regulation of endothelial behavior. This work establishes a biosynthesis-integrated strategy that connects molecular editing during cellulose formation with hierarchical material organization and subsequent biological programming.
records.authors: Yang G, Tang G, He Q, Zou S, Wang H, Huang G, Yin W, Shi Z, Chen Z, Yin L, Chen G.

records.title: PM₂.₅-Associated Variation in Airborne Antimicrobial Resistance Gene Abundance During Winter Smog Episodes in Urban Pakistan (2022–2023)
records.abstract: Abstract    Airborne particulate matter (PM₂.₅) is a major component of winter smog and has been increasingly recognized as a potential carrier of microbial contaminants, including antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs). However, limited data are available on the distribution of airborne ARGs associated with PM₂.₅ in urban environments of Pakistan.  Objective  This study aimed to quantify the relative abundance of clinically relevant ARGs in PM₂.₅-associated bacterial communities across three cities of Pakistan and to evaluate their association with air pollution and meteorological conditions.  Methodology  PM₂.₅ samples were collected from Lahore, Islamabad, and Okara during the winter months (November–December 2022 and 2023). External DNA (eDNA) associated with particulate matter was extracted and analysed using quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR). The relative abundance of selected ARGs (  sul1, blaTEM, blaCTX-M-32, blaNDM-1, vanA, vanRA, tnpA, intI1  , and  blaTEM-F  ) was determined using the 2^(-ΔCt) method and normalized against the 16S rRNA gene. Environmental parameters, including PM₂.₅ concentration, Air Quality Index (AQI), temperature, and humidity, were also assessed.  Results  Lahore exhibited the highest pollution levels, with PM₂.₅ concentrations reaching 276.6 ± 27.4 µg/m³ and AQI values up to 289.3 ± 42.7. PM₂.₅ showed strong positive correlations with AQI (r = 0.92) and relative humidity (r = 0.91) and a negative correlation with temperature (r = − 0.38). Distinct spatial variation in ARG relative abundance was observed across the study sites. The  blaNDM-1  gene demonstrated the highest relative abundance, particularly in Lahore (0.077) and Islamabad (0.056), while  vanA  showed a comparatively higher abundance in Okara. Other ARGs, including  blaTEM-F, sul1  , and  intI1  , exhibited variable distribution patterns across cities, indicating heterogeneous environmental resistome profiles.  Conclusion  The findings reveal significant spatial variability in airborne ARG relative abundance associated with PM₂.₅ and highlight the influence of environmental conditions on resistome distribution. These results underscore the importance of monitoring airborne antimicrobial resistance in polluted urban environments and provide baseline data for future environmental and public health assessments.
records.authors: Khan MI, Amin A, Khalid N, Ahmed I.

records.title: Demographic variation of viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus among Round Gobies in the St. Lawrence River.
records.abstract: ObjectiveWe investigated the demographic dynamics of viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus (VHSV) infections in wild Round Goby Neogobius melanostomus from the nearshore habitats of the upper St. Lawrence River from 2018 to 2022. We examined viral prevalence and titers between Round Goby sexes and age-classes to identify how demography correlates with prevalence and amplification of this pathogen within this host species.MethodsReverse-transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction was used to detect and quantify viral N-gene genetic material in pooled organ (i.e., liver, kidney, spleen) and brain tissues of wild Round Gobies that were collected from the upper St. Lawrence River. Age and sex were assigned to each individual to elucidate how patterns of infection prevalence and amplification vary depending on demography within this host species.ResultViral hemorrhagic septicemia virus was detected by reverse-transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction in 49.62% of the sampled Round Gobies, with significant variation in prevalence and titers observed across demographic groups. Sex-based VHSV prevalence was 15.87% in females and 55.95% in males, and infected fish of both sexes contained similar median viral titers. Age-based prevalence increased with age, ranging from 14.29% in age-1 fish to 68.35% in age-4 fish, whereas viral titers were highest in age-2 fish and decreased with age thereafter.ConclusionRound Gobies exhibit a high prevalence (49.62%) of VHSV infections. However, the pathogen is distributed unevenly among demographics within this species. Both sex and age interact with the infection status of an individual.
records.authors: Haws AL, Getchell RG, Farrell JM.

records.title: Single-Nucleus Transcriptomics Reveals Cell Type Specific Defence Responses and Identifies AhWRKY40 as a Key Regulator of Peanut Resistance to Sclerotium rolfsii.
records.abstract: Peanut stem rot caused by Sclerotium rolfsii is a devastating soil borne disease that severely constrains peanut production worldwide. Despite its economic importance, highly resistant peanut cultivars are still largely unavailable, and the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying peanut resistance remain poorly understood. We obtained a total of 29,308 high-quality nuclei, annotated five major cell types, and detected 52,819 expressed genes. Comparative analysis revealed widespread transcriptional reprogramming and a predominance of downregulated genes in response to pathogen infection, accompanied by a substantial reduction in cell abundance across all cell populations. Notably, epidermal cells harboured the highest proportion of disease resistance genes. Pseudotime trajectory analysis further demonstrated that S. rolfsii infection altered cellular transcriptional states and induced cell type specific immune reprogramming. Integrative analyses combining gene coexpression, pseudotime dynamics, virtual knockout, and transgenic validation consistently identified AhWRKY40 as a key regulatory factor associated with disease resistance. Overexpression of AhWRKY40 enhanced resistance to S. rolfsii and was accompanied by increased accumulation of jasmonic acid (JA) and salicylic acid (SA), suggesting its involvement in hormone-mediated defence responses. Collectively, our study provides new insights into the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying peanut resistance to stem rot, identifies AhWRKY40 as a promising candidate gene for disease resistance, and establishes a valuable resource for functional genomics and molecular breeding to improve southern blight resistance in peanut.
records.authors: Sun Z, Liu H, Hong Y, Umer MJ, Wang W, Liu P, Shen H, Pu X, Zhang J, Sun D.

records.abstract: Jatropha leaf yellow mosaic virus, within the genus Begomovirus, is an economically important plant virus associated with yellow mosaic disease in Jatropha curcas. We report a coding-complete DNA-A genome sequence from a naturally infected castor bean (Ricinus communis) in India.

records.title: Profiling of RNA 8-oxoG marks in Escherichia coli identifies critical intrinsic characteristics that contribute to 8-oxoG accumulation in bacteria.
records.abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are environmentally ubiquitous and have pervasive impacts on cellular homeostasis. RNA is vulnerable to oxidative chemical alterations from myriad endogenous and exogenous sources. The most common chemical modification resulting from ROS exposure to RNA is 8-oxo-7,8-dihydroguanine (8-oxoG). While 8-oxoG modifications are known to impact mRNA processing, understanding the broader biological impact of 8-oxoG requires knowledge of how these modifications accumulate. In this work, we assessed the disparate enrichment of 8-oxoG modifications within RNAs in the E. coli transcriptome using an RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing technique with a high-affinity 8-oxoG antibody (8-oxoG-RIP-Seq). Our investigation of the RNA 8-oxoG enrichment landscape uncovered intrinsic RNA characteristics that correlate with 8-oxoG enrichment. These findings suggest intrinsic characteristics of RNA, most notably relative abundance, CDS length and G‑nucleotide composition, significantly influence RNA 8-oxoG accumulation. We harnessed these properties to construct a simple multiple linear regression model that predicts RNA 8-oxoG accumulation, which we validated in E. coli. This model was subsequently applied to predict 8-oxoG‑enriched RNA species in four other bacterial species spanning a wide range of oxidative stress tolerances; these predictions suggest that 8-oxoG accumulation is species dependent, with limited overlap in RNAs and functional pathways that are more susceptible to 8-oxoG accumulation. Further evaluation of this model in the extremophile D. radiodurans revealed a substantial reduction in predictive power. Overall, these findings better inform understanding of RNA 8-oxoG patterns in bacteria and have broader impacts towards advancing knowledge of the connection between RNA oxidation and cellular homeostasis.
records.authors: Burroughs MR, Quiñones-Diaz BI, Grismore KB, Contreras LM.

records.title: Transcription of the uropathogenic Escherichia coli vat gene is driven by multiple promoters whose activity is modulated by the cyclic AMP receptor protein.
records.abstract: Uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC), a cause of urinary tract infections, expresses various virulence factors to enable it to infect and persist, overcoming host defences. One of these is the vacuolating autotransporter toxin (Vat), which causes vacuole formation and cellular damage in bladder epithelial cells. Bacteria tightly regulate transcript initiation of most virulence factor genes using either bespoke transcription factors, or, sometimes, global transcription factors, such as the cyclic AMP receptor protein (CRP), which regulates hundreds of bacterial genes, typically responding to nutritional stress. We report that CRP binds to the regulatory region of the vat gene and describe the complex nature of regulation of vat gene transcription in UPEC CFT073. In vivo and in vitro analysis revealed that whilst the vat regulatory region contains a CRP-activated promoter, P1, two additional promoters, P2 and P3, ensure that net promoter activity is not dependent on CRP. Functional -10 and -35 elements were identified for the P2 promoter, which is suppressed by CRP binding, blocking the -35 element. Expression from the P3 promoter is also supressed by binding of CRP over the transcript start site.
records.authors: Hothersall J, Mao Y, Yang J, Bai G, Syeda N, Alhammadi MM, Haycocks JRJ, Grainger DC, Browning DF, Busby SJW.

records.title: Inhibitory Effect of Trichoderma harzianum Strain A3.1 Against Fusarium Species Causing Fig Root Rot.
records.abstract: To identify the causal pathogen of fig root rot in Artux, Xinjiang, China and screen high-efficacy biocontrol agents, diseased fig root tissues were used as research materials. Pathogen isolation, morphological characterization, molecular identification and pathogenicity assays were sequentially performed to characterize the disease-causing fungus, followed by screening of antagonistic microorganisms. The results demonstrated that the pathogen responsible for fig root rot was Fusarium kazakhstanicum. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of F. kazakhstanicum causing fig root rot on Ficus carica in China. A highly effective antagonistic fungal strain designated A3.1 was isolated from the rhizosphere soil of healthy fig trees, and was identified as Trichoderma harzianum based on morphological traits and molecular phylogenetic evidence. Dual-culture assays revealed that T. harzianum A3.1 achieved a mycelial growth inhibition rate of 72.5% against F. kazakhstanicum. Light microscopic and scanning electron microscopy observations further illustrated that T. harzianum A3.1 severely disrupted the hyphal architecture of the pathogen, causing hyphal deformation and granular deposits at the contact sites. This strain possesses great application prospects for biocontrol against the pathogen causing fig root rot, and this research lays a foundation for developing environmentally sustainable control strategies of fig root rot in Xinjiang, China.
records.authors: Sijia Z, Guorong L, Deng X, Halifu S.

records.title: Mapping HIV reservoir geography: lessons for cure from the Last Gift rapid autopsy cohort.
records.abstract: Purpose of reviewDeep tissue reservoirs remain a major barrier to HIV cure. Their anatomical distribution and connectivity are difficult to study in living people. We examine how the Last Gift rapid-autopsy cohort clarifies reservoir connectivity, persistence behind anatomical barriers, and variation within organs, and consider the implications for cure.Recent findingsTissue studies reveal HIV reservoirs that are interconnected across yet differ between and within anatomical sites. Viral sequence analyses suggest that blood links tissue reservoirs, with gut and lymphoid tissues acting as hubs of viral dispersal. Recovery of replication-competent HIV from brain microglia during suppressive antiretroviral therapy (ART) provides direct evidence of a resident brain reservoir. Even within the gastrointestinal tract, HIV DNA burden and transcriptions vary by region, with different microbiome associations in the small and large bowel.SummaryHIV reservoir geography supports durable ART-free remission as a practical goal. Achieving this goal will likely require combination therapies with complementary functions and tissue access. Because tissue heterogeneity limits what negative biopsies can establish, remission should be assessed through carefully monitored analytical treatment interruption and long-term follow up.
records.journal: Current opinion in HIV and AIDS
records.authors: Birabaharan M, Immer A, Gomez AN, Valdes D, Smith DM.

records.title: Multifaceted roles of 3C-like protease in porcine enteric coronavirus immune evasion and antiviral targeting.
records.abstract: Porcine enteric coronaviruses, including porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV), porcine transmissible gastroenteritis virus (TGEV), porcine deltacoronavirus (PDCoV), and swine acute diarrhea syndrome coronavirus (SADS-CoV), have resulted in significant economic losses for the global swine industry and have raised substantial public health concerns due to their potential for cross-species transmission and zoonotic risk. As positive-sense single-stranded RNA viruses, these coronaviruses possess genomes that encode a set of nonstructural proteins essential for viral replication. Among these, the 3C-like protease (3CLpro) is highly conserved and plays an indispensable role in processing viral polyproteins. The 3CLpro exhibits a characteristic three-domain architecture featuring a conserved Cys-His catalytic dyad, with its dimerization being critical for catalytic activity. This protease specifically cleaves key molecules involved in the signaling pathways of innate immunity and programmed cell death. Despite sequence variations among α-, β-, γ-, and δ-coronaviruses, the catalytic core and substrate-binding pockets of 3CLpro remain structurally conserved, rendering this protease an ideal target for broad-spectrum antiviral agents. Targeting 3CLpro presents a promising strategy for combating porcine coronavirus infections. This review summarizes the structural characteristics, catalytic mechanisms, specific cleavage of host proteins, and the potential for antiviral drug development related to porcine coronavirus 3CLpro, aiming to provide a theoretical basis for elucidating its multifunctional roles in viral replication and immune regulation.
records.authors: Huang Y, Tian C, Cui H, Zheng L, Chen H, Zhang Y, Zhao Y, Ma S.

records.title: Fructobacillus fructosus isolated from palm wine: functional screening and safety evaluation as a potential probiotic.
records.abstract: Fructobacillus fructosus, a specialized fructophilic lactic acid bacterium from traditional fermented ecosystems, remains largely unexplored for its functional probiotic properties. This study established a robust, experimentally validated in vitro baseline of the probiotic potential and safety profile of the Fructobacillus fructosus strain MRS-3 isolated from traditional palm wine. The taxonomic identification was confirmed by 16 S rRNA gene sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. In vitro screening assays were used to evaluate the gastrointestinal survivability (acid/bile tolerance) and cell surface traits (autoaggregation, hydrophobicity, and Caco-2 cell adhesion) of the isolate. Baseline biological safety was quantitatively determined using minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values against reference breakpoints and a hemolysis assay. Strain MRS-3 was confirmed as Fructobacillus fructosus (GenBank: PV123975.1) by 16 S rRNA gene sequencing and exhibited growth across a broad range of pH, salt concentrations, and temperatures. It demonstrated tolerance to acidic and bile salt conditions, with viable counts ranging from 5.3 to 5.9 and 5.4 to 5.98 log CFU/mL, respectively. The strain showed high auto-aggregation (94.8%) and cell-surface hydrophobicity toward xylene (90%), toluene (90.9%), and hexane (76%), together with co-aggregation with selected indicator strains and measurable adhesion to Caco-2 intestinal epithelial cells. No hemolytic activity was observed, and inhibition zones were observed in the antibiotic susceptibility study under the experimental conditions spanning 18 to 27 mm. The results obtained strongly support the potential of Fructobacillus fructosus MRS-3 isolated from palm wine as a safe and functional probiotic candidate. This study provides a critical empirical baseline for the genus, demonstrating that its phenotypic traits merit future targeted in vivo validation.

records.title: Single-Cell Transcriptome-Wide Mendelian Randomization and Colocalization Analysis Reveals Immune Cell-Specific Mechanisms in Alzheimer's Disease
records.abstract: Objective:  To integrate single-cell expression quantitative trait locus (sc-eQTL), Alzheimer's disease (AD) genome-wide association study (GWAS), and Bayesian colocalization analyses, in order to systematically identify candidate causal genes and potential immune mechanisms that specifically regulate AD risk in peripheral immune cells. Methods: Using the cis-eQTLs of 14 peripheral blood immune cell types from the OneK1K single-cell eQTL dataset as exposure data and the AD GWAS (GCST90565439) as outcome data, a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis was performed. Weak instrumental variables were removed using F-statistics, and approximately independent genetic instruments were obtained by linkage disequilibrium pruning. For significant gene-cell type associations, compareCluster functional enrichment, Bayesian colocalization, and phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) were further performed, and the 1M-scBloodNL dataset was used for replication validation. Results: The MR analysis identified 187 gene-cell type associations significantly associated with AD risk, involving 161 candidate causal genes. Among them, 141 genes showed significant associations in only a single immune cell type, suggesting that AD-related immune genetic regulation has marked cell type specificity. Functional enrichment analysis showed that the significant genes in different immune cell types were enriched in biological processes including MHC class II antigen presentation, phagocytosis, membrane invagination, and positive regulation of T cell activation. Colocalization analysis indicated a strong shared genetic signal between TNF expression in CD4+SOX4+ T cells and AD risk (PP.H4 = 0.833). In the 1M-scBloodNL replication analysis, several candidate genes showed consistent direction and nominal significance. The PheWAS results suggested that the significant phenotypic associations of the TNF instrumental variable were mainly concentrated in immune- and hematology-related traits, with no genome-wide significant neurological phenotypic associations observed. Conclusion: This study suggests that single-cell eQTL-MR combined with colocalization analysis can be used to dissect the cell type-specific genetic regulatory mechanisms of peripheral immunity in AD. The genetically predicted expression of TNF in CD4+SOX4+ T cells may represent an important immune-related signal for AD risk, but further validation in independent populations and functional experiments is still required.

records.title: High Neuronal PAS Domain Protein 2 Expression Associated with Poor Prognosis, Tumor Immune Infiltration, and Adenosine Pathway Markers in Lung Cancer.
records.abstract: This study aims to explore the clinical significance of neuronal PAS domain protein 2 (NPAS2) in lung cancer, its relationship with the tumor immune microenvironment, and its potential upstream non-coding RNA (ncRNA) regulatory network. By analyzing transcriptomic data and clinical information from the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database, prognostic genes were identified, and NPAS2 expression was analyzed in lung adenocarcinoma and lung squamous cell carcinoma to determine its associations with patient survival and immune cell infiltration. Immunohistochemical analysis was also performed to compare NPAS2 expression between lung cancer tissues and adjacent non-tumor tissues. NPAS2 expression was elevated in tumor tissues, with higher expression associated with reduced overall survival. This association remained significant in multivariate Cox regression analysis (hazard ratio (HR) = 1.11687, P = 0.0252). In the analyzed dataset, a diagnostic model incorporating NPAS2, epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), marker of proliferation Ki-67 (MKI67), and tumor protein p63 (TP63) yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.987. Immune infiltration analysis revealed that in lung adenocarcinoma and lung squamous cell carcinoma, NPAS2 expression was positively correlated with CD4⁺ T cell and neutrophil infiltration, as well as with the expression of the immune checkpoint molecule sialic acid-binding immunoglobulin-like lectin 15 (SIGLEC15). Additionally, NPAS2 expression was positively correlated with the adenosine pathway markers CD39 and CD73. Bioinformatics analysis further identified a potential regulatory axis of NORAD/AC087477.2-hsa-miR-106a-5p/hsa-miR-17-5p-NPAS2. These results suggest that NPAS2 may be a candidate biomarker for lung cancer diagnosis and prognosis assessment and may be associated with tumor immune cell infiltration and adenosine-related immune regulatory processes. However, further functional experiments and clinical validation are needed to clarify its potential molecular mechanism and clinical application value.

records.title: Formal Description of Cladocopium proximale sp. nov., a Coral Photosymbiont From the C1 Radiation.
records.abstract: Coral reefs are among the most biodiverse ecosystems on Earth and rely on endosymbiosis with Symbiodiniaceae, a diverse family of dinoflagellates essential for coral nutrition and which also play an important role in thermal tolerance. Despite their ecological importance, resolving species boundaries within Symbiodiniaceae remains challenging, partly due to limited phylogenetic signal in commonly used genetic markers and the absence of broadly accepted criteria for species delimitation. Refining taxonomic resolution is therefore critical for understanding symbiont diversity, distributions, and evolutionary relationships. In this study, we delimit two closely related Cladocopium species using a meta-haplotype framework applied to two hypervariable loci-the ITS2 region and the psbA non-coding region (psbAncr). Slowly evolving markers failed to differentiate Cladocopium proximale (SCF049; described here) from its sister species C. proliferum. In contrast, consistent genetic differences between the two taxa were detected across both hypervariable regions. Together with morphological differences, these results support the recognition of C. proximale and C. proliferum as distinct species. Our results highlight the value of combining multiple hypervariable markers to improve taxonomic accuracy in Symbiodiniaceae, providing a stronger basis for understanding how symbiont diversity and ecological differentiation may influence coral resilience and responses to environmental change. More broadly, closely related Symbiodiniaceae such as these provide important systems for examining speciation processes, including potential ecological differentiation and reproductive compatibility.
records.authors: Terzi G, van Oppen MJH, Seveso D, Nitschke MR.

records.title: Genome-Wide Characterization of HERV-Derived RNA Regulatory Potential in the Human Transcriptome.
records.abstract: Human endogenous retroviruses (HERVs) comprise nearly 8% of the human genome, and their long terminal repeats (LTRs) are well-established sources of transcriptional regulatory elements. However, their contribution to RNA-level regulatory features remains largely unexplored. Here, we present a genome-wide characterization of the RNA regulatory potential of 53,176 HERV internal regions and 560,594 LTRs. We found 16.2% more predicted RNA-binding protein motif occurrences in HERV internal regions than expected after controlling for dinucleotide composition. At the subfamily level, overall motif abundance was elevated in HERVH but remained close to expectation in HERVK (HML-2). Conserved retroviral protein domains incorporated into transcripts were mostly located in exceptionally long terminal exons, approximately 7-fold longer than those of other multi-exon transcripts. HERV internal sequence overlapped 4,074 annotated long noncoding RNA genes and accounted for more than 80% of the gene body of 144, most of them functionally unannotated. Finally, 6,583 unique antisense LTRs at transcript termini formed SPARCS-like candidate configurations that could support antisense RNA pairing; protein-coding genes carrying them in 3' untranslated regions showed enrichment for immune signaling and recombination-related terms. These results provide a genome-wide framework of candidate HERV-derived RNA regulatory features and transcript architectures for experimental testing.
records.authors: Montserrat-Ayuso T, Pujol A, Esteve-Codina A.

records.title: The transcription factor SiROCX coordinates a stage-specific xylan- and cellulose-degrading secretome during immune-compatible colonization of monocot roots by Serendipita indica.
records.abstract: Intracellular accommodation of beneficial fungi requires controlled remodelling of host cell walls while avoiding excessive activation of plant immune responses. During colonization of monocot roots, the endophytic fungus Serendipita indica induces a suite of carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) targeting xylan and cellulose, but how this program is transcriptionally controlled in basidiomycetes is unknown. Here, we combined co-expression network analysis of time-resolved colonization transcriptomes with DNA affinity purification sequencing (DAP-seq) of module-associated transcription factors. This identified SiROCX, a Zn2Cys6 transcription factor of an Agaricomycetes-specific Roc1/ROCX lineage, whose DAP-seq-defined regulon is enriched in CAZyme genes. Inducible overexpression of SiROCX activated representative targets, enriched the secretome in CAZymes and enhanced xylanase and cellulase activities on xylan and delignified alcohol-insoluble residue (dAIR) of barley roots under in vitro conditions. Premature activation of this program during barley colonization was associated with early induction of a host immune marker despite comparable fungal biomass, consistent with a role for temporal control in maintaining symbiotic compatibility. Together, these findings identify SiROCX as a major regulator of a host-adapted cell wall-degrading secretome and reveal an Agaricomycetes-specific regulatory module that coordinates host cell wall remodelling with immune-compatible symbiotic colonization.
records.authors: Armbruster L, Brands M, Baumgart L, Dreesmann F, Leson L, Peltz N, Ramírez V, Zhang Y, Nassr T, Langen G, Pauly M, Zuccaro A.

records.title: scPhyloGRN: gene regulatory network inference guided by lineage topology in single-cell developmental data.
records.abstract: MotivationGene regulatory network (GRN) inference from single-cell transcriptomes is complicated by expression patterns associated with both cell state and shared ancestry. Cellular phylogenies provide developmental context, but incorporating relationships among individual cells into gene-level regulatory inference remains challenging.ResultsWe present scPhyloGRN, a supervised framework that integrates single-cell gene expression with cellular phylogeny to prioritize directed transcription factor (TF)-target candidates within the observed gene set. The framework maps cell ancestry to gene associations that guide graph construction, attention in a dual-stream encoder, and lineage-consistency regularization. We evaluated scPhyloGRN against ten methods across 17 dataset-reference settings spanning four mouse embryos and one Caenorhabditis elegans dataset. scPhyloGRN showed an overall advantage in regulatory edge prioritization, supported by additional evaluations using shared candidate spaces. Removing lineage information reduced AUPRC in the ablation analyses, while branch-level and regulator-level analyses showed improved ranking and recovery of reference-supported regulatory candidates.Availability and implementationSource code and analysis workflows are available at https://github.com/Maria0852/scPhyloGRN, with a versioned archive at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22793831.
records.authors: Meng R, Wang K, Hu J, Hu Z, Zhou D.

records.title: Laryngeal Cancer Microbiome Study Reveals Parvimonas and Campylobacter as Potential Therapy Targets.
records.abstract: ObjectiveLaryngeal cancer accounts for 40% of head and neck malignancies and 1% of all cancer-related deaths worldwide. We evaluated the laryngeal cancer microbiome to identify cancer-specific genera as potential treatment targets.MethodsA prospective study was conducted using 57 laryngeal mucosal samples from 24 treatment-naive laryngeal cancer patients and 33 patients who were undergoing otolaryngological surgery unrelated to oral or laryngeal diseases (01/2023-09/2025). DNA was extracted and amplified in triplicate, targeting the V3/V4 region of the 16S rRNA gene, followed by paired-end 2 × 300 bp sequencing on the Illumina NextSeq 2000. Amplicon sequence variants were identified via DADA2 and assigned to genera using a naive Bayes classifier. Two samples with zero classified read pairs were excluded.ResultsMost patients were male (87.5% cancer, 66.7% controls) and smokers (83.3% cancer, 54.5% controls). Cancer patients' core laryngeal microbiomes uniquely contained Parvimonas (3.67%; 95% CI: 0.70%-6.64%), and Campylobacter (1.12%; 95% CI: 0.60%-1.63%), while control patients' uniquely contained Corynebacterium (2.97%; 95% CI: 0.00%-7.67%) and Alloprevotella (1.34%; 95% CI: 0.64%-2.04%). Cancer samples were significantly enriched in 19 genera, notably Peptococcus (2.93, q = 0.0003), Campylobacter (1.68, q = 0.009), and Parvimonas (2.02, q = 0.03), compared to controls.ConclusionsLaryngeal cancer patients' samples displayed microbial dysbiosis, with enrichment of microbes present in gastrointestinal cancers, cervical cancer, and inflammatory states; they also exhibited loss of immunoprotective taxa. These findings support that microbiome profiling can distinguish malignant mucosa and guide future studies targeting genera increased in cancer, including Parvimonas and Campylobacter.Level of evidence: 3

records.title: Relevance of the Avalon Assemblage as an Astrobiological Analog for Icy Ocean Worlds.
records.abstract: We discuss the astrobiological potential of Earth's first animals--the nearly 600-million-year-old Avalon assemblage--and the relevance that these ancient communities may have for the search for life on icy or cold water worlds. The Avalon assemblage originated on deep, dark, salty, and cold seafloors with intriguing similarities to hypothesized icy ocean world habitats. These fossils provide an opportunity to study the signatures of entire communities of organisms that lived under conditions unlike those on Earth today. We discuss how information gleaned from the Avalon assemblage applies to the search for life on icy ocean worlds and explore how the physicochemical nature of their habitat could provide insights for astrobiology search strategies. Although the focus in astrobiology is on microbial communities, complex macroscopic life modifies its environment in ways and at scales that microbes cannot. The Avalon assemblage allows investigation of the circumstances under which such life emerged, clarifying the role of stochastic and probabilistic processes in evolution. Avalonian communities and their paleoenvironments capture the ecosystems of a world in transition from microbe- to animal-dominated, illuminating the potential changes driven by these first animals-and their potentially detectable biosignatures. We close by framing questions that can leverage insights from the Avalon assemblage for biosignature detection and identify research opportunities for further exploration.

records.title: Advances in assessing donor organ quality and perioperative risk for kidney transplantation.
records.abstract: Kidney transplantation faces persistent challenges in accurately evaluating donor organ quality and predicting long-term outcomes, with traditional assessment methods demonstrating limited predictive capacity. The increasing utilization of marginal-quality donor organs has intensified the need for sophisticated evaluation strategies. Machine perfusion technology has transformed organ preservation from mere static storage to a dynamic platform potentially enabling real-time monitoring, assessment, and interventions during the preservation period. Molecular profiling technologies such as genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics could provide refined biomarkers for donor kidney assessment across several phases of kidney transplantation. The first window arises during donor evaluation. Techniques such as high-resolution molecular typing, genetic profiling, epigenomic markers, and artificial intelligence-enhanced imaging provide additional information compared to traditional scoring systems. During organ preservation, a second window emerges, allowing additional, isolated assessment of the organ after procurement but before transplantation. Machine perfusion systems enable sampling of perfusate and tissue for multi-omics analysis to characterize injury or function, although most candidate biomarkers remain at the discovery or early validation stage. After transplantation, donor-derived cell-free deoxyribonucleic acid, urinary chemokines, and advanced imaging modalities offer non-invasive early detection of graft injury. Clinical translation of these new techniques faces substantial challenges: most studies are single-center and have small sample sizes, assay standardization remains incomplete, and evidence linking biomarker-guided decisions to improved long-term graft survival is lacking. Machine learning may enhance risk stratification but remains largely unvalidated in prospective trials. Future progress requires a shift from short-term endpoint prediction to long-term outcome validation through multicenter studies, standardized protocols, and equitable implementation strategies.
records.authors: Zuo Y, Lantinga VA, Orozco-García E, Ogurlu B, Moers C.

records.title: Functional characterization of IFNγrel in Takifugu obscurus and its roles in host immune response and lipid metabolism.
records.abstract: As a member of the type Ⅱ IFNs, IFNγrel exhibits distinct functional roles in immune modulation and host metabolism in teleost. In our previous study, an IFNγrel homolog was identified in the obscure puffer Takifugu obscurus (ToIFNγrel), and the function and regulatory activity of ToIFNγrel were further investigated in the present study. The transcriptional levels of ToIFNγrel were constitutively detected in all the six examined tissues under normal physiological conditions, with the highest expression observed in the intestine, and the lowest in head kidney. The transcripts of ToIFNγrel exhibited significant upregulation in liver, spleen, and head kidney following various bacterial challenge, whereas almost no significant responses were detected in head kidney post poly(I:C) stimulation. Notably, in vitro antiviral assays showed that recombinant protein of ToIFNγrel (rToIFNγrel) treatment effectively alleviated Chinese chub virus (CCV)-induced cytopathic effects in Channel catfish ovary (CCO) cells, suggesting the potential antiviral activity of ToIFNγrel. In addition, rToIFNγrel treatment reduced intracellular Aeromonas hydrophila loads in CCO cells, as determined by CFU assays, without affecting cell viability. In vivo administration of rToIFNγrel significantly increased the transcription of interferon receptor components (IFNgR1 and IFNgR2) and interferon-stimulated genes (Mx1 and PKR2), as well as genes related to innate immune sensing (cGAS), inflammatory signaling (NF-κB), and metabolic regulation (mTOR), whereas no significant changes were observed in tnf14 and il1 expression. Furthermore, the contents of triacylglycerols (TAGs) and cholesteryl esters (CEs) in the liver and intestine were significantly increased following rToIFNγrel stimulation, accompanied by increased CD36 expression and decreased ATGL and ATP5D expression. In contrast, the expression of the lipid droplets (LDs) marker protein PLIN3 showed no significant change, suggesting that rToIFNγrel promotes neutral lipid accumulation and alters lipid metabolism-related gene expression, whereas its effect on LD formation remains to be determined. These results collectively demonstrate that ToIFNγrel exerts immunoregulatory roles not only by enhancing the expression of immune-related genes but also by modulating host lipid metabolism, which would provide new insight into the multifunctional roles of IFNγrel between immune signaling and lipid homeostasis in teleost.
records.authors: Cui N, Feng B, Xiao L, Zhou S, Xu J, Qin J, Zhao Z, Song X.

records.title: Epigenetic regulation of macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) by DNA methylation during Vibrio anguillarum infection in Ruditapes philippinarum.
records.abstract: To investigate the effects of Vibrio anguillarum infection on the expression of macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) and DNA methylation of its promoter in the Manila clam Ruditapes philippinarum, we analyzed MIF sequence homology and phylogenetic relationships, temporal expression patterns after V. anguillarum infection, and promoter DNA methylation profiles, and used a dual-luciferase reporter assay to validate the regulatory effect of methylation on promoter activity. The results showed that the conserved domain of R. philippinarum MIF exhibited the highest homology with those of Meretrix meretrix and Mercenaria mercenaria. qRT-PCR analysis showed that MIF expression was significantly upregulated 12 h after V. anguillarum infection, peaked at 48 h (approximately 5.64-fold higher than the level at 0 h), and then returned to basal levels. Bisulfite sequencing PCR (BSP) analysis showed that MIF promoter methylation levels decreased significantly at 24 h and 48 h after infection, with the most pronounced demethylation observed at CpG 3, CpG 9, and CpG 11. Promoter methylation levels were significantly negatively correlated with MIF expression (R = -0.7552, P = 0.0062). The dual-luciferase reporter assay showed that in vitro methylation treatment significantly decreased MIF promoter activity. These results suggest that V. anguillarum infection may upregulate MIF expression by inducing promoter demethylation, thereby contributing to the host immune response. This study provides a reference for understanding the immune regulatory mechanisms underlying the resistance of R. philippinarum to V. anguillarum infection from an epigenetic perspective.
records.authors: Huang T, Li J, Nie H.

records.title: Structural Diversity and Functional Roles of the Internalin Family Proteins in Listeria monocytogenes.
records.abstract: Listeria monocytogenes is an important foodborne intracellular pathogen that can cause listeriosis in humans and animals, with a relatively high mortality rate. Internalin (Inl) family proteins are critical virulence factors of L. monocytogenes and play essential roles in bacterial adhesion, host cell invasion, tissue colonization, immune evasion, and systemic infection. In recent years, with the continuous advancement of genomics, structural biology, and host-pathogen interaction studies, an increasing number of internalin family members and their biological functions have been identified. Different internalins exhibit significant differences in receptor recognition, tissue tropism, and pathogenic mechanisms. This review systematically summarizes the structural characteristics and classification of the internalin family in L. monocytogenes, with particular emphasis on recent advances in the functions of major family members, including InlA, InlB, InlC, InlK, InlF, InlP, InlL, and InlJ, in intestinal invasion, penetration of the placental and blood-brain barriers, intracellular survival, immune evasion, biofilm formation, and host interactions. Furthermore, recent research hotspots in the functional characterization of internalin proteins are discussed, along with their potential applications in elucidating virulence mechanisms, vaccine development, and targeted prevention and control strategies. This review aims to provide a theoretical reference for further investigations into the pathogenic mechanisms of L. monocytogenes and the development of novel prevention and control strategies.
records.authors: Leng Q, Ma Y, Xia X, Qin X, Hirata T, Dong Q, Li Z.

records.title: Microbial metabolism of methotrexate produces a STAT3 signaling molecule that alleviates gut inflammation.
records.abstract: Methotrexate (MTX) is a gold standard therapy for inflammatory diseases but has mixed therapeutic success in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). The gut microbiota impact MTX efficacy and toxicity by metabolizing MTX and altering its bioavailability, yet how inflammation alters this metabolism, and how the resulting metabolites act on the host, remain poorly understood. Here, we find that gut microbes, notably Clostridium asparagiforme, metabolize MTX via carboxypeptidase G2 (CPDG2) to produce deoxyaminopteroic acid (DAMPA). In intestinal epithelial cells, DAMPA preserves mitochondrial health through mitochondrial signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) signaling and enhances mitophagy. DAMPA administration attenuates intestinal inflammation in vivo, and remodels colonic mitochondrial pathways. IBD mouse models show reduced microbial CPDG2 and DAMPA, while patients with IBD show reduced CPDG2 gene abundance and suppressed DAMPA-enriched mitochondrial pathways, potentially explaining MTX outcomes in IBD. Together, these findings reframe microbial MTX metabolism from passive drug detoxification to active regulation of host mitochondrial and inflammatory homeostasis.
records.authors: Cho J, Danner R, Kim WS, Lopez L, Williams J, Singh A, Han JA, Van Vranken JG, Walker AS, Rhoads TW, Chaudhari SN.

records.title: Broad vaccine protection against globally diverse influenza A/H5Nx viruses.
records.abstract: Influenza A/H5Nx viruses continue to diversify and undergo gene reassortment as they infect avian and mammalian hosts worldwide. The severity of human infections varies substantially between different H5 clades and neuraminidase (NA) reassortants, creating unpredictable pandemic risk. Existing H5 vaccines, typically based on a single hemagglutinin (HA) strain, cannot keep pace with this natural variation. To address this problem, we computationally engineer HA, NA, and M2 antigens representing the global antigenic space of circulating H5Nx viruses, prioritizing N1 and N6 subtypes associated with the highest threat in humans. The resulting digitally immune-optimized mRNA vaccine, DVX-panH5Nx, elicits broad HA neutralization and NA inhibition across divergent clades in mice and ferrets. Compared to WHO candidate vaccine viruses (CVVs), DVX-panH5Nx confers superior protection against antigenically distinct H5N1 challenges spanning two decades of viral evolution, demonstrating that computationally designed multivalent antigen vaccines can overcome natural influenza diversification and provide a scalable strategy for pre-pandemic preparedness.

records.title: Layered double hydroxides functionalized electrospun recycled polyamide 6 from fishing nets: structure-property relationships for antimicrobial non-woven fabrics.
records.abstract: Plastic pollution, particularly marine plastic waste from discarded fishing nets, represents a significant environmental challenge and highlights the need for effective strategies to recover and valorize end-of-life polymers. Polyamide 6 (PA6) fishing nets are an underexploited source for the development of high-value functional materials. This work develops antimicrobial non-woven fabrics (NWFs) from recycled PA6 (rPA6) incorporating organo-modified Mg/Al layered double hydroxides (LDHs) intercalated with antimicrobial anions, namely ascorbate (ASA), ferulate (FER), salicylate (SAL), and citrate (CA), into rPA6, followed by electrospinning. The resulting nanofibrous NWFs were characterized by Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FESEM), Fourier Transformed Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), Wide Angle/Small Angle X-ray Scattering with micro-beam (μWAXS/μSAXS), thermal analysis and tested against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus. Homogeneous nanofibers were obtained and LDH incorporation preserved rPA6 chemical structure while reducing crystallinity. rPA6/LDH-FER, rPA6/LDH-ASA, and rPA6/LDH-CA, showed 96.7 to 99.9% bacterial mortality. After thermal aging at 115 °C, LDH-containing NWFs exhibited improved structural stability. These results demonstrate the feasibility of converting recycled PA6 fishing-nets into functional antimicrobial nanofibrous fabrics through LDH functionalization and electrospinning, supporting circular and sustainable applications of marine recycled polyamides.

records.title: Lessons learned from model species: Molecular markers for anthropogenic pollutant toxicity in cetaceans.
records.abstract: The planet is currently facing a triple crisis driven by climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution. While the effects of environmental contaminants on reproduction, neurological function, and immune processes are well established in model species, far less is known about their impacts on marine sentinels such as cetaceans. Although contaminant burdens can be quantified, there is a lack of validated biomarkers that reliably capture molecular and cellular effects, limiting robust impact assessment and conservation strategies. Cetaceans exhibit unique physiological and metabolic adaptations, including specialised lipid dynamics and life-history traits, complicating direct extrapolation from model organisms. Here, we review current knowledge of biomarkers associated with three major contaminant classes: persistent organic pollutants (POPs), heavy metals, and microplastics. Candidate biomarkers such as cytochrome P4501A1, acetylcholinesterase, and metallothioneins are well characterised in experimental systems but show inconsistent responses in cetaceans, influenced by ecological, physiological, and methodological factors. Emerging evidence indicates that microplastics may drive gut inflammation, microbiome disruption, and systemic stress responses, although validated biomarkers remain scarce. Overall, we highlight the limitations of single-marker approaches and the need for integrative frameworks capturing complex, multi-stressor responses across biological scales. Future efforts should prioritise robust, early-warning biomarkers that account for species-specific physiology, trophic ecology, and cumulative exposure. Progress will require cross-disciplinary collaboration, integration of multi-omics tools, and improved standardisation of methods. Strengthening biomarker frameworks in cetaceans is essential for advancing marine conservation and understanding shared risks to ocean and human health.
records.authors: von Hellfeld R, Gade C, Williams RS, Derous D.

records.title: Precision recreation and multiplex stacking of disease-resistance alleles in tomato using optimized prime editing.
records.abstract: Prime editing enables precise modification of plant genomes and provides a means to recreate beneficial alleles underlying agronomically important traits. However, efficient and multiplexable prime editing systems remain limited in dicot crops. Here, we developed optimized prime editing systems for tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) and applied them to engineer and stack disease-resistance alleles. Using three tomato prime editors, TomPE2, TomPE6c, and TomPE7, we recreated a naturally occurring resistance-associated deletion identified in pepper by precisely deleting two leucine residues from the CYSTM-domain proteins SlBs5 and SlBs5L. The resulting tomato lines exhibited enhanced resistance to Xanthomonas, demonstrating that a resistance allele can be functionally recreated across related crop species. In parallel, introduction of premature stop codons into the susceptibility gene SlDMR6 conferred resistance to both Xanthomonas and Pseudomonas syringae. Transcriptome profiling revealed distinct defense states: Slbs5/Slbs5L plants predominantly exhibited enhanced pathogen-induced defense responses, whereas Sldmr6 plants showed elevated basal defense. Comparison of prime editor architectures and culture temperatures revealed differences in editing activity and precision, with TomPE6c producing the highest proportion of precise edits. We further developed a modular multiplex prime editing system capable of simultaneously modifying multiple loci, enabling resistance alleles and regulatory variants to be combined within a single generation. The engineered alleles were stably inherited, and resistance phenotypes were maintained under elevated temperature conditions. Together, these results establish prime editing as an effective platform for precise recreation, engineering, and multiplex stacking of disease-resistance alleles and provide a framework for accelerating resistance breeding in crops.

records.title: Development of a tryptophan-based dual selection system to investigate S-layer spatial organization during cytokinesis in Sulfolobus acidocaldarius.
records.abstract: Sulfolobus acidocaldarius is a thermoacidophilic archaeon used as a model system for studying fundamental cellular processes and for emerging biotechnological applications. However, the limited availability of selectable markers restricts advanced genetic manipulation in this organism. Here, we report the development of a tryptophan auxotrophy-based selection system in S. acidocaldarius. A ΔtrpBA mutant was constructed in the ΔpyrE background strain using a classical pop-in/pop-out recombination strategy. The resulting mutant exhibited little impairment of growth in rich medium, likely due to exogenous tryptophan supplied by complex nutrients, but failed to grow in a newly developed defined Brock-based amino acid dropout medium lacking tryptophan. Exploiting both uracil and tryptophan auxotrophies, we achieved dual-plasmid co-transformation and co-expression of the surface layer proteins and a dominant-negative mutant of the AAA-ATPase Vps4, revealing the accumulation of surface layer lattice forming protein SlaA at the midzone of division-arrested cells and its membrane anchor SlaB. Together, these results provide evidence for spatial regulation of S-layer assembly during archaeal cytokinesis while expanding the genetic toolkit available for S. acidocaldarius.

records.title: Genes in the Light: A Scoping Review of Bacterial Transcriptional Responses to Visible Range Radiation Across Wavelength and Dose.
records.abstract: Non-phototrophic bacteria do not use light for energy, yet many detect visible radiation and reorganise gene expression accordingly. Two routes are involved: dedicated photoreceptors (flavin-binding BLUF and LOV domains, biliverdin-binding bacteriophytochromes and cobalamin-binding CarH/LitR regulators), and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated when endogenous porphyrins and flavins absorb light, which trigger an oxidative-stress programme without any photosensory protein. This scoping review maps which genes change expression under visible light (400-700 nm) and how responses vary with wavelength, dose and context. We searched Elicit, PubMed/MEDLINE and Europe PMC, performed citation chasing, and charted 70 core primary studies. Blue light (400-470 nm) is reported to produce the largest transcriptional changes in most direct comparisons. Blue-light responses are frequently but not universally characterised by induction of oxidative-stress defences and repression of carbohydrate metabolism, virulence determinants and quorum-sensing systems; important exceptions exist, including up-regulation of type III secretion genes in Pseudomonas syringae. Red and far-red light (620-760 nm) elicits substantial change chiefly in species encoding bacteriophytochromes. Temperature determines whether photoreceptor-dependent regulation occurs at all: in Listeria monocytogenes and Acinetobacter baumannii it operates at environmental temperatures and is attenuated or reversed at 37 °C. Dose-response data and functional validation are scarce, and dosimetry is reported in incompatible units; standardised dosimetry, time-resolved designs and phenotypic confirmation are the principal needs.
records.authors: Yousuf Azeemi ST, Azeemi S, Shaukat SF, Mahmood K.

records.title: Genomic signatures of reproductive isolation are decoupled from floral divergence in a long-standing hybrid zone.
records.abstract: A central goal in evolutionary biology is to understand how species boundaries are maintained despite gene flow. Two North American wildflower species with divergent floral syndromes, Penstemon davidsonii (bee syndrome) and P. newberryi (bird syndrome), have formed hybrid zones in the eastern Sierra Nevada for at least 85 years. We combined multiple approaches to test whether divergent floral syndromes enforce reproductive isolation as predicted by classic models of pollinator-driven ecological speciation. The two parent species exhibited strong divergence across multivariate trait space and have maintained genomic differentiation despite persistent hybridization. Floral hue, a key component of pollination syndrome, mapped to a single genomic region containing two candidate genes with large effects on anthocyanin pigment composition. Pollinator visual models indicated that genetic variation at this region affects detectability to hummingbirds, but not bees. Genomic cline analyses identified many significantly steep clines, suggesting a polygenic basis to reproductive isolation. Surprisingly, these barriers appear unrelated to floral isolation; the major floral hue locus exhibits a strikingly shallow genomic cline and elevated heterozygosity, suggesting pervasive gene flow. Our results reveal that conspicuous trait divergence can be decoupled from reproductive barriers, challenging assumptions about how reproductive isolation is maintained in hybridizing populations.
records.journal: Evolution; international journal of organic evolution
records.authors: Stone BW, Williams NH, Depatie TH, Radford ZJ, Mosley AM, Wessinger CA.

records.title: Cytoplasmic ATR orchestrates PRRSV and EBOV replication organelle assembly via vimentin phosphorylation.
records.abstract: The ataxia telangiectasia-mutated and Rad3-related (ATR) kinase is a well-established master regulator of the DNA damage response and replication stress. In this study, we uncover an unexpected, conserved role of ATR in promoting the replication of two distinct RNA viruses-an arterivirus and a filovirus-through vimentin phosphorylation. Acute pharmacologic inhibition or knockdown of ATR robustly suppress viral replication and sharply reduce the formation of double-membrane vesicles and membrane-less condensates that serve as replication organelles (ROs) for these divergent viral classes. Notably, although ATR is recruited to cytoplasmic ROs throughout the viral life cycle, it acts specifically at the replication stage without affecting viral attachment, entry, or egress. We further show that ATR directly interacts with and phosphorylates vimentin within ROs, driving vimentin rearrangement and delineating RO boundaries. Mechanistically, ATR-dependent phosphorylation of vimentin at Ser459 is indispensable for RO formation during infection by both PRRSV and EBOV. Together, these findings reveal a conserved ATR-vimentin signaling axis that promotes RO biogenesis across diverse RNA viruses, defining a noncanonical function of cytoplasmic ATR in orchestrating the assembly of both membrane-bound and membrane-less replication compartments via vimentin phosphorylation.
records.authors: Xu C, Xia Y, Cao Z, Xu X, Xiang Y, Li F, Li P, Chiu S, Cai G, Wang X.

records.title: Raman spectra identify vancomycin-resistant phenotypes and their transcriptomic features in Staphylococcus aureus.
records.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is a pathogenic bacterium that has been linked to multiple epidemics of novel antibiotic resistance. Vancomycin is the first-line antibiotic treatment for methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) infections; however, various vancomycin-non-susceptible MRSA strains have emerged globally. Rapid assessment of the resistance levels and the underlying molecular profiles is crucial for preventing their spread and for counteracting resistance. Nevertheless, a broad resistance spectrum and diverse genetic alterations have hindered these efforts. Here, we demonstrated that vancomycin resistance levels of various MRSA strains can be determined using dimension-reduced Raman spectra obtained from single cells. Furthermore, transcriptome profiles of different strains can be predicted from these spectra using simple linear regression. This Raman-transcriptome correspondence enables mapping of transcriptomic components onto a dimension-reduced Raman space, allowing for characterization of gene groups associated with different phenotypes. Additionally, single-cell Raman spectroscopy has successfully identified a strain with higher phenotypic heterogeneity, which was subsequently validated by single-cell growth analysis. Overall, our results demonstrate the efficacy of Raman spectroscopy for identifying resistant phenotypes, their associated features for gene expression, and intrapopulation phenotypic heterogeneity.ImportanceThe spread of antibiotic-resistant bacteria threatens human health worldwide. Rapid identification of antibiotic resistance and molecular-level features of an infected pathogen is crucial for treating patients and counteracting the emergence and spread of new resistant bacteria. Here, we demonstrate that Raman spectra, measurable by exposing individual cells to a focused laser, can be used to infer the resistance phenotypes and global gene expression profiles of different Staphylococcus aureus strains. Furthermore, we present a method to visualize transcriptome components using the major axes of the dimension-reduced Raman space linked to important phenotypic features, such as resistance and virulence. This method identifies several gene sets related to crucial phenotypic features of pathogenic bacteria. Our results demonstrate a novel application of spectroscopy in microbiology by enabling the simultaneous identification of resistant and virulent phenotypes, as well as the underlying gene expression features.
records.authors: Kamei K-iF, Okura R, Kobayashi-Kirschvink KJ, Yamaguchi T, Katayama Y, Wakamoto Y.

records.title: Polyphosphate and Disordered Hfq Regions Drive DNA Compaction through Conformation-Dependent Interactions.
records.abstract: The RNA-binding protein Hfq and inorganic polyphosphate (polyP) were previously suggested to promote DNA compaction of AT-rich regions by forming heterochromatin-like structures, yet the underlying molecular mechanism remains unclear. Here, we combine coarse-grained and all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the interplay between Hfq, polyP, and DNA. Under physiological conditions, polyP electrostatically interacts with the distal faces of multiple Hfq hexamers, clustering them near DNA and leaving the proximal faces available to interact with the DNA minor groove via the disordered N-termini, thereby promoting compaction. While this mechanism shows limited dependence on DNA sequence, it is highly sensitive to environmental conditions. Under high-salt conditions, electrostatic interactions are screened, weakening polyP-Hfq association and limiting Hfq clustering, while stabilization of non-canonical DNA conformations exposes hydrophobic surfaces. These changes shift the mode of Hfq interaction with DNA toward its distal face and disordered C-termini, favoring hydrophobic interactions and reducing compaction. Together, our findings reveal a conformation-dependent switch in Hfq-DNA interaction modes governed by cellular conditions, providing a molecular framework for environment-responsive genome organization in bacteria.
records.authors: Navon Y, Levy Y.

records.title: A naturally occurring recombinant PRRSV with a JXA1-derived nsp9 fragment is associated with enhanced virulence in piglets.
records.abstract: Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV) nonstructural protein 9 (nsp9), the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, has been implicated as a critical virulence determinant of highly pathogenic PRRSV (HP-PRRSV) through reverse genetics studies with engineered chimeric viruses. However, field isolates that naturally carry such nsp9-centric recombination events-thereby serving as potential in vivo models-remain exceptionally rare. Here we report the isolation and characterization of a novel PRRSV strain TJ25928 from a farm in China experiencing a severe PRRS outbreak. TJ25928 possesses the characteristic 131-amino-acid deletion pattern of NADC30-like strains and phylogenetically belongs to Lineage 1.8. Recombination analysis revealed a distinct configuration: the backbone of TJ25928 is derived from NADC30-like strains, while a discrete fragment within the nsp9 coding region (nt 7856-8923) is derived from JXA1-like HP-PRRSV. The boundaries of this nsp9 fragment overlap substantially with the nsp9 segment previously implicated in fatal virulence in engineered chimeric viruses. In piglet challenge experiments, TJ25928 induced significant febrile response (8-12 days post-infection), pronounced growth suppression (approximately 28% reduction in total weight gain at 21 days post-infection), and 33.3% (1/3) mortality. TJ25928 represents an important example of a field isolate that naturally carries the nsp9 recombination configuration previously studied by reverse genetics, providing a valuable natural model for future investigations into the role of nsp9 in PRRSV virulence. These findings underscore the pathogenic potential of nsp9 recombination events in the field and offer a useful tool for future mechanistic studies on PRRSV virulence.

records.title: Positive promotion effect of negative potential on propanethiol degradation in microbial electrolytic cells.
records.abstract: Volatile organic sulfur compounds (VOSCs) are typical odorous pollutants that are difficult to abate. The effective removal of VOSCs by microbial electrolytic cells (MECs) is a promising strategy for reducing mitigation. This work employed propanethiol (PT) as a representative contaminate and explored the performance of MEC by controlling anodic potentials at -0.4, -0.2, 0, 0.2, 0.4 V (vs. Ag/AgCl). The results indicated that the potential of -0.2 V and -0.4 V increased PT removal by 8.2% and 13.9%, while sulfate conversion rose by 6.7% and 12.6%, demonstrating the prominent enhancement of negative polarization for PT remediation. Low-negative bioanode potentials of -0.4 V and -0.2 V drove high sulfur-to-sulfate conversion of 51.2% and 45.3%, highest protein/polysaccharide ratio of 1.37 and outer-membrane c-type cytochromes content of 36.7 μmol/cm3. Moreover, microbial community analysis showed that the abundance of functional species of Acinetobacter sp. and Thiobacillus sp. were increased. Furthermore, the observed nanowires together with metagenomic evidence further demonstrated that negative potentials exerted positive effects on microbial electroactivity. Overall, this study elucidates bioanode potential driven PT degradation of in MECs, providing valuable implications for abatement of VOSCs via bioelectrochemical systems.
records.authors: You J, Liu Z, Li Z, Ji Z, Yu J, Qu M.

records.title: TRACE: a framework for traceable biomedical resource construction demonstrated through single-cell glaucoma data
records.abstract: The growing availability of public omics datasets presents opportunities for biomedical research, yet constructing research question-driven resources from distributed studies remains challenging due to heterogeneous data, incomplete metadata and limited documentation of curation decisions. Here, we present TRACE (Traceable Resource Assembly and Curation Ecosystem), a general framework that links systematic knowledge discovery, data curation and resource delivery while preserving provenance throughout resource construction. We demonstrate TRACE through TRACE-scGlaucoma, a curated single-cell transcriptomics resource for glaucoma and optic nerve biology. Systematic screening identified 57 eligible studies, of which 42 provided accessible datasets comprising approximately 3.3 million cells. The resource provides harmonised metadata, standardised cell-type annotations and reusable expression objects while retaining original study information and curation provenance. We demonstrate its analytical utility through cellular enrichment of glaucoma GWAS-associated genes, comparing candidate drug-repurposing signals across distinct biological contexts and assessment of cell-type annotation reliability. TRACE provides a systematic and traceable approach to transforming fragmented public datasets into reusable biomedical resources, supporting reproducible analyses and future extensions across disease areas and data modalities.

records.title: Physiological mapping and prediction reveal stress-responsive translation initiation landscapes
records.abstract: Translation initiation defines the protein output of the transcriptome, but its physiological dynamics in cells and tissues remain incompletely characterized. Here we develop TISCA2, an inhibitor-free method that captures eIF5B-associated initiating ribosomes to map translation initiation sites genome-wide. By directly identifying start sites rather than inferring translation from elongating-ribosome periodicity, TISCA2 improves the detection of short and overlapping translons. Translation of a subset of TISCA2-identified translons is supported by N-terminal proteomics and HLA-I immunopeptidomics. The arsenite-induced integrated stress response broadly redistributes start-site usage, reducing upstream initiation in favor of downstream initiation. TISCA2 further reveals tissue-specific initiation landscapes in vivo, with increased detection of downstream candidate start sites in the testis. Finally, we develop IncepTIS, a sequence-based deep learning model that predicts position-resolved and condition-dependent initiation landscapes. IncepTIS-guided optimization generates de novo mRNA 5′ leaders with stress-responsive initiation patterns. Together, TISCA2 and IncepTIS provide an experimental and computational framework for mapping, predicting and engineering translation initiation in mammalian cells and tissues.

records.title: Gut Roseburia hominis-derived 10-hydroxystearic acid alleviates metabolic disorder by restoring hepatic fatty acid metabolism
records.abstract: Metabolic disorders and health-promoting dietary interventions represent complementary contexts of metabolic impairment and improvement, providing an opportunity to identify gut microbial taxa associated with both disease status and dietary response. Here, we integrated five independent human cohorts spanning metabolic disorders and dietary interventions and identified Roseburia hominis as a gut microbial taxon that consistently decreased in metabolic disorders and increased after dietary interventions. Beyond species abundance, strain-level genetic variation in R. hominis provided additional information for distinguishing metabolic disorder status and stratifying cardiometabolic severity. Integration of phenotype-associated variants with circulating metabolomics prioritized ohyA, encoding an oleate hydratase, as a candidate functional determinant linking R. hominis genetic variation to host metabolic heterogeneity. An ohyA-based genetic burden score was associated with adverse cardiometabolic traits and changed longitudinally during dietary intervention, while circulating metabolites statistically accounted for part of the associations between ohyA variants and host phenotypes. Functional experiments demonstrated that R. hominis OhyA protein converts oleic acid to 10-hydroxystearic acid (10-HSA), whereas an OhyA carrying five prioritized missense substitutions showed markedly impaired enzymatic activity. In high-fat diet-fed mice, 10-HSA attenuated body-weight gain, improved glucose homeostasis and insulin sensitivity, and reduced dyslipidemia and hepatic steatosis. Multi-omics profiling revealed limited remodeling of the gut microbiota but pronounced hepatic transcriptional and metabolic responses, characterized by activation of PPARα-associated lipid-metabolic pathways, altered fatty-acid oxidation and desaturation, and remodeling of hepatic lipid composition. Together, these findings establish a diet-responsive R. hominis-OhyA-10-HSA axis linking microbial variation to host metabolic dysfunction and show that 10-HSA can improve metabolic health in mice.

records.title: Fluorescence microscopic evidence for intracellular silicon storage pools in diatoms and their partial separation
records.abstract: Diatoms are unicellular algae that occur ubiquitously in almost every salt- and freshwater habitat on earth. Silicic acid is taken up from the environment and stored in intracellular silicon storage pools (SSPs) to form species specific silica based cell walls (frustules). During biosilica formation in the silicon deposition vesicle (SDV), the silicon is transported from SSPs into the SDV. The present contribution describes the fluorescence microscopic visualization and quantification of silica solely formed from SSPs under silicon starvation. Labeling with the fluorescence marker PDMPO demonstrates continuing cell growth and cell division without silicon uptake from the environment. The SSPs of Cyclotella nana may account for up to 1/3 of total cellular silicon and intracellular concentrations up to ca. 540 mM, significantly beyond the saturation level (2 mM). The chemical state and localization of SSPs within cells are yet unclear. Here, we report a method for subcellular fractionation of C. nana by density gradient centrifugation. Quantification of cytoplasmic silicon yields 3 to 10% of the total cellular silicon corresponding to intracellular concentrations of ca. 50 to 160 mM. Labeling with NMR active 29Si shows that this silicon occurs as condensed silica, i.e., silicic acid is converted into condensed silica after uptake. However, the detected intracellular silicon concentrations are lower than the value of ca. 540 mM predicted by the fluorescence experiments. It is thus concluded that the missing SSP silicon is either present in the form of large aggregates or compartments. Alternatively, they may also be bound to cell wall biosilica.
records.authors: Reichelt T, Breyer J, Brunner E.

records.title: Second-site capsule-locus mutations, not Ade efflux disruption, determine phage susceptibility across an Acinetobacter baumannii transposon mutant panel
records.abstract: Resistance-Nodulation-Division (RND) efflux pumps have been implicated in phage adsorption in several Gram-negative bacteria, suggesting that AdeABC, AdeFGH and AdeIJK, the three characterised RND efflux systems of multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, could play a similar role. We tested this hypothesis using five phages (Equilibrator, Taro, AT01, BB02, and AC03) and a panel of 13 A. baumannii strains, including nine AB5075 transposon mutants affecting AdeABC, AdeFGH, or AdeIJK. Host-range testing, efficiency-of-plating assays, capsule-associated density measurements, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and whole-genome sequencing were performed to assess the relationship between genotype and phage infection. Overall, the data did not support a role for the Ade components as receptors. Phages Equilibrator, Taro and AT01 formed plaques on every strain, and the restricted host ranges of BB02 and AC03 did not correspond to disruption of a particular efflux system. Sequencing instead identified second-site mutations in the KL25 capsule locus in six of the ten AB5075 strains. These included a 1,998-bp deletion affecting wzc, substitutions in mnaA and mnaB, an ISAba13 insertion in a putative glycosyltransferase and a subpopulation-associated frameshift in wzx. AC03 formed plaques on all six strains with capsule-locus changes but on none of the five strains without them. Capsule dependence differed among the other phages: relative to the parental AB5075, infection by these phages, Equilibrator, Taro and BB02, was restricted on the capsule-deficient wzc::T26 strain, whereas AT01 efficiency was only slightly reduced. Insertion-site mapping also distinguished a near-terminal adeK insertion that retained the parental antimicrobial phenotype from an early adeK insertion associated with loss of AdeIJK function. Together, these findings identify capsule-locus variation as the strongest correlation with phage susceptibility in this panel and demonstrate the importance of verifying mutant genomes before assigning phenotypes to their annotated insertions.

records.title: Nematode species differ in susceptibility and response to the nematode-trapping fungus Arthrobotrys oligospora
records.abstract: Fungal predators of nematodes are widespread and represent promising candidates for biological control of parasitic nematodes. However, the behavioural and molecular mechanisms underlying nematode-fungus interactions remain poorly understood, especially for nematodes other than Caenorhabditis elegans. We investigated the interactions between the nematode-trapping fungus Arthrobotrys oligospora and three nematode species: (i) free-living C. elegans, (ii) fig-associated C. inopinata, and (iii) the free-living adult life cycle stage of the gastrointestinal parasite Strongyloides ratti. A. oligospora trapped S. ratti more efficiently than either C. elegans or C. inopinata. Behavioural analyses revealed species-specific differences in nematode locomotion. S. ratti moved slower, travelled shorter distances and showed lower displacement than Caenorhabditis spp. To test whether locomotion influences fungal trapping, we examined eight C. elegans mutants with hyper- or hypoactive locomotory phenotypes. Although both groups moved at similar speeds, hyperactive mutants showed greater displacement, which positively correlated with trap formation but did not explain trapping efficiency by A. oligospora. We investigated the fungal response during interaction with the three nematodes. Exposure to S. ratti, but not to Caenorhabditis spp, resulted in reduced sporulation and differential expression of sporulation-associated genes. In nematodes, myosin-related genes responded to A. oligospora in a species-specific manner, including upregulation in C. elegans and downregulation in S. ratti. These transcriptional changes may reflect alterations in muscle structure, including reduction in dense body and mitochondrial size in Caenorhabditis species but not S. ratti during A. oligospora exposure. Together, our findings demonstrate that both fungal and nematode responses are nematode species dependent. These results improve our understanding of nematode-fungus interactions and highlight the importance of nematode species when developing nematode-trapping fungi as a biological control agent.
