records.title: Mapping the regulatory wiring of endothelial cell differentiation reveals a critical role for Hippo mechanosignaling
records.abstract: At each step of development, stem cells encounter a branching decision to differentiate into one type of cell or another. This decision is executed through the action of competing gene programs that specify different cellular identities. Consequently, creating a comprehensive map of the gene programs that drive each branching step of human cell differentiation remains a long-sought goal of developmental and stem cell biology. Here, we introduce a framework combining genome-wide CRISPR screens, single-cell readouts, and gene program inference to systematically discover and characterize regulators of cell differentiation. This framework includes a method for CRISPR perturbations paired with single-cell RNA-seq called circular capture Perturb-seq (CC-Perturb-seq), which improves gRNA detection from split-pool combinatorial indexing protocols and enables perturbing many candidate regulators to map their effects on gene programs. We applied this framework to map how human pluripotent stem cells differentiate into arterial endothelial cells (ECs), and identified 174 regulators that promote or inhibit EC differentiation. By tracking gene programs across three stages of differentiation, we resolved when and how regulators divert cells toward alternative fates. This map revealed an unexpected requirement for the Hippo mechanosignaling pathway in EC specification. During lateral mesoderm differentiation, Hippo mechanosignaling was required to activate ETV2, the master transcriptional regulator of endothelial identity. Inhibiting Hippo blocked ETV2 even in the presence of VEGF and diverted progenitors to a mesenchymal fate in vitro. Likewise, Hippo signaling was required for maximal etv2 expression in developing zebrafish embryos. Conversely, pharmacologically activating the Hippo pathway increased the purity of both arterial and venous EC differentiation in vitro. Our framework thus identifies novel regulators of endothelial cell differentiation, improves stem-cell differentiation protocols via manipulation of mechanosignaling, and provides a generalizable platform for mapping the regulatory wiring of human development.

records.title: Bacillus cereus MHI 86 and Bacillus thuringiensis 5-29 both produce the antilisterial bacteriocin thuricin S – analysis of antimicrobial spectrum, stability, and producer strain suitability, including cytotoxicity evaluation
records.abstract: Abstract    Thuricin-like bacteriocins are known for their potent antibacterial properties. This study characterizes thuricin S from  Bacillus (B.) cereus  MHI 86 and  B. thuringiensis  5–29 previously isolated from foods. Cell-free supernatants and partially purified thuricin S exhibited antibacterial activity against Gram-positive species, including  Listeria  and  Bacillus  . Thuricin S production started at mid exponential growth phase. Minimum inhibitory concentrations against  L. monocytogenes  were 5.73 µg/mL (MHI 86) and 10.77 µg/mL (5–29). Both genomes harbor thuricin S-encoding open reading frames. From 8 h of growth, transcription of the bacteriocin gene cluster was consistently detected with most prominent bands at 120 bp. Accordingly, antibacterially active peptides were found at ~ 3.1 kDa, consistent with the size of thuricin S. Ultra-performance liquid chromatography-electrospray ionization mass spectrometry confirmed the molecular mass of the partially purified peptides as 3137.6 Da. The bacteriocins were active at neutral and acidic pH (3–7) and up to 80°C. In conclusion, this study is the first to provide a comparative characterisation of thuricin S in two different  Bacillus  spp. It sheds light on the genetic and transcriptional basis of thuricin S production, as well as its growth and production kinetics, antimicrobial activity, molecular weight, stability, and associated toxin production and cytotoxicity. Notably, thuricin S can be used as a natural agent against  L. monocytogenes  to control post-pasteurisation contamination.
records.authors: Batman SG, Kittler S, Plötz M, Dräger G, Jessberger N.

records.title: Physicochemical Characterization, Cytotoxicity, and Antimicrobial Activity of Polymeric Nanoparticles for Ocular Delivery of Norfloxacin
records.abstract: Abstract    Ocular infections, can lead to severe complications, and may result in vision loss, if not treated effectively. Norfloxacin (NFX), a broad-spectrum fluoroquinolone antibiotic, acts by inhibiting bacterial DNA replication and transcription and is effective against drug-resistant pathogens commonly associated with serious ocular infections. However, its poor water solubility limits its therapeutic potential for ocular delivery. In this study nanoparticles was formulated with Eudragit® RS 100 (ERS100) and Polycaprolactone (PCL) to enhance the ocular bioavailability of NFX. The nanoparticles were prepared using the spray-drying method. According to the characterization studies the optimized formulation exhibited a particle size of 383.43 ± 8.01 nm, a low PDI of 0.135 ± 0.01, and a positively charged zeta potential of + 34.97 ± 0.22 mV, indicating excellent stability and favorable interaction with the negatively charged ocular surface, which may enhance the ocular bioavailability of NFX. Cytotoxicity studies using the MTT assay on the human retinal pigment epithelial cell line (ARPE-19) confirmed the ocular safety of the nanoparticles, as their IC  50  values vastly exceeded their minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs), indicating a broad therapeutic safety margin. Antimicrobial efficacy was further confirmed through disk diffusion and MIC assays. Based on the obtained results, it can be concluded that ERS100–PCL-based nanoparticles have strong potential as an effective ocular delivery system for NFX in the treatment of severe ocular infections.
records.authors: ÖZDEMİR İ, AYKAÇ K, ÖZMEN CK, ŞENEL B, SOYER P, BAŞARAN E.

records.title: Editing of SpNRAMP3, SpCAX3, and SpHMA3 differentially affects cadmium concentrations and growth responses in Sedum plumbizincicola.
records.abstract: Sedum plumbizincicola is a Cd/Zn hyperaccumulator with exceptional Cd tolerance and shoot accumulation capacity. Here, bioinformatic analysis, subcellular localization, heterologous expression in yeast, and CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing were combined to characterize the role of SpNRAMP3 in Cd homeostasis and tissue Cd allocation and its functional relationships with SpCAX3 and SpHMA3. SpNRAMP3 encodes a protein with 11 predicted transmembrane domains and shows a localization pattern consistent with tonoplast association; it is expressed in roots, stems and leaves and displays Cd-responsive expression. Heterologous expression of SpNRAMP3 in yeast increased cellular Cd accumulation and conferred Cd hypersensitivity. Two independent SpNRAMP3-edited lines showed greater Cd sensitivity and lower Cd concentrations in young leaves, supporting a role for SpNRAMP3 in Cd homeostasis, growth response, and tissue Cd allocation. Heterologous expression of SpCAX3 also altered cellular Cd accumulation and Cd sensitivity in yeast. Compared with the wild type, the spnramp3spcax3 double-edited lines showed 72.5-79.8% lower Cd concentrations in young leaves and reduced relative growth inhibition under Cd stress, whereas the spnramp3sphma3 lines showed 28.2-58.6% lower Cd concentrations in young leaves but substantially greater growth inhibition. These results suggest that SpHMA3 primarily mediates vacuolar Cd sequestration, whereas SpNRAMP3 and SpCAX3 may contribute to Cd homeostasis and tissue Cd allocation through distinct but functionally connected processes. These proteins may act together to support Cd hyperaccumulation and hypertolerance in S. plumbizincicola. This study provides a framework for understanding Cd homeostasis and tissue Cd allocation in hyperaccumulator plants and identifies candidate targets for genome-editing-based improvement of phytoremediation.

records.title: Ecological and Molecular Basis of Capripoxvirus Cross-Host Transmission: From Transmission Networks to Adaptive Evolution.
records.abstract: BackgroundCapripoxvirus (CaPV), comprising sheeppox virus (SPPV), goatpox virus (GTPV) and lumpy skin disease virus (LSDV), represents a growing transboundary threat to global livestock, with expanding geographic distribution and increasingly prominent cross-species transmission in mixed farming systems.ObjectivesThis review systematically examines the multifaceted drivers of CaPV spillover from ecological, molecular and evolutionary perspectives.MethodsThis review integrates ecological, molecular and evolutionary analyses, incorporating mathematical modelling and summarising advances in CRISPR/Cas-based diagnostics.ResultsEcologically, a tripartite network involving habitat sharing, landscape permeability (e.g., forest farmland edges) and arthropod vectors is proposed; mathematical modelling identifies vector-to-host ratio and vaccination coverage as critical modulators of outbreak severity. Molecularly, genetic plasticity in terminal genomic regions (e.g., ankyrin family) and host range genes (HRGs) such as M062R, M159, and LSDV012 enable antagonism of host restriction factors including SAMD9, IFIT1 and PKR, with the C7L superfamily playing a pivotal role in breaching species barriers. Evolutionarily, recombination-driven diversification, immune selection pressure and genetic bottlenecks collectively shape adaptive radiation and frequent host jumping events. Advances in CRISPR/Cas-based diagnostics are summarised. However, live attenuated vaccines show limitations in safety and efficacy.Conclusions and clinical relevancePersistent challenges include ecological surveillance, molecular discrimination of the three species and vaccine-wild type recombination risks. By integrating these disciplines, this review offers a comprehensive framework for understanding CaPV cross-species transmission and supports the design of precision control strategies targeting ecological and molecular vulnerabilities.
records.authors: He Z, Zhang J, Kuang S, Li S, Chen J, Yang J, Ma Z, Ding J, Zhang B, Zhang Y.

records.title: Beyond occurrence: matrix-dependent microbial ecological responses to pharmaceutical and personal care products between water and surface sediments in an urbanized river-bay continuum.
records.abstract: Pharmaceutical and personal care products (PPCPs) are ubiquitous in urbanized estuarine and coastal systems, yet their associations with microbial communities and functional potential under environmentally realistic exposure conditions remains poorly understood, particularly across contrasting environmental matrices. Here, 36 PPCPs were systematically characterized over a year across water and surface sediments in the Shenzhen River-Bay system to elucidate their contamination patterns, ecological risks, and associations with microbial communities. PPCPs exhibited pronounced matrix-specific spatiotemporal dynamics, with concentrations reaching 4354.35 ng/L in water and 1497.25 ng/g dw in surface sediments during autumn. Distinct compositional profiles between the two matrices further revealed contrasting exposure patterns along the river-bay continuum. Integrated risk prioritization identified seven priority PPCPs, with distinct risk profiles emerging between water and surface sediments. Notably, PPCPs exhibited stronger independent associations with microbial community variation than major environmental parameters in both matrices, highlighting their ecological relevance at environmentally realistic concentrations. Moreover, PPCP-microbe-function relationships displayed pronounced matrix dependence: PPCPs showed significant positive direct associations with carbon-, phosphorus-, and sulfur-related functional potential in water and nitrogen-related functional potential in surface sediments. Collectively, these findings reveal associations among PPCPs, microbial communities, and nutrient-related functional potential across environmental matrices, highlighting the need to account for matrix-specific environmental contexts alongside contaminant concentrations in ecological risk assessment.
records.authors: Deng Y, Chen X, Zou J, Tang T, Sheng Y, Tang S, Zhang X.

records.title: Sub-Inhibitory Plant-Derived GRAS Compounds and the Salmonella Type III Secretion System: A Critical Review and a Genotype-Informed Path Forward.
records.abstract: Plant-derived compounds that are generally recognized as safe (GRAS) suppress Salmonella virulence gene expression at concentrations that do not inhibit growth. A recent comprehensive review covered this phenomenon broadly across membrane, efflux, quorum-sensing, and biofilm mechanisms. The present review takes a narrower view and examines one axis, the Type III Secretion System (T3SS) that translocates effector proteins during host-cell invasion. At growth-curve-confirmed sub-inhibitory concentrations, eugenol, thymol, carvacrol, and cinnamaldehyde downregulate T3SS-associated transcripts. In the most well-studied cases, this downregulation also extends to effector proteins. That evidence is summarized here and placed alongside the adjacent quorum-sensing, biofilm, and sub-MIC antibiotic literature, together with reporting gaps in PCR primer background and amplicon efficiency that limit how far some of these results can be pushed. Two questions relevant to pre-harvest control, with poultry production as the primary applied context, remain largely unaddressed. The first is whether the magnitude of virulence suppression varies predictably across genetically diverse Salmonella strains at two main resolutions: serovar and SNP-variation within a serovar. The second question is whether structure-guided computational screening can expand the candidate pool beyond the four essential oil constituents that dominate this review. To define potential targets for such screens, the 30 Salmonella T3SS structures currently available in the Protein Data Bank are summarized here by functional class. Answering both questions would move the field toward genomically informed, strain-specific compound selection as a precision pre-harvest intervention.

records.title: CgSTAT1 regulates the production of multiple immune effectors in anti-bacterial immune response in oyster.
records.abstract: Signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) is the critical component of the JAK/STAT signaling pathway. In the present study, a STAT homologue (termed CgSTAT1) was characterized from oyster Crassostrea gigas. The open reading frame of CgSTAT1 cDNA was of 2982 bp encoding a polypeptide of 993 amino acid. The mRNA transcripts of CgSTAT1 were observed in all tested various tissues, with the highest level in hemocytes. After Vibrio splendidus stimulation, the mRNA expression of CgSTAT1 was significantly up-regulated in hemocytes, and CgSTAT1 translocated from hemocyte cytoplasm into nucleus. In CgSTAT1-knockdown oyster, the mRNA expressions of CgIL17-2, CgIL17-6, CgTNF-1, CgDefh2 and CgNOS in hemocytes were significantly decreased after V. splendidus stimulation. The bacterial clearance ability in cell-free hemolymph of STAT1-RNAi oyster decreased significantly, and the NO concentration also declined. These results collectively demonstrated that CgSTAT1 played important roles in regulating the anti-bacterial immune response by triggering the expression of immune effectors.
records.authors: Wang L, Wu Z, Sun J, Yang W, Mu S, Liu Z, Li X, Song L.

records.title: Vernalization-associated induction of BdFUL2 and its contribution to flowering time in Brachypodium distachyon.
records.abstract: The genome of grass model plant Brachypodium distachyon has four FRUITFULL (FUL) genes. Among them, only the function of BdVRN1/FUL1 in flowering time has been elucidated, the functions of other three BdFUL proteins remain largely unknown. In this study, we investigated the involvement of BdFUL2 in response to vernalization firstly. Similar to BdVRN1, we found that the H3K4me3 level and the expression of BdFUL2 are regulated by vernalization. Then, the contribution of BdFUL2 to flowering time was identified under long day conditions by generating RNA interference lines. Consistent with late flowering phenotype, the expression of several flowering related genes was altered in BdFUL2 RNA interference plants, such as BdFT1, BdFT2, BdVRN2. The results of electrophoresis mobility shift and yeast one hybrid experiments showed that BdFUL2 can directly bind to BdFT2 promoter. Furthermore, we verified the interaction between BdFUL2 and BdVRN1 by BIFC and CO-IP. Additionally, we found that BdFUL2 is associated with gibberellin synthesis. Our findings extend the understanding of the function and mechanism of FUL transcription factors in flowering time.
records.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
records.authors: Li H, Su Y, Fan J, Sun X.

records.title: C-Terminal Dimerization Enables Assembly of Ebola Virus VP30 Oligomers with transcriptional support activity.
records.abstract: Ebola virus VP30 is a multifunctional phosphoprotein essential for initiating viral transcription. VP30 functions as a homo-oligomer, where oligomerization is critical for its transcriptional-support activity. While a tetra-leucine motif in the N-terminal region (amino acids (aa) 100-105) mediates oligomerization, the structural determinants and functional relevance of a VP30 dimerization motif in the C-terminus remained poorly defined. Using a novel high-resolution (1.43 Å) crystal structure and biochemical approaches, we identified residues 142ITLL145 in the VP30 C-terminal domain (CTD) as key contributors to VP30 dimerization. Alanine conversions of these residues (VP30-CTD142-145A) disrupted CTD dimerization, as demonstrated by native mass spectrometry, size-exclusion chromatography with multi-angle light scattering, and split-GFP complementation assays. Notably, VP30-CTD functions as a dominant-negative inhibitor of full-length VP30 in a minigenome assay, whereas the dimerization-deficient mutant VP30-CTD142-145A does not. Critically, introduction of these mutations into full-length VP30 completely abolished viral transcription in minigenome assays. Recombinant EBOV carrying the VP30 dimerization mutations could not be rescued in cell culture, demonstrating that VP30-CTD dimerization is essential for viral replication. Together, these findings establish that CTD-mediated dimerization is essential for VP30's transcriptional support activity and virus propagation, identifying VP30 dimerization as a previously uncharacterized determinant of the viral replication cycle. Importantly, the dimerization interface is conserved among filoviruses, suggesting it represents a broadly conserved and potentially targetable vulnerability for antiviral intervention.
records.authors: Veeck C, Werner AD, Mais CN, Hartlieb B, Bange G, Becker S.

records.title: Chronic exposure to sulfur species, sodium metabisulfite and methionine, causes gut microbial dysbiosis and impairs intestinal health in adult zebrafish model.
records.abstract: Sulfur species (SS) are well documented for their toxicity in respiratory and dermal systems; however, their effects on the gastrointestinal (GI) microbiome remain largely unexplored. This research investigated the impact of prolonged exposure to high concentrations of sodium metabisulfite (SM) and L-methionine (MET), administered individually and in combination, on gut microbial composition and intestinal health in zebrafish. High concentrations of SM and MET, particularly in combination, significantly reduced somatic growth and intestinal weight and altered the GI microbiome, as confirmed by 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing. The highest combination group showed the greatest relative enrichment of the family Enterobacteriaceae and the genus Enterobacter compared with the control. This dysbiosis-like condition coincided with elevated intestinal sulfide levels, increased total SS accumulation, and lower relative short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) levels. High SS exposure also impaired intestinal digestive enzymatic activity and triggered oxidative stress, evidenced by reduced antioxidant defenses. Histopathological evaluation further confirmed structural injury to the intestinal mucosa, including goblet cell hyperplasia. At the transcriptional level, high SS exposure dysregulated intestinal pro-inflammatory and pro-apoptotic gene expression and upregulated ptgs2a/COX-2 protein expression. Conversely, MET at low individual doses did not show these adverse changes and was instead associated with greater relative abundance of the commensal bacterium Cetobacterium and higher relative SCFA levels. It was also associated with higher antioxidant and digestive enzyme activity, lower MDA levels, and lower baxa expression. In conclusion, these results provide evidence that prolonged exposure to excess SS drives Enterobacteriaceae-dominated gut dysbiosis, redox imbalance, and mucosal inflammation in adult zebrafish.
records.journal: Comparative biochemistry and physiology. Toxicology & pharmacology : CBP
records.authors: Aswinanand B, Karuppiah P, Balasubramanian B, Arasu MV, Namasivayam SKR, Arockiaraj J.

records.title: Surface engineering of cell-derived particles for targeted delivery of genome editors.
records.abstract: Genome editing technologies hold significant promise for the treatment of genetic disorders, but safe and efficient delivery remains a major barrier to their clinical translation. Cell-derived particles, including extracellular vesicles (EVs) and virus-like particles (VLPs), have emerged as promising non-viral delivery platforms, offering biological compatibility and the capacity to package and deliver genome editors as ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complexes in a transient manner that reduces the risk of off-target editing. The surface composition of these vehicles is shaped by their biogenesis pathway and their cell of origin, which in turn govern their cellular tropism. Through various engineering strategies, including producer cell engineering, viral-glycoprotein pseudotyping, and post-isolation surface modifications, this tropism can be expanded or redirected toward cell types and tissues beyond the liver. Here, we review the biology underlying cell-derived particle surface composition and the targeting strategies employed to engineer cell-type specificity.
records.authors: DeAgazio C, Singh A, Banskota S.

records.title: Pandemic-Driven Shifts in RSV Diversity, Evolution, and Global Spread
records.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic dramatically disrupted the seasonal circulation of RSV, with subsequent heterogeneous global resurgence. We aimed to characterize how pandemic-era disruptions restructured global RSV transmission dynamics, evolutionary patterns, and drivers of reemergence. We show that RSV-A and RSV-B genetic diversity underwent profound pandemic-associated suppression followed by heterogeneous resurgence. The post-pandemic period was characterized by pronounced changes in diversity, with the emergence of novel RSV-A genotypes (A.D.3 and A.D.5.2) and the expansion of the RSV-B, B.D.E.1 genotype. The recovery of RSV-B deviated strongly from neutral expectations and positive selection was detected at 20 sites in the G glycoprotein, F fusion protein, and M2-2 regulatory protein. Phylogeographic reconstruction revealed a sharp decline in international viral spread during the pandemic, followed by increasing persistence. Europe consistently served as the predominant global source, followed by Western Pacific and North America. Air-travel volume was the strongest predictor of dissemination (log coefficient >0.68 for both subtypes). Post-pandemic RSV resurgence represented fundamental epidemiological restructuring shaped by a population bottleneck, positive selection and major impact of air-travel. These findings underscore the need for robust genomic surveillance to track the global circulation of lineages, and to monitor effectiveness of pharmaceutical interventions given the emergence of new genotypes. One Sentence Summary  Air Mobility and Diversifying Selection Shape Post-Pandemic RSV Global Diversity
records.authors: Gustani-Buss E, Weinberger DM, Grubaugh ND, Colizza V, Shao Y, Suchard M, Evers A, Mazur NI, Wildenbeest JG, Lebbink RJ, van Zoggel HJ, Bont L, Lemey P.

records.title: VaccineScout: A Computational Framework for Guiding the Composition and Valency of SARS-CoV-2 Vaccine Updates
records.abstract: The continual evolution of SARS-CoV-2 necessitates periodic vaccine updates to maintain immunity against newly emerging variants. However, vaccine design remains largely guided by experimental serological studies, and there is no publicly available computational framework to help systematically prioritize vaccine variants and guide valency selection. Here, we analyze over 14 million SARS-CoV-2 genomes collected globally between 2021 and 2025 and find that over half of spike amino acid sequences (primary vaccine target) observed during the first six months after vaccine selection were already circulating at the time of selection, compared with only 5-10% of sequences during the subsequent six months. These findings provide quantitative support for annual COVID-19 vaccine updates. We further show that circulating variant prevalence and open-source variant fitness predictors can both effectively rank circulating variants by their future prevalence. Motivated by these findings, we developed VaccineScout, a computational framework that recommends vaccine candidates by minimizing the average spike amino acid substitution distances to the forecasted prevalence of circulating variants. VaccineScout also helps determine vaccine valency by quantifying diminishing returns as additional variants are introduced. Retrospective analyses showed that VaccineScout-recommended candidates either matched U.S. Food and Drug Administration recommendations or had lower average spike sequence distances to future variants and higher fitness. In addition, their spike distances to future variants were comparable to an oracle selection informed by future prevalence, indicating near-optimal performance by this metric. Together, VaccineScout introduces an in silico framework for systematically prioritizing SARS-CoV-2 vaccine candidates for costly downstream experimental validation.
records.authors: Gangwar P, Khanna S, Wertheim J, Lin B, Turakhia Y.

records.title: MET inhibition exploits conserved regulatory dependencies in malignant rhabdoid tumors
records.abstract: Malignant rhabdoid tumors (MRTs) are lethal, yet genomically simple childhood cancers characterised by universal SWI/SNF dysregulation. Despite this shared molecular framework, the regulatory programs sustaining MRTs and how they wire actionable dependencies, remain poorly defined. Here, we integrated single-cell multi-omic profiling and spatial transcriptomics across anatomically and molecularly diverse MRTs, generating a comprehensive multimodal MRT dataset at single-cell resolution. We leveraged this resource to identify candidate tumor-specific dependencies, which were subsequently functionally validated in vitro and in vivo in matched patient-derived models. We found that distinct malignant subpopulations are spatially patterned in complex environmentally shaped topologies, consistent with reciprocal interactions with stromal and immune compartments contributing to intratumoral transcriptional diversity. We identified recurrent transcriptional metaprograms conserved across patients and molecular subtypes, including a previously undescribed shared core rhabdoid program, as well as a metaprogram characterized by extracellular matrix interactions, and preferentially localized in tumor-stroma intermixed neighborhoods, supporting identification of niche conditioning cues. Mechanistically, we identified regulatory wiring driving these metaprograms, with the core shared rhabdoid programme coordinated by a circuit centred on TCF12, ZNF148 and CHD2. Guided by target nominations from our integrated analyses, we performed a curated drug screen using patient-derived MRT models and validated HGF/MET signaling as a selective vulnerability in extrarenal rhabdoid tumors. Pharmacologic MET inhibition was cytotoxic in sensitive models and induced a complete response in vivo using a clinically approved compound. Importantly, MET expression in primary tumors correlated with response, supporting biomarker-guided patient stratification for immediate clinical translation. Collectively, our findings define the molecular architecture of MRTs, reveal conserved regulatory programs beyond anatomical and molecular subtypes, and highlight a targetable signaling axis with immediate translational potential, establishing a framework for precision therapy in this lethal pediatric malignancy. Highlights  Comprehensive multimodal atlas of malignant rhabdoid tumors (MRTs) integrating single-cell multi-omics, spatial transcriptomics, and in vivo functional validation in matched patient-derived models. Recurrent malignant transcriptional metaprograms are conserved across MRT subtypes and are spatially zonated within tumors, highlighting plasticity in response to environmental cues. A core rhabdoid regulatory circuit centred on TCF12/ZNF148/CHD2 coordinates the principal shared malignant program. Drug screening and functional validation identify core regulatory circuit-linked HGF/MET axis dependence in a subset of MRTs. Treatment with a clinically approved MET inhibitor induces striking complete response in vivo in MET-high tumors, supporting MET IHC-guided patient selection and immediate therapeutic translation.

records.title: GPBench: A benchmark framework for genomic prediction
records.abstract: Genomic prediction (GP) has emerged as a powerful data mining strategy for disease risk assessment and molecular breeding. GP leverages genome-wide genetic variations and phenotypic information through a computational model to estimate genetic potential or disease risk. However, the field of GP still faces several major challenges: (i) dataset bias and insufficient representativeness; (ii) the lack of standardized evaluation protocols and a systematic benchmarking framework; (iii) heavy reliance on empirical expertise for experimental result interpretation, which hinders large-scale and systematic analysis. These issues make it difficult to conduct systematic cross-species evaluation and comparison of GP methods, and their authentic applications. To address these challenges, we established a standardized and extensible GP benchmark framework-GPBench. We first collected and harmonized public datasets from 16 species, covering animals, plants, and microorganisms, comprising 57 traits, 40,821 samples, and 493,821 single-nucleotide polymorphisms. Then, using the standardized datasets, the framework evaluates 21 GP models and provides a unified assessment across four dimensions: effectiveness, sensitivity, robustness, and scalability. Furthermore, we developed a large language model-based intelligent analysis system to facilitate the interpretation of GP experiments and model recommendations. GPBench provides the community with a fair, unified, and scalable platform (https://www.sdu-idea.cn/GPBench/) and an open-source library for comparing and optimizing GP methods, ultimately accelerating the application of GP in life sciences and biomedical research.
records.authors: Zhang X, Luo H, Li G, Zhang X, Wang S, Liu L, Guo M, Tan Q, Domeniconi C, Chen J, Wang J, Yu G.

records.title: Large-scale AI-guided discovery of antifreeze peptides reveals functional tandem-repeat architectures
records.abstract: Despite growing demand for biocompatible materials that regulate ice crystallization in cryopreservation, antifreeze peptide discovery remains constrained by limited candidate sequence diversity and reliance on known protein scaffolds. Here, we establish an AI-guided discovery framework integrating multimodal antifreeze protein prediction, generative sequence expansion and local sequence-pattern analysis. AFPFusionLM combines protein sequence and structure-aware representations, achieving an AUROC of 0.937 and an AUPRC of 0.957 on an independent reference set. Antifreeze-domain-adapted protein sequence generation and multi-model consensus screening of UniProt, glacier metagenomes and generated sequences yielded 87,305 candidate protein records. Large-scale sequence analysis revealed recurring periodic sequence architectures across multiple candidate protein clusters, enabling the identification of short-peptide families with shared repeat features and their natural variants. Experimental evaluation revealed ice recrystallization inhibition activity in multiple peptides from repeat-associated families, with inhibitory effects comparable to or greater than those of reference peptides reported in the literature. Cell-based experiments using a representative peptide-containing formulation also supported its cryoprotective potential under reduced-DMSO conditions. These findings show that large-scale sequence exploration can reveal function-associated peptide sequence architectures, providing a research framework for the systematic discovery and subsequent optimization of antifreeze peptides.

records.title: Transmural Single-Nucleus Transcriptomics Nominates Candidate Disease Programs in Human Necrotizing Enterocolitis
records.abstract: Background:  & Aims: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a life-threatening disease of premature infants marked by inflammation, ischemia, mucosal injury, and, in advanced cases, necrosis extending into deeper layers of the intestinal wall. Because NEC affects specialized, interacting cells in a developing intestine, we used single-nucleus transcriptomics to build a transmural, cell-type-resolved map and nominate hypothesis-generating disease programs distinct from maturation. Methods: Full-thickness intestinal specimens from fetal/prenatal controls, acute NEC cases, and infant controls were analyzed by single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq). Fetal and infant samples served as developmental references. Analyses included cell annotation, NEC-versus-infant differential expression, gene ontology (GO), cross-lineage recurrence, cell death signatures, and developmental maturity. Results: We profiled 53,735 nuclei by snRNA-seq and resolved 34 epithelial, stromal, vascular, immune, neuronal, glial, and smooth muscle populations. We used a morphology-based nuclei scoring system for sample selection that predicted high-quality transcript recovery. NEC nuclei were represented across this cellular landscape, with recurrent gene-expression changes suggesting shared inflammatory recruitment, antimicrobial/redox defense, stress adaptation, complement/vascular activation, reduced homeostatic signaling, and cell death-associated regulation. Developmental maturity analysis identified fetal-like expression levels in subsets of NEC-regulated genes. Proliferative crypt populations retained DNA repair/cell-cycle programs with inflammatory, hypoxic, and ER-stress features, while absorptive enterocytes showed reduced digestive, transport, detoxification, and terminal villus-function programs. Secretory-lineage changes implicated goblet mucus-barrier responses with reduced glycosylation, trafficking, and hydration; enteroendocrine changes in epithelial defense, metabolic stress, and neural signaling; and Paneth cell retention of antimicrobial effector transcripts despite altered ER quality control, autophagy, and granule delivery in NEC. Non-epithelial programs implicated stromal Wnt/BMP niche loss, impaired lymphatic drainage/scavenging, macrophage cytokine activation with reduced clearance machinery, neuroglial circuit defects, and altered smooth muscle contraction-relaxation balance. Conclusions: This single nuclear intestinal cell atlas nominates multicellular programs that may govern NEC initiation, progression toward tissue destruction, and resolution toward functional recovery.

records.title: Sarrella massiliensis gen. nov. sp. nov., a new gut genus isolated from the stool of a healthy donor
records.abstract: Strain Marseille-QA0792 (=CSUR QA0792, CECT 31199) was isolated from the feces of a healthy person using the culturomics method. The fecal sample originated from leftover material collected for a fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) procedure, obtained during a routine screening in accordance with the guidelines of the French National Agency for Medicines and Health Products Safety (ANSM). This strain is Gram-stain-negative, rod-shaped, non-motile, and non-spore-forming. It is strictly anaerobic, with optimal growth at 37°C. Strain Marseille-QA0792 presented its highest 16S rRNA identity, 96.2%, with ″Merdibacter massiliensis″ strain Marseille-P3254 (not validly published) (accession number  LT598590 ) and ANI similarity of 75.0% with the same species. Among validly published species, strain Marseille-QA0792 showed its highest 16S rRNA gene sequence similarity (91.5%) with Faecalicoccus acidiformans strain 37-2a (accession number  HQ452864 ), whereas all computed average nucleotide identity (ANI) values were below 75%. Genome sequencing revealed a genome size of 2.67 Mb and a G+C content of 50.01%. This species is classified within the Erysipelotrichaceae family in the Bacillota phylum. Thus, we isolated for the first time a novel genus named Sarrella massiliensis gen. nov., sp. nov., strain Marseille-QA0792. This discovery highlights the importance of continuing culturomics efforts to explore the human microbiome.
records.authors: Semmar R, Beye M, Orain N, Robinne S, Alibar S, Bakour S, Lagier J, Dubourg G, Tidjani Alou M, Valles C.

records.title: A conserved thermodynamic signature links transcriptome organization to growth state
records.abstract: Living systems operate far from thermodynamic equilibrium, sustaining complexity through continuous free-energy influx and heat dissipation. Yet the higher-order functional constraints imposed by non-equilibrium dynamics remain largely unexplored. To formalize how changes in cellular entropy production constrain intracellular organization across proliferative state transitions, we developed a stochastic-thermodynamic model linking reduced dissipative drive to transient increases in intracellular configurational entropy. Within this framework, we examined abundance-weighted predicted RNA folding stability as a transcriptome-level projection of the intracellular configurational remodelling. Consistent with the model, transcriptome reorganization across the cell cycle produces coordinated, phase-dependent changes in the distribution of transcript-level RNA folding free energies. Extending this analysis to stress adaptation, we find that human cancer cells exposed to molecularly targeted agents and nutrient-limited  Escherichia coli converge on expressed RNA pools enriched for transcripts with less negative RNA folding free energies, despite marked heterogeneity in the transcriptional responses within each system. Opposing shifts during acquired resistance under continued drug exposure and bacterial recovery from starvation further support an association with growth state.  Together, these findings suggest that transcriptome organization extends beyond gene-regulatory programs to collective biophysical properties that may reflect non-equilibrium constraints shaping cellular-state transitions.
records.authors: Zivieri R, Reeves J, Pattnaik S, Martins Reis A, Xu A, Thomas DM, Deveson I, Cipponi A.

records.title: Design and Recombinant Production of Proline-rich Antimicrobial Peptide 385P
records.abstract: Abstract    The rapid emergence of antimicrobial resistance has increased the search for alternative agents with novel mechanisms of action. Here, we established an end-to-end framework for the rational development of proline-rich antimicrobial peptides (PrAMPs), integrating computational motif discovery, peptide design, recombinant production, and biological characterization. Conserved motifs from highly active PrAMPs were identified and ranked using MEME and rationally assembled to generate the 36-amino acid peptide 385P. A C-terminal hexahistidine-tagged construct (r385P) was successfully produced in  Pichia pastoris  GS115 and confirmed by SDS-PAGE, Western blotting, and His-tag ELISA. r385P exhibited broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, with MICs of 4–32 µg/mL against Gram-negative bacteria, 2–32 µg/mL against Gram-positive bacteria, and 64 µg/mL against  Candida albicans  and  Candida glabrata  , with the highest antibacterial activity against  Listeria monocytogenes  and  Acinetobacter baumannii  . r385P exhibited strong antibiofilm activity, achieving 83.83% inhibition against  Escherichia coli  O157:H7 at MIC/2 and complete inhibition against  Staphylococcus aureus  at MIC. FICI assays revealed antibiotic- and species-dependent interactions, including synergy with kanamycin against  Klebsiella pneumoniae  (FICI = 0.375) and consistent additive interactions with tetracycline. r385P retained full antimicrobial activity after exposure to 50–200 mM NaCl and 1–4 h of trypsin treatment, while MICs increased two- and four-fold following exposure to 65 and 95°C, respectively. Hemolysis remained below 4% at 256 µg/mL, while MRC-5 cell viability was 71% at 320 µg/mL. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the potential of conserved-motif assembly as a practical strategy for developing functionally robust PrAMP candidates.
records.authors: Kesmen Z, Canpolat M, Herdem D.

records.title: HLA-B*57 as a Dominant Genetic Determinant of HIV-1 Elite Control: Comparative Reanalysis of MHC Variant Associations in European andAfrican-American Cohorts A reanalysis of published genomic association data
records.abstract: Abstract  Background  HIV-1 elite controllers (EC) maintain undetectable viral loads without antiretroviral therapy; a phenotype strongly linked to variation in the Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC). HLA-B*57:01 is the most replicated genetic association with elite control in individuals of European ancestry, with HLA-B*57:03 identified as its counterpart in African-ancestry populations. Whether the structure of this association – its dose-dependence and independence from other MHC signals – has been characterized consistently across both ancestries has not been addressed in accessible form. Methods  Using published allele/carrier frequencies from Rahmouni et al. (2025, 2023), we analyzed a European cohort (543 elite controllers, 3,272 uninfected controls) and an African-American cohort (759 HIV-1-seropositive individuals enriched for elite controllers, cs1 + cs2, ICGH consortium). For the European cohort, we performed: (1) primary HLA-B*57 association testing, (2) a nine-variant MHC panel analysis, (3) a viral-load trend test, and (4) an HLA-B*57-Stratified Association Analysis. For the African-American cohort, we tested enrichment of rs1131446 (the HLA-B*57:03 tag SNP) relative to its background frequency in the general African population (1000 Genomes AFR, n = 661). All tests used Fisher's exact test with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction where applicable. records.abstract: Abstract  Background  Lymphovascular invasion (LVI) is one of the early routes of gastric cancer dissemination. Tissue-associated microorganisms and ketone-body metabolism may be associated with aggressive disease, but parallel between-group differences cannot establish a microbial–metabolic mechanism. This study integrated a discovery cohort with paired gastric tissue 16S rRNA and targeted metabolomics data, together with public transcriptomic, single-cell, methylation, dependency, and perturbation resources. Methods  Clinical LVI labels were available for 66 gastric cancer cases, of which 65 had both 16S and metabolomics data (32 LVI-negative [V0] and 33 LVI-positive [V1] cases). We evaluated microbial diversity, community composition, genus-level differences, and a random forest classifier with rigorous control of information leakage, and implemented a mutually exclusive two-stage descriptive genus screen. The strict tier required a mean relative abundance of ≤ 0.01% in V0 and ≥ 0.05% in V1, and a pseudocount-adjusted fold change of ≥ 10; genera that did not meet the strict-tier criteria entered a relaxed additional tier, which required a V1 cumulative genus-table count of ≥ 20 and a ≥ 10-fold increase in mean abundance. Genera with a V0 cumulative count of 0 were treated as zero-baseline candidates, for which fold changes were not estimated. We subsequently analyzed the tissue β-HB signal and the paired bridging relationship between continuous Tundrisphaera abundance and β-HB. We evaluated 6 prespecified non-immune programs in GSE62254, TCGA-STAD, GSE246963, GSE237876, GSE163558, GSE239676, and GSE261635: ketone-body handling, butyrate metabolism, fatty acid degradation, EMT/ECM invasion, endothelial/angiogenic activity, and epithelial integrity. DepMap and LINCS analyses were used only to prioritize experimental candidates. The β-HB signal was higher in V1 (median, 68.49) than in V0 (median, 39.31; Mann–Whitney P = 0.0220318), but the metabolome-wide FDR was 0.9758. records.title: Turnip crinkle virus coat protein determines whether salicylic acid promotes or restricts infection
records.abstract: Abstract  Turnip crinkle virus (TCV) coat protein (CP) coordinates virion assembly, immune recognition, and RNA silencing suppression, but how these functions shape disease remains unclear. We redirected CP from the nucleus by appending an identical nuclear export signal to either terminus. Despite similarly reducing nuclear CP accumulation, N- and C-terminal modifications produced opposing effects on disease, viral accumulation, particle formation, and HRT-mediated recognition, indicating that sustained nuclear CP is dispensable for these outcomes. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses revealed that disease severity closely tracked salicylic acid (SA) accumulation. Genetic disruption of SA biosynthesis reduced chlorosis and necrosis, establishing SA as a driver of TCV-associated disease. However, SA had CP-dependent effects on viral accumulation, promoting WT and N-NES infection while restricting C-NES. The R6A CP mutant uncoupled disease from viral burden, inducing SA and severe symptoms despite reduced accumulation. Thus, CP determines SA induction and whether an SA-rich environment favors or restricts TCV.
records.authors: Rademacher D, Kingsolver B, Dawane A, May J.

records.title: Strain-resolved comparative genomics and functional characterization of culturable lactic acid bacteria from Guizhou sour soup
records.abstract: Abstract    Guizhou sour soup is a traditional fermented food and a reservoir of diverse lactic acid bacteria (LAB), yet the strain-resolved genomic architecture and functional heterogeneity of its culturable LAB remain poorly defined. We established a large culture collection and integrated comparative genomics with targeted analyses of bile salt hydrolase (BSH), exopolysaccharide/capsular polysaccharide (EPS/CPS) loci, genomic safety, and in vitro phenotypes to evaluate strain-level diversity and identify traits relevant to functional strain selection. Among 1,741 culturable isolates recovered from red and white sour soups, Lactobacillales accounted for 85.69% and 95.24%, respectively. Whole-genome sequencing of 172 isolates, comprising 92  Lacticaseibacillus paracasei  , 30  Lactiplantibacillus plantarum  , and 50  Limosilactobacillus fermentum  , revealed open pan-genomes with distinct species-level functional architectures.  L. paracasei  showed the greatest accessory-genome contribution,  L. plantarum  the highest mean normalized BSH representation, and  L. fermentum  distinct oxidative-stress- and amino-acid-associated profiles. No antimicrobial resistance or virulence-associated genes were detected at the applied screening thresholds. BSH analyses showed lineage-specific sequence variation but conserved catalytic Cys2 and ligand-proximal architecture, whereas EPS/CPS loci varied among species and strains. Cholesterol removal was strongly strain- and condition-dependent:  L. paracasei  R1156 reached 71.69 ± 4.84% in standard MRS, while  L. plantarum  R2345, R2037, R1621, and R203 maintained 56.85–64.32% removal under 0.1% bile salts, exceeding the reference strain  Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus  GG (LGG). These findings establish a strain-resolved genomic and phenotypic resource and demonstrate the value of integrating comparative genomics with direct phenotypic screening for rational selection of food-associated LAB for further biotechnological evaluation.
records.authors: bai f, wang n, liu y, wen q, hu c, zhu s, mou r, yang r, han y, luo p.

records.title: Toxic mercury, aquatic ecosystem collapse, and the ancient Lowland Maya.
records.abstract: Environmental impacts endured by the Lowland Maya during the Classic Period (250 to 920 CE) included droughts, deforestation, and soil erosion. Recent studies on mercury (Hg) pollution and cyanotoxins suggest that degraded water quality was also a stressor for the Pre-Columbian Maya. Hg in the Maya region is related to use of both elemental mercury and mineral cinnabar (HgS), the latter used as a red pigment. Questions, however, remain concerning the toxicity of Hg or the consequences of prehistoric Hg exposure on ecosystem and human health. Here, we show that Classic Period Hg concentrations in sediment cores from two lakes on the Yucatán Peninsula exceeded modern sediment Hg toxicity thresholds by orders of magnitude for centuries during ancient Maya occupation. Sediments also have evidence of aquatic food web collapse (algae, bacteria, cyanobacteria, ostracods, snails, and nonbiting midges), coincident with the time of high Hg concentrations, confirming that Hg toxicity was an additional environmental stressor for Classic Maya populations.
records.authors: Waters MN, Wooten SL, Abrook AM, Brenner M, Curtis JH, Langdon PG, Medina-Gonzalez RM, Paradeisis-Stathis S, Vachula RS.

records.title: A biofilm-derived peptide as an underwater adhesive.
records.abstract: Wet adhesives that perform under water have broad applications in industrial and biomedical settings. To date, molecular designs for underwater adhesives have largely been inspired by marine animals including mussels and barnacles. Here, we propose bacterial biofilms as an alternative source of inspiration for underwater adhesives. Specifically, we demonstrate the application potential of a peptide derived from biofilms formed by the notorious pathogen Vibrio cholerae. We characterize the ability of this biofilm-derived peptide to adsorb onto various surfaces and to glue wet surfaces by using a combination of confocal microscopy, molecular dynamics simulations, atomic force microscopy, lap shear tests, and spectroscopic tools. We further show that the peptide can coaggregate with microspheres acting as an effective flocculant. Our results open new design possibilities for underwater adhesives inspired by natural biofilms.

records.title: Massively parallel self-assembly of suspendable microcompartments for functional cell screening.
records.abstract: Modern biology increasingly demands platforms that can compartmentalize and analyze single cells and cell-cell interactions at massive scale, yet existing compartmentalization strategies based on microfluidics suffer from critical limitations. Emerging lab-on-a-particle technologies such as nanovials enable anchored single cells or small groups of cells to be isolated and assayed in a fully suspendable and parallelized manner using standard instrumentation, although their open architectures can result in loss of growing or un-attached cells. Here, we introduce capped nanovials: self-assembling hydrogel compartments formed by docking spherical capping particles into bowl-shaped nanovials. We routinely achieve capping of >80% of all nanovials in a sample and >90% sorting yield by flow cytometry, making the capped nanovial system well-suited for preparing and running large-scale assays. Furthermore, we demonstrate stable clonal expansion of single mammalian, yeast, and bacterial cells; growth-based selections of >10,000 colonies; enhanced signal-to-noise in secretion assays; and high-purity selection of antibody-secreting cells based on activation of co-encapsulated T cell reporters (>30-fold signal, up to 100% selection purity). By combining the simplicity of a well plate with the functional precision of droplet microfluidics without requiring oil or custom instrumentation, capped nanovials realize accessible, high-throughput, and high-resolution experimentation.

records.title: Explainable computational framework for subtype classification and biomarker identification in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma using machine learning.
records.abstract: The precise classification of basal, classical, atypical, and mesenchymal subtypes of Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (HNSCC) is crucial for advancing precision oncology. Our research aims to develop an explainable subtype classification model for HNSCC.These molecular subtypes have been previously defined; reliable and meaningful computational methods for the classification of molecular subtypes and prioritization of molecular biomarkers for each subtype do not exist. We developed an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) model that classifies molecular subtypes based on combined transcriptomic profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA-HNSC) and Gene Expression Omnibus (GSE65858). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to quantify the importance of genes for model predictions. Subsequently, genes with high predictive importance were analyzed in protein-protein interactions using STRING, and hub genes were identified by Maximum Clique Centrality (MCC) and used for the identification of candidate biomarkers for each of the subtypes. We employed machine learning methods such as Random Forest (RF), Logistic Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), AdaBoost (AB), Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Gaussian Naive Bayes (GNB), XGBoost (XGB), and Gradient Boosting (GB). The XGBoost model achieved an accuracy of 95% after hyperparameter tuning and cross-validation. Biologically relevant subtype-specific biomarkers associated with each molecular subtype were identified. To highlight the potential biological functions of these biomarkers, pathway analysis was performed. Further assessment of these genes, such as survival analysis and druggability, showed promise for the development of targeted therapies.
records.authors: Rajan A, Biji CL, Sinha MG, Oviya IR.

records.title: Genetic analysis of 7,000 year old preserved goat leather from Cueva de los Murciélagos (Albuñol, Spain).
records.abstract: Advances in ancient DNA research have expanded the range of materials from which genetic information can be recovered, enabling the analysis of atypical materials. These often preserve both host and exogenous DNA, for example due to handling or native microbes, offering a window into past diversity. Here we report one such exceptional material: a well-preserved goat leather specimen from Cueva de los Murciélagos (Albuñol, Spain), associated with an Early Neolithic context. Archaeozoological analyses show clear evidence of tanning and anthropogenic modification of the skin, while radiocarbon dating confirms it to be ~ 7,250-7,000 years old. We generated genome-wide data from the leather (Murciélagos1) and demonstrated that it derives from a domestic goat of European ancestry. Comparisons with modern goats show highest affinity to the Bermeya breed from northern Spain, demonstrating genetic connectivity in goat herds from the Neolithic to present day Iberia. We additionally recover fragmented DNA from the leather deriving from human and canid sources, the former likely reflecting handling/wearing of the leather and the latter indicating post-depositional disturbance. Murciélagos1 represents one of the oldest nuclear genome data from organic remains outside of high altitude, high latitude regions, and demonstrates the value of ancient DNA analysis in exceptional cases of organic preservation.

records.title: Gamma irradiation concerning genetics of Ralstonia solanacearum and export quality in potatoes.
records.abstract: BackgroundPotato brown rot, caused by Ralstonia solanacearum, is an important quarantine disease that can seriously affect tuber quality and limit the movement and marketability of potatoes. Gamma irradiation may help control the pathogen after harvest, but the dose used can also affect the nutritional value and quality of potato tubers.PurposeWe aimed to study the genetic diversity of the potato brown rot pathogen, Ralstonia solanacearum, using molecular markers. We also evaluated how irradiation affects the physicochemical properties of treated and untreated potato tubers.Materials and methodsCommercial potato varieties were collected from major potato-growing areas of Bangladesh for pathogen isolation and irradiation studies. Forty-two bacterial isolates were characterized on TTC medium and examined using PS-1/PS-2 PCR, 16S rRNA sequencing, phylotype-specific PCR, and mutS amplification. After irradiation, the tubers were assessed for weight loss, ascorbic acid, anthocyanin, carotenoid, total soluble solids (TSS), and mineral content.ResultsVirulent isolates produced the expected 553-bp PS-1/PS-2 amplicon. Sequence analysis placed a representative isolate close to Asian Ralstonia reference strains, while phylotype-specific PCR generated a 213-bp product corresponding to phylotype IV. The pathogen-specific 553-bp amplicon remained detectable up to 5.5 kGy but was not detected at 6 kGy under the conditions used in this study. A reduction in mutS band intensity was also observed following irradiation. The effects of irradiation on tuber quality varied with cultivar and dose. Ascorbic acid and carotenoid contents generally decreased with increasing irradiation dose, whereas anthocyanin and TSS remained comparatively stable. Mineral concentrations were generally higher in irradiated tubers than in untreated samples.ConclusionGamma irradiation reduced the detectability of the pathogen-specific PCR target, although this does not confirm complete pathogen inactivation. Irradiation conditions require optimization to balance pathogen suppression and nutritional quality. Further viability testing and genomic characterization are recommended.
records.authors: Haque MM, Haque M, Hasna MK, Khalil MI, Mortuza MF, Hossain MA, Paul NR, Akter S, Mehedi MNH.

records.title: Bioremediation potential assessment of the developed Microalgae-Bacterial Biofilm using 3D-printed PLA carriers.
records.abstract: The high energy demand of conventional wastewater treatment and the depletion of freshwater resources call for cost-effective and sustainable treatment solutions. Microalgae-based systems have gained attention due to their dual role in nutrient removal and biomass valorization. This study investigates a Coupled Microalgae-Bacterial Biofilm (CMBB) system for the bioremediation of primary-treated domestic wastewater, developed by immobilizing an indigenous microalgae-bacterial consortium on in-house-designed three-dimensional (3D) printed polylactic acid (PLA) carriers. After 5 days of enrichment, each carrier accumulated 231 ± 7.83 mg of biomass. The carriers were evaluated in laboratory-scale batch reactors (1.2 L working volume; n = 3) at 50%, 75% and 100% surface-area coverage over a 7-day treatment cycle. The 75% coverage gave the highest organic removal: after a hydraulic retention time (HRT) of 5 days it removed 87.21 ± 2.1% of total COD, 81.82 ± 2.15% of soluble COD (sCOD) and 69.32 ± 3.2% of BOD5, and BOD5 removal rose to 76.14% after day 7. At all coverages, ammoniacal nitrogen was removed by 95-98%, nitrate by about 65-69% and phosphate by about 83% within 7 days. Nitrate did not accumulate, which indicates that nitrogen removal was dominated by assimilation into algal-bacterial biomass, possibly together with simultaneous nitrification-denitrification, rather than by nitrification alone. Effluent tCOD fell below the 80 mg/L irrigation-reuse limit within 3 days at 75% and 100% coverage, and BOD5 fell below 30 mg/L by day 7. Under the same experimental conditions, the attached biofilm performed efficiently in removal of tCOD, sCOD and BOD5 than free (suspended) consortium cells. Combining indigenous consortia with engineered 3D-printed carriers is a promising low-energy route to decentralized wastewater treatment, nutrient recovery and water reuse; pilot-scale validation under field conditions is the next step.
records.authors: Singh B, Dhir A, Rout PR, Mamane H, Sharma SG.

records.title: Epigenetic and transcriptional control of sexual development in the multicellular Sordariomycete fungi.
records.abstract: SUMMARYMany Sordariomycete fungi produce flask-shaped perithecia that encapsulate meiotic cells and facilitate dispersion of sexual spores. Perithecial development represents a striking example of complex multicellularity in fungi, requiring coordinated gene regulation through transcriptional, chromatin-based, and post-transcriptional mechanisms. This review summarizes recent work to dissect sexual development in several well-studied fungi: Neurospora crassa, Sordaria macrospora, Podospora anserina, and Fusarium graminearum. Studies with these fungi have uncovered interconnected regulatory mechanisms that coordinate fruiting body development. Transcription factor networks control differentiation of perithecial tissues and cell types. Chromatin regulators, such as histone chaperones, ATP-dependent chromatin remodelers, acetyltransferases, and Polycomb Repressive Complex 2, impact major developmental transitions. In addition, post-transcriptional mechanisms that operate during sexual development play critical regulatory roles. Recoding of the transcriptome by A-to-I mRNA editing is specific to perithecia and is essential for sexual development of N. crassa and F. graminearum. Finally, sex-specific genome defense pathways protect genome integrity and are essential for the completion of meiosis in some species. We summarize recent advances and highlight the remarkable regulatory complexity underlying fruiting body development in Sordariomycete fungi. In addition, we identify key open questions for future research.
records.authors: Deaven AM, Lewis ZA.

records.title: Transgene expression kinetics and replication potential of recombinant adenovirus serotype 4 in a mouse model and its use as a herpes simplex virus vaccine.
records.abstract: Human adenovirus serotype 4 (Ad4) is used as a replication-competent oral vaccine that safely and effectively prevents Ad4 respiratory illness in US military personnel. Recombinant Ad4 vaccine candidates elicit mucosal and systemic immune responses against respiratory viruses in hamsters, nonhuman primates, and humans. Although evaluation of Ad4 vaccine candidates in mice would be extremely useful given the number of immunologic tools available, this has been limited by concerns about reduced viral replication in these animals. Here, we generated recombinant Ad4 vectors that express either luciferase (Ad4-Luc), green fluorescent protein (Ad4-EGFP), or herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2) glycoprotein D (Ad4-gD2) to identify transgene expression kinetics, the presence of Ad4 vector replication, and HSV-2 immune responses and protection against HSV-2 infection. Local luciferase activity was observed from 7 h to 20 days after intranasal inoculation of BALB/c and humanized mice. Subsequent inoculations with Ad4-Luc showed reduced luciferase expression in BALB/c mice but robust expression in humanized mice, suggesting an immune response to the vector in wild-type mice. Ad4 DNA production, but not luciferase activity, was reduced in the lungs of BALB/c mice treated with cidofovir before inoculation with Ad4, implying that Ad4 replicated, albeit at a low level, in the lungs. Intranasal vaccination of mice with Ad4-gD2 resulted in HSV-2-neutralizing antibodies in the serum and, after HSV-2 intravaginal challenge, reduced disease scores, increased survival, and reduced shedding. Overall, the BALB/c mouse model is semi-permissive to Ad4 mucosal infection, but transgene expression is sufficient for the study of Ad4-based vaccine candidates.ImportanceMucosal surfaces serve as the primary site of infection and shedding for many viral pathogens. Immune responses at mucosal sites provide protection, but few mucosal vaccines are licensed. The oral replication-competent adenovirus serotype 4 (Ad4) vaccine is used to prevent respiratory illness in military recruits, has an extraordinary record of safety and efficacy, and has been tested as a recombinant platform for other viruses. Further development of this vaccine platform has been partially hindered by the perceived inability to evaluate vaccine candidates in mice. Here, we characterize recombinant Ad4 transgene expression kinetics and viral replication after inoculation at various sites and show protection against herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2) genital disease in mice after intranasal vaccination. We show that Ad4 can induce protective efficacy, even in a semi-permissive mouse model, suggesting this is a promising vector for HSV-2 and potentially other viral pathogens.

records.title: Introducing SARS-CoV-2 wastewater surveillance in Lebanon.
records.abstract: Wastewater surveillance (WWS) gained global attention during the COVID-19 pandemic as an early warning system to continuously monitor SARS-CoV-2 and its evolving variants. The aim of this study is to detect and sequence SARS-CoV-2 in wastewater from an area in Lebanon that hosts vulnerable groups of Lebanese residents and refugees. A total of 188 wastewater samples were collected from 18 manholes between 20 February 2023 and 31 May 2023. Viral RNA extraction, RT-PCR, and genomic sequencing were performed. Eighteen percent of collected samples were SARS-CoV-2-positive. Omicron BA.2 was the only circulating variant in February. An overlap between Omicron BA.2 (33.33%) and B.1.1-like sublineages, including C.26 (16.67%), B.1.1.207 (16.67%), B.1.1.214 (16.67%), and C.2.1 (16.67%) was detected in March. In April, while Omicron circulation decreased to 12.5%, a BA.1 and BA.2 recombinant (XM) was detected. The lack of disaggregated data sets and case-specific SARS-CoV-2 reports from the study site residents limited our ability to perform correlation and comparative analyses between wastewater and national clinical data. However, wastewater samples showed higher positivity rates during most of the months prior to national surges of cases. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating WWS in public health interventions to complement clinical and epidemiologic surveillance.ImportanceWastewater surveillance (WWS) is a valuable environmental surveillance tool that facilitates the real-time detection of circulating viruses and emerging variants. The COVID-19 pandemic has led to significant acceleration in the use of WWS as an early warning system for detecting SARS-CoV-2 and monitoring community transmission. This is the first study introducing SARS-CoV-2 community-based WWS in Lebanon. The findings of this study highlight the importance and feasibility of implementing WWS in a limited-resource setting to complement epidemiological surveillance in monitoring trends of SARS-CoV-2 at the population/community level.
records.authors: Bou Hamdan M, Mroweh M, Abou Hassan F, Germani A, Dejong J, El-Jardali F, Melhem NM, CAEP Study Group.

records.title: Recombinant Fusion of Polyglutamic Acid Enhances Cell-Penetrating Peptide-Mediated CRISPR-Cas9 Delivery.
records.abstract: Genome editing has been revolutionized by Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR)-associated protein 9 (Cas9) technology. However, efficient intracellular delivery of Cas9 ribonucleoprotein (RNP) remains a major challenge, particularly in cells that are refractory to conventional transfection methods. Integrating viral vectors carry a risk of insertional mutagenesis, whereas physical methods such as electroporation are not well suited for in vivo or clinically relevant applications. Cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) offer a promising alternative for direct RNP delivery, although their efficiency is often limited by endosomal entrapment and limited cytosolic release. In this study, we developed two recombinant CPP-fused Cas9 proteins, polyglutamate (PE)-trans-activator of transcription (TAT)-nuclear localization signal (NLS)-Cas9 (PETATCas9) and TAT-NLS-Cas9 (TATCas9), designed to improve solubility, membrane penetration, RNP complex formation, and nuclear targeting. PE tag in PETATCas9 was introduced to optimize charge balance and reduce nonspecific electrostatic interactions between TAT and guide RNA (gRNA), thereby enhancing RNP stability and delivery performance. Both recombinant proteins were expressed, purified, and assembled with gRNA into functional RNP complexes for delivery into SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells. The optimized CPP-Cas9 RNP system enabled efficient intracellular delivery and glucosylceramidase beta 1 (GBA1) gene editing in SH-SY5Y cells. These findings establish PETATCas9 as a scalable, transient, nonviral, and self-delivering RNP platform for CRISPR-based genome editing in cells that are refractory to conventional transfection methods.
records.authors: Sharma A, Seo Y, Park TS.

records.title: An ancestral T2 RNase provides insights into the origin and evolution of self-incompatible S-RNase.
records.abstract: With the evolution of true floral structures, angiosperms have become the most diverse and successful plant group, a success largely attributed to the genetic diversity generated by self-incompatibility. The canonical S-RNase (class III T2 RNase)/F-boxes locus that mediates gametophytic self-incompatibility is present across multiple lineages of core eudicots, and its origin has been traced back to the last common ancestor of core eudicots. However, because class III T2 RNases are completely absent from non-eudicot taxa, the origin of this S-RNase/F-boxes locus remains elusive. Here, we identify a rare class TI T2 RNase (EVM0017713)/F-boxes locus in the basal eudicot Akebia trifoliata as a candidate S-locus for late-acting self-incompatibility, sharing molecular features with the S-RNase/F-boxes locus. The class TI T2 RNase subfamily exhibits a continuous gradient transition from class I to class III T2 RNase subfamilies in terms of phylogenetic distribution, molecular structural characteristics, physicochemical properties, and gene structure. Crucially, the class TI EVM0017713/F-boxes locus is ancient and collinear with the S-RNase/F-boxes loci. These results suggest that the class TI T2 RNase/F-box locus may represent an ancestral form of the S-RNase/F-box system, offering new insights into the origin and evolution of plant self-incompatibility.
records.authors: Yang H, Li J, Zhong S, Han R, Yi X, Chen C, Hu X, Li Q, Luo P.

records.title: Tongue Microbiota in Children with Geographic Tongue: A Pilot Case-Control Study.
records.abstract: This study aimed to explore the characteristics of tongue microbiota in children with geographic tongue (GT) and provide microecological evidence for elucidating the occurrence and progression mechanism of GT. 16S rDNA high-throughput sequencing combined with bioinformatic analysis was adopted to compare the species differences of tongue microbial communities between children with GT and healthy children. The microbial richness of tongue coating in children with GT was markedly lower than that in healthy children (p Prevotella, Veillonella, and Actinomyces, while the tongue coating of children with GT was predominated by Neisseria, Pasteurellaceae, and Streptococcus. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes functional pathway enrichment analysis demonstrated an overall downregulation trend of metabolic functions in tongue coating microbiota of children with GT, with main differential pathways in histidine metabolism and teichoic acid biosynthesis. These results indicate that the onset of GT is highly correlated with abnormal enrichment of Neisseria, Pasteurellaceae, and Streptococcus. Imbalance of the tongue coating microbial communities may be involved in the development of GT.

records.title: Dynamic GelMA/Oxidized Hyaluronic Acid Hydrogels Enable Acid-Accelerated Localized Delivery of Photothermal Melatonin-Derived Carbon Dots for Infected Bone Repair.
records.abstract: Infected bone defects remain difficult to reconstruct because bacterial persistence, acidic stress, excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), inflammatory dysregulation, and impaired osteogenesis reinforce one another. Here, sulfur-doped melatonin carbon dots (DM-CDs) were synthesized from melatonin and d-cysteine and immobilized within a gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA)/oxidized hyaluronic acid hydrogel (GH-DM) through dynamic Schiff-base interactions. Sulfur-containing surface states endowed DM-CDs with strong 808 nm absorption, an approximately 50% photothermal conversion efficiency, stable heating cycles, and NIR-amplified antibacterial activity. The melatonin-derived surface simultaneously scavenged ROS, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, and was associated with increased Nrf2 and Sirt1 transcript levels together with recovery of CAT and SOD activities in mouse bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). Under acidic conditions, dynamic imine interactions were associated with modestly accelerated DM-CD release, whereas NIR irradiation provided an external means to amplify local heating and antibacterial performance. GH-DM reduced planktonic bacterial viability and biofilm biomass, decreased cell-associated Staphylococcus aureus signals, and enhanced BMSC osteogenic differentiation, as shown by ALP activity, matrix mineralization, and increased RUNX2, ALP, COL1, and OCN expression. Mouse BMSC RNA sequencing revealed enrichment of collagen-containing extracellular-matrix programs and attenuation of NF-κB, IL-1β, IL-6, and osteoclast-differentiation-related signatures. Separate LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 experiments supported attenuation of a pro-inflammatory state and increased IL-10 expression. In infected femoral defects, GH-DM plus NIR markedly reduced bacterial burden and improved trabecular regeneration, with no detectable major-organ histopathology or abnormalities in the measured hematological, hepatic, and renal indices. These findings support a locally delivered carbon-dot hydrogel with acid-accelerated release that coordinates infection control, redox protection, inflammatory regulation, and bone regeneration.
records.authors: Xie E, Wu Y, Wang A, Liu X, Cang D, Zou G, Yin J.

records.title: Classical guinea pig coat phenotypes are associated with variants in  FGF5  and  CELSR1
records.abstract: ABSTRACT  Classical Mendelian coat phenotypes in the domestic guinea pig,  Cavia porcellus , were central to early studies of mammalian genetics, yet their molecular bases remain unresolved. Long fur is characterized by elongated hair, and rough coat by whorled patterns of fur orientation. Here, we performed genome-wide association mapping using exome and whole-genome sequencing data to identify the genetic basis of both phenotypes. Mapping of long fur identified a locus containing  FGF5 and resolved the association to a premature stop codon, independently confirming a previously proposed candidate variant. Mapping of rough coat identified a locus containing  CELSR1 , an atypical cadherin and core component of the planar cell polarity (PCP) pathway, resolving the association to an in-frame proline insertion in its extracellular domain. The variant is associated with a dominant rough-coat phenotype, unlike previously characterized recessive mouse  Celsr1 alleles, which produce a similar hair-patterning phenotype only when homozygous. The mouse alleles are also associated with severe developmental abnormalities, including open neural tube, which are not observed in rough-coat guinea pigs. This dominant, tissue-specific phenotype suggests that the insertion alters CELSR1 function in a previously undescribed manner. Consistent with this possibility, the rough-coat variant localized normally to cell-cell junctions in cultured mouse keratinocytes and retained its ability to recruit Fzd6 and Vangl2, demonstrating preserved molecular interactions involved in PCP junction assembly. These findings resolve the molecular basis of two classical guinea pig coat phenotypes and identify a naturally occurring, dominant  CELSR1 allele associated with a mode of PCP disruption distinct from previously characterized alleles.
records.authors: Halley M, Bierle CJ, Hsieh P, Zaidi A, Albert FW, Cetera M.
