records.title: Bacterial and host cell-specific delivery of BMP, GrpE, and pMGA antigens via attenuated Salmonella confers bivalent protection against Mycoplasma gallisepticum and Salmonella Gallinarum in chickens.
records.abstract: Mycoplasma gallisepticum and Salmonella Gallinarum (SG) are economically important bacterial pathogens affecting poultry production, yet no single vaccine addresses both pathogens simultaneously. We engineered a recombinant SG vaccine strain, JOL3203, based on the dual-expression plasmid pJHL270, incorporating functionally distinct prokaryotic and eukaryotic cassettes to deliver two complementary Mycoplasma gallisepticum antigens from a single immunization regimen. The bacterial cassette under the Ptrc promoter expressed a multi-epitope chimeric antigen derived from conserved B-cell, MHC class I, and MHC class II epitopes of the BMP, GrpE, pMGA1.2, and pMGA1.3 proteins. The host cell cassette under the CMV promoter expressed a domain-based fusion antigen incorporating the N-terminal 400 residues of the BMP family protein, the C-terminal 250 residues of GrpE, and immunodominant pMGA epitopes. This dual-expression strategy was designed to promote antigen presentation through both exogenous and endogenous processing pathways, thereby stimulating complementary CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T-cell responses. In silico analyses predicted high antigenicity, favorable structural quality, and strong interaction with chicken TLR2-2. Expression was confirmed by western blotting at 32 kDa in bacterial lysates and 83 kDa in infected chicken bone marrow-derived macrophages, with transcription validated by RT-PCR. JOL3203 achieved 100% survival in safety evaluations versus 83% mortality in the wild-type SG group, with minimal systemic dissemination and histopathological changes. Vaccination elicited robust Mycoplasma-specific systemic IgY, mucosal IgA, expanded CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell populations, upregulated MHC class I and II expression, and a balanced Th1/Th2 cytokine profile of IFN-γ, TNF-α, and IL-4. Following intratracheal challenge, vaccinated birds showed significantly reduced tracheal colonization by color-changing unit assay, decreased mucosal thickening, and improved average daily weight gain versus PBS controls. JOL3203 further conferred 100% survival against lethal SG challenge compared with 75% mortality in PBS controls, with significantly reduced hepatic and splenic bacterial burdens. These findings demonstrate that the pJHL270 dual-expression platform provides a safe and effective strategy for simultaneous protection against Mycoplasma gallisepticum and SG while supporting its broader application as a modular live-vector vaccine platform for poultry.
records.authors: Bakhsh M, Kwon J, Gabasa DME, Depasupil AM, Cabarles JC, Lee JH.

records.title: Temporal changes in Zika virus populations during infection of three Aedes mosquito species.
records.abstract: Zika virus (ZIKV) is a mosquito-borne flavivirus transmitted mainly by Aedes aegypti and Ae. albopictus, although other species are potential vectors. ZIKV quasispecies may change during mosquito infection, but their dynamics across mosquito species remain poorly understood. We compared ZIKV quasispecies in experimentally infected Ae. aegypti, Ae. albopictus, and the potential vector Ae. japonicus. Viral genomes from pooled samples representing different mosquito body parts and infection periods were analysed by next-generation sequencing, and variant frequencies were evaluated using multivariate analyses. We identified 333 nucleotide variants in the viral open reading frame, including 142 nonsynonymous substitutions. Variant frequency patterns were significantly associated with mosquito species and infection period, whereas no significant associations were detected with body part or viral titre. Subset analyses revealed an association with infection period in Ae. japonicus, but not in the combined Ae. aegypti and Ae. albopictus dataset, although differences in sampling periods limited interspecies comparisons. Three nonsynonymous substitutions were shared among species: T442I and I446T in the envelope (E) protein near the N444 glycosylation motif, and Q2893K in NS5. T442I and I446T frequencies generally increased during infection in Ae. albopictus and Ae. japonicus, whereas they initially increased but declined at the final sampling point in Ae. aegypti. Q2893K remained relatively stable. T442I and I446T also increased during serial passage in Ae. albopictus-derived C6/36 cells. These recurrent frequency increases are consistent with positive selection, although their functional significance remains undetermined.
records.authors: Shimooka M, Miki K, Sasaki R, Eshita Y, Orba Y, Sawa H, Muramatsu Y, Uchida L.

records.title: Functional characterization of MfJAZ1 from Medicago falcata as a negative regulator of cold tolerance in transgenic Arabidopsis.
records.abstract: Jasmonate ZIM-domain (JAZ) proteins are essential transcriptional repressors in the jasmonic acid (JA) signaling pathway, crucial for coordinating plant growth and stress responses. However, the specific function of MfJAZ1 in regulating cold tolerance in Medicago falcata remains unclear. In this study, MfJAZ1 was cloned from M. falcata cv. Hulunbuir. The encoded protein localizes to the nucleus and its expression is induced by low temperature, drought, salt, alkali, and abscisic acid treatments. Under low temperature treatment, Arabidopsis plants overexpressing (OE) MfJAZ1 exhibited a lower survival rate than the wild-type (WT), accompanied by decreased catalase (CAT) activity and increased malondialdehyde (MDA) content, whereas the atjaz1 mutant showed the opposite trend. Complementation of the atjaz1 with MfJAZ1 largely restored these physiological indices to WT levels. Furthermore, under cold stress, the expression levels of cold-responsive genes were lower in OE plants than in WT, and significantly lower than those in atjaz1. A 933 bp promoter fragment of MfJAZ1, isolated via genome walking, contains cis-elements related to light, hormone, and stress responses. Yeast one-hybrid (Y1H) and Luciferase (LUC) assays suggested a potential association between MfClpP and the MfJAZ1 promoter. Yeast two-hybrid (Y2H) and Bimolecular Fluorescence Complementation (BiFC) assays demonstrated that MfFdC2 interacts with the TIFY domain of MfJAZ1 protein. However, the specific functional significance of the direct transcriptional targets of MfJAZ1 and its interaction with MfFdC2 remains to be determined. Collectively, these results suggest that overexpression of MfJAZ1 negatively regulates the cold tolerance of Arabidopsis by diminishing antioxidant enzyme activity and suppressing the expression of cold-responsive genes. Our findings have laid the foundation for future research on the functional significance of MfClpP-MfJAZ1-MfFdC2 during cold stress.
records.authors: Chai L, Qian K, Yang H, Liu Y, Chen M, Sun J, Nurbiya M, Zhang P.

records.title: Proteolytic feedback of quorum sensing promotes infection by  Pseudomonas aeruginosa
records.abstract: ABSTRACT  Quorum sensing (QS) enables bacteria to coordinate collective behaviors in response to population density. However, the mechanisms by which QS circuits are reset or attenuated remain poorly understood. In  Pseudomonas aeruginosa , the LuxR-type transcription factor RhlR controls virulence gene expression at high cell density, requiring both its cognate acyl-homoserine lactone signal and the accessory protein PqsE for full activity. Here, we show that RhlR abundance is actively controlled by ATP-dependent proteolysis through a self-limiting negative feedback loop. We identify an N-terminal degron within RhlR that is protected from protease recognition by PqsE binding and is required for degradation by both the Lon and the ClpP1-ClpP2 protease complex. Removal of this degron stabilizes RhlR, advancing the timing of QS-regulated gene expression, enhancing biofilm formation, imposes a competitive fitness cost  in vitro , and reduced virulence in an acute mouse lung infection. Mechanistically, RhlR directly activates transcription of  clpP2 , encoding a subunit of the protease complex required for its own degradation, establishing a self-limiting negative feedback loop. Disruption of RhlR DNA binding stabilizes the receptor through dual effects on reduced  clpP2 expression and increased PqsE availability via the loss of RhlR- dependent repression of  pqsE . Together, these findings reveal proteolytic turnover as an underappreciated regulatory layer of QS-activation and establish a mechanism for how receptor turnover may facilitate the transition away from high-cell density states.
records.authors: Mallery CP, Fernandes SE, Schumacher ML, Pope AN, Dillow H, Mendoza AG, Jorth PA, Paczkowski JE.

records.title: Marine oil snow formation in microcosm incubations of artificial seawater at 4 °C
records.abstract: Abstract   An oil spill in the Arctic would have far-reaching impacts on the environment, the biota, and the Inuit communities that depend on this unique ecosystem for their livelihoods. Due to the rapid retreat of sea ice in the region, the Arctic is becoming more vulnerable to oil spills. Since microorganisms are the first responders to oil contamination, understanding their behavior is critical for designing bioremediation approaches tailored to Arctic conditions. In this study, we conducted microcosm experiments at 4 °C in the dark to simulate an Arctic oil spill, using crude oil and diesel as hydrocarbon sources. Biostimulation was tested with the addition of nutrients NaNO  3 and KH  2 PO  4 , and soy lecithin–Tween 80 dissolved in ethanol as an alternative dispersant. Microcosms were placed on tube rollers at 3 rpm to mimic natural wave action and run with appropriate controls to assess microbial community shifts. Our objectives were to characterize the early microbial succession associated with oil degradation and marine oil snow (MOS) formation, and to determine how nutrients, dispersants, oil type (crude vs. diesel), photochemical aging (fresh vs. weathered), and oil concentration influence these processes.  We observed that the combined effect of nutrients and dispersant resulted in rapid MOS formation, occurring as early as 30 minutes after the initial setup. Microbial taxa exhibited varying tolerance to different concentrations of the same oil, and the dominant hydrocarbon degraders in fresh diesel treatments were distinctly different from those in weathered diesel. Furthermore, the nutrient–dispersant treatment promoted an earlier succession of oil-degrading taxa compared to nutrient-only or dispersant- only treatments. Together, these results highlight the importance of cold-adapted microbial communities in driving early oil degradation and MOS formation in Arctic waters, and they provide insights relevant to the development of Arctic-specific bioremediation strategies.

records.title: Oil biodegradation and marine oil snow formation in Arctic seawater microcosms at 4 °C
records.abstract: Hudson Bay is a sub-Arctic inland sea characterized by seasonal sea-ice cover, which governs marine circulation, biological productivity, and ecosystem structure. In recent decades, the duration of sea-ice cover has declined, resulting in longer ice-free seasons that are expected to elevate marine activity and environmental exposure to anthropogenic disturbances. As such, the potential for oil spill incidents associated with increased marine operations is expected to rise. To understand microbial biodegradation dynamics associated with marine oil snow (MOS), seawater microcosms amended with diesel fuel were incubated at 4 °C for 6 weeks. We amended all our microcosms with UV-weathered Churchill diesel fuel at 1% (v/v). 16S rRNA sequencing of the incubations revealed a decline in overall microbial diversity and a dramatic increase in specialized oil-degrading taxa, with  Pseudomonas and  Pseudoalteromonas being the main taxa involved, as both effectively degrade hydrocarbons under ambient and stimulated conditions. Biostimulation with nutrients (NaNO  3 , KH  2 PO  4 ) and an alternative dispersant at 0.1% (v/v) resulted in a greater abundance of MOS aggregates and rapid enrichment of oil-degraders. Simple n-alkanes exhibited the highest biodegradation loss relative to complex polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs); however, biostimulation did not substantially enhance their degradation. Additionally, UV weathering resulted in a 22% loss of PAHs, which is three times higher than the UV loss observed for n-alkanes. Biostimulated samples exhibited an elevated transfer of high molecular weight alkanes and PAHs from the oil into the aqueous phase, accompanied by a rapid enrichment of oil-degrading taxa.
records.authors: Vidanage T, Desmond D, Isleifson D, Stern G, Collins RE.

records.title: Resolving Gene-Metabolism Links through Multi-Metabolite mQTL Commonality Analysis
records.abstract: High-throughput metabolomics detects so many compounds that most studies use only a fraction of them, focusing on the few metabolites with an annotated structure or substructure. Metabolite genome-wide association studies of specialized metabolism detect many metabolite quantitative trait loci (mQTLs), but most associated metabolite features remain unannotated, limiting gene discovery. In leaves of 362 tomato accessions under control and water-deficit conditions, only 13 of the 826 metabolite features associated with 77 reproducible mQTLs were annotated with good confidence. To study the mQTLs with the largest impact, we developed commonality analysis, an approach that does not depend on well-studied pathways. Commonality analysis uses biologically defined groups, such as the features associated with one mQTL, to infer relatedness between metabolites. By identifying the fragments, neutral losses or mass transformations that are common in a group, it links the group to a substructure, pathway or reaction, and can extend annotation within the group. Most high-impact mQTLs had a significantly distinct fragment commonality, whose outstanding fragments suggested the pathway involved and its candidate gene. We demonstrate the approach in three representative mQTLs: (i) common fragments pointed to a sinapoyl-hexose pathway and a serine carboxypeptidase-like candidate acyltransferase; (ii) common fragments marked the features associated with a purine permease as nitrogen-containing, which isotope labeling then supported; (iii) a common 2.02 Da transformation pointed to a double-bond reduction and a putative reductase. Overexpression of each gene reproduced the commonality patterns, supporting the candidate genes and showing that the approach also applies to experimentally defined metabolite groups.

records.title: cGAS integrates Toll-like receptor signaling in platelets to promote thromboinflammation
records.abstract: Thromboinflammation is driven by innate immune signaling and promotes tissue injury during sepsis. Activation of platelets by bacterial products and alarmins amplifies inflammation, coagulation, and thrombotic dysfunction. However, the mechanisms by which these diverse inflammatory signals converge to elicit common platelet responses remain largely undefined. Mitochondria are key integrators of cellular stress responses and can activate innate immune pathways through the release of mitochondrial DNA and engagement of the DNA sensor cGAS. We therefore hypothesized that stimulation of innate immune receptors generates endogenous cGAS ligands within platelets, providing a unifying mechanism by which distinct inflammatory cues converge on cGAS-STING signaling. Here, we demonstrate that activation of TLR4, TLR1/2, and TLR5 engages a platelet-intrinsic mtDNA-cGAS-STING axis that promotes platelet activation. In a model of endotoxemia, genetic deletion of cGAS reduced platelet activation, thrombocytopenia, pyroptosis and the early systemic inflammatory response. Platelet transfer experiments further established that platelet-intrinsic cGAS is sufficient to amplify inflammatory responses  in vivo . Mechanistically, we demonstrated that cytosolic accumulation of mtDNA and activation of cGAS-STING signaling pathway in platelets are dependent on mitochondrial calcium uniporter (MCU) and correlated with the loss of mitochondrial membrane potential and the production of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species. In contrast, canonical platelet agonists activated platelets independently of cGAS and failed to induce substantial cytosolic mtDNA accumulation. Importantly, this signaling architecture was conserved in human platelets, where TLR1/2-mediated activation required MCU- and STING-dependent signaling, whereas responses to thrombin receptor-activating peptide and collagen-related peptide remained largely unaffected. Together, these findings identify cGAS as an intracellular signal integration node that allows diverse innate immune receptors to converge on a common platelet activation pathway through sensing of mitochondria-derived DNA, allowing a rapid platelet response to microbial products.
records.authors: Bidias AR, Arsenault L, Fleury S, Welman M, Osouf M, Germain M, Pernet E, Lordkipanidzé M, Pepin G.

records.title: Runs That Succeed and Are Wrong: An Audit of Silent Failures in a Multi-Omics Platform’s Validation Runs
records.abstract: Bioinformatics pipelines can finish with a success status, write parseable summaries and report wrong results. We audited the 42 validation runs of a multi-omics Nextflow platform that the author built, reading the summary archived for each run; every summary records the status “success”. Of the runs, 14 carry a confirmed silent failure in one of five classes, each traced to code. Bulk RNA-seq of fly, Arabidopsis and yeast was quantified against a default human transcript index, and fly and bacterial variants were annotated with the human SnpEff database. The proteomics pipeline’s false discovery rate (FDR) filter aborted on an option that OpenMS had renamed, and a shell fallback passed the unfiltered list on, as we reproduced in the OpenMS build behind its container. Metabolomics features were matched across samples on exact rounded keys, so that the matrix paired almost none of the features that replicate injections of one reference plasma share. And a spatial run filed as a brain section processed bronchoalveolar-lavage reads from another study. In the validation’s later round, its model judge gave the maximum score on every metric to answers that repeated the failures’ signatures: the expected answers came from the same summaries, and the metrics measure agreement with them, not whether a summary is true. A mapping-rate floor, which only five of the failed runs report, catches three. Checks written after the failures were known flag all 13 failures of the four classes they target, as they must, since a failure counts as confirmed only when its summary shows the signature; no check looks for reads from another study. Only clean runs test the checks, and no provenance, identity or invariant check flags any of the nine clean runs, a result that allows a false-positive rate as high as 34 percent; the checks behind eight of the 13 detections never ran on a clean run. On the run outputs, the checks catch the same failures and, after a fix to the audit’s strain table that had flagged a control, flag no clean run. How well the checks detect failures they were not written for is untested.

records.title: Transition-Based Analysis Distinguishes Stage-Associated and Subtype-Specific lncRNA Signatures in Breast Cancer
records.abstract: Molecular profiling of cancer samples has traditionally emphasized protein-coding genes and microRNAs, whereas long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) remain challenging to characterize because of their generally low expression levels and poorly understood biological functions. Thousands of lncRNAs are expressed in cancer, but their contributions to tumor heterogeneity and clinical characterization have largely been overlooked. Here, we systematically analyzed lncRNA expression in the breast cancer cohort from TCGA. We developed a transition-based framework to distinguish lncRNAs consistently expressed across samples from those exhibiting statistically significant expression differences between consecutive clinical stages. Using a stringent (|z|>3) threshold, we identified four sets of transition-associated lncRNAs (Tr-lncRNAs) with directional expression changes across clinical stages. An orthogonal analysis identified subtype-associated lncRNAs (St-lncRNAs) based on maximal expression variance, distinguishing Luminal A, Luminal B, HER2-positive, and basal-like tumors. The 30 most informative lncRNAs revealed that subtype-associated patterns remained broadly consistent across clinical stages. Genomic-context analyses revealed frequent antisense relationships between lncRNAs and their counterpart protein-coding genes, raising the possibility of regulatory interactions. In addition, statistical integration of Ribo-seq evidence with translation-initiation criteria identified several lncRNA encoding micropeptides, which could expand the repertoire of candidate cancer antigens. Finally, ST8SIA6-AS1, MAPT-IT1, and LINC01087 were associated with patient survival across independent breast cancer studies. Together, these findings establish a framework for distinguishing stage-associated expression changes from subtype-associated patterns and prioritizing understudied transcripts as candidate indicators of breast cancer characteristics and progression.

records.title: Characterization of Pulmonary Tropism, Expression Kinetics and Safety of the Novel Adeno-Associated Virus-LungM3 Vector.
records.abstract: This study investigated the lung-targeting characteristics, dose- and time-dependent effects, and safety of a novel engineered adeno-associated virus (AAV) vector, AAV-LungM3. In vitro, mouse primary lung organoids were transduced with AAV-LungM3 at doses of 103, 104, and 105 vector genomes (vg)/cell, and transduction was evaluated by fluorescence detection. For in vivo validation, C57BL/6 mice received intratracheal injection of AAV-LungM3 at doses of 0.5 × 1011, 1.0 × 1011, and 2.0 × 1011 vg. Flow cytometry was performed to assess the dose-dependent transduction specificity and efficiency of AAV-LungM3 in type I alveolar epithelial cells (AT1 cells) and type II alveolar epithelial cells (AT2 cells). Using the favorable dose determined by the dose-response assay, the temporal changes in AT2 cell transduction specificity and efficiency were further monitored over a 4-week period. In addition, hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining, detection of peripheral blood inflammatory factors, and analysis of plasma biochemical indicators were used to evaluate early-phase safety. In vitro transduction increased in a dose-dependent manner. In vivo assays revealed that the AT2 cell transduction specificity of AAV-LungM3 decreased gradually with increasing viral dose, whereas its transduction specificity for AT1 cells increased. Nevertheless, no significant differences in the transduction efficiency of AT1 cells and AT2 cells were observed among all dose groups. Longitudinal monitoring indicated that week 2 was the preferred time point for AAV-LungM3 transduction. In conclusion, under the tested conditions, AAV-LungM3 exhibited targeting specificity to AT2 cells and favorable in vivo expression with no observed toxic effects, serving as a potential delivery platform for pulmonary gene therapy.
records.authors: Nie H, Du J, Feng X, Fan J, Wang R, Li Q, Cao K, Gao C, Liu W, Jiang J, Wang Z, Zeng L.

records.title: Genetic architecture of bone strength and composition in White Leghorn laying hens.
records.abstract: BackgroundSkeletal issues such as fractures and poor bone quality are increasingly recognized for their negative impacts on animal welfare and the economic challenges they bring to the poultry industry. Previous pedigree-based analyses in White Leghorn laying hens have reported moderate heritabilities for cortical and medullary bone composition traits (ranging from 0.18 to 0.41) and strong genetic correlations (0.69 to 0.90) with tibia breaking strength and density. This study uses genome-wide association studies (GWAS) to identify genetic markers associated with bone strength and composition traits, aiming to advance our understanding of the genetic architecture of bone quality in White Leghorn laying hens.ResultsWe identified a set of markers on chromosome 20 (11.55-12.29 Mb) in strong LD with each other (r2 > 0.8), significantly associated with humeral stiffness, and overlapping with humeral strength and tibial cortical thickness. These markers were located within the previously identified QTL on chromosome 20 for bone biomechanical strength and body weight. This region harbors a bone morphogenetic protein 7 gene (BMP7) with a known role in skeletogenesis and growth in chicken. Genetic markers with the strongest suggestive association with organic and mineral contents, and total amount of carbonate in bone mineral MinCO3 1415 in tibia medullary bone were detected on chromosome 1 (173.5-173.6 Mb). This region contains the long non-coding RNALOC107052041 (LncFAM), which has previously been mapped within growth-related QTL and its polymorphisms have been associated with body weight and skeletal dimensions in chickens. Finally, more accurate heritabilities were estimated for thermogravimetry measurements of bone compositional traits as compared to infrared spectroscopy, with medullary organic and mineral contents being the most heritable (~0.19) and highly correlated with tibia density (0.7).ConclusionsThis study identified genomic loci associated with variation in bone quality traits, providing candidates for functional validation and for future evaluation of their potential to improve the prediction of bone strength in laying hens.
records.authors: Kurta K, Wilson PW, Andersson B, Schmutz M, Cavero D, Enrich-Essvein T, Crespo-Lopez L, Rodriguez-Navarro AB, Dunn IC, de Koning DJ, Johnsson M.

records.title: Antiviral Cytokine Signaling in Insects: Functional Parallels with Vertebrate Interferon Antiviral Immunity.
records.abstract: The absence of homologs for interferons and their receptors in insect genomes has long suggested that insects lack inducible antiviral responses. However, recent accumulating evidence calls this view into question. In this review, we summarize key findings and recent advances in this emerging field. Several secreted factors that respond to viral infection have been identified in insects, including Vago and Vago-like proteins; among these, members such as CxVago and BmVago activate downstream antiviral responses through the JAK/STAT pathway. Homologs of vertebrate interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) including CH25H, NFIL3, MxL1, and viperin have also been demonstrated to possess antiviral activities in insects. These findings outline a functional cascade of "virus-induced secreted factor - receptor recognition - signal transduction-antiviral effector" suggesting the presence of antiviral cytokine signaling in insects that is functionally parallel to the vertebrate IFN system. Although this field remains in its infancy, the available evidence has laid a foundation for future investigations. Further studies are needed to systematically identify novel antiviral cytokine molecules, validate functional receptors, and elucidate downstream signaling networks and effector mechanisms.
records.authors: Huang Y, Swevers L, Feng M.

records.title: Analysis of pathological changes and virus-susceptible cells in the testes following MPXV infection in a rhesus macaque model.
records.abstract: Monkeypox virus (MPXV) is an emerging public health threat, with increasing epidemiological and clinical evidence supporting sexual transmission, including detection of viral DNA in semen. However, the pathogenic mechanisms of MPXV within the male reproductive system remain poorly defined. We employed a rhesus macaque model to investigate MPXV-induced testicular alterations. Combining bulk RNA sequencing, histopathological analysis and immunofluorescence staining, we characterized testicular pathology, viral antigen distribution, and host responses during the early stage of infection. We found that MPXV did not induce marked inflammation or widespread cell death, and seminiferous tubule architecture remained largely intact during infection. Furthermore, within seminiferous tubules, Sertoli cells showed higher proportion of MPXV antigen co-localization than spermatogonia and spermatocytes, whereas in the interstitium, vascular endothelial cells and immune cells, including macrophages and T cells, showed prominent MPXV antigen detection, consistent with a potential contribution of hematogenous dissemination to testicular involvement. MPXV infection was associated with downregulation of the Sertoli cell marker SOX9 and alterations in tight junction-associated proteins, suggesting changes in Sertoli cell characteristics and BTB-associated molecular features. Transcriptomic analysis revealed changes in interferon-related antiviral pathways and complement-related gene expression, with C1q-positive signals detected in both interstitial and seminiferous tubular regions. In addition, changes in spermatogenesis-related gene expression were observed, which may reflect alterations in the spermatogenic microenvironment. Collectively, this study provides a quantitative characterization of early MPXV-testis interactions and cellular tropism across multiple testicular cell types in a non-human primate model, and provides insights into the pathological and immune responses associated with MPXV infection.
records.authors: Chang JT, Lin KQ, Liu LB, Yang W, Fan DY, Xue J, Wang PG, An J.

records.title: Enantioselective biodegradation of the pyrethroid (±)-alpha-cypermethrin by the bacteria Priestia megaterium CBMAI 2842 isolated from citrus culture.
records.abstract: Intensive use of pesticides to control agricultural pests has raised environmental concerns, making it necessary to adopt efficient strategies for treating contaminated areas. In this study, we evaluated the biodegradation potential of the bacterium Priestia megaterium CBMAI 2842, isolated from orange leaves, toward (±)-α-cypermethrin. Biodegradation assays were carried out in the presence of 100 mg·L-1 (±)-α-cypermethrin at 32 °C for 1, 3, 5, and 10 days, with monitoring by high-performance liquid chromatography with UV-Vis detection. P. megaterium CBMAI 2842 showed biodegradation potential, promoting 51% and 48% degradation of (±)-α-cypermethrin after 5 and 10 days, respectively, in a non-supplemented system (without nutrient broth). With nutrient broth supplementation, biodegradation increased, reaching 75% after 5 days. Chiral HPLC/UV-Vis analyses indicated no enantiomeric selectivity between 1 and 3 days of incubation in the non-supplemented system. However, after 5 and 10 days, preferential degradation of the (+)-(1R,cis,αS) enantiomer was observed, resulting in enrichment of the residual (-)-(1S,cis,αR) enantiomer, with enantiomeric excesses of 26% and 12%, respectively. In the nutrient-broth-supplemented system, after 5 days, higher biodegradation and a high enantiomeric excess (e.e. = 94%) were observed for the enantiomer (-)-(1S,cis,αR). Additionally, integrating untargeted metabolomics with bioinformatics tools, including MetaboAnalyst and GNPS feature-based molecular networking, enabled the putative annotation of metabolites with the exploration of metabolic changes and pathways associated with bacterial biodegradation. Additionally, the tentative annotation of eleven metabolites by gas and liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry enabled the proposal of an α-cypermethrin biodegradation pathway, expanding knowledge about the environmental fate of these compounds and identifying an efficient biocatalyst., i.e., P. megaterium CBMAI 2842 for decontamination processes.
records.authors: Rezende de Souza G, Pinto Moreno da Silva Alves MA, Magnani RF, Birolli WG, Porto ALM.

records.title: Generalists and specialists in industrial wastewater treatment system: Niche differentiation shapes distinct bacterial diversity and assembly patterns.
records.abstract: Microbial habitat generalists and specialists coexist in environment and exert distinct influences on community dynamics. However, a knowledge gap remains regarding the assembly patterns and ecological functions of these two groups in full-scale industrial wastewater treatment plants (IWWTPs). Here, we explored the ecological characteristics of generalists and specialists from 11 IWWTPs, including 3 different wastewater types and 4 WWTP compartments. Owing to niche breadth differences, generalists and specialists differ substantially in community diversity, assembly processes, r-K life strategy selection, and ecological functions. The generalists exhibited higher niche breadth, community alpha diversity / compositional similarity, and weaker dispersal limitation. In contrast, specialists showed the opposite trend. The generalists and specialists exhibited distinct r-K life strategy preference, which specialists tended to be r-strategists, while generalists tended to be K-strategists. Moreover, some genera including Hyphomicrobium, Thauera, Acinetobacter were identified as biomarkers which could distinguish different IWWTPs. The generalists and specialists showed stronger positive associations with pollutant removal in anoxic and oxic tank, respectively. Functional differences between these two groups existed in different environmental conditions. Our study enhances the ecological understanding on IWWTPs bacterial generalists and specialists and provide a foundation for further studies on the community regulation strategy.
records.authors: Chen W, Wei J, Chen D, Su Z, Xiong F, Li Y, Wen D.

records.title: Advancing terpenoid biosynthesis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae: Synthetic biology approaches for efficient longifolene production.
records.abstract: The sustainable microbial production of high-value terpenoids like longifolene represents a critical frontier in green manufacturing, yet it is often hindered by systemic metabolic inefficiencies in microbial hosts. To address this, we present a comprehensive systems metabolic engineering framework in Saccharomyces cerevisiae that integrates three complementary modules to overcome the key bottlenecks of enzyme catalysis, cofactor supply, and precursor availability. First, we enhanced the catalytic module by employing the RII dimerization/docking domain-RI anchoring disruptor (RIDD-RIAD) peptide-mediated enzyme assembly and structure-guided Pinus sylvestris longifolene synthase (psTPS) variant screening, 'which improved whole-cell longifolene production under the tested conditions. Second, to resolve nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH) cofactor imbalance, we engineered a dual-regeneration system by introducing an exogenous formate dehydrogenase (FDH) and simultaneously amplifying endogenous pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) flux. Third, we reprogrammed central carbon metabolism by integrating the non-oxidative glycolysis (NOG) pathway and deleting the transcriptional repressors DOS2 and YNR063W, and was associated with a larger steady-state cytosolic acetyl-CoA pool, the essential terpenoid precursor. This multi-pronged strategy culminated in a highly optimized strain that achieved a titer of 92.84 mg/L in shake-flask cultures. Critically, the process was successfully scaled to a 5 L bioreactor under fed-batch conditions, yielding 4181.51 mg/L total longifolene at 204 h (3484.79 mg/L extracellular and 696.72 mg/L cell-associated), the highest total titer among the microbial reports identified in Supplementary Table S4. Differences in product recovery and cultivation protocols limit direct process comparisons. Our work demonstrates that coordinated optimization of enzyme assembly, cofactor regeneration, and carbon-flow reprogramming can substantially improve longifolene biosynthesis in S. cerevisiae. This study provides a longifolene-focused case study for modular pathway optimization, while broader application of this strategy to other terpenoids or natural products will require further pathway-specific validation.
records.authors: Zhang W, Xin Y, Li S, Shen X, Zhang J, He H, Xiang S, Ba L, Liu Y.

records.title: Informatics for the Planet: Integrating Species, Ecosystems, and Geophysical Data to Manage the Health of Earth Systems.
records.abstract: UnlabelledBiomedical and health informatics has traditionally focused on human-centric clinical data to support individual patient care and health systems. However, contemporary health challenges driven by climate change, biodiversity loss, and ecological degradation demand an expanded paradigm that addresses interdependencies among human, animal, and environmental health. This editorial introduces a new JMIR Medical Informatics section called "Planetary Health Informatics"-an essential evolution extending informatics praxis beyond human health care and toward Earth's interconnected systems. JMIR Medical Informatics is launching a call for papers for this new section dedicated to advancing planetary health informatics (PHI) theory, methods, and applications for a sustainable future shaped by humans' impact on Earth. We invite authors to submit work that explores how PHI integrates species, ecosystem, and geophysical data to address critical global challenges, including metagenomic disease surveillance, climate-related hazard forecasting, environmental pollution monitoring, and health infrastructure decarbonization. By synthesizing broader ecological frameworks, we present a road map for transforming fragmented data streams into planetary-scale intelligence.
records.authors: Gray K, Benis A, Dueholm Müller S, Winkel K, Borda A.

records.title: A Plasmodium knowlesi A1-H.1 transcriptome time course focusing on the late asexual blood stages.
records.abstract: The zoonotic parasite Plasmodium knowlesi is closely related to Plasmodium vivax, the second leading cause of human malaria. P. knowlesi line A1-H.1 can be maintained in human erythrocytes and is an experimental model for P. vivax biology. We present the first transcriptome time course of the intraerythrocytic developmental cycle (IDC) of P. knowlesi A1-H.1 grown in human normocytes. Bulk RNA-sequencing was performed at five IDC stages using tightly synchronised cultures, enabling identification of constitutively expressed genes and stage-specific biomarkers, and investigation of temporal expression patterns of multigene families. Comparative analysis with P. vivax orthologues revealed strong genome-wide conservation of temporal expression. Analysis of invasion-associated genes and ApiAP2 transcription factors identified genes with conserved expression patterns for which P. knowlesi is likely a good model to study the P. vivax gene. To support comparative analyses, we developed an open-access interactive webtool to explore and visualise P. knowlesi - P. vivax - P. falciparum orthologue expression across the IDC (https://interactive.itg.be/app/pk-orthologue-expression-viewer). This time course dataset provides a reference transcriptome framework for P. knowlesi A1-H.1 and a resource for comparative Plasmodium biology. The interactive webtool facilitates rapid identification of candidate genes with conserved temporal expression, streamlining functional studies in which P. knowlesi A1-H.1 serves as a model for P. vivax.
records.authors: De Meulenaere K, Díaz-Delgado D, Monsieurs P, Sauve E, Cortés A, Knuepfer E, Rosanas-Urgell A.

records.title: Liver concentrations of JNJ-73763989 siRNA triggers in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB): The INSIGHT study panel 3 results.
records.abstract: BackgroundJNJ-73763989 is a 2:1 combination of 2 N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc)-conjugated short interfering RNAs (siRNA) targeting the S (daplusiran) and X (tomligisiran) regions of the hepatitis B virus genome. In phase 2b studies, 48 weeks of JNJ-73763989-based combination treatments led to dose-dependent reductions in viral markers, including hepatitis B surface antigen. The objective of the INSIGHT study Panel 3 was to quantify intrahepatic concentrations of the siRNAs in human livers during and after treatment.MethodsIn the open-label, single-arm, single-center study, participants with chronic hepatitis B received 48 weeks of treatment with JNJ-73763989 200 mg every 4 weeks and nucleos(t)ide analog, with optional pegylated interferon α2a 180 µg weekly added after Treatment Week (TW) 40. Core liver biopsies were collected at TW12, TW40, and at Follow-up Week (FUW) 24.ResultsLiver biopsies were available from all 4 participants at TW12 and from 3 at TW40 and FUW24. Between TW12 and TW40, liver concentrations of daplusiran and tomligisiran increased 1.5- to 2.6-fold, consistent with intrahepatic accumulation. Twenty-eight weeks after the last injection of JNJ-73763989, the triggers were still measurable in 2 of 3 participants with 4.5- to 15-fold reduced concentrations from peak levels; the estimated liver half-life ranged from approximately 2.9 to 16.1 weeks.ConclusionsIn this first study to assess liver concentrations of GalNAc-siRNA in humans with sequential biopsies, long persistence of JNJ-73763989 triggers in human livers may partially explain the prolonged suppressive effect on viral parameters observed in phase 2 studies.
records.authors: Asselah T, Vilgrain V, Kakuda TN, Ediage EN, Snoeys J, Menasria Benazzouz S, Jezorwski J, Kim L, Lenz O, Guinard-Azadian C, Biermer M.

records.title: SpoIVA contributes to efficient engulfment through a cytoskeletal-like mechanism during Bacillus subtilis sporulation.
records.abstract: During endospore (spore) development in bacteria, asymmetric cell division generates two transcriptionally distinct cellular compartments, the mother cell and future spore (forespore). Signaling between these cells leads to sequential and compartmentalized transcription, along with key morphogenetic events, including the phagocytic-like process of engulfment and the recruitment of coat proteins to the engulfing membrane. The SpoIVA ATPase is an essential sporulation protein that assembles into static filaments at the forespore surface during engulfment, where it functions as the basement layer for coat assembly. Here, using Bacillus subtilis, we reveal an additional role for SpoIVA during engulfment. Cytological analysis of a spoIVA null mutant (ΔspoIVA) revealed engulfment defects, such as septal membrane bulges and asymmetric membrane migration, similar to those typically associated with impaired peptidoglycan remodeling during engulfment. Engulfment defects were exacerbated when ΔspoIVA was combined with mutants known to impact engulfment progression and efficiency. Importantly, a spoIVA mutant (K30A) impaired for ATP hydrolysis and filament formation in vitro but partially functional for coat assembly in vivo closely phenocopies the spoIVA null mutant engulfment defects. Based on these data, we propose a model whereby SpoIVA polymerization at the spore surface, independent of coat assembly, plays a mechanical and structural role during engulfment, akin to the cytoskeletal proteins that drive phagocytosis in eukaryotic cells.IMPORTANCEEndospore formation relies on membrane remodeling to generate highly resistant dormant spores in human, animal, and insect pathogens. During engulfment, the mother-cell membrane migrates around the forespore in a phagocytic-like process, while the spore coat is simultaneously assembled. SpoIVA is widely recognized as the ATPase that polymerizes at the forespore surface to nucleate assembly of the multilayered spore coat. Here, we demonstrate that SpoIVA also performs a distinct function during engulfment that is independent of its role in coat formation. Cells lacking SpoIVA, or carrying a polymerization-defective SpoIVA variant, exhibit membrane deformations characteristic of impaired engulfment. We propose that SpoIVA polymers provide structural and mechanical during engulfment, analogous to the role of cytoskeletal systems during eukaryotic phagocytosis.

records.title: Peptidoglycan remodeling prevents antibiotic resistance during oxidative stress.
records.abstract: The bacterial small RNA (sRNA) OxyS is expressed in Escherichia coli during oxidative stress. The sRNA OxyS enhances cell survival by controlling genes involved in the regulation of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and iron-sulfur (Fe-S) cluster formation. Here, we used the MS2 affinity purification coupled with RNA sequencing (MAPS) technique to identify new target mRNAs of the sRNA OxyS. Our analysis revealed a significant enrichment of mepS mRNA, which encodes a peptidoglycan endopeptidase that promotes cell growth. Our results confirm a previous report on the sRNA OxyS repressing the translation of mepS. We also found that an ΔoxyS background facilitates the emergence of mutations, conferring increased resistance to the last-resort antibiotics polymyxin B and E (colistin), but only in the presence of the target mepS gene. This suggests that the translation repression of mepS by OxyS could prevent mutations in bacterial DNA during H2O2-induced oxidative stress. Moreover, we show that adding the antioxidant thiourea or sequestering iron in the ΔoxyS background effectively reduces the emergence of resistance against both polymyxin B and colistin. These results suggest that reactive oxygen species (ROS), in conjunction with intracellular iron, play a key role in driving the emergence of antibiotic resistance. Overall, our work underlines a mechanism of antimicrobial emergence implicating oxidative stress, intracellular Fe, and cell wall remodeling in E. coli.IMPORTANCEThis study uncovers an underexplored link between peptidoglycan remodeling and oxidative stress responses during exposure to antibiotics. By elucidating how MepS and the sRNA OxyS interact in the presence of polymyxins and oxidative stress, our study suggests that MepS may exert an anti-mutator function. The repression of mepS translation by OxyS seems to limit the emergence of antibiotic resistance driven by DNA mutations. Together, these findings suggest cell wall remodeling and oxidative stress response pathways as promising targets to enhance antibiotic efficacy and limit the emergence of resistance.
records.authors: Sukadi Miala J, Arcand-Carrier L, Lapointe R, Morin C, Sasseville C, Lalaouna D, Massé E.

records.title: Rifamycin use and gut microbial antibiotic resistance genes in cirrhosis: Results from a double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial.
records.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance gene (ARG) carriage is associated with poor outcomes in patients with liver cirrhosis, which is worsened by repeated antibiotic exposure and hospitalizations. While the semi-synthetic rifamycin derivative, rifaximin, has recently been linked to ARG expansion preclinically, the effects of rifamycin SV MMX (RiVM) on the gut resistome remain unknown. We evaluated longitudinal resistome changes with RiVM in cirrhosis. The randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled RIVET trial (15 RiVM, 15 placebo) included compensated cirrhosis patients who underwent shotgun metagenomic sequencing before/after 30 days of therapy. ARGs were annotated using the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database. The longitudinal resistome was evaluated using univariable and multi-variable methods (LEfSe, paired-Wilcoxon testing, and MaAsLin3), and machine learning (ML) was used to determine ARG changes at subject and group levels. RiVM induced minimal perturbation of the gut resistome, without significant change in ARGs versus after FDR adjustment. Complementary approaches (univariable and multivariable) identified a trend towards lower vancomycin resistance ARGs, including vanW and vanT operon-associated genes, after RiVM exposure. In contrast, several Enterobacteriaceae-associated multidrug efflux regulators (including evgS, emrK, and mdtA) showed nominal increases post-rifamycin that did not withstand FDR. Group-level ML demonstrated limited discrimination between groups; however, within-subject longitudinal models achieved improved classification performance. No increase in infections or treatment-related safety concerns was observed. We conclude that rifamycin MMX was not associated with infections and did not enrich antimicrobial resistance genes compared to placebo in a small randomized 30-day clinical trial in patients with compensated cirrhosis. There was a tendency towards reduced vancomycin resistance and ARG reduction after rifamycin exposure. Registration: NCT04082780 www.clinicaltrials.gov.

records.title: E8^E2 controls the formation of E2-positive replication centers that precede E4 expression during productive HPV16 infection.
records.abstract: Human papillomaviruses (HPVs) couple their replication cycle to keratinocyte differentiation. Viral genomes are maintained at low copy numbers in undifferentiated cells and undergo amplification within nuclear replication foci in differentiated suprabasal cells. The viral proteins E2 and E8^E2 function as activators and repressors of viral replication, respectively. Using a novel polyclonal antiserum together with the monoclonal antibody 22E2-B9, which recognize both E2 and E8^E2, we identified distinct nuclear E2 foci in keratinocytes harboring episomal HPV16 wild-type (wt) or E8^E2 mutant genomes. These foci colocalized with viral genomes and the cellular proteins RPA32, RAD51, γH2AX, and BRD4, consistent with viral replication centers. Cell-cycle analysis showed that E2 foci formed during the S phase and persisted into the G2 phase. Loss of E8^E2 expression or repression activity increased the number of replication foci and induced diffuse nuclear E2 staining. Only a subset of E2 focus-positive cells expressed the late viral protein E4, indicating that replication centers arise before robust late gene expression. In organotypic cultures, E2 focus-positive/E4-negative cells were detected in suprabasal layers before E2 focus-positive/E4-positive cells, whereas E2-negative/E4-positive cells suggested dynamic regulation of E2 during productive infection. Moreover, many wt cells displayed E2 focus phenotypes resembling E8^E2 mutant cells, suggesting that E8^E2 activity declines during keratinocyte differentiation. These findings demonstrate that E2-positive viral replication centers are tightly regulated by E8^E2, emerge early during productive HPV16 infection, and are accompanied by dynamic modulation of E2 and E8^E2 during the productive phase of the viral life cycle.ImportanceHuman papillomaviruses (HPVs) couple their replication cycle to keratinocyte differentiation, but the mechanisms controlling productive viral genome amplification remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify distinct E2-positive nuclear replication centers in HPV16-infected keratinocytes and show that they contain viral genomes and cellular factors involved in DNA replication and repair. We demonstrate that these structures form during the S phase, persist into the G2 phase, and arise before robust expression of the late viral E4 protein, indicating that viral genome amplification is initiated earlier in the productive cycle than previously appreciated. We further show that the viral repressor E8^E2 regulates the organization of E2-positive replication centers and that E8^E2 activity appears to decline during keratinocyte differentiation. Together, our findings reveal dynamic regulation of E2 and E8^E2 during productive HPV16 infection and provide new insights into how viral genome amplification and late gene expression are coordinated in differentiating epithelial cells.
records.authors: Kuehner F, Hirn F, Beyer M, Straub E, Rehm TM, Renner J, Roos N, Iftner T, Wieland A, Stubenrauch F.

records.title: Atp12 regulates mitochondrial fusion and chronological aging through Fzo1 in Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
records.abstract: Atp12 is known as a chaperone for mitochondrial ATP synthase assembly, yet its functions and mechanisms in regulating mitochondrial and cellular aging remain elusive. In this study, we demonstrate that Atp12 plays a critical role in regulating mitochondrial dynamics and chronological lifespan (CLS) in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe. We found that Atp12 localizes to mitochondria, and its deletion leads to severe mitochondrial fragmentation, reduced complex II activity, dissipation of mitochondrial membrane potential, and a marked shortening of CLS. Mechanistically, Atp12 acts partially independently of ATP synthase, as the Δatp12Δatp1 double mutant exhibited more severe defects in mitochondrial function and viability than either single mutant, and its mitochondrial morphology resembled that of Δatp12 rather than Δatp1. Transcriptomic and phenotypic analyses identified Fzo1, a mitofusin essential for mitochondrial fusion, as a key downstream target of Atp12 in regulating cellular aging. Further analysis revealed that Atp12 physically interacts with Fzo1 and stabilizes its protein levels. Genetic epistasis experiments demonstrated that Fzo1 insufficiency largely accounts for the mitochondrial fragmentation and functional decline observed in Δatp12 cells, as Fzo1 overexpression effectively rescues these defects. Collectively, these findings uncover a novel function of Atp12 in maintaining mitochondrial homeostasis and delaying cellular aging by stabilizing the mitochondrial fusion machinery. Given the evolutionary conservation of Atp12 from yeast to humans, this study provides a mechanistic framework for understanding how the coordination of mitochondrial biogenesis and dynamics drives the aging process.IMPORTANCEMitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of cellular aging, but how mitochondria are regulated at the molecular level to influence cellular longevity remains elusive. Here, we reveal that Atp12, a conserved chaperone for ATP synthase assembly, also serves as a stabilizer of the mitofusin Fzo1 to preserve mitochondrial fusion and chronological lifespan in fission yeast. Through direct physical interaction, Atp12 sustains Fzo1 protein levels, thereby maintaining mitochondrial morphology, respiratory function, and cell survival, a function that is largely independent of its canonical role in ATP synthase. This discovery uncovers an unexpected link between a mitochondrial assembly factor and organellar dynamics, establishing the Atp12-Fzo1 axis as a conserved regulatory node that couples mitochondrial quality control to the aging process.
records.authors: Liu Z, Zhu G, Zeng Y, Deng B, Su Y, Zheng X, Yao R.

records.title: Disruption of OsNLP4-mediated nitrate signaling alters root exudate composition and root-associated bacterial communities in rice.
records.abstract: OsNLP4 is a master regulator of nitrate signaling, but its ecological role in the root-associated bacterial communities is unknown. This study investigated how OsNLP4-mediated nitrate signaling influences root-associated microbial composition and root exudate metabolism. We found that the osnlp4 mutants exhibited distinct root-associated bacterial communities compared to the WT under non-nitrogen-fertilized conditions, with a significant enrichment of Bradyrhizobium and other bacterial taxa with potential roles in nitrogen cycling. Isolated Bradyrhizobium strains showed increased colonization in the osnlp4 mutant. Metabolomic analysis revealed increased secretion of sugars and phosphoric acid, along with a lower C:N ratio, in the osnlp4 mutant root exudates. Bacterial growth and chemotactic responses differed between WT- and osnlp4-derived root exudates, and sugars enriched in osnlp4 exudates elicited chemotactic responses in isolated Bradyrhizobium strains. These metabolic changes were associated with differential bacterial responses to WT and osnlp4 root exudates and may contribute to the altered root-associated bacterial community. Taken together, our results suggest that OsNLP4 links nitrate signaling and nitrogen metabolism with root-associated bacterial community assembly. Disruption of OsNLP4 reprograms root exudation and reshapes root-associated microbial communities, highlighting an association between nitrate signaling, nutrient allocation, and root-associated bacterial community assembly in rice.

records.title: Identification of auxin response factor ARF27 as a regulator of maize root morphogenesis.
records.abstract: Auxin is a central phytohormone that mediates root development. This study investigated the genetic basis of auxin-mediated primary root growth in Zea mays (maize) seedlings, which is not well-understood in this key cereal crop. To address this knowledge gap, 618 accessions from the Wisconsin Diversity panel were leveraged for a genome wide association study (GWAS) followed by reverse genetics and in silico gene regulatory network reconstruction (GRN). The GWAS identified several candidate genes associated with variation in root growth responses, including RAMOSA2 and multiple members of the AUXIN RESPONSE FACTOR (ARF) gene family. Maize AUXIN RESPONSE FACTOR27 (ZmARF27), an ortholog of Arabidopsis ARF7 and ARF19, was prioritized for functional characterization. A reduction in ZmARF27 levels led to short primary roots, insensitivity to exogenous auxin, and altered transcriptional responses. Reconstruction of an ZmARF27 GRN included known maize classical root development genes, such as ROOTLESS CONCERNING CROWN ROOTS, numerous auxin pathway genes, and genes associated with cell wall biogenesis. Altogether, this study identifies ZmARF27 as a novel genetic driver of auxin-mediated root growth and gene expression in maize.
records.authors: Dash L, Draves MA, Khangura RS, McReynolds MR, Muench RL, Cowling CL, Song G, Dilkes BP, Walley JW, Kelley DR.

records.title: Integrative bioinformatics and experimental validation of the prognostic and functional relevance of XDH and ITPA in non-small cell lung cancer.
records.abstract: Purine metabolism has been implicated in tumor biology and immune regulation, but the clinical and biological relevance of purine metabolism-related genes in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains incompletely defined. Transcriptomic data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and the Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) project, together with TCGA clinical data, were analyzed to identify differentially expressed purine metabolism-related genes and assess their prognostic associations. Immune infiltration was evaluated using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA), and single-cell transcriptomic datasets were analyzed to characterize the cellular context of candidate genes. Stemness features and drug sensitivity were assessed using transcriptome-based computational models. XDH and ITPA protein expression was examined by Western blotting and immunohistochemistry (IHC) in an independent NSCLC cohort and in cell models. Stable knockdown of XDH or ITPA was performed in H1299 cells, with key functional findings further evaluated in A549 cells. Cisplatin sensitivity was assessed using cell-viability dose-response assays in H1299 and A549 cells. Several purine metabolism-related genes were upregulated in NSCLC and associated with overall survival (OS). XDH and ITPA showed higher protein expression in tumor tissues and were associated with adverse clinicopathological features and poorer survival. Higher expression of these genes was also associated with altered immune infiltration patterns. The messenger RNA-based stemness index (mRNAsi) was associated with ITPA and XDH expression in different directions, whereas higher XDH expression was associated with higher predicted half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) values for cisplatin. Knockdown of XDH or ITPA attenuated proliferative, clonogenic, migratory, and invasive phenotypes in H1299 cells, with key findings reproduced in A549 cells. XDH knockdown also reduced the experimentally determined cisplatin IC50 in both H1299 and A549 cells. XDH and ITPA may represent candidate prognostic and functionally relevant purine metabolism-related genes in NSCLC. The integrated clinical, computational, and cellular findings support their association with NSCLC progression-related phenotypes, while the underlying molecular mechanisms and broader clinical applicability require further investigation.
records.authors: Zhang W, Song J, Zhu H, Wang Y, Wang H, Li X.

records.title: Human senataxin uses distinct peripheral elements to unwind R-loops and act on RNA polymerase II
records.abstract: ABSTRACT  Persistent R-loops and paused or stalled RNA polymerase II (RNAPII) elongation complexes can threaten genome stability. Senataxin (SETX) contributes to R-loop resolution and RNAPII regulation, but their intimate connection during transcription makes the individual contributions of these activities difficult to distinguish in cells. To determine whether these activities rely on the same molecular features, we investigated the structure and biochemical properties of the SETX helicase domain (SETX-HD). Cryo-EM defines the conserved helicase core and RNA-binding channel of SETX-HD, while biochemical analyses identify distinct roles for two peripheral elements: a previously uncharacterised C-terminal RNA-binding domain (CT-RBD) and the prong subdomain. In reconstituted mammalian transcription assays, SETX-HD promotes passage beyond a defined RNAPII pause and elongation-complex dissociation on the same template. The CT-RBD stabilises RNA engagement and is required for efficient R-loop unwinding, whereas its deletion preserves both RNAPII-associated activities. Conversely, replacing the native SETX prong with its fungal Sen1 counterpart preserves R-loop unwinding but impairs both RNAPII outcomes. These reciprocal separation-of-function effects establish that a common SETX-HD RNA-translocation core depends on distinct peripheral elements for R-loop unwinding and action on mammalian RNAPII. This separation provides a direct route to determine how these activities contribute to SETX function in cells.
records.authors: Lanicek M, Sedova K, Hasanova Z, Porrua O, Sebesta M.

records.title: A candidate  HNRNPU  –  CHD2  RNA-processing axis in neurodevelopmental disease
records.abstract: Heterozygous loss-of-function variants in  HNRNPU , which encodes a nuclear RNA-binding scaffold protein, cause a neurodevelopmental disorder with epilepsy, intellectual disability and brain malformations, but the programs that link  HNRNPU dosage to neuronal dysfunction remain poorly defined. We depleted  HNRNPU in Human embryonic kidney 293T (HEK293T) cells, profiled gene expression and alternative splicing, intersected the two datasets, and asked which of the resulting genes already carried a neurodevelopmental annotation. Knockdown produced 5,643 differentially expressed genes and 21,728 high-confidence splicing events; 1,222 genes changed at both levels, and two pre-specified neurodevelopmental panel genes were among them:  CHD2 and  DYRK1A . In K562 eCLIP experiments, 107 reproducible  HNRNPU peaks were detected across the  CHD2 gene body, and three of the four regulated exons introduce a reading-frame shift whose premature termination codon lies far upstream of the final exon junction, predicting nonsense-mediated decay. Public K562 knockdown data reproduced the rise in  CHD2 mRNA and the same skipped-exon change, and  CHD2 depletion in the neural line SH-SY5Y altered cell-cycle, DNA-repair and neural gene programs. HNRNPU therefore constrains a frameshift-prone splicing switch in  CHD2 , a candidate route from  HNRNPU haploinsufficiency to loss of functional  CHD2 if these transcripts are degraded.  Highlights  HNRNPU depletion changes  CHD2 expression and exon inclusion in human cells.  eCLIP places  HNRNPU on  CHD2 RNA, consistent with direct control of its splicing.  Three  CHD2 exons are frameshift-prone, predicting loss of full-length  CHD2 .
records.authors: Tang H, Xiao Z, Wang R, Babarinde IA, Huang S, Hutchins AP, Ma G.

records.title: Putative biosurfactants from polar microbial consortia
records.abstract: Biosurfactants (BS) are amphiphilic microbial metabolites that are biodegradable, low in toxicity, and environmentally compatible, making them attractive for applications in food, pharmaceutical, and bioremediation industries. This study investigated the phylogenetic composition and biosurfactant-producing potential of marine oil snow (MOS)-associated microbial consortia from the Churchill Marine Observatory, western Hudson Bay. MOS aggregates were cultivated in mineral Bushnell–Haas (BH) medium supplemented with 3% (w/v) NaCl, using motor oil as the sole hydrocarbon source. Enrichment cultures capable of growth in BH medium were subsequently evaluated for biosurfactant production using qualitative and quantitative assays at 4 °C and 20 °C. All cultures were maintained as enrichment consortia throughout the study. A total of eight enrichment cultures were identified as biosurfactant-producing consortia. 16S rRNA gene sequencing revealed that  Pseudoalteromonas dominated all consortia, while  Paraglaciecola, Marinomonas , and other taxa were present at varying relative abundances. Although none of the consortia exhibited high emulsification activity (E  24 > 40%), biosurfactant yields were significantly higher at 4 °C. Additionally, three consortia tested positive for rhamnolipid-type biosurfactant production.

records.title: Antibiotics drive immunometabolic rewiring of human immune responses
records.abstract: Antibiotics are routinely evaluated for their antimicrobial activity, potential host toxicity, and disruption of the microbiome. Certain antibiotics can also impact cell-intrinsic host processes, including evolutionarily conserved processes in the mitochondria. These raise the possibility that antibiotics can directly impact host immunity, which relies on mitochondrial function for their immunometabolic activation. However, the immunological consequences of most antibiotics in current use have not been systematically examined. Here, we performed a comprehensive analysis of the effects of clinically used antibiotics on activation of primary human immune cells. We uncovered an underappreciated antibiotic-specific modulation of immune function in healthy individuals and infectious disease patients. Focusing on the immunomodulatory antibiotic ciprofloxacin, we found altered mitochondrial gene expression across multiple immune populations, driving distinct, lineage-specific responses and heightened sensitivity of T-cells. Ciprofloxacin impaired primary human T-cell expansion and activation and altered mitochondrial function and metabolism. We further demonstrated immunomodulatory effects of selected antibiotics in response to inactivated bacteria and during live viral infection. Finally, to test the implications of our findings in vivo, we showed that immune activation is altered shortly after a single dose of antibiotic administration in mice. This work established a widespread impact of antibiotics on immune-cell function, and identified mitochondrial perturbation as one underlying mechanism, with implications for host-pathogen interactions and antimicrobial therapy.

records.title: Activity of Aztreonam-Avibactam and Comparators against Difficult-To-Treat Resistant (DTR) Enterobacterales from European Medical Centres Stratified by Infection Type and Country (2021– 2025)
records.abstract: Abstract  Background: Difficult-to-treat resistant (DTR) isolates, defined as bacterial isolates expressing nonsusceptibility to all first-line agents, is a major problem worldwide. We evaluated the activity of aztreonam-avibactam and comparators against DTR Enterobacterales from European medical centres. Methods: 30,345 Enterobacterales isolates were consecutively collected from 41 European medical centres in 19 countries in 2021–2025. Isolates were susceptibility tested by broth microdilution and MIC interpreted according to EUCAST breakpoints. The collection included 1113 DTR isolates, defined as a carbapenem-resistant isolate (MIC ≥4 mg/L for meropenem and/or imipenem) not susceptible to fluoroquinolones. All DTR isolates were screened for β-lactamase genes by whole genome sequencing. Results were stratified by infection type and country. Results: Aztreonam-avibactam was active against 99.6% of DTR (MIC50/90, 0.25/0.5 mg/L), and exhibited consistent activity against DTR isolates from all infection types. Cefiderocol was active against 78.8% of DTR isolates; ceftazidime-avibactam, meropenem-vaborbactam, imipenem-relebactam, and the aminoglycosides exhibited limited activity against these organisms. The frequency of DTR was higher among isolates from pneumonia (6.6%) compared to other infection types (2.3–3.4%) and varied from 0.0% (Switzerland) to 19.7% (Poland) among countries. DTR susceptibility to aztreonam-avibactam ranged from 94.4% (France) to 100.0% (14 countries). Aztreonam-avibactam retained potent activity against DTR isolates nonsusceptible to ceftazidime-avibactam (99.2% susceptible), meropenem-vaborbactam (99.6% susceptible), and/or cefiderocol (97.8% susceptible). The most common carbapenemase identified among DTR isolates was NDM (41.2% of DTR), followed by OXA-48–like (38.2%), and KPC (34.3%). Moreover, 99.6% of metallo-β-lactamase (MBL) producers were susceptible to aztreonam-avibactam and 68.2% were susceptible to cefiderocol. Conclusions: Aztreonam-avibactam retained potent activity against DTR Enterobacterales from European medical centres and its activity was not adversely affected by clinically relevant carbapenemases or resistance to agents currently used to treat multidrug-resistant Enterobacterales. The activities of other β-lactamase inhibitor combinations and cefiderocol were compromised by the increased occurrence of MBL producers.
records.authors: SADER HS, MENDES RE, PEREZ K, STONE G, PAPP-WALLACE KM, CASTANHEIRA M.

records.title: Glucocorticoid regulation of the human noncoding genome.
records.abstract: Glucocorticoids (GCs) are widely used anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive agents known to induce substantial changes in gene expression, yet their effects on noncoding RNAs such as long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) or microRNAs (miRNAs) remain poorly characterized. Here, we present the first comprehensive and systematic analysis of GC regulation of the noncoding genome across nine human primary cell types from both hematopoietic and nonhematopoietic lineages. In vitro GC treatment was applied to each cell type, with transcriptomic profiling (total RNA-seq and small RNA-seq) at 2 and 6 h posttreatment. We identify more than 2000 GC-responsive noncoding transcripts, including 654 annotated lncRNAs, 1376 novel lncRNAs, and 39 miRNAs. The noncoding RNA response to GCs is highly cell type dependent: 80% of GC-responsive lncRNAs and 97% of miRNAs are unique to a single cell type. Hematopoietic cells exhibit a greater magnitude of lncRNA induction compared with nonhematopoietic cells. Notably, GC treatment uncovers dozens of facultative, stimulus-dependent lncRNAs. GC-responsive transcripts span diverse lncRNA classes, with enrichment of host lncRNAs. In contrast, only a limited number of miRNAs are GC responsive. GC regulation of transcript abundance for miRNAs and their host lncRNAs appears to be independent. Our results, which are accessible through an interactive web application, establish a framework for studying how noncoding transcription contributes to physiological and clinical heterogeneity in GC responses. The newly identified GC-responsive noncoding transcripts could represent biomarkers of GC exposure, determinants of GC sensitivity or resistance, or candidate regulators of tissue-specific GC effects.
records.authors: Tran T, Kwiat R, Cao Q, Kuhn S, Howe KN, Gadkari M, Franco LM.

records.title: Viral haplotype reconstruction from long reads with virCHap.
records.abstract: Resolving genomes at the haplotype level for viral populations is crucial for understanding the prevalence of viral diseases and for the development of effective therapeutic treatments. However, viral haplotype reconstruction still presents challenges, such as an unknown number of strains, high interstrain similarity, repetitive regions, and difficulties in abundance estimation. Here, we develop virCHap, a new reference-based haplotype phasing algorithm for viruses, which applies graph partitioning followed by iteratively quantifiable cluster merging on long-read sequencing data. Benchmarking on simulated and real data sets demonstrates that virCHap outperforms current tools in terms of recall, accurate abundance estimates, and read clustering accuracy. On a simulated large-genome VZV experiment, virCHap has a 96% recall, 13.6% higher than the second-best method, and has the most accurate abundance estimates. On a real five-strain PVY data set, virCHap has a precision exceeding 94.4%, a recall of >97%, and a read clustering accuracy of 93.4%, outperforming the second-best method by 33%. On a real six-strain SARS-CoV-2 data set, virCHap achieves >96.7% accuracy, and the most accurate abundance estimates within the spike (S) gene.
records.authors: Gao Y, Liu B, Li G, Yu T.

records.title: Genetic susceptibility to anterior cruciate ligament rupture in females: a systematic review of female-stratified candidate-gene evidence and the absence of genome-wide studies.
records.abstract: ObjectiveTo systematically synthesise and critically appraise genetic association studies reporting female-stratified evidence for anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) rupture.DesignSystematic review.Data sourcesWeb of Science, Scopus, Ovid MEDLINE and the Cochrane Library were searched from database inception to 21 December 2025, which was the predefined search date for this review.Eligibility criteria for selecting studiesHuman genetic association studies reporting female-stratified ACL rupture outcomes or extractable female-only data were included. Studies reporting combined-sex analyses without extractable female data were excluded. Due to predefined heterogeneity in phenotypes, populations and genetic models, findings were synthesised narratively.Results19 studies met the inclusion criteria, predominantly small candidate-gene case-control designs. Importantly, these publications did not represent 19 independent cohorts. The largest prospective cohort included 790 women at risk at baseline, of whom 58 sustained an incident ACL injury and 732 remained without incident injury. COL5A1 rs12722 was the most frequently reported female-stratified candidate variant. Positive single-variant estimates principally concerned CC homozygotes under a recessive model and arose from South African samples with documented participant reuse. Separate allelic associations were also reported. Independence of this signal was limited by probable cohort overlap, heterogeneous genetic models and null prospective evidence. Evidence for other collagen, proteoglycan, inflammatory and extracellular matrix remodelling genes was inconsistent. No female-stratified genome-wide association studies were identified.ConclusionsCOL5A1 rs12722 is the most frequently reported female-stratified candidate variant, but independent replication is not established. Positive recessive estimates concern CC homozygotes and should not be extended to heterozygotes. Small samples, participant reuse, heterogeneous genetic models and null prospective evidence limit certainty. Female-stratified associations do not establish sex-specific effects. Evidence derives predominantly from women of European ancestry, and generalisability to other ancestries remains unknown. Current findings do not support genetic screening for ACL rupture risk in female athletes; adequately powered, female-stratified genomic studies with rigorous phenotyping and independent replication across diverse ancestries are needed.
records.authors: Edmonds CJ, Browne GJ, Khan WS, McDonnell SM.

records.title: Dynamic balance of sparse flux vectors for efficient simulation of culture dynamics and metabolic network reduction.
records.abstract: Dynamic Flux Balance Analysis (DFBA) enables simulation of microbial culture dynamics under changing environmental conditions but remains computationally expensive for tasks such as parameter calibration and bioprocess control when applied to genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs). To address this, we introduce Dynamic Flux Vector Balancing (DFVB), a mathematical reformulation that solves an equivalent problem using a pre-computed sparse basis of flux solutions. This new algorithm enables an automatic, simulation-based network reduction. We show that DFVB exactly reproduces the DFBA culture dynamics in large-scale GEMs, while reducing the number of active reactions by up to 70% and accelerating simulations by up to threefold. Also, it identifies inactive reactions more accurately than Flux Variability Analysis (FVA) when compared to transcriptomic data profiles. Furthermore, during kinetic parameter estimation in two fermentation scenarios, DFVB achieved equal or superior calibration accuracy compared to standard DFBA. By circumventing solution degeneracy, DFVB yielded dynamic predictions with reduced uncertainty, despite inherent parameter identifiability limits. Together, these results position DFVB as a scalable and efficient alternative to DFBA, easing the integration of GEMs for bioprocess simulation and optimization.
records.authors: García IT, Torrealba C, Luna R, Pérez-Correa JR, Saa PA.
