records.title: Evaluation of linkage disequilibrium, haplotype block structure, and historical effective population size in the Iranian Turkmen horse.
records.abstract: This study used the Illumina Equine SNP70 BeadChip to investigate whole-genome linkage disequilibrium (LD), haplotype block structure, and historical effective population size (Ne) of the Iranian Turkmen horse. Genotyping was performed on 70 samples, of which 62 passed quality control and were retained for analysis. We estimated the extent of LD using r2 and D' measures and characterized haplotype block structure and historical Ne. Gene Ontology (GO) and pathway enrichment analyses were performed to identify biological functions associated with genes within the detected haplotype blocks. Across all SNP pairs analyzed (distance ≤ 5 Mb), mean r2 was 0.04, while mean D' was 0.47. Mean r2 for the closest SNP pairs (2. A total of 5,155 haplotype blocks were detected, mainly on chromosome 1, involving 16,553 SNPs and encompassing 29% of all SNPs in the genome. The estimated Ne decreased with increasing number of generations, indicating the need for adequate conservation measures to ensure the genetic diversity of this valuable breed. GO and pathway enrichment analysis of genes within the longest haplotype blocks showed significant overrepresentation of biological processes related to steroid metabolism, oxidative demethylation, apoptotic signaling, chemical carcinogenesis, and retinol metabolism. These findings suggest candidate biological processes that require further validation.

records.authors: Rahimi M, Foroutanifar S, Moradi Shahrbabak H, Abdolmohammadi A.

records.title: Multi-omics studies show that naringin improves cyclophosphamide-induced testicular and intestinal damage by enhancing energy metabolism.
records.abstract: Cyclophosphamide (CTX) is an anticancer agent that severely impairs male reproductive health. Naringin (NAR), a flavonoid compound, has the potential to ameliorate CTX-induced damage; however, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, an integrative approach combining transcriptomics, microbiome analysis, and serum metabolomics was employed to comprehensively evaluate the protective effects of NAR on reproductive function in CTX-treated mice. Microbiome analysis revealed that NAR restored CTX-induced alterations in gut microbial composition. Metabolomic profiling demonstrated that NAR stabilised cholesterol metabolism and primary bile acid biosynthesis, increased serum choline levels, and alleviated reproductive dysfunction in CTX-exposed mice. Transcriptomic analyses of the testes and intestine indicated that NAR modulated glycolysis and the MAPK signalling pathway in CTX-treated mice. Validation of serum metabolites further supported their role in promoting intestinal and testicular development. Research indicates that naringin ameliorates cyclophosphamide-induced reproductive risks in males, partly due to its enhancement of energy metabolism.
records.journal: The Journal of steroid biochemistry and molecular biology

records.title: Divergent hydraulic safety and efficiency trade-offs of woody plants are associated with mycorrhizal types at the global scale.
records.abstract: The hydraulic safety-efficiency trade-off is a core mechanism for woody plants to adapt to their environments. Symbiosis with different mycorrhizal fungi (arbuscular mycorrhiza, AM and ectomycorrhiza, ECM) may affect plant water acquisition strategies. However, whether the hydraulic trade-off strategies of woody plants differ among mycorrhizal types, and what drives these differences, remains unclear. Therefore, this study integrated global plant hydraulic parameters and climate data by mycorrhizal type to explore the associations between mycorrhizal types and plant hydraulic strategies and identify the main driving factors. After controlling for phylogeny, plant growth form, height, and climate, we found that AM plants had significantly larger conduit diameters (38.32 μm) than ECM plants (27.75 μm). The safety-efficiency slope was significantly steeper in ECM than in AM plants, indicating a greater efficiency cost for ECM plants to enhance safety. Environmental factors had different driving effects, water availability dominated AM plant trade-off strategies (38.63%), whereas temperature was a key driver for ECM plant hydraulic strategies (42.08%). Partial least squares path modeling (PLS-PM) further revealed that climate indirectly affects AM tree height by regulating conduit diameter and trade-off positions (Residuals/Distance), whereas ECM tree height is primarily directly driven by trade-off traits. In conclusion, differentiation in hydraulic trade-off strategies is an important mechanism for woody plants with different mycorrhizal types to adapt to different environments, providing a new perspective for understanding plant hydraulic responses to global change.

records.title: AtATO interacts with the senescence-related repressor AtWDS1 to negatively regulate age-dependent and dark-induced leaf senescence in Arabidopsis.
records.abstract: Although many achievements have been made in understanding the mechanisms underlying age-dependent and induced leaf senescence, the precise regulatory pathway involved remains to be elucidated. AtWDS1, which is a nuclear-localized negative senescence regulator in Arabidopsis thaliana, was characterized in a previous study. In this study, AtATO, encoding an SF3a factor, was identified when AtWDS1-interacting proteins were screened and was further verified using yeast two-hybrid assays and bimolecular fluorescence complementation. YFP-tagged AtATO protein in A. thaliana mesophyll protoplasts revealed that AtATO localized to the nucleus and cytoplasm. An analysis of the AtATO T-DNA insertion mutant (atato) revealed a premature senescence phenotype, chlorophyll loss, and up-regulated expression of senescence-associated genes. Compared with those from the wild-type plants, the leaves from the atato mutant became chlorotic faster and had greater H2O2 accumulation under dark conditions. Phenotyping of the atato mutant indicated that AtATO suppressed developmental and dark-induced leaf senescence. In addition, atato mutants presented reduced tolerance to oxidative stress, accompanied by changes in the transcription levels of genes associated with the oxidative stress response and increased cell death. Taken together, these results suggest that AtATO functions as a novel modulator of leaf senescence in A. thaliana in response to developmental and stress signals.

records.title: Sex-Stratified Transcriptomic Analysis of Cord-Blood Endothelial Colony-Forming Cells from Pregnancies Complicated by Gestational Diabetes.
records.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and maternal obesity are intrauterine metabolic exposures associated with altered fetal development and increased cardiovascular risk later in life. Increasing evidence suggests that fetal responses to these exposures are sex-dependent; however, the regulatory mechanisms underlying sex-specific vascular programming remain poorly understood. Using purified neonatal endothelial colony-forming cells (ECFCs), a progenitor population of fetal vasculature, we performed a sex-stratified transcriptomic analysis of pregnant mothers classified as lean, overweight, or GDM. Differential expression, pathway enrichment, transcription factor activity inference, kinase network reconstruction, and connectivity mapping were integrated to characterize sex-dependent regulatory responses to maternal metabolic dysfunction. Male and female ECFCs exhibited markedly divergent transcriptomic responses to GDM. Correlation between male and female fold-change estimates was negligible (r = -0.01), and the female-specific signal was not detectable when sex was modeled as a covariate rather than as a stratifying variable. Female GDM-exposed ECFCs demonstrated coordinated enrichment of cell-cycle- and DNA replication-associated pathways together with recurrent prioritization of E2F-family regulators across multiple analytical approaches. In contrast, the male response was comparatively limited and was associated with distinct transcriptional changes, including AKT3-associated pathways. Notably, E2F1 transcript abundance remained relatively stable despite coordinated expression changes among E2F-associated target genes. Independent endothelial transcriptomic datasets, drawn from previously published findings rather than independent reanalysis, provided complementary biological context rather than direct validation, consistent with enrichment of E2F-associated programs in GDM-exposed ECFCs and greater transcriptional responsiveness in female endothelial cells reported elsewhere. These findings indicate that fetal sex is a major determinant of the endothelial progenitor response to maternal metabolic dysfunction and that biologically relevant signals may be obscured in pooled analyses. Our results support the existence of sex-dependent regulatory programs associated with fetal vascular responses to GDM and identify an E2F1-associated regulatory framework as a candidate mechanism warranting further investigation.
records.authors: Adegbaju MS, Babayeju O, Morenikeji OB, Ojurongbe O, Thomas BN.

records.title: Starve, stress, and mate: Activation of the CCAAT-Binding complex overrides sterility of mating-type heterozygous Candida albicans
records.abstract: Sexual reproduction in the human fungal pathogen Candida albicans is typically restricted by a strict genetic lock: the a1-α2 repressor present in standard mating-type heterozygous (MTLa/α) diploid strains, which actively represses mating competency. While severe environmental pressures are known to influence fungal development, the molecular mechanisms that allow cells to override this genetic sterility block remain poorly understood. Here, we identify the highly conserved CCAAT-binding complex (CBC) as the critical developmental hub that integrates environmental stress to unlock mating in heterozygous diploids. By combining proteomic mapping (ChIP-SICAP) and transcriptomics (RNA-Seq) to define the regulatory network of the core CBC subunit Hap5, we demonstrate that CBC hyperactivation completely overrides the a1-α2 repressor. This activation triggers a robust white-to-opaque phenotypic switch and initiates a mating-competence program in MTLa/α strains genetically locked in a sterile state. Crucially, this developmental transition is antagonized by the iron-regulatory partner Hap43, but is strictly dependent on physical interaction at the chromatin level with Cap1, the master regulator of the oxidative stress response. Our findings reveal that the CBC and Cap1 couple metabolic starvation (glucose and iron limitation) and oxidative stress to a core reproductive program, providing a mechanistic basis for how C. albicans bypasses genetic constraints on sexual reproduction to generate genetic diversity under hostile host conditions.
records.authors: van Wijlick L, Martinez de San Vicente K, Sertour N, Rai L, LeibundGut-Landmann S, Bachellier-Bassi S, d'Enfert C.

records.title: Discovery and Deployment of Herbicide Tolerance in Domesticated Pennycress (Thlaspi arvense L.) to Enable Modern Agronomic Integration.
records.abstract: Modern agronomic systems for large-scale oilseed production rely heavily on chemical weed control, presenting a barrier to the adoption of newly domesticated crops that lack herbicide tolerance. Pennycress (Thlaspi arvense L.), a domesticated winter oilseed developed to increase land productivity and support sustainable biofuel production, is highly sensitive to commonly used herbicides targeting acetolactate synthase (ALS) and 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase (HPPD). Here, we report complementary strategies for identifying and deploying herbicide-tolerant alleles in pennycress. ALS inhibitor tolerance was identified through Ethyl methanesulfonate (EMS)-derived chemical mutagenesis, whereas HPPD inhibitor tolerance was explored using a microbial-based rational enzyme design platform as proof of concept. Selected alleles were introduced into advanced germplasm via homology-directed repair (HDR) and evaluated across developmental stages. Plants carrying the P187S mutation in the ALS gene exhibited robust tolerance at both seedling and rosette stages without detectable penalties to growth or seed yield. In contrast, the G419A allele in the HPPD gene conferred tolerance to residual herbicide activity when overexpressed but showed limited efficacy when expressed from its native locus, indicating context-dependent functionality. Collectively, this study demonstrates the feasibility of integrating herbicide tolerance into a newly domesticated oilseed crop and highlights the utility of combining mutagenesis-based discovery, rational enzyme engineering, and precision genome editing to support agronomic compatibility and crop deployment.
records.authors: Howard JM, Tuite M, Mueth T, Varela MC, Lazzaro M, Lieber L, Liu S, Rai KM, Chopra R.

records.title: Deep Phenotyping Reveals Evolution in T cell Phenotype after Hexaviral-specific T cell Infusion Post Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant.
records.abstract: Viral infections are common following hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HCT) and multivirus-specific T cell therapies have been utilized to treat or prevent several viral infections and reactivation. In this study, we evaluated a novel donor-derived hexaviral specific T cell (hVST) product targeting cytomegalovirus (CMV), adenovirus (AdV), Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV), human polyomavirus (BKV), human parainfluenza virus 3 (HPIV3), and human herpes virus 6 (HHV6). This hVST product was tolerated in 5 adult and 9 pediatric patients with toxicities limited to grade I-II cytokine release syndrome (n=2), immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (n=1) and chronic GVHD (n=1). Three months post-treatment, 8/8 evaluable patients with active viral infections achieved a partial or complete response to at least one target virus. Single cell gene expression of hVST products showed CD4+ and CD8+ T cells with effector memory and activation markers (n=4). In evaluable recipients (n=4) following hVST infusion, there was a shift from a naïve and indistinct T cell profile pre infusion to predominantly memory T cell populations in the peripheral blood after hVST infusion (median 70 days). These data suggest that hexaviral specific T cells have potential for preventing and treating multiple viruses in patients post-HCT.

records.title: Bacterial protein function prediction via multimodal deep learning.
records.abstract: Bacterial proteins are specialized with extensive functional diversity for survival in diverse and stressful environments. A significant portion of these proteins remains functionally uncharacterized, limiting our understanding of bacterial survival mechanisms. Hence, we develop Deep Expression STructure (DeepEST), a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts protein function in bacteria by assigning Gene Ontology (GO) terms. DeepEST comprises two modules: a multi-layer perceptron that uses gene expression and gene location, and a protein structure-based module that uses predicted structures and amino acid sequences. Within DeepEST, we integrate these modules through a learnable weighted linear combination and introduce a novel masked loss function to fine-tune the structure-based predictor for bacterial species. These choices are well suited for bacteria, in which functionally related genes frequently colocalize and are cotranscribed within operons, allowing transcription dynamics to serve as informative, condition-dependent signals. We show that DeepEST outperforms existing protein function prediction methods on a 25-species benchmark, relying solely on amino acid sequence or protein structure. Averaged over the 25 species, DeepEST reaches a protein-centric F max of 0.689 and a term-centric micro-AUPRC of 0.756, a relative improvement of 4.4% and 11.6% over the second-best method, the structure-based predictor DeepFRI. Moreover, DeepEST predicts GO terms for unclassified hypothetical proteins across 25 human bacterial pathogens, supporting their experimental characterization. DeepEST bridges organism-specific data integration and structure-based transfer learning, providing a method tailored for bacterial protein function prediction in settings with structural and multi-condition expression data.
records.authors: Miklautz L, Fernandez L, Muzio G, Adamer M, Borgwardt K, Avican K.

records.title: Perspective. Precision Nutrition at a Crossroads: From Biological Prediction to Contextual Implementation.
records.abstract: Precision nutrition has substantially reshaped nutritional science by demonstrating that individuals can respond differently to identical dietary exposures. Advances in genomics, metabolomics, proteomics, microbiome research, wearable technologies, digital health, and artificial intelligence have improved our ability to characterize biological heterogeneity and predict individual responses to diet. However, demonstrating such variability does not necessarily result in nutritional strategies that provide clinically meaningful benefits beyond established evidence-based care. A critical distinction should therefore be made between precision nutrition as a discovery science, which has convincingly established interindividual heterogeneity in dietary responses, and precision nutrition as an intervention science, which must demonstrate meaningful incremental value over dietary approaches already supported by clinical evidence. Despite increasingly sophisticated technologies and predictive models, evidence of consistent improvements in long-term health outcomes, cost-effectiveness, scalability, and equity remains limited. In this Perspective, we argue that precision nutrition has reached a critical crossroads. We distinguish prediction of individual responses, which is only one route to precision nutrition, from treatment-effect heterogeneity, treatment selection and clinical utility. We then propose contextual precision nutrition as a translational framework that integrates biological responsiveness with the behavioral, psychological, social, cultural, economic, and environmental determinants of dietary behavior. Rather than claiming novelty for these components, the framework integrates them into a decision logic that asks whether biological information improves the selection of a dietary strategy beyond routine information and established care, and how that strategy can be delivered and sustained. It complements population-based dietary recommendations by refining their implementation and maximizing adherence and real-world effectiveness. Ultimately, the success of precision nutrition will be determined not by the sophistication of its predictions but by its ability to translate biological knowledge into interventions that are clinically effective, scalable, equitable, and sustainable, thereby improving both individual and population health.
records.authors: Salas-Salvadó J, García-Gavilán J, Ni J, Hernández-Cacho A, Plaza-Diaz J.

records.title: Rapid Colony Identification of Listeria monocytogenes and Other Listeria Species by PCR.
records.abstract: Conventional confirmation of Listeria monocytogenes from food samples involves enrichment, selective plating, and biochemical identification. Colony confirmation is a process that can take 3-5 days. We validated a multiplex PCR assay for the rapid identification of Listeria colonies at the genus level and the specific detection of L. monocytogenes directly from both selective and non-selective agars. The assay targets three markers: hlyA (152 bp, L. monocytogenes-specific), prs (370 bp, Listeria genus-specific), and 16S rRNA (107 bp, internal amplification control). Validation using 226 isolates (117 L. monocytogenes, 44 other Listeria spp., 65 non-Listeria) demonstrated 100% inclusivity and 100% exclusivity. Results were consistent across Oxford, Agar Listeria media, RAPID'L.mono, PALCAM, with isolate identifications confirmed by whole-genome sequencing. Although MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry also provides rapid identification, it requires specialized instrumentation and may not be available in all food microbiology laboratories. In contrast, this PCR assay reduces turnaround time to less than 4 hours and aligns with ISO 16140-6 and Health Canada guidelines for confirmatory testing. Additional evaluation of recently described Listeria species and haemolytic L. innocua strains, presented separately, identified atypical amplification profiles that highlight potential imitation in the broader applicability of the assay.
records.authors: Teixeira JS, Fava N, Flint A, Weedmark K, Iugovaz I, Plante D, Pagotto F.

records.title: The origin of Group B Streptococcus in Australian dogs, cats and cows.
records.abstract: Streptococcus agalactiae, known in human medicine as Group B Streptococcus (GBS), affects numerous animal species, including dairy cattle and companion animals such as dogs and cats. In cattle, where GBS is a common cause of mastitis, host-specialist and host-generalist clades have been detected, whereas data on the origin of companion animal GBS is limited and somewhat contradictory. Here, we analyse a collection of 39 animal GBS isolates from Australia. Based on core genome analysis, the population composition matches the globally observed pattern of occurrence of host-specialist and host-generalist GBS in cattle, represented here by clonal complex 61/67 and sequence type (ST) 23, respectively, and host-generalist GBS in companion animals belonging to multiple sequence types and serotypes. Accessory genome analysis identifies non-exclusive but statistically significant and positive associations between the lactose operon and bovine isolates, and between the scpB gene or antimicrobial resistance genes and companion animal isolates. Proviral regions were detected in all isolates, whereby some phages or phage-inducible chromosomal islands (PICI) were associated with specific sequence types, e.g., phage E2 with ST67 from cattle and phage F2 with ST19 from companion animals. In agreement with results from Europe, our data suggest that GBS infections in dogs and cats are potentially derived from humans and may represent cases of reverse zoonosis.
records.journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases
records.authors: Aubry E, Furfaro LL, Ong XY, Gibson JS, Clark R, Bosward KL, Zadoks RN.

records.title: Multi-copy genomic integration and constitutive expression of high redox potential fungal laccase in Pichia pastoris and its application in dye decolorization.
records.abstract: Fungal high redox potential laccases (HRPLs) are promising biocatalysts for industrial applications, yet large-scale utilization is often bottlenecked by production systems requiring toxic inducers. In this study, a full-length laccase gene and its corresponding cDNA from the white-rot fungus Trametes sanguinea IIP-32 were cloned and characterized. Sequence alignment revealed a conserved Leu-Glu-Ala tripeptide and a Phe residue as the axial ligand to the T1 copper site, confirming the enzyme as an HRPL. To address the bioprocess limitations associated with conventional methanol-inducible systems, the cDNA was integrated into the glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase locus of Pichia pastoris X-33 for constitutive expression. Post-transformational vector amplification yielded multi-copy transformants harboring up to ~5 gene copies. The recombinant laccase (rLAC) expression in batch flask cultivation yielded a volumetric activity of 330 U/L. The rLAC (~58 kDa) exhibited optimal activity at pH 2.2 for 2,2'-azino-bis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) (ABTS) and pH 3.0 for 2,6-dimethoxyphenol. rLAC retained ≥65% initial activity across pH 3.0-6.0 over five days, and exhibited a thermal inactivation temperature (T50) of ~61.43 °C. Kinetic analysis revealed strong affinity for ABTS (Km = 87 μM). The enzyme demonstrated high stability in complex conditions, maintaining ~100% relative activity in 50% (v/v) acetone and showed increased activity (124%) in 5 mM cetyltrimethylammonium bromide. In the presence of 1-hydroxybenzotriazole, rLAC achieved 51-97% decolorization of malachite green, methyl orange and acridine orange. This study demonstrates that the constitutively expressed T. sanguinea IIP-32 HRPL presents a robust and competitive biocatalytic platform for environmental applications.
records.authors: Rawal RS, Suman SK.

records.title: Template-dependent RNA polyadenylation by SARS-CoV-2 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase.
records.abstract: The RNA genome of the human Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) and its mRNAs contain a poly(A) tract at the 3' end of the positive strand that is essential for their replication, translation and stability. Viral RNAs maintain poly(A) tails despite the lack of a cytoplasmic polyadenylation machinery, but the underlying mechanisms remain unknown. Here, we investigated the activity of SARS-CoV-2 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) with synthetic and natural primer-template RNA substrates and discovered that RdRp could extend the 3' end of the RNA primer beyond the template end. This activity depends on the presence of a homopolymeric sequence at the 5' end of the template strand and is probably explained by 'slippage' and reannealing of the primer 3' end to this sequence. In the case of viral minus-strand templates containing a homopolymeric uridylate sequence this activity can ensure the extension of the poly(A) tail in the plus-strand products synthesized by RdRp. We establish the requirements for this activity in vitro and propose that it may have an important role in SARS-CoV-2 replication and mRNA synthesis inside cells.
records.authors: Petushkov I, Kulbachinskiy A.

records.title: ROS/pH/glucose-responsive hydrogel based on 3-aminophenylboronic acid-modified hyaluronic acid and PVA loaded self-assembled ursolic acid/β-acids nanoparticles accelerates MRSA-infected diabetic wound healing.
records.abstract: Bacterial infection severely delays the healing of diabetic wounds. Although hydrogels are widely explored as wound dressings, many lack the multi-responsiveness needed to adapt to the dynamic microenvironment of infected wounds. Herein, we designed a nanocomposite hydrogel that integrates antibacterial and antioxidant functions with responsiveness to ROS, pH, and glucose. First, self-assembled spherical nanoparticles (size 3+ were fabricated. These nanoparticles exhibited potent antioxidant and antibacterial properties, and their assembly mechanism was elucidated through experimental methods and molecular simulations. A triple-responsive hydrogel (UAHPHY) was prepared by 3-aminophenylboronic acid grafting hyaluronic acid and subsequently crosslinking with polyvinyl alcohol. Incorporating the nanoparticles into this three-dimensional porous hydrogel preserved their antibacterial and antioxidant bioactivities. The drug-loaded hydrogel maintained high viability of L929 fibroblasts and HUVECs for 72 h, promoted L929 proliferation, enhanced HUVEC-mediated tube formation, and displayed a low hemolytic rate. In an MRSA-infected diabetic wound model, the hydrogel markedly accelerated wound closure over 14 days. RNA-seq analysis revealed that the resulting UAHPHY hydrogel promoted wound healing might by activating the PI3K/AKT as an associated pathway. Collectively, this microenvironment-adaptive functional hydrogel offers an effective therapeutic strategy for treating MRSA-infected diabetic wounds.
records.authors: Tian B, Xu C, Qiao X, Liang R, Cao J, Hua S, Zhang X, Zhang F, Li S, Ma D, Liu J, Ding L.

records.title: Neutrophil Extracellular Traps Orchestrate Diabetic Podocytopathy Through ROS/NLRP3/Pyroptotic Axis and Gut-Kidney Microbiota Crosstalk.
records.abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a common microvascular complication of diabetes mellitus (DM). Emerging evidence indicates that neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) contribute significantly to podocyte injury in DN:however, the specific underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study demonstrates that NET biomarkers are elevated in diabetic mice and patients with diabetes and positively correlate with DN severity. Treatment with deoxyribonuclease Ⅰ (DNase I), which degrades NETs, partially prevented podocyte dysfunction and renal injury. Mechanistically, NET formation triggered excessive generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), activating the nuclear factor-κB ( NF-κB) signaling pathway and NOD-like receptor protein 3 ( NLRP3) inflammasome, thereby inducing podocyte pyroptosis. Furthermore, increased gut microbiota dysbiosis,characterized by decreased probiotic diversity and increased pathogenic bacteria, was observed in DN mice. DNase I treatment restored probiotic diversity, highlighting a potential interaction between NETs and gut microbiota in DN progression. Collectively, our findings suggest that NETs critically mediate diabetic podocyte dysfunction through ROS-induced activation of NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated pyroptosis and gut microbiota dysbiosis, underscoring the therapeutic potential of targeting NETs in DN treatment.
records.authors: Wang Y, Li G, Chen W, Chang X, Wang P, Tian J, Zhang J, Han H, Zhou X, Liu G, Fan W, Ren X.

records.title: Direction-aware multi-cohort integration reveals biologically coherent but directionally discordant peripheral-blood transcriptomic signatures in major depressive disorder.
records.abstract: Peripheral-blood transcriptomic studies of major depressive disorder (MDD) frequently identify biologically coherent signals but show limited cross-cohort reproducibility. The study applied a direction-aware, multi-cohort framework that distinguished discovery, internal prediction, external association, directional replication and matched cross-omic support. Discovery analyses were conducted in GSE255685, comprising 180 participants with MDD and 99 controls. Differential-expression, functional-enrichment, protein-protein interaction and leakage-controlled machine-learning analyses identified 375 differentially expressed genes, including 112 with higher and 263 with lower expression in MDD. Convergent analyses implicated three principal biological components involving ribosome-associated translation, mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, and chemokine-linked inflammatory or immediate-early stress signalling. Integration of 11 predictive, explainability and network-topology rankings using a rule-based support criterion yielded an exploratory 18-gene discovery-prioritization family. In a held-out test set of 56 participants, logistic-regression and support-vector-machine models each achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.999 and an accuracy of 98.2%, indicating strong within-cohort discrimination but not external clinical validation. External RNA assessment in GSE251778 identified significant candidate-family associations for TRIM56, PPP1R15A, DDIT3 and NFKBIA; however, all four effects were opposite to those observed in discovery, and 15 of 18 genes had opposite-direction estimates across cohorts. Thus, no gene met the prespecified criterion for strict same-direction replication. Among 146 participants with matched RNA, microRNA and DNA-methylation data, 241 microRNA-mRNA associations remained FDR-significant, including 36 directionally coherent inverse pairs involving 10 genes. Five CpG-mRNA associations were significant despite the absence of targeted differential methylation. No candidate-gene stress-response contrast survived multiple-testing correction. These findings show that pathway-level coherence and strong internal classification do not necessarily translate into portable gene-level biomarkers. Direction-aware integration may therefore be essential for distinguishing reproducible molecular features from cohort-dependent peripheral-blood expression states in MDD.
records.authors: Abbas K, Alam M, Usmani N, Habib S.

records.title: Biomimetic mycobacterial dual spatiotemporal targeting induces trained immunity for tuberculosis photothermal immunotherapy and relapse prevention.
records.abstract: BackgroundTuberculosis (TB) treatment remains hindered by three intertwined challenges, drug delivery barriers, immune evasion, and high relapse rates. Despite advances in nanocarriers and immunomodulation, an integrated platform that achieves precise targeting, potent sterilisation, immune remodelling, and durable protection is still lacking.MethodsA biomimetic DNA tetrahedral phototherapy system (TDN + AIE@MM) was constructed using Mycobacterium marinum membrane modification to mimic trained immunity and enable dual spatiotemporal targeting of granulomas and lymph nodes. Through natural membrane ligand recognition, the system delivered payloads to immunosuppressive granulomas and antigen-retarded lymph nodes. Upon NIR-II irradiation, the AIE agent generated local hyperthermia to kill intracellular Mycobacterium tuberculosis and released antigens to activate adaptive and long-term memory immune responses.FindingsTDN + AIE@MM exhibited uniform size, good stability, and preserved membrane proteins. In vitro, it showed superior targeting to H37Ra and macrophages over unmodified controls. Under 808 nm laser irradiation, it achieved >99% killing of extra- and intracellular H37Ra, induced M1 polarisation with pro-inflammatory cytokines (IFN-γ, IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α), and enhanced T-cell proliferation and antigen-specific responses. In vivo, it achieved spatiotemporal dual-targeting to granulomas and lymph nodes, increased CD80+/CD86+ antigen-presenting cells and CD4+ T-cell activation, and reduced lung bacterial load. For immune memory, TRM (CD8+CD69+CD103+) reached 21.8% on day 42, approximately two-fold higher than rifampicin (Rif). In a rechallenge relapse model, the 84-day relapse rate was 16.7% versus 66.7% for Rif, with higher memory B cells and TEM, confirming durable protection.InterpretationThese findings show that TDN + AIE@MM integrates physical sterilisation, immunosuppression reversal, and durable immune memory via dual spatiotemporal targeting, effectively addressing the three core challenges in TB therapy, namely delivery barriers, immune evasion, and relapse risk, and offering a promising strategy for immunotherapy and relapse prevention.FundingPrevention and Control of Emerging and Major Infectious Diseases-National Science and Technology Major Project, the Project Department for Supporting the Research and Innovation Capabilities of Young Teachers in Universities-Pilot Program for Provincial Coordination, the National Natural Science Foundation of China, the Yunnan Provincial Department of Science and Technology-Kunming Medical University Special Projects, the Shenzhen University 2035 Program for Excellent Research, and the Scientific Research Fund of the Yunnan Provincial Department of Education.

records.title: Parental obesity is associated with altered hematopoiesis and impaired viral immunity in offspring.
records.abstract: The prevalence of obesity among adults of childbearing age has tripled worldwide since 1975. Obesity during pregnancy has been linked to impaired neonatal immunity and a higher risk of infections in childhood but the causal mechanisms have not been defined. Using a mouse model of diet-induced obesity, we documented impaired antiviral immunity in the offspring of obese mice, corresponding with reduced cell-mediated immune responses. This included lower frequencies of Tbet+ CD4+ T helper 1 cells and a decrease in cytotoxic CD8+ T cells in the lungs of mice infected with respiratory Sendai virus, and confirmed in spleens from mice infected with LCMV. Consistent with impaired cellular immunity, single-cell transcriptomic analysis of bone marrow revealed altered hematopoiesis in these offspring, with evidence of interferon-induced skewing toward myelopoiesis at the expense of lymphocyte development. Our studies provide an in-depth transcriptomic profile of immune cell progenitors in the bone marrow paired with mature innate and adaptive immune cell populations in lymph nodes at single-cell resolution. Results suggest that compromised immune protection from viral infections in the offspring of obese mice stems from altered lymphocyte development that is influenced by inflammatory interferon signaling in bone marrow.
records.authors: Allene EC, Sundarraj SP, Alibolandi Z, Khojandi N, Piening E, Piening A, Pritchett M, Shornick LP, Teague RM.

records.title: Programming immunity in situ: A new frontier of in vivo cell engineering.
records.abstract: In vivo cell engineering enables the direct programming of immune cells inside patients. Instead of isolating, modifying, and reinfusing cells, therapeutic instructions are delivered directly to selected immune cells through lipid nanoparticles or viral vectors. This approach could facilitate rapid and scalable deployment of varied immune cell therapies across disease contexts. Early clinical studies in oncology and autoimmunity demonstrate increasing technical and clinical feasibility. The next challenge lies in enhancing precision to ensure that vectors reach the target cell type and tissue, deliver the appropriate payload, and produce desired transient or durable activity. Progress in targeting ligands, vector design, biodistribution control, and genome editing is beginning to address these barriers. Ensuring safety against immunogenicity, inflammatory toxicity, off-target editing, and uncontrolled persistence remains a central priority. By mastering these constraints, in vivo engineering could turn endogenous immune cells into therapeutic agents generated directly in the body, expanding cell therapy to diseases refractory to current modalities.
records.authors: Mietz J, Merlotti A, de Fougerolles A, Demaria O, Vivier E.

records.title: Yellow fever virus infection triggers the assembly of compositionally unique and specialised stress granules.
records.abstract: The phase separation of biomolecules into stress granules (SGs) allows the cell to tightly regulate translation activity in response to different stimuli, such as oxidative stress, starvation, or the recognition of non-cellular RNA. Recent reports suggest SGs induced during viral infection may act as a crossroad between the cellular stress response and the activation of the innate immune response. Here, we aimed to dissect the role of SGs in the context of yellow fever virus (YFV) infection. We found that YFV infection with both 17D vaccine and Asibi pathogenic strains resulted in translational shut-off and the formation of SGs at 48 hours post infection (hpi), although viral infection was already apparent at 24 hpi. This delay may be coupled to the ability of the YFV capsid to inhibit SG formation through an interaction with the SG scaffolding protein G3BP1. To elucidate the role of YFV-induced SGs during infection, we inhibited SG assembly using a small-molecule inhibitor as well as siRNA-mediated knockdown of SGs and found that while SG formation does not impact viral replication, silencing of SG scaffolding proteins is associated with increased expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISG). Uncovering the proteome of YFV-induced SGs, our compositional analysis revealed a unique composition, distinct from NaAs-induced SGs, which displayed enrichment in mitochondrial proteins. Further functional analysis revealed that YFV infection is associated with mitochondrial damage and dysfunction, which coincides with formation of virus-induced SGs. Together, we propose that YFV-induced SGs may be involved not only in the modulation of cellular homeostasis but also in influencing mitochondrial functions.
records.authors: Jakob C, Streicher F, Lopez-Nieto M, Eke L, Sow AA, Lee D, Wu J, Taylor JP, Matia-Gonzalez AM, Jouvenet N, Locker N.

records.title: Opportunities and Challenges in Clinical and Preclinical Drug Development for Mycobacterium marinum.
records.abstract: Over recent decades, non-tuberculous mycobacterial infections have increased significantly. Mycobacterium marinum, a widely distributed environmental pathogen, can cause cutaneous and invasive diseases in humans and aquatic animals. Over the past century, our understanding of this pathogen has evolved from early descriptions of "swimming pool granuloma" to recognition of its intracellular lifestyle, granulomatous host responses, and genetic and functional similarities to Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Despite these advances, clinical management remains challenging. Current regimens are largely extrapolated from anti-tuberculous therapy. These regimens show variable efficacy and require prolonged treatment durations, and there is a near-total absence of randomized controlled trials specifically for M. marinum. The emergence of intrinsic and acquired resistance further complicates treatment decisions. On the preclinical front, drug screening using M. marinum as a surrogate model for tuberculosis has increased substantially over the past two decades, yet the translation of candidate compounds to clinical use remains slow. This Review examines the opportunities and persistent challenges in drug development for M. marinum over the past century, tracing the evolutionary trajectory from empirical combination therapy to mechanism‑based drug discovery. It outlines the pathogenic mechanisms of M. marinum, evaluates the resistance profiles of current clinical drugs and treatment regimens under clinical investigation, and introduces promising small‑molecule compounds. We also highlight critical knowledge gaps, including the near-total absence of dedicated clinical trials for M. marinum, the lack of predictive animal models, poorly defined compound targets, and insufficient surveillance of drug resistance. Addressing these gaps is essential to translate preclinical progress into tangible clinical benefit and to close the long‑standing translational gap in this field.
records.authors: Jing QQ, Wang WH, Zhang Q, Xu TY, Wei MY, Shao CL.

records.title: Rapid detection of Peste des Petits ruminants virus using RT-LAMP with FTA card-based sample preservation.
records.abstract: BackgroundPeste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) is an economically important viral disease of small ruminants caused by Small Ruminant Morbillivirus (formerly PPRV), and it is endemic in Pakistan. Flinders Technology Associates (FTA®) cards allow transport of viral samples without the need for cold chain maintenance. This study aimed to evaluate the stability of PPRV RNA on FTA cards at different temperatures and to assess the performance of a newly developed reverse-transcriptase loop-mediated isothermal amplification (RT-LAMP) assay for PPRV detection.MethodsForty-seven clinical samples (swabs, tissues, blood) from sheep and goats suspected of PPR were spotted onto FTA cards. RNA was extracted from all 47 samples using the simplified FTA card-based protocol. RT-LAMP, conventional RT-PCR, and antigen-capture ELISA were performed. The detection limit was evaluated using seven RNA concentrations. Five PPRV-positive samples on FTA cards were stored at various temperatures for up to one year.ResultsAmong 47 samples, positivity rates were 39 (83.0%) by ELISA, 42 (89.4%) by RT-PCR, and 45 (95.7%) by RT-LAMP. The detection limit of RT-LAMP (1.14 × 10⁻³ ng/µl) was tenfold lower than RT-PCR (1.14 × 10⁻² ng/µl). RT-LAMP detected PPRV RNA from FTA cards stored for 1 year at - 20 °C, 8 weeks at 4 °C, 2 months at 15-25 °C, and 3 weeks at 37 °C. At - 20 °C, all five samples remained detectable throughout 12 months. At 4 °C, 3/5 remained positive at 8 weeks. At room temperature, 2/5 remained detectable at 8 weeks. At 37 °C, 3/5 remained detectable at 3 weeks.ConclusionThe developed RT-LAMP assay is more sensitive than conventional RT-PCR and ELISA for PPRV detection. FTA cards provide reliable sample transport and storage at varying temperatures. However, experimental specificity testing using confirmed PPRV-negative samples is recommended before field deployment.
records.authors: Uroog L, Khan SU, Abubakar M, Manzoor S, Ahmad A, Zahur AB, Kabir A.

records.title: Rapid visual detection of Streptococcus agalactiae in tilapia using recombinase polymerase amplification combined with lateral flow strips.
records.abstract: Streptococcus agalactiae critically endangers tilapia farming and causes substantial economic losses to aquaculture. In this study, a rapid and efficient recombinase polymerase amplification-lateral flow strip (RPA-LFS) assay targeting the conserved cfb gene was established for the detection of S. agalactiae. Specific RPA primers were designed for the target region of the cfb gene, and an RPA-LFS system was developed based on primer-probe amplification and colloidal-gold visualization. Conventional PCR was performed in parallel to compare detection performance. The results showed that the F3/R primer pair exhibited the highest specificity under the optimized conditions of 28 °C for 15 min. The lowest detectable DNA concentration was 2.054 × 10-6 ng/uL. Further sample testing showed that the minimum detectable bacterial copy number was 8.55 × 103 copies/µL for RPA-LFS and 8.55 × 104 copies/µL for conventional PCR. These results confirmed that the developed RPA-LFS assay had significantly higher detection sensitivity than conventional PCR and showed strong potential for the early surveillance and effective control of streptococcosis in tilapia farming.
records.authors: Guan M, Si Z, Lin J, Huang S, Yu Y, Li Y, Yi Y, Shi J.

records.title: Functional involvement of AMPK in Lumpy skin disease virus replication and associated cellular stress responses.
records.abstract: Lumpy skin disease virus (LSDV) infection induces extensive cellular stress responses and metabolic reprogramming in host cells. However, the regulatory mechanisms linking these changes to viral replication remain unclear. In this study, MAC-T cells were used as an in vitro infection model to investigate LSDV-induced cellular stress responses and their impact on viral replication. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that LSDV infection activated pathways associated with energy stress, oxidative stress, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, suggesting disruption of cellular energy homeostasis and redox balance. Transmission electron microscopy further demonstrated mitochondrial structural damage in infected cells. Subsequent analyses showed that the ATP/AMP ratio and lactate metabolism decreased during infection, accompanied by elevated mitochondrial calcium levels and excessive reactive oxygen species accumulation. Mechanistically, LSDV infection activated the PERK-eIF2α-ATF4-CHOP and IRE1α-JNK-BECN1 pathways, indicating induction of ER stress-related signaling. Given the role of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) as a central metabolic stress sensor, we further examined its function during LSDV infection. LSDV infection enhanced AMPK activation, as evidenced by increased phosphorylation of Thr172. Inhibition of energy stress, oxidative stress, or ER stress reduced AMPK phosphorylation to varying degrees, suggesting that multiple stress responses collectively contribute to AMPK activation. Furthermore, AMPK inhibition impaired LSDV replication, while downstream analysis revealed that AMPK activation promotes autophagosome formation. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that LSDV-induced cellular stress responses activate AMPK signaling to facilitate viral replication, providing new insights into host metabolic regulation and identifying AMPK as a potential antiviral target.

records.title: Secondary growth in the tomato stem is suppressed by the flowering regulators FUL2 and STM3
records.abstract: Herbaceous eudicot crops such as tomato accumulate substantial amounts of secondary xylem in their stems, particularly in the basal part. As plants progress from the vegetative phase to flowering and fruit development, secondary growth continues to provide mechanical support and facilitate transport. To uncover how secondary growth is regulated in the tomato stem, we used laser capture microdissection RNA-seq to establish tissue-specific transcriptomic profiles. This revealed that key regulators associated with wood formation in poplar are also acting in tomato. Furthermore, we found that the flowering regulators FUL2 and STM3 are substantially expressed in xylem tissue. Subsequent functional analysis identified FUL2 and STM3 as key repressors of secondary growth, with ful2 or stm3 knock-out mutants exhibiting strongly increased secondary growth in older tomato stems. Notably, a higher order mutant in which both ful2 and stm3 were knocked out displays a similar non-additive phenotype, indicating, together with yeast two-hybrid data showing physical interaction, that FUL2 and STM3 act together in a complex. The expression levels of both genes remain low until after the floral transition but strongly rise during subsequent stem development. Transcriptomic analyses in ful2, stm3, and wild-type stems at stages before and after detectable anatomical differences, showed that the FUL2-STM3 complex represses distinct sets of NAC and MYB candidate regulators associated with xylem development. Interestingly, FUL2 and STM3 control these regulators in a stage- and position-dependent way, with candidates showing upregulation only at later stages in mid-height stems being already upregulated at earlier stages in basal stem regions. Our findings provide a tissue-resolved transcriptomic resource for tomato stems and reveal a role for FUL2 and STM3 in limiting secondary xylem accumulation as stem development progresses.
records.authors: Pandey K, Appiah AP, van Velzen R, Zahn IE, Basu E, Angenent GC, Deuss PJ, Bemer M.

records.title: TGF-b/TIF1g signaling restrains CD8+ T cell expansion while preserving cytotoxic competence
records.abstract: Transforming growth factor b exerts complex and often opposing effects on CD8+ T cell biology, yet the molecular mechanisms that distinguish these functions remain poorly understood. Here, we identify TIF1g (TRIM33) as a critical signal threshold regulator that couples TGF b signaling to CD8+ T cell activation and cytotoxic function. In the presence of TGF b, TIF1g deficient CD8+ T cells bypass canonical suppressive signals and acquire a transcriptional program characterized by enhanced activation and proliferation. Despite this hyperactivated state, TIF1g deficient cells fail to acquire full effector function, exhibiting markedly reduced Granzyme B and Perforin expression under TGF b signaling. We confirmed this functional uncoupling in vivo using a secondary Listeria monocytogenes challenge model, in which TIF1g deficient CD8+ T cells underwent robust expansion yet failed to efficiently control bacterial infection because of impaired cytotoxic activity. In a lymphopenic homeostatic proliferation model, TIF1g deficiency disrupted cellular quiescence, leading to excessive proliferation and spontaneous effector differentiation. Consistent with these findings, loss of TIF1g accelerated B16 melanoma growth and was associated with reduced Perforin expression in tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells. Together, these findings identify TIF1g as a key regulator of TGF b mediated CD8+ T cell responses, uncoupling activation from cytotoxic differentiation and revealing a mechanism by which TGF b independently regulates proliferative and effector programs.

records.title: Integrative identification of Tetratostichococcus sp. CCAH0201 (Trebouxiophyceae, Chlorophyta) from Rhizophora leaves in the Can Gio Mangrove Forest, Vietnam
records.abstract: A microalgal strain from Rhizophora leaves in the Can Gio Mangrove Forest, Vietnam, was examined by light microscopy and three molecular markers. Thirty-six cells from 22 micrographs measured 6.68-12.74 by 3.49-4.79 micrometres. Homologous phylogenetic windows comprised 550 nucleotides for SSU rDNA, 711 for ITS and 1,170 for rbcL. CCAH0201, P1 and Tetratostichococcus jenerensis SAG 2138 shared the SSU 3-prime sequence, whereas ITS and rbcL placed CCAH0201 with P1 (SH-aLRT/UFBoot 87/94 and 96.9/99). CCAH0201 differed from P1 at 22/711 ITS and 4/1,170 rbcL sites. Structure-guided ITS2 comparison identified one strict CBC, one two-sided change from a wobble pair and three hemi-CBCs relative to P1. CCAH0201 is thus identified as Tetratostichococcus sp. in a lineage close to P1.

records.title: LAP-TLR2 Axis Drives Inflammatory Pathology during Listeria monocytogenes Gastroenteritis
records.abstract: Listeria monocytogenes (Lm) causes acute gastroenteritis that precedes systemic invasive listeriosis, yet the molecular mechanisms coordinating bacterial virulence with host inflammatory responses during the enteric phase remain poorly understood. We show that Lm-associated gastroenteritis is dose-dependent, and a high infectious dose (~1x10^10 CFU/mouse), reflecting epidemic cases, recapitulates hallmark features of gastroenteritis in a mouse model, including early onset, epithelial erosion, and profound inflammatory cell infiltration. We identify Listeria adhesion protein (LAP), rather than classical virulence factors such as internalin A and listeriolysin O, as the primary mediator of enteric pathology, driving epithelial cell death and neutrophil recruitment. Transcriptomic (mRNA-seq) profiling implicates LAP-driven engagement of the TLR2-MyD88 pathway. Using the HEK-Dual hTLR2 (NF-kB) reporter cell line and TLR2 knockout mice, we show that LAP engages TLR2 to activate TNFalpha; NF-kB signaling and compromises the gut epithelial barrier. Disease severity correlates with myeloid hyperactivation and intestinal ion channel dysregulation, as CD11b-; mice exhibit attenuated diarrhea despite elevated bacterial tissue loads. Finally, studies in MLCK knock-out mice confirm that this myeloid-driven pathology requires MLCK-dependent tight junction opening for paracellular neutrophil migration, which works in concert with LAP-TLR2 signaling during Lm-induced gastroenteritis.

records.title: Deprivation of dietary fiber promotes low-grade neuroinflammation and anxiety-like behavior in mice
records.abstract: Background:  Intestinal health is an important determinant of brain function in that an array of gut perturbants, especially those targeting microbiota, influence behavior. Fermentable dietary fiber nourishes gut microbiota and, consequently, promotes gut health. We hypothesized that depriving mice of fermentable dietary fiber would impact their brain and behavior. Methods: Male C57BL/6J mice were fed standard grain-based chow (GBC), a compositionally defined diet (CDD) which mimics macronutrient content of GBC but lacks fermentable fiber, or CDD supplemented with the fermentable fiber inulin (CDD+INU). Mice were subjected to behavioral testing 6-8 weeks later followed by analysis of the gut brain axis. Results: Relative to GBC-fed mice, CDD-fed mice exhibited low-grade gut inflammation and a reduction in open-field center exploration, signaling heightened anxiety-like behavior. CDD+INU fully reversed these abnormalities arguing they were a consequence of fiber deprivation. Analysis of the gut microbiome and serum metabolome showed that CDD+INU increased oxidative phosphorylation and immune suppressive metabolites. Flow cytometric and transcriptomic analyses of the brain revealed an array of pro-inflammatory alterations in myeloid cells, CD4+ T-cells, microglia and astrocytes in mice fed CDD but not CDD+INU. Most notably, microglia and astrocytes from mice fed CDD, but not CDD+INU, displayed reduced mitochondrial respiration and greater glycolytic activity. CDD, but not CDD+INU consumption also reduced the abundance of oligodendrocytes and neurons, and increased hippocampal pro-inflammatory gene expression. Conclusions: Deprivation of fermentable fiber results in coordinated changes in brain immune composition and glial metabolic state that is associated with increased anxiety-like behavior.

records.title: Aging, HIV Status, and Sex Differentially Influence Antiretroviral Therapy Disposition Pathways in Rectosigmoid Tissue and Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells
records.abstract: People living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) are increasingly surviving into older age due to the effectiveness of antiretroviral (ARV) therapy (ART), creating a growing population in whom age-related changes may influence treatment outcomes. Although aging is known to affect drug disposition, the molecular mechanisms by which aging alters ARV pharmacology remain incompletely understood, particularly within tissue compartments, including the rectosigmoid region of the colon, that serve as sites of HIV transmission and persistence. To address this knowledge gap, we used proteomics by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) to evaluate the impact of age and HIV status on proteins and pathways relevant to ARV disposition in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) and rectosigmoid colon tissue obtained from young (18-50) HIV-seronegative adults, older (65-80) HIV-seronegative adults, and older virally suppressed people living with HIV. We found that aging and HIV infection differentially influenced proteins predominantly within nucleos(t)ide reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) pathways, in rectosigmoid tissue and PBMC. HIV-associated effects to the proteome were more prominent in PBMC, whereas aging produced broader alterations in ARV disposition-related proteins in rectosigmoid tissue, including proteins involved in drug transport, intracellular drug activation, dephosphorylation, and nucleotide homeostasis. Several age-associated changes were further influenced by biologic sex, suggesting that aging may not affect ARV disposition uniformly across populations. To place these findings within a broader context, pathway analyses were performed that identified extensive tissue-specific remodeling associated with aging and HIV infection involving drug disposition, immune regulation, cellular metabolism, and disease-related pathways. Notably, aging was associated with alterations in pathways relevant to nucleotide metabolism and gastrointestinal tissue function, suggesting that processes beyond traditional drug transport and metabolism pathways may contribute to variability in ARV disposition with advancing age. Together, these findings identify aging as an important modifier of pathways that regulate ARV disposition within compartments relevant to HIV transmission and persistence. While the clinical consequences of our findings are unknown, these data provide a mechanistic foundation for future studies investigating whether age-associated changes influence the effectiveness of ART and HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis in older adults.

records.title: O Marco de Acessibilidade e Equidade Genômica (GEAF): Um Marco Dimensionalmente Consistente para a Modelagem da Acessibilidade Financeira e da Equidade em Terapias Genômicas e Regenerativas
records.abstract: Contexto Os avanços na edição gênica baseada em CRISPR e nos modelos de embriões derivados de células-tronco criaram oportunidades biomédicas substanciais, acompanhadas de preocupações éticas e distributivas significativas. As terapias genômicas e regenerativas personalizadas aprovadas nos Estados Unidos até o momento desta redação têm preços de tabela que variam de aproximadamente $2.2 milhões (Casgevy) a $4.25 milhões (Lenmeldy), com vários outros produtos aprovados com preços entre esses valores (p. ex., Lyfgenia, $3.1 milhões; Hemgenix, $3.5 milhões). Isso levanta a questão de como a acessibilidade econômica, o acesso, a conformidade ética e a desigualdade distributiva podem ser representados conjuntamente em um único índice matematicamente coerente, que apoie a análise de políticas. Métodos Auditamos um índice composto proposto anteriormente, o Genomic Equity Accessibility Framework (GEAF = ((A × E) − (C × I)) / (P + R) × 100), e identificamos uma incompatibilidade dimensional entre seus termos, uma faixa de saída ilimitada e não interpretável de forma independente, e entradas de cenários inconsistentes com as estimativas de custo citadas em outras partes do mesmo manuscrito. Reconstruímos o GEAF como um composto ponderado, normalizado e limitado (0–100) de seis componentes adimensionais – acesso, conformidade ética, acessibilidade econômica, equidade (desigualdade inversa), força das políticas e eficiência da pesquisa –, derivado por meio da teoria da utilidade multiatributo. Testamos a fórmula reconstruída em casos algébricos extremos, aplicamo-la a sete cenários ilustrativos reespecificados, cujas entradas de custo estão ancoradas na literatura citada sobre preços de tabela, e realizamos análises de sensibilidade univariadas, bivariadas e probabilísticas de Monte Carlo (10,000 iterações). Resultados O índice reconstruído (GEAF′) é limitado em [0,100], monotônico em cada componente e comporta-se de maneira consistente nos extremos algébricos. Nos sete cenários ilustrativos, o GEAF′ variou de 27.9 (sem intervenção de equidade, custo ao preço de tabela) a 86.5 (cenário totalmente otimizado de precificação escalonada e políticas). A análise de sensibilidade univariada identificou o custo (C) e o fator de desigualdade (I) como os dois maiores determinantes de parâmetro único do índice em condições de referência, seguidos da conformidade ética (E). A simulação de Monte Carlo (10,000 iterações por regime), que propagou pressupostos declarados e não empíricos de incerteza dos parâmetros, produziu uma média de 32.6 no cenário de referência (intervalo de 90 %, percentis 5 a 95, aproximadamente 22.9–42.9) e uma média de 72.4 no cenário de intervenção de equidade (intervalo de 90 % de aproximadamente 62.9–81.1), sem sobreposição entre as duas distribuições simuladas. Conclusões O GEAF′ oferece uma forma transparente, reprodutível e dimensionalmente coerente de combinar acessibilidade econômica, acesso, conformidade ética e equidade distributiva em um único índice comparativo para cenários de políticas de terapias genômicas e regenerativas. Ele é apresentado como uma estrutura conceitual e metodológica candidata, e não como uma ferramenta preditiva ou clínica validada empiricamente; as afirmações quantitativas sobre reduções de custo no mundo real foram removidas, a menos que diretamente respaldadas por evidências citadas. A calibração empírica prospectiva com dados reais de acesso, preços e resultados de políticas é identificada como um passo seguinte necessário antes que o GEAF′ seja usado na avaliação de tecnologias em saúde ou em decisões de alocação de recursos.   Versão em Inglês: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0359782

records.title: Una tradu El Marco de Accesibilidad y Equidad Genómica (GEAF): un marco dimensionalmente coherente para modelar la asequibilidad y la equidad en las terapias genómicas y regenerativas
records.abstract: Background:  Advances in CRISPR-based gene editing and embryo models derived from mother cells have created important biomedical opportunities, along with considerable ethical and distributive concerns. Personalized genomic and regenerative therapies approved in the United States at the time of writing this work have list prices ranging from approximately $2.2 million (Casgevy) to $4.25 million (Lenmeldy), with several other approved products whose price falls between these figures (e.g., Lyfgenia, $3.1 million; Hemgenix, $3.5 million). It poses the question of how to jointly represent inequality, accessibility, ethical compliance and distributive inequality in a single mathematically coherent index that serves as support for policy analysis. Methods We audited a previously proposed composite index, the Genomic Equity Accessibility Framework (GEAF = ((A × E) − (C × I)) / (P + R) × 100), and we identified a dimensional incompatibility between its terms, an output range not allocated and not independently interpretable, and input data from scenarios incoherent with cost estimates cited elsewhere in the same manuscript. We reconstructed the GEAF as a weighted, normalized and scored (0–100) composite of six dimensionless components – accessibility, ethical compliance, equality, equity (inverse inequality), policy solidity and research efficiency –, derived through multi-attribute utility theory. We add the reconstructed formula to tests with extreme algebraic cases, we apply it to a series of re-specified illustrative scenarios whose cost data is anclan in the literature cited on list prices, and we perform univariant, bivariant and probabilistic Monte Carlo sensitivity analyzes (10,000 iterations). Results The reconstructed index (GEAF′) is based on [0,100], is monotonous in each component and behaves coherently at algebraic extremes. In several illustrative scenarios, the GEAF′ oscillated between 27.9 (without equity intervention, cost at list price) and 86.5 (fully optimized scaled price and policy scenario). The univariate sensitivity analysis identified the cost (C) and the inequality factor (I) as the biggest determinants of a single index parameter in reference conditions, followed by ethical compliance (E). The Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 iterations per regime), which propagates stated and empirical assumptions of parameter uncertainty, produces an average of 32.6 in the reference scenario (90% range, 5th to 95th percentiles, approximately 22.9–42.9) and an average of 72.4 in the equity intervention scenario (90% range of approximately 62.9–81.1), without undermining between the simulated distributions. Conclusions GEAF′ provides a transparent, reproducible and dimensionally coherent way to combine equity, accessibility, ethical compliance and distributive equity in a single comparative index for policy scenarios on genomic and regenerative therapies. It is presented as a candidate conceptual and methodological framework, not as an empirically validated predictive or clinical tool; Quantitative statements about cost reductions in the real world have been eliminated, unless they are supported directly by cited evidence. The prospective empirical calibration with real data on accessibility, prices and policy results is identified as a necessary next step before the GEAF′ is used in the evaluation of health technologies or in resource allocation decisions. Versão em inglês: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0359782

records.title: Transcriptome-Proteome Decoupling in Smoking-Induced Cardiovascular Disease: A Multi-Omics Mendelian Randomization Study
records.abstract: Abstract  Objective: Smoking is a major modifiable cardiovascular risk factor. We aimed to dissect the causal relationships between multiple smoking phenotypes and cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), and critically evaluate whether smoking-induced molecular alterations propagate linearly from DNA methylation to gene expression and circulating proteins. Methods: We performed bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) for 11 smoking behaviors and 12 CVD outcomes, and applied multivariable MR (MVMR) to estimate direct effects independent of cardiometabolic confounders. To investigate molecular mechanisms, we integrated summary-data-based MR (SMR) with blood cis- expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) data and performed Bayesian colocalization between smoking-associated DNA methylation (mQTL), gene expression, and plasma/cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) protein QTL (pQTL). Finally, we systematically interrogated the cross-platform coverage of candidate proteins across major proteomic datasets. Results: Genetically proxied "ever smoked" and "cigarettes per day" significantly increased the risk of CAD, PAD, and HF, with direct effects persisting independent of cardiometabolic confounders. eQTL-SMR identified 640 genes shared across CVD subtypes. However, this cascade was not linear. While 11 CpG-gene pairs showed robust mQTL-eQTL colocalization, the classical smoking marker AHRR showed a complete absence of colocalization (PP.H3 = 0.94–1.00), indicating that epigenetic imprints reflect exposure rather than causal mediators. A second layer of systemic decoupling was observed between transcription and the proteome. Among the seven candidate genes with robust mQTL-eQTL colocalization, six were entirely absent from the SomaLogic 7k official menu. For the sole covered gene, SPTLC2, eQTL-pQTL colocalization was negative in both plasma (PP.H1 = 0.65) and CSF (minimum P = 4.96×10⁻⁴). In parallel, pQTL MR independently identified 18 subtype-specific causal proteins (e.g., ABO for DVT/PE, CTF1/VPS29 for CAD) that were not direct downstream effectors of smoking. Conclusion: Smoking behaviours exert heterogeneous effects on CVDs through shared upstream transcriptional programs with subtype-specific downstream protein effectors. However, this process is characterized by multi-layer decoupling—driven by the systematic exclusion of intracellular regulatory proteins from current proteomic platforms. Our findings redefine the molecular architecture of smoking-induced CVD and highlight the necessity of distinguishing molecular enrichment from shared causal continuity in multi-omic MR studies.
records.authors: Ying S, Chen Q, Liu X, Zhang P, Fu N, Liu Y.

records.title: Functional convergence of soil fungal communities with biotic homogenization in a biodiversity hotspot
records.abstract: Abstract    Aims  Soil fungal communities playcritical roles in ecosystem functions. However, soil fungal communities are becoming homogenization under human disturbance although the functional consequences remain poorly understood.  Methods  Here we investigated soil fungal community composition, diversity, and functional guild structure acrossagroecosystems, grasslands, and forests in four isolated valleys of the Mountains of Southwest China, a globally recognized biodiversity hotspot. We characterized the patterns of biotic homogenization and the relative abundance of functional guilds. Community assembly processes were inferred using the iCAMP framework.  Results  Agroecosystems harbored 30.3% higher phylotype richness than grasslands but exhibited significantly lower β-diversity (3.25% and 4.71% lower than grasslands and forests, respectively) and higher biotic homogenization degrees. Agroecosystems hosted more abundant plant pathogens than forests and grasslands (by 361.5% and 354.0%, respectively) and more saprotrophs (by 91.3% and 72.8%), but substantially fewer ectomycorrhizal fungi (93.3% lower than forests). Soil fungal communities in agroecosystems showed the highest importance of homogeneous selection, whereas heterogeneous selection was lowest, consistent with the homogenization pattern. The richness and abundance of plant pathogens and saprotrophs increased whereas those of ectomycorrhizal fungi decreased with biotic homogenization. Bin-level assembly analysis revealed that the assembly processes were associated with functional guilds. Soil total phosphorus, nitrate, and C:P ratio were key environmental drivers of homogenization and functional guild shifts.  Conclusions  These findings demonstrate that agricultural activities drive fungal community convergence through environmental filtering, with cascading effects on functional guilds that may compromise ecosystem multifunctionality and long-term soil health.
records.authors: Yan B, Sun Y, Li L, He G, Zhang M, Fang H, Shi L.

records.title: Human parvovirus B19-associated Evans syndrome with fulminant hematologic onset mimicking thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura: a case report
records.abstract: Abstract    Background  Human parvovirus B19 infection rarely presents with severe bicytopenia and multiorgan involvement. Acute presentations with fulminant immune-mediated cytopenia closely mimic severe thrombotic microangiopathies (TMAs) like thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP), making early diagnosis highly challenging.  Case presentation  A 65-year-old male was admitted with hematemesis and melena. Suspecting thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura or other thrombotic microangiopathies, emergency plasma exchange and continuous renal replacement therapy were immediately initiated. Crucially, pre-treatment samples for ADAMTS13 and metagenomic next-generation sequencing were collected prior to these interventions. Following rapid clinical deterioration requiring endotracheal intubation, intravenous methylprednisolone was initiated. Initial platelet and hemoglobin levels were 3×10⁹/L and 90 g/L, which subsequently plummeted to nadirs of 1×10⁹/L and 46 g/L. Immunohematological tests identified immune-mediated cytopenia: a weakly positive direct antiglobulin test for IgG, positive C3, and spherocytes. ADAMTS13 activity was normal. The pre-treatment metagenomic next-generation sequencing exclusively detected parvovirus B19 (21632 reads), shifting the diagnostic focus to B19-associated Evans syndrome. Following comprehensive therapy, the patient demonstrated a progressive regenerative erythropoietic response. He was successfully extubated, with platelets recovering to 174×10⁹/L and hemoglobin to 86-87 g/L.  Conclusions  Parvovirus B19 should be actively considered in adults presenting with fulminant immune-mediated bicytopenia mimicking TTP. Procuring critical etiological and immunohematological samples prior to plasma exchange is essential to establish an accurate final diagnosis.
records.authors: Xie Z, Zou X, Zhang L.

records.title: From Access to Appropriate Use: Reimbursement Design for Pathogen Nucleic Acid Diagnostics across Six Health Systems, 2014–2026
records.abstract: Abstract  Background  Pathogen nucleic acid diagnostics answer questions that culture, antigen detection and serology cannot answer within the treatment-decision window — slow-growing and fastidious organisms, paucibacillary disease, and genotypic resistance — yet are persistently reimbursed below that value; we ask whether that mismatch is transitional or structural. Methods  We compare six health systems (China, the United States, Germany, France, England, Japan) under a most-different-systems design, tracing three index technology classes defined by target scope — single-pathogen detection with or without a resistance-conferring variant; multi-pathogen targeted detection by multiplex or isothermal amplification or panel enrichment with sequencing; and untargeted metagenomic sequencing of the primary specimen — through a three-gates framework (approval, price assignment, coverage) using primary policy documents, 2014–2026, under confidence-tiered verification. Results  All six systems impose the same three gates, but the binding gate differs: China's price-item gate is being removed by the 2026 national price-item guideline (trial), which standardises item definitions but not price levels, so the binding constraint migrates to insurance listing rather than disappearing; the United States binds at clinical-utility evidence; Germany at coverage. A "double squeeze" of inpatient diagnosis-related-group bundling and outpatient price compression (Medicare's ratcheted PAMA repricing, repeatedly deferred; China's volume-based procurement cuts of 47–77%; Japan's FY2014 256-item fee cut) suppresses adoption of cost-effective tests. Five innovation carve-outs echoing the coverage-with-evidence-development concept underperform for diagnostics: Germany's inpatient innovation channel (NUB) integrated 105 of more than 3,400 methods into regular payment in 2005–2020 (single peer-reviewed source); Medicare's molecular-panel coverage policy excludes metagenomic sequencing from its scope, with no affirmative coverage elsewhere. Regulatory review itself ranges from months (Japan's targets; US 510(k) goals) to multiple years (China's Class III elapsed times; EU notified-body backlogs). For metagenomic sequencing, Gate 1 is a laboratory-accreditation regime rather than product review, and the longest lags sit at the approval–payment interface (median 5.7 years from FDA authorisation to nominal Medicare coverage in a 2016–2019 cohort; diagnostics' lags were shorter). Conclusion  The reimbursement gap is structural and is best explained by the externalisation of diagnostic value across budget silos; closing it requires diagnostic-specific payment design coupled to prescriber competency in test selection.

records.title: A history of type 2 diabetes results in immune dysregulation and failure to contain a fatal fungal infection
records.abstract: Abstract    Glucose metabolism enables antimicrobial defences, but it also contributes to pathogen proliferation and immune evasion. A key disease of glucose metabolism, type 2 diabetes (T2D), leads to worse outcomes of  Candida albicans  infections with poorly understood mechanisms. Here we used genetic and dietary animal models of T2D and show that, following bloodstream  C. albicans  infection, T2D animals develop strongly exacerbated disease across several T2D aetiologies. Obesity alone (without overt hyperglycaemia) is sufficient to worsen  C. albicans  disease, but it does not fully recapitulate the severity in T2D hosts that are both obese and overtly hyperglycaemic. Mechanistic analyses showed that a convergence of pathogen and host factors leads to poor outcomes in T2D.  C. albicans  exploits poor host glycaemic control through activation of a transcriptional program for glucose utilisation to drive pathogen proliferation. This, combined with dysregulated immunity characterised by increased pro-inflammatory responses and reduced interferon and NK cell signatures, leads to host failure in restricting fungal growth. We further show that life-long metabolic dysregulation, rather than blood glucose levels at infection, drives poor infection outcomes. Our study illuminates host and pathogen mechanisms leading to worse fungal infection in T2D, provides a rich multi-omics resource for understanding fungal infection in metabolic diseases, and suggests that long-term control of metabolic dysregulation, rather than acute lowering of glucose, is essential for improving survival.
