records.title: Cytomegalovirus and cancer stem cells: a hidden alliance in tumor progression and therapy resistance.
records.abstract: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) is a widely spread β-herpesvirus that can establish life-long latency in the human host and remains asymptomatic in healthy immunocompetent hosts. In immunocompromised populations, such as transplant recipients, HIV/AIDS patients, and cancer patients, CMV presents an opportunity to reactivate and influence disease progression. There is a growing, but still contested, body of evidence suggesting that while CMV is not a classical oncogenic virus, it may act as an oncomodulatory virus, exerting an indirect impact on tumor biology. CMV DNA, RNA, or proteins have been detected in tumors such as glioblastoma, breast, colorectal, and pancreatic cancers in several studies, although other studies using comparable or more sensitive assays have failed to detect the virus in the same tumor types, so this association should not be regarded as established. In addition, CMV presence in tumor tissues is associated with immune suppression, therapy resistance, angiogenesis, and inflammation-all indicators of hallmark cancer progression. Of particular interest related to CMV in the context of cancer is its potential relationship with cancer stem cells (CSCs), a rare cell subpopulation of tumor cells, although a potent subpopulation for self-renewal, metastasis, and resistance to conventional cancer therapies. CMV has been shown to modulate numerous signaling pathways (Wnt/β-catenin, PI3K/Akt, Notch, and This review summarizes emerging connections between CMV infection and CSC biology, highlighting the ability of the virus to alter tumor behavior through effects on pluripotent transcription factors (i.e., Oct4, Sox2, Nanog), modulation of cytokine networks (i.e., IL-10, TGF-β), and inducing immune escape mechanisms. As we develop a better understanding of the CMV-CSC connection, this may inform new therapeutic strategies that utilize antiviral approaches to work alongside contemporary CSC-targeted therapies, providing relief in instances of drug resistance, relapse, and poor prognosis in CMV-positive tumors. We also critically appraise the strength and consistency of the underlying evidence, propose reasons for conflicting findings, and put forward a context-dependent, bidirectional model of CMV-CSC interaction together with testable predictions.

records.title: Experimental evolution reveals temporally opposing roles for Csu pili during  Acinetobacter baumannii  respiratory infection
records.abstract: Multidrug-resistant (MDR)  Acinetobacter baumannii is an opportunistic pathogen responsible for a wide range of infections, including ventilator-associated pneumonia, bloodstream infections, and urinary tract infections. Most studies investigating  A. baumannii pulmonary pathogenesis rely on acute pneumonia models that use high bacterial inocula and do not recapitulate the prolonged infections observed in some patients. Recently, our laboratory developed a murine model of chronic pulmonary infection that enabled the identification of virulence factors specifically required for long-term lung persistence. To investigate how  A. baumannii adapts during chronic pulmonary infection, we performed an experimental evolution study using this model. This approach revealed an unexpected role for the archaic chaperone-usher (Csu) pili in  A. baumannii pathogenesis. At early time points, Csu expression reduced bacterial burdens in both acute and chronic pneumonia models, an effect associated with enhanced host inflammatory responses. In contrast, at later stages of chronic infection, Csu promoted bacterial persistence, potentially by facilitating adhesion to pulmonary epithelial cells. These opposing effects were conserved across two distinct  A. baumannii clinical isolates. We also found that Csu contributes to bacterial colonization in a catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI) model in a strain-dependent manner. Together, these findings reveal an infection-stage-dependent role for Csu in  A. baumannii pathogenesis, demonstrating that a bacterial surface structure can impair early colonization while promoting long-term persistence.  Author summary  Understanding how bacterial pathogens establish and maintain infections requires identifying the factors that promote their survival within the host. Currently, most experimental models of  Acinetobacter baumannii infections focus on acute infections, potentially overlooking bacterial factors that are required for prolonged infections. In this study, we investigated how  A. baumannii , a major cause of hospital-acquired infections, adapts to the lung environment during chronic infection. Using experimental evolution, we identified a novel role for Csu pili, surface structures traditionally associated with biofilm formation. Rather than promoting bacterial fitness throughout infection, Csu pili exhibited opposing effects depending on disease progression. Their expression was detrimental to bacterial fitness during early infection, a phenotype associated with increased host inflammatory responses, but became advantageous during prolonged infection, potentially by enhancing bacterial association with respiratory epithelial cells. Importantly, these opposing effects were observed in distinct clinical isolates, suggesting that this phenomenon is not restricted to a particular bacterial strain. Our findings highlight how the contribution of individual virulence factors can change over the course of infection and underscore the importance of considering infection duration when studying bacterial pathogenesis.
records.authors: Cavinato L, Jackson-Litteken CD, Nawrocki EM, Dubey N, Tai C, Janet-Maitre M, Cooper VS, Stallings CL, Di Venanzio G, Feldman MF.

records.title: Filament assembly confers the mechanical resilience of the IFI16 restrictosome
records.abstract: Interferon-inducible protein 16 (IFI16) is a mammalian innate immune sensor composed of a filament-forming pyrin domain (PYD) followed by tandem HIN200 domains that bind nucleic acids. First recognized as a major regulator of inflammatory responses against cytosolic double-stranded (ds)DNA, IFI16 filaments have been implicated in several key mechanical processes involving both host and pathogens, including viral replication restriction, latency regulation, replication-stress responses, and DNA-damage responses. Moreover, IFI16 filaments are ultra-stable, a key trait believed to drive its autoantigenicity. Although recent studies reported that IFI16 undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) via disordered linkers and multivalent protein•dsDNA interactions, whether such a metastable entity provides a framework for the mechanical activities of IFI16 remains unknown. Here, we show that PYD-driven filament assembly confers the mechanical stability of IFI16 condensates by compacting DNA into ultra-stable tangles capable of withstanding forces sufficient to induce duplex deformation. By contrast, HIN200•dsDNA complexes are much more sensitive to ionic perturbation, DNA pretension, and mechanical interference. Together, we demonstrate that filament assembly allows IFI16 to act as a mechano-sensitive restrictor.
records.authors: Stallings CM, Garg A, Sohn J.

records.title: JAK1/2 Inhibition Restores Tissue Integrity by Rewiring Type 1/2 Immunity Toward Targetable IL-17 Responses
records.abstract: Effective immune responses require coordinated communication between immune and epithelial cells to eliminate pathogens while limiting tissue damage. Disruption of this balance drives chronic inflammation and progressive tissue destruction. The Janus kinase (JAK) pathway coordinates cytokine signaling across these compartments and has emerged as a therapeutic target in inflammatory diseases. However, the consequences of JAK inhibition within a complex inflammatory environment remain incompletely understood. Here, we dissect the molecular, cellular, immunological and phenotypical effects of topical JAK1/2 inhibition in a chronic model of tissue-destructive skin inflammation driven by barrier dysfunction and bacterial superinfection. Single-cell transcriptomics and functional profiling revealed that JAK1/2 blockade selectively suppressed pathogenic CD8⁺ T cells and their IFN-γ production while shifting Th2-polarized CD4⁺ T cells toward a Th17 phenotype, preserving type 3 immunity consisting of IL-17A-producing γδ-T cells and neutrophil responses. This immune rebalancing occurs rapidly and concomitantly with the restoration of epithelial barrier integrity through tight junction reinforcement, followed by recovery of antimicrobial defenses and reduced bacterial burden. Combination of JAK1/2 and IL-17A blockade further improved tissue homeostasis by targeting residual type 3-driven pathology. Thus, JAK1/2 inhibition acts as selective immunomodulator rather than a broad immunosuppressant, targeting pathogenic type 1/2 responses while preserving type-3-associated antimicrobial defense programs. These findings reveal how JAK1/2 inhibition coordinates immune rebalancing with epithelial repair and support its therapeutic potential in chronic type 1/2-driven inflammatory disease, while identifying residual IL-17A-mediated pathology as a target for combination therapy.
records.authors: Jin R, Strobl K, Artner-Gent L, Tuechler J, Gladkova M, Mann U, Farlik M, Barozzi I, Sibilia M, Bauer T.

records.title: XRN1-dependent RNA homeostasis regulates hepatitis D virus
records.abstract: ABSTRACT  Hepatitis delta virus (HDV) infection causes the most severe form of viral hepatitis, yet the host mechanisms restricting HDV replication remain poorly understood. Although HDV infection activates the MDA5-LGP2 pathway and induces robust interferon (IFN) responses, these antiviral programs have limited impact on viral replication. Here we identify the 5’-3’ exoribonuclease XRN1 as a key regulator of HDV infection. Loss of XRN1 in hepatoma cells increased double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) levels and induced interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs), including MDA5 and MAVS, and limited HDV infection. XRN1 deficiency enhanced ADAR1-mediated RNA editing, revealing a dynamic interplay between endogenous dsRNA metabolism and antiviral sensing. Inhibition of type I IFN signaling restored MDA5 expression and rescued HDV replication in XRN1-deficient cells. To identify the downstream effectors responsible for this restriction, we combined transcriptomic profiling with functional siRNA screening and identified DUSP5 and SIRPA as previously unrecognized ISGs with anti-HDV activity. Together, our findings establish XRN1 as a gatekeeper of dsRNA homeostasis that controls HDV replication through innate immune activation and reveals host antiviral effectors that may provide therapeutic opportunities for chronic hepatitis D. Graphical abstract  Activation of dsRNA sensing pathway following XRN1 depletion upregulates IFN production and IFN downstream pathways, leading to increases in host defenses to HDV infection. In addition XRN1 depletion increases ADAR1 expression, which increases L-HDAg levels and suppresses HDV replication. Image created in BioRender :  https://BioRender.com/t73u45i AUTHOR SUMMARY  Hepatitis D virus causes the most severe form of viral hepatitis, yet how our cells defend against this virus remains poorly understood. Although infection triggers strong immune responses, their effects on viral replication are limited. In this study, we identified XRN1, an enzyme involved in cellular RNA degradation, as an important regulator of hepatitis D virus infection. We found that loss of XRN1 causes the accumulation of double-stranded RNA, activates antiviral immune responses, and suppresses viral replication. We also observed increased RNA editing, highlighting the connection between RNA metabolism and antiviral immunity. Furthermore, we identified two previously unrecognized antiviral factors, DUSP5 and SIRPA, that contribute to controlling viral infection. Our findings reveal how cellular RNA degradation regulates antiviral defenses and suggest potential new approaches to treating chronic hepatitis D.
records.authors: Tsukuda S, Boutasbih M, Wing PA, Fedorov A, Zhu X, Rehwinkel J, Balfe P, McKeating JA.

records.title: Integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analysis identifies BCHE and FOXM1 as oxidative-stress markers linked to prognosis and immune-microenvironment remodeling in nasopharyngeal carcinoma
records.abstract: Abstract  Background  Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), an Epstein–Barr virus–associated head-and-neck cancer, typically carries dense yet dysfunctional immune infiltrates. Oxidative stress shapes both tumor progression and immune escape; whether oxidative-stress genes (OSGs) carry prognostic and immunological information in NPC has not been examined at bulk and single-cell resolution. Methods  Three NPC microarray cohorts (GSE12452, GSE53819 and GSE64634) were integrated using robust rank aggregation and ComBat-corrected limma, and genes identified by both strategies were intersected with 1,398 OSGs from GeneCards. Candidate prognostic OSGs were tested in the RNA-seq cohort GSE102349 (n = 88) using univariate Cox, LASSO and multivariable Cox regression together with Kaplan–Meier analysis, time-dependent ROC curves and a nomogram. We further applied Hallmark gene-set enrichment, CIBERSORT, an immune-cell LASSO signature, checkpoint correlation, ssGSEA and drug-sensitivity prediction, and replicated the findings in three independent cohorts and a single-cell RNA-seq dataset (GSE150430), where in-silico knockout, transcription-factor regulon, trajectory and cell–cell communication analyses were also performed. Results  Of 722 consistent differentially expressed genes, 67 were NPC-specific OSGs. BCHE emerged as the consistently prognostic OSG (univariate HR = 1.85, P = 0.009; optimal-cutoff Kaplan–Meier P = 0.003, high-versus-low HR = 4.1; the sole LASSO-retained multivariable term). FOXM1 failed multivariable retention but still defined a high-risk subgroup by optimal-cutoff Kaplan–Meier (P = 0.012, HR = 4.4). Enrichment analysis tied FOXM1 to E2F/G2M/MYC proliferation programs and BCHE to epithelial–mesenchymal-transition and Wnt signaling; both genes were inversely related to interferon and complement pathways. A ten-cell immune signature and checkpoint correlations outlined an immune-suppressed compartment. At single-cell level, both genes localized to malignant cells within a shared early malignant state, and malignant–immune crosstalk was dominated by MIF- and galectin-mediated signaling. Conclusion  Convergent bulk and single-cell evidence supports BCHE as a prognostic OS marker for risk stratification and FOXM1 as a proliferation-linked marker of malignant state in NPC. Both track with immune-microenvironment remodeling and await experimental and prospective validation.

records.title: Staged sternal distraction for early thoracic expansion in Shwachman-Diamond syndrome.
records.abstract: Shwachman-Diamond syndrome (SDS) is a rare inherited multisystem disorder with variable skeletal involvement; severe neonatal thoracic dystrophy is uncommon but can cause thoracic insufficiency and mimic Jeune syndrome. We report staged sternal distraction in a 5-month-old infant with a severely constricted thorax, pulmonary hypoplasia, refractory pulmonary hypertension, tracheostomy-dependent respiratory failure and an iatrogenic posterior tracheal wall injury. Subsequent trio long-read genome sequencing identified compound heterozygous pathogenic variants in SBDS, c.183_184delinsCT (p.Lys62Ter), inherited paternally, and c.258+2T>C, inherited maternally, establishing a molecular diagnosis of SDS. At presentation, the chest circumference measured 36cm, compared with an age-expected value of 41cm. The patient underwent staged median sternotomy distraction followed by stabilisation with custom fibular allograft struts. At approximately 3 months, chest circumference had increased to 41cm, peak inspiratory pressures had decreased from 40-50cm H2O to the mid-20cm H2O range, pulmonary hypertension was no longer evident on echocardiography, and the tracheal injury had healed. At 6 months, he remained on home mechanical ventilation, with peak inspiratory pressures in the upper 20cm H2O range. To our knowledge, operative thoracic expansion specifically for SDS-associated thoracic insufficiency has not previously been described. In carefully selected infants with severe thoracic insufficiency who are not yet candidates for conventional thoracic reconstruction, staged sternal distraction may serve as an interim strategy to achieve meaningful thoracic expansion.
records.journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
records.authors: Jarrin Lopez A, Zhao A, Darawsheh R, Kephart D, Sebastian VA, Idowu O, Babbitt C, Kim S.

records.title: Differential transcriptomic responses of pmgA and ssr1600 single-knockout mutants to short-term and prolonged high-light exposure in the cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803.
records.abstract: PmgA and Ssr1600, homologs of the anti-sigma factor and the anti-sigma antagonist of the bacterial partner-switching system, respectively, are involved in coordination of the repression of photosystem I content and chlorophyll biosynthesis under prolonged high-light (HL) conditions in the cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803. To characterize the transcriptional responses associated with PmgA and Ssr1600 during HL acclimation, we compared global gene expression profiles of the wild-type (WT) and knockout strains of pmgA (ΔpmgA) and ssr1600 (Δ1600) under low-light conditions and at 15 min, 1 h and 12 h after the shift to HL. The knockout of pmgA or ssr1600 induced temporally distinct transcriptomic alterations between short-term and prolonged HL exposure. At 15 min, Δ1600, but not ΔpmgA, showed enhanced induction of stress-responsive genes, including sigB and heat-shock genes, together with derepression of pmgA. At 12 h, both mutants showed significant upregulation of genes related to chlorophyll biosynthesis, photosynthetic electron transport, nitrogen assimilation, and amino acid biosynthesis. Considering that Ssr1600 does not accumulate in ΔpmgA, these observations can be explained by a shift in the role of Ssr1600, from the suppressor of the amplification of the stress response by PmgA under short-term HL conditions to a factor mediating signal output from the PmgA-Ssr1600 module under prolonged HL conditions, although the contribution of secondary effects cannot be excluded. Our transcriptomic data do not support the hypothesis that PmgA acts as a canonical anti-sigma factor for any of the sigma factors examined in this study, SigB, SigD and SigE, under either condition.
records.authors: Nakamura R, Kawai S, Hirose Y, Hihara Y.

records.title: Collagen-stimulating activity of a pentapeptide conjugate and self-assembly into micelles.
records.abstract: We present a lipopeptide conjugate, farnesyl-mercapto(diethylene glycol)-KTTKS (FMdEG-KTTKS), designed to include the KTTKS collagen-stimulating sequence attached to a terpenoid branched lipid chain via a short hydrophilic spacer. This conjugate stimulates fibroblasts to produce greater than 200% more collagen per cell than conventional stimulants. This activity is observed at low concentration, well below a critical micelle concentration (CMC) determined by fluorescence probe measurements. Above the CMC, this molecule self-assembles into well-defined spherical micelles, as shown by cryogenic-transmission electron microscopy (cryo-TEM) and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS). The behaviour of this conjugate is contrasted with that of related lipopeptides: FMdEG-KTTKS forms micelles across a wide pH range, instead of nanotapes observed for C16-KTTKS (Matrixyl™). The molecule is shown to stimulate production of type I collagen (beneficial for anti-aging treatments) and promotes repopulation of fibroblasts in a cell monolayer after scratching, as a simple model for skin injury. FMdEG-KTTKS also has anti-inflammatory activity, reducing the production of nitrite in macrophages challenged with bacterial lipopolysaccharide.
records.authors: de Mello L, Castelletto V, Seitsonen J, Hamley IW.

records.title: Early Renal microRNA Signatures of Septic Acute Kidney Injury in Neonatal Pigs.
records.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a major complication of neonatal sepsis, yet the early molecular events underlying sepsis-associated AKI (SA-AKI) in the maturing kidney remain poorly defined. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are post-transcriptional regulators of gene expression that may contribute to the inflammatory, stress, and remodeling responses associated with SA-AKI. We profiled renal miRNA expression in neonatal pigs 12 h after cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)-induced polymicrobial sepsis. CLP increased plasma lactate, C-reactive protein, and procalcitonin and was accompanied by evidence of kidney injury, including increased plasma creatinine, symmetric dimethylarginine, and urinary neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin. NanoString profiling of 803 endogenous miRNAs, followed by sequence-based porcine annotation, identified a distinct renal miRNA signature that separated CLP and sham kidneys by principal component analysis. Differential expression analysis identified 14 upregulated and 5 downregulated miRNAs in septic kidneys. Several differentially expressed miRNAs were associated with biomarkers of systemic inflammation and kidney injury. Integrating miRNA profiles with target-gene expression revealed inverse miRNA-mRNA relationships involving PTGS2, FOS, AKT1, KLF6, NF-κB1, and SMAD2, with ssc-miR-374b-5p showing the broadest inverse relationship with these upregulated targets. Pathway enrichment analysis further implicated HIF-1, TGF-β, FoxO, autophagy/mitophagy, cell-cycle regulation, focal adhesion, and cellular senescence. Collectively, these findings demonstrate rapid remodeling of the renal miRNA landscape during early polymicrobial sepsis and identify candidate miRNA-mRNA regulatory networks that may contribute to the early pathogenesis of neonatal SA-AKI.
records.authors: Adepoju AE, Fanous MS, Michael OS, Cruz JE, Mankuzhy PD, Adebiyi A.

records.title: Recent Developments in (Archaeal) Pyrrolysine and Selenocysteine Specification and Metabolism.
records.abstract: Although many naturally occurring modified amino acids have been identified in living organisms, only two, selenocysteine and pyrrolysine, are genetically encoded. Each amino acid is inserted cotranslationally into proteins imparting catalytic functionality. Both selenocysteine and pyrrolysine are encoded in genes by what are otherwise stop codons. The 2 aa contrast in how they are biosynthesized. Selenocysteine is synthesized on the dedicated tRNASec following serylation by seryl-tRNA synthetase. Pyrrolysine is made as a free amino acid and then used to aminoacylate its specific tRNAPyl by pyrrolysyl-tRNAPyl synthetase. The 2 aa further differ in how message context influences translation. Translation of UGA as selenocysteine relies heavily on the presence of a specific messenger RNA (mRNA) sequence found in the transcript. In contrast, local message context stimulates, but is not required for, relatively efficient translation of UAG as pyrrolysine.
records.journal: Cold Spring Harbor perspectives in biology
records.authors: Peiter N, Rother M, Krzycki JA.

records.title: Calcium, 25-hydroxyvitamin D, and postpartum hemorrhage: A 2-sample Mendelian randomization study.
records.abstract: We aimed to evaluate the causal effect of calcium and 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] on the risk of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) using a 2-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) study. Instrumental variables for calcium and 25(OH)D were selected from corresponding large-scale genome-wide association studies. Summary-level data on PPH were obtained from the latest R10 release of the FinnGen consortium. Inverse-variance weighting (IVW) was performed as the main MR analysis, and MR-Egger and weighted median were performed to strengthen the final MR estimates. Sensitivity analyses were applied to detect possible heterogeneity or pleiotropy. One hundred and four single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) for calcium and 117 SNPs for 25(OH)D were selected as candidate instrumental variables. In this study, the MR estimates for calcium and 25(OH)D remained consistent before and after removing confounder-related SNPs. The IVW method suggested a potential inverse association between genetically predicted calcium and PPH (odds ratio [OR] = 0.89, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.80, 0.99, P = .036); however, this finding was not supported by the pleiotropy‑robust MR‑Egger (OR = 0.89, 95% CI: 0.72-1.11, P = .303) or weighted median (OR = 0.90, 95% CI: 0.74-1.10, P = .302) methods. No heterogeneity or pleiotropy was observed in Cochran's Q test (P = .825), MR-Egger intercept test (P = .976), or the MR-Pleiotropy Residual Sum and Outlier (MR-PRESSO) Global Test (P = .842) in the determination of the role of calcium levels in PPH. However, no significant genetic evidence was found to support a causal relationship between 25(OH)D and PPH (IVW: OR = 0.98, 95% CI: 0.85-1.12, P = .735; MR-Egger: OR = 1.01, 95% CI: 0.82-1.25, P = .912; Weighted median: OR = 1.08, 95% CI: 0.85-1.36, P = .525). In summary, our primary analysis suggested a potential inverse association between serum calcium and PPH, but this was not supported by sensitivity analyses robust to pleiotropy, warranting cautious interpretation. For 25(OH)D, our analysis did not provide sufficient evidence to support or refute a causal role in PPH, largely due to limited statistical power.

records.title: Intestinal tuberculosis with multiple intestinal perforations in a 5-month-old infant: The role of metagenomic next-generation sequencing: a case report and literature review.
records.abstract: RationaleIntestinal tuberculosis (ITB) is a chronic infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex and is relatively rare in infants. However, severe complications such as intestinal perforation can pose significant clinical challenges. We report the clinical features, diagnosis, and therapeutic management of intestinal perforation caused by ITB in an infant.Patient concernsA 5-month-old male infant presented with fever and abdominal distension, which progressed to intestinal obstruction and multiple perforations involving the distal ileum and appendiceal region. The clinical presentation was atypical.DiagnosesThe diagnosis was established through surgical exploration and metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS).Conventional investigations, including the tuberculin skin test using purified protein derivative and interferon-gamma release assay, were negative. mNGS of peritoneal drainage fluid detected mycobacterium tuberculosis complex with 2868,520 sequence reads, and Ziehl-Neelsen staining of mesenteric nodule specimens was positive for acid-fast bacilli.InterventionsThe infant underwent surgical intervention for the intestinal perforations, followed by the standard four-drug anti-TB regimen (rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol) together with linezolid, imipenem, and amikacin.OutcomesThe infant showed substantial clinical improvement, with weight gain and encouraging developmental progress; although the ileostomy remains in situ, closure is planned after full nutritional recovery. To our knowledge, this is among the youngest reported cases of postnatally acquired primary ITB presenting with multiple intestinal perforations in an infant without a known history of TB exposure.LessonsIn infants with severe unexplained intra-abdominal infection and inconclusive conventional TB investigations, mNGS may facilitate the early diagnosis of ITB. Timely surgical intervention combined with anti-TB therapy may improve outcomes in these critically ill patients.
records.authors: Wang B, Simijiang Y, Kaheman G, Cui Y, Akemu Y, Shawutali N.

records.title: Effuseotrichosporon baotianmanense sp. nov., a novel yeast species isolated from rotting wood in China.
records.abstract: Two novel yeast strains, designated NYNU 211158 and NYNU 211179, were recovered from decaying wood samples collected in the Baotianman Nature Reserve, Henan Province, central China. Molecular phylogenetic analyses based on the D1/D2 domain of the LSU rRNA gene and the internal transcribed spacer (ITS) regions indicated that the closest known relative of these strains is the described species Effuseotrichosporon vanderwaltii. Sequence comparisons revealed that the novel strains differ from the type strain of E. vanderwaltii by 15 nucleotide substitutions (2.2%) in the D1/D2 domain and five nucleotide substitutions (1.0%) in the ITS region. Physiologically, the novel strains can be distinguished from E. vanderwaltii by their capacity to assimilate lactose, raffinose, inulin, N-acetyl-d-glucosamine, glycerol, erythritol, ethanol, methanol, citrate, 2-keto-d-gluconate, 5-keto-d-gluconate and ethylamine. On the basis of these molecular and phenotypic divergences, the strains are proposed to represent a novel species, Effuseotrichosporon baotianmanense sp. nov., with the holotype designated as CICC 33543T (MycoBank MB 864553).

records.title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Proteomic Analyses Reveal a Diverse Venom Repertoire in Macrothele guizhouensis.
records.abstract: The venom of spiders in the family Macrothelidae is a rich source of bioactive molecules with potential biomedical and agricultural applications, yet the venom composition of Macrothele guizhouensis remains poorly understood. Here, integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses were used to characterize its venom repertoire. Venom-gland transcriptomics identified diverse toxin-related transcripts, including cysteine-rich peptides (CRPs) and venom-associated proteins, while proteomics confirmed multiple secreted venom components. RT-qPCR analysis of representative toxin genes provided additional descriptive evidence for their expression patterns in the venom gland. Structural and evolutionary analyses revealed both conserved toxin scaffolds shared with related Macrothele species and divergent, lineage-specific peptides that may represent novel toxin variants. Several CRPs displayed structural features resembling those of known ion-channel-modulating toxins, including a double-knot peptide that represents a candidate for future functional investigation. These findings provide the first comprehensive molecular characterization of M. guizhouensis venom, expand current knowledge of toxin diversity and evolution in Macrothelidae, and establish a foundation for the discovery and functional characterization of bioactive peptides with pharmaceutical and pest-management potential.
records.authors: Zhang M, Yin W, Zheng Y, Li Z, Yang Z, Yang Z.

records.title: Metabolomic Changes in Biofilm of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Under Early-Stage Tobramycin Treatment Identified by 2D NMR-Based COLMARq.
records.abstract: Biofilms are estimated to account for a large proportion of persistent microbial infections and are associated with substantial mortality in hospitals. Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms exhibit higher resistance to antibiotics compared to their planktonic growth form, making them difficult to eradicate and contributing to the mounting global challenge posed by infectious diseases. To gain deeper insights into the metabolic response of biofilms to antibiotic pressure, we conducted a quantitative, untargeted metabolomics analysis using heteronuclear 2D NMR spectroscopy. Biofilms were grown in the presence of sub-inhibitory concentrations of tobramycin, and metabolic alterations were identified and quantified using the COLMARq analysis platform. Our analysis revealed significant metabolic shifts even at low doses of tobramycin with key metabolites such as UDP-glucose increasing and putrescine decreasing. Pathway enrichment analysis highlighted alterations in amino acid biosynthesis, energy metabolism, and stress response pathways. Notably, the accumulation of glutathione disulfide indicates enhanced oxidative stress, while the depletion of β-alanine, succinate, and GABA suggested metabolic shifts linked to biofilm adaptation. These findings provide new insights into the metabolic reprogramming of biofilms under antibiotic treatment and offer perspectives into biofilm behavior in the case of Pseudomonas aeruginosa when exposed to antibiotics from an early stage of infection.
records.authors: Choo M, Li DW, Lee K, Sindeldecker D, Bruschweiler-Li L, Brüschweiler R.

records.title: Preclinical Evaluation of cRGD-Functionalized Lipid-Polymer Hybrid Nanocarriers for Anti-VEGF Gene Therapy in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
records.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains one of the most aggressive breast cancer subtypes owing to its high metastatic potential and the absence of effective molecularly targeted therapies. Although cRGD-functionalized nanocarriers have been extensively investigated for TNBC treatment, most reported systems primarily deliver chemotherapeutic agents or short regulatory RNAs. In the present study, we developed and preclinically evaluated a cRGD-functionalized lipid-polymer hybrid gene delivery system (cRGD-LPH-GDS) specifically engineered for the delivery of therapeutic plasmid DNA (pDNA) targeting the VEGF/VEGFR2 signaling axis. The nanosystem was prepared by a self-assembly approach using DSPE-PEG-Maleimide and cyclic arginine-glycine-aspartic acid (cRGD), yielding nanoparticles with a mean hydrodynamic diameter of 19.40 ± 0.43 nm, a zeta potential of +22.8 ± 1.6 mV, and a polydispersity index of 0.25. The hybrid formulation demonstrated effective protection of pDNA against serum- and DNase I-mediated degradation while maintaining reversible cargo release under destabilizing conditions. In vitro studies demonstrated acceptable cytocompatibility, enhanced receptor-mediated cellular uptake, improved transfection efficiency, and significant suppression of VEGF-A expression in 4T1 cells. Competitive receptor-blocking experiments further confirmed the contribution of αvβ3 integrin-mediated targeting to the enhanced biological activity of the targeted formulation. In an orthotopic 4T1 BALB/c mouse model, intratumoral administration of cRGD-LPH-GDS:pDNA significantly inhibited tumor growth, reduced intratumoral VEGF-A expression, and prolonged survival without evident systemic toxicity. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that integration of a lipid-polymer hybrid structure with therapeutic plasmid DNA delivery and cRGD-mediated targeting provides an effective non-viral system for anti-angiogenic gene therapy. The developed nanosystem represents a promising foundation for the further preclinical development of targeted pDNA delivery strategies for TNBC.

records.title: Epidemiology, Clinical Features, and Advances in Diagnosis and Treatment of Chlamydia psittaci Pneumonia: A Narrative Review.
records.abstract: Chlamydia psittaci pneumonia is an underrecognized zoonotic infectious disease that primarily involves the lungs but frequently affects extrapulmonary organ systems. Clinical and radiological features are nonspecific, and diagnosis remains challenging. Culture, although the gold standard, is slow, low-yield, and requires biosafety level 3 facilities; serology is limited by cross-reactivity and the need for paired sera; and polymerase chain reaction, although rapid, generally targets selected genes and is often used only when clinical suspicion is high. The widespread use of metagenomic next-generation sequencing and targeted next-generation sequencing has increased the reported detection of C. psittaci, largely reflecting improved diagnostic capability rather than a proven increase in disease incidence. Tetracyclines remain first-line therapy; macrolides and fluoroquinolones are alternatives, although fluoroquinolone monotherapy may fail in severe disease. Evidence for combination therapy and newer agents such as omadacycline remains limited, and the true disease burden is likely underestimated because surveillance is incomplete. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on epidemiology, clinical and radiological features, diagnosis, and treatment of C. psittaci pneumonia and highlights key evidence gaps.
records.authors: Fang C, Xu L.

records.title: Links Between Environmental Quality, Gut Microbiota, and Host Performance in Nutrient-Impacted Springs.
records.abstract: Microbial symbionts may enhance adaptation to environmental stress, yet their role in nutrient-enriched freshwater habitats remains unclear. We conducted a full-factorial laboratory experiment with least killifish, Heterandria formosa, manipulating water chemistry from four Florida springs and gut microbiota inoculations from conspecifics at those sites. Sequencing of 16S rRNA revealed that gut microbial richness was higher in fish reared in less nutrient-loaded waters, but inoculation treatments, if successful, did not produce significant shifts in composition. Gut communities consistently differed from ambient water, with enrichment of Pseudomonadota and Planctomycetota. Females grew more slowly in the most polluted water. In a parallel result, males displayed higher mass-specific metabolic rates in the most nutrient-loaded water. Reproductive output per female nearly doubled when experimental microbiota and water originated from the same site, despite stable microbial diversity, though parentage and inoculation success were not verified; therefore, these results should be interpreted cautiously. These results indicate that environmental quality shapes gut microbiota and host performance, and that matching microbial communities to habitat conditions can boost reproduction. Such interactions may contribute to freshwater fish resilience and merit integration into conservation strategies.

records.title: Cul4b sustains cell cycle in germinal center B cells and enables protective humoral immunity against influenza A virus.
records.abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) are a major public health burden, infecting millions of people worldwide. Seasonal vaccines mitigate disease, in part, by triggering the production of IAV-specific antibodies by B cells. Viral evasion and limited vaccine-induced immunity pose barriers to vaccine effectiveness, warranting further investigation of factors influencing protective immune responses. The generation of affinity-matured antibodies is critical for antiviral immunity. This relies on germinal center (GC) B cells, which undergo multiple rounds of somatic hypermutation, proliferation, and selection. Cullin-4b (Cul4b) acts as the backbone for the Cullin Ring Ligase 4 (CRL4), an E3 ubiquitin ligase complex that ubiquitylates proteins for degradation by the proteosome. CRL4 is critical for regulation of DNA damage responses and cell cycle maintenance, essential for B cells to mount a robust humoral response. Here we investigate the role of Cul4b in B cell responses to IAV using mice lacking Cul4b in B cells. We found that Cul4b promoted viral clearance and anti-IAV antibody titers post-infection and immunization, and Cul4b was required for optimal vaccine-mediated protection against infectious challenge. Additionally, we found that Cul4b supports GC B cell populations and promotes their cell cycle maintenance in vivo. We conclude that B cell intrinsic Cul4b is essential for optimal GC and antibody responses after acute IAV exposure. Further investigation of CRL4 in B cells is warranted to elucidate its potential as a therapeutic target to improve vaccine efficacy.
records.authors: Davis D, Mejia L, Renshaw L, Muramatsu H, Jun RHJ, Divakar Rao S, Spinola O, Pardi N, Moser E.

records.title: Dengue Virus Pathogenesis: Innate Immune Signaling and Cell Death Receptor Pathways.
records.abstract: BackgroundThe infection caused by the dengue virus (DENV) involves a complicated interaction between viral replication and the body's immune responses. As the first line of defense, the innate immune response limits viral replication but can also lead to immunopathology if it is improperly regulated. The DENV activates several pattern-recognition receptor (PRR) pathways, such as the RIG-I-like receptor (RLR), the Toll-like receptor (TLR), and the cGAS-STING signaling pathway, all of which control interferon and inflammatory responses.ObjectivesThe purpose of this review is to outline the molecular mechanisms involved in the process of innate immune recognition and signaling when DENV infects cells, with a specific focus on the virus's immune-evasion tactics and the relationship between innate immune signaling and programmed cell death; it also examines the possible implications of these pathways for the development of a dengue vaccine and for antiviral approaches.DiscussionThe RNA of DENV is mainly detected by RNA-sensing pathways such as the RLRs and TLRs, while cGAS-STING signaling can be triggered indirectly as a result of virus-associated cellular stress and the presence of cytosolic DNA. DENV counteracts these antiviral responses by acting on key signaling molecules such as MAVS, STING, TBK1, IRF3, and STAT2, thus promoting viral persistence and replication. At the same time, death-receptor pathways involving tumor necrosis factor receptor (TNFR), Fas (CD95), and TNF-related apoptosis-inducing ligand (TRAIL) receptors control caspase-8-dependent apoptosis and may play a role in the elimination of infected cells as well as in causing tissue injury and immunopathology. The interaction between innate immune signaling, inflammatory responses, and caspase-8-mediated cell death therefore serves as an important factor in determining the balance between antiviral protection and disease progression. If these mechanisms are understood, this could form the basis for developing strategies that boost antiviral immunity while reducing excessive inflammation and pathological cell death.ConclusionThe way in which dengue disease develops is due to the continuous interaction between the body's antiviral innate immune responses, the virus's ability to evade the immune system, and programmed cell death. It might be possible to enhance control of dengue disease by targeting these closely related pathways, whether by means of vaccine development, antiviral drugs, or therapies that act on the host. Yet any intervention focused on a specific pathway will need to take into account the stage of the disease, the cellular environment, and the possible risk of weakening the protective antiviral immunity.

records.title: A Standalone Flavoprotein Monooxygenase Directs Divergent Tropolone Skeletal Editing through Baeyer-Villiger-Triggered Rearrangement.
records.abstract: Late-stage oxidative remodeling of tropolone cores underpins the remarkable scaffold diversity in fungal meroterpenoid biosynthesis. However, the mechanistic basis by which a single enzymatic catalyst diverts a common substrate toward carbon-excising ring contraction versus carbon-retentive skeletal rearrangement remains elusive. Here, via comparative transcriptomics and targeted gene deletion, we identified a standalone host-encoded class A flavoprotein monooxygenase, ANIA_01821 (AN1821), as indispensable for tropolone ring remodeling in Aspergillus nidulans. A functionally homologous enzyme, AO090103000276 (AO276), from Aspergillus oryzae was further characterized as a tractable biocatalyst for in vitro studies. Reconstitution assays using purified AO276 revealed that this single flavoprotein monooxygenase alone converts the bistropolone meroterpenoid eupenifeldin into both ring-contracted phenolic products and carbon-retentive bridged polycycles, establishing a unified enzymatic origin for two structurally distinct natural-product scaffolds. Structure-guided mutagenesis uncovered a precisely organized electrostatic network that is critical for flavin-dependent oxygenation. Complementary well-tempered metadynamics simulations and quantum-chemical calculations support a Baeyer-Villiger branching mechanism, wherein the AO276 active site may preferentially stabilize alternative migration-competent conformations of a putative Criegee intermediate. Each conformation aligns a distinct C-C bond in an antiperiplanar geometry relative to the O-O bond; restricted conformational interconversion within the active site could preserve the initial reactive geometry and bias divergent carbon migration. Collectively, our findings identify conformational preorganization as a plausible contributor to regiodivergent enzymatic Baeyer-Villiger catalysis, offering a rational strategy for steering oxidative skeletal remodeling in complex natural product molecules.

records.title: [A case of Mowat-Wilson syndrome due to a de novo c.3515del frameshift variant of ZEB2 gene].
records.abstract: ObjectiveTo explore the genetic etiology of a fetus with Mowat-Wilson syndrome (MWS) due to a novel de novo heterozygous frameshift variant of ZEB2 gene.MethodsA pedigree presenting at the Affiliated Women and Children's Hospital of Ningbo University in February 2024 was enrolled. Clinical data were retrospectively analyzed. Amniotic fluid samples of the fetus and peripheral blood samples of the couple were collected for trio-whole exome sequencing (Trio-WES). Candidate variant was verified by Sanger sequencing. The pathogenicity of the candidate variant was assessed based on guidelines from the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG). Postnatal follow-up was performed, and the pathogenicity of the variant was re-assessed by incorporating newly acquired phenotypic features. This study was approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of the hospital (Ethics No.: EC2023-094).ResultsPrenatal ultrasonography at 20+2 weeks of gestation identified ventricular septal defect, overriding aorta and polyhydramnios. Trio-WES revealed that the fetus has harbored a novel c.3515del (p.Met1172ArgfsTer69) heterozygous frameshift variant of the ZEB2 gene. Sanger sequencing confirmed that neither parent has carried the same variant. Based on the ACMG guidelines, the variant was initially classified as a variant of uncertain significance (VUS) based on PVS1_Moderate+PM2_Supporting+PS2_Supporting criteria. After birth, the infant exhibited typical MWS features including hypertelorism, low-hanging columella, neck hypotonia, cerebral hypoplasia, corpus callosum agenesis, and abnormal earlobe morphology. Growth delay, feeding difficulties, and motor delay were observed at 4-month follow-up. Combined with postnatal phenotypic data, the variant was re-classified as likely pathogenic (LP) based on PVS1_Moderate+PM2_Supporting+PS2_Moderate+PP4_Supporting criteria.ConclusionThe newly identified ZEB2 c.3515del represents a likely pathogenic variant, which expanded the mutational spectrum of the ZEB2 gene. Longitudinal prenatal-to-postnatal phenotypic integration is critical for re-assessing VUS in MWS patients and providing evidence-based references for prenatal genetic diagnosis and genetic counseling of similar cases.

records.title: Environmental Drivers of Nontuberculous Mycobacteria in Tropical Freshwater Systems.
records.abstract: Whilst microbial diversity still remains largely unexplored across environments and scales, microbial biogeography is shaped by edaphic and ecological drivers, and shifts in microbial community composition are frequently associated with host community structure and health. Nontuberculous mycobacteria represent a striking example of environmental microorganisms with opportunistic pathogenic potential. Unfortunately, understanding of their diversity and distribution in tropical freshwater environments remains limited, while such knowledge is crucial for predicting disease emergence and transmission. Here we aimed at (i) identifying microhabitat abiotic and biotic drivers influencing their diversity and distribution in French Guiana, (ii) comparing their diversity and distribution between French Guiana and Côte d'Ivoire, and (iii) examining co-occurrences between mycobacterial communities in different environmental contexts. By deploying an eDNA-based metabarcoding approach from tropical freshwater ecosystems, we suggest that their diversity and distribution are mainly driven by habitat type (urban vs. rural), sample type (water vs. sediment), and local abiotic factors such as phosphorus levels in sediments (with species-specific effects). Moreover, we found a stratified distribution of mycobacteria depending on sediment texture (fine silts vs. coarse sand) and depth. Overall, we suggest that their ecological interactions may occur at the microhabitat level rather than following clear biogeographic patterns.
records.authors: Combe M, Bouam A, Dizoe S, Davoust B, Drancourt E, Messeca D, Valentini A, Blaizot R, Gozlan RE.

records.title: Inhalation of Gardenia jasminoides flower essential oil attenuates stress-associated neurobehavioral abnormalities in mice.
records.abstract: BackgroundGardenia jasminoides Ellis is a traditional medicinal and aromatic plant, but the neurobehavioral potential of its flower-derived essential oil remains insufficiently understood.PurposeThis study aimed to evaluate whether G. jasminoides flower essential oil (GEO) inhalation attenuates chronic stress-associated neurobehavioral abnormalities and to characterize the accompanying hippocampal, metabolic, and gut microbial responses.MethodsGEO was chemically profiled by headspace solid-phase microextraction coupled with gas chromatography-mass spectrometry and evaluated in a chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) mouse model. Mice were exposed to GEO by inhalation during the final 2 weeks of the 6-week CUMS procedure. Behavioral performance was assessed using the open field test, elevated plus maze, tail suspension test, forced swim test, and sucrose preference test. Hippocampal morphology, inflammatory and oxidative stress-related indices, neurochemical markers, serum corticosterone, serum metabolomics, hippocampal transcriptomics, gut microbiota composition, and hippocampal neuroimmune/synaptic signaling markers were further analyzed.ResultsChemical profiling tentatively annotated 59 volatile constituents in GEO, with linalool and linalyl acetate identified as the predominant constituents. GEO inhalation attenuated CUMS-associated behavioral abnormalities, with significant changes observed most consistently in the GEO-20 group. GEO exposure was also associated with increased hippocampal dendritic spine density relative to the CUMS group, lower inflammatory and oxidative stress-related indices, higher hippocampal brain-derived neurotrophic factor, γ-aminobutyric acid, and 5-hydroxytryptamine levels, and lower serum corticosterone. Serum metabolomics identified GEO-20-associated changes in metabolic features and pathways involving nucleotide/purine metabolism, arachidonic acid-related lipid mediator pathways, bile acid-related metabolism, and neuroactive metabolic processes. Hippocampal transcriptomics identified GEO-20-associated changes in neuroimmune-, neuroactive ligand-receptor-, and γ-aminobutyric acid synapse-related transcriptional profiles. Gut microbiota analysis revealed GEO-20-associated changes in microbial richness, community composition, discriminatory taxa, and genus-level co-occurrence patterns. Targeted molecular assays showed lower hippocampal glial reactivity and inflammatory signaling-related markers after GEO exposure, whereas GEO-20 was associated with higher levels of mitochondrial regulatory and synaptic plasticity markers.ConclusionGEO inhalation attenuated chronic stress-associated neurobehavioral abnormalities in mice and was accompanied by changes in hippocampal neuroimmune and synaptic plasticity-related markers, together with broader systemic metabolic and microbial responses.
records.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
records.authors: Bian X, Liu J, Zhao X, Zhang Y, Zhang T, Yang X, Sun X.

records.title: ME53 Modulates AcMNPV Proliferation via Interaction with GP64 and miR-34-5p-Targeted Synergistic Insecticidal Strategy against Spodoptera frugiperda.
records.abstract: This study developed a chemical engineering strategy to improve baculovirus biopesticides by engineering the Autographa californica multiple nucleopolyhedrovirus (AcMNPV) and regulating host metabolism in Spodoptera frugiperda. Overexpression of the me53 gene enhanced the viral replication, nucleocapsid assembly, and budding virus titers. ME53 interacted with GP64 via hydrogen bonds to promote the membrane fusion. Meanwhile, miR-34-5p negatively regulated AcMNPV proliferation, and inhibition of this miRNA upregulated me53 and GP64. In larvae, miR-34-5p disturbed the metabolism and impaired development. Combining the me53-overexpressing virus with miR-34-5p inhibition synergistically accelerated killing and increased mortality. Engineered viruses were stably produced and showed an improved virulence and safety. This work provides an efficient, eco-friendly biopesticide platform through genetic engineering and host metabolic regulation, supporting sustainable pest control.
records.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
records.authors: Wang C, Hou S, Fu Y.

records.title: Identification and Engineering of an l-Threonine Aldolase from Agrobacterium pusense for Efficient l-Serine Synthesis.
records.abstract: l-Serine is a high-value amino acid, but enzymatic production is limited by insufficient catalytic activity and limited formaldehyde tolerance. A metagenomic library derived from glufosinate-exposed soil was mined to identify an l-threonine aldolase from Agrobacterium pusense (ApLTA). The substrate tunnel and active pocket were engineered through tunnel analysis, structural comparison, consensus design, and residue plasticity-guided polarity scanning. The resulting quadruple mutant D88M/T202S/A57S/F234M (Mut4) exhibited 48.5-fold higher catalytic efficiency than wild-type ApLTA. At 1 M formaldehyde loading, Mut4 increased l-serine concentration from 23.0 to 87.3 g L-1, with a space-time yield of 21.8 g L-1 h-1, the highest reported for LTA-catalyzed l-serine synthesis. Mut4 also showed enhanced activity toward multiple aromatic aldehydes. Molecular dynamics simulations further revealed the molecular basis for its enhanced catalytic efficiency. This study provides the first demonstration of highly efficient l-serine synthesis using an engineered LTA and offers a new strategy for enzymatic l-serine production.
records.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
records.authors: Sun S, Guo M, Zhou Y, Deng F, Wang H, Wei D.

records.title: Lactate Metabolic Restriction Is Linked to Granulosa Cell Dysfunction and Early Atresia-Like Changes via H4K12la-Mediated Epigenetic Remodeling and p53 Signaling in Goats.
records.abstract: Lactate metabolism is a pivotal component of the follicular microenvironment, yet how altered lactate availability influences granulosa cell (GC) fate during early follicular atresia remains elusive. We found significantly lower lactate concentrations in the follicular fluid of atretic goat follicles compared to healthy counterparts. In vitro, pharmacological inhibition of lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) depleted intracellular lactate, leading to suppressed GC proliferation and G0/G1 arrest without increasing apoptosis. Notably, these proliferative defects were significantly attenuated by exogenous sodium L-lactate supplementation, suggesting that lactate availability plays an important role in GC cell-cycle progression. Transcriptomic profiling further indicated a broad suppression of cell-cycle and DNA replication programs following LDH inhibition. At the epigenetic level, restricted lactate availability was associated with decreased global protein lactylation and specific reductions in histone H4 lysine 12 lactylation (H4K12la). Integrative analysis of CUT&Tag data identified the checkpoint regulator growth arrest and DNA damage-inducible alpha (GADD45A) as a candidate target associated with altered H4K12la occupancy. CUT& RUN-qPCR confirmed reduced H4K12la enrichment at the GADD45A promoter, while siRNA-mediated GADD45A knockdown partially alleviated the LDH inhibition-induced G1/S arrest. Furthermore, metabolic stress was accompanied by activation of p53-mediated signaling, characterized by elevated γH2AX, p53, p21, and p38 levels. Silencing TP53 attenuated GADD45A induction and partially restored proliferative markers. Collectively, our findings support a model in which restricted lactate metabolism is associated with impaired goat primary GC proliferation, potentially through a coordinated mechanism involving H4K12la-mediated epigenetic remodeling and p53-associated stress signaling, both converging on GADD45A and contributing to early follicular degeneration.
records.authors: Zhu M, Zhou Z, Li D, Yu W, Wang J, Wang L, Wan Y.

records.title: A practical resource for multi-omics data integration in microbial systems.
records.abstract: The increasing availability of microbial multi-omics datasets has created new opportunities to explore complex biological systems. However, exploration remains limited by the lack of accessible, reproducible workflows that integrate multiple omics layers and deliver easily interpretable visualizations of functional and pathway-level insights. Here, we present an R-based workflow for integrated analysis and network-based interpretation of microbial multi-omics data. The workflow enables microbiologists to analyse transcriptomic, proteomic and metabolomic datasets either individually or in combination, apply univariate and multivariate approaches for biomarker discovery and generate interpretable visualizations of functional and pathway-level signatures. Implemented as a multi-step R Markdown workflow, the resource leverages established open-source tools, including mixOmics for biomarker identification and omics integration and clusterProfiler for functional enrichment analysis. Functional integration is then performed on the enrichment results themselves rather than on individual features. By combining functional annotations from distinct omics layers, strains or conditions into a unified network, it enables simultaneous visualization of functional connectivity and of the sources from which each response was recovered, so that conserved and condition-specific responses can be identified directly rather than reconciled across separate outputs. A dedicated Shiny application makes this framework fully dynamic, allowing users to interactively filter, interpret and prioritize shared and condition-specific biological responses. We demonstrate its utility using a publicly available Streptococcus pyogenes dataset, revealing both shared and strain-specific functional responses to human serum. This resource provides an adaptable framework for systematic multi-omics analysis, improving accessibility and reproducibility and facilitating functional interpretation of microbial responses to diverse environments.

records.title: Protein Isoaspartate Repair in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: An Integrative Bioinformatic Analysis of the PCMT Gene Family.
records.abstract: Protein homeostasis is a fundamental determinant of neuronal survival, and its disruption contributes to the pathogenesis of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Protein L-isoaspartate O-methyltransferases (PCMTs) are evolutionarily conserved proteins involved in the recognition and processing of damaged proteins through the repair of isoaspartyl residues and protein quality-control pathways; however, their potential involvement in ALS remains largely unexplored. Here, we performed a comprehensive in silico characterization of the PCMT family (PCMT1, PCMTD1, and PCMTD2) by integrating structural, transcriptomic, single-cell, genetic, and protein modeling analyses. Domain analysis demonstrated that all three proteins share a conserved PCMT domain, while predicted S-adenosylmethionine-binding motifs were identified in PCMT1 and PCMTD2 but not PCMTD1, indicating evolutionary conservation with functional divergence. Expression profiling revealed that PCMT family genes are expressed in ALS-relevant tissues and broadly distributed across neuronal, glial, vascular, and immune cell populations in both healthy and ALS-associated brain single-cell data sets. Analysis of multiple independent ALS transcriptomic cohorts identified consistent upregulation of PCMT family members, with PCMTD1 exhibiting the most reproducible disease-associated expression changes across nervous system tissues and peripheral blood. Gene set correlation analyses further revealed distinct relationships between PCMT expression and neuronal pathways, with PCMT1 showing positive associations with axonal transport and synaptic signaling, whereas PCMTD1 and PCMTD2 displayed largely inverse correlation patterns. Rare missense variants identified in ALS patients were predicted to impair protein function and decrease protein stability, while structural modeling suggested that several substitutions may disrupt conserved residues and the local protein architecture. Collectively, these findings identify the PCMT family as previously underexplored candidates associated with ALS and provide a comprehensive framework for future mechanistic studies investigating their roles in neuronal protein homeostasis and neurodegeneration.

records.title: GmRVE8a, a circadian clock-associated gene, negatively regulates flowering and maturity in soybean.
records.abstract: Precise regulation of flowering time and maturity is critical for achieving high and stable soybean yields, and the circadian clock plays a central role in coordinating these developmental transitions. Soybean is a typical short-day crop with a pronounced photoperiodic response; however, the molecular mechanisms linking circadian regulation to photoperiod-dependent flowering and maturity remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated genome-wide association analysis with deep learning approaches using 257 soybean germplasm accessions spanning 14 maturity groups and identified GmRVE8a, a homolog of the Arabidopsis circadian clock gene REVEILLE, as a strong candidate locus associated with soybean maturity across two field environments. Haplotype analysis demonstrated that accessions carrying the GmRVE8aH1 haplotype consistently flowered and matured significantly later than those carrying GmRVE8aH2. Functional validation revealed that knockout of GmRVE8a markedly accelerated flowering and maturity, whereas overexpression of GmRVE8a significantly delayed both processes. qRT-PCR assays further suggested that GmRVE8a may repress flowering and delay maturity by promoting the expression of GmFT4, a flowering-inhibitory member of the FT family, and is unlikely to act by directly regulating E1 expression. Collectively, our findings suggest GmRVE8a as a circadian clock-associated negative regulator of soybean flowering and maturity, and highlight it as a promising candidate for molecular breeding aimed at improving adaptation to diverse photoperiodic environments.

records.title: Single-cell transcriptomics revealed immunological and molecular profiling of pangolin viruses at the viral interface.
records.abstract: Pangolins have been identified as potential intermediate hosts for various viruses, including coronaviruses related to SARS-CoV-2 and MERS-CoV, yet the cellular mechanisms underlying their viral susceptibility remain poorly understood. Here, we establish the first comprehensive single-cell transcriptomic atlas for two pangolin species Manis pentadactyla and Manis javanica, generated through single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of 245 618 high-quality cells from 12 major tissues, combined with 123 bulk transcriptome datasets. This resource is integrated with cross-species data from Homo sapiens, Eptesicus fuscus, Sus scrofa, Mus musculus, and Panthera tigris. Our analysis reveals a myeloid-biased hematopoiesis in pangolin bone marrow, dominated by monocytes and T cells, which contrasts sharply with the lymphoid-skewed composition observed in H. sapiens and M. musculus. We also identify species-specific features, including thyroid-specific expression of FKBP5 in M. pentadactyla, and MIF-signaling-mediated cellular interactions in intestinal lymph. Furthermore, key viral receptors ( AXL, NRP1, DPP4, ACE2, SCARB1, and UVRAG) are broadly expressed in immune cells (e.g., B cells, T cells, and macrophages), fibroblasts, and endothelial cells across tissues, as confirmed by single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses. Cross-species comparisons reveal fundamental differences in splenic immune architecture, hematopoietic lineage distribution, and viral receptor expression. Together, these findings based on single-cell transcriptomic profiling establish a molecular and cellular framework for understanding pangolins as potential mixing vessels for viruses and provide a foundation for the targeted surveillance of emerging zoonotic pathogens.

records.title: Microbe Profile: Saccharopolyspora erythraea: antibiotic factory and biosynthetic model organism.
records.abstract: Saccharopolyspora erythraea is a filamentous actinomycete best known as the industrial source of erythromycin, a macrolide antibiotic that remains an important medicine and precursor for the semisynthetic drugs clarithromycin and azithromycin. Beyond its industrial importance, S. erythraea has had a profound influence on natural product bioscience. Studies of erythromycin biosynthesis led to the discovery of modular polyketide synthases and established the principles of assembly-line enzymatic logic that underpin modern understanding of microbial polyketide biosynthesis. Consequently, S. erythraea has served both as an antibiotic production platform and as a model organism for investigating and engineering complex biosynthetic pathways. Continued efforts to understand its metabolism, genetic changes during strain improvement, and the reprogramming of its polyketide synthase machinery are expected to support the development of next-generation antibiotics and biotechnological applications.

records.title: A Multidimensional Framework for Integrated Toxicity Assessment and Prioritization of Naphthenic Acids in Marine Medaka (Oryzias melastigma): Neurotoxicity and Mechanistic Insights.
records.abstract: Petroleum pollution poses a major challenge to global environmental health. Petroleum-derived naphthenic acids (NAs) are frequently detected in marine environments, yet their multidimensional toxicity and mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we developed an integrated toxicity framework combining bioassays, toxicity screening, computational simulations, transcriptomics, and bioinformatics to characterize NAs toxicity in marine medaka (Oryzias melastigma). A concentration gradient spanning environmentally detected levels to higher-effect concentrations (0.015-30 mg/L) revealed developmental defects, cardiac suppression, behavioral disruption, and metabolic dysfunction. CRITIC-AHP-based prioritization identified neurotoxicity as the predominant toxicity dimension, with cyclopentylpropionic acid (CPPA) and cyclohexylpropionic acid (CHPA) identified as major contributors. Mechanistically, these compounds were associated with distinct candidate pathways involving CXCR3-CXCL10 neuroinflammatory responses and DPP10-Kv4.2 ion homeostasis disruption. Their divergent toxicity profiles may be associated with differences in hydrophobicity and molecular flexibility. Rescue experiments supported these pathways, restoring swimming velocity by 60.32% and 62.09%, respectively. Furthermore, NAs induced neurobehavioral alterations and transcriptional signatures overlapping with Alzheimer's disease-associated genes, with 14 and 12 candidate genes identified for CPPA and CHPA. Collectively, this study provides a cross-scale perspective linking physicochemical properties, toxicity pathways, and adverse outcomes of NAs, offering a conceptual approach for toxicity screening and mechanism elucidation of contaminants.

records.title: Molecular Size Mediates Sunlight Effects on the Biodegradation of Aquatic Dissolved Organic Matter: Insights from the Reservoir Wetland and Incubation Experiment.
records.abstract: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) in aquatic ecosystems is crucial to climate, water quality, and water sanitation. However, little is known about how photochemical and biological processes interact to regulate the cycling of DOM in water environments. Here, we investigate the photobiochemical processing of different molecular weight (MW) fractions of aquatic DOM by incubating them with microbes in the dark and light/dark cycling environments via microcosm experiments. Light exposure has distinct effects on the medium (MMW; 1-20 kDa) and low (LMW; <1 kDa) MW fractions and can enrich photoautotrophic bacteria and taxa that could benefit the utilization of aromatic compounds. The decay of the MMW fraction displays the highest light sensitivity, with light increasing the net depletion of tannin- and condensed aromatic-like molecules and production of labile substrates (e.g., protein-like) from photoautotrophic bacteria. In contrast, the net decomposition of the LMW fraction is the least promoted by light exposure, as light induces the net production of complex aromatic molecules that are more persistent. Our findings provide new insights into the photobiochemical and molecular mechanisms underlying the ecological impacts of aquatic DOM and their relevance for wider processes.
records.authors: Zhou P, Tian L, Song S, Siddique MS, Friese K, Herzsprung P, Tanentzap AJ, Graham N, Yu W.

records.title: Large Methane Emissions during Ice-Melt Periods in a Temperate Pond.
records.abstract: Large methane (CH4) emissions during ice-melt periods have been frequently reported in lakes, but whether similar processes occur in ponds remains largely unknown. Here, we conducted observations in a temperate pond across two consecutive ice seasons (2022-2024), with daily sampling during ice melt, to characterize ice-melt CH4 dynamics, reveal potential CH4 production pathways, and estimate the contribution of ice-melt emissions to the annual CH4 budget. CH4 concentrations increased sharply prior to ice melt, resulting in a diffusive pulse during the ice-melt periods (20.1 ± 14.1 mg m-2 h-1), approximately 11 times higher than that during observed ice-free periods (1.8 ± 2.5 mg m-2 h-1). In contrast, CH4 ebullition during ice melt remained low (0.21 ± 0.15 mg m-2 h-1). Despite the brief duration (∼7 days), ice-melt CH4 emissions accounted for 8.7% of annual total CH4 emissions (diffusion + ebullition) and 22.3% of annual diffusive CH4 emissions from June 2022 to May 2023. Variations in water chemistry and sediment microbial communities suggest that both anaerobic and aerobic CH4 production may have contributed to these emission pulses. Particularly, CH4 concentration increased concurrently with chlorophyll a and dissolved oxygen before ice melt, suggesting possible phytoplankton-derived CH4 production under oxic conditions. Given the ubiquity of seasonal freeze-melt cycles in temperate ponds, incorporating ice-melt CH4 fluxes is necessary to refine global CH4 budget estimates.
records.authors: Niu X, Yan Z, Hao L, Liu L, Li SL, Peacock M.

records.title: Randomization of the Damaged Base-Capping Loop Rewires Substrate Specificity in Formamidopyrimidine-DNA Glycosylase.
records.abstract: Formamidopyrimidine-DNA glycosylase (Fpg) is a bacterial base excision repair enzyme that removes 8-oxoguanine (8-oxoG) and some other oxidatively damaged nucleobases from DNA. Fpg hydrolyzes the N-glycosidic bond of the damaged nucleotide and nicks DNA at the resulting apurinic/apyrimidinic (AP) site by β-elimination. Together with bacterial endonuclease VIII and eukaryotic homologues, more specific for damaged pyrimidines, Fpg belongs to a helix-two-turn-helix (H2TH) superfamily of DNA glycosylases. Crystal structures of Fpg reveal that the enzyme recognizes 8-oxoG by flipping it out of the DNA duplex and capping it with a flexible tetrapeptide loop. However, this loop is poorly conserved and contacts 8-oxoG only through the main-chain amides, raising questions about the enzyme specificity determinants. To clarify the mechanism of 8-oxoG recognition, we have produced and characterized five variants of Fpg from Lactococcus lactis with a randomized capping loop. All of these mutants were deficient in 8-oxoG repair, both in vitro and in the E. coli complementation assay, yet retained the ability to bind AP site-containing DNA, form a Schiff base covalent reaction intermediate, and catalyze β-elimination. The mutants were still active in the removal of 5-hydroxyuracil (OHU), an alternative Fpg substrate. All loop mutants showed relaxed opposite-base specificity, processing AP sites and OHU opposite either C or A. Thus, whereas the general architecture of the active site in H2TH DNA glycosylases is permissive for the excision of a wide range of oxidized bases, the capping loop endows Fpg with the specificity for its biologically relevant substrate, 8-oxoguanine.

records.title: [Advances in the application of metal-organic framework materials for rapid detection of contaminants in aquatic products].
records.abstract: Aquatic products are rich in high-quality protein and essential nutrients such as minerals，fatty acids，and vitamins，offering significant nutritional value. However，during their production and processing，they are susceptible to contamination by hazardous substances including heavy metals，veterinary drug residues，illegal additives，and pathogenic microorganisms. Thus，rapid detection technologies serve as a critical means for the timely identification of such food safety issues. However，the complex matrix of aquatic products presents significant analytical challenges，making separation and enrichment steps generally essential prior to detection. Current rapid detection methods often lack compatible rapid sample pretreatment approaches，which can lead to issues such as false positives or missed detection. Among the novel materials，metal-organic frameworks （MOFs） have emerged as a potential class of porous materials for the separation and detection of contaminations in aquatic products owing to their exceptional properties. Firstly，the ultra-high specific surface areas provide abundant active sites. Secondly，the uniform and tunable pore sizes can be tailored for molecular sieving and selective adsorption. Moreover，they are easy to functionalize through pre-design or post-synthetic modification，allowing the introduction of specific binding sites，catalytic moieties，or functional molecules. Lastly，MOFs are constructed through the coordination-driven self-assembly of metal ions and organic linkers，endowing them with considerable structural diversity that can be tailored for diverse applications. These attributes make MOFs exceptionally promising as advanced materials for tackling complex analytical challenges in food safety. This review provides a comprehensive and systematic summary of the application advances of MOFs and their composite materials in the rapid detection of contaminants in aquatic products over the past decade. In sample pretreatment，MOFs and their composites serve as superior adsorbents in various sample preparation techniques such as solid-phase extraction，solid-phase microextraction，magnetic solid-phase extraction，stir bar sorptive extraction，and QuEChERS. For solid-phase microextraction （SPME），MOFs coated on fibers enhance the extraction efficiency of volatile or semi-volatile compounds. In magnetic solid-phase extraction （MSPE），magnetic MOF composites enable rapid separation from liquid samples using an external magnet，significantly simplifying and expediting the process. These applications significantly enhance the selectivity and enrichment efficiency of contaminants in aquatic products while simplifying the pretreatment process. In rapid detection，MOF composites are used to develop enhanced detection platforms by leveraging their unique optical，electrochemical，and catalytic properties. In electrochemical analysis，conductive MOFs or MOF-modified electrodes amplify the signals of targets. For fluorescence detection，luminescent MOFs serve as sensitive probes，often in ratiometric modes to improve accuracy. MOFs also act as excellent substrates or enhancers in surface-enhanced Raman scattering （SERS） platforms，boosting Raman signals for ultra-sensitive detection of molecules. In immunoassays，MOFs are used as label carriers or signal amplifiers，improving detection limits for targets. Additionally，when integrated with aptamer-based biosensors，the large surface area of MOFs allows high-density immobilization of aptamers，enabling highly specific and sensitive detection of targets in complex matrices. These methods offer high sensitivity，specificity，and potential portability，providing innovative solutions for detecting trace contaminants in the complex matrix of aquatic products. Furthermore，this review discusses the challenges and future prospects of MOFs for the analysis of aquatic products. The significant challenges include the limited hydrolytic stability or chemical stability of certain MOFs in complex media，potential matrix effects in real samples that can affect performance，and the need for scalable and cost-effective synthesis of functionalized MOFs. Future efforts should focus on designing more stable and target-specific functionalized MOFs，promoting the integration of sample pretreatment and detection processes，and incorporating artificial intelligence for data analysis to establish an intelligent rapid detection system for aquatic product safety，which is of great significance for safeguarding public health.
