records.title: AURKA, BIRC5 and AURKB as core signature genes associated with endocrine-disrupting chemical exposure in Hepatocellular carcinoma.
records.abstract: PurposeThis study aimed to systematically explore the molecular mechanisms of Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) induced by endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) and identify core signature genes with clinical utility.MethodsBioinformatics analysis, machine learning, and in vitro experiments were integrated. TCGA-LIHC (The Cancer Genome Atlas-Liver Hepatocellular carcinoma) and GSE76427 datasets were used for target screening and validation. Toxicological analysis, target prediction, functional enrichment, Protein-protein interaction (PPI) network, and three machine learning algorithms were applied to prioritize signature genes. In vitro experiments verified the effects of single EDC on HCC cells and gene dependence.ResultsAURKA (Aurora Kinase A), BIRC5 (Baculoviral IAP Repeat Containing 5) and AURKB (Aurora Kinase B) were identified as core signature genes, consistently upregulated in HCC with AUC (area under the curve) > 0.77. Their low expression correlated with better survival rate. EDCs (e.g., MBP) promoted HCC proliferation and invasion, which was dependent on AURKA. Signature genes negatively correlated with anti-tumor immune infiltration.ConclusionAURKA, BIRC5, and AURKB were identified as candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets potentially mediating EDC-induced HCC, providing insights into EDC-related hepatocarcinogenesis mechanisms.
records.authors: Liu Q, Zhu H, Gao H, Yang F, Zhang S, Wang X, Hao Y, Niu Z, Zhou X.

records.title: Metabolic cascades drive spatial prebiotic fermentation in a defined gut consortium
records.abstract: Dietary fiber deficiency shifts the gut microbiota to degrade host mucus, compromising intestinal homeostasis. Mechanistically linking in vitro metabolic dynamics of fiber degradation to in vivo outcomes remains challenging due to a lack of representative model systems. Introducing spatial mucin structures to a defined Oligo-Mouse-Microbiota (OMM12) in vitro consortium allowed us to recapitulate the spatio-temporal dynamics of xylooligosaccharide (XOS) processing in gnotobiotic mice. XOS supplementation rapidly established a stable community state in vitro and in vivo across compositional, metabolic and transcriptional levels. XOS supplementation established distinct functional guilds: Bifidobacterium animalis and Blautia coccoides partitioning xylose and arabinose catabolism, whilst profiting from XOS degradation by Bacteroides caecimuris. Along the colonic axis, a spatial XOS gradient exposes Bl. coccoides's substrate preference for xylose and drives longitudinal functional adaptations. Altogether, our predictive platform proves that regional microenvironments govern prebiotic efficacy, highlighting spatial cascades as essential parameters for targeted microbiome interventions.
records.authors: Berthold DL, Realini NR, Sichert A, Hausmann A, Sauer U.

records.title: Integrative multi-omics re-analysis of public sequencing and metabolomics repositories defines the mucosal immune and metabolic landscape of  Helicobacter pylori  infection and supports CagW as a rational mRNA-LNP vaccine antigen
records.abstract: Background  Helicobacter pylori colonises 40-45% of the global population, is a WHO Group I carcinogen, and is increasingly hard to eradicate amid rising resistance; no vaccine is licensed. CagW, a VirB6-family cagPAI component, has been advanced as a DNA-vaccine antigen that protects mice; a codon-optimised CagW-Fc mRNA in lipid nanoparticles (mRNA-LNP) is a candidate antigen design intended to engage humoral and cellular immunity. To define the infected gastric mucosal niche in which such a vaccine must operate, we mined public sequencing, single-cell and metabolomics repositories.  Methods  NCBI GEO, MetaboLights and NCBI Protein were interrogated. Bulk transcriptomes of  H. pylori -infected vs uninfected gastric epithelial cells (GSE295523; 24 libraries: HGC27, AGS, MKN45, GES-1) were re-analysed with a cell-line-blocked design; DEGs (BH-adjusted) were annotated via g:Profiler (GO, KEGG, Reactome) and 13 functional signatures scored. Single-cell composition was quantified from a mouse gastric scRNA-seq atlas (GSE224840; 16,434 cells) and sorted gastric CD8+ tissue-resident memory (TRM) vs splenic memory T cells (GSE216894). Targeted gastric metabolomics was re-analysed for epithelial ornithine decarboxylase (Odc) deletion (MTBLS3235) and cystathionine-gamma-lyase (Cth) deletion (MTBLS2851). CagW conservation was computed across 400 NCBI records (286 variants) with Kyte-Doolittle topology and four B cell epitope scales.  Results  Infection induced 326 up- and 115 down-regulated genes (FDR  1), dominated by TNF/NF-kappaB (KEGG hsa04668, P=5.5×10-11), integrated stress response (ATF4-CHAC1-DDIT3-TRIB3-ASNS) and Th17 chemokines (CXCL8 +3.43, CCL20 +1.32, CXCL1 +1.30, IL23A +1.02). MHC-I presentation rose (Delta-z +0.76; MHC-II unchanged); the arginine/polyamine module (SLC7A1 +1.19, ARG2 +1.33, SAT1 +1.50, ODC1 +0.58) was co-induced. scRNA-seq showed immune expansion in infected mucosa (39.8% vs 21.2% cells; OR 2.46; cell-level frequencies reported descriptively because cells are not independent; direction confirmed at sample level, n=4 vs 4), driven by plasmacytoid DCs (OR 8.9), neutrophils (OR 3.0), macrophages (OR 2.7) and cDCs (OR 2.1), with epithelial de-differentiation. Gastric CD8+ TRM cells showed a residency-effector program (Itgae +6.2, Cd69 +2.3, Gzmb +4.8, Ifng +5.3) with egress-gene loss (Sell -11.4, S1pr1 -9.7, Klf2 -5.2). Metabolomics confirmed both nodes: Odc deletion raised arginine (+3.08) and Cth deletion raised spermidine (+0.40) while lowering leukotriene B4 (-0.33). CagW was conserved across 286 variants (median 98.3% identity; 96.4% residues >=95% conserved), carried four transmembrane helices, and showed a surface-biased conserved epitope envelope at residues 505-530 and 63-79. Conclusions  Public multi-omics define an NF-kappaB/ATF4-driven, Th17-polarised, metabolically stressed niche where antigen-presenting cells expand, epithelium de-differentiates, and CD8+ TRM cells act locally. Here CagW is exceptional among cagPAI antigens: near-universal conservation plus an accessible, conserved surface. These findings provide a systems-level rationale for prioritising CagW as a conserved, epitope-accessible vaccine antigen and inform next-generation multi-antigen designs.

records.title: In vivo frataxin expression of a triplex purified minicircle.
records.abstract: Friedreich's ataxia (FRDA) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder caused by (GAA•TTC)n repeat expansions in the Frataxin (FXN) gene, resulting in reduced expression of Frataxin, a mitochondrial protein essential for energy production and iron-sulfur cluster assembly. Minicircles (MCs) are non-viral DNA vectors offering improved safety and efficiency over conventional plasmids. We used a novel method to purify MCs using biotin-conjugated triplex-forming and strand-invading oligonucleotides (ONs). A 21 bp H-DNA-forming sequence was incorporated into the plasmids to enhance binding specificity of the ONs. The ON-plasmid complexes were removed using streptavidin magnetic beads. This approach yielded highly purified MCs. In FRDA patient-derived fibroblasts, the purified MCs expressed FXN mRNA and restored Frataxin protein levels to those observed in healthy cells, demonstrating the therapeutic potential of this approach. More interestingly, MC-FXN treatment of an FRDA mouse model using hydrodynamic tail vein injection resulted in an 18-fold and 3-fold increase of Frataxin in the mice livers and hearts, respectively, supporting the translational relevance of this modality.

records.title: Analysis of antiviral effects of anti-EGFR DNA aptamers against African swine fever virus in Vero cells.
records.abstract: African swine fever virus (ASFV) causes high mortality in pigs and severe socio-economic losses worldwide. With no effective vaccines or antiviral drugs currently available, novel therapeutic strategies are urgently needed. Since ASFV exploits the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) for host cell entry, targeting EGFR could reduce viral uptake. We developed novel EGFR-specific DNA aptamers and investigated their anti-ASFV and virucidal activities using cytopathic effect (CPE)-based assays in Vero cells. Aptamer safety was evaluated by assessing cytotoxicity and genotoxicity using the MTT and comet assays, respectively. Aptamers showed no virucidal, cytotoxic, or genotoxic activity. Treatment of Vero cells with the dimeric anti-EGFR aptamer significantly reduced viral titers by 47% at 10 μM without cytotoxic or genotoxic effects. We also report, for the first time, that cetuximab (an anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody) at concentrations 0.017 and 0.034 μM reduced ASFV titers by 43-57% comparable to that of the dimeric aptamer. These findings identify the dimeric anti-EGFR aptamer as a promising compound for further analysis of antiviral effectiveness against ASFV in porcine macrophages in vitro and in vivo.

records.title: CRISPR/Cas9-directed engineering of Clostridium beijerinckii enhanced butanol production from whey permeate.
records.abstract: Whey permeate (WP), an abundant, lactose-rich byproduct of the dairy industry, constitutes an environmental and economic burden on the industry. Despite the high fermentable sugar content of WP, its bioconversion to biobutanol is limited by poor lactose-utilization culminating in low solvent productivity by native solventogenic microorganisms. In this study, we report CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome engineering of Clostridium beijerinckii NCIMB 8052 (hereafter, C. beijerinckii) to improve butanol production from lactose-rich WP. A native putative lactose transporter encoded by Cbei_4545 and an aldehyde reductase (mgR) from Clostridium pasteurianum were integrated into the chromosome of C. beijerinckii at the acetoacetate decarboxylase gene locus to improve lactose utilization and solvent production. The resulting recombinant strain was evaluated alongside the wildtype using lactose, untreated WP, and ion exchange (Amberlite™) resin-treated WP. Across all feedstocks tested, the recombinant strain consistently outperformed the wildtype, producing peak butanol titers of 7.9 g/L, 9.7 g/L, and 20.9 g/L on lactose, WP, and resin-treated WP, respectively, compared to 4.3 g/L, 7.1 g/L, and 11.3 g/L for the wildtype. These results demonstrate the utility of targeted CRISPR/Cas9 genome engineering to substantially improve lactose utilization and butanol production in C. beijerinckii. In this work we constructed a strain of C. beijerinckii with strong potential for conversion of abundant and cost-effective WP to biobutanol.

records.title: DNA-PK inhibition overcomes resistance to oncolytic virotherapy.
records.abstract: Oncolytic virotherapy is a promising therapeutic strategy that uses replication-competent viruses to selectively destroy malignancies. However, the therapeutic effect of certain oncolytic viruses (OVs) varies among cancer patients. Thus, it is necessary to overcome resistance to OVs through rationally designed combination strategies. Here, through an anticancer drug screening, we show that DNA-dependent protein kinase (DNA-PK) inhibition sensitizes cancer cells to OV M1 and improves therapeutic effects in refractory cancer models in vivo and in patient tumour samples. Infection of M1 virus triggers the transcription of interferons (IFNs) and the activation of the antiviral response, which can be abolished by pretreatment of DNA-PK inhibitor (DNA-PKI), resulting in selectively enhanced replication of OV M1 within malignancies. Furthermore, DNA-PK inhibition promotes the DNA damage response induced by M1 virus, leading to increased tumour cell apoptosis. Together, our study identifies the combination of DNA-PKI and OV M1 as a potential treatment for cancers.

records.title: cGAS-STING dependent immunity in insects: insights from Drosophila flies.
records.abstract: The cGAS-STING pathway constitutes an evolutionarily ancient antiviral defense mechanism, originating in bacteria. It is conserved in most animals, although with some differences. In insects, the model Drosophila melanogaster provides unique opportunities to decipher the function and regulation of this important pathway in hosts beyond mammals and shed light on its evolution. Here, we review recent advances in Drosophila that clarify the relationship between the cGAS-STING and IMD pathways, which both act through the NF-κB transcription factor Relish. We next consider the expansion of the cGLR family in Drosophila flies and the unexpected discovery of new cyclic dinucleotides (CDNs) besides cGAMP. We present the contribution of these CDNs in induction of systemic immunity and immune training in flies and discuss the conservation of these properties in other insects.
records.authors: Cai H, Wei Z, Huang J, Duan X, Imler JL.

records.title: Identifying phase separation modulators mediated by the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein using a structure-based drug discovery approach.
records.abstract: IntroductionAs severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) continues to evolve through mutations and acquire resistance to existing antiviral agents, the persistence of post-pandemic infections remains a significant global health concern. To address these challenges, it is crucial to develop novel therapeutic agents that target previously unexplored viral or host mechanisms.ObjectivesThe nucleocapsid (N) protein of SARS-CoV-2 plays a critical role in viral RNA replication and genome packaging through its ability to undergo liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS). Targeting the condensation of N-RNA complex could potentially serve as an effective therapeutic strategy against coronavirus infections. The present study provides a successful exemplification of antiviral agent discovery by targeting the viral N protein on the basis of its structural characteristics.MethodsA total of 23 virtual screening compounds and 16 hit derivatives were prepared. Their binding affinity and antiviral activities were evaluated using surface plasmon resonance and immunofluorescence assay, respectively. The impact of these compounds on condensate formation was verified through fluorescence recovery after photobleaching, as well as the inhibition of N condensate formation in cells.ResultsStructure-based virtual screening, target protein binding affinity quantification, and cell culture-based anti-SARS-CoV-2 assays enabled the identification a hit compound, D21. Subsequent structural optimization of series I and II yielded compound II8, which exhibits stronger binding affinity for the N protein and effectively inhibits the formation of N-RNA condensates, thereby demonstrating its potential to modulate LLPS, a mechanism underlying its antiviral activity. In vivo evaluation showed that II8 displays antiviral activity in a human ACE2-expressing mouse model when administered intranasally as a pre-incubated mixture with SARS-CoV-2. Due to the pharmacokinetic profile of compound II8, further structural modifications are still required.ConclusionOur findings suggest that compound II8 may serve as a localized prophylactic nasal spray, providing valuable insights for further development of LLPS modulators as next-generation antiviral agents.
records.authors: Du S, Jang Y, Hu X, Li P, Wang B, Ra HS, Kang D, Wang X, Wang N, Liu X, Kim M, Zhan P.

records.title: A zinc-sequestering polymer disrupts zinc homeostasis to suppress fungal viability and virulence.
records.abstract: Zinc is a central structural cofactor in fungi, supporting transcriptional control and mitochondrial function, and its tightly regulated homeostasis presents an underexploited antifungal intervention point. Targeting zinc-dependent architectures offers a mechanistically distinct alternative to conventional membrane- or cell wall-directed antifungals. Here we report a zinc- deprivation fungicide (ZDF) by grafting high-affinity bipyridine chelators onto ε-poly-l-lysine, enabling intracellular sequestration of labile zinc without overt membrane disruption. ZDF-induced zinc depletion disrupts zinc-dependent RNA processing, particularly mitochondrial tRNA modification, thereby collapsing mitochondrial translation, impairing oxidative phosphorylation, and inducing profound energetic failure. ZDF further remodels zinc-dependent regulatory networks, downregulating drug efflux to restore azole-resistant strains and suppressing biofilm maturation via zinc-responsive Zap1-Dpp1-farnesol axis. This strategy shows high selectivity over mammalian cells, and outperforms clinical azoles in murine cutaneous wound and rabbit keratitis models. By employing the unique role of zinc as an essential structural cofactor for fungal transcriptional regulators, this work defines intracellular zinc sequestration as a non-membrane-directed antifungal strategy that exploits a central regulatory dependency in fungi.

records.title: Integrating single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing with ML algorithms identified MYBL2 as a candidate transcriptomic biomarker for diagnosing laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC).
records.abstract: Laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) poses significant clinical challenges due to pronounced tumor heterogeneity. To identify robust, consistent biomarkers across cohorts, we integrated bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data from GSE127165 and GSE142083 and validated candidate biomarkers in the external cohort GSE13060. Candidate gene prioritization incorporated differentially expressed genes, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) results, and markers of malignant epithelial cells exhibiting high copy number variation (High-CNV) derived from single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) (GSE206332). Additional analyses included functional enrichment, immune association (adjusted for tumor purity), quasi-temporal analysis, and CellChat inference to elucidate the biological roles of top genes. The integrated approach identified 254 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), comprising 86 upregulated and 168 downregulated genes. WGCNA revealed a tumor-associated module containing 870 genes. Intersecting these findings with high-CNV malignant epithelial markers reduced the candidate pool to 16 genes, and LASSO regression retained five key features: MYBL2, KRT17, UCHL1, PTHLH, and ODC1. Among these, MYBL2 demonstrated the strongest and most consistent performance. MYBL2 was further associated with proliferative programs, including E2F targets, the G2/M checkpoint, DNA repair, and MYC targets. Gene signatures from these subclusters were enriched in bulk tumors and positively correlated with MYBL2 expression in independent cohorts. The results also indicate that MYBL2-high malignant epithelial states are linked to distinct connectivity patterns within the tumor microenvironment.
records.authors: Mehrabi T, Isavi M, Gholami A, Hamidieh AA, Heidarzadeh-Pilehrood R.

records.title: Dual-vector nanoengineered mRNA-CRISPR delivery systems for precision gene therapy in choroidal melanoma.
records.abstract: Choroidal melanoma is the most common primary intraocular malignancy, and effective gene therapy remains limited by ocular barriers, tumor heterogeneity, and inefficient nucleic acid delivery. This review critically analyses the molecular rationale, engineering principles, emerging nanoarchitectures, biological validation, and translational prospects of dual-vector nanoengineered mRNA-CRISPR delivery systems for precision gene therapy in choroidal melanoma. The manuscript also highlights key challenges and future strategies for clinical implementation. Current evidence indicates that dual-vector platforms enable independent optimization of mRNA and CRISPR cargos while maintaining coordinated spatiotemporal therapeutic activity. We conducted a literature search in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for relevant studies published from January 2015 to September 2026. Functional cargo partitioning, vector modularity, programmable intracellular trafficking, and ocular-targeted nanoengineering improve delivery precision and reduce biological compromise associated with co-encapsulation. Lipid, polymeric, hybrid, biomimetic, and viral-nonviral architectures each provide distinct engineering advantages depending on therapeutic objectives. Preclinical studies support enhanced genome editing, transient protein restoration, improved tumor suppression, and reduced off-target effects. Nevertheless, manufacturing scalability, regulatory standardization, long-term safety, and clinical validation remain major barriers to translation. Dual-vector nanoengineered mRNA-CRISPR systems represent a promising next-generation platform for precision gene therapy in choroidal melanoma by enabling coordinated and programmable therapeutic delivery. Continued advances in modular nanoengineering, personalized cargo selection, and clinically scalable manufacturing will be essential for successful translation into precision ocular oncology.
records.authors: Thakur SK, Malviya R, Chandra P, Sridhar SB, Shareef J, Wadhwa T.

records.title: Systematic assessment of transcriptomic and phenotypic biological profiling for mechanism-based hazard assessment using target-annotated reference chemicals in renal proximal tubular epithelial cells.
records.abstract: Integrating high-throughput in vitro data into next-generation risk assessment (NGRA) workflows requires screening strategies that yield quantitative potency estimates and mechanistically interpretable biological signals. Transcriptomic and morphological profiling are increasingly adopted for early-stage hazard identification by enabling triage of substances for resource-intensive follow-up and prioritizing candidates most likely to present meaningful risk. In this study, we aimed to characterize biological concordance and uncertainty by quantifying how well high-throughput transcriptomics (HTTr) and Cell Painting PLUS (CPP) bioactivity profiles recover target-relevant biological signals in immortalized human renal proximal tubule epithelial RPTEC/TERT1 cells using 313 reference chemicals with high-confidence target annotations. Through quality control procedures and biological activity filters we yielded 142 reference chemicals spanning 66 different targets, which were systematically evaluated for biological concentration-responses by HTTr and CPP. HTTr was evaluated using TXG-MAPr-based qualitative and quantitative gene network activity analysis. HTTr showed the most prominent activity for targets that were highest expressed in RPTEC/TERT1 cells. Active chemical-pairs showed strong gene network activity correlation albeit with different potencies. Similarly, the highest transcriptomic concordance was observed for reference chemicals acting in the same pathway, such as EGFR/MEK or PI3K/AKT/mTOR. CPP often showed high sensitivity primarily at the organelle level providing limited mechanistic insight for chemical grouping. Collectively, the results support HTTr and CPP as complementary early-tier assays within an in vitro weight-of-evidence safety testing framework. Although CPP is suitable as a cost-effective screening modality, HTTr offers higher mechanistic resolution for mode-of-action inference in high-throughput bioactivity screening and therefore remains necessary for high-confidence mechanistic interpretation.

records.title: JrTTG2 confers drought tolerance in walnut via the JrGSTU8-mediated antioxidant pathway and interaction with JrEPSIN1.
records.abstract: Drought significantly limits the productivity and quality of Juglans regia, yet the regulatory mechanisms governing drought tolerance in this economically vital nut tree remain largely elusive. Here, we report that the WRKY transcription factor JrTTG2 acts as a central hub in the walnut drought response by integrating transcriptional and protein-interaction networks. We identified JrTTG2 as a hypersensitive early-response gene, exhibiting a robust 333-fold induction in walnut roots under drought stress. Ectopic expression of JrTTG2 in Arabidopsis and poplar significantly enhanced drought tolerance, primarily by maintaining root architecture, increasing biomass, and reducing oxidative damage. Conversely, RNAi-mediated silencing of PagTTG2 in poplar led to stunted root systems and compromised antioxidant defense under water deficit. Transcriptomic and molecular analyses revealed that JrTTG2 directly binds to the W-box in the promoter of the JrGSTU8 gene to activate its transcription, thereby facilitating ROS scavenging. Furthermore, yeast two-hybrid and BiFC assays demonstrated that JrTTG2 physically interacts with the vesicle trafficking protein JrEPSIN1. Both JrGSTU8 and JrEPSIN1 showed highly synchronized induction with JrTTG2 in walnut roots during drought. Taken together, this study provides a novel dimension to the molecular mechanisms of woody plant adaptation and offers a promising candidate gene for breeding drought-tolerant walnut varieties.
records.authors: Li D, Peng S, Lu Y, Xie M, Wang T, Chen S, Xu ZF, Yang G.

records.title: Multimodal profiling and intersectional genetics reveal CA1 border inhibitory neuron diversity and postnatal emergence of retrosplenial connectivity
records.abstract: ABSTRACT  Inhibitory neurons (INs) at the stratum radiatum/stratum lacunosum-moleculare border of hippocampal CA1 comprise diverse populations, including long-range-projecting neurons that innervate the retrosplenial cortex (RSCtx). However, their molecular organization and developmental connectivity remain poorly understood. Here, we combine multimodal transcriptomic profiling, intersectional genetics, and retrograde tracing to characterize CA1 border INs. We identified two major caudal ganglionic eminence-derived,  Cxcl14 -enriched populations distinguished by  Syt6/Cck -related and  Ntng1 -expressing transcriptional profiles. We then generated a  Cxcl14 -Cre mouse line that, when combined with an IN-specific viral enhancer, provides genetic access to CA1 border INs. Retrograde labeling established that CA1 INs projecting to the RSCtx belong to the  Ntng1 -expressing population, and that this long-range projection emerges during postnatal mouse development, between postnatal days 3 and 5. Finally, analysis of genes encoding cell-surface proteins, key regulators of connectivity, revealed distinct expression profiles in RSCtx-projecting and SYT6-positive INs. Together, these findings establish a molecular and developmental framework for CA1 border IN diversity and provide a genetic strategy for investigating the assembly and function of these inhibitory circuits.

records.title: APOSTART1 and APOSTART2 role in female gametophyte progression in Arabidopsis thaliana.
records.abstract: Main conclusionAtAPOSTART1 and AtAPOSTART2 contribute to female gametophyte development in Arabidopsis thaliana, with their mutation affecting megaspore degeneration and female gametophyte progression. Apomixis is a form of asexual seed reproduction that allows clonal plant propagation. Because it does not naturally occur in major crop species, its introduction could enable the fixation of elite hybrid genomes, leading to consistent high-quality yields of grains, fruits, and vegetables. Despite its significance, many aspects of apomictic reproduction remain poorly understood. PpAPOSTART6 was previously identified as a promising candidate gene associated with apomixis in Poa pratensis, a species exhibiting aposporic apomixis. PpAPOSTART6 is expressed in sexual Poa pratensis ovules throughout development, whereas in apomictic accessions, its expression is delayed at later stages of -ovule development. To gain further insight into PpAPOSTART6 function, we have studied the expression and function of its closest orthologs in Arabidopsis thaliana, AtAPO1 and AtAPO2 (formerly EDR2). Analysis of atapo1 atapo2 double mutant revealed defects in spore degeneration and in the proper differentiation of the functional megaspore and subsequent female gametophyte development, supporting a role for AtAPO1 and AtAPO2 in the degeneration of non-functional megaspores. Together with subcellular localization analyses and genetic evidences, our results support a role for AtAPO1 and AtAPO2 in megaspore degeneration, potentially involving programmed cell death and mitochondrial function. These findings provide a functional framework for further investigating PpAPOSTART6 association in apomixis regulation.
records.authors: Petrella R, Gabrieli F, Cavalleri A, Marconi G, Cucinotta M, Albertini E, Colombo L.

records.title: cAMP receptor proteins in mycobacteria.
records.abstract: Cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) signaling is a major regulatory system in mycobacteria, and the cAMP receptor protein (CRP) serves as its principal transcriptional effector. In Mycobacterium tuberculosis, CRP controls a broad regulon associated with metabolic adaptation, respiration, cell envelope-associated processes, dormancy-related resuscitation, and virulence. Structural and biophysical studies have demonstrated that mycobacterial CRPs differ from the classical Escherichia coli paradigm: apo-CRP adopts restrained or asymmetric conformations, whereas cAMP binding promotes a more symmetric, DNA-binding-competent state and enhances the specificity of CRP-DNA interactions. In Mycobacterium smegmatis, the major paralog Crp1 (MSMEG_6189) regulates metabolic and respiratory adaptation, oxidative stress defense, and isoniazid susceptibility, whereas Crp2 (MSMEG_0539) appears to play a more limited or subsidiary role. Recent findings further reveal that CRP activity is modulated by lysine acetylation, cooperative promoter recruitment with the virulence-associated response regulator PhoP, and respiratory inhibition-induced increases in intracellular cAMP, thereby linking metabolic and respiratory status to adaptive and virulence-associated gene regulation. This review summarizes the structure, allosteric regulation, regulon, and physiological functions of mycobacterial CRPs, highlighting their role as central integrators of cAMP signaling, respiratory and metabolic state, persistence-associated physiology, and antibiotic susceptibility.
records.authors: Oh JI, Oh Y, Hwang Y.

records.title: Towards personalized and lifestyle-inspired soil management: lessons from the gut microbiome.
records.abstract: Soil microorganisms are key drivers of ecosystem functions supporting biodiversity, food production, and climate regulation. Restoring multiple ecosystem functions under intensive land-use and climate change requires steering microbiome composition. However, this remains challenging due to the high complexity of soils and the assembly rules of their microbiomes. As the extensively studied human gut microbiome has considerable similarities with the soil microbiome, we explore advances in steering the human gut microbiome composition to improve the steering of soil microbiomes.

records.title: SerRS2 Identifies an Inflamed-Exhausted Hepatocellular Carcinoma Phenotype with Enhanced DNA-Sensing and Increased Anti-PD-1 Responsiveness.
records.abstract: BackgroundSeryl-tRNA synthetase 2 (SerRS2, encoded by SARS2) is a mitochondrial aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase essential for mitochondrial protein translation and homeostasis. Its clinical and immunological significance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains unclear.MethodsTranscriptomic and clinical data from 371 TCGA-LIHC patients were analyzed to evaluate SerRS2 expression, prognosis, immune infiltration, T-cell exhaustion, and DNA-sensing-related features. Four single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets were analyzed to characterize the cellular distribution of SerRS2. Public immunotherapy cohorts were evaluated for associations between SerRS2 expression and immune checkpoint blockade outcomes, and an independent HCC cohort was used for qPCR validation. Group comparisons were performed using Student's t-test or Wilcoxon rank-sum test, correlations using Pearson or Spearman analyses, and survival outcomes using Kaplan-Meier analysis with the Log rank test, as appropriate.ResultsSerRS2 was significantly upregulated in HCC and associated with advanced pathological stage and poorer survival. Elevated SerRS2 expression was consistently associated with increased CD8+ T-cell infiltration and exhausted T-cell abundance and positively correlated with PDCD1, TOX, LAG3, HAVCR2, and CTLA4. SerRS2 was also positively associated with cGAS (MB21D1) and DDX41, but not STING1, and SerRS2-high tumors exhibited increased exhaustion and DNA-sensing scores. Collectively, these findings support a SerRS2-associated inflamed-exhausted immune phenotype characterized by increased CD8+ T-cell infiltration, T-cell exhaustion-related features, and enrichment of DNA-sensing-related transcriptional programs. Single-cell analyses revealed heterogeneous SerRS2 expression across multiple cellular compartments, supporting its interpretation as a tissue-level rather than tumor-cell-specific signal. In public cross-tumor immunotherapy cohorts, elevated SerRS2 expression was associated with improved outcomes following PD-1 blockade, whereas comparable associations were not consistently observed for PD-L1 or CTLA-4 blockade, suggesting potential relevance of the SerRS2-associated immune phenotype to PD-1 blockade. These immune associations were further supported by qPCR validation in an independent HCC cohort.ConclusionSerRS2 is associated with an inflamed-exhausted immune phenotype in HCC and may represent a candidate tissue-level biomarker for immune stratification. Its potential relevance to PD-1 blockade warrants prospective validation in HCC-specific immunotherapy cohorts.
records.authors: Li P, Zhu G, Li D, Liang M, Zhang L, Li J, Jia Y, Zou B.

records.title: Targeting Skin Hyperpigmentation with Nature-Derived Tyrosinase Inhibitors: Sources, Mechanisms, and Translational Challenges.
records.abstract: Skin hyperpigmentation represents a highly prevalent dermatological issue that severely affects skin appearance and quality of life. Tyrosinase is well recognized as the critical rate-limiting enzyme in the melanin biosynthesis pathway, making it a prime target for skin-lightening interventions. Although synthetic depigmenting agents are widely used in cosmetics, their clinical applications are severely restricted by safety concerns, skin irritation, and chemical instability. In recent years, natural tyrosinase inhibitors originating from plants, fungi, marine organisms, and microbial metabolites have attracted extensive attention due to their promising efficacy, structural diversity, and multi-target activities, although long-term clinical and systemic safety data remain limited. This review comprehensively summarizes the molecular mechanisms underlying melanogenesis inhibition by natural compounds, their major biological sources, and representative active components, as well as key evidence from in vitro enzymatic assays, cellular models, and human clinical trials. We further discuss critical challenges in formulation development, including chemical instability, insufficient skin permeability, and safety considerations for long-term topical use. Finally, future research directions and translational opportunities are explored. By integrating recent advances and unresolved bottlenecks, this review aims to provide a scientific basis and rational guidance for the design and development of safe and effective natural-based skin-lightening products.
records.authors: Sun Z, Li Y, Wang X, Wang R, Ma W.

records.title: MicroRNA-26 Family in Human Diseases: Context-Dependent Regulation, Biomarker Potential, and Preclinical Nano-Delivery Strategies.
records.abstract: PurposeThis review aims to summarize the expression patterns, molecular mechanisms, and preclinical nanodelivery strategies of microRNA-26 (miR-26) family members, and to critically evaluate their potential as biomarker candidates and preclinical therapeutic targets in human diseases, including cancers, cardiovascular diseases, metabolic disorders, and neurodegenerative conditions.MethodsA structured narrative review was performed in PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar from database inception to August 2026. Peer-reviewed original articles and reviews in English were included. Data on miR-26 isoform expression, target genes, signaling pathways, therapeutic modulators, and nanocarrier systems were extracted and narratively synthesized. A four-tier evidence classification system (Levels I-IV) was applied to distinguish well-established findings from speculative or inferred associations.ResultsmiR-26 family members-predominantly miR-26a-5p and miR-26b-5p-are highly conserved small non-coding RNAs that post-transcriptionally regulate proliferation, differentiation, apoptosis, metabolism, and immunity in an isoform-specific and context-dependent manner. In most solid tumors, miR-26a-5p and miR-26b-5p are downregulated and function as tumor suppressors, although context-dependent oncogenic roles exist. Circulating and tissue miR-26 isoform levels show statistically significant associations with diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment response in several cancers, supporting their utility as biomarker candidates. However, direct miR-26 mimics or inhibitors remain exclusively preclinical, with no human clinical trials initiated to date. Lipid-, polymer-, and inorganic-based nanocarriers are being explored in preclinical models, but their precision, safety, and biodistribution require systematic validation. Clinical-stage agents targeting downstream effectors of miR-26-regulated pathways do not constitute direct miR-26 modulation and should not be presented as miR-26 therapeutics.ConclusionmiR-26 family members serve as versatile regulatory hubs and biologically plausible biomarker and preclinical therapeutic target candidates. At present, miR-26 should be viewed primarily as a validated biomarker associate and a promising preclinical target-not as an established therapeutic modality. CRISPRa, microbiome-miR-26 interactions, and AI-assisted nanorobots remain future hypotheses rather than established translational strategies.
records.authors: Wang R, Ge R, Li Z, He Z, Pan Y, Zhao X.

records.title: Dietary caffeic acid phenethyl ester alleviates copper-induced hepatointestinal damage by modulating lipid metabolism, intestinal microbiota, and oxidative-inflammatory responses in yellow catfish (Pelteobagrus fulvidraco).
records.abstract: The widespread application of copper (Cu) in aquaculture poses severe hepatointestinal toxicity risks to teleosts. This study investigated the ameliorative effects of dietary caffeic acid phenethyl ester (CAPE) on Cu-induced hepatointestinal damage in yellow catfish (Pelteobagrus fulvidraco). Following a four-week feeding trial with graded CAPE (0, 200 (LCAPE), and 1000 mg/kg (HCAPE)) intervention and a subsequent 7-day Cu challenge (0.8 mg/L), Cu-exposed fish exhibited elevated mortality, growth retardation, hepatic steatosis, and systemic oxidative stress. Concurrently, Cu toxicity disrupted the intestinal microecology by depleting commensal taxa potentially associated with host homeostasis (e.g., Phyllobacterium and Methylobacterium) and favouring stress-associated or potentially opportunistic taxa (e.g., Sediminibacterium and Bradyrhizobium). Conversely, CAPE intervention, particularly the HCAPE group, effectively improved survival rate, fortified intestinal physical barriers (increased goblet cell number and zo1 expression), and alleviated hepatic triglyceride accumulation. CAPE intervention enhanced intestinal and hepatic antioxidative capacity and alleviated Cu-induced lipid dysmetabolism and tissue lesions, which might be associated with the potential regulation of the SIRT1/FXR signalling axis and the PKC/p38MAPK/NF-κB inflammatory pathway. However, the LCAPE group did not resolve transcriptional inflammation, exhibiting elevated hepatic nfκb and il1β as well as increased intestinal il1β and reduced zo1 expression relative to the Cu group. Furthermore, CAPE induced a dose-dependent modulation of the intestinal microbiota composition; the LCAPE group significantly restructured the taxonomic composition, enriching commensal genera such as Variovorax while reducing the relative abundance of potentially opportunistic genera including Sediminibacterium and Staphylococcus. In contrast, the HCAPE group exhibited negligible genus-level differences compared to the Cu group. In conclusion, dietary CAPE alleviates Cu-induced hepatointestinal injury in yellow catfish, an effect associated with improved lipid metabolic parameters, altered intestinal microbial composition, and enhanced antioxidative and anti-inflammatory defences, highlighting its protective application in fish under Cu exposure.
records.journal: Comparative biochemistry and physiology. Part D, Genomics & proteomics
records.authors: Wang L, Xue X, Li Y, Cao J, Wang S, Li J, Liu S, Chu L.

records.title: Microplastics amplify Cr(VI)-mediated RP4 plasmid conjugative transfer through coupled interfacial, oxidative, and metabolic regulation.
records.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) can accumulate heavy metals and influence plasmid-mediated antibiotic resistance gene (ARGs) transfer, yet the regulatory mechanisms under metal-associated MP exposure remain poorly understood. Here, a polystyrene microplastic-Cr(VI) composite (PSMPs@Cr) was established to investigate RP4 plasmid conjugative transfer by integrating physicochemical characterization, physiological measurements, transcriptomic analysis, and multivariable modeling. PSMPs@Cr exhibited a non-monotonic effect on conjugative transfer, with the highest conjugative transfer frequency (9.4 × 10-2) observed at 20 ppm Cr loading, representing a 4.75-fold increase compared with the control. Cr adsorption reconstructed the MP interface by modifying surface charge, wettability, morphology, and colloidal stability, which was accompanied by altered bacterial adhesion behavior. Meanwhile, PSMPs@Cr exposure induced coordinated changes in ROS accumulation, antioxidant responses, ATP production, membrane-associated functions, and energy metabolism. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed treatment-dependent regulation of oxidative stress, membrane transport, cellular communication, and metabolic pathways. Random forest-SHAP analysis identified zeta potential, CAT activity, ATP, and ROS as relatively important variables associated with CTF variation. Overall, PSMPs@Cr-associated ARGs transfer was linked to coupled interfacial, redox, and energetic processes rather than a single regulatory pathway, providing new insights into how microplastic-metal interactions influence plasmid-mediated horizontal gene transfer under complex contaminant exposure scenarios.
records.authors: Zhang L, Zhang J, Pan H, Li H, Guo H, Wang T.

records.title: Environmental determinants of large vessel vasculitis onset: a scoping review with complementary narrative synthesis of genetic susceptibility.
records.abstract: ObjectivesLarge vessel vasculitis (LVV), including giant cell arteritis (GCA) and Takayasu arteritis (TAK), are rare immune-mediated disorders characterized by inflammation of large arteries. Epidemiological patterns, marked geographic gradients, age and sex differences, and temporal clustering, suggest that environmental factors contribute to disease onset in genetically susceptible individuals, yet no systematic mapping of this evidence exists. The study sought to systematically map current evidence on environmental exposures investigated in relation to LVV onset, identify methodological gaps, and characterize research priorities. Genetic susceptibility data were additionally synthesized to contextualize gene-environment interactions.MethodsWe conducted a scoping review following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed and Embase were searched from inception to August 2026. Studies were eligible if they assessed environmental exposures in relation to GCA or TAK onset using an epidemiological design with a comparator group, Mendelian randomization, or mechanistic approach with direct relevance to human susceptibility. Genetic susceptibility was synthesized through a complementary narrative review.ResultsOf 3,596 records identified, 2,137 were screened after deduplication, and 44 studies were included in the narrative synthesis, of which 34 with established temporality and epidemiological design were summarized in a structured evidence table. Air pollution, infections, antibiotic use, hormonal exposures, and cardiometabolic factors emerge as candidate environmental modulators of LVV onset, although causal links remain uncertain. Genetic susceptibility implicates antigen presentation, immune regulation, innate immune activation, and vascular remodeling pathways, which likely modulate individual responsiveness to environmental triggers.ConclusionsThis review identifies multiple candidate environmental exposures in LVV and highlights critical methodological gaps regarding exposure timing and genomic integration. Integrative exposomic-genomic approaches represent the critical next step toward identifying modifiable risk factors and preventive strategies.
records.authors: Pacoureau L, Barde F, Yates M, Pagnoux C, Nguyen Y, Seror R.

records.title: A MultiOmics time-resolved systems map of gene regulation in  Toxoplasma gondii
records.abstract: Understanding how  T. gondii builds an invasion-competent cell has been limited by its rapid, asynchronous division cycle, incomplete gene function annotation, and studies that have examined one regulator or complex at a time. Here, we placed acute perturbation of 21 transcriptional and epigenetic factors, promoter occupancy, chromatin accessibility, and molecular validation on a common single-cell clock. The resulting consensus map links the lytic-cycle programs to candidate activating and repressive inputs, organizes genes into 108 co-regulated communities, and nominates regulatory partnerships that would not have emerged from any single data type. The work bridges three longstanding gaps: it resolves perturbation responses in cell-cycle time, distinguishes promoter occupancy from perturbation-linked regulation, and turns a large multidimensional dataset into an experimentally navigable map. We indeed confirmed known factor interactions such as MORC/HDAC3, and recovered combinations such as the Cdc5/SNIP1 and DMAP1/EPL1 as coregulatory nodes (that in other systems have been described to cooperate). Furthermore, we discovered a novel apicomplexan specific combination of AAF1/AP2XI-5 that provides mechanistic insights of the unique AP2 transcription factor family.

records.title: Fe-N Bonded g-C<sub>3</sub>N<sub>4</sub>/LaFeO<sub>3</sub> S-Scheme Heterojunction Nanosheets as a Sunlight-Driven Photocatalytic Antimicrobial Platform for Marine Antifouling.
records.abstract: Marine biofouling poses significant challenges to maritime industries and threatens environmental sustainability and ecological security. Photocatalytic antimicrobial platform has emerged as promising antifouling strategy in marine applications. In this study, an S-scheme heterostructure of g-C3N4/LaFeO3 nanosheets with Fe─N bonding is constructed to serve as a highly efficient and stable photocatalytic antimicrobial platform for marine use. The material demonstrates excellent antifouling performance, achieving 99.9% eradication of E. coli and 100% degradation efficiency of methylene blue. Through combined experimental characterization and density functional theory calculations, a unique photochemical-physical synergistic reinforcement mechanism is proposed. The S-scheme heterojunction, featuring a built-in electric field and Fe─N electron transfer channels, not only facilitates charge transfer and separation but also lowers the reaction energy barrier of key intermediates and accelerates surface photocatalytic kinetics, thereby promoting continuous reactive oxygen species generation. Furthermore, the nanosheet structures exhibit strong electrostatic attraction toward bacterial cell membranes, leading to physical insertion and membrane damage. This synergistic mechanism contributes to outstanding antibacterial and biofilm inhibition performance. Notably, the exceptional antifouling efficacy is maintained for approximately 180 d in real marine environments. These results underscore the practical potential and feasibility of the developed platform for real-world applications in shallow sea settings.
records.authors: Ran L, Zhang Y, Tang Q, Leung MKH, Ran B.

records.title: Creation and evaluation of induced allotetraploids from wild Arachis species expands the genetic reservoir for peanut early leaf spot resistance.
records.abstract: Early leaf spot (ELS), caused by Passalora arachidicola, remains one of the most economically important foliar diseases of peanut (Arachis hypogaea), and resistance within the cultivated germplasm is limited. Fungicide applications are commonly used to manage this disease, but this practice increases production costs, the risk of fungicide resistance, and environmental concerns. Wild Arachis species harbor diverse resistance alleles, but their direct use in breeding is constrained by ploidy barriers. In this study, eight induced allotetraploids derived from nine wild Arachis species were produced. Along with their diploid parents, they were evaluated for ELS resistance using in vitro detached leaf bioassays. Disease resistance was quantified using multiple components, including incubation period, lesion number, sporulation, and diseased leaf area. Several allotetraploids-particularly MagDio1, MagKuhl1, MagHoeh1, and ValMicro1-exhibited significantly reduced lesion development, limited sporulation, and slower disease progression compared with cultivated controls. In all cases, induced allotetraploids displayed resistance levels equal to or greater than those of both diploid parents, indicating enhanced resistance following allotetraploidization. Notably, Arachis hoehnei and its derived allotetraploid consistently exhibited strong resistance across disease components, identifying this phylogenetically distinct species as a novel resistance source. These results demonstrate that induced allotetraploids represent peanut-compatible reservoirs of diverse ELS resistance alleles and provide practical resources for breeding programs aimed at developing cultivars with more durable and diversified resistance to early leaf spot.
records.authors: Dong A, Hopkins M, Bertioli D, Leal-Bertioli S.

records.title: Recurrent Neurodevelopmental Disorder Associated With a Dominant-Negative TOP2B H63Y Variant.
records.abstract: We describe a 7 year-old boy with severe neurodevelopmental disorder, medically-refractory epileptic encephalopathy, hyperkinetic movement disorder, hypotonia, cerebral and cerebellar atrophy and hypomyelination who was found to have a heterozygous de novo TOP2B NM_001330700.2:c.187C>T, p.(His63Tyr) variant. This is the third individual reported with the H63Y variant and severe neurodevelopmental disorder. The phenotype associated with the H63Y variant differs greatly from the TOP2B-related Immunodeficiency and Congenital Anomalies Spectrum (TICAS) syndrome that has been reported with heterozygous loss-of-function variants affecting the TOPRIM domain and adjacent regions of TOP2B. DNA topoisomerase II beta (TOP2B) is an essential enzyme that resolves DNA supercoils and knots to facilitate transcription and replication. To investigate the functional impact of this variant, we studied the homologous yeast variant, top2 H20Y (H20Y). Homozygous H20Y strains exhibited reduced viability, while heterozygous H20Y acted as a loss-of-function allele incapable of supporting growth. Overexpression of the chimeric human H63Y variant in yeast was lethal. Despite its dysfunction, H63Y retains partial enzymatic activity and appears to function as a dominant negative variant that induces DNA damage. Thus, this work establishes a novel gene-disease association between TOP2B-H63Y and a neurodevelopmental disorder we propose to name TOP2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder. Further studies should elucidate the pathogenic mechanisms underlying H63Y-associated phenotypes.
records.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
records.authors: Ha ZY, Dinatto L, Meagher K, Guimond C, Friedman JM, Stirling PC, Patel MS.

records.title: Phosphorylation of RpoD upregulates suilysin and enhances Streptococcus suis virulence.
records.abstract: Streptococcus suis (S. suis) is a prevalent zoonotic pathogen that severely threatens the swine industry and human public health. Suilysin (SLY), a major pore-forming toxin of S. suis, is indispensable for bacterial hemolytic activity and systemic pathogenicity, yet the upstream regulatory mechanism controlling SLY production remains unclear. Serine/threonine kinase (STK) has been characterized to modulate bacterial physiology and virulence by phosphorylating multiple substrate proteins. Our previous phosphoproteomics analysis indicated that the housekeeping sigma factor RpoD was a potential STK substrate. In vitro phosphorylation assays combined with mass spectrometry, co-immunoprecipitation and site-directed mutagenesis confirmed that STK directly phosphorylated RpoD at Thr-208 residue. Phenotypic tests revealed that RpoD phosphorylation had no obvious impact on bacterial growth and biofilm formation but specifically promoted the thermotolerance and hemolytic activity of S. suis. Notably, the rpoD overexpression mutant strain SC19-rpoD significantly upregulated the transcription and protein production of SLY, whereas the phosphorylation-deficient mutant SC19-rpoD T208A abolished this promotion effect, indicating that Thr-208 phosphorylation is required for sly upregulation, although the underlying molecular mechanism remains to be fully defined. Furthermore, mouse infection models demonstrated that the SC19-rpoD T208A mutant exhibited alleviated splenic pathological injury, reduced bacterial loads in multiple organs, and significantly improved host survival, indicating that the loss of RpoD phosphorylation impairs S. suis virulence. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that STK-mediated phosphorylation of RpoD at Thr-208 is required for sly upregulation and contributes to the S. suis pathogenesis.
records.authors: Tian Y, Zhao Z, Yin H, Liu X, Fu J, Gao L, Li Y, Fang R, Peng L.

records.title: Retrospective analysis of the transmission of difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa - genotype beats phenotype.
records.abstract: BackgroundDifficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (DTRPA) represents a challenging resistance phenotype with carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa playing a major role. However, carbapenemase-negative DTRPA (CN-DTRPA) are more susceptible to reserve antibiotics and rarely reported in outbreaks, differing from frequently outbreak-associated carbapenemase-producing DTRPA (CP-DTRPA) with limited therapeutic options. Despite, international guidelines recommend equal infection prevention and control (IPC) measures. Here, we analysed the transmission of CP-DTRPA and CN-DTRPA using epidemiology and whole-genome sequencing (WGS).MethodsClinical DTRPA isolates collected between 2019 and 2024 were subjected to WGS. Genetic clusters were defined using cgMLST thresholds of ≤ 11 and ≤ 3 allelic differences. Epidemiological relatedness was estimated on hospital stay, interpatient contact and environmental exposures. For possibly epidemiologically linked cases, precolonisation with carbapenem-susceptible P. aeruginosa (CSPA) and antibiotic exposure during hospitalisation were assessed.ResultsAmong 190 DTRPA isolates, CN-DTRPA (79.5%) was predominant compared to 20.5% CP-DTRPA, mainly carrying blaVIM-2. Twelve genetic clusters involving 39 patients were identified. Seven clusters (CP-DTRPA n = 4; CN-DTRPA n = 2, CP-DTRPA/CN-DTRPA-mixed n = 1) showed possible epidemiological relatedness. CP-DTRPA isolates were frequently associated with clusters (OR 17.47, 95% CI 7.43-41.08) and environmental transmission. Diverse CN-DTRPA were rather linked to interpatient CSPA-transmission following CN-DTRPA emergence after prolonged antibiotic exposure.ConclusionCN-DTRPA predominated and displayed high diversity, consistent with possible antibiotic-driven resistance development in precolonised patients. In contrast, less frequent and less diverse CP-DTRPA were associated to outbreaks. These findings highlight the need to evaluate differentiated IPC strategies, including targeted screening and environmental interventions for CP-DTRPA, while further investigating the potential role of antimicrobial stewardship in preventing the emergence of CN-DTRPA. Multicentre studies are required for evidence-based IPC strategies.
records.authors: Jasuja JK, Maurer PM, Carlsen L, Klupp ET, Belmar Campos CE, Rohde H, Aepfelbacher M, Knobloch JK.

records.title: Virus detection in Culicoides biting midges during the BTV-3 outbreak in north-west Germany 2024.
records.abstract: BackgroundBluetongue virus (BTV), Schmallenberg virus (SBV) and epizootic hemorrhagic disease virus (EHDV) are arthropod-borne pathogens that are transmitted by biting midges of the genus Culicoides. Following the initial introduction of BTV in central Europe in 2006, the emergence of SBV in 2011, and the first detection of EHDV in southern Europe in 2022, it became evident that Culicoides-borne viruses pose a significant threat to European livestock. In 2023, BTV serotype 3 was detected for the first time in the Netherlands and subsequently caused a severe outbreak in Germany in 2024. The aim of this study was to compare the prevalences of the viruses in the Culicoides population during the BTV-3 outbreak in north-west Germany in 2024.MethodsCulicoides were caught by UV-light traps on 14 farms from April to October 2024 in north-west Germany. 337,359 of those were selected for virus screening and sorted into 7,549 pools based on their morphology. The pools were tested by real-time RT-PCRs for the genomes of SBV, BTV and EHDV. Virus-positive pools were further analyzed in species-specific PCRs to identify the Culicoides species present.ResultsA total of 1,359 pools (18.0%) tested positive for BTV-RNA, while 402 pools (5.3%) showed SBV-RNA. None of the pools were positive for EHDV. The majority of the positive pools contained specimens of the Culicoides subgenus Avaritia Fox. A smaller part belonged to the subgenus Culicoides Latreille. The taxa most commonly found in the virus-positive pools of the subgenus Avaritia were C. obsoletus clade O1, C. scoticus and C. dewulfi. The most prevalent taxa in the virus-positive pools of the subgenus Culicoides were C. punctatus, C. pulicaris and C. lupicaris haplotype L1.ConclusionsWe confirmed the ongoing circulation of SBV as well as an extensive BTV circulation in the Culicoides vectors of the subgenera Avaritia and Culicoides in north-west Germany in 2024. Despite belonging to different virus families, the circulation patterns of BTV and SBV observed over the months were very similar, showing peaks in August.
records.authors: Zeiske S, Kampen H, Scheuch D, Sick F, Beer M, Voigt A, Werner D, Wernike K.

records.title: Alleviation of ammonia inhibition associated with enhanced quorum sensing signaling system under trace elements supplementation during biomethanation.
records.abstract: Anaerobic digestion (AD) represents a mature and extensively adopted technique to dispose organic waste, yet ammonia toxicity remains a major bottleneck for stable AD operation. For activating methanogenesis-related enzymes, regulating the microbial community structure, and optimizing the reaction efficiency of AD process, supplementation of trace elements has been validated as an effective approach to counteract ammonia inhibition. However, mechanisms of how different trace elements modulate the biosynthesis and release of N-acyl homoserine lactones (AHLs), as well as the subsequent relieving ammonia inhibition are still unknown. Therefore, the current study investigated the effects of different trace elements on the secretion of AHLs under ammonia stress. The results showed that optimal concentrations of Fe, Co and Ni could enhance the secretion of AHLs, mainly N-butyryl-DL-homoserine lactone (C4-HSL) and N-hexanoyl-L-homoserine lactone (C6-HSL), and adjust microbial social behaviors under high ammonia levels. In addition, microbial community changes (enriched Bacteroidetes_vadinHA17, Syntrophomonas and Methanosarcina) were closely associated with increased methane production and stimulated AHLs accumulation by trace elements. Furthermore, increased AHLs signals correlated with intercellular communication could regulate critical genes transcription (glk, pgk, and yhdR) and enzymes synthesis (glucokinase, acetate kinase, and Coenzyme-B sulfoethylthiotransferase) to alleviate ammonia inhibition during the whole AD process. Trace elements could serve for multiple enzymes, which could be beneficial for AHL secreting hydrolytic-acidogenic consortia. The current study could provide primary insights for applying trace elements to relieve ammonia stress via AHLs regulation.

records.title: Scallops as an emerging platform toward functional reproductive endocrinology.
records.abstract: Scallops have become one of the few molluscan systems in which reproductive endocrinology can be examined beyond descriptive molecular surveys. This review summarizes a series of studies that have progressively positioned scallops as an emerging experimental platform for advancing functional approaches in comparative reproductive endocrinology. Early work identified GnRH/CRZ-superfamily peptides and their receptors in scallops, showing that these ancient neuropeptide-GPCR modules are present in bivalves and may have multifunctional roles, but should not be interpreted as direct counterparts of the vertebrate hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis. Molecular analyses of sterol-related and nuclear-receptor-related pathways, together with sex-identification markers, further suggest that scallops provide a useful system for examining candidate mechanisms associated with gametogenesis, sex differentiation, and the stable maintenance of sexual phenotypes, without assuming vertebrate-type sex steroid regulation. At the cellular level, studies of germ cells and gonadal somatic cells have revealed the importance of the gonadal niche, whereas scallop hemocytes have emerged as experimentally accessible primary cells for cellular-level functional assays, rather than as established reproductive endocrine target cells. A major technical breakthrough has been the discovery and application of a strong OsHV-1 promoter, which has enabled transient transgene expression in scallop cells. Combined with primary hemocyte culture, this system has supported subcellular localization assays, recombinant protein production, and functional assessment of genes of interest, thereby providing a complementary route to gene function analysis in bivalves where individual-based functional genetics remains difficult. Despite current limitations, including low transfection efficiency, interindividual variability, and the limited extrapolation of hemocyte-based phenotypes to gonadal or organism-level reproductive physiology, scallop cell-based platforms provide a promising foundation for hypothesis-driven comparative endocrinology. These advances illustrate how non-model molluscs can be developed from observational subjects into experimentally testable systems, offering new perspectives on endocrine evolution, reproductive regulation, and physiological integration in marine invertebrates.
records.authors: Nagasawa K, Yoon J, Osada M.

records.title: Discovering multi-omics predictors for lithium response in bipolar disorder by integrating proteomic and genomic data: A 6-month follow-up study.
records.abstract: BackgroundReliable predictors of lithium response in bipolar disorder (BD) are unavailable, and reported predictors have rarely been temporally validated. We examined whether baseline proteomic, clinical, and polygenic information predicts lithium response using a temporal validation design.MethodsPatients with BD from three hospitals were assessed over six months (acute) or at baseline (stable maintenance); lithium response was rated with the Alda scale. Of 295 participants with complete multi-omic data, 228 in the acute phase entered prediction analyses: elastic-net models (responders, Alda A ≥ 7) developed in an earlier cohort (n = 110) were applied to a later, separately assayed validation cohort (n = 118).ResultsIn the validation cohort, the protein model showed modest discrimination (AUC = 0.58, 95% CI 0.47-0.70; permutation p = 0.060), whereas clinical (AUC = 0.51) and polygenic (AUC = 0.46) models did not transfer, and combining modalities did not improve prediction. In an exploratory comparison of clear responders and non-responders (Alda A ≥ 7 vs ≤3), protein models reached AUC 0.67-0.70. Protein discrimination was similar with validation-blind preprocessing but weaker in sensitivity analyses.LimitationsValidation was temporal rather than site-independent, and most patients were already taking lithium at baseline sampling.ConclusionsUnder temporal validation, baseline proteomic profiles carried at most modest information about lithium response, and clinical and polygenic predictors did not transfer. Candidate markers need external validation in larger cohorts sampled before lithium initiation.

records.title: Human hair-bearing skin organoids reveal cell type-specific susceptibility and innate immune responses to herpes simplex virus 1.
records.abstract: Epithelial surfaces are the primary sites of lytic herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) infection following initial exposure or reactivation from latency. To model this complex environment, we used human hair-bearing skin organoids and combined single-cell spatial transcriptomics with imaging to map viral spread and host responses across skin architecture. Our data suggest delayed progression of the HSV-1 life cycle in epidermal keratinocytes and hair follicle cells compared to the dermis. Infection triggered spatially organized host responses, including induction of IER3 in papillary fibroblasts. In basal keratinocytes, IRF3 was up-regulated in both infected and neighboring uninfected cells, consistent with paracrine activation of antiviral signaling. Inflammatory responses were compartmentalized in a cell type-specific manner, with TNFSF9 (4-1BBL) induced in papillary fibroblasts and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) induced in keratinocytes. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays confirmed secretion of these cytokines and the TNF-α-responsive chemokines CXCL2 and CXCL10. CXCL2 expression was enriched in cells adjacent to TNF-α-expressing cells, highlighting spatial coordination of inflammatory signaling. While interferon-β reduced viral replication, TNF-α and 4-1BBL did not, suggesting that their primary role is to orchestrate immune cell recruitment and activation. These findings establish human hair-bearing skin organoids as a physiologically relevant model for investigating spatial host-HSV-1 interactions.

records.title: Functional dissection of conserved RNAi pathways in antiviral immunity of several hemipteran insects.
records.abstract: The small silencing RNA pathways are crucial post-transcriptional gene silencing mechanisms involved in antiviral defense, gene regulation, and transposon suppression. In insects, the three main pathways are the microRNA (miRNA), Piwi-interacting RNA (piRNA), and small interfering RNA (siRNA) pathways. While these pathways are well-studied in model insects like fruit flies and mosquitoes (Order: Diptera), their functions in non-model insects remain largely unexplored. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive functional screening of core RNAi-related genes in a hemipteran insect, the small brown planthopper (Laodelphax striatellus). Our results demonstrated that genes in the miRNA pathway (AGO1 and DCR1) and the piRNA pathway (Piwi and AGO3) are essential for the survival, development, and fecundity of L. striatellus, but they are not actively involved in the antiviral response. Unexpectedly, knocking down the key siRNA pathway gene DCR2 did not produce a detectable change in viral accumulation or the abundance of virus-derived small interfering RNAs. This finding suggests that substantial depletion of DCR2 does not detectably impair the measured antiviral siRNA responses in L. striatellus under our experimental conditions. A similar lack of detectable antiviral phenotypes following DCR2 knockdown was observed in three other representative hemipteran insects from different families/genera (Sogatella furcifera, Nilaparvata lugens, and Bemisia tabaci). Additionally, CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of DCR2 resulted in embryonic lethality in homozygous mutant strains of L. striatellus, while heterozygous mutants showed significantly prolonged developmental duration. Functional RNAi-of-RNAi assays further demonstrated that DCR2 pre-knockdown did not detectably reduce silencing of a subsequently introduced dsRNA reporter in L. striatellus, and DCR2-heterozygous mutants with reduced DCR2 expression showed no change in viral accumulation. These results reveal an essential developmental role for DCR2 and indicate that partial DCR2 depletion does not measurably compromise antiviral immunity under the tested conditions. Collectively, our findings broaden our understanding of the organization and biological functions of small silencing RNA pathways in hemipteran insects.

records.title: Genetic Range of Xanthomonas phaseoli pv. phaseoli as Revealed by Phylogeographic Analyses.
records.abstract: Common bacterial blight of common beans caused by various Xanthomonas species is considered a significant threat to bean production worldwide. In this study, common bean-associated xanthomonads in Iran were investigated using a multilocus phylogeographic approach. Majority of the bacterial strains investigated in this study were isolated in 2023-2024, while a number of 1990s and 2000s Iranian strains were also included in the analyses. Phylogenic analyses using the sequences of four housekeeping genes showed that among 45 strains isolated from common bean across nine Iranian provinces, 44 strains belonged to Xanthomonas phaseoli pv. phaseoli, while one strain was identified as Xanthomonas citri pv. fuscans. Multilocus sequence analysis showed that all strains collected in 2023-2024 in Iran along with four strains isolated in 1999, 2006, and 2020 clustered into a monophyletic clade. Multilocus sequence typing of the Iranian strains along with 29 worldwide strains retrieved from the NCBI GenBank revealed low genetic diversity within the global population of X. phaseoli pv. phaseoli. Majority of the worldwide X. phaseoli pv. phaseoli strains belonged to the same haplotype. However, a distinct haplotype containing only the strains isolated in Iran was observed, with no members from the worldwide population. Our analysis provides novel insight into the population structure of common bacterial blight pathogen on a global scale. Emergence of a novel lineage of X. phaseoli pv. phaseoli in Iran raises concerns about further expansion of the pathogen and highlights the need for strict quarantine measures in a global scale.

records.title: A promoter SNP enhancing GaOFP17 expression in upland cotton reduces cotton boll and seed sizes via interaction with NF-YC4.
records.abstract: Single boll weight and seed size are key determinants of cotton yield. Our previous study demonstrates that the gene OFP17 regulates boll and seed sizes in an introgression line of G. arboreum in the Gossypium hirsutum background, but the underlying genetic mechanisms remain elusive. Here, virus-induced gene silencing and virus-induced gene overexpression of OFP17 were performed in cotton. And ectopic expression of OFP17 in Arabidopsis thaliana was conducted. The results indicated that OFP17 negatively regulates boll and seed sizes. Promoter activity assays revealed a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) in the OFP17 promoter was the causal variant, regulating promoter activity and the OFP17 gene expression level, consistent with its phenotypic differences. A yeast two-hybrid and bimolecular fluorescence complementation, and subcellular localization showed that OFP17 physically interacts with the transcription factor GhNF-YC4, which in turn interacts with the DELLA protein GhGAI, a repressor of gibberellin signaling. Intriguingly, overexpression of GaOFP17 in Arabidopsis led to hypersensitivity to abscisic acid (ABA) during seed germination, accompanied by upregulation of AtNF-YC4, AtGAI, and the ABA-responsive gene AtABI5. In conclusion, a model is proposed that OFP17, via interaction with NF-YC4, may modulate a DELLA-dependent transcriptional network that integrates gibberellin and ABA signaling to control boll and seed sizes. These findings provide new insights into the transcriptional regulation of boll and seed sizes and suggest potential genetic targets for improving cotton yield.
records.authors: Xu M, Feng L, Zhang Z, Liu S, Feng G, Wang N, Ai N, Zhou B.

records.title: Machine Learning-Enhanced Terahertz-Colorimetric Dual-Mode Metadevice Based on Metallic Nanonetworks for microRNA Panel Assays.
records.abstract: Early diagnosis and accurate staging are essential for improving treatment efficacy and clinical outcomes of pancreatic cancer (PC), but remain challenging because of limited early PC-specific biomarkers and high-performance detection methods. In this paper, we developed a machine learning (ML)-enhanced terahertz (THz)-colorimetric dual-mode metadevice based on metallic nanonetworks for multiplexed microRNA (miRNA) detection and early PC diagnosis. Clinical sample measurements and bioinformatics analysis identified miRNA-21, miRNA-1290, and miRNA-320a as candidate PC biomarkers. Target miRNAs triggered the assembly of DNA-functionalized Fe and Au nanoparticles (NPs) with PEI-modified CuS NPs into ternary Fe/Au/Cu nanonetworks, generating THz and colorimetric signals through their dielectric and peroxidase-like properties. This target-triggered assembly enabled three-miRNA panel analysis without enzyme-mediated nucleic acid amplification and achieved attomolar-level miRNA profiling. Six ML algorithms were integrated to develop predictive models for PC diagnosis and staging. Linear discriminant analysis (LDA) achieved diagnostic accuracies of 97.8% (95% CI: 88.2-99.9%) in the training cohort (n = 45) and 96.7% (95% CI: 82.8-99.9%) in the validation cohort (n = 30), with 100% sensitivity for early PC in both cohorts. Compared with CA19-9, CA125, and CEA, the multiplexed miRNA-based dual-mode metadevice showed higher efficacy (area under the curve, AUC: 1.00 vs 0.905), supporting its potential for clinical miRNA-based liquid biopsy.

records.title: Yeast PI(3,4,5)P3 controls vacuole fusion through Vam7 and membrane microdomain assembly.
records.abstract: Membrane trafficking is regulated by the spatiotemporal distribution of phosphoinositides. The endolysosomal pathway is controlled by PI3P, PI(4,5)P2 and PI(3,5)P2, whereas a role for PI(3,4,5)P3 is less clear. We report that Saccharomyces cerevisiae produces PI(3,4,5)P3 through Vps34 activity using PI(4,5)P2 as a substrate. In vitro assays showed that dioctanoyl (C8) PI(3,4,5)P3, the PI(3,4,5)P3-binding domain Grp1-PH, and the phosphatase PTEN blocked vacuole fusion. Fluorescence microscopy showed that PI(3,4,5)P3 was present on vacuoles and the plasma membrane and that its presence was eliminated by inhibiting Vps34. Importantly, PI(3,4,5)P3 was required for the enrichment of Ypt7 and the HOPS subunit Vps33 at vertex domains. Blocking PI(3,4,5)P3 also caused the release of the soluble SNARE Vam7, leading to inhibited trans-SNARE pairing. Finally, we show that PI(3,4,5)P3 is needed for vacuole acidification in vivo. These results demonstrate that PI(3,4,5)P3 affects multiple factors in vacuole function.

records.title: Constructing event graph and mining critical paths of Ebola virus disease: a public health emergency analysis based on WHO disease outbreak news.
records.abstract: BackgroundMost Ebola virus disease research focuses on clinical diagnosis or static knowledge networks, limiting dynamic spatiotemporal analysis of epidemic evolution. We examined whether an event graph derived from World Health Organization (WHO) Disease Outbreak News (DONs) could reconstruct outbreak evolution across reports and identify response-timing patterns, including delayed interventions, unactioned risk assessments, and cross-border escalation.MethodsWe retrospectively analysed 346 Ebola-related DON reports published through August 2025. We used a large language model-assisted framework to extract events and their relationships. We built an event graph in Neo4j and applied a bounded depth-first search procedure that removed cycles, generated candidate paths, and selected critical paths across six dimensions: case burden, spatial spread, international risk signals, intervention measures, path length, and graph structural importance.ResultsThe graph comprised 2233 event nodes and 10,479 relations across 155 event groups; 47 representative critical paths were selected. Laboratory confirmation often marked the shift from uncertain signals to an organised response. Healthcare-facility exposure and community deaths served as sentinel events for infection-control review and transmission-chain investigation. Preparedness, surveillance, and contact tracing generally followed spatial spread and international-risk signals rather than general border restrictions. Repeated burden updates without documented interventions indicated potential response or reporting gaps. Although established control measures aligned with WHO advice, the report defined explicit triggers, deadlines, inter-agency handoffs, and completion indicators less clearly.ConclusionsThe event graph reconstructed longitudinal outbreak and response trajectories that are difficult to capture through descriptive summaries or entity-centred knowledge graphs. Effective Ebola response depends not only on available control measures but also on activating them at appropriate transition points. This framework complements, rather than replaces, WHO guidance, real-time surveillance, and formal epidemiological causal inference.
records.authors: Ni Z, Sun Y, Feng G, Wei J.
