records.title: Scale-dependent shifts in climatic and anthropogenic drivers of riverine dissolved organic matter dynamics.
records.abstract: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) is central to the global carbon cycle, yet how urbanization interacts with climate to shape riverine DOM dynamics across scales remains poorly understood, limiting our ability to predict aquatic carbon feedbacks under global change. Here, we integrate a five-year intensive monitoring dataset from a representative peri‑urban watershed (Zhangxi River, eastern China) with a global meta-analysis encompassing 1844 data points across six continents, to disentangle the multiscale drivers of riverine DOM based on its optical properties (UV-Vis absorbance and fluorescence). We show that urbanization is the strongest driver in our regional dataset, whereas climate‑associated drivers and topography emerge as dominant drivers in the global meta‑analysis. This scale‑dependent pattern suggests a potential shift, which we propose as the Scale‑Dependent Driver Shift (SDDS) hypothesis requiring further independent testing. Urbanization consistently elevates DOC concentrations and shifts DOM composition toward protein‑rich, microbially derived components with lower aromaticity and higher bioavailability across watershed gradients. Globally, urban watersheds exhibit recurrent anthropogenic DOM signatures across temperate and subtropical regions characterized by enhanced lability and reduced compositional complexity compared to natural systems, though we caution that the global dataset is biased toward mid‑latitude regions, and extrapolation to tropical or wetland systems warrants further investigation. Random forest and variance partitioning analyses supported a scale‑dependent driver shift: human activities emerged as dominant predictors regionally, while climatic and topographic constraints structured global biogeographic patterns. Based on these findings, we propose the SDDS as a working hypothesis that offers a potential framework to reconcile long‑standing discrepancies between climate‑focused and human‑focused studies. Our results suggest that ongoing urbanization may decouple riverine carbon dynamics from natural climate‑associated drivers, with potential consequences for carbon mineralization, greenhouse gas emissions, and global carbon cycle feedbacks.
records.authors: Tang J, Liang Y, Zhong N, Bu Q, Yang L, Xu Y.

records.title: Maternally derived antibodies impair the development of the adaptive immune response in piglets upon influenza A virus infection and have a limited effect on viral detection.
records.abstract: The presence of maternally derived antibodies (MDAs) can affect infection dynamics and the immune response in piglets during swine influenza A virus (swIAV) infection. This study aimed to investigate the impact of MDAs on swIAV infection characterized by the duration of swIAV RNA shedding, and serological antibody response in piglets under field conditions. The study was conducted in two Danish sow herds over a six-week period and included five sows with each four piglets in both herds. In addition to unknown previous natural swIAV exposure, sows had been vaccinated with Respiporc FLU3 in Herd 1 one month before study initiation and with Respiporc FLUpan in Herd 2 four months before study initiation. Blood and colostrum samples were collected from the sows on the day of farrowing, whereas nasal swabs and blood samples were collected twice and once weekly, respectively from the piglets. Viral load was estimated by reverse-transcriptase quantitative PCR and swIAV antibody levels in serum and colostrum were assessed by an swIAV-NP ELISA, serum neutralization and hemagglutinin inhibition -tests. Marked variation in antibody levels was observed between herds, sows, and piglets. swIAV RNA was detected in 6/20 piglets in Herd 1 and 17/20 in Herd 2. Due to the twice-weekly sampling interval, exact shedding durations could not be determined. Antibody titers at day 3 were not associated with protection against infection (p > 0.05). However, higher swIAV-NP titers prior to infection were negatively associated with shedding duration in Herd 2 (ρ = -0.67, p < 0.01). Higher swIAV-NP MDA levels were also associated with decreased serological responses after infection (ρ = -0.57, p < 0.05). Overall, MDAs showed limited protection against infection and suppressed adaptive antibody responses in a titer-dependent manner. These findings highlight substantial variability in passive immunity under field conditions and its importance for immune development in piglets.
records.authors: Pedersen K, Gregersen PM, Weber NR, Larsen LE, Ryt-Hansen P.

records.title: tRNA-derived fragments restrict KSHV lytic replication through miRNA-like repression of host pro-viral signalling networks
records.abstract: Transfer RNA derived fragments (tRFs) are emerging regulators of gene expression. Despite mounting evidence of their functional relevance in cellular and pathological processes, their roles in virus infection remain poorly understood. Here, we show that host tRFs are dynamically reprogrammed during Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) lytic replication and function as potent antiviral effectors. Transcriptome-wide profiling revealed extensive remodelling of the tRF landscape following viral reactivation, identifying a subset of tRFs; tRFs (tRF-His-GTG, tRF-Gly-CCC, and tRF-Lys-CTT) that are robustly induced independently of parental tRNA abundance. Functional analyses demonstrate that these tRFs suppress viral gene expression and infectious virion production. Mechanistically, we show that tRF-His-GTG and tRF-Lys-CTT engage canonical RNA silencing pathways by associating with AGO2 complexes and mediating sequence-specific repression of host target genes. Among these targets, we identify SHF as a critical pro-viral factor that promotes PI3K/Akt signalling, cellular survival and efficient viral replication. Collectively, our findings define a previously uncharacterised host defence pathway in which tRFs restrict KSHV replication by targeting host factors required for efficient viral propagation, thus expanding the functional repertoire of non-coding RNAs in antiviral immunity.
records.authors: Matandirotya LT, Murphy J, Tucker J, Whitehouse A.

records.title: Ribosomal biogenesis factor links ribosome homeostasis to host relevant stress survival in  Aspergillus fumigatus
records.abstract: The inhalation of  Aspergillus fumigatus spores into the human pulmonary tract places conidia in direct contact with host immune cells which deploy a coordinated killing mechanism aimed at conidia clearance and preventing invasive infection. The fungus also employs cellular processes that aid its survival during these host mediated stresses, which allows the conidia to sustain growth while resisting attacks by the host immune cells. Ribosomal biogenesis plays a vital role in growth, survival, and stress adaptation in eukaryotic cells. In filamentous fungal pathogens, this process supports the transition of inhaled spores into invasive hyphae and is therefore an important aspect of fungal pathogenicity. It is, however, unclear whether ribosomal biogenesis factors contribute to stress survival beyond their canonical ribosomal roles and provision of support for vegetative growth. In this study, we investigated the role of  A. fumigatus ribosomal biogenesis factor BFR2 in contribution to fungal stress survival and resistance to neutrophil killing. In agreement with its ribosomal biogenesis role, the repression of BFR2 impairs 18S ribosomal rRNA formation, and this impairment directly extends to the inhibition of germination and vegetative growth of fungal colonies. We optimized an “induction/shut-off” system that allows the transient expression of BFR2 in swollen conidia followed by subsequent depletion of BFR2 to investigate its role in stress response outside of its ribosomal biogenesis role. This transient induction followed by shut-off did not result in detectable reduction in ribosomal RNA abundance, global translation capacity, and biomass accumulation therefore indicating that pre-induction of BFR2 supports normal growth physiology in  A. fumigatus over the duration tested. Nevertheless, the depletion of BFR2 following a transient induction increased  A. fumigatus susceptibility to oxidative, replication and DNA-damaging stress while preserving tolerance to endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress. The depletion of BFR2 under these conditions also increased  in vitro neutrophil mediated killing without altering conidia uptake. In a mouse model of invasive aspergillosis, BFR2 depletion reduced conidial survival within neutrophils and pulmonary fungal burden, and in an immunocompromised mice model, the depletion of BFR2 attenuated virulence thereby extending survival by a few days. These findings identify BFR2 as a crucial link between ribosomal biogenesis and fungal stress survival during host relevant stresses. Thus, targeting ribosomal biogenesis factors that underpin stress survival represents a promising strategy for antifungal development that could target both ribosomal biogenesis function and also stress response functions.
records.authors: Adeoye JA, Hayby H, Shlezinger N.

records.title: Maternal microbiota shapes brain and neuroendocrine development in piglets.
records.abstract: The maternal microbiota plays a critical role in early-life development, yet how maternal microbiota exposure shapes cellular and neuroendocrine programs during mammalian development remains poorly understood. Here, leveraging germ-free (GF) and maternal microbiota transplantation (MMT) models, we generated an integrated multi-organ porcine atlas by combining multi-regional single-nucleus RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, bulk RNA sequencing of intestinal tissues, and metabolomics. Across five brain regions and the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, we profiled 673,623 high-quality nuclei and revealed microbiota-dependent remodeling of neuronal and glial states across early postnatal developmental stages. MMT reshaped neuronal maturation programs, altered the distribution of immature neuronal states, and elicited region-specific transcriptional responses in glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons. MMT also reorganized neuron-glia interaction networks, accompanied by trends toward increased plasma glutamic acid and glutamine levels. Across the gut-brain-neuroendocrine axis, MMT was associated with coordinated remodeling of HPA-axis cellular communication, stress-response transcriptional programs, and immune signatures, together with reduced circulating cortisol levels. Integrated intestinal analyses revealed segment-specific transcriptional and metabolic remodeling, including alterations in tryptophan/indole-related metabolites and immune-associated pathways. Cross-species stratified linkage disequilibrium score regression further identified enrichment of human cognitive and neuropsychiatric trait-associated genetic signals within cell-type-specific gene signatures derived from microbiota-responsive porcine cell populations. Our study establishes a large-animal cellular atlas linking maternal microbiota-responsive remodeling across the brain, gut, and neuroendocrine axis, providing a translational framework for understanding how early-life microbial signals shape mammalian developmental physiology.

records.title: Single-cell multi-omics reveals distinct regulatory architectures coordinating carbon assimilation and cyclic electron flow in maize C<sub>4</sub> photosynthesis.
records.abstract: C4 photosynthesis arose repeatedly through redeployment of pre-existing regulatory circuitry, yet how a shared regulatory system coordinates its interdependent photosynthetic functions remains unresolved. Here we integrate single-nucleus RNA-seq and sci-ATAC-seq with bulk histone profiles from mesophyll- and bundle sheath-enriched fractions and transcription factor binding profiles obtained in protoplasts. We compare the C4 shuttle and Calvin-Benson-Bassham cycle with NDH-mediated cyclic electron flow in bundle sheath cells. Selected carbon assimilation loci were associated with differential H3K27me3, whereas the NDH-associated branch showed regulatory inputs linked to DNA binding with one finger (DOF) transcription factors. Dissection of the ZmNdhU promoter identifies a 49 bp DOF-responsive cis element whose activity is sensitive to local sequence context and insertion position in the promoter constructs tested and that supports vascular bundle-associated reporter expression in a heterologous promoter context. Bundle sheath-enriched expression of ZmDOF30 increases NDH-associated expression, cyclic electron flow, leaf ATP content and photosynthetic performance. In a field trial, the transgenic lines showed increased growth and biomass. Comparative analyses revealed lineage-associated variation in predicted promoter-proximal DOF-binding potential within a broader H3K27me3-associated transcription factor background. These findings distinguish regulatory configurations among maize photosynthetic modules and identify DOF-NDH regulation as a candidate route for improving photosynthetic performance in maize, with broader relevance to NADP-ME grasses.
records.authors: Li C, Zhang Y, Lin K, Liu X, Zhang H, Yang J, Zhao C, Yang L, Long Z, Li Y, Deng Q, Ma B, Wei T, Zhong S, Zhu X, Li P, Pan X, Tu X.

records.title: Carrier-Free Hydrogel From Metal Ion and Near-linear Herbal Polysaccharide With Photothermal and Self-adaptive Multienzyme-Like Activity for Healing MRSA-infected Diabetic Wound.
records.abstract: Carrier-free hydrogel from herbal polysaccharide and metal ion coordination holds great potential for diabetic wound therapy, yet near-linear/linear herbal polysaccharide suffers from intramolecular hydrogen-bond-mediated chain entanglement that blocks metal ion coordination and hydrogel assembly. Herein, Polygonatum sibiricum polysaccharide (PSP) with a linear β-1,4-linked glucan/mannan backbone was isolated and served as model to investigate the assembly of near-linear polysaccharide via metal ion coordination. Rapid gelation can be realized by adjusting the pH of PSP solution to 11-12 followed by Cu2+ introduction. In resultant hydrogel, PSP functions as carrier and exhibits ROS-scavenging and immunomodulatory capacity, whereas Cu2+ acts as cross-linker and endows the hydrogel with POD-, SOD-, CAT-mimicking and photothermal activity. This hydrogel displays pH-adaptive enzyme behavior: SOD converts excess superoxide anion radical into H2O2 under initial nearly neutral conditions, subsequent weakly acidic microenvironment trigger POD-mediated hydroxyl radical generation for synergistic photothermal sterilization. After bacterial clearance, restored neutral pH activates SOD- and CAT-like activity to decompose H2O2 into O2 and alleviate tissue hypoxia, driving wound transition from inflammation to remodeling for high-quality diabetic wound repair. Overall, this study establishes a carrier-free hydrogel fabrication strategy based on near-linear polysaccharide and metal ion coordination, and provides an enzyme-mimetic catalytic hydrogel dressing for infected diabetic wound.

records.title: Clinical Prospect of Novel Therapies for Functional Cure in Chronic Hepatitis B.
records.abstract: BackgroundChronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major global health problem. Functional cure is defined as sustained hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) seroclearance with undetectable HBV DNA 24 weeks after cessation of therapy. It has emerged as a clinically meaningful endpoint, associated with regression of liver fibrosis, reduced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk, and a lower treatment burden. However, current CHB therapies, including nucleos(t)ide analogues (NUCs) and pegylated interferon-α (Peg-IFNα), rarely lead to functional cure despite adequate viral suppression, leading to a notable portion of patients remaining at risk for adverse liver-related outcomes, including hepatic decompensation and HCC. Hence, novel therapeutic agents are aimed at accelerating towards functional cure. They are categorized as virus-targeting and immunomodulatory therapies.MethodsThis review summarizes the clinical evidence for emerging therapies aimed at acheiving functional cure, with a particular focus on RNA-targeting therapies. It also discusses practical considerations relevant to treatment selection.ResultsAmong these novel therapies, RNA-targeting therapies are currently the most promising, with bepirovirsen (an unconjugated antisense oligonucleotide) standing out as the only agent completed in Phase III study showing efficacious results. Combination regimens that use RNA-targeting therapies as backbone are increasingly pursued, leveraging potential synergistic effects to achieve higher rates of HBsAg seroclearance.ConclusionRNA-targetting therapies and combination regimens offer promising approaches in attaining functional cure in CHB. Further research should emphasize on the long-term efficacy and safety for these novel agents.
records.authors: Ho KC, Hui RW, Mak LY, Yuen MF.

records.title: Acute measles encephalitis in adults: a case series in Vietnam.
records.abstract: BackgroundAcute measles encephalitis is a rare but severe complication of measles, particularly in adults, and carries high mortality and a substantial risk of neurological sequelae. Two mechanisms are recognized: direct viral invasion of the brain, termed primary measles encephalitis, and an immune-mediated postinfectious process, termed acute postinfectious measles encephalitis. Most descriptions come from children, and the presentation, pathogenesis, and management of adult disease remain poorly defined.Case presentationWe describe four adults (aged 34-45 years) admitted with fever, rash, and altered mental status. Acute measles infection was confirmed by serum measles-specific IgM or measles virus RNA on real-time reverse-transcription PCR. Measles virus RNA was detected in cerebrospinal fluid in Case 1, indicating primary measles encephalitis. Case 2 was initially mistaken for varicella because of an atypical vesicular rash. Case 3 developed quadriparesis and sphincter dysfunction with electromyographic evidence of bilateral S1 radiculopathy; spinal imaging was not performed. Case 4 showed progressive thalamic and temporal lesions on magnetic resonance imaging. Cerebrospinal fluid pleocytosis ranged from 57 to 1046 cells/µL, and improved in most patients within 3 days of intravenous immunoglobulin. Two patients recovered without neurological sequelae, one survived with residual deficits, and one died from persistent cerebral injury complicated by multidrug-resistant septic shock.ConclusionsIn adults, acute measles encephalitis may reflect a biphasic process that combines direct viral neuroinvasion with immune-mediated inflammation, rather than a purely postinfectious phenomenon. Intravenous immunoglobulin was temporally associated with clinical and biochemical improvement, but its therapeutic role cannot be established from a case series and requires controlled study.
records.authors: Nguyen HQ, Cao HD, Van Do T, Doan TT, Nguyen HV, Nong VM, Van Bui C, Bui HN, Luong GH, Aoki Y, Takahashi K, Smith C, Dao CX, Van Vu G.

records.title: Genome-wide association study of human papillomavirus infection and persistence in women living with HIV in Rwanda.
records.abstract: BackgroundWe conducted an explorative genome-wide association study (GWAS) in East Africa to identify host genetic variants associated with the acquisition and persistence of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection.MethodsWe genotyped 385 Rwandan women living with HIV and selected host biomarker assay signals from genital swab samples using qPCR. We compared women who cleared HPV over a two-year interval (operationally defined as persistent infection), with those who did not. Exploratory gene-based aggregation analyses of rare and low-frequency variants represented on the genotyping array were also performed.ResultsIn the primary cluster-stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel analysis, rs13158830 within PPARGC1B exceeded the conventional genome-wide significance threshold for persistent HPV infection. The nearby MIR378A gene-expression assay signal was higher in HPV-positive women but did not distinguish clearance from persistence.ConclusionsWe identified an exploratory host genetic association with persistent HPV infection and several additional candidate loci. The lead rs13158830 signal remained evident in Fisher exact testing and PC-adjusted Firth regression, but the small number of carriers produced substantial uncertainty. These findings require replication in independent cohorts.Clinical trial registrationNot applicable.

records.title: Immune surveillance of cellular damage: lessons from Caenorhabditis elegans.
records.abstract: Innate immune systems must detect infection rapidly and reliably, yet pathogens can often evade direct recognition by host pattern-recognition receptors. An alternative and increasingly appreciated strategy is damage-driven immune surveillance, whereby hosts detect pathogen-induced perturbations to essential cellular and tissue functions rather than microbial molecules themselves. This mode of detection is particularly prominent in Caenorhabditis elegans, which lacks professional immune cells and most canonical innate immune receptors, and therefore relies extensively on monitoring disruptions to core homeostatic pathways. Perturbations to protein translation, proteostasis, mitochondrial function, genome and nucleolar integrity, lysosomal homeostasis, and Golgi function can all trigger immune responses. Recent studies have further uncovered roles for inter-organelle communication, effector-triggered surveillance of lysosome-related organelles, and physiological signals such as intestinal distension in regulating immune activation. Here, we integrate these advances into an organelle- and tissue-centric framework and explore parallels with other organisms to identify emerging and potentially conserved principles of damage sensing in innate immunity. These findings highlight the surveillance of cellular homeostasis as a central strategy for immunity that operates beyond canonical pattern-recognition mechanisms.
records.authors: Ghosh A, Singh J.

records.title: An Electron Defect Engineering-Based Nanoparticle to Precisely Trigger Peroxynitrite Release to Synergistically Eliminate Bacteria and Alleviate Inflammation.
records.abstract: The threat of bacterial infections such as Glaesserella parasuis and Streptococcus suis urges the development of advanced therapeutic strategies. To address this challenge, HAPC was designed with cascading responsiveness. When exposed to 640-660 nm red light, the electron-deficient porphyrin-zirconium MOF (PCN-224) can effectively use its natural photosensitive nature to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) and trigger subsequent reactions. Within the acidic conditions at the infection site, arginine (Arg) was triggered to release nitric oxide (NO), which may subsequently interact with ROS to form peroxynitrite (ONOO-) putatively contributing to enhanced antibacterial activity. The MIC for SS was just 0.25 µg/mL, making it four times more efficient than the free antibiotic CIP. Our study suggests that ONOO- potentially influenced the primary inflammatory pathway NF-κB and decreased the transcription levels of inflammatory mediators with TNF-α decreased by 10-fold for and IL-1β by 2.5-fold for respectively, ensuring antibacterial and anti-inflammatory responses at the same time. Experiments in vivo indicated that HAPC treatment could successfully clear bacteria from the infection site and hasten wound recovery, eventually decreasing the wound area to around 3%. This research showed that HAPC, via a proposed cascade mechanism originating from its material properties, offers a highly efficient, biosafe approach to combat zoonotic drug-resistant bacterial infections.
records.authors: Liu S, Huang Y, Lei X, Cui K, Lei Z.

records.title: Combining single-cell data with machine learning characterizes the molecular landscape of keratoconus.
records.abstract: PurposeKeratoconus (KC) is a progressive disorder characterized by corneal ectasia, corneal thinning, and conical protrusion, which can lead to diminished vision and corneal scarring. However, the molecular mechanism underlying KC has not yet been fully elucidated. In this study, we combined bioinformatics tools and experimental assays to uncover cell-type-specific pathogenic regulators and candidate diagnostic biomarkers of KC.MethodsWe analyzed the KC-associated bulk mRNA expression dataset GSE151631 (19 KC, 7 controls) and the single-cell RNA sequencing dataset GSE285060 (5 KC, 3 controls) from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. After quality control, dimensionality reduction, clustering, and annotation of single cells, we assessed each subpopulation's role in the disease and conducted differential expression analysis on the most relevant subpopulation. Feature selection was then performed on the bulk RNA-seq dataset using LASSO regression and SVM-RFE algorithms to identify candidate diagnostic genes. As a preliminary in vivo validation, an acute rabbit model of KC was induced by intrastromal injection of collagenase type II, and corneal tissues were harvested at day 7 to assess key gene expression at the mRNA level by RT-qPCR and to qualitatively assess protein expression trends by representative immunofluorescence images. We also performed immune infiltration analysis, Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA), Gene Set Variation Analysis (GSVA), transcriptional regulatory networks construction, pseudotime trajectory analysis, and connectivity map (cMap)-based drug prediction.ResultsCorneal stromal cells exhibited the highest contribution to the disease state. Three key genes (KIAA0930, CCDC85B, and KLHL21) were identified as candidate diagnostic biomarkers. Notably, KIAA0930 was upregulated in the rabbit KC model, while CCDC85B and KLHL21 were downregulated, consistent with bioinformatic analysis. Immune infiltration analysis indicated increased cytolytic activity and CD8+ T cells in KC samples, with key genes showing significant correlations with various immune cell types and factors. GSEA and GSVA analyses revealed that these three genes are linked to ECM-receptor interaction, MAPK, PI3K-Akt, and WNT/β-catenin signaling pathways. Pseudotime analysis revealed distinct transcriptional states between KC and control cells. Several small-molecule compounds, including menadione and PAC-1, were computationally predicted to show negative connectivity with the KC-associated gene expression signature.ConclusionsOur study identifies KIAA0930, CCDC85B, and KLHL21 as promising candidate biomarkers for KC diagnosis and highlights corneal stromal cells as a central contributor to KC pathological progression. By combining single-cell transcriptomics and machine learning with preliminary validation in an acute rabbit model, this work provides a molecular framework for early KC diagnosis and therapy, pending validation in chronic models and human cohorts.
records.authors: Fang X, Han P, Chen S, Zhang J, Hua X, Chen P.

records.title: The myeloid transcription factor PU.1 acts through three distal and proximal enhancers to drive TNF induction in human alveolar macrophages.
records.abstract: Macrophages are activated by infection via TLR signaling and produce pro-inflammatory cytokines, including TNF. However, enhancers regulating TNF transcription in human macrophages have not been well investigated. Here, using next-generation sequencing methods, we identify six candidate enhancers within a 131 kb region around the TNF locus in primary human alveolar macrophages. Three enhancers -distal -16kbTNF, -7.1kbTNF, and proximal enhancer PETNF -directly regulate TNF transcription upon TLR3 stimulation. Deletion of the distal -16kbTNF enhancer led to a 73% reduction in TNF gene transcription in response to poly(I:C) stimulation. Additionally, deletion of the -7.1kbTNF enhancer resulted in a 41% reduction in TNF mRNA, while deletion of the PETNF enhancer resulted in a 52% reduction. A high-throughput reporter assay identified DNA fragments that drive enhancer activity. Mutagenesis analysis of transcription factor binding motifs revealed that PU.1-binding sites are required for enhancer activity. Further analysis demonstrates that PU.1, rather than EGR1 or AP-1, is the master regulator, regulating TNF enhancer activities and TNF transcription. This study shows that PU.1 plays a critical role in driving TNF enhancer activity and mRNA expression in human macrophages.
records.authors: Gao J, Li Y, Zhao D, Guan X, Motsinger K, Gutierrez A, Lamichhane A, Luo Y, Scott-Browne J, Chu HW, Huang H.

records.title: Cordyceps proteins: An uncharted frontier in therapeutic bioactive research.
records.abstract: Cordyceps is of importance in Asian medicine. Research has focused on small molecules, but little attention was given to protein-based bioactive compounds from Cordyceps despite their therapeutic promise. This study highlights the current evidence on the five major classes of protein found in Cordyceps species: proteases, cordymin, lectins, superoxide dismutases (SOD) and ribosome inactivating proteins (RIPs). The pharmacological, biochemical, functional insights and the biological importance of these proteins were highlighted and the gaps that present constrains to their clinical use. Cordymin, a low molecular weight (10.9 kDa) antifungal peptide isolated from C. militaris, exhibits HIV-1 reverse transcriptase inhibitory and antiproliferative activity, yet its three-dimensional structure, detailed pharmacokinetic profile and molecular mechanism remain largely unknown. Proteases catalyse the hydrolysis of peptides and amino acids. Although proteases have shown promising potential as a thrombolytic agent, detailed studies of substrate specificity, catalytic mechanisms and inhibitor interactions are still lacking. While Cu/Zn-SOD has successfully been cloned and expressed from C. militaris, other important isoforms such as fungal RIPs remain one of the least explored protein families of Cordyceps. Given the clinical success of plant derived RIP based immunotoxins, the development of lectin-RIP conjugates from Cordyceps for targeted cancer therapy represents a particular but underexplored research direction. This review highlighted proteins of cordycipitoid fungi as an underexplored reservoir of bioactive molecules with significant potential for therapeutic development. A more systematic and interdisciplinary research effort will be essential to unlock their value and advance this field.

records.title: First-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in participants with mismatch repair-deficient advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer (KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15): interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial.
records.abstract: BackgroundA need exists for first-line chemotherapy-free options in advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer. We therefore assessed the efficacy, quality of life, and safety of first-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer.MethodsThe KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15 multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial was conducted at 122 centres in 24 countries in the Americas, Asia, Europe, and Oceania. Adult participants (≥18 years) with inoperable, stage III or IV, persistent, advanced, or recurrent dMMR endometrial cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to intravenous pembrolizumab 400 mg every 6 weeks for up to 18 cycles or intravenous carboplatin area under the curve 5 mg/mL or 6 mg/mL per min plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 on day 1 of each 3-week cycle for six cycles. Randomisation was stratified by disease status, histology, and previous receipt of (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy. Primary endpoints were progression-free survival per RECIST version 1.1, by blinded independent central review, and overall survival. This trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05173987, and is ongoing.FindingsBetween Feb 22, 2022, and Dec 12, 2023, 299 participants were assigned to pembrolizumab (n=149) or carboplatin plus paclitaxel (n=150). At the cutoff for the prespecified interim analysis in the intention-to-treat population (April 24, 2026), median progression-free survival was 38·2 months (95% CI 17·9 months-not reached) in the pembrolizumab group versus 8·4 months (6·8-10·4) in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·57, 95% CI 0·42-0·79; p=0·0002). Estimated progression-free survival was 75% (95% CI 67-81) versus 76% (68-82) at 6 months, 67% (59-74) versus 40% (32-48) at 12 months, and 53% (44-61) versus 30% (22-38) at 36 months. The prespecified statistical significance criterion for overall survival was not met at the interim analysis (medians not reached; HR 0·77, 95% CI 0·52-1·15; p=0·10). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 27 (18%) of 149 participants in the pembrolizumab group and 73 (51%) of 144 in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group. Treatment-related adverse events of any grade that occurred in at least 25% of participants in either group included alopecia (three [2%] of 149 in the pembrolizumab group, 72 [50%] of 144 in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group), anaemia (seven [5%], 71 [49%]), nausea (seven [5%], 41 [28%]), decreased neutrophil count (five [3%], 40 [28%]), peripheral neuropathy (none, 38 [26%]), and fatigue (20 [13%], 37 [26%]). Treatment-related adverse events led to treatment discontinuation in 14 (9%) of 149 participants in the pembrolizumab group and 21 (15%) of 144 participants in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group; they resulted in death in two participants in the pembrolizumab group (hepatic failure and bacterial meningitis [n=1 each]) and one participant in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group (pulmonary embolism).InterpretationFirst-line pembrolizumab showed a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival, with lower frequency of overall and grade 3 or above treatment-related adverse events. The study did not compare pembrolizumab monotherapy with the current standard of care (immunotherapy plus chemotherapy).FundingMerck Sharp & Dohme, a subsidiary of Merck & Co.

records.title: In vivo genome-editing therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy: Preclinical studies and first-in-human trial.
records.abstract: We report the preclinical and early clinical evaluation of in vivo genome editing for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), delivered via a single AAV9 vector. In humanized DMD mice, systemic administration achieved targeted genome editing, partial dystrophin restoration, and improved muscle function. In non-human primates, efficient on-target editing was achieved with no dose-limiting toxicity identified under the conditions tested. In an open-label, dose-escalation, first-in-human clinical trial (NCT06594094), post-treatment muscle biopsies provided early molecular evidence of hfCas12Max-mediated genome editing and detectable dystrophin expression in participants with DMD. However, at the higher dose level (1.0 × 1014 vg/kg), one participant experienced a treatment-related fatal serious adverse event, characterized by marked complement activation and systemic cytokine response shortly after dosing. This work provides initial human proof-of-concept for muscle genome editing while crucially highlighting the critical role of immunologic risks and the narrow therapeutic window of systemic adeno-associated virus (AAV)-CRISPR therapies, underscoring the need to develop safer dosing and immunomodulation strategies.

records.title: Potential influence of landscape structure on water quality and phytoplankton community in highly degraded urban lakes: Implications for restoration.
records.abstract: Urban lakes are of particular concern in urban landscapes, as they provide ecological, social and economic benefits, but are under strong human pressure. The current study examined eleven urban lakes that differ in their morphometric and hydrological characteristics and were located across various macroregions of Poland. The aim was to examine potential relationships among landscape structure, water quality, and phytoplankton communities across three buffer zones (10 m, 100 m, and 1000 m), selected to reflect different spatial scales of land use/land cover (LU/LC). The urban lakes were characterised by different phytoplankton biomass, with a maximum of 181.3 mg/l. Most of them were dominated by toxic or potentially toxic cyanobacteria. Land use/cover explained the greatest percentage of variability (24.3%) in phytoplankton composition in the 100 m buffer zone. However, this relationship was only suggestive and did not reach the conventional level of statistical significance. In contrast, LU/LC explained little of the variation in physicochemical parameters across three spatial scales, accounting for up to 0.6% in the 10 m buffer zone, but with no statistically significant relationships. Phytoplankton play a more important role than other water quality parameters and can serve as a more sensitive indicator, providing complementary information for assessing the impact of landscape structure. Despite the large proportion of forest and seminatural areas, the urban lakes were classified as highly degraded, exhibiting poor or bad water quality, which can be more related to historical pollution than to current landscape structure. Our results indicate that a 100 m wide buffer zone may be a useful study-specific spatial scale for considering shoreline and surrounding LU/LC management. They can be prioritised for protection and restoration activities, as well as for planning future spatial development. Restoring natural vegetation within this zone may reduce the nutrient inflows and slow the process of cultural eutrophication. However, further studies with a larger number of lakes are needed to confirm these relationships.

records.title: WG-am combinations restore antiviral potency against fostemsavir and lenacapavir-resistant HIV-1.
records.abstract: BackgroundResistance to fostemsavir (FTR) and lenacapavir (LEN) poses critical challenges for heavily treatment-experienced (HTE) people with HIV-1 who have exhausted conventional therapeutic options. We evaluated the antiviral synergy of tryptophylglycine-amide (WG-am), a naturally occurring dipeptide from HIV-1 elite controllers that inhibits viral entry and reverse transcription, in combination with seven antiretrovirals against FTR- and LEN-resistant HIV-1 viruses.MethodsCombination assays were performed in TZM-bl cells using a 7×7 dose-matrix format against nine HIV-1 viruses with defined FTR- or LEN-resistance mutations. Synergy was quantified using the zero-interaction potency (ZIP) model in SynergyFinder across all concentrations and at the ≥90% viral inhibition threshold. Three priority combinations - with ibalizumab (IBA), darunavir (DRV), and FTR - were validated in activated PBMCs from three independent donors.ResultsWG-am demonstrated synergistic or additive interactions with all seven antiretrovirals; no antagonism was detected. IBA and DRV showed the highest and most consistent synergy across both resistance backgrounds. FTR showed paradoxical synergy against FTR-resistant virus (peak ZIP 15.58 against S375T). At the ≥90% inhibition threshold, 87.3% (55/63) of combination pairs were synergistic. PBMC validation confirmed synergy for all six priority combinations (ZIP 11.01-17.19), with WG-am + FTR scores exceeding TZM-bl values in primary cells.ConclusionsWG-am-based combinations demonstrate synergistic antiviral activity against FTR- and LEN-resistant HIV-1 in reporter cells and primary immune cells. IBA, DRV, and FTR are identified as priority combination partners for WG-am as a component of resistance-informed salvage regimens for HTE patients with limited treatment options.

records.title: A Conceptual Framework for Understanding Intelligent Behavior in Fungal Mycelia.
records.abstract: Fungi exhibit remarkably complex behavior through their mycelial networks, which consist of thread-like structures known as hyphae. Recent research on saprotrophic fungi has demonstrated that their mycelium behaves in ways that indicate memory, learning, decision-making, and problem-solving based on spatial pattern recognition-all of which are considered intelligent features. I present a framework to study the behavior of fungal mycelia as an emergent entity from decentralized control of numerous simple reactions at the hyphal level. The framework is based on the concept of swarm intelligence, for which internal communication is the key mechanism. Consistent with Trewavas' definition, the intelligence of a mycelium is evaluated purely in terms of its behavior and does not presuppose any form of consciousness. The paper also reviews recent findings that support the potential role of electrical signal transfer across the mycelial network as the mechanism that enables fungal mycelia to engage in intelligent behavior. The fungal mycelial network therefore provides a useful model for studying intelligent behavior in non-neural organisms and its evolution from unicellular to multicellular systems.

records.title: Global high rates of anaerobic methane oxidation at marine cold seeps recorded by isotope bonding in seep carbonates.
records.abstract: Microbial anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM) regulates the flux of methane (CH4) released from anoxic marine sediments into the ocean. However, variations in AOM rates, especially at dynamic environments such as cold seeps, are difficult to constrain, hindering robust projections of marine CH4 flux in a changing climate. Here, we quantify AOM rates at global marine cold seeps based on isotope bonding in methane-derived authigenic carbonates. We show through model simulations that 13C-18O bond abundance in these carbonates quantitatively records AOM rates at marine cold seeps and validate this proxy using compiled datasets of seep carbonate isotope compositions and independent AOM rate measurements. Accordingly, we estimate a mean AOM rate of [Formula: see text] mol·m-2·yr-1 and a consumption of [Formula: see text] Tg·yr-1 CH4 at modern global cold seeps, but potentially [Formula: see text] times as high an AOM rate and CH4 sink over the last ~100 kyr. Our results highlight the important role of cold seeps in the global marine CH4 cycle despite their relatively minuscule footprint.

records.title: Vaccinia virus growth factor induces divergent signaling programs and biological outcomes from cellular epidermal growth factor.
records.abstract: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) signaling is a major pathway that controls cellular growth, survival, proliferation, and differentiation. Viruses often hijack this pathway to create a favorable environment to support their replication. Vaccinia virus (the prototype member of poxviridae) encodes its own viral growth factor (VGF). VGF is a secreted viral polypeptide with sequence and structural homology to the cellular EGF, which binds to and activates EGFR signaling. Studies from our lab and others have shown that VGF promotes metabolic reprogramming, cell motility, virulence, and spread during VACV infection. However, it remains unclear whether VGF fully mimics EGF signaling or selectively rewires downstream pathways to meet the specific demands of viral replication. To address this question, we used quantitative global phosphoproteomics to systematically compare signaling programs induced by EGF and VGF in primary human foreskin fibroblasts. By analyzing global phosphorylation patterns, kinase activity inference, and motif enrichment, we found that although both peptides engage the same EGFR receptor, EGF and VGF induce distinct downstream phosphorylation and bias downstream kinase activities. Transcriptomic analysis provided a complementary view of the cellular responses to the ligand treatment. Moreover, we found that VGF is more effective at promoting VACV plaque formation than EGF, thereby providing functional support to the VGF-biased EGFR signaling nodes important for viral spread. These findings highlight differences in how viral and cellular growth factors activate EGFR signaling and position poxviral growth factors as powerful tools for examining the fundamental principles of cellular signaling.
records.authors: Pant A, Dsouza L, Yang Z.

records.title: SIR2-mediated filament assembly activates the NLR-like protein Avs5 for bacterial antiviral defense.
records.abstract: Like mammalian nucleotide-binding and oligomerization domain receptors (NLRs), bacterial NLR-like proteins mediate antiviral defense. Avs5, a representative of a large family of short bacterial NLR-like proteins, contains an N-terminal SIR2 effector, a central nucleotide-binding domain (NBD), and a C-terminal sensor domain. Whereas canonical inflammasome NLRs use NBD oligomerization to nucleate effector-domain filaments, Avs5 forms SIR2-mediated filaments that couple receptor assembly to NADase activation. In the resting state, ATP-bound Avs5 is monomeric and subsequently forms a SIR2-mediated dimer that likely represents an intermediate in a stepwise activation pathway. Upon activation, ATP-dependent conformational remodeling of the NBD promotes conversion of these dimers into active filaments. Structure-guided mutagenesis, biochemical assays, and functional analyses show that filament assembly is required for efficient NAD+ hydrolysis and antiphage defense. These findings reveal an effector-driven activation mechanism and extend the principles by which NLR proteins couple higher-order assembly to immune defense across domains of life.
records.authors: Wang C, Xie J, Shen Z, Ehrmann JF, Yu C, Fang MX, Wu H, Fu TM.

records.title: Molecular Underpinnings and Prevalence of Donor Cell-Derived Hematologic Neoplasms among Spanish Transplantation Centers.
records.abstract: Donor cell-derived hematologic neoplasm (DDHN) is defined as a de novo hematologic malignancy originated from transplanted donor stem cells, distinct from the original recipient's disease (ORD). Its prevalence and biological mechanisms remain poorly defined. We conducted a nationwide study to estimate the prevalence of DDHN and characterize its clinical and molecular features. Twenty-four transplantation centers systematically reviewed their allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) cohorts. DDHN diagnosis required cytogenetic or molecular donor-origin confirmation. Molecular studies included germline-augmented targeted NGS, whole-exome sequencing, and donor-recipient comparative analyses. We identified 39 DDHN cases diagnosed between 2007 and 2025. Among 8,465 allo-HSCT performed between 2013-2022, DDHN prevalence was 0.28%, with a marked predominance after related-donor compared with unrelated transplantation (0.41% vs. 0.06%, p=0.0026). Median latency from transplantation to DDHN diagnosis was 56 months. Most DDHN were myeloid neoplasms, predominantly myelodysplastic neoplasms (51%) and acute myeloid leukemia (36%). Molecular characterization, available in 33 cases, revealed germline predisposition as the predominant underlying mechanism. Pathogenic/likely pathogenic germline variants were identified in 10 cases, involving DDX41 (n=7), CEBPA (n=2), and CHEK2 (n=1), all after a related-donor transplantation. DDX41-associated DDHN showed recurrent somatic hits and low genomic complexity. Donor-derived clonal hematopoiesis was confirmed in only one myeloid case involving U2AF1. These findings support inherited germline predisposition as the potential main molecular driver of DDHN after related allo-HSCT, reinforcing the recommendation for comprehensive germline evaluation of patients at ORD diagnosis prior to transplantation, followed by targeted cascade screening of candidate related donors.

records.title: Fucoxanthin and the gut microbiota-organ axis: linking low bioavailability, microbial metabolites and multi-organ protection.
records.abstract: Fucoxanthin is a marine carotenoid whose broad effects in experimental models contrast with its limited oral bioavailability. Human exposure to fucoxanthin-derived compounds varies with the food matrix and dosing regimen, with fucoxanthinol being the principal reported circulating metabolite. This review evaluates the proposed fucoxanthin-gut microbiota-organ framework across the gut-liver, gut-brain, and gut-lung axes, systemic metabolism, and tumor biology and immunity, distinguishing direct fucoxanthin evidence from mechanistic extrapolation and assessing dietary dose relevance. Animal studies associate fucoxanthin with microbiota remodeling, improved intestinal barrier function, and reduced lipopolysaccharide translocation. These alterations could influence short-chain fatty acid, bile acid, and tryptophan-derived metabolite signaling, although complete microbiota-metabolite-receptor pathways remain insufficiently validated. Fecal microbiota transplantation supports a microbial contribution to colorectal cancer protection in one mouse model, whereas gut-brain and gut-lung mechanisms remain largely inferential. Many nominal human-equivalent doses derived from animal studies exceed estimated dietary intakes, and cellular fucoxanthin concentrations often exceed circulating human fucoxanthinol concentrations. Human colonic exposure remains unquantified and cannot be inferred from plasma concentrations. Future studies should integrate causal models, luminal and systemic exposure measurements, targeted metabolomics, and human trials to establish the nutritional relevance of fucoxanthin.
records.authors: Wang C, Li X, Wang Y, Cheng J, Guan R, Yang G.

records.title: Spinal Cord Stimulation Attenuates Cognitive Deficits in Chronic Pain in Association with Modulation of the Microglial lnc-PCM1/PCM1/PKC/IFN-γ Signaling Network.
records.abstract: Neuroinflammation plays a pivotal role in chronic pain with cognitive dysfunction (CPCD), a debilitating condition where effective treatments are limited. While spinal cord stimulation (SCS) is an established analgesic therapy, its potential to ameliorate cognitive deficits via central immunomodulation remains largely unexplored. A rat model of CPCD was generated by spared nerve injury (SNI). RNA sequencing was used to identify SCS-regulated long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in the prefrontal cortex (PFC). The functional involvement of the candidate microglial transcript NONRATT012007.2 (hereafter termed lnc-PCM1) was examined using adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated manipulation, behavioral testing, molecular assays, and primary-cell conditioned-medium experiments. SCS improved cognitive performance in CPCD rats. lnc-PCM1 was predominantly expressed in microglia and was reduced after SCS. Lower lnc-PCM1 expression was accompanied by increased pericentriolar material 1 (PCM1), reduced protein kinase C (PKC) phosphorylation and IFN-γ abundance, less M1-polarized microglial activation, and lower pro-inflammatory cytokine release. Conditioned medium from manipulated microglia produced corresponding changes in neuronal oxidative stress, mitochondrial membrane potential, apoptosis-related proteins, and synaptic markers. In vivo overexpression of lnc-PCM1 or knockdown of PCM1 partially attenuated the cognitive and neuroinflammatory effects associated with SCS. The findings support an association between the cognitive effects of SCS and modulation of a microglial lnc-PCM1/PCM1/PKC/IFN-γ signaling network in the PFC. Because formal epistasis and IFN-γ neutralization or receptor-blockade experiments were not performed, the directionality and IFN-γ dependence of this network remain to be established.

records.title: Development and Characterization of VNARs Targeting Edwardsiella piscicida GAPDH.
records.abstract: Edwardsiella piscicida is an intracellular bacterial pathogen that causes edwardsiellosis in Japanese flounder and poses a serious threat to aquaculture. Surface-localized glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) has been implicated in bacterial adhesion and immune recognition, making it a promising antigenic target for infection control. In this study, we generated shark-derived variable domains of immunoglobulin novel antigen receptors (VNARs) targeting recombinant GAPDH from E. piscicida and evaluated their potential as antibody-based agents for controlling edwardsiellosis. A banded houndshark (Triakis scyllium) was immunized with recombinant GAPDH, and anti-GAPDH VNARs were subsequently isolated from the spleen using a combination screening method. Three VNAR clones, designated 2 - 1, 3 - 2, and 4-11, exhibited concentration-dependent binding to recombinant GAPDH and retained their binding activity after exposure to high temperatures or acidic conditions. Epitope binning indicated that the three clones recognized non-overlapping epitopes. Among the tested fish-pathogenic bacteria, clones 2 - 1 and 4-11 preferentially bound Edwardsiella species, including E. piscicida and E. anguillarum. In GAPDH activity assays, the combination of clones 2 - 1 and 4-11 showed the strongest inhibition of recombinant GAPDH activity, with an IC50 of 9.5 ng/ml. The same combination also most effectively inhibited E. piscicida growth in vitro, with an IC50 of 13.6 µg/ml. In a Japanese flounder challenge test, combined administration of clones 2 - 1 and 4-11 resulted in a final survival rate of 91.7%. These findings suggest that anti-GAPDH VNARs may provide a promising antibody-based strategy for the control of edwardsiellosis in aquaculture.
records.authors: Yoshizawa S, Kato M, Hanyu Y, Koiwai K, Hirono I, Kondo H.

records.title: Synergistic effect of zinc oxide nanoparticles and antibiotics: a strategy to combat bacterial resistance.
records.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) continues to compromise the clinical utility of conventional antibiotics, highlighting the need for innovative adjuvant strategies. Zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO-NP) have gained attention due to their intrinsic antimicrobial properties and capacity to potentiate antibiotic activity through multimodal mechanisms. This scoping review systematically mapped current evidence on ZnO-NP with antibiotics combinations (ZnO-NP-antibiotic) following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Searches in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science identified 14 eligible studies. To ensure comprehensive coverage of the literature, an additional manual search was conducted using Google Scholar and the reference lists of the included studies, and 10 further articles were identified. In total, 24 articles are included in this scoping review. Most investigations relied on simple physical mixtures (n = 13); while fewer explored conjugation between ZnO-NP-antibiotic (n = 3); encapsulated systems (n = 4); or drug-loaded (n = 4). Better antimicrobial activity was consistently reported across multiple antibiotic classes. Although all studies evaluated planktonic activity, only 10 incorporated biofilm models. Notably, translational maturity remains limited: more than half of the studies (n = 14) did not include toxicity assessment, and safety evaluation was considered based on in vitro cytotoxicity assays (n = 5); in vivo investigations (n = 5) or Hen's Egg Test-Chorioallantoic Membrane (HET-CAM) (n = 1). These findings indicate that ZnO-NP-antibiotic systems remain predominantly in the early stages of development. Future progress will require standardized antibiofilm methodologies, systematic toxicological profiling, pharmacokinetic characterization, and mechanistic validation to establish reproducible structure-activity relationships. Addressing these translational and regulatory challenges will determine whether nanoparticle-mediated synergy can advance beyond a laboratory proof-of-concept toward clinically viable antimicrobial strategies.
records.authors: Salto MP, de Freitas NG, Fanhani FC, Ferreira LM, Junior JAO, Lemaire L, Dos Santos JL, Chiavacci LA.

records.title: Dual-aptamer magnetic capture and electrochemical detection of influenza B and respiratory syncytial viruses in artificial saliva.
records.abstract: Saliva is a promising non-invasive specimen for respiratory virus diagnostics but its biochemical complexity challenges direct interfacing with affinity-based biosensors. We report a dual-aptamer magnetic-capture electrochemical assay for detection of influenza B virus (IBV) and human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) in artificial saliva. For each target virus, two sequence-distinct DNA aptamers are used: an amino-modified capture aptamer (IBV1 or RSV1) covalently coupled to ∼5 µm polydopamine-coated magnetic microparticles by direct Schiff-base reaction with the polydopamine quinone/catechol surface, and a thiol-modified detection aptamer (IBV2 or RSV2) self-assembled on screen-printed gold electrodes via thiol-gold chemistry. After a single multiplexed batch capture step with both aptamer-magnetic-particle types, the pellet is split and analysed in parallel on the two aptamer-modified electrodes by square-wave voltammetry (SWV). Langmuir analysis of the SWV calibration curves yielded apparent dissociation constants of Kd = 177 ± 62 PFU mL-1 (IBV) and 226 ± 85 PFU mL-1 (hRSV), with detection limits of 15 and 11 PFU mL-1, respectively. Log-linear calibration spanned 101-104 PFU mL-1 on both channels (n = 4 concentrations, R2 = 0.995 and 0.990) with sensitivities of 8.58 and 6.61 µA per decade, so that each virus-specific assay covers three orders of magnitude of viral load. The sequence-orthogonal dual-aptamer geometry-capture and detection recognitions targeting non-identical epitopes-is proposed as the structural mitigation. This proof-of-concept establishes a programmable, saliva-compatible architecture reconfigurable for emerging respiratory pathogens by aptamer substitution alone.
records.authors: Demirel DS, Polat N, Eligul H, Altuner EE, Dursun AD, Kibar G, Yegin Z, Çetin B, Ozalp VC.

records.title: In Step, the sole  Drosophila  TENT5 poly(A) polymerase, is required for spermatid elongation and individualization
records.abstract: Cytoplasmic poly(A) tail length is a key regulator of mRNA translation and stability, controlled in part by non-canonical poly(A) polymerases of the TENT5 family, which are required for gametogenesis in mice. We characterize the sole  Drosophila melanogaster TENT5 ortholog, which we name  in step (  isep ). Although identified as a candidate target of the eye-specification factor Eyeless,  isep mutants have normal eyes; instead,  isep is essential for male fertility. The  isep gene and its protein are expressed in spermatocytes and in elongating spermatids and are concentrated at the distal end of spermatid cysts. Mutant spermatids fail to elongate normally and to individualize. Whole-testis poly(A) tail sequencing revealed that, unexpectedly for the loss of a poly(A) polymerase, median tail length increased in mutants, with lengthened transcripts enriched for roles in axoneme assembly. Both wild-type and a predicted catalytically inactive Isep rescued sterility. We propose that Isep controls localized translation of axonemal transcripts at the spermatid tip, largely independently of its poly(A) polymerase activity.  Article summary  This work contributes to the  Drosophila spermatogenesis community by identifying a previously unknown factor,  isep , the fly’s only  TENT5 , which makes flies a model to study this enzyme family. This work traces the expression pattern of both  isep’s transcripts and protein. Loss-of-function alleles generated by CRISPR-Cas9 mutagenesis result in complete male sterility, and immunofluorescence shows defects in spermatid elongation and individualization (separation into individual sperm). Mutant testes have longer median poly(A) tails, and lengthened transcripts are enriched for spermatogenesis and axonemal (sperm tail) genes. This work also suggests that the predicted poly(A) polymerase activity may be dispensable for spermatogenesis.
records.authors: Al-Nouman A, Helms K, Falk BL, Brill JA, Curtiss J.

records.title: Utilizing a Variant Prioritization Approach to Explore Genetic Variants in Cervical Cancer Cases among Malawian Women
records.abstract: SUMMARY  Introduction  Cervical cancer (CC) represents a neoplastic transformation of the cervical epithelium. CC is the third most common cancer type in Malawi. In 2018, the estimated cervical cancer mortality rate was 51.5 deaths per 100,000 women per year among Malawian women. Although recent burden association and meta-analysis studies have identified candidate cervical cancer susceptibility variants in Malawian women, they did not establish the functional significance of individual variants. Aim  This study aimed to identify germline genetic variants most likely to contribute to cervical cancer susceptibility among Malawian women. Methodology  Whole blood samples were collected from 20 newly diagnosed cervical cancer patients at the Malawi National Cancer Treatment Centre between October and December 2023, and whole genome sequencing was performed. Variants were annotated via VEP and prioritized by ClinVar pathogenic status, Condel (SIFT and PolyPhen2) and minor allele frequency (MAF ≤ 0.1) in the 1000 Genomes project and GenomAD databases. Genes containing the prioritized variants were annotated using the DAVID tool. Results  We identified five known pathogenic variants in the  ROS1 gene among Malawian cervical cancer patients. We also identified 51 moderate impact variants, 64.7% of which were located in known genes associated with CC, including  ADRB1, APOBEC3B, FAT1, IL12RB1, DST, EXO1 and  FGFRL1 genes.  Discussion and Conclusion  The presence of known pathogenic variants in the  ROS1 gene, which is associated with a high recurring rate of CC, as well as the identified moderate impact variants in other genes associated with CC, provide novel insights into the genetic landscape of cervical cancer in Malawi and highlight potentially functional variants that warrant further investigation.
records.authors: Gwayi S, Tomoka T, Chimusa ER, Fedoriw Y, Kumwenda B.

records.title: Genomic diversity and phenotypic heterogeneity of Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates causing bloodstream infection in an infectious disease hospital in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
records.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae has been traditionally considered an opportunistic pathogen, now otherwise healthy individuals commonly present with K. pneumoniae blood infections, which can result in serious complications such as liver abscesses and septic shock. Consequently, the bacterium has become a leading cause of human disease. Along with classical K. pneumoniae (cKp), which is an important reservoir of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes, hypervirulent K. pneumoniae (hvKp) is increasingly becoming of high clinical concern because it carries numerous virulence factors. A high proportion of bloodstream infections (BSIs) in Vietnam are associated with K. pneumoniae, with the epidemiology, population structures and transmission dynamics of hvKp being well described. However, little is known about how virulence-associated traits contribute to increased pathogenicity in this setting and which genetic determinants may be attributable to the virulence variation. In this cross-sectional study, we used a subset of clinical isolates to define the genomic structure and population of K. pneumoniae BSI isolates and additionally comprehensively characterised specific phenotypic features of hvKp associated with clinical manifestations. A genomic analysis of 83 random selected K. pneumoniae BSI isolates defined that lineage of KpI was the most common lineage (91.5%). The hypervirulent sequence type 23 (ST23) was the most prevalent (18.5%), followed by the multidrug resistance (MDR) lineages ST15 and ST17 (7.7% each). Specific hvKp ST23 phenotypic virulence assays showed considerable variation in virulence potential despite possessing a comparable compendium of virulence factors. Comprehensive analysis of genomic variations across the ST23 isolates revealed different genetic backgrounds and distinct mutations occurred on essential genes that might be involved the obsereved phenotypic diversity. These findings show the pathogenic potential of hvKp isolates from Vietnam, and also highlight the need for improved phenotype prediction to understand the clinical threat from strains in this groups.
records.authors: Nguyen Thi Nguyen T, Lee WH, Ragotte RJ, Vinh PV, Huong LNP, Short FL, Boinett CJ, Baker S.

records.title: Predicting carbapenemase production in Pseudomonas aeruginosa using machine learning on disk diffusion data
records.abstract: Abstract    Purpose  : Detection of carbapenemase-production in  Pseudomonas aeruginosa  is challenging due to the co-occurrence of multiple resistance mechanisms. We developed a novel machine learning approach to predict carbapenemase production based on inhibition zone diameters (IZD) from routine disk diffusion testing.  Methods  : A CatBoost model (CBM) was trained on 246 whole-genome-sequenced clinical  P. aeruginosa  isolates, including 95 carbapenemase-producing  P. aeruginosa  (CPPA). Models based on different antibiotic combinations were evaluated and externally validated on two independent datasets. Performance was benchmarked against the phenotypic screening algorithm described by Gill  et al.  Results  : For Dataset 1, CBM achieved a sensitivity and specificity of 94% and 98%, compared with 94% and 38% for the Gill  et al.  algorithm. For Dataset 2, sensitivity/specificity were 95%/98% for CBM vs 100%/0% for the Gill algorithm. This represented a reduction in isolates requiring confirmatory testing of 76% in Dataset 1 and 52% in Dataset 2.  Conclusions  : CatBoost models trained on IZD represent a valuable tool for carbapenemase prediction in PA, substantially improving diagnostic performance and reducing the number of confirmatory tests required. These findings highlight the potential of machine learning to streamline the detection of resistance mechanisms within routine susceptibility testing workflows and may improve recognition of CPPA, especially in resource-limited settings.  Importance  : This approach could reduce unnecessary confirmation-testing for carbapenemases in  P. aeruginosa  , saving time and resources in clinical settings. It underscores the value of integrating machine learning with phenotypic data to address antimicrobial resistance challenges.
records.authors: Hamprecht A, Schaffarczyk L, Muhsal L, Laufenberg R, Pfennigwerth N, Gatermann S, Mancini S, Egli A, Nolte O, Strodthoff N.

records.title: CausalDiffChem: Causal Network Restoration for Therapeutic Prioritization and Repurposing Across Diseases
records.abstract: Abstract  Computational drug repurposing commonly relies on transcriptomic signature matching to identify compounds that reverse disease-associated gene expression, but such approaches do not distinguish putative causal drivers from downstream consequences of disease. Here, we present CausalDiffChem, a causal-network-guided framework that reconstructs disease-specific structural causal models from transcriptomic data using the NOTEARS algorithm and prioritizes compounds according to net_correction, a measure of network restoration under a simulated intervention propagated through the inferred linear structural causal model. We applied CausalDiffChem to multiple sclerosis, sarcoidosis, leishmaniasis and Alzheimer's disease, comprising 408 disease samples and 374 healthy controls. Independently reconstructed networks recovered biologically coherent disease-associated architecture, including a dominant apolipoprotein D interaction in Alzheimer's disease and a macrophage-associated regulatory axis in sarcoidosis. Screening FDA-approved, clinical-stage and preclinical compound libraries identified disease-specific candidates and recurrent prioritization across independently constructed networks. Cisplatin ranked first in both the FDA-approved and clinical-stage sarcoidosis libraries and recurred among the top-ranked candidates across multiple diseases, whereas memantine hydrochloride ranked first across all three compound libraries in leishmaniasis with identical restoration scores. Gene-level analyses further showed that high aggregate restoration could coexist with limited correction of dominant network interactions or discordant global alignment, demonstrating that network restoration, breadth and global transcriptional similarity capture complementary dimensions of therapeutic response. CausalDiffChem therefore provides an interpretable framework for prioritizing therapeutics according to their predicted effects on disease-specific regulatory structure, without requiring curated pathway annotations, and generates experimentally testable hypotheses for drug repurposing across heterogeneous diseases.
records.authors: Armah F, Abor E, Sam P, Sarpong E, Ghartey-Kwansah G.

records.title: Global trait patterns and the economics spectrum of wood-inhabiting fungi
records.abstract: Abstract  Wood-inhabiting fungi drive woody debris decomposition and forest carbon cycling, with their functional trait trade-offs and environmental adaptation strategies substantially shaping forest carbon sink dynamics. However, global-scale functional trait trade-offs and the adaptive responses to environmental gradients remain poorly understood. Here, we synthesized 26 key traits across 7,454 wood-inhabiting fungal species, integrating with approximately 4.58 million georeferenced occurrence records, to investigate the multidimensional trade-offs, environmental driving mechanisms, and future shifts of fungal functional traits. Our results reveal that fungal traits exhibit intramodule synergy and intermodule trade-offs. Three-dimensional functional axes cumulatively explain 72.1% of the total trait variation, with the microscopic reproductive–dispersal investment axis contributing 42.4%, as the primary driver of functional evolution. Climate and topography hierarchically govern trait axes: temperature and precipitation suppress microscopic reproductive–dispersal traits, whereas elevation positively regulates basidial and spore dimensions. Along the resource acquisition axis, temperature and elevation reduced generative hyphae, precipitation suppresses skeletal hyphae, and temperature, precipitation, and LAI synergistically promote binding hyphal thickening, with slope and aspect exerting secondary modulation. Environmental gradients elicited non-linear responses, low latitudes moderately expand reproductive–dispersal structures, whereas high latitudes exhibit compensatory decrease–increase patterns and trait decoupling, shifting toward brown-rot, gymnosperm-associated, monomitic, and thick-walled spore strategies. Under future climate change, fungal traits are projected to reorganize through macroscopic expansion, microscopic contraction, and hyphal reinforcement. This study establishes the first global wood-inhabiting fungal economics spectrum, elucidating adaptive mechanisms including stress compensation and macro-micro trait decoupling, and identifying key environmental dimensions underlying functional differentiation. This framework may improve the parameterization of fungal functional traits in Earth system models and improve mechanistic predictions of forest carbon-cycle feedbacks.
records.authors: Zhu B, Liu S, Zhang S, Ni C, Han M, Xu C, Ma H, Mo L, Jönsson M, Bässler C, Cui B.

records.title: Probiotic Traits and Anti-Biofilm Potential of Bacillus subtilis JS03 From Freshwater Sponge Ephydatia fluviatilis Against Clinical Pathogens
records.abstract: Abstract    Probiotics have been used for centuries to stimulate the immune system and serve as a promising alternative to antibiotics. This study investigated whether  Bacillus subtilis  JS03, isolated from the freshwater sponge  Ephydatia fluviatilis  , possesses significant probiotic characteristics. The isolate was identified through Gram staining, colony morphology, biochemical tests, and 16S rDNA sequencing, and screened for amylase, cellulase, gelatinase, protease, and lipase production, all yielding positive results. Probiotic characterization included survival at varying pH (1–5), bile salt concentrations (0.15–3%), sodium chloride concentrations (1–5%), and temperatures (40–80°C), alongside evaluation of auto-aggregation, hydrophobicity, and hemolytic activity. The isolate demonstrated moderate acid tolerance, with 80.76% survival at pH 3–4, 96.55% survival at 3% bile salt (3.5 × 10⁷ CFU/mL), relative growth OD of 0.617 at 1% NaCl, and 88.4% viability at 60°C for 30 min.  B. subtilis  JS03 exhibited strong antibacterial activity against  S. aureus  MTCC 737 (20 mm inhibition zone) and other clinical pathogens, including Coagulase-negative  Staphylococcus  spp., MSSA, and  Enterococcus faecalis  . Antimicrobial susceptibility testing revealed sensitivity to norfloxacin, ciprofloxacin, chloramphenicol, meropenem, and imipenem, with resistance to penicillin, ampicillin, tetracycline, and streptomycin. Non-hemolytic activity and absence of lecithinase production indicated no major pathogenic traits. Overall,  B. subtilis  JS03 demonstrates robust stress tolerance and significant antimicrobial activity, supporting its strong potential as a probiotic candidate.

records.title: Layered glycoprotein nanoparticles co-delivering Meretrix meretrix-derived peptide and astaxanthin attenuate cyclophosphamide-induced immunosuppression.
records.abstract: Marked differences in solubility and stability between hydrophilic bioactive peptides and hydrophobic carotenoids constrain their synergistic oral delivery. Building on the complementary activities of Meretrix meretrix-derived immunomodulatory peptide (MMIP) and astaxanthin (AST), this study developed co-loaded nanoparticles, HLC10, featuring a BSA-dextran glycoprotein core and a composite outer layer of hyaluronic acid (HA) and yeast β-glucan. Hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic interactions, and electrostatic forces collectively drive the multicomponent assembly. By tuning particle interfacial hydration and the dispersion state of the payloads, the formulation improved co-encapsulation capacity, processing and storage stability, and gastrointestinal bioaccessibility of MMIP and AST. The composite polysaccharide outer layer further increased particle accumulation in Peyer's patches-associated regions and increased uptake by RAW264.7 macrophages. Oral HLC10 administration ameliorated cyclophosphamide-induced immunosuppression, restored immune organ and ileal architecture, and produced coordinated shifts in gut microbiota, fecal short-chain fatty acids, and spleen nucleotide-related metabolic profiles. These findings support the immunomodulatory potential of HLC10, but the evidence remains largely limited to endpoint measures in animal models, and direct validation of cellular functions and the underlying mechanisms is still required. Overall, this stratified co-assembly strategy offers a feasible route for the synergistic oral delivery of food-derived active ingredients with markedly different physicochemical properties.
records.authors: Wu W, Cai J, Wu Z, Cao W, Lin H, Gao J, Fan X, Qin X, Zheng H.

records.title: Early Response of Five Wine Grape Cultivars to Agrobacterium vitis Infection Suggests a Role of STS in Plant Defense.
records.abstract: Crown gall disease, caused by Agrobacterium vitis, is a global threat to viticulture that severely compromises vine vigor and berry quality. To elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying grapevine resistance, five cultivars were inoculated with A. vitis strain A10 under controlled greenhouse conditions. Pathological assessments revealed divergent disease progression patterns among cultivars in which Yan73 (Y73) and Muscat Blanc (MB) exhibited higher resistance, whereas Y73 displayed mild disease development. Conversely, Merlot (ML), Cabernet Sauvignon, and Chardonnay showed rapid symptom development, and ML was identified as the most susceptible, characterized by the highest incidence and severity. Given that bacterial pathogens such as A. vitis are notoriously difficult to eradicate after infection, characterizing the early infection phase is critical for effective management. Comparative transcriptional analysis (RNA-seq) was conducted to capture the early molecular responses across these cultivars. Differentially expressed genes shared among cultivars were significantly enriched in pathways related to plant-pathogen interaction, stilbene biosynthesis, and responses to oxygen levels. Notably, ethylene signaling and response pathways were predominantly enriched in the relatively resistant cultivars Y73 and MB, suggesting their pivotal role in early defense. Further investigation into the stilbene synthase (STS) pathway revealed that its primary catalytic product, resveratrol (Res), serves as a key defensive metabolite. In vivo assays demonstrated that exogenous Res treatments significantly attenuated disease incidence and severity in a dose-dependent manner. Overall, this study outlines the early immune response of grapevine to A. vitis infection and highlights the importance of STS and ethylene pathways in resistance, providing potential targets for breeding crown gall-resistant grape cultivars.
records.authors: Miao L, Chen S, Zhu J, Yu C, Fang Y, Liu X, Ge Q.
