records.title: Elevated environmental CO  2  stimulates photosynthesis and induces differential oxidative responses in two Caribbean reef-building coral species
records.abstract: Reef-building corals maintain intracellular photosymbiosis with dinoflagellate algae, allowing them to use photosynthetic products as metabolic fuel. Carbon dioxide (CO  2 ) is a key substrate for photosynthesis, but its rapid increase in the global ocean due to anthropogenic emissions (known as “ocean acidification”) may disrupt coral symbiosis. We examined the effects of elevated CO  2 on photosynthetic O  2 production, oxidative damage, and antioxidant systems in the Caribbean reef-building corals  Porites astreoides and  Orbicella franksi . Coral colonies collected at 3m depth in Bocas del Toro (Panama) were exposed to control (∼390 μatm CO  2 , pH ∼8.00) or elevated CO  2 (∼1,060 μatm CO  2 , pH ∼7.70) conditions in outdoor flow-through aquaria for 10 days. Flowing seawater had higher O  2 concentrations in elevated CO  2 tanks, with the largest differences at higher irradiance. Microsensor measurements confirmed that acute and chronic exposure to elevated CO  2 significantly stimulated photosynthetic O  2 production in both species. Despite increased O  2 production. neither species showed significant changes in lipid peroxidation, reduced glutathione, or superoxide dismutase, catalase, and glutathione-S- transferase activities. Protein oxidation was unchanged in  O. franksi but significantly decreased in  P. astreoides . These results are consistent with partial relief of carbon limitation in  P. astreoides symbionts under elevated CO  2 , potentially improving photosynthetic efficiency and decreasing reactive oxygen species production. These findings support the resilience of  P. astreoides to OA and suggest that elevated CO  2 may increase daytime O  2 levels on future reefs, with implications for the aerobic metabolism of reef organisms.
records.authors: Tresguerres M, Sabatini S, Linsmayer L, Galindo-Martínez C, Thies A, Hamilton T, Kline DI.

records.title: Two decades of changing Enterococcus epidemiology and antimicrobial susceptibility in a Brazilian tertiary university hospital, 2002–2023
records.abstract: Abstract    Background  Enterococcus  spp. are major opportunistic hospital pathogens characterised by remarkable environmental persistence, genomic plasticity, and the ability to acquire antimicrobial resistance determinants. This study aimed to evaluate the occurrence, temporal dynamics, clinical distribution, and phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility trends of  Enterococcus  spp. clinical isolates in a tertiary teaching hospital in southern Brazil over a 22-year period (2002–2023). Methods  A retrospective, observational study based on positive clinical cultures from hospitalised patients. After applying the inclusion and exclusion criteria, unique isolates were analysed for species, clinical specimens, hospital ward, hospital outcome, and antimicrobial resistance. The study was divided into two periods: January 2002 through March 2019, and April 2019 through December 2023. Results  A total of 6,283 isolates were included, comprising 4,881 (77.7%)  E. faecalis  and 1,286 (20.5%)  E. faecium  . Urine was the primary clinical specimen for both species. An increase in the frequency of isolates was observed in recent years, peaking in 2021 for  E. faecalis  and in 2022 for  E. faecium  .  E. faecium  maintained high resistance rates, whereas in  E. faecalis  , vancomycin resistance increased from 6.6% to 25.2% between the analysed periods. Linezolid resistance remained low in both species. Conclusions  Although  E. faecalis  predominated throughout the period,  E. faecium  was disproportionately associated with bloodstream infections, Intensive Care Unit (ICU) admissions, deaths, and antimicrobial resistance. The significant increase in antimicrobial resistance among both species underscores the importance of continuous microbiological surveillance and species-specific analysis, as well as the need to strengthen infections prevention and control measures.

records.title: TSOpt: Fast and robust training-set design for genomic selection and sparse testing
records.abstract: Abstract  Which candidates are phenotyped largely decides the accuracy of genomic prediction, yet few programmes design training sets formally. Existing tools evaluate the design criterion, the mean generalised coefficient of determination (CDmean), in a reduced marker space or repeatedly inside stochastic searches, optimise for one assumed heritability, and offer little built-in support for multi-environment trials or historical records. TSOpt removes these limits. It updates the exact CDmean by rank-one steps, so a design for several hundred lines takes about 0.1 s, averages the criterion over the unknown heritability, and uses one engine for line × environment and line × trait units, lines already phenotyped, hybrids, plot costs and major genes. We tested it on 328 elite lines from eight seasons of the International Rice Research Institute’s irrigated breeding programme. Twenty-five TSOpt lines predicted untested lines as accurately as 76–167 random lines. TSOpt raised predictive ability over random sampling by 0.097 (95% confidence interval 0.045–0.150), was ahead of STPGA on average, and ran at least 900 times faster. With a quarter of line × season combinations tested over four seasons, its sparse-testing allocations predicted untested combinations better than balanced random allocation, even when scored with correlations unseen by the design; with half tested, it did not. Forward in time, all design methods gained little and the full history remained the best training set. On six public panels TSOpt matched STPGA, TSDFGS and published TrainSel designs, much faster. Lines with the highest mean relationship to the targets never beat random choice.

records.title: Optimization of AAV9 Dose and Fluorescein Concentration for Vagus Nerve Injection in Rats
records.abstract: Background:  /Objectives: Direct intraneural delivery of adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9) via peripheral nerves remains largely unexplored. This study evaluated the feasibility of AAV9 delivery into the vagus nerve, identified an optimal dose, and determined an optimal fluorescein dye concentration for tracking injection fidelity. Methods: Rats received left vagus nerve injections of 5 µL AAV9/GFP at doses of 2.5 × 10⁹, 2.5 × 10¹⁰, 7.6 × 10¹⁰, 2.5 × 10¹¹, or 6.5 × 10¹¹ vector genomes (vg)/rat, mixed with 1% luxol fast blue dye. Controls received vehicle with dye. Transduction in the nodose ganglia of the vagus nerve and medulla was assessed. Fluorescein compatibility was evaluated in CHO Lec2 cells using concentrations of 0%, 0.0001%, 0.004%, and 0.01% at high and low multiplicities of infection. In vivo compatibility was subsequently confirmed using 2.5 × 10¹¹ vg/rat with 0.001%, 0.002%, 0.004%, or 0.008% fluorescein. Results: Transduction of critical autonomic nervous system sites increased with dose. The two highest doses (2.5 × 10¹¹ and 6.5 × 10¹¹ vg/rat) produced abundant, comparable transduction in the nodose ganglia and medulla, identifying 2.5 × 10¹¹ vg/rat as the optimal dose. Fluorescein did not inhibit AAV9 transduction in CHO Lec2 cells at the concentrations tested. In vivo, 0.004% fluorescein provided clear visualization during vagus nerve injection. Conclusions: Direct intraneural administration of AAV9/GFP at 2.5 × 10¹¹ vg/rat with 0.004% fluorescein offers an effective formulation for vagus nerve delivery in rats. Further validation and dose-scaling studies are suggested to establish feasibility for translation to larger animals and humans.
records.authors: Regmi NL, Armao D, Chen X, Hu Y, Bailey RM, Gray SJ.

records.title: Diversity and Fungicide Sensitivity of Colletotrichum Species Causing Glomerella Leaf Spot and Apple Bitter Rot in Northern China.
records.abstract: Glomerella leaf spot (GLS) and apple bitter rot (ABR), collectively associated with over 20 Colletotrichum species, are two distinct diseases that cause substantial losses in apple production. In this study, phylogenetic analysis of 177 isolates collected across five provinces in northern China identified four species within the Colletotrichum gloeosporioides species complex, namely C. aenigma, C. fructicola, C. gloeosporioides, and C. siamense. C. siamense was the dominant agent of ABR (68.8%), whereas C. aenigma was the primary cause of GLS (76.9%), a pattern distinct from pathogen populations in the American continents. Fungicide profiling of the 177 isolates revealed that 41.2% of isolates showed high-level resistance to the quinone outside inhibitor (QoI) fungicide pyraclostrobin, largely attributable to the G143A mutation in the cytb gene. In contrast, sensitivity to the DMI fungicide difenoconazole remained largely unaltered. Inter- and intraspecific variation in fungicide tolerance was evident, with C. aenigma exhibiting significantly greater tolerance to both pyraclostrobin and difenoconazole compared with C. siamense. Further screening of nine additional fungicides identified prochloraz, fluazinam, penthiopyrad, and cyprodinil as highly effective against pyraclostrobin-resistant isolates. This study reveals the diversity of Colletotrichum pathogens of apple in northern China, highlights a critical need for fungicide resistance surveillance in production, and provides useful information for mitigating QoI fungicide resistance based on rational fungicide rotation.
records.authors: Chen W, Wu C, Ma H, Wu R, Zheng Y, Qiao Z, Qaisar MH, Zhang R, Sun G, Zhu M, Liang X.

records.title: Layer-number-controlled Fe-tea polyphenol metal-phenolic network-coated PLCL/gelatin electrospun membranes for active preservation of yellow sweet cherries.
records.abstract: To address postharvest fruit spoilage from microbial contamination and oxidation, biodegradable PLCL/gelatin electrospun membranes were functionalized with layer-number-controlled Fe-tea polyphenol (Fe-TP) networks via layer-by-layer assembly. Fe-TP deposition increased fiber diameter, improved hydrophilicity, and enhanced mechanical strength while maintaining flexibility. Increasing the number of assembly cycles enhanced TP release and antioxidant activity, delayed degradation, and improved antibacterial activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. Cytocompatibility and hemolysis assays indicated favorable biosafety. SEM and leakage assays suggested membrane disruption and intracellular leakage as possible antibacterial mechanisms. In yellow sweet cherry preservation, the Fe-TP effectively delayed decay. Although Fe-TP/PLCL-Gel 8 exhibited stronger antibacterial and hydrophilic performance, the Fe-TP/PLCL-Gel 4 achieved the best overall balance of mechanical properties, release, safety, and preservation efficacy, with a day-7 decay rate of only 1.85% ± 3.21%, versus 50.00% ± 5.56% for PE control. This layer-optimized multifunctional electrospun membrane offers a highly effective, promising material for fruit preservation.
records.authors: Liu J, Yan T, Wang Q, Bao J, Li Y, Piao J, Chai H, Zhou G.

records.title: A fibril-selective single-domain antibody targets pathogenic amyloid-β assemblies and protects human neurons.
records.abstract: Alzheimer disease is characterized by extracellular amyloid-β deposition that contributes to neuronal dysfunction and degeneration. Although anti-amyloid-β antibodies reduce plaque burden, their use requires monitoring for amyloid-related imaging abnormalities. Here, phage display against immobilized Aβ40 fibrils representing a patient-relevant polymorph identified J8, a fibril-selective, Fc-free single-domain antibody. J8 bound fibrils with high apparent affinity, showed no detectable binding to monomeric Aβ40, decorated fibril surfaces, and recognized plaque-associated amyloid in Alzheimer disease brain tissue. During concurrent fibril exposure, J8 reduced apoptotic signaling in human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived cortical neurons and forebrain organoids. Single-nucleus profiling of pooled organoids identified fibril-associated stress programs and opposite-direction expression patterns in the FibJ8 condition; fibril-associated changes showed the strongest directional concordance with advanced disease pathology. These findings identify J8 as a fibril-selective candidate and support organoid-based evaluation of anti-amyloid reagents as a fit-for-purpose preclinical tool.
records.authors: Greenlee MA, Amniouel S, Rivera I, Suh J, Martinez NJ, Simeonov A, Head E, Tycko R, Zheng W, Fleming BD, Zhang Q.

records.title: Computational prioritization and molecular dynamics analysis of FOXA2 missense variants with potential relevance to colorectal cancer.
records.abstract: The pioneer transcription factor FOXA2 controls developmental gene programmes, metabolic homeostasis and epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity, and its expression dysregulation is a recognized feature of colorectal cancer. The structural and thermodynamic consequences of FOXA2 missense variants remain poorly defined. We interrogated 659 missense SNPs across the human FOXA2 locus within an integrated multi-algorithm framework. Sequential filtering with SIFT, PolyPhen-2, PhD-SNP and SNPs&GO converged on three high-confidence deleterious variants (M190I, R197Q and L402P), which were profiled further with ConSurf, I-Mutant 2.0, MUpro, MutPred2 and DynaMut2. Conservation and structural mapping placed M190I (ConSurf-8) and R197Q (ConSurf-9) in the winged-helix DNA-binding domain (PF00250) and L402P (ConSurf-5) in the HNF_C domain (PF09354). R197Q is solvent-exposed and predicted to perturb promoter DNA contacts, whereas the buried M190I and L402P substitutions are predicted to act through local destabilization at the substitution site. In three independent 50-ns molecular dynamics replicates per system, all variants deviated from wild-type backbone behavior. M190I converged prematurely into a displaced conformational state, whereas R197Q and L402P continued to drift late in the trajectories. Backbone fluctuations increased non-locally, clustering in flexible regulatory segments (~290-316) and the C-terminal transactivation domain 2 (452-456). Principal component analysis indicated a more concentrated collective-mode structure in the mutants, and dynamic cross-correlation analysis weakened residue coupling, consistent with disrupted long-range communication. Of twelve trajectory-level comparisons, only the R197Q hydrogen-bond reduction reached nominal significance (p = 0.025, Hedges' g = -2.28), indicating a large reduction in average hydrogen-bond count relative to wild-type; the remaining eleven comparisons showed non-significant moderate-to-large effects. Expression enrichment was highest in colorectal cancer cell lines, providing expression-level context for FOXA2 in CRC biology. These findings computationally prioritize M190I, R197Q and L402P as candidates for experimental validation.

records.title: USF2 deficiency enhances intracellular clearance of Salmonella Typhimurium via xenophagy and LC3-associated phagocytosis.
records.abstract: The upstream stimulatory factor 2 (USF2) is a transcription factor known as a transcriptional activator that binds to E-box motifs in gene promoters. Recently, we reported that USF2 is also a transcriptional repressor of the genes that encode lysosomes and autophagy machinery, and that its deficiency results in the elevation of autophagy. The present study was designed to determine whether the absence of USF2 is responsible for more effective protection of the host cells from bacterial infection and intracellular bacterial growth. In this context, we employed Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium (S. Typhimurium) as a model pathogen and monitored the changes in intracellular bacterial burden observed in the wild-type (WT) cells and USF2-deficient cells over the time course of infection. The number of intracellular bacteria increased after infection in WT cells but remained similar or decreased in USF2-deficient cells. This phenomenon was observed in various cell types, including mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs), RAW264.7 macrophage-like cells, and primary bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs). The phagocytosis levels were the same in WT and USF2-deficient macrophages, but the latter had a higher basal autophagy, increased lysosome abundance, and increased expression of lysosomal genes. In addition, the components of LC3-associated phagocytosis (LAP), such as LC3B and RUBICON, together with reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, were elevated in USF2-deficient macrophages. Our results demonstrated that the enhanced autophagy in non-phagocytic cells and the elevated autophagy and LAP in phagocytes both contribute to the improved clearance of intracellular pathogens in USF2-deficient cells.
records.authors: Kwon J, Jeon J, Kim JW, Bae H, Kim J, Yu YS, Baek SH, Kim KI.

records.title: Antimicrobial susceptibility and virulence phenotypes of Escherichia coli isolated from bovine milk and feces in Brazil.
records.abstract: Escherichia coli is a versatile pathogen that causes bovine mastitis and acts as a reservoir of virulence and antimicrobial resistance genes, causing risks to both animal and public health. This study characterized 83 E. coli isolates from milk samples of cows with clinical (n = 19) or subclinical mastitis (n = 33) and fecal samples from lactating cows (n = 31) in Brazil. The isolates were evaluated for phylogenetic group, antimicrobial susceptibility, extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL), plasmid-mediated colistin resistance (mcr), O157 genotype, and biofilm formation. Phylogenetic classification revealed predominance of phylogroups A and B1. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing showed resistance to phenicols (38.6%), β-lactams (27.7%), polymyxins (20.5%), and tetracyclines (20.5%), with multidrug resistance (MDR) observed in 20.5% of isolates, most frequently among clinical mastitis and fecal strains. ESBL production was detected in 47.4% of the isolates evaluated, often concomitant with MDR. All isolates tested negative for the mcr genes, despite 20.5% being colistin-resistant, and were also negative for the O157 antigen. Biofilm formation was widespread, observed in 79.5% of the isolates. These results demonstrated the circulation of diverse antimicrobial-resistant profiles of E. coli strains in Brazilian dairy farms. Taken together, the coexistence of multidrug resistance, ESBL production, and biofilm-forming ability among isolates from mastitic milk and bovine feces indicates that antimicrobial-resistant E. coli strains are present in both clinical and intestinal reservoirs within dairy herds. Furthermore, the detection of colistin-resistant isolates lacking the investigated mcr genes suggests the involvement of alternative resistance mechanisms that warrant further investigation.

records.title: Aircraft and Airport Wastewater Surveillance for Public Health Preparedness Demands an Integrated and Sustainable Approach.
records.abstract: As domestic and international travel has expanded, the risk of the cross-border dissemination of infectious pathogens has increased, as clearly evidenced during the COVID-19 pandemic. Aircraft- and airport-based wastewater surveillance can provide timely, aggregate evidence of pathogen circulation among mobile populations and may complement clinical, genomic, and syndromic surveillance at points of entry. The strongest evidence for this approach comes from SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection and variant monitoring in aircraft lavatory wastewater, airport terminal wastewater, and airport-associated wastewater systems. However, aviation wastewater signals require cautious interpretation because detectability depends on pathogen shedding dynamics, passenger lavatory use, flight duration, sampling matrix, sample volume, assay sensitivity, sequencing depth, and the availability of epidemiological metadata. This structured narrative review synthesizes current evidence on aircraft and airport wastewater surveillance and examines the scientific determinants that influence surveillance validity and interpretation. Key methodological considerations include sampling design, sample preservation, nucleic acid extraction, molecular detection, sequencing, bioinformatics, inhibition assessment, recovery controls, assay sensitivity, and quality assurance. The review emphasizes that wastewater signals are aggregate and matrix-dependent and should not be interpreted as individual-level diagnosis, direct evidence of transmission, or definitive attribution to a specific flight, route, country, or population. Although SARS-CoV-2 surveillance is comparatively well-documented, multi-pathogen surveillance for enteric viruses, respiratory viruses, vaccine-preventable infections, emerging pathogens, and antimicrobial resistance markers requires pathogen-specific validation and clearer interpretation criteria. Aircraft and airport wastewater surveillance is therefore best viewed as an early-warning and situational-awareness approach whose value depends on converting technical signals into scientifically interpretable evidence.
records.authors: Vaidya SR, Pandey PG, Giri S, Pati S.

records.title: Nelfinavir Synergizes with Cisplatin and Promotes GSDME-Associated Lytic Cell Death in Platinum-Resistant Ovarian Cancer Cells.
records.abstract: Background/Objectives: Platinum resistance limits the efficacy of ovarian cancer treatment and arises through multiple mechanisms, including enhanced DNA repair, activation of stress responses, and increased survival signaling. Nelfinavir (NFV), an HIV protease inhibitor with reported anti-tumor activity, is a candidate for drug repurposing, but its interaction with cisplatin (CDDP) in ovarian cancer has not been established. Here, we investigated whether NFV enhances CDDP cytotoxicity in platinum (Pt)-resistant ovarian cancer cells and characterized the associated cell death response. Methods: Drug interaction was assessed using cell vitality and viability assays and Loewe additivity modeling together with Bliss and ZIP analyses. Cell death was characterized by Annexin V/7-AAD staining, mitochondrial membrane potential analysis, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release, immunoblotting, pharmacological caspase inhibition, and bulk mRNA sequencing with differential expression and gene set enrichment analyses. Results: NFV synergistically enhanced CDDP cytotoxicity across three Pt-resistant ovarian cancer cell lines, reducing CDDP IC50 values by 4.2-5.8-fold and producing mean Loewe synergy scores of approximately 25-30. Combination treatment increased LDH release and was accompanied by caspase-8, caspase-3, PARP, and the pore-forming death effector gasdermin E (GSDME) cleavage. Caspase inhibition attenuated viability loss and GSDME processing. Transcriptomic analysis identified enrichment of stress- and death-associated programs, including the unfolded protein response (UPR), apoptosis, reactive oxygen species (ROS)-associated signaling, and TNF/NF-κB signaling. Conclusions: Together, these findings demonstrate a reproducible synergistic interaction between CDDP and NFV in Pt-resistant ovarian cancer cells and characterize an associated lytic cell death phenotype involving apoptotic signaling and accompanied by GSDME processing. These findings support further investigation of NFV as a repurposed combination partner to enhance CDDP cytotoxicity in Pt-resistant ovarian cancer.
records.authors: Forgie BN, Prakash R, Marno D, Abdalbari FH, Zorychta E, Noman ASM, Goyeneche AA, Gilbert L, Burnier JV, Telleria CM.

records.title: Yield and Yield Components in Soybean Using Genome-Wide Association Studies, GWAS: Current Status, Challenges, and Breeding Prospects.
records.abstract: Molecular-genetic analysis of soybean yield and yield components under drought is a crucial element for the development of effective breeding strategies and sustainable agricultural production. The aim of this review is to critically analyse current data from genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and identified genetic loci, SNP markers, and candidate genes associated with yield components in soybean in dry conditions with limited water supply and adequate watering (controls). In the results, 346 genetic associations, and 229 candidate genes with KEGG-based potential functions were sufficiently described in published papers and selected for the current study. Three statistically significant metabolic pathways were identified with isoflavonoid biosynthesis, glycosaminoglycan degradation and cysteine and methionine metabolism. The main limitation of the presented analysis was found in the low level of heritability for the studied traits, together with human factors such as carrying out and interpreting GWAS affecting the results presented in the current study. Additionally, complex multigenic controls were reported for the studied traits in soybean and a high level of genotype × environment interactions. Nevertheless, the presented data provide a basis for developing molecular strategies to improve soybean yield in conjunction with better potential drought tolerance.
records.authors: Amangeldiyeva A, Didorenko S, Maikotov B, Jenisbayeva A, Shavrukov Y, Yerzhebayeva R.

records.title: Shenqi Granules Ameliorate Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury by Regulating Glucocerebrosidase and Uridine Metabolism in Microglia.
records.abstract: Objective: Shenqi Granules is a traditional Chinese medicine formula derived from the classic prescription Shenqi Formula (SQF), composed of Astragali Radix (Huangqi) and Codonopsis Radix (Dangshen). SQF shows neuroprotection in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI), but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Methods: The rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) was established using the suture method to evaluate the neuroprotective effect of SQF. Blood-absorbed components were identified via UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS, and potential targets and pathways were predicted through network pharmacology. Non-targeted metabolomics of serum and feces was performed using UHPLC-Orbitrap MS, and core metabolic pathways were selected based on regulation magnitude (RM). Gut microbiota structure was analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing, with associations between microbiota and metabolites assessed via the Mantel test and redundancy analysis (RDA). Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was applied to screen core Hub genes for ischemic stroke (IS). Based on single-cell RNA data, a uridine transport/metabolism-associated transcriptional signature score (Uridine_Score) was constructed, and cell type-specific coupling between glucocerebrosidase (GBA) and this transcriptional signature was analyzed. Microglial temporal trajectory analysis was conducted using Monocle3. Molecular docking between core components and GBA was verified by AutoDock, and GBA mRNA expression was confirmed by RT-qPCR. Results: High-dose SQF reduced infarct volume and neuronal damage and improved behavior. A total of 28 absorbed components and 31 shared IS targets were identified. Metabolomics revealed nucleotide metabolism as a core pathway common to both serum and fecal samples. SQF restored gut-blood uridine balance (serum uridine 0.41× Sham → 0.85× post-SQF), reduced fecal dTMP and hypoxanthine. 16S rRNA sequencing demonstrated that the overall correlation between microbial community structure and nucleotide metabolites was statistically significant (Mantel r = 0.307-0.321, p p Conclusions: SQF reprograms nucleotide metabolism via the gut-blood axis and enhances microglial GBA-uridine transport/metabolism-associated transcriptional coupling.

records.title: Expression Profile of Transfer RNA-Derived Fragments in Chinese Mitten Crab (Eriocheir sinensis) After Challenge with Aeromonas hydrophila.
records.abstract: The Chinese mitten crab (Eriocheir sinensis) is an important cultured crab in China; however, its aquaculture productivity is severely limited by bacterial pathogens, including Aeromonas hydrophila. Transfer RNA-derived fragments (tRFs) are an emerging class of functional small non-coding RNAs that have been implicated in host-pathogen interactions and immune regulation; yet, their roles in the antibacterial defense of crustaceans remain poorly understood. To investigate the immune response of the Chinese mitten crab to A. hydrophila infection, we employed high-throughput sequencing to characterize the expression profiles and functional features of tRFs in crab hemocytes following a bacterial challenge. The results revealed that tRFs exhibited a conserved length distribution (15-20 nt) and subtype composition, with 5'-tRFs representing the dominant subtype in both control and infected groups. Notably, infection specifically induced the abundance of tRF fragments of 35-nt tRF fragments and slightly altered the proportion of tRF subtypes. Differential expression analysis identified 415 significantly upregulated and 3 downregulated tRFs upon A. hydrophila infection, suggesting widespread changes in tRF abundance during infection. Target prediction and functional enrichment analyses were performed for the top 30 differentially expressed tRFs; the predicted targets were significantly associated with VEGF signaling pathway, DNA replication proteins, FoxO signaling pathway, and NF-kappa B signaling pathway. The reliability of the sequencing data was confirmed by stem-loop RT-qPCR validation. Collectively, our findings advance the understanding of tRF expression in crustacean immunity and suggest that tRFs may be associated with the immune response of crabs against bacterial infection, pending functional validation.

records.title: An Evidence-Tiered Developmental Framework for Congenital Vertebral Malformations: Spatiotemporal Thresholds in Genotype-Phenotype Interpretation.
records.abstract: Congenital vertebral malformations (CVMs) encompass formation, segmentation and mixed defects, with or without scoliosis. This narrative review relates human genetic findings to paraxial mesoderm specification, somitogenesis, sclerotome differentiation and vertebral morphogenesis. An author-defined evidence hierarchy distinguishes established disease relationships, emerging susceptibility mechanisms and hypothesis-generating observations; it is not a formal ClinGen classification. Replicated TBX6 dosage mechanisms and disease-specific segmentation disorders provide stronger etiological evidence than candidate-gene burden signals, regulatory hypotheses or accessible-tissue methylation associations. Evidence is assigned to a defined gene-disease or mechanism-phenotype relationship, not to a gene or pathway universally. Building on previous developmental and gene-environment models, we outline a conceptual spatiotemporal threshold framework in which dosage, developmental stage, tissue distribution and modifiers may influence vertebral anatomy. No numerical human threshold has been established. Explicit appraisal criteria, relationship-specific evidence summaries and proposed experimental tests separate demonstrated findings from extrapolation. Standardized vertebral and rib phenotyping, associated anomalies and inheritance remain essential for genomic interpretation. Molecular diagnosis may inform counseling and syndrome-specific evaluation but does not independently establish prognosis or surgical indications.
records.authors: Wang X, Zhang Q, Ji E, Sui Y, Zhu Q, Li K, Xue X.

records.title: Optimization and Comparative Evaluation of DNA Extraction Protocols for Arbuscular Mycorrhizal Fungi in Coffee Roots.
records.abstract: Molecular studies of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) in coffee root require DNA extracts that are sufficiently pure for PCR amplification. Coffea arabica roots remains challenging because of the abundance of phenolic compounds, polysaccharides, and other inhibitors. This study compared four DNA extraction protocols, including two CTAB-based phenol-chloroform methods, a commercial extraction kit, and a modified commercial kit incorporating mechanical disruption, proteinase K predigestion, and β-mercaptoethanol treatment. Quality of total DNA extracts was assessed using NanoDrop spectrophotometry (A260/A280 and A260/A230 ratios), agarose gel electrophoresis, and PCR amplification of the AMF SSU (18S rDNA) region using AMV4.5NF/AMDGR primers. Conventional phenol-chloroform methods yielded high DNA concentrations but poor purity, indicating substantial co-extraction of inhibitory compounds. The commercial kit without predigestion yielded lower spectrophotometric purity but still produced successful AMF-targeted PCR amplification. In contrast, the modified protocol yielded the highest spectrophotometric purity ratios while retaining successful amplification across all samples. These results indicate that incorporation of the predigestion step was associated with higher post-extraction spectrophotometric ratios without compromising successful AMF-targeted PCR amplification. The optimized protocol provides a reproducible method for obtaining PCR-quality DNA from coffee roots and represents a methodological contribution to molecular studies of the diversity of AMF and other root-associated microorganisms in coffee agroecosystems.

records.title: The Role of the OBSCN Gene in Cardiomyopathy: A Review of Molecular Mechanisms and Clinical Significance.
records.abstract: Cardiomyopathies are genetically heterogeneous myocardial diseases that can lead to heart failure, arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death. OBSCN encodes obscurin, a giant sarcomere-associated protein involved in sarcomere organization, cytoskeletal coupling, calcium handling, and cell-cell adhesion signaling. This review synthesizes current evidence on OBSCN variants in cardiomyopathy, focusing on their spectrum, phenotypic associations, and potential pathogenic mechanisms. Curated variants were systematically interpreted according to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) and the Association for Molecular Pathology (AMP) guidelines. Putative truncating variants predominated among variants of uncertain significance, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy was the most frequently reported phenotype. Co-occurring variants in established or candidate cardiomyopathy-associated genes were reported for some OBSCN variants, particularly missense variants. However, co-occurrence alone does not establish an independent pathogenic contribution, oligogenic inheritance, or a genetic modifier effect. Potential mechanisms include obscurin insufficiency, destabilization of sarcomeric scaffolding, impaired sarcoplasmic reticulum coupling, dysregulated calcium homeostasis, altered mechanotransduction, and defective intercellular adhesion. Overall, OBSCN is an emerging but incompletely characterized cardiomyopathy-associated gene, and truncating variants warrant further clinical and mechanistic investigation.

records.title: Dissecting the Radioresponse Heterogeneity of Lung Adenocarcinoma Cells From the Perspective of Transcriptional and Regulatory Landscape.
records.abstract: Radioresistance severely compromises radiotherapy efficacy for lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), yet the intrinsic heterogeneity of cellular radioresponses among isogenic tumor cells remains poorly characterized. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin with high-throughput sequencing (scATAC-seq) to dissect the transcriptional and regulatory landscape underlying heterogeneous radioresponses in single-cell-derived LUAD cells following 6 Gy γ-ray irradiation. We found that isogenic LUAD cells harbored intrinsic molecular determinants for divergent radiosensitivity and displayed heterogeneous radioresponsiveness upon irradiation. A radiation-associated transcriptional cell state, coupled with DNA damage repair, apoptosis, and cell cycle regulation, emerged at 6 h post-irradiation. Inhibition of lysine demethylase 4B (KDM4B) enhanced LUAD radiosensitivity by intensifying DNA damage, whereas reduced expression of cyclin B1 (CCNB1) and DNA topoisomerase IIα (TOP2A) potentially contributed to radiation-triggered G2/M arrest. Notably, the radiation-associated regulatory cell state emerged earlier than radiation-induced transcriptional cell state. RNA polymerase II subunit A (POLR2A) functioned as a core regulator in high-responsive LUAD cells. Based on these findings, we proposed a hypothesis for the radiosensitization of LUAD cells. Collectively, this study provides multilayer mechanistic insights into LUAD radioresponse heterogeneity and yields actionable molecular candidates for developing improved radiosensitization strategies to advance precise radiotherapy for LUAD.

records.title: Long-term Effectiveness, Treatment Persistence, and Timing of Virological Failure With Long-Acting Cabotegravir Plus Rilpivirine in Real-World HIV Care: RELATIVITY Cohort.
records.abstract: BackgroundLong-acting injectable cabotegravir plus rilpivirine (CAB + RPV LA) is an established maintenance option for virologically suppressed people with human immunodeficiency virus-1 (HIV-1), but long-term real-world persistence and virological failure (VF) data remain limited.MethodsRELATIVITY is an ongoing nationwide ambispective multicenter cohort of adults with HIV who switched from suppressive oral antiretroviral therapy to CAB + RPV LA in routine care in Spain. Data through 1 March 2026 were analyzed. The outcomes were virological suppression, treatment persistence, protocol-defined VF, and time to discontinuation-related events. Virological failure was defined as 2 consecutive HIV-1 RNA values ≥200 copies/mL or 1 value ≥500 copies/mL prompting discontinuation.ResultsAmong 3349 participants, 3343 had valid follow-up dates; the median follow-up was 25.1 months (19.3-30.8). Virological suppression was documented in 3197/3349 (95.5%) overall and 3197/3309 (96.6%) with an evaluable closest viral load; 40 (1.2%) lacked an evaluable value. Injection adherence was ≥90% in 3257/3280 (99.3%) evaluable participants. Overall, 2979/3349 (89.0%) remained on CAB + RPV LA. Virological failure occurred in 28/3349 (0.8%); 20/28 (71.4%) occurred within the first 12 months after switching. Emergent integrase strand transfer inhibitor and/or nonnucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor resistance was detected in 19/28 VF cases, and 24/28 achieved virological suppression after switching to oral therapy. Treatment-limiting injection-site reactions and systemic adverse events occurred in 2.4% and 1.6%, respectively.ConclusionsLong-acting injectable cabotegravir plus rilpivirine showed high virological suppression and persistence beyond 2 years in routine care. Virological failure was uncommon and clustered mainly within 12 months, supporting early virological monitoring and prompt resistance-guided management.

records.title: Astragali Radix-Curcumae Rhizoma synergistically potentiates 5-fluorouracil antitumor efficacy in colorectal cancer by disrupting DNA repair-cell cycle coordination.
records.abstract: BackgroundAstragali Radix (HQ) and Curcumae Rhizoma (EZ), collectively termed AC, are commonly used as an herb pair in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) for colorectal cancer (CRC). Although AC has been used as an adjuvant to chemotherapy, the molecular basis by which it enhances the efficacy of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) remains incompletely defined.MethodsThe antitumor effect of AC alone and in combination with 5-FU was evaluated in a HCT116 xenograft mouse model and in CRC cell lines with different genetic backgrounds. Potential systemic toxicity was assessed using serum biochemical markers. Transcriptomic changes induced by AC were analyzed by RNA sequencing and integrated with network pharmacology and The Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) (GSE17536, GSE17537, GSE41258, GSE20916). Key targets were validated by Western blotting and immunofluorescence. Cell viability, drug interaction, apoptosis, cell-cycle distribution and DNA damage were assessed using CCK-8 assays, Synergy Finder analysis, flow cytometry, and γ-H2AX staining. Bioavailable AC-derived constituents were characterized by UPLC-QTOF-MS, and candidate active compounds were further evaluated by molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, cellular thermal shift assay, and functional validation.ResultsAC potentiated the antitumor efficacy of 5-FU in vivo and did not exacerbate 5-FU-associated hepatic or renal biochemical toxicity under the tested conditions. In vitro, AC-containing serum extracts inhibited CRC cell viability, induced reversible G2/M-phase arrest, and enhanced 5-FU sensitivity in HCT116, CT26, and HCT15 cells. AC treatment caused limited early apoptosis, whereas delayed apoptosis was observed after prolonged exposure, suggesting that cell-cycle arrest represents the primary early response. RNA-seq and integrative analyses showed that AC suppressed pathways associated with DNA replication, mismatch repair, ribosome biogenesis, and cell-cycle progression. AC downregulated key regulators involved in cell-cycle control, DNA repair, and stress-survival signaling, including PLK1, CDK1, CCNB1, CDC25A, c-JUN, MSH2, BRCA1, and p-AKT. Combination treatment further increased γ-H2AX accumulation and reduced cell-cycle regulatory proteins. Functional validation indicated that c-JUN overexpression partially attenuated AC-mediated 5-FU sensitization, whereas pharmacological AKT inhibition partially mimicked the sensitizing effect of AC. Among the serum-exposed constituents, Demethoxycurcumin and Kumatakenin were identified as bioavailable active compounds that partially recapitulated the effects of AC by inducing G2/M-phase arrest and enhancing the antiproliferative activity of 5-FU. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and CETSA supported their target engagement with cell-cycle regulators, particularly CCNB1 and CDK1.ConclusionAC enhances the therapeutic efficacy of 5-FU in CRC by weakening DNA repair-cell-cycle coordination and stress-survival signaling, thereby increasing 5-FU-induced DNA damage and promoting cell-cycle arrest. Demethoxycurcumin and Kumatakenin may represent important bioavailable contributors to this chemosensitizing effect, although the complete AC extract likely acts through multi-component and multi-target mechanisms. These findings provide mechanistic support for the use of AC as an adjunctive strategy to improve 5-FU-based chemotherapy in CRC.
records.authors: Wang S, Huang K, Cheng Y, Sun C, Wang K, He Q, Yin G, Tang D, Zhang Y, Tan X.

records.title: Genome-wide analyses identify 60 loci associated with liver triglyceride content.
records.abstract: We performed a large-scale genome-wide association study meta-analysis of magnetic resonance imaging-derived liver triglyceride content across 71,488 European-ancestry participants from the UK Biobank, approximately doubling the sample size of previous genome-wide association studies1. We identified 60 independent loci, including 31 not previously reported, and estimated the single nucleotide polymorphism-based heritability of liver triglyceride content at 25%. Integrative fine-mapping and gene-prioritization analyses nominated candidate effector genes for 48 loci. Of the 31 newly identified variants, 14 were validated in meta-analyses of clinically diagnosed metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (42,163 cases and 1,646,254 controls). People in the highest versus lowest decile of a polygenic risk score for liver triglyceride content had 2.71-fold higher odds of cirrhosis and 7.47-fold higher odds of hepatocellular carcinoma. Plasma proteins associated with the liver triglyceride polygenic risk score were enriched for metabolic remodeling and inflammatory pathways, with liver-enriched protein signatures increasing and visceral adipose signatures decreasing with higher genetic risk. Together, these findings refine the genetic architecture of liver triglyceride content, linking polygenic susceptibility to downstream metabolic and inflammatory pathways and providing insights into the genetic basis of steatotic liver disease.

records.title: Pseudouridylation landscape across 42 nuclear-encoded S. cerevisiae tRNAs.
records.abstract: Pseudouridine is the most abundant RNA base modification due to its prevalence in tRNA and rRNA, where it serves as a key modulator of structure and function. Yet, in the widely used model organism, the budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae, tRNA pseudouridine sites have not been comprehensively annotated. Here, we performed two high-throughput methods established for detecting tRNA pseudouridylation positions: Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS) and 2-bromoacrylamide-assisted cyclization sequencing (BACS). Using DRS, we sequenced cytosolic tRNA from seven pseudouridine synthase (PUS) knockout S. cerevisiae strains, including deletion strains of Pus1, Pus3, and Pus7. Analysis of these data verified thirty-two existing pseudouridine annotations and predicted an additional ten previously unannotated pseudouridine sites. Our analysis also revealed DRS signal changes at several non-uridine sites with the loss of a PUS, including apparent changes in modification abundances at position 37 upon deletion of Pus3. Liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) and primer extension assays, however, indicated no change in the abundance of these modifications with the loss of Pus3, underscoring the need for caution in interpreting DRS-based signal changes. Using BACS, we confirmed the ten DRS-predicted novel sites, while further detecting eleven additional previously unannotated pseudouridine sites. Combining existing modification annotations from the Modomics database with our DRS and BACS datasets, we created a map of all detected pseudouridines-totaling 126 sites, including 21 novel sites-and the enzymes responsible for their catalysis, across the forty-two nuclear-encoded S. cerevisiae tRNA isoacceptors.
records.authors: Barry ML, Abu-Shumays RL, Barnes LE, Shaw EA, Reinsch JL, Basham ZD, Jain M, Koutmou KS, Garcia DM.

records.title: Impact of nationwide parvovirus B19 DNA screening and identification of transfusion-transmitted infections.
records.abstract: Background and objectivesParvovirus B19 (B19V) testing is often not required to release blood components. However, the European Pharmacopoeia requires that plasma pools for fractionation contain no more than 104 IU/mL of B19V DNA. In France, pool B19 nucleic acid testing (NAT) screening was performed by Établissement Français du Sang since 2015. Since June 2024, positive pools are broken down into individual testing, allowing for the identification and management of infected blood donations.Materials and methodsB19V NAT is performed in pools of 96 donations (P96) with the DPX Parvo/hepatitis A virus assay (Roche). A P96 with a viral load >104 IU/mL B19V DNA is considered positive. All individual donations (IDs) testing reactive for B19V by ID-NAT are excluded from plasma-based medicinal products production, and the corresponding blood components are destroyed if not yet transfused.ResultsFrom June 2024 to June 2025, 99 of 2,627,678 donations (3.7/100,000) were B19V DNA positive. All blood components related to 90 donations were discarded. Of the remaining nine donations, 13 blood components (9 platelet concentrates [PCs] that had undergone pathogen reduction (PR) and four red blood cell [RBC] concentrates) were transfused before NAT results were obtained. Two B19V transmissions were reported in recipients (0.078/100,000 transfusions) after transfusion of 1 PR-PC and 1 RBC unit.ConclusionB19V DNA testing for plasma intended for fractionation performed in blood services helps in avoiding transmissions by the related blood components, provided positive donations are detected prior to their transfusion. Delayed availability of results may result in transfusion-transmitted B19V infection, which cannot prevented by current PR technology.
records.authors: de la Taille V, Bacquet C, Guillet M, Barday G, Monnier C, Maccio G, Gallian P, Destras G, Cam SL, Pouchol E, Peyrard T, Tiberghien P, Laperche S.

records.title: Analytical validation of MethyLiverDx-Sigma, a plasma cfDNA methylation assay for hepatocellular carcinoma detection.
records.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance relies on ultrasonography and alpha-fetoprotein, both limited in sensitivity for early-stage disease; aberrant methylation of circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) offers a promising blood-based approach. Reported here is the analytical validation of MethyLiverDx-Sigma (MLDx-s), an assay that detects methylated RNF135 and DNMT3A in bisulfite-converted plasma cfDNA by methylation-specific PCR with high-resolution melting (HRM), with GAPDH as an endogenous control. Performance was evaluated following CLSI EP05-A3, EP07, EP12-A2, and EP37. Precision of quantification cycle (Cq) and melting peak temperature (Tm) was assessed by variance-component analysis within one site and across two sites and two operators. Because precision studies used bulk bisulfite-converted reference DNA, the reported coefficients of variation (CVs) primarily characterize the PCR-HRM detection module; end-to-end variability in clinical plasma specimens may be higher. Interference and cross-reactivity were evaluated in low-positive and contrived-negative samples against reproducibility-derived limits, with dose-response testing of reactive substances. Detection was 100% at both levels, and every run met control-validity criteria. Cq repeatability CVs ranged from 0.53% to 1.68%, and total reproducibility CVs ranged from 1.10% to 2.37%; all Tm CVs were ≤0.20%. All 18 interferents and 16 microbial cross-reactants evaluated in low-positive samples met the predefined acceptance criteria. In negative samples, hemoglobin, SARS-CoV-2, and measles virus produced concentration-dependent non-specific amplification, and dose-response testing established their respective no-effect concentrations. These findings characterize the analytical precision and multisite reproducibility of the PCR-HRM detection module and the analytical specificity of MLDx-s, complementing its previously reported clinical performance for plasma-based HCC detection.
records.authors: Kim SC, Choi H, Chung J, Lee ST, Kim YJ.

records.title: Emergence of bimodal First Passage Time distributions from Transcription Translation Coupling.
records.abstract: Transcription and translation are fundamentally stochastic processes that drive significant variability in mRNA and protein levels within living cells. In certain cellular environments, these processes occur simultaneously, motivating the Transcription-Translation Coupled (TTC) model. We present a simple model of stochastic gene regulation incorporating TTC that yields bimodality in protein synthesis dynamics. By casting the estimation of protein synthesis times as a first-passage time (FPT) problem, we demonstrate that TTC generates robust bimodal FPT statistics with possible implications for bacterial survival strategies.
records.authors: Saha A, Ghosh A.

records.title: Functional analysis of SmCSN5 in salt stress tolerance of Salvia miltiorrhiza.
records.abstract: Salt stress limits plant growth, but the contribution of COP9 signalosome subunit 5 (CSN5) to salt tolerance in Salvia miltiorrhiza remains unclear. Here, we combined heterologous overexpression in Arabidopsis thaliana with overexpression and RNA interference in S. miltiorrhiza hairy roots. SmCSN5 transcript abundance increased with NaCl concentration and showed a transient response to 150 mM NaCl, peaking at 6 h among the sampled times. SmCSN5 overexpression improved germination and growth under salt stress and was associated with higher proline accumulation and antioxidant enzyme activities. Overexpressing Arabidopsis also maintained higher relative water content and chlorophyll content, with lower electrolyte leakage, malondialdehyde content, and ROS-associated staining. Separate ion measurements showed lower Na⁺ content, higher K⁺ content, and lower Na⁺/K⁺ ratios in overexpressing Arabidopsis and hairy roots. SmCSN5 RNA interference produced opposite physiological and ion-accumulation responses in hairy roots. Yeast two-hybrid and luciferase complementation assays identified SmCBL3 as a candidate SmCSN5-interacting protein. Collectively, these findings support a positive role for SmCSN5 in salt tolerance, accompanied by improved antioxidant defense, osmotic adjustment, and ion homeostasis. Whether these responses improve medicinal metabolite production under salinity remains unresolved.

records.authors: Shao S, Wang M, Zhu W, Ma P.

records.title: The conserved function of bHLH121 and overexpression of N-terminal bHLH121 fragment suppresses iron deficiency response in Arabidopsis.
records.abstract: Iron (Fe) homeostasis is fundamental to plant growth and development and is centrally regulated by a well-conserved network of basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) transcription factors. In Arabidopsis thaliana, bHLH121 regulates the expression of FER-like iron deficiency-induced transcription factor (FIT) and clade Ib bHLH38/39/100/101 genes, among others. However, its functional conservation remains unexplored, and some contradictory results have been reported regarding the effects of bHLH121 overexpression. Here, we investigated the evolutionary conservation of bHLH121 through complementary tests in the Arabidopsis bhlh121 mutant created by CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing. We also investigated the effects of ectopically expressing full-length, N-terminal, and C-terminal fragments of bHLH121 on plant responses to Fe deficiency in Arabidopsis. Transgenic plants overexpressing the full-length bHLH121 driven by the cauliflower mosaic virus 35S promoter (bHLH121 ox) resulted in shorter roots and more severe leaf chlorosis compared to wild-type plants under Fe-limiting conditions. Moreover, overexpression of the N-terminal fragment (N121 ox) rendered plants highly sensitive to Fe deficiency, whereas overexpression of the C-terminal fragment (C121 ox) did not. Consistent with the phenotypic observations, N121 ox plants accumulated lower Fe content, and the ferric chelate reductase activity was significantly reduced. In N121 ox plants, the induction of key Fe regulatory genes, especially FIT, was significantly inhibited under Fe deficiency. Confocal imaging showed that both N121-GFP and C121-GFP fusion proteins could localize to the nucleus. Electrophoretic mobility shift assay showed that both full-length bHLH121 and N121 could effectively bind the probes derived from the promoter of FIT. The present work reveals a conserved function of bHLH121 in Fe homeostasis across several dicot species and demonstrates that overexpression of N121 potently suppresses Fe deficiency responses in Arabidopsis.

records.title: Integrative single-cell and computational pathology analyses reveal a C11orf24-associated stem-like epithelial population linked to tumor microenvironment remodeling and immune evasion in bladder cancer.
records.abstract: BackgroundCancer stem-like cells drive tumor progression and therapeutic resistance, yet the epithelial stemness hierarchy in bladder cancer (BLCA) remains poorly defined. We aimed to characterize stemness-associated epithelial populations and their clinical significance.MethodsWe analyzed single-cell RNA sequencing data from 92,218 cells across 13 treatment-naïve BLCA samples to characterize epithelial stemness and tumor-microenvironment interactions. Spatial transcriptomics and independent bulk cohorts were used for orthogonal and clinical validation. An HStem-associated histopathology-based prognostic model was developed by integrating quantitative image features with deep-learning representations, followed by functional validation of the candidate gene C11orf24.ResultsWe identified a highly stem-like epithelial population (HStem) at the apex of the differentiation hierarchy, exhibiting MYC activation, oxidative phosphorylation, and DNA repair enrichment, with preferential presence in advanced-stage tumors. HStem cells were inferred to serve as major communication hubs within the TME, interacting extensively with fibroblasts and endothelial cells via MIF-CD74/CXCR4 and MIF-CD74/CD44 axes. An 86-gene HStem signature enabled development of a robust image-based prognostic model. High-risk tumors showed immune exclusion, immunosuppressive enrichment, T-cell dysfunction, and predicted checkpoint blockade resistance. C11orf24 emerged as a candidate stemness-associated regulator; C11orf24-positive cells displayed enhanced stemness and stromal interactions. Functional experiments demonstrated that C11orf24 perturbation altered clonogenic growth, migration, and invasion in BLCA cells. Pharmacogenomic analyses identified predicted therapeutic vulnerabilities that warrant experimental validation.ConclusionsWe identify an HStem population associated with BLCA progression, microenvironmental remodeling, and immune evasion. Integrating single-cell and spatial transcriptomics with computational pathology, we establish a clinically relevant stemness framework and identify C11orf24 as a potential therapeutic target, offering opportunities for stemness-directed precision oncology.
records.authors: Wang Y, Zhang S, Luo X, Wang Z, Wang Y, Li N, Liu Y, Gao J, Zhang R, Jia Z, Shi R, Zhang L.

records.title: Early treatment with tecovirimat against mpox disease in cynomolgus macaques.
records.abstract: BackgroundTecovirimat was developed as an antiviral countermeasure against orthopoxviruses and approved by the US Food and Drug Administration Animal Rule based on efficacy in preclinical studies and clinical pharmacokinetic and safety trials. However, recent randomised clinical trials in patients with mpox who initiated tecovirimat an average of 6-9 days after onset of symptoms did not show improvement in time to resolution of skin lesions. Here, we evaluated whether timing of tecovirimat initiation influenced antiviral efficacy following mpox infection in nonhuman primates and defined the therapeutic window for treatment initiation.MethodsIn this randomised preclinical study, 32 cynomolgus macaques were challenged intravenously with 1 × 106 TCID50 mpox clade IIb virus. Oral tecovirimat (10 mg/kg, once daily for 14 days) treatment was initiated on Day 2 (post-exposure and pre-symptomatic), Day 5 (early symptomatic), or Day 9 (peak symptomatic) after mpox challenge, or no treatment was given as a control group. The primary study endpoint was area under the curve (AUC) and peak numbers of progressive skin lesions. The secondary endpoint was AUC and peak levels of plasma viral loads. Additional analyses included total skin lesions, adaptive immune responses, and transcriptomic signatures.FindingsTreatment adherence was 100%. All tecovirimat-treated animals survived to study completion on Day 28, whereas two untreated control animals required early euthanisation on Days 16 and 17. Tecovirimat efficacy was time-dependent. Progressive skin lesion AUC was significantly lower when treatment was initiated on Day 2 (P  0.99).InterpretationIn this randomised preclinical study, tecovirimat demonstrated antiviral therapeutic efficacy but only when initiated early prior to peak viraemia. These findings emphasise the importance of early initiation of treatment and define the therapeutic window for optimal tecovirimat treatment in nonhuman primates.FundingThis study was supported by SIGA Technologies.
records.authors: Rössler A, Aid M, Ayala-Bernot J, Liu J, Russo AT, Grosenbach DW, Lovejoy C, Cook A, Andersen H, Hruby DE, Barouch DH.

records.title: Life Histories, Breeding Systems, and Life Cycles in Brood-Site Pollination Mutualisms.
records.abstract: In brood-site pollination mutualisms (BSPMs), insect pollinators breed within the plants that they pollinate. Organisms involved in BSPMs show adaptations in life-history strategies and life cycles. BSPM plants are monoecious or dioecious, or have bisexual flowers; are monocot or dicot; and are angiosperms or gymnosperms. All plants are perennial, mostly iteroparous, while a few are semelparous. The highly specific pollinators are mostly small-sized wasps, micromoths, thrips, fungus gnats, flower weevils, beetles, and gall midges. Most BSPMs involve ovule/seed parasites, while larvae also consume pollen, other floral tissues, and fungi. Active pollination occurs only in ovule/seed parasites, accompanied by special pollen-deposition structures and reduced pollen:ovule ratios. Quiescent stages involving egg, larval, prepupal, and pupal diapause enable synchrony with plant reproduction. Prolonged flower longevity enables the completion of larval growth. Haplodiploidy via arrhenotoky or paternal genome elimination often occurs. Many brood sites constitute mating arenas and impose restriction of mating opportunities.
records.authors: Borges RM.

records.title: The mRNA-based RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 induces robust and durable CD4<sup>+</sup> T cell responses against RSV in younger and older adults.
records.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a health threat, particularly for infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Although neutralizing antibodies can help limit infection and viral replication, T cells are essential for reducing disease severity. Assessment of age-related declines in T cell function are important for vaccine evaluation. We used intracellular cytokine staining, activation-induced marker, and Meso Scale Discovery assays and single-cell multiomic profiling to evaluate RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 responses in younger and older adults. mRNA-1345 induced comparable CD4+ and CD8+ T cell responses in both cohorts, with CD4+ responses persisting for 24 months. The CD4+ response was strongly T helper 1 (TH1)-polarized, with increased interferon-γ, interleukin-2, and tumor necrosis factor-α and minimal TH2 cytokines. Both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells showed increased polyfunctionality that remained elevated at 2 years. Single-cell and T cell receptor repertoire analyses showed similar Pre-F-specific phenotypes, transcriptional profiles, and clonal overlap across age groups, supporting robust, durable cellular immunity after mRNA-1345 vaccination. These findings indicate shared vaccine-elicited T cell immunity in adults.

records.title: Wolbachia outcompetes mosquito-borne viruses by reprogramming host ATPSβ1-driven ATP metabolism toward symbiotic proliferation.
records.abstract: Wolbachia endosymbionts confer broad-spectrum resistance to mosquito-borne viruses. While the antiviral metabolites in Wolbachia-Aedes have been identified during viral replication, the core metabolic gene underlying this defense across the entire viral infection cycle remains undefined. Here, we demonstrated for the first time that Wolbachia strongly suppressed the emerging alphavirus Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus, extending its known antiviral spectrum. Transcriptomic and functional analyses revealed ATP synthase beta subunit 1 (ATPSβ1) as a key metabolic hub hijacked by both MBV and the symbiont. Without Wolbachia symbiosis, dengue virus and VEEV induced ATPSβ1 to promote viral binding via the viral envelope protein and increased intracellular ATP production for viral replication. Conversely, Wolbachia overrode ATPSβ1-mediated viral binding and redirected ATPSβ1-driven ATP synthesis to fuel its proliferation, strengthening antiviral activity. Pharmacologically, adenosine increased Wolbachia wAlbB density and potently suppressed viral infection in Ae. aegypti and Ae. albopictus cells. Oligomycin reduced intracellular ATP and inhibited viral infection in Wolbachia-free Ae. aegypti cells. Collectively, Wolbachia repurposes dual-functional ATPSβ1, which governs MBV binding and replication, into a potent antiviral effector through a metabolic tug-of-war over host ATP during symbiont-virus competition. Moreover, we highlight interventions targeting the ATPSβ1-driven metabolism as promising strategies to curb MBV transmission.
records.authors: Yuan H, Zhang Y, Zhao Y, Wang C, Zhou Y, Ni Q, Li X, Zhang B, Wang Y, Cai L, Liu H, Wang J, Gong J, Zhang M, Xi Z, Pan X.

records.title: Lyssavirus matrix protein stabilizes RGS4 to suppress ferroptosis via incomplete autophagy and iron metabolic reprogramming.
records.abstract: Rabies virus (RABV), the prototypical lyssavirus, suppresses neuronal ferroptosis through lipid droplet (LD) biogenesis, which is a critical immune evasion strategy we previously identified. However, the mechanistic link between LD formation and ferroptosis regulation during RABV infection remains poorly defined. Here, we report that RABV upregulate Regulator of G Protein Signaling 4 (RGS4), a ferroptosis-associated regulator, and this induction is strictly dependent on triglyceride synthesis and subsequent LD formation. Functionally, genetic or pharmacological inhibition of RGS4 elevates ferroptosis susceptibility, thereby restricting viral replication. Mechanistically, RGS4 depletion reduces HERC2, impairing the assembly of branched K48/K63 ubiquitin chains on NCOA4, which is essential for its proteasomal degradation, thereby enhancing NCOA4 stability. Stabilized NCOA4 promotes ferritinophagy, leading to degradation of ferritin heavy chain (FTH) and ultimately inducing ferroptosis. Critically, we identified that the lyssavirus matrix (M) protein directly counteracts this pathway: M protein inhibits RGS4 degradation via the Cys/N-degron system through incomplete autophagy, stabilizing RGS4 to maintain HERC2 expression, promote NCOA4 ubiquitination, and attenuate ferritinophagy. This mechanism reduces ferroptosis susceptibility and enables viral replication. Our findings unveil a novel lyssavirus-specific regulatory axis, RGS4-HERC2-NCOA4-FTH, that modulates ferroptosis, highlighting the critical role of ferroptosis in lyssavirus infection and pathogenesis.
records.authors: Zhao J, Chen P, Sun M, Liang C, Fu ZF, Zhao L, Zhou M.

records.title: Particulate Matter Exposure and Accelerated Cardiovascular Aging: Mechanistic Evidence, Biomarker Integration, and the PACA Framework.
records.abstract: Particulate matter exposure, particularly PM2.5 and ultrafine particles, is a well-established risk factor for cardiovascular morbidity. However, whether pollution-associated cardiovascular abnormalities represent transient toxicity, cumulative injury, developmental programming, aging-like phenotypes, or a genuine alteration in the trajectory of cardiovascular aging remains unresolved. Here, we propose the Pollution-Accelerated Cardiovascular Aging (PACA) framework as a conceptual, hypothesis-generating approach for interpreting this distinction. Rather than proposing new molecular mechanisms, we integrate established pathways, including mitochondrial and redox dysfunction, genomic and epigenetic alterations, cellular senescence and senescence-associated secretory phenotype signaling, impaired proteostasis, endothelial dysfunction, and autonomic dysregulation within an explicit evidentiary framework. We also consider the pulmonary neural cardiac axis as a potential route through which pulmonary sensory activation may influence autonomic regulation, calcium handling, and cardiac electrophysiological function. To distinguish exposure-associated toxicity from evidence consistent with altered cardiovascular aging, we introduce a Temporal-Evidence Matrix that integrates exposure kinetics, life-course timing, persistence and recovery after exposure cessation, exposure response relationships, and longitudinal change relative to age-referenced comparators. Persistence, incomplete recovery, or cumulative loss of cardiovascular reserve support chronic or sustained injury but do not independently establish accelerated aging. Stronger evidence for PACA requires repeated longitudinal demonstration that particulate exposure is associated with a greater rate or altered trajectory of aging-related cardiovascular or biological change than expected from chronological aging. Finally, we propose a tiered biomarker framework that separates candidate biological-aging integrators from mechanistic stress and injury indicators and contextual inflammatory markers, while treating vascular and cardiac functional or imaging measures as complementary cardiovascular phenotypes. The principal contribution of PACA is therefore evidentiary rather than mechanistic, providing a structured approach for testing whether particulate exposure is associated with cardiovascular toxicity alone or with an altered cardiovascular-aging trajectory.
records.authors: Yadav P, Bhakta-Guha D, Nagarajan D, Mani KP, Mondal R, Guha G, Kurian GA.

records.title: Myco-degradation of anthraquinone dyes by immobilized white-rot fungal consortium and toxicity assessment.
records.abstract: Anthraquinone (AQ) dyes widely used in textile industries cause serious environmental and health risk due to their persistence and toxicity. In this context, myco-remediation using white-rot fungal consortium (WRFC) immobilized in chitosan beads demonstrated mixture of AQ dyes (MAQD) biodegradation with enhanced dye decolorization efficiency (97.35%) within 8 h. Further, FTIR analysis confirmed structural disruption of MAQD, including aromatic ring cleavage and functional group transformation. Moreover, LCMS analysis revealed formation of several low molecular weight intermediate organic acids such as phthalic, oxalic, malonic, succinic, fumaric, malic, citric and isocitric acids, suggesting progressive degradation of MAQD and possible microbial transformation of the degradation products. The findings were also validated by SEM and TEM analysis of the chitosan beads which evidenced WRFC immobilization and ultrastructural changes on post exposure to MAQD. The decolorization data were described using a first-order kinetic model, with the highest rate constant observed at 200 ppm. Toxicity assessment of treated (using WRFC immobilized in chitosan beads) MAQD water demonstrated substantial detoxification evidenced by 80% survival of Danio rerio in acute tests, HeLa cell line maintained 84% viability even after 24 h, comet assays indicated reduced DNA damage, and Vigna radiata exhibited normal germination and growth. These findings confirm the synergistic action of enzymatic degradation and biosorption by immobilized WRFC and highlight chitosan beads as a robust carrier matrix. This eco-friendly strategy effectively reduces dye toxicity, offering a promising approach for sustainable industrial wastewater management.

records.title: Rifampicin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis implant-associated infections: the therapeutic potential of ceftaroline and daptomycin combinations.
records.abstract: Rifampicin-resistant (RIF-R) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis (MRSE) pose a significant challenge in managing implant-associated infections (IAIs). However, the functional consequences of rpoB mutations leading to RIF resistance remain poorly characterized, particularly their impact on bacterial fitness and treatment response. We analyzed clinical RIF-R and RIF-susceptible (RIF-S) MRSE isolates from a single-center IAI cohort. RIF-R strains showed delayed exponential growth and exhibited a reduced growth rate during the exponential phase, while biofilm formation remained largely unchanged. To investigate resistance-associated phenotypes, we induced RIF resistance in three clinical RIF-S strains using subinhibitory exposure in a murine tissue cage model. Sequencing revealed rpoB mutations in cluster I, frequently at codons 481 and 486. One mutant, R611 (Ser486Tyr), mirrored mutations from a clinical isolate and exhibited slower growth, reduced cell density, and markedly increased biofilm production with unchanged susceptibilities to vancomycin or daptomycin compared to its RIF-S parent, S611. In vivo, R611 was more competitive in the planktonic phase, while S611 dominated the adherent fraction. Time-kill assays demonstrated strong bactericidal activity of daptomycin combined with ceftaroline or fosfomycin. In the murine model, ceftaroline monotherapy was partially effective, whereas daptomycin/ceftaroline achieved the highest cure rates even against clinical RIF-R strains at the minimum infective dose, with efficacy decreasing markedly at higher bacterial inocula. These findings reveal fitness trade-offs linked to rpoB-mediated resistance and support ceftaroline-based combinations as a potential treatment strategy for RIF-R MRSE in IAIs, particularly when bacterial burden can be reduced.

records.title: Novel approaches to target prostate cancer stem cells driving therapy resistance and cancer progression.
records.abstract: Prostate cancer remains one of the most common malignancies in men, and its global burden continues to rise. Although androgen deprivation therapy and other standard treatments can provide substantial disease control, advanced tumors may progress to castration-resistant prostate cancer, which is associated with poor outcomes. Preclinical and translational evidence implicates prostate cancer stem-like cells (PCSCs) in treatment persistence, progression, and relapse, without establishing them as the sole cause of resistance in patients. PCSC-associated states share functional traits with normal stem cells, including self-renewal and survival under stress; reduced androgen receptor activity occurs in some, but not all, stem-like populations. Their behavior is influenced by the genomic context, including PTEN loss, TP53/RB1 alterations, SPOP mutations, and TMPRSS2-ERG rearrangements, as well as hypoxia, stromal interactions, and inflammatory signaling. These alterations are not specific markers of PCSC identity. Multiple interconnected pathways, notably PI3K/AKT/mTOR, RAS/MAPK, Hedgehog, Wnt/β-catenin, Hippo, JAK/STAT, Notch, EGFR, and hypoxia-driven HIF signaling, provide candidate therapeutic targets. Additional strategies include modifying the microenvironment to suppress epithelial-to-mesenchymal plasticity, restoring tumor-suppressive microRNAs, and developing checkpoint inhibitors, vaccines, and CAR-T cells against relevant tumor-associated antigens. Most PCSC-specific evidence remains experimental, even when a pathway-directed agent has clinical activity or regulatory approval in a molecularly selected prostate cancer population. Clinical tumor responses do not by themselves demonstrate selective PCSC depletion. This narrative review distinguishes mechanistic findings from clinical outcomes and considers limitations involving marker specificity, model selection, drug delivery, toxicity, and therapeutic escape. Functionally validated biomarkers and appropriately designed combination trials are needed to determine whether targeting PCSC-associated states can improve durable disease control.

records.title: Severity-stratified, longitudinal cis-eQTL mapping enables high-sensitivity detection of candidate causal genes for critical COVID-19
records.abstract: Host genetic variation influences heterogeneity in infectious disease severity. Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified 69 lead single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) associated with critical COVID-19, but most lack known regulatory mechanisms. To date, the genetic cis-regulatory effects of critical COVID-19 GWAS lead SNPs have not been systematically characterized across acute illness and convalescent phases in a COVID-19 specific cohort. Here, performing severity-stratified, longitudinal cis-expression quantitative trait loci (cis-eQTL) mapping and colocalization with critical COVID-19 GWAS signals, we find that host cis-regulatory effects vary across clinical severity and disease phase. We analyzed peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 1,031 patients in the Immunophenotyping Assessment in a COVID-19 Cohort (IMPACC), a prospective multicenter study of adults hospitalized with COVID-19, profiled across 10 timepoints spanning acute illness and convalescence. We identified 23 GWAS lead SNPs that colocalized with cis-eQTLs at 26 candidate causal genes, with 16 detectable only when severity stratification and longitudinal sampling were incorporated. A colocalized, protective allele (chr19:4,717,660) at the TMIGD2 locus upregulated TMIGD2 expression exclusively during the acute phase in the prolonged-critical/fatal cohort, with no detectable effect in the rapid-recovery cohort. Our results show that host genetic effects on critical COVID-19 can be context-dependent, with cis-regulatory effects varying across clinical severity and disease phase. Severity-stratified, longitudinal cis-eQTL designs have greater sensitivity to identify candidate causal genes for critical COVID-19 GWAS associations than single-timepoint cross-sectional studies.

records.title: Host response and cell fates of human U937 monocytes upon infection with vancomycin-resistant  E. faecium
records.abstract: In recent years,  Enterococcus faecium has become a high-priority human opportunistic pathogen, especially due to its antibiotic and environmental resistance, promoting hospital-acquired infections. However, its interaction with host cells remains poorly understood.  In this study, we investigated the interaction of four recently collected, clinical vancomycin-resistant  Enterococcus faecium (  VREfm ) isolates with the human U937 cell line. Early after infection, we observed close bacterial association with U937 monocytes and features suggestive of internalization. We thus investigated host cell fates after washing at 2 hours post infection (hpi) to concentrate on effects induced by internalized bacteria or those with direct host cell contact.  Whereas viability was not impaired at 6 hpi, moderate cell death was induced to an isolate-specific extent at 24 hpi, which was abrogated when direct host-pathogen contact as prevented via boyden chamber cell culture inserts, but was enhanced by TNF-R1 deficiency. Host mRNA sequencing revealed a consistent pattern of differentially expressed genes across all  VREfm isolates, suggesting a shared innate immune and stress-related response at 6 hpi, with functionally enriched biological processes related to leukocyte activation, cytokine signaling, programmed cell death, and RNA stability.  Together, these data show that  VREfm triggers an early pro-inflammatory transcriptional response in U937 monocytes without immediate cytotoxicity in U937 monocytes, while late-stage isolate-specific cell death induction depends on direct host cell contact or internalization and involves TNF-R1 mediated regulation. Our findings may assist future efforts to understand how  VREfm triggers host cell damage that contributes to severe inflammation and systemic infection such as persistent bacteremia.  One-Sentence Summary  Vancomycin-resistant  Enterococcus faecium closely associates with U937 monocyte membranes and displays features suggestive of internalization, triggering early proinflammatory transcriptional responses and later, isolate-specific cytotoxicity that requires direct host-pathogen contact and is modulated by TNF-R1.
