records.title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing-Integrated Fibroblast Markers and Candidate Drug-Target Associations in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
records.abstract: BackgroundPancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has dismal outcomes and is shaped by a fibroblast-rich tumor microenvironment (TME). A cell type-resolved, module-level understanding of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and their therapeutic relevance remains incompletely characterized.MethodsWe integrated single-cell RNA-seq data from six treatment-naïve PDAC resection specimens in GSE212966; individual tumor-stage information was not available in the public metadata. Standardized preprocessing, clustering, and major-cell-type annotation were performed. Contact-mediated intercellular signaling toward fibroblasts was profiled. High-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA) was applied to fibroblasts to identify co-expression modules and hub genes. Associations with overall survival were assessed by univariate Cox models and Kaplan-Meier analysis; immune infiltration was evaluated with CIBERSORT and ESTIMATE; pathway associations were examined by gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA). Candidate compounds were screened via Enrichr/DSigDB and docked to target proteins using a PyMOL-Chem3D-AutoDockTools workflow. SEMA3C was further examined in PDAC cell lines by siRNA-mediated knockdown followed by qRT-PCR, CCK-8, wound-healing, and Transwell invasion assays.ResultsWe resolved 10 cell subpopulations and observed broad contact signals to fibroblasts, including the CD99-CD99 axis. hdWGCNA delineated fibroblast modules, from which four key modules were prioritized. Five genes-SEMA3C, PMP22, CPE, SNX9, and UACA-were significantly associated with overall survival. These biomarkers showed both positive and negative associations with specific immune-cell fractions but were positively correlated with the StromalScore, ImmuneScore, and ESTIMATEScore. High-expression groups were enriched for cancer-relevant programs such as epithelial-mesenchymal transition, inflammatory response, and TNFα-NF-κB signaling, whereas several proliferative and metabolic pathways were enriched in the CPE-low group. In vitro, siRNA-mediated SEMA3C knockdown in PANC-1 and Capan-2 cells reduced cell viability, wound closure, and invasion, supporting a cell-intrinsic protumorigenic role of SEMA3C in PDAC cells. Coumestrol emerged as a computationally prioritized compound, and molecular docking predicted a potentially favorable interaction with SNX9 (predicted binding energy -7.5 kcal/mol); this association requires experimental validation.ConclusionAn integrative single-cell and network framework identified fibroblast-related co-expression modules and five survival-associated genes in PDAC. The prognostic relevance of these genes and the predicted coumestrol-SNX9 association require further independent and experimental validation.
records.authors: Ji T, Wu H, Zheng Z, Ma K.

records.title: Enhanced efficacy of gene therapy using a ubiquitous promoter to treat growth hormone-resistant Laron dwarfism in a mouse model.
records.abstract: Laron syndrome is a rare disorder caused by a loss-of-function mutation in the growth hormone receptor (GHR), resulting in severe postnatal growth failure that is partially corrected by systemic recombinant human IGF-1 therapy. In our previous study, liver-specific mouse GHR expression using an adeno-associated virus serotype 8 (AAV8) significantly but partially restored growth in a GHR-deficient mouse model, and was of similar order to treatment with recombinant IGF-1. Here, we investigated if increasing the vector dose and expanding transgene expression beyond the liver would enhance therapeutic efficacy. Laron dwarf mice were treated with a four-fold higher dose of AAV8 expressing mouse GHR with either a liver-specific promoter (AAV8-HLP-mGHR) or a ubiquitous promoter (AAV8-CAG-mGHR). While both strategies increased hepatic Igf1 transcriptions and increased serum IGF1 with decreased serum growth hormone, ubiquitous GHR expression resulted in nearly 25 to 30% greater improvement in body size and more than an 8% greater improvement in skeletal growth in treated female mice. These findings establish ubiquitous GHR expression as a more effective strategy and support the future development of systemic GHR restoration approaches for the treatment of Laron syndrome.
records.journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy
records.authors: Sia KC, Gan SU, Fu ZY, Kopchick JJ, Waters MJ, Lee KO.

records.title: High-throughput single-transcription factor-mediated direct cell-fate engineering.
records.abstract: Engineering cell identity has transitioned from descriptive developmental biology into a predictable, quantitative discipline. Central to this transition is the discovery that single transcription factors (TFs) can act as master regulators, capable of bypassing hierarchical developmental constraints to directly reprogram cell fate. Although early studies relied on candidate-based approaches, recent technological advances in high-throughput methods and single-cell multi-omics have revolutionized the field. In this Review, we focus on the emergence of large-scale single-TF overexpression screens as a discovery engine for lineage regulators. We discuss how systematic overexpression screens, particularly in pluripotent stem cell systems, have enabled the identification of single TFs with cell-fate reprogramming potential. We examine the shift from bulk transcriptomics to single-cell trajectory inference, which reveals the inherent heterogeneity, rapid kinetics, and stochastic nature of fate reprogramming. Furthermore, we interrogate the mechanistic features that need to be considered during fate transitions, such as pioneer factor activity, chromatin competence, and dosage-dependent lineage bifurcations. By integrating large-scale TF overexpression data with multi-omic readouts, we discuss principles for cell-fate engineering and define successful conversion through transcriptional stability, epigenetic memory, and functional maturity. This systematic perspective provides a roadmap for the precise generation of therapeutic cell types in regenerative medicine.
records.authors: Jang Y, Lee M, Kim J.

records.title: Triptonide alleviates sepsis-associated acute lung injury by suppressing the STAT3/HIF-1α-mediated aerobic glycolysis in macrophages.
records.abstract: Background and purposeSepsis-associated acute lung injury (SA-ALI), represents a major contributor to mortality among septic patients during the early hyperinflammatory phase. Triptonide, a diterpenoids extract from Tripterygium wilfordii Hook f has anticancer and contraceptive effects. However, its potential and mechanism in SA-ALI are largely unknown. This study aims to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy and elucidate underlying mechanisms of triptonide in SA-ALI to identify new clinical strategies.Experimental approachLipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced endotoxemia model or caecal ligation and puncture (CLP) model was used to induce SA-ALI in mice, accompanied by treatment with triptonide, triptolide and 2-methoxyestradiol. Parallel in vitro experiments involved LPS-treated mouse primary macrophages cultured with or without triptonide. Transcriptomic sequencing of macrophages was performed to explore the anti-inflammatory mechanisms of triptonide, which were further substantiated using specific activators, inhibitors and adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated gene targeting.Key resultsOur data shows that triptonide effectively inhibits macrophage pro-inflammatory activation, reduces pulmonary inflammation and alleviates SA-ALI pathology (i.e. inflammatory cell infiltration, oedema and cell apoptosis), thereby improving the survival of septic mice. Transcriptomic sequencing combined with metabolic analysis shows that triptonide suppresses aerobic glycolysis in pro-inflammatory macrophages by inhibiting the Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription 3 (STAT3)/Hypoxia inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) axis. Notably, the therapeutic efficacy of triptonide against SA-ALI was abolished in myeloid cell-specific HIF-1α overexpressed mice (LyzM-CreDIO-hif1a mice).Conclusions and implicationsTriptonide protects against SA-ALI by suppressing the STAT3/HIF-1α signalling axis, thereby inhibiting aerobic glycolysis-mediated pro-inflammatory macrophage activation, which suggests that triptonide is a promising therapeutic strategy for SA-ALI.
records.authors: Zhu J, Ou Z, Ma H, Huang Q, Pan L, Xie H, Pan G, Jin S.

records.title: PhYAB4 directly activates PhAGL6-2 to regulate lip-related organ curvature morphology in Paphiopedilum henryanum.
records.abstract: The orchid lip is a highly specialized floral organ that contributes to floral architecture and pollinator interaction. However, the developmental and molecular mechanisms underlying lip-related organ curvature in Paphiopedilum remain poorly understood. Using Paphiopedilum henryanum and its Type A peloric mutant, we found that visible divergence between wild-type petals and mutant lip-like petals begins at Stage 4. Curvature was associated with adaxial-abaxial epidermal cell number imbalance in the distal region, whereas average epidermal cell area remained largely unchanged. Transcriptome and expression analyses identified PhAGL6-2 as a lip-associated AGL6 homolog enriched in lips and lip-like petals during Stages 4-5. PhAGL6-2 was preferentially expressed on the abaxial side, particularly in regions associated with curvature. Virus-induced gene silencing-mediated silencing of PhAGL6-2 in Dendrobium Chao Praya Smile and P. henryanum affected perianth organ curvature, suggesting a broader role in floral organ morphogenesis. The YABBY transcription factor PhYAB4 directly bound the AGTGTG motif in the PhAGL6-2 promoter and activated its transcription. Silencing PhYAB4 reduced PhAGL6-2 expression and caused stronger floral curvature, lip outgrowths, and partial disruption of floral symmetry. These findings identify a PhYAB4-PhAGL6-2 pathway associated with epidermal cell number imbalance and lip-related organ curvature.
records.authors: Yin Y, Li Y, Zeng J, Li L, Wu K, Deng X, Zhuang H, Feng C, Kang M, Zeng S, Fang L.

records.title: In Vivo CRISPR Base Editing of ANGPTL3 for Durable Lipid Lowering.
records.abstract: Circulating concentrations of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and triglyceride-rich lipoproteins are leading risk factors for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease1. Despite several approved lipid-lowering medications, most patients fail to achieve target lipid levels under the chronic care treatment model2,3. Here, we describe a potential single-course treatment in which an infusion of guide RNA and mRNA encoding a CRISPR adenine base editor-encapsulated within a GalNAc-lipid nanoparticle-leads to durable, liver-selective inactivation of angiopoietin-like 3 (ANGPTL3), a known driver of increased LDL-C and triglyceride concentrations. Analyses in human liver cells in vitro confirmed that the base editor introduces a DNA base-pair change at the target ANGPTL3 locus with no detectable off-target editing at any of approximately 3000 candidate sites or treatment-related structural variants. Targeted ANGPTL3 inactivation in nonhuman primates was well-tolerated and led to a > 90% mean reduction in circulating ANGPTL3 protein, with durability confirmed out to 3 years following a single dose. In mouse and nonhuman primate models of hyperlipidemia, gene inactivation was associated with reductions of approximately 40 to 50% in LDL-C and 50 to 70% in triglycerides. These results provided the scientific foundation for initiation of an ongoing first-in-human clinical trial in patients with refractory hyperlipidemia syndromes.

records.title: Berberine attenuates cigarette smoke extract-induced stress and senescence-associated changes in human brain microvascular endothelial cells.
records.abstract: ObjectiveThe aim of this study is to investigate the protective effects of berberine (BBR) against cigarette smoke extract (CSE)-induced injury in human brain microvascular endothelial cells and to identify candidate molecules and associated candidate molecules.MethodshCMEC/D3 cells were exposed to 4% CSE and/or 7.5 μM BBR for 24 h. Inflammation, oxidative stress, and senescence-associated phenotypes were assessed. Previously generated CSE-responsive transcriptomic data were integrated with ChEMBL-derived candidates, followed by enrichment, weighted prioritization, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, and docking.ResultsCompared with CSE alone, BBR co-treatment increased cell viability (P ConclusionBBR attenuates CSE-induced oxidative stress, inflammation, and senescence-associated alterations in hCMEC/D3 cells. These effects may be associated with modulation of interconnected cellular stress responses.

records.title: Inhibitory action of Origanum onites essential oil on scorpion venom induced smooth muscle contractions.
records.abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevanceAndroctonus crassicauda and Mesobuthus gibbosus are scorpions with powerful toxins with causes of envenomations leading to death but they are also potential candidates for drug development. Pharmacological investigations on venoms of Androctonus crassicauda (Acr) and Mesobuthus gibbosus (Mgb) are few. Ethnopharmacological use of Origanum species against envenomations was noted by Dioscorides.Aim of the studyAim of the study was to investigate actions of Acr and Mgb on prostatic and epididymal segments of isolated rat vas deferens and to investigate effects of Origanum onites essential oil (OOeo) against actions of these venoms.Materials and methodsAcr and Mgb were tested on phenylephrine- CaCl2- and KCl-induced contractions of prostatic and epididymal segments of isolated rat vas deferens. Effects of OOeo on actions of venoms were tested. Regular expressions were used for short linear motifs and Clustal omega for multiple sequence alignment of toxins and TRPA1.ResultsBoth venoms inhibited phenylephrine-induced contractions but augmented KCl-induced contractions. CaCl2-induced contractions were not affected. Parallel shift of dose-response curve of Mgb was found. Molecular mimicry using GxxxG (GG4) motif that has the structure [GS]xx[FY]GYC was found indicating role of TRPA1 ion channels. This motif was evolutionary conserved from Cnidaria to mammals. Dose-dependent inhibitory actions of OOeo against Acr-induced contractions of epididymal vas deferens indicated possible roles of TRPA1 and voltage-dependent Na+-channels.ConclusionContractile actions of the venoms on vas deferens and dose dependent inhibitory actions of OOeo against these venoms supply pharmacological evidence for the ethnopharmacological use of OOeo.

records.title: Integrative Multi-Omics Reveals Differential Mechanisms of Four TCM Formulations in Treating Insomnia via Syndrome-Compound-Metabolite Association Networks.
records.abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevanceGuipi Pills (GPW), Wuling Capsule (WLC), Bailemian Capsule (BLMC), and Zaoren Anshen Capsule (ZRASC) are representative traditional Chinese medicine formulations for treating insomnia based on different syndromes of Heart-Spleen Deficiency, Heart-Kidney Disharmony, Liver Qi Stagnation with Yin Deficiency, and Heart Blood Deficiency, respectively. However, their molecular mechanisms remain unclear.Aim of the studyTo elucidate the "same disease, different treatment" mechanisms of these four formulations against sleep deprivation-induced insomnia through an integrated multi-omics and network pharmacology strategy.Materials and methodsChemical constituents were characterized by UHPLC-Orbitrap-MS/MS. A meta-analysis evaluated clinical differences and syndrome consistency. Subsequently, A mouse model of sleep deprivation was established; behavioral tests and HE/Nissl staining were performed. On this basis, fecal 16S rRNA gene sequencing, serum metabolomics, and hypothalamic transcriptomics were integrated to construct a microbiota-metabolite network. Furthermore, network pharmacology and molecular docking predicted component-target interactions. Finally, key protein expression was validated by western blot.ResultsUHPLC-Orbitrap-MS/MS identified 87, 56, 163, and 128 compounds from GPW, WLC, BLMC, and ZRASC, respectively. Meta-analysis (62 RCTs, 6,045 patients) showed WLC and BLMC reduced PSQI scores alone or in combination; ZRASC benefited only in combination, and GPW combination benefit was borderline. Syndrome-efficacy interactions were inconsistent. In mice, all formulations alleviated neuronal damage despite heterogeneous behavioral improvements. All four formulations suppressed Alistipes and commonly reversed 39 serum metabolites enriched in glutathione metabolism and pentose phosphate pathway. Each formulation showed syndrome-related metabolic regulation. Hypothalamic transcriptomics revealed commonly downregulated genes (S100a9, Gbp5, Fpr1, Tnfsf8) and distinct patterns: lipid metabolism-immune suppression (GPW), transcriptional-metabolic inhibition (WLC), prolactin signaling (BLMC), and PPAR-driven energy repair (ZRASC). In an exploratory analysis, the number of microbiota-metabolite association pairs increased from WLC (158) to GPW (393), BLMC (836), and ZRASC (1,243); this gradient is hypothesis-generating and warrants independent validation.Network pharmacology and molecular docking predicted potential formulation-specific and common inflammatory pathway targets. Finally, western blot showed all formulations downregulated iNOS and COX2; all except WLC upregulated SLC7A11, GPX4, FTH, and Bcl2 (P ConclusionIn this study, these four formulations showed heterogeneous, syndrome-associated patterns across microbiota remodeling, metabolic reprogramming, anti-inflammation, and anti-ferroptosis, which may help generate hypotheses regarding the "same disease, different treatment" principle. The findings provide a mechanistic basis for clinical application and a methodological reference for TCM modernization.

records.title: Patient-anchored pharmacological modeling prioritizes combined miR-4651/miR-6126 for experimental validation in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.
records.abstract: Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome (HGPS) is characterized by accelerated vascular aging, but therapeutic development is constrained by sparse longitudinal clinical data and the limited number of independent biological models. We developed a patient-anchored framework integrating longitudinal cardiovascular phenotyping, endothelial transcriptomics, LMNA cryptic splicing, biological-line-preserving virtual populations, treatment counterfactuals and lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery optimization. The index patient showed progressive carotid disease and worsening diastolic indices despite preserved systolic function. In HGPS endothelial cells, disease-associated transcriptional structure persisted after adjustment for cell-cycle and flow-related effects across 20,404 non-cell-cycle genes (Spearman ρ = 0.706), with inflammatory activation remaining directionally positive in all five leave-one-line-out refits. Hierarchical modeling generated 2,000 virtual profiles per condition for uncertainty propagation without increasing biological sample size or statistical power. Under the prespecified treatment operators, patient-informed counterfactual simulations ranked combined miR-4651/miR-6126 above either single agent across 6-, 12- and 24-month horizons; however, a separate uncalibrated structural sensitivity model showed that dual-treatment superiority was not robust to matched total miRNA cargo and hypothetical competitive or antagonistic interactions. A four-dimensional computational LNP optimization screen evaluated 18,072 regimens, retained 2,567 Pareto-nondominated solutions and narrowed these to 30 model-prioritized delivery configurations for experimental evaluation. Together, these analyses connect observed HGPS vascular pathology with biologically constrained therapeutic prioritization, identify combined miR-4651/miR-6126 as a model-prioritized candidate requiring matched-dose experimental validation, rather than an intervention with established superiority, and define a model-prioritized LNP delivery space for HGPS vascular disease.

records.title: Dupilumab modulates type II IL-4/IL-13 receptor-expressing immune cells in eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis.
records.abstract: BackgroundEosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis (eCRS) is a refractory type 2 inflammatory disease characterized by nasal polyp formation and eosinophilic infiltration. Although dupilumab, an IL-4Rα-blocking antibody, demonstrates clinical efficacy, its cellular mechanisms within nasal polyps remain unclear.ObjectiveTo define the cell type-specific effects of dupilumab in eCRS, we examined IL-4/IL-13 receptor-dependent transcriptional responses in tissue-resident immune cells.MethodsNasal polyp and peripheral blood samples were collected from five patients with eCRS before and after dupilumab treatment. Single-cell RNA sequencing on four paired cases, spatial transcriptomics, and immunostaining were performed. In vitro stimulation of human conventional dendritic cells (cDCs) validated IL-4/IL-13-regulated pathways.ResultsDupilumab improved symptoms and attenuated eosinophilic inflammation. Across annotated populations, the number of differentially expressed genes correlated positively with pre-treatment IL13RA1 expression. Accordingly, myeloid cells, particularly cDCs, which predominantly express type II IL-4/IL-13 receptors, showed the broadest transcriptional changes, including downregulation of ALOX15; ALOX15 inhibition abrogated IL-4/IL-13-induced CCL13 and CCL22 expression in cDCs. After treatment, pathogenic Th2 cell subset expressed lower IL1RL1 and AREG. IGHE and IL4R expression in CD23-positive B cells declined, as did PRDM1 and ELL2 in plasma cells. In one paired case, spatial analysis identified fewer TLS-like aggregates and lower detection of ALOX15 and IGHE transcripts after treatment.ConclusionDupilumab preferentially remodels type II IL-4/IL-13 receptor-expressing immune cells, particularly polyp cDCs, while selectively reprogramming Th2, B, and plasma cells. Identification of ALOX15 as a candidate mediator in cDCs provides mechanistic insight that may inform optimization of type 2-targeted therapy in eCRS.

records.title: NFYA-transcriptionally activated MTHFD2 promotes cervical cancer progression by inducing mitochondrial dysfunction via AMT.
records.abstract: Cervical cancer is the fourth most common cancer among women worldwide, and advanced disease remains difficult to treat due to recurrence, metastasis, and drug resistance. Abnormal mitochondrial metabolism, particularly one-carbon folate metabolism, plays a key role in cancer progression. This study investigated the role of MTHFD2, a key enzyme in one-carbon metabolism, in cervical cancer. By integrating transcriptomic data from public databases (GSE9750, GSE63514, TCGA-CESC), we identified 168 persistently upregulated genes mainly enriched in folate one-carbon metabolism pathways. Correlation analysis with a mitochondrial gene database identified four candidate genes, among which MTHFD2 showed the most pronounced upregulation in the three datasets and 20 paired clinical cervical cancer tissues, and was therefore selected for functional studies. Functional experiments in HeLa cells showed that MTHFD2 silencing significantly inhibited proliferation and invasion, promoted apoptosis, and impaired mitochondrial function, including increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels and reduced basal mitochondrial respiration and ATP production. Mechanistically, NFYA transcriptionally activated MTHFD2, and MTHFD2 interacted with AMT, upregulating AMT expression and activating the glycine cleavage system (GCS), thereby enhancing mitochondrial metabolism. Consistently, silencing either NFYA or AMT suppressed malignant phenotypes of cancer cells. In vivo, downregulation of NFYA, MTHFD2, or AMT inhibited the growth and mitochondrial metabolism of cervical cancer xenografts. In summary, this study identifies MTHFD2 as a potential therapeutic target for metabolic intervention in cervical cancer and provides new insights into its role in tumor biology.
records.authors: He Y, Xie T, Zhou F, Gong Y, Tai Y, Zhang W.

records.title: From prediction to creation: How AI-driven design is reshaping microbial biocatalysis.
records.abstract: Enzyme engineering has long relied on rational design and directed evolution, yet both remain bounded by natural enzyme space - a constraint felt acutely across the largely uncharacterised microbial world. The 2021 advent of accurate structure prediction marked an inflection point, catalysing AI methods that now extend far beyond folding. These tools are organism-agnostic; the microbial domain is their proving ground because it supplies both the uncharacterised sequence space and the expression hosts. Here we examine three stages: mining microbial sequence space; generative design, whether conditioned on structure or sequence; and machine learning-guided directed evolution. We trace the trajectory from reading the protein universe toward writing it, asking where each has delivered for microbial biocatalysis. Because published claims are hard to compare, we propose a tiered framework - catalysis, selectivity, producibility, process fit - for judging whether an AI-designed enzyme is a useful biocatalyst rather than merely a functional protein.
records.authors: Guirimand G, Mall R, Patel C, Kudo H, Matsuda M, Courdavault V, Hasunuma T.

records.title: HAUS5 defines a mitogen-activated protein kinase/extracellular signal-regulated kinase-dependent epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity program and therapeutic vulnerability to Belinostat in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
records.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by high aggressiveness and limited therapeutic options. However, the molecular determinants driving ccRCC progression and therapeutic vulnerability remain incompletely defined. Through integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses, we identified HAUS5 as a tumor-enriched factor that was highly expressed in ccRCC tissues and tumor-derived epithelial cells. Elevated HAUS5 expression was associated with adverse clinicopathological features and poor overall survival. Functional assays showed that HAUS5 depletion suppressed ccRCC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and xenograft tumor growth. Mechanistically, HAUS5 was associated with MAPK/ERK signaling activation and epithelial-mesenchymal transition, whereas EGF partially rescued the inhibitory effects induced by HAUS5 knockdown. In addition, drug sensitivity analysis identified Belinostat as a candidate compound associated with HAUS5 expression, and functional experiments showed that Belinostat attenuated HAUS5-associated malignant phenotypes. Collectively, these findings suggest that HAUS5 contributes to ccRCC progression through a MAPK/ERK-associated EMT program and may be linked to differential sensitivity to Belinostat.
records.authors: Chi Y, Li Y, Yang B, Ding G, Tang C, Sun F, Li Q, Zhang R, Ma J, Zhang H, Wu J, Li Y.

records.title: Spatial control of enzyme orientation at the lipid droplet interface enables regio- and chemoselective metabolic flux.
records.abstract: Precise spatial control over multienzyme cascade reactions is increasingly recognized as a design lever in synthetic biology for enhancing catalytic performance and directing metabolic flux. By emulating principles of cellular compartmentalization, synthetic scaffolds and engineered interfaces have emerged as powerful platforms to modulate intermediate channeling and reaction efficiency in complex biocatalytic systems. However, robust and spatially defined immobilization of multienzyme assemblies within physicochemically optimal compartments remains challenging because of the dynamic intracellular environment. Here, we reprogram the amphiphilic interface of yeast lipid droplets (LDs) as a programmable scaffold system to support regio- and chemoselective localization of enzymes. Guided by molecular dynamics simulations, we designed LD-anchoring motifs to direct the enzyme orientation at the LD monolayer interface, yielding cytosol-facing or LD inner-facing configurations. Using this designed LD-anchoring motif, we spatially reorganize a trienzyme cascade for prodeoxyviolacein (PDV) biosynthesis across the cytosol-LD interface, facilitating directional conversion of hydrophilic substrates into hydrophobic products. This spatial reorganization substantially improved PDV production by 1300%, achieving 46.25 milligrams per liter. Our approach offers a modular and tunable platform for engineering spatially organized and readily deployable enzyme cascades, opening avenues for biosynthetic catalysis at organellar interfaces.
records.authors: Son SH, Bae S, Moon SY, Kim M, Oh SS, Son CY, Lee JY.

records.title: Uncovering the immune microenvironmental atlas of breast cancer molecular subtypes based on single-cell transcriptomics.
records.abstract: Breast cancer progression is closely linked to immune cells within the tumor microenvironment (TME), but the immune landscape differences across HER2-positive (HER2+), triple-negative (TNBC), and ER-positive (ER+) subtypes have yet to be systematically characterized. In this study, we characterized immune landscape differences across HER2-positive (HER2+), triple-negative (TNBC), and ER-positive (ER+) breast cancers using single-cell RNA sequencing data, focusing on T cells, macrophages, and B cells. Our analysis revealed that cytotoxic CD8 + T cells were more abundant in TNBC but showed signs of dysfunction. Macrophage subsets, including an NDUFB8 + population, exhibited divergent functional orientations across subtypes. B cells in TNBC exhibited functional alterations, characterized by a decreased proportion of plasmablasts and an increased proportion of memory B cells. Single-cell regulatory network inference and clustering (SCENIC) analysis predicted a set of subtype-specific candidate transcription factors (TFs), including E2F8 across all subtypes and ATF7 in HER2 + tumors, whose activity correlated with clinical outcomes. Finally, mapping multicellular communication networks revealed both conserved and subtype-specific signaling pathways. Together, these results present a detailed transcriptional landscape of immune heterogeneity in breast cancer and contribute novel insights that may inform the design of subtype-specific immunotherapies.
records.authors: Lin S, Zheng Y, Chen Z, Patrice MD, Wang L, Li X, Zhang Y, Zhang X.

records.title: Innate immune mechanisms of HIV control and reservoir regulation in elite and posttreatment controllers.
records.abstract: Purpose of reviewElite controllers (ECs) and posttreatment controllers (PTCs) provide complementary models of HIV remission, demonstrating that sustained viral control can occur in the absence of continuous antiretroviral therapy. Increasing evidence suggests that innate immune mechanisms may contribute to both viral suppression and reservoir regulation.Recent findingsRecent studies have identified adaptive-like natural killer (NK) cell programmes, trained innate immune responses, enhanced dendritic-cell sensing pathways and distinct myeloid cell phenotypes associated with controller status. ECs and PTCs also exhibit favourable reservoir characteristics, including reduced frequencies of intact proviruses, restricted transcriptional activity and deep proviral latency. Emerging evidence suggests a relationship between innate immune programmes and reservoir regulation; however, direct mechanistic links remain incompletely understood.SummaryControllers represent a heterogeneous spectrum of remission phenotypes characterised by distinct innate immune signatures and reservoir landscapes. While innate immunity is increasingly associated with favourable reservoir characteristics, whether these programmes actively shape reservoir restriction or arise as a consequence of reduced viral persistence remains unresolved. Addressing this question may provide important insights for durable HIV remission and future cure strategies.
records.journal: Current opinion in HIV and AIDS
records.authors: Mohamed A, Zungu Y, Thobakgale CF.

records.title: Gene cloning and characterization of porcine AANAT, preparation of polyclonal antibody, and its expression and distribution in pigs.
records.abstract: BackgroundArylalkylamine N-acetyltransferase (AANAT) is a member of the GCN5-related N-acetyltransferase (GNAT) superfamily and catalyzes the acetylation of arylalkylamine substrates to regulate melatonin synthesis. However, the characterization and antibody preparation of the porcine AANAT have not been reported.Methods and resultsThis study, we cloned the porcine AANAT gene, performed sequence analysis, constructed a prokaryotic expression vector, expressed the recombinant protein, generated a polyclonal antibody, and examined AANAT expression and distribution in pigs. The results showed that the cloned porcine AANAT gene was 880 bp in length, containing an 819 bp CDS that encoded 272 amino acids. In terms of homology and genetic evolution, porcine AANAT is most closely related to warthog, with nucleotide and amino acid homology of 96.21% and 90.81%, respectively. Porcine AANAT belongs to an intracellular hydrophilic protein without signal peptide and transmembrane structure, and contains multiple antigenic sites. Its secondary structure is similar to its tertiary structure, enabling it to interact with key enzymes involved in melatonin synthesis. We constructed the pET32a(+)-pAANAT recombinant plasmid, and expressed the His-tag-pAANAT fusion protein under the condition of 0.5 mmol/L IPTG induction at 25℃ for 12 h. Using this purified protein, we successfully prepared high-titer (> 1:819,200) porcine AANAT polyclonal antibodies that can detect the porcine AANAT protein. Additionally, tissue expression analysis showed that AANAT mRNA/protein was mainly expressed in the pineal gland and pituitary, with the highest protein expression level detected in the pineal gland; immunohistochemistry further showed that AANAT-positive signals were predominantly localized in the cytoplasm of pinealocytes.ConclusionsThese findings provide a foundation for further investigation of the function of porcine AANAT and its role in regulating melatonin synthesis.
records.authors: Ma Z, Wang D, Li H, Chen G, Wang Y, Li J, Chen F.

records.title: Molecular mechanisms of diethyl phthalate enhanced invasion in gastric cancer revealed by integrative network toxicology machine learning and in vitro analyses.
records.abstract: Diethyl phthalate (DEP) is a ubiquitous environmental endocrine-disrupting chemical to which human populations are widely exposed. Increasing evidence links DEP to the malignant progression of solid tumors; however, the key molecular networks and experimentally validated mechanisms underlying DEP-enhanced invasion in gastric cancer (GC) remain largely undefined. Four transcriptomic datasets from the Gene Expression Omnibus were integrated to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs), followed by weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) to determine tumor-associated key modules. Potential DEP targets were predicted using multiple databases and intersected with-related DEGs and key module genes to define core candidate genes. Functional enrichment and network analyses were then performed. Subsequently, a multi-model ensemble machine learning framework combined with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based interpretability was applied to prioritize candidate genes. Molecular docking was used to evaluate the potential binding affinity between DEP and key target proteins. Finally, the effects of DEP on oxidative stress, migration and invasion, cytoskeletal remodeling, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) were experimentally validated in AGS and HGC-27 cells. Thirteen core candidate genes were identified. Functional enrichment analyses primarily implicated lysosomal proteolysis, extracellular matrix remodeling, and chromatin remodeling and epigenetic regulation. Among the evaluated machine learning models, the gradient boosting machine (GBM) model demonstrated the best overall diagnostic performance. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis of an additional random forest model highlighted CTSB, PLAU, ALDH3A1, ATAD2, and CBX7 as influential features for GC classification. Molecular docking predicted potential interactions between DEP and these candidate proteins. In vitro experiments demonstrated that DEP exposure increased intracellular reactive oxygen species levels and promoted cell proliferation, migration, and invasion in AGS and HGC-27 cells. These effects were accompanied by filamentous actin (F-actin) reorganization, increased RhoA and MLC1 expression, decreased E-cadherin expression, and increased N-cadherin and vimentin expression, consistent with EMT-related alterations. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that DEP exposure enhances invasion-related malignant phenotypes in gastric cancer cells and identify candidate molecular targets potentially associated with GC progression. Although network toxicology, machine learning, and molecular docking provide complementary evidence for target prioritization, further functional studies are required to determine whether these candidate targets directly mediate DEP-induced cellular effects.
records.authors: Guo T, Hou S, Cao J, Duan J, Liu W, Wu T, Hou S.

records.title: Calycosin attenuates a TGF-β-responsive COL3A1-associated fibroblast program in non-small cell lung cancer.
records.abstract: Fibroblast-derived extracellular-matrix programs are prominent in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but bulk transcriptomic signals do not identify the relevant cellular compartment or establish whether candidate stromal programs respond to defined compounds. We integrated cell-resolved multi-omics analyses with fibroblast perturbation experiments to prioritize an Astragalus-associated stromal program and test its response to calycosin. A systematic public-data workflow integrated curated compound-target relationships with transcriptomic, co-expression, proteomic, single-cell, microenvironmental, dependency, protein-interaction, perturbational, and ranking-robustness evidence. Experimental validation used four independent biological repeats in TGF-β1-activated MRC-5 human lung fibroblasts together with a minimal four-donor primary NSCLC CAF validation set, with calycosin, the TGF-β receptor inhibitor SB431542, and COL3A1 loss- and gain-of-function perturbations. A separate concentration-response experiment evaluated calycosin at 5, 10, and 25 µM, with molecular, signaling, viability, and conditioned-medium effects on A549 and NCI-H520 spheroid invasion assessed across the dose range. The formal cross-cohort intersection identified four candidates shared by LUAD and LUSC-MMP1, MMP9, COL3A1, and PPARG. COL3A1 had concordant RNA-protein support, fibroblast-enriched single-cell expression, and recurrent associations with CAF signatures. In the principal TGF-β1-activated MRC-5 experiment, 25 µM calycosin reduced COL3A1 expression from 4.57- to 2.50-fold, collagen III secretion from 3.82 to 2.26 ng/105 cells/16 h, the α-SMA-high fraction from 64.5% to 33.5%, and CAGA activity from 4.14- to 2.38-fold. In a separate four-repeat dose series (0, 5, 10, and 25 µM), the means of eight molecular and functional endpoints declined with dose; paired-repeat linear-dose slopes were negative (two-sided P = 9.83 × 10-6 to 2.71 × 10-4), although not every replicate decreased strictly at 5 µM. In GSE153935, COL3A1 was enriched in fibroblasts (7/7 evaluable matched donors; exact signed-rank P = 0.0156). All four primary CAF donors showed a reduction in COL3A1, ACTA2, and conditioned-medium-driven A549 invasion with calycosin, but none of the three contrasts met the familywise Holm threshold (adjusted P = 0.0679). At the highest dose, MRC-5 live-cell fractions and tumor-spheroid viability were modestly reduced, so a viability-related contribution to invasion outcomes cannot be excluded. COL3A1 knockdown reduced selected activation endpoints and overexpression partly restored A549 invasion under calycosin treatment. Public cohort data, an independent single-cell dataset and perturbation experiments in MRC-5 fibroblasts support a calycosin-responsive, TGF-β-associated fibroblast phenotype marked by COL3A1. Four primary NSCLC CAF cultures showed the same direction of effect, but none of the calycosin comparisons remained significant after multiplicity adjustment, so these data are preliminary. COL3A1 perturbation altered selected fibroblast-conditioned readouts. Direct calycosin-COL3A1 binding, exclusive mediation, and a toxicity-independent anti-invasive effect remain to be tested.

records.title: The mycotoxin zearalenone couples secondary metabolism to  N  -acetylglucosamine catabolism
records.abstract: Fungal secondary metabolites are often viewed as terminal products of specialized metabolism, yet how their production influences the physiology of the producing organism remains poorly understood. Here, we show that zearalenone (ZEA) production is functionally coupled to  N -acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc) catabolism in  Fusarium graminearum . Transcriptome profiling of a  ZEB2 -overexpressing strain revealed enrichment of GlcNAc metabolic functions, and exogenous ZEA induced key catabolic genes independently of Zeb2. Among pathway components,  NAG , encoding GlcNAc-6-phosphate deacetylase, was critical for GlcNAc utilization, and its loss caused severe GlcNAc-dependent growth inhibition. Genetic impairment of  NAG was poorly tolerated under elevated ZEA pathway activity. Conversely,  NAG overexpression increased tolerance to exogenous ZEA and alleviated the growth defect associated with  ZEB2 overexpression. Together, these findings reveal a functional connection between secondary metabolite production and primary nutrient metabolism and suggest that ZEA-associated metabolic remodeling contributes to the fitness of the producing fungus.
records.authors: Lee N, Yang J, Park J, Han JW, Kim H, Son H.

records.title: A mammalian fibroblast zoo reveals barriers to cross-species virus replication and differential regulation of antiviral immunity
records.abstract: Virus zoonosis represents a continual threat to humans. Viruses emerge in humans directly or indirectly through interactions with mammals. However, our understanding of virus-host susceptibility across the diversity of mammals is limited and experimental model systems are restricted to a very small set of model organisms. Mammals are highly diverse and different habitats, lifestyles, diets, and exposures to different pathogens have driven substantial genetic diversity. We generated a library of primary fibroblasts across 86 mammalian species and used these cells to build an atlas of virus-host susceptibility across a panel of arboviruses that infect diverse mammals including humans. Perturbing the innate immune system revealed some virus-host pairs where restriction is controlled by the immune system and others where there is an incompatibility with host factors. Transcriptomic profiling of the library in response to virus sensing mimicked by poly(I:C) or antiviral signaling with type I interferon reveals a core set of conserved genes that respond as well as substantial species- and order-specific responses. Together these data provide a comparative atlas of innate immune responses across mammals and offer a window into how these systems have evolved across animals.

records.title: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Reveals Tumorigenic Lineages and Interactions Persisting and Evolving From Premalignancy to Cancer in the Stomach
records.abstract: Background:  & Aims Gastric cancer is often diagnosed at advanced stages, making the premalignant window critical for early detection. However, the epithelial changes that characterize this stage remain poorly defined. We used CTLA4-knockdown (CTLA4KD) mice, which model human CTLA4 insufficiency-associated gastric cancer, that develops autoimmune gastritis, metaplasia, and adenocarcinoma, to define molecular changes across disease progression. Methods Single-cell RNA sequencing and 40-color spectral flow cytometry were performed on gastric tissue across premalignant and cancer stages. We evaluated epithelial lineage relationships, cell-cell communication pathways, and candidate markers at the transcript and protein levels in murine and human gastric adenocarcinoma. Results We identified a metaplastic/tumorigenic population in CTLA4KD mice that emerged in premalignancy with a chief cell transcriptomic origin. Cell-cell communication analysis revealed a progressive increase in fibronectin (FN1) signaling from premalignancy through cancer, transitioning from stromal to autocrine signaling in the metaplastic/tumorigenic population. Expression of Embigin (EMB), a fibronectin receptor, increased at both transcript and protein levels in premalignancy and remained elevated in cancer. EMB⁺ epithelial cells co-expressed CD133, a cancer stem cell marker, consistent with a stem-like phenotype. EMB expression was also higher in human gastric adenocarcinoma than in matched normal tissue. Conclusions Using a model that captures the full histopathological cascade of gastric tumorigenesis, we delineate single-cell transcriptional programs that persist and evolve from premalignancy to adenocarcinoma. In-depth computational analyses identified novel markers involved in cell-cell communication during tumorigenesis, including EMB, an epithelial marker that persists from premalignancy through cancer in the murine model and validated in human gastric adenocarcinoma, suggesting EMB as a marker of premalignant progression.
records.authors: Vazquez EN, Lozano CC, Sun X, Torres Juvier D, Li CM, El-Rifai W, Zaika A, Ban Y, Guo Y, Cai X, Chen Z.

records.title: Multimodal cellular context enables molecular phenotyping from single-molecule trajectories
records.abstract: Single-molecule tracking (SMT) provides direct measurements of molecular dynamics in living cells, but motion alone rarely specifies the underlying biological process, without accounting for the cellular environment in which that motion occurs. Here, we present MIST (Multimodal Interpretation of Single-molecule Trajectories), a framework that brings the paradigm of image-based profiling to single molecules by integrating trajectory dynamics, emitter properties and cellular context into a common, reusable phenotype space. Using a reference panel of nine proteins in live Escherichia coli, we show that multimodal context more than doubled protein-specific information relative to trajectory features alone, a gap that learned trajectory representations did not close. MIST allowed de novo identification of shared transcription-translation phenotype at the nucleoid periphery. A fixed reference space detected effects of previously uncharacterized MukB ATPase mutations without retraining. MIST provides an interpretable and extensible framework for comparing proteins, mutants and conditions within a common space of molecular phenotypes.
records.authors: Redchuk T, Rehm L, Sui Y, Mäkelä J.

records.title: spearfish: ultrafast Δ-mapping of long reads to redundant transcriptomes
records.abstract: In a transcriptome, isoforms share most of their sequence, and gene families add further near-copies. Yet most long-read mappers treat each isoform as a separate target and repeat seeding, chaining and alignment for each.  We introduce spearfish, a long-read mapper built for this redundancy. Its delta mapping (Δ-mapping) computes each target's alignment-score difference from the best candidate. It skips sequence that all candidates share, which cannot change the difference, and aligns where they differ once per distinct sequence rather than once per target. Seeds come from locally consistent parsing (LCP), so every isoform that contains an exon receives the same seeds in its interior. Collapsing them gives a core graph, a de Bruijn-like graph whose size is bounded by the distinct exonic sequence plus a small term per splice junction, independent of the number of isoforms. Over this graph, spearfish computes the exact colinear chaining score of every candidate transcript, sharing dynamic-programming state among transcripts via a procedure which we prove is equivalent to chaining on each transcript separately.  Across RNA-seq experiments, using 32 threads, spearfish maps reads 26-83× faster than minimap2 in at most a seventh of the memory, and 2.6-11.3× faster than lr-kallisto's pseudoalignment. On simulated reads it ranks the true transcript first more often than minimap2 on HiFi reads and within 0.5 percentage points of it on ONT reads at 95% accuracy. When using spearfish's Δ-mapping with oarfish for abundance estimation, the abundance estimates match or improve on those that make use of minimap2's alignments on both simulated reads (especially when they are untrimmed) and on seven SG-NEx runs with spike-ins, and quantification is 3.0-8.8× faster than lr-kallisto in going from reads to abundances.
records.authors: Abdelgawad H, Martayan I, MARCHET C, Patro R.

records.title: Annexin A1-Mediated Therapeutic Effect of Extracellular Vesicles Derived from Thrombin- Preconditioned Mesenchymal Stromal Cells in Experimental Necrotizing Enterocolitis
records.abstract: Abstract  Background  Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a devastating inflammatory disease in premature infants lacking specific treatment. Extracellular vesicles from thrombin-preconditioned mesenchymal stromal cells (thMSC-EVs) show enhanced therapeutic efficacy over naïve MSC-EVs. This study aimed to identify the key enriched therapeutic factor and its mechanism in experimental NEC. Methods  Comparative proteomic profiling (LC-MS/MS) of thMSC-EVs was performed to identify candidate proteins. NEC was induced in neonatal mice (P4) using formula feeding, LPS, and stress. thMSC-EVs were administered intraperitoneally. Bulk RNA-sequencing and multi-omics ligand-receptor analyses of the mouse ileum integrated proteomic and transcriptomic data. The candidate, Annexin A1, was validated using in vitro LPS-induced inflammation and multiple-hit (HIT) models, assessing viability, barrier integrity, and NF-κB and Wnt/β-catenin signaling following treatment with thMSC-EVs, the Annexin A1 mimetic peptide (Ac2-26), and ANXA1-knockdown MSC-derived EVs (siANXA1-MSC-EVs). Results  Proteomic analysis showed thMSC-EVs were significantly enriched with anti-inflammatory proteins, including a 3.8-fold increase in ANXA1. In the NEC model, thMSC-EVs attenuated intestinal necrosis and apoptosis, suppressed the mucosal antimicrobial response, and promoted tissue repair. Multi-omics ligand-receptor analysis identified the Annexin A1–formyl peptide receptor 1 interaction as the most prominent therapeutic axis. In vitro, Ac2-26 replicated the effects of thMSC-EVs, restoring cell viability and ZO-1 expression and suppressing NF-κB while restoring Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Conversely, siANXA1-MSC-EVs showed a significantly, though partially, diminished therapeutic effect. Conclusion  Thrombin preconditioning amplifies the ANXA1 content within MSC-EVs. This enriched ANXA1 exerts a dual therapeutic effect in NEC by suppressing TLR4/NF-kB-mediated inflammation and promoting Wnt/β-catenin-mediated epithelial regeneration via the FPR signaling. Our findings establish ANXA1 as a major, though not exclusive, effector of thMSC-EVs and as a novel therapeutic target for NEC, supporting thMSC-EVs as a potent cell-free therapeutic agent.
records.authors: Kwon C, Hwang S, Kim YE, Yang M, Ahn SY, Sung SI, Chang YS.

records.title: Induction of walnut callus and physiological and molecular differences among tissues with varying degrees of browning
records.abstract: Abstract    Immature cotyledons from ‘Xiangling’ walnut (  Juglans regia  L.) donor trees were used to screen callus induction conditions and characterize six browning grades (S1–S6). Single-factor experiments with three biological replicates per concentration identified 1 mg L⁻¹ α-naphthaleneacetic acid, 0.5 mg L⁻¹ 6-benzyladenine, and 200 mg L⁻¹ ascorbic acid as the concentrations yielding the highest mean induction rates in their respective screens (87.8%, 85.6%, and 88.9%). At these concentrations, approximately 11% of induced calli exhibited more severe browning (S4–S6), while 62%–64% showed some browning (S2–S6). Morphological observations, histology, a 40 min 2,3,5-triphenyltetrazolium chloride (TTC) reduction assay, and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction provided complementary assessments of tissue condition. Mean apparent TTC reduction activity decreased from 1409.4 ± 42.8 in S1 to 275.6 ± 13.1 μg TTC equivalents g⁻¹ fresh weight h⁻¹ in S5. The eight candidate embryogenesis-related genes reached their highest mean expression in S2–S4:  JrSERK1  and  JrBBM1  in S2;  JrBBM2  and  JrLEC2  in S3; and  JrLEC1  ,  JrAGL15  ,  JrFUS3  , and  JrWOX2  in S4.  JrLEC2  reached 9.86-fold relative to uncultured cotyledons. In S6,  JrSERK1  and  JrBBM1  expression was below control levels, whereas the other six genes remained elevated. Histology revealed variation in cell arrangement, staining, and tissue continuity. These findings identify favorable induction conditions and characterize browning-associated physiological and molecular variation, providing a basis for prioritizing S2–S4 for embryogenic competence assessment and subsequent regeneration studies.
records.authors: Huang X, Chang Q, Liang Z.

records.title: Integrated in silico network toxicology, machine learning and molecular simulations to predict candidate colorectal cancer-related targets of three novel non-phthalate plasticizers
records.abstract: Abstract    Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health burden, and chronic exposure to environmental xenobiotics is increasingly implicated in colorectal tumourigenesis. Alternative non-phthalate plasticizers (DOTP, DINCH and TMCH) have been widely adopted as safer substitutes for conventional phthalates, yet their colorectal carcinogenic potential and underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. We therefore implemented an integrative computational toxicology workflow combining carcinogenicity prediction, compound-target mining, functional enrichment, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), large-scale machine-learning screening, multi-omics validation, immune-infiltration analysis, molecular docking and 100 ns all-atom molecular dynamics simulation. TMCH exhibited the highest predicted carcinogenic probability, and 79 genes shared between plasticizer exposure and CRC pathogenesis were identified. Among 118 machine-learning pipelines, a Random Forest plus linear discriminant analysis model using 20 of the 79 genes was selected on parsimony grounds, and SHapley Additive exPlanations prioritised five core targets:  ABCG2  ,  CDK1  ,  CA7  ,  MET  and  TDP2  . Multi-cohort transcriptomics, immunohistochemistry and single-cell profiling confirmed their dysregulated expression with distinct cell-type tropism, whereas CIBERSORT and ESTIMATE analyses linked these genes to specific immune-cell subsets and to the global immune-stromal microenvironment. All five genes achieved strong diagnostic performance but showed divergent prognostic associations. Docking predicted favourable binding of DOTP-ABCG2 and DINCH-CDK1, whereas TMCH bound weakly to all five proteins despite its high predicted risk; molecular dynamics simulations supported the structural stability of the DOTP-ABCG2 complex. Collectively, this in silico study provides testable hypotheses rather than causal proof and nominates five candidate targets for experimental toxicological validation.
records.authors: Lou W, Ren W, Chen B.

records.title: Matched cerebrospinal fluid and bone marrow single cell transcriptomics highlights the CXCR4-CXCL12 axis in ALL CNS disease
records.abstract: Abstract  Central nervous system (CNS) relapse in acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) poses a significant clinical challenge. Although experimental studies have highlighted candidate genes for CNS involvement, studies in humans are scarce. We used single-cell transcriptomic profiling of leukemic cells in matched cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), bone marrow and blood of patients with ALL to identify genes and cell states associated with CNS involvement and relapse. CSF leukemic cells showed a distinct expression profile with lipogenic metabolic rewiring and occupied transcriptional states more closely related to bone marrow than to blood. Trajectory analysis identified six genes with progressively increased expression toward CSF-associated leukemic states (SMAP2, CXCR4, SPRY1, PLD1, HSPB1 and ARPP21). Among 16 genes previously implicated in ALL CNS disease in experimental models, CXCR4, SCD, VEGFA and SPP1 were significantly increased in CSF, and CXCR4 was further increased in patients with relapse (log2FC 2.1, p = 0.00096). Supporting this, patients with CNS relapse had higher soluble CXCL12 in CSF (p = 0.044) and higher bone marrow CXCR4 surface expression at diagnosis (p = 0.034) than patients without relapse. In conclusion, single-cell transcriptomics identified molecular alterations associated with ALL CNS disease. The CXCR4–CXCL12 axis stands out as a marker of CNS relapse in ALL and a promising therapeutic target.

records.title: Structural Modelling and Clinical Interpretation of CDKN1B and CDKN2C Variants in Patients with MEN-like Phenotypes: A Case Series.
records.abstract: BackgroundMultiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN) syndromes involve tumors in multiple endocrine organs. Distinguishing MEN1 from rarer MEN-like syndromes, including MEN4 caused by pathogenic germline CDKN1B variants, can be challenging.MethodsWe describe four individuals from two families, integrating clinical, biochemical and imaging findings with germline whole-exome sequencing, evolutionary conservation, in silico variant-effect prediction, structural modeling and molecular dynamics. Tumor tissue was unavailable for somatic sequencing or loss-of-heterozygosity analysis.ResultsProband 1, initially suspected of MEN1 because of a nonfunctioning pituitary microadenoma, bilateral adrenal hyperplasia and primary hyperparathyroidism, carried a pathogenic germline CDKN1B frameshift variant, p.Lys96GlnfsTer29. Proband 2 carried the CDKN2C p.Leu107Val variant, classified as a variant of uncertain significance, and had hyperthyroidism, primary hyperaldosteronism, nephrolithiasis, primary hyperparathyroidism, a nonfunctioning pituitary microadenoma and a pancreatic mucinous cystic neoplasm. The variants showed distinct predicted mechanisms. The CDKN1B frameshift preserves the kinase-inhibitory domain but removes the C-terminal regulatory region of p27Kip1 and is predicted to trigger nonsense-mediated decay. In contrast, CDKN2C Leu107 is evolutionarily invariant and buried within the hydrophobic core of ankyrin repeat 4; substitution by valine reduced local hydrophobic packing, consistent with partial destabilization rather than protein loss. The two variant-positive sons of Proband 2 were asymptomatic, and no variant-positive individual carried a MEN1 mutation.ConclusionsThese findings support CDKN1B testing in MEN1-negative patients with MEN features and highlight CDKN2C as a candidate contributor to MEN-like phenotypes. Integrated clinical, genetic, conservation and structural data may support future re-evaluation of p.Leu107Val while preserving its current VUS classification.
records.authors: Papadopoulou-Marketou N, Milou C, Papakonstantinou E, Vlachakis D, Sertedaki A, Poulios E, Chrousos GP.

records.title: Hydrogen production and fermentation in heliobacteria.
records.abstract: Heliobacteria are the only phototrophic members of the gram-positive bacteria. Heliomicrobium modesticaldum can grow chemotrophically in the dark using pyruvate as a carbon source. It can grow phototrophically only on acetate (plus CO2). We found that dihydrogen production occurred only when fixing N2 and increased ~5-fold upon replacing N2 with argon. Introduction of genes encoding a [FeFe] hydrogenase and maturases (hydAEFG) from Acetivibrio thermocellus conferred the ability to produce H2 at much higher levels. The modified cells made the most H2 when grown chemotrophically, less when grown mixotrophically, and none when grown phototrophically, suggesting that only excess electrons were available for H2 production. We tested several molecules as potential reduced fermentation products by this species. Only propanoate was observed, and its extracellular concentration could reach several millimolar. There was an inverse correlation between light intensity and propanoate production when the cells were grown on pyruvate, and phototrophic cultures produced no detectable propanoate. We conclude that propanoate is the major reduced fermentation product made by Hmb. modesticaldum, and we propose a pathway to produce it that is essentially a mini-cycle within the reductive TCA (rTCA) cycle, combining the first four reactions of the rTCA cycle with methylmalonyl-CoA mutase and epimerase, and methylmalonyl-CoA:pyruvate carboxytransferase. This pathway would, in effect, dispose of four reducing equivalents while driving the conversion of pyruvate to propanoate. The genes for the last six enzymes of this pathway seem to be part of an operon; the genes and potential operon are conserved in other heliobacteria, suggesting that this pathway exists in all or most heliobacteria.ImportanceThis study establishes that heliobacteria, the only phototrophic members of the Bacillota, produce propanoic acid as the reduced fermentation product when growing chemotrophically. The pathway used to make it resembles that of the Propionibacteria, except in the context of a mini-cycle within the reductive TCA (rTCA) cycle. This work confirms that the Heliomicrobium genus lacks a functional hydrogenase to make hydrogen as a way to dispose of excess electrons. Finally, it is shown that these organisms can be engineered to make dihydrogen as a reduced fermentation product if the genes for a clostridial hydrogenase and assembly proteins are expressed in Heliomicrobium modesticaldum.

records.title: Atomic-Scale Design, Performance Degradation Mechanisms, and System Integration of Multi-Principal Element Hydrogen Storage Materials.
records.abstract: Solid-state metal hydrides offer high volumetric hydrogen density and intrinsic safety for hydrogen storage, yet their practical application is severely hindered by poor room-temperature thermodynamics, sluggish kinetics, impurity gas poisoning, difficult activation, and cycling degradation. Multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) have recently emerged as promising candidates to overcome these bottlenecks through their vast compositional space, severe lattice distortion, and synergistic cocktail effect. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in MPEAs for solid-state hydrogen storage, bridging atomic-scale design to system-level performance. A unified composition-process-structure-property framework is established that integrates engineering-driven design rules, post-processing techniques, multi-scale computations, machine learning (ML), and high-throughput experiments. Using advanced in situ and ex situ characterization, the atomic-scale origins and cross-scale evolution of surface poisoning, hydrogen-induced amorphization (HIA), disproportionation, pulverization, and defect accumulation. A theoretical framework linking electronic structure to heat and mass transport is further developed, and hydrogen storage bed design, device integration, fuel-cell coupling, manufacturing scalability, and cost analysis are discussed. Finally, key scientific and engineering challenges and future research directions are outlined. This review provides scientific guidance for designing MPEA-based solid-state hydrogen storage systems with high capacity, long cycle life, high poisoning tolerance, fast de-/hydrogenation kinetics, and low cost.
records.authors: Wu Y, Qi X, Zhou Y, Liu H, Yuan T, Jiang J, Chu F, Zhou Q, Zhou P, Xiao X, Chen L.

records.title: Dual‑targeting therapeutic strategies for glioblastoma (Review).
records.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most aggressive primary malignant tumour, owing to intratumoural heterogeneity, adaptive resistance, and an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Dual‑targeting strategies aim to exploit complementary therapeutic vulnerabilities; however, their mechanisms of action and levels of supporting evidence vary considerably. The present narrative review evaluates single‑molecule inhibitors, dual‑antigen cellular therapies, oncolytic virus platforms, nanocarrier systems, and combination approaches directed against glioma stem‑like and differentiated cellular states or spatially distinct tumour regions. Distinctions are made between molecular co‑inhibition, dual‑antigen recognition, coordinated drug delivery, and multimodal therapeutic strategies. Evidence derived from isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)‑mutant glioma and other malignancies is considered separately from evidence in IDH‑wildtype GBM. Vorasidenib (AG‑881) inhibits both mutant IDH1 and mutant IDH2 within the same metabolic pathway; however, its clinical benefit in grade 2 IDH‑mutant glioma does not demonstrate efficacy in GBM. Most alternative approaches remain at the preclinical stage, whereas early cellular therapy approaches have shown biological activity alongside significant limitations in response durability and neurological tolerability. Key challenges examined include clonal evolution, lineage plasticity, epigenetic and metabolic adaptation, patient stratification, and integration with radiotherapy. Translational priorities include confirming adequate drug exposure and engagement of both targets, identifying biologically appropriate patient populations, establishing tolerable treatment schedules, and streamlining manufacturing processes. Limiting tumour adaptation remains a testable therapeutic hypothesis rather than an established clinical outcome of dual targeting. Future progress will depend on research that links mechanistic complementarity to durable disease control and acceptable toxicity.

records.title: Lactylation in the regulation of macrophage polarization: Mechanisms pathophysiological significance (Review).
records.abstract: Macrophage polarization is regulated by metabolic reprogramming epigenetic modifications. The discovery of histone lysine lactylation has revealed that lactate is not merely a glycolytic end product but also an important metabolic signal linking cellular metabolic status to gene expression programs. Lactylation modulates both histones (such as H3K18la) non‑histone proteins (such as nuclear factor‑κB p65 hypoxia‑inducible factor‑1α), thereby influencing macrophage polarization through transcriptional regulation signal transduction. Its functions are highly context‑dependent. In the tumor microenvironment, it predominantly promotes M2‑type immunosuppression; in certain neuroinflammatory conditions, it may be associated with M1‑like phenotypes; in metabolic diseases, it may exacerbate pro‑inflammatory damage. This modification involves extensive crosstalk with acetylation, methylation, other epigenetic modifications, constituting a complex regulatory network. However, current research faces critical bottlenecks: The intracellular source metabolic flux of lactyl‑CoA remain unclear; the substrate specificity physiological relevance of candidate writers, such as E1A‑binding protein p300 CREB‑binding protein, erasers, such as sirtuin 2, remain controversial; a bona fide reader domain that specifically recognizes lactylated lysine has not been identified; in vivo causal evidence remains limited. Future efforts should integrate multiomics technologies, genetic manipulation tools, precision delivery systems to decipher the spatiotemporal regulatory networks of lactylation, thereby facilitating the identification of new therapeutic targets strategies for inflammatory, neoplastic, metabolic diseases.

records.title: Gene therapy for epilepsy: From SCN1A to broadened therapeutic horizons (Review).
records.abstract: Genetic epilepsy, for which the molecular mechanisms are relatively well defined in numerous monogenic forms, represents an attractive model for the transition from symptomatic seizure control to mechanism‑driven correction. However, gene therapy strategies differ in their mechanisms of action, adaptability to specific mutations and translational maturity, making rational selection of interventions based on variant‑specific functional consequences an important clinical challenge. The present review examined five nucleic acid‑based therapeutic strategies, namely gene supplementation, enhancement of endogenous gene expression, gene silencing, DNA editing and RNA editing, for major causative genes, using mutation‑specific functional consequences [loss‑of‑function (LOF) vs. gain‑of‑function] as the primary framework for therapeutic decision‑making. The mechanisms and suitability of each approach are analysed, and their performance in terms of cell‑type specificity, delivery vectors and safety is evaluated by integrating evidence from animal models, induced pluripotent stem cell‑derived neurons and organoids and clinical trials. The present review also summarised key translational barriers, including vector cargo constraints, blood‑brain barrier penetration, off‑target and immune‑associated risks, therapeutic dosing windows and the timing of developmental intervention. Antisense oligonucleotides and regulatory adeno‑associated viral approaches, supported by mature delivery platforms and manageable safety profiles, have progressed furthest towards clinical validation. Endogenous gene activation strategies, such as CRISPR activation, offer a gene replacement‑free approach for LOF disorders but remain preclinical. DNA and RNA editing, while potentially capable of durable disease modification, require further evidence on delivery efficiency and long‑term homeostatic safety. Gene therapy for genetic epilepsy is undergoing a key transition from proof‑of‑concept studies to individualised clinical application. Future progress will depend on integrating personalised intervention design, multi‑target therapeutic combinations, artificial intelligence‑assisted sequence optimisation and standardised translational models, with the potential to drive a paradigm shift from seizure suppression to mechanistic correction.

records.abstract: Supramolecular Fe3+-tannic acid shells are formed around living Saccharomyces cerevisiae through eosin Y-mediated photo-oxidation of Fe2+-tannic acid species under visible light. records.title: FaWRKY7 modulates jasmonate signaling responses and enhances strawberry fruit resistance to Botrytis cinerea.
records.abstract: WRKY transcription factors and jasmonic acid (JA) signaling are essential for plant responses to stress, but their roles in strawberry resistance to Botrytis cinerea remain unclear. Here, we investigated the function of FaWRKY7 in strawberry fruit and transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana. FaWRKY7 expression was significantly induced at 72 h after B. cinerea inoculation. Transient overexpression of FaWRKY7 enhanced strawberry fruit resistance to B. cinerea, whereas silencing increased susceptibility. Similarly, FaWRKY7-overexpressing Arabidopsis plants showed enhanced resistance to B. cinerea and greater responsiveness to exogenous methyl jasmonate (MeJA), although basal levels of free JA, JA-Ile, and OPDA were not detectably altered in non-inoculated samples. Pharmacological assays further showed that FaWRKY7-mediated resistance was maintained under MeJA treatment and only partially reduced by Jarin-1, an inhibitor of JA-Ile formation, indicating that this effect is only partially dependent on JA-Ile formation. Mechanistically, DAP-seq, yeast one-hybrid, EMSA, and dual-luciferase assays showed that FaWRKY7 directly binds to the promoters of FaJAZ4 and FaJAZ8 and represses their transcription. These findings indicate that FaWRKY7 enhances resistance to B. cinerea, at least in part by directly repressing FaJAZ4 and FaJAZ8 and thereby modulating jasmonate signaling responses.

records.title: SERPINE1 Identifies a Shared Injury-associated Molecular Signature in Intracerebral Hemorrhage and Epilepsy.
records.abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and epilepsy are clinically linked neurological disorders, yet their shared molecular features remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify shared molecular candidates across ICH and epilepsy by integrating transcriptomic data with a curated set of genes with established circadian relevance. Transcriptomic datasets for ICH and epilepsy were retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus, and candidate genes were curated from the Molecular Signatures Database and GeneCards. Differentially expressed candidate genes were intersected, and an integrative machine-learning framework-including Boruta, LASSO, XGBoost, and CatBoost-was applied to prioritize shared genes. Integrated machine-learning and network analyses nominated SERPINE1 for further investigation. Single-sample gene set enrichment analysis identified higher scores for porphyrin, folate and pterine, and arachidonic acid metabolism in both disease comparisons. SERPINE1 expression correlated positively with arachidonic acid metabolism scores in both datasets, while Hallmark gene set enrichment analysis linked its expression to inflammatory transcriptional signatures, including TNFA signaling via NFKB and IL6-JAK-STAT3 signaling. Gene interaction, drug-mRNA, transcription factor-mRNA, and competing endogenous RNA networks further characterized its regulatory and pharmacological context. Independent bulk transcriptomic datasets and experimental models supported SERPINE1 upregulation, with single-nucleus RNA-sequencing providing complementary cellular context, while single-nucleus analyses and immunostaining further supported its preferential microglial localization. Collectively, these findings identify SERPINE1 as a shared injury-associated molecular feature of ICH and epilepsy, with preferential microglial localization and associations with inflammatory transcriptional signatures and metabolic pathway scores. Although SERPINE1 is known to be clock-regulated, whether its temporal expression pattern is altered in ICH or epilepsy remains to be determined.

records.title: RNA-seq-based allele-specific expression reveals candidate expressed-variant differences in DMD<sup>mdx</sup> rat muscle.
records.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is a severe X-linked disorder characterized by progressive muscle degeneration due to dystrophin deficiency. While the primary variant in the DMD gene is well-characterized, disease severity often varies, suggesting the involvement of additional genetic modifiers. In this study, we performed high-resolution allele-specific expression (ASE) and single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) analyses using RNA-Seq in DMDmdx and wild-type (WT) Sprague-Dawley rats derived from the same breeding lineage. Despite this shared lineage, we detected a higher number of significant RNA-seq-supported ASE-associated SNPs in DMDmdx rats (3,440) compared to WT controls (1,883). However, these findings should be interpreted as candidate allelic imbalances requiring orthogonal validation. Functional annotation and in silico protein stability analyses predicted that several missense variants, including variants in Myh2, Myh3, Ttn, Obscn, and Aldoa, may affect protein function or stability. Functional enrichment analyses identified pathways related to muscle contraction, cytoskeletal organization, and immune responses. Together, these findings indicate differences in the RNA-seq-supported ASE profiles of DMDmdx and WT muscle and provide candidate loci for independent validation and further investigation of potential disease-modifying mechanisms in DMD.

records.title: SLC25A1/CIC supports osteoclastogenesis by coordinating mitochondrial bioenergetics and redox homeostasis.
records.abstract: Osteoclastogenesis requires precise coordination between mitochondrial bioenergetics and anabolic programs, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we identify the mitochondrial citrate carrier (CIC, encoded by SLC25A1) as a crucial link that couples mitochondrial bioenergetics to glutathione (GSH)-dependent redox regulation during osteoclastogenesis. CIC expression was elevated in the osteoclast-lineage cells  from postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP) patients and ovariectomized (OVX) mice, and was positively correlated with classical osteoclast markers. During osteoclastogenesis, CIC was progressively upregulated. Pharmacologic inhibition of CIC with CTPI-2 not only suppressed osteoclastogenesis but also disrupted core metabolic processes, including tricarboxylic acid cycle engagement, amino acid biosynthesis, and mitochondrial respiration. Integrative transcriptomic and metabolomic profiling further revealed a compensatory shift toward enhanced GSH synthesis. Mechanistically, CIC associated with the glutamate-cysteine ligase modifier subunit (GCLM), linking mitochondrial metabolic regulation to the GSH synthetic machinery. CIC inhibition increased GCL activity, intracellular GSH content, and the GSH/GSSG ratio, accompanied by reduced reactive oxygen species accumulation. The functional importance of the GSH axis was evident, as GCL inhibition by buthionine sulfoximine partially reversed the anti-osteoclastogenic effects of CIC inhibition. Consistently, osteoclast-targeted silencing of CIC in OVX mice mitigated bone loss. Collectively, these findings support a role for CIC as a metabolic integrator of energy and redox metabolism in osteoclasts, and highlight its potential as a candidate target for limiting excessive bone resorption in PMOP.
