records.title: Diversification of budding yeast polarization dynamics after compensatory experimental evolution
records.abstract: Essential cellular processes evolve under strong selection, yet protein networks underlying conserved functions can vary substantially. To what extent evolution constrains the intracellular dynamics of proteins performing essential functions is currently largely unknown. Here, we characterize budding yeast polarization phenotypes along a previously established evolutionary recovery trajectory, compensating for the loss of near-essential polarity gene BEM1. Through quantitative live cell imaging, we show that loss of BEM1 weakens and destabilizes polarization. Surprisingly, in recovered evolved lineages, protein dynamics change significantly compared to the ancestor: most notably, presence of main regulator Cdc42-GTP is strongly decreased, while polarisome member Spa2 localizes more slowly into mobile foci. Although separate phenotypic characteristics are only weakly constrained, we find evidence of effective protein-independent localization modes, revealing signs of convergence along the evolutionary trajectory. Together, our results show that evolution can restore global cellular function without conserving microscopic organization, instead giving rise to novel molecular phenotypes.
records.authors: Glazenburg M, Laan L.

records.title: Harnessing catalytic knowledge to guide enzyme discovery and evolution with AlphaEnzyme
records.abstract: Retrieving an enzyme for a target reaction provides a starting point for evolution, but predicting how to improve it remains difficult. This requires connecting evolutionary information with the structural and chemical context of catalysis. Here we present AlphaEnzyme, an enzyme foundation model built on a structure-grounded representation of an enzyme paired with its reaction, from which catalytic compatibility, kinetics and mutational response are read out together. On a time-separated benchmark, AlphaEnzyme achieves a top-1 catalyst retrieval success rate of 30.1%, against 17.2% for the strongest baseline. Michaelis constant predictions achieve the highest rank correlations among the compared methods, reaching 0.64 for enzymes sharing at most 40% identity with the kinetic training set. The model also enriches high-fitness TrpB variants at a budget of 16 candidates without target-specific fitness training. In prospective transaminase engineering, several prioritized variants exceed the parent, with the best design yielding a 30.4-fold increase in product signal in a lysate-based assay while retaining (R)-selectivity. Together, AlphaEnzyme provides a common molecular basis for selecting starting enzymes and prioritizing sequence changes for their improvement.
records.authors: Liu Y, Zheng S.

records.title: Metformin lowers HMGA1a and RBM3 protein in breast cancer cells, and its effect on ESR1 splicing depends on cell density and exposure time
records.abstract: The ESR1 gene produces ERα46, an N-terminally truncated isoform generated by skipping of exon 1, which is reduced in tamoxifen-resistant breast cancer cells. We have reported that metformin moves the ratio of full-length ERα to ERα46 in opposite directions in MCF-7 cells and their tamoxifen-resistant subline TAMR1, and that metformin reduces TAMR1 xenograft growth (Harada et al., Am J Pharm Health Res 2022;10(11)). That report leaves two questions open: whether the effect is dosedependent and stable across culture conditions, and what splicing factor might carry it. Here we report the experiments that bear on both. Across a full dose range from 0.25 to 5 mM at high seeding density, metformin produced no consistent change in the full-length share of ESR1 transcript in either line: densitometry of the gel gave 42%, 43%, 42%, 43%, 45% and 48% in MCF-7 cells and 55%, 44%, 52%, 47%, 68% and 43% in TAMR1 cells. The reported shift therefore depends on the seeding density used, and the comparison that produced it is not reproduced at high density. At low density the MCF-7 response persisted to 48 h (52%, 62% and 68% at 0, 2.5 and 5 mM). Metformin lowered HMGA1a protein in MCF-7 cells and showed the same tendency in TAMR1 cells, at both seeding densities, and lowered RBM3 protein in TAMR1 cells at 24 and 48 h. HMGA1a is the factor we previously showed to generate ERα46 by trapping U1 snRNP at an upstream pseudo-5′ splice site, so a fall in HMGA1a predicts less ERα46, the opposite of what was seen in TAMR1 cells at low density. The fall in RBM3, the protein through which metformin alters splicing in myotonic dystrophy, is the more plausible candidate. RT-PCR of the xenograft tumours from the earlier study detected full-length ESR1 transcript in the untreated and tamoxifen-plus-metformin groups but not in the singleagent groups, with amplification failing in several lanes; these panels do not separate the treatments. Taken together, the direction of the metformin effect on ESR1 splicing is conditional on culture density and does not survive a dose-response test at high density, and HMGA1a is unlikely to be the factor that carries it.
records.authors: Harada Y, Tanaka T, Hamaguchi Y, Horita Y, Harada H, Mori M, Murata Y, Ohe K.

records.title: FeatureMAP enables network-guided interpretation of untargeted metabolomics
records.abstract: Untargeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) metabolomics generates thousands of features, but incomplete metabolite annotation and reliance on predefined pathways limit their biological interpretation. Here we present FeatureMAP, an LC-MS feature-centric computational framework that integrates multi-evidence metabolite annotation, network-guided refinement, metabolic module discovery, and structured large language model-based functional interpretation. Across ten public datasets, FeatureMAP improved MS1-based metabolite candidate prioritization while reducing annotation redundancy. In semi-synthetic benchmarks, FeatureMAP recovered coordinated metabolic perturbations, achieving 92% recovery of a simulated perturbation, and distinguished concurrent metabolic processes. Controlled benchmarks further evaluated functional interpretation under competing metabolite-level signals. Based on FeatureMAP, we additionally developed PhenoMAP, a phenotype-aware knowledge graph comprising 12,929 dysregulated metabolic modules from 501 human metabolomics studies spanning 326 phenotypes. Module-level comparisons revealed reproducible metabolic similarities across independent studies and biologically supported relationships among phenotypes. Application to Alzheimer's disease cerebrospinal fluid and cellular datasets identified convergent membrane-lipid alterations and implicated galactose-linked glycosphingolipid remodeling. Together, FeatureMAP and PhenoMAP enable network-grounded interpretation of incompletely annotated LC-MS metabolomics data and systematic investigation of metabolic dysregulation across biological conditions.

records.title: Beneath functional traits: material organization in postgenomic ecology and evolution
records.abstract: Ecology has progressed from describing species diversity through taxonomic indices to explaining ecological processes using functional traits. Yet traits such as growth, body size, reproduction, and resource-use efficiency are compressed representations of biological systems whose functions emerge from complex material organization. Here, I develop trait compression as the many-to-one relationship through which distinct biochemical and material states generate similar conventional ecological traits. Drawing on the view of organisms as open, far-from-equilibrium multielement systems, I argue that elemental inventories and log compositional coordinates (LCCs) offer tractable descriptions of material organization without requiring exhaustive molecular reconstruction. Environmental geochemical heterogeneity in natural rock pools and ionomic variation among laboratory-maintained isolates of the zooplankter, Daphnia, illustrate the diversity of material conditions and organismal states. Observations of experimentally evolved populations of the bacterium, Serratia marcescens, demonstrate that similar growth rates can accompany distinct multielement compositions. Reanalysis of recombinant Daphnia pulicaria clones further reveals substantial variation in body phosphorus (P) content among clones exhibiting overlapping growth rates, but little improvement in predicting growth across phosphorus environments when body P is included alongside initial growth. Together, these observations illustrate trait compression while distinguishing material heterogeneity from its predictive consequences. I propose that material-state differences become ecologically consequential when they predict distinct responses among organisms exhibiting similar initial traits. Trait compression thus identifies a testable limitation of conventional trait-based approaches and provides a framework for connecting biochemical organization to ecological prediction and evolutionary outcomes.

records.title: IL-4 Licenses B Cell Activation Through Cholesterol Synthesis
records.abstract: Abstract  IL-4 is a pleiotropic cytokine that was first identified as a B cell co-mitogen over 30 years ago1. However, how IL-4 signaling mechanistically supports B cell proliferation is incompletely understood. Here, we find that the cholesterol biosynthetic program is transcriptionally upregulated by IL-4 signaling during the early B cell response to influenza virus infection and is required for B cell activation in vivo. Induction of lipid synthesis genes required both STAT6 and SREBP2 transcription factors, allowing IL-4 activated B cells to enter the cell cycle and proliferate in the absence of lipids. Genetic inhibition of de novo cholesterol synthesis via SREBP2 deletion reduced plasmablasts and subsequent germinal center B cell formation at steady state and following influenza infection. SREBP2-deficency blocked IL-4 mediated cell cycle entry, ER expansion, and subsequent proliferation in a cholesterol dependent manner. Further mechanistic studies revealed that ER cholesterol content promoted sustained STAT6 signaling associated with ER expansion and B cell survival. In sum, we demonstrate that the well-known ability of IL-4 to act as a B cell growth factor is through a previously unknown rewiring of specific lipid anabolic programs, relieving sensitivity of cells of environmental nutrient availability.

records.title: The growth characteristics and metabolic profiling of Δ 5,7 -sterols and fatty acids in Schizochytrium sp. S31 under different culture conditions
records.abstract: Abstract    Schizochytrium  is a promising thraustochytrid cell factory for co-producing high-value bioactives; however, its growth and bioactive accumulation depend heavily on culture conditions. This study systematically investigated the growth characteristics and the changes in Δ  5,7  -sterols, fatty acids and astaxanthin of  Schizochytrium  sp. S31 under different concentrations of glucose (0–120 g/L), sea salt (0–130 g/L) and pH (3.5–7.5). Sea salt exerted a markedly stronger influence on sterol profiles and fatty acid contents than glucose or pH. Low salinity (10 g/L), with ergosterol constituting the largest proportion (41%), maximized total fatty acid (41.3% DCW) and DHA (7.3% DCW) contents, whereas higher salinities shifted sterol composition toward C28-Δ  5,7  and increased trace astaxanthin levels. The maximum cell dry weight of 17.4 g/L was obtained at 60 g/L glucose, 20 g/L sea salt and pH 5.5, which was also the optimum condition for the simultaneous accumulation of Δ  5,7  -sterols (50.73 mg/L), docosahexaenoic acid (DHA, 1097 mg/L) and astaxanthin (0.11 mg/L). Transcriptomic analysis revealed a crosstalk among sterol, DHA and astaxanthin biosynthetic pathways in  Schizochytrium  sp. S31, and low salinity enhanced fatty acid β-oxidation to elevate the acetyl-CoA supply toward the mevalonate (MVA) pathway, while downregulating crtI and crtR to suppress downstream astaxanthin accumulation. Additionally, candidate genes involved in key phytosterols synthesis were identified. These findings provide critical insights into the biosynthetic regulation of sterols, astaxanthin, and DHA in thraustochytrids, highlighting their potential for the co-production of these high-value bioactives.
records.authors: Zhang X, He P, Liao Y, Peng J, Yuan J, Zhao J.

records.title: Long-read full-length transcriptome sequencing reveals multilayered sex-associated isoform regulation in thyroid carcinoma
records.abstract: Abstract  Background  Sex disparities in thyroid carcinoma are well recognized, yet their molecular basis at the transcript isoform level remains poorly understood. We aimed to determine whether sex-associated molecular differences extend beyond gene-level expression to coordinated remodeling of transcript isoforms. Methods  Tumor tissues from ten thyroid carcinoma patients (four males, six females) were profiled by Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) full-length transcriptome sequencing. Gene-level, transcript-level and post-transcriptional analyses, including differential expression, alternative splicing, alternative polyadenylation and differential transcript usage, were integrated. External validation was performed by exon-usage analysis of the TCGA-THCA cohort (505 primary tumors). Results  We identified 14,420 genes and 32,269 transcripts, including 1,064 novel genes and 9,755 novel transcripts. Transcript-level analysis detected 2,052 differentially expressed transcripts, nearly twice the number of differentially expressed genes (1,144), with 627 alterations detectable only at the isoform level. Sex-associated analysis revealed 68 differential splicing events (predominantly exon skipping), 340 alternative polyadenylation events, 94 3′UTR remodeling events and 956 transcripts with altered isoform preference. Integration across layers yielded 56 consistently dysregulated candidates, represented by SNHG5 and PTCSC2. External TCGA-THCA exon-usage analysis reproduced sex-associated signal at JPX and SNHG5 that was undetectable at the gene-expression level. Using GTEx normal thyroid (v8, n = 578; v10, n = 587) and TCGA adjacent-normal tissue (n = 59) as references, only 28 genes (26 in v10) showed sex-biased expression in normal thyroid, almost all sex-chromosomal or immunoglobulin genes, and no autosomal gene passed correction in tumours; 1,917 of the 2,139 sex-associated event genes (89.6%) showed no sex-biased gene-level expression in either normal thyroid or tumour. Conclusions  Sex-associated regulation in thyroid carcinoma is mediated through coordinated changes in transcript abundance and transcript identity, establishing isoform-resolved profiling as an essential complement to conventional gene-level analysis of endocrine tumor heterogeneity.
records.authors: Dilinigaer D, Rousuli Y, Aini A, Ran D.

records.title: Splice switching of membrane-bound FLT1 into a soluble protein as a treatment for pathological angiogenesis
records.abstract: Abstract    Pathological retinal neovascularization is associated with dysregulated vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) signaling. Soluble FLT1 (sFLT1), an endogenous VEGF decoy receptor, is generated through alternative 3′-end processing of  FLT1  pre-mRNA. We investigated the cis-regulatory elements that control this process and used splice-switching oligonucleotides (SSOs) to increase sFLT1 production. Two overlapping SSO panels were screened in HEK293FT cells using qPCR and ELISA. We validated lead candidates in CRISPRa-engineered,  FLT1  -enriched Müller glial cells using qPCR, ELISA, and a VEGF-responsive luminescence assay. Proximal SSOs increased sFLT1 without altering total  FLT1  transcript levels, indicating altered RNA processing rather than increased gene expression. Distal SSOs also enhanced sFLT1 by targeting polyadenylation signals. SSO-16 and SSO-19 produced the greatest increases in sFLT1 and significantly attenuated VEGF signaling. These findings identify  FLT1  intron 13 regulatory elements as promising therapeutic targets for retinal vascular disease while preserving  FLT1  expression and supporting targeted modulation of VEGF signaling.
records.authors: Wazan LE, Kadife E, Harper A, Kumar S, Brownfoot FC, Liu G.

records.title: Cross-sectional Plasma Metabolomic Profiles across Acute, Recovery-Stage, and Recurrent Ischemic Stroke: A Quality-Control and Multiplicity-Aware Exploratory Study
records.abstract: Abstract  Background and Purpose: Plasma metabolomics may capture biological heterogeneity across clinically defined ischemic stroke states, but small discovery datasets require careful control of analytical variability, metabolite-annotation uncertainty, and multiple testing. We assessed whether a four-group cross-sectional plasma dataset contained reproducible global or feature-level differences after explicit quality-control filtering and multiplicity correction. Materials and Methods: Plasma samples from 40 participants were compared across healthy control (HC), acute ischemic stroke (AIS), recovery-stage stroke, and recurrent ischemic stroke (RIS) groups (n = 10 per group). Positive- and negative-ion untargeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) feature tables were analyzed separately using the documented detection, transformation, normalization, pooled-quality-control (QC), and imputation workflow. Global structure was assessed by principal component analysis and one-factor PERMANOVA with 1,999 permutations. Feature-wise differences were evaluated by Kruskal-Wallis tests with Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction within ion mode. Results: After QC filtering, 1,605 positive-mode and 872 negative-mode feature rows remained. PCA showed extensive overlap among groups. PERMANOVA did not support a global group effect in positive mode (pseudo-F = 0.988, R² = 0.076, P = 0.486) or negative mode (pseudo-F = 1.168, R² = 0.089, P = 0.117). Although 68 positive-mode and 77 negative-mode features had nominal omnibus P Conclusions: No global or feature-level difference met multiplicity-controlled criteria in this pilot dataset. The nominal signals should therefore be regarded as candidates for targeted chemical confirmation and longitudinal validation rather than as stage-specific or recurrence-associated biomarkers.

records.title: Aqueous Humor Proteomic Analysis Identifies Diagnostic Biomarkers for Autoimmune Optic Neuritis
records.abstract: Abstract  Autoimmune optic neuritis (AON) is an inflammatory optic neuropathy that commonly presents with acute or subacute visual loss. In the early stage, AON may overlap clinically with other optic neuropathies, particularly non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION). Although serum and cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers can provide diagnostic assistance, they do not directly reflect the local ocular microenvironment. In this study, aqueous humor (AH) was used as a local liquid biopsy source to identify candidate molecules associated with AON. Data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomics was applied to analyze AH proteins obtained from patients with AON, patients with NAION, and presbyopic surgical controls (CTL group) during anterior chamber paracentesis or surgery. Candidate biomarkers were subsequently quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Proteomic analysis identified 4,264 proteins from 18 samples. Gene Ontology annotation and functional analysis showed that AON-related biological processes were mainly associated with immune responses, ganglioside biosynthesis, glycoprotein biosynthesis, lysosomal function, and protein translation. Candidate protein selection integrated fold change, biological module relevance, protein-protein interaction (PPI) network centrality, and ELISA feasibility, leading to the selection of lactoferrin (LTF), ribosomal protein SA (RPSA), and ATPase H+ transporting V1 subunit A (ATP6V1A) for further validation. The results showed that LTF concentration differed significantly between the AON and CTL groups and demonstrated diagnostic utility in receiver operating characteristic analysis, suggesting that LTF may serve as a potential aqueous humor biomarker for AON. In contrast, RPSA and ATP6V1A did not show stable intergroup differences during validation; nevertheless, the protein translation stress and lysosome-related pathways represented by these molecules suggest corresponding functional alterations in the AH microenvironment of AON. Overall, this study provides an initial characterization of the AH proteomic profile in AON and indicates that AH proteomics may offer a new approach for elucidating local pathological mechanisms and identifying fluid-based diagnostic biomarkers for AON.
records.authors: mao q, zhang m, huang s, zhang j, luo j, gu h, guan h, ji m.

records.title: Review on physics of Higgs-R2inflation.
records.abstract: Higgs inflation, identifying the standard model (SM) Higgs boson as the, causes a unitarity issue during the preheating epoch after inflation in its simplest form, calling for a UV completion. Higgs-inflation serves as a natural candidate for the UV completion of Higgs inflation, providing a consistent framework to describe the inflationary dynamics till the end of reheating. Higgs-inflation contains a new scalar degree of freedom, the scalaron, which unitarizes the theory in the same way that the Higgs boson unitarizes the electroweak gauge boson scatterings in the SM. In this short review, we summarize the physics of Higgs-inflation. A particular emphasis is put on its particle physics aspects, such as the unitarity structure, frame-independence, and the renormalization group evolution.

records.title: Supersonically sprayed Sr-Fe<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub>/Fe<sub>3</sub>C textile electrodes as flexible supercapacitors.
records.abstract: Flexible supercapacitors require electrode materials that simultaneously provide high conductivities, abundant electrochemically active sites, and rapid ion transport pathways. In this study, we developed hybrid Sr-Fe3O4/Fe3C/reduced graphene oxide (rGO) electrodes supported on conductive carbonized cotton fabric via a combination of solvothermal synthesis and supersonic cold-spray deposition, followed by controlled annealing. The cold-spray process facilitated the uniform, binder-free deposition of rGO-enwrapped Sr-Fe precursor particles onto temperature-sensitive cotton textiles without structural damage. Subsequent carbonization induced a phase evolution toward a mixed Fe3O4/Fe3C morphology that was strongly coupled with the graphitized carbon matrix. Systematic annealing between 750 and 825 °C revealed that the microstructure, crystallinity, and phase distribution were temperature-dependent. The optimal SF775 electrode was uniformly coated with Sr-Fe3O4/Fe3C and rGO on a carbonized cotton fibrous network. The SF775 electrode delivered a maximum areal capacitance of 1050 mF cm-2 at 5 mA cm-2, along with an energy density of 145.8 µWh cm-2 at a power density of 10 mW cm-2. Furthermore, the device exhibited excellent mechanical flexibility and durability, retaining its performance after 1000 bending cycles. These results indicate that high-performance textile-based Sr-Fe3O4/Fe3C electrodes produced via cold-spray deposition and thermal phase evolution are promising candidates for wearable supercapacitors.
records.authors: Lim W, Kim YI, Lee Y, Joshi B, Samuel E, Aldalbahi A, Periyasami G, Lee MW, Lee HS, Yoon SS.

records.title: Integrative Transcriptomic Meta-Analysis Reveals SIRT1-SNCA Correlation in Parkinson's Disease
records.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that affects midbrain dopaminergic neurons without any approved therapy. Candidate molecular targets identified in one model are not always traceable across the postmortem, induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC), and cell-based systems used to study PD, which complicates clinical translation. To address this gap, we performed an integrative transcriptomic meta-analysis of 33 publicly available datasets across postmortem human brain, iPSC-derived models, and dopaminergic cell lines of PD. Differential expression and functional enrichment analyses were combined with STRING protein-protein interaction networks, followed by drug-gene interaction screening against a polyphenol panel. Overall, resveratrol was recovered in all 33 comparisons, independent of model system, tissue, and genetic background. We associated resveratrol with 30 distinct target genes, and SIRT1 was itself a recovered target in 6 comparisons spanning all three model systems. Finally, we resolved the SIRT1-SNCA relationship into four directional patterns that differed by model, inverse in postmortem brain and positive in acutely toxin-exposed cells. These findings support a candidate, context-dependent resveratrol-SIRT1 axis in PD.
records.authors: Cimen H, Sonmez E, Hotaslier F.

records.title: Neuropeptide Systems in Substance use Disorders: Therapeutic evidence and molecular mechanisms.
records.abstract: BackgroundSubstance use disorders remain a major global health challenge, with limited pharmacological options and no approved medications for several addictive substances. Peptide-based therapeutics have emerged as promising candidates because they regulate neural circuits involved in reward, motivation, stress, and energy homeostasis.ObjectiveThis narrative review summarizes current evidence for therapeutic peptides in substance use disorders, examines their molecular mechanisms, evaluates advances in peptide engineering and delivery technologies, and discusses future translational and precision-medicine strategies.MethodsA structured narrative review was conducted according to the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles recommendations. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, Google Scholar, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched (January 2000-July 2026) using controlled vocabulary and free-text terms related to therapeutic peptides, receptors, delivery systems, and substance use disorders.ResultsFifteen peptide and neuropeptide systems were identified. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists currently show the strongest clinical evidence, particularly for alcohol use disorder, while findings for nicotine, cocaine, and opioid use disorders remain limited. Oxytocin, orexin receptor antagonists, ghrelin, and dynorphin-related therapies demonstrate encouraging early findings. In contrast, corticotropin-releasing factor type-1 and neurokinin-1 receptor antagonists show target engagement without consistent clinical benefit. Several systems, including neuropeptide Y, galanin, pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide, cocaine- and amphetamine-regulated transcript, melanocortins, and enkephalins, remain largely preclinical. Advances in peptide engineering, nanotechnology, blood-brain barrier delivery, intranasal administration, and long-acting formulations may overcome pharmacokinetic limitations.ConclusionsPeptide therapeutics represent a rapidly evolving strategy for addiction treatment. Future progress will depend on integrating peptide engineering, targeted delivery platforms, biomarker-guided patient selection, and well-designed clinical trials to expand effective.
records.authors: Nejhaddadgar N, Imani NS, Isazadehfar K, Jamali Z.

records.title: Recurrent transcriptional signatures of acquired chemoresistance across cancer models.
records.abstract: Chemoresistance is the innate or acquired ability of cancer cells to evade the cytotoxic effects of chemotherapeutic agents. This hypothesis-generating study presents a systematic comparative analysis of public transcriptomic datasets associated with acquired chemoresistance to major drugs including doxorubicin, cisplatin, and gemcitabine. The aim was to identify recurrent drug-specific gene expression patterns in drug-resistant cancer cells relative to their drug-sensitive parental cells. Publicly available microarray datasets of breast, ovarian, neuroblastoma, bladder, and gallbladder chemoresistant cell lines were retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Differential expression analysis using R/Bioconductor revealed distinct and overlapping signatures of chemoresistance across different cancer types. In doxorubicin-resistant breast cancer, recurrently dysregulated genes included IL-18, CD44, FN1, EGFR, and the histones H2BC10 and H2BC7. Neuroblastoma and ovarian cancer cell datasets shared Differentially Expressed Genes (DEGs) including ABCB1, RUNDC3B, CROT, and TP53TG1. TMEM47 was the only common DEG among all three (breast cancer, neuroblastoma, and ovarian cancer) doxorubicin-resistant datasets, although with tissue-dependent regulation. Gemcitabine resistance signatures in bladder and gallbladder cells include EPCAM, AGR2, NRP2, FGF1, CTH, TENM2, and the long non-coding RNAs APCDD1L-DT and LINC01234. Combined gemcitabine/5-FU resistance revealed common patterns of resistance in gallbladder and colon cancer cell lines. In cisplatin-resistant ovarian cancer cells, LAMA2 and SOX8 were differentially expressed with a consistent direction of change in all datasets in which they were measured. These recurrent associations do not establish causality; rather, they prioritize candidate genes for functional validation in future studies of chemoresistance.
records.authors: Zampetakis I, Gkogkou E, Trougakos IP.

records.title: Starch-chitosan composite particle-stabilized Pickering emulsions for oral celastrol delivery and gut-brain axis-mediated neuroinflammation therapy.
records.abstract: Celastrol (Cel) is a potent natural anti-inflammatory agent whose clinical utility is severely limited by its poor aqueous solubility and negligible oral bioavailability. Herein, we report a surfactant-free oil-in-water Pickering emulsion (C-PE/Cel) stabilized by composite particles of acid-hydrolyzed corn starch and chitosan for oral Cel delivery and gut-brain axis-mediated neuroinflammatory therapy. Controlled sulfuric acid hydrolysis for 6 days was used to tune starch surface amphiphilicity for effective interfacial anchoring, while electrostatic chitosan coating at 1.0 wt% reversed the particle zeta potential from negative to positive, thereby enhancing intestinal retention. C-PE/Cel exhibited high encapsulation efficiency and good colloidal stability at 25 °C for at least 55 days when prepared at an optimized water-to-oil ratio of 3:1. In vitro, C-PE/Cel demonstrated enhanced cellular uptake by Caco-2 human colorectal adenocarcinoma cell monolayers and superior suppression of lipopolysaccharide-induced oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction in the RAW 264.7 mouse monocyte-macrophage cell line. In a chronic LPS-induced murine neuroinflammation model, oral administration of C-PE/Cel restored intestinal barrier integrity by upregulating zonula occludens-1 protein expression and reshaping the gut microbiota by enriching beneficial taxa (e.g., Lachnospiraceae_NK4A136_group and Odoribacter) while reducing potentially pathogenic Ruminococcaceae. Furthermore, integrated 16S ribosomal ribonucleic acid and brain transcriptomic analyses revealed that the therapeutic effects were mediated via the gut-brain axis, involving the downregulation of immunoglobulin-related genes and the upregulation of fatty acid β-oxidation markers. This study established a simple, green, polysaccharide-based Pickering emulsion platform for the oral delivery of hydrophobic therapeutics targeting central nervous system disorders.
records.authors: Li X, Ren T, Du Y, Zhao Y, Li Y, Tang Y, Xu W.

records.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis suggest a possible association between M1-like macrophage cuproptosis and angiogenic impairment in exercise-deficiency-associated sarcopenia.
records.abstract: Sarcopenia is a geriatric syndrome characterized by the progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass and function. While physical inactivity is a primary risk factor of sarcopenia, the underlying molecular mediators remain poorly studied. By combined analysis of human bulk transcriptomic data and single-cell RNA sequencing data, we identified a cuproptosis-associated transcriptional signature significantly enriched in both human sarcopenia and exercise-deprivation models. Our analyses suggest that M1-like macrophage may be particularly vulnerable to cuproptosis due to elevated SLC31A2 expression, potentially contributing to their depletion in the sedentary muscle microenvironment. Intercellular communication modeling further implied that the reduction in M1-like macrophage may impair CXCL8-mediated (or its murine functional analogs) signaling to endothelial tip cells, a process essential for microvascular maintenance. To provide physiological context, we validated these findings in an aged sarcopenia murine model (24-month-old C57BL/6 J). In the gastrocnemius muscle of sarcopenic mice, we observed a significant decrease in muscle fiber cross-sectional area (CSA) alongside a concurrent reduction in F4/80⁺CD86⁺ M1-like macrophage and VEGFR2⁺/CD31⁺ endothelial tip cells. Collectively, our study provides associative link for a candidate mechanistic axis-SLC31A2-mediated cuproptosis in M1-like macrophage-that potentially links physical inactivity to vascular rarefaction in sarcopenia. These findings offer a new framework for investigating the immune-vascular crosstalk in muscle aging and highlight potential therapeutic targets for intervention.
records.authors: Li S, Wu X, Jia R, Liu J, Jia C, Deng L, Xue Q, Li X, Cong F, Wang S, Wei Y, Wang J.

records.title: Bridging HRMS spectra and anti-Staphylococcus aureus activity by machine learning for prioritization of putative antibacterial contaminants in wastewater.
records.abstract: Antibacterial contaminants are an increasing environmental and public health concern, yet prioritizing compounds with potential antibacterial activity in wastewater remains challenging. We developed machine learning models linking MS/MS-derived probabilistic fingerprints to activity against Staphylococcus aureus, enabling activity-guided prioritization before structural elucidation. Among 36 machine learning and deep learning configurations across different algorithms and fingerprint representations, MLP_PubChem and XGBoost_PubChem achieved the highest observed test F1 scores in positive- and negative-ion modes, respectively (0.48 and 0.42; AUROC, 0.84 for both). SHAP analysis examined feature contributions in positive-ion RF_Both and negative-ion XGBoost_PubChem. For wastewater screening, positive-ion MLP_Both (test F1, 0.475; AUROC, 0.847) and negative-ion XGBoost_PubChem prioritized 89 of 3797 successfully scored features, reducing the immediate follow-up list by 97.66%. Database searches yielded 39 candidate annotations for structural investigation. Retrospective screening identified MS/MS matches to prioritized candidate features in public wastewater datasets from multiple geographical regions. A web application is available at https://huggingface.co/spaces/dgfhdu/P-A to support candidate screening. By focusing structural elucidation on features with predicted anti-S. aureus activity, this workflow supports non-targeted screening guided by biological activity.
records.authors: Feng S, Li S, Shi X, Ying M, Ji M, Lou J, Yan X, Wu G, Zhang XX.

records.title: Multi-omics integration identifies core genes, molecular subtypes, and IDI1-centered immune microenvironment mechanisms in coronary artery disease.
records.abstract: BackgroundCoronary artery disease (CAD) is the leading cause of death worldwide, but its molecular mechanisms remain unclear.MethodsWe integrated transcriptomic datasets (GSE113079, GSE98583, GSE71226) and single-cell RNA sequencing data (GSE159677) from GEO. Differential expression analysis, WGCNA, machine learning, molecular clustering, immune infiltration analysis, CellChat, in silico knockout, and PheWAS were applied to investigate CAD-related molecular networks.ResultsWe identified 99 DEGs and the MEturquoise module as a CAD-associated module. Machine learning initially identified four candidate genes (RC3H1, IDI1, RAB2A, and SIRPB2); however, only IDI1 was retained after external validation and single-cell intersection. Single-cell analysis revealed macrophage expansion and specific IDI1 enrichment in Cycling cells and immune populations. CAD was classified into two molecular subtypes with distinct immune profiles. Cell communication analysis identified SPP1, TNF, CCL, and MIF pathways as key inflammatory regulators. Virtual knockout simulation of IDI1 affected hemostasis, Toll-like receptor signaling, and collagen degradation pathways. PheWAS showed no significant phenotype-wide associations for IDI1.ConclusionThis study identified IDI1 as a CAD-associated candidate gene, revealed immune-based molecular subtypes of CAD, and suggested that IDI1 and inflammatory signaling pathways may serve as potential therapeutic targets, providing insights into precision classification and targeted therapy for CAD.
records.authors: Sun Q, Zhou Z, Liang S, Yang H, Wu A.

records.title: Molecular mechanisms underlying plant adaptation to low potassium stress.
records.abstract: Potassium (K+) is an essential macronutrient and the most abundant inorganic cation in plant cells. Efficient acquisition, allocation, and homeostatic maintenance of K+ are critical for plant growth, development, and stress tolerance. However, K+ availability in soils is often limited and highly variable, necessitating sophisticated adaptive mechanisms to maintain K+ homeostasis under Low K+ (LK) stress. Over the past decade, substantial progress has been made in dissecting the molecular regulatory networks that govern plant responses to LK stress. Here, we review recent advances in the two central K+ uptake systems, the Shaker-type channel Arabidopsis K+ Transporter 1 (AKT1) and High-Affinity K+ Transporter 5 (HAK5). We further summarize the CBL-CIPK calcium-signaling network as a central hub for decoding LK signals. It operates through sequential activation of a tonoplast-localized CBL2/3-CIPK module and a plasma membrane-localized CBL1/9-CIPK23 module. This temporal ordering is supported by the earlier activation of the tonoplast module, which is itself required for the full activation of the plasma membrane module. We highlight its newly discovered antagonistic crosstalk with the target of rapamycin complex (TORC) growth pathway, which couples K+ status to the balance between growth and stress adaptation. We further present an expanding transcriptional regulatory network, with particular attention to the functional roles of newly identified transcription factors in modulating LK responses. We also discuss conserved and distinct regulatory mechanisms characterized in major cereal and economic crops. Together, these post-translational and transcriptional mechanisms clarify how plants sense and adapt to potassium deficiency, and offer theoretical guidance and candidate genetic targets for breeding potassium-efficient crop varieties.

records.title: The Good, the Bad, the Ugly (and the Blind): The Role of Aryl Hydrocarbon Receptor in Health and Disease
records.abstract: Chronic inflammation and subfertility converge on a number of ligand-dependent transcription factors induced by chemically heterogeneous environmental exposures. Foremost among them is the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR), of the basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH)–PER-ARNT-SIM (PAS) superfamily. Identified first as the receptor for dioxins and long regarded as a mediator of xenobiotic toxicity, AhR is now established as a regulator of physiological homeostasis, responding to microbial, dietary, phytochemical substances and endogenously generated metabolites. In this review, we examine AhR ligands and the transcriptional programmes they elicit, organising the evidence around one distinction: whether a ligand is a substrate for the cytochrome P450 enzymes it induces, and therefore self-limiting, or whether it persists and converts a single exposure into a chronic stimulus. We follow the receptor through the gastrointestinal tract, skin and adipose tissue; through the eye, where biallelic loss-of-function genetic variants cause foveal hypoplasia and retinitis pigmentosa and through the reproductive axis, where AhR sets ovarian aromatase expression, follicular recruitment, spermatogenesis and trophoblast invasion. Spanning the good, the bad, the ugly and the blind, we argue that therapeutic progress depends not on deciding whether to activate or inhibit AhR, but on confining modulation to a defined tissue, ligand residence time and transcriptional output.
records.authors: Semerikova T, Dakhnevich A, Aftabsavad S, Galieva A, Egorov AD.

records.title: Multiscale and physically consistent multitask learning for protein melting temperature prediction.
records.abstract: Protein thermal stability determines the functional viability of proteins in industrial and biomedical applications. We developed an Evolutionary Scale Modeling Cambrian-based multiscale multitask predictor for protein melting temperature (ESMTmP). The model leverages a frozen 300-million-parameter Cambrian encoder to extract residue representations. These features are refined by residual temporal convolutions. Furthermore, global statistical pooling, local multiscale convolutions, and multi-head attention are integrated through residual gated fusion. This framework unifies adaptive representation learning with continuous temperature regression and ordered multi-threshold classification. It also introduces monotonicity regularization to encourage order-consistent probability outputs. The model was trained on 30,076 observations and evaluated on 531 exact-identity-separated held-out proteins. ESMTmP achieved a root mean square error (RMSE) of 7.42 °C and a mean absolute error of 5.64 °C. Additionally, the coefficient of determination reached 0.8112 with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.9014. Compared with an encoder baseline, the RMSE decreased from 7.87 to 7.42 °C. Multitask learning further reduced this error from 7.61 to 7.42 °C relative to a regression-only variant, demonstrating that auxiliary supervision effectively limits large prediction errors. Across five temperature thresholds from 40 to 80 °C, the mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve reached 0.9462. The mean F1 score was 0.8663 with no monotonicity violations. ESMTmP provides monotonically ordered predictions to efficiently prioritize thermostable protein engineering candidates prior to experimental screening.Supplementary informationThe online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13205-026-05122-1.
records.authors: Min R, Lin C, Teng X, Zhang D, Li C, Yi X, Wang X.

records.title: Polyphenol supplementation and skeletal muscle health in older adults: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials.
records.abstract: Sarcopenia is a progressive age-related skeletal muscle disorder characterized by the decline of muscle mass and function, driven by mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and chronic low-grade inflammation. Polyphenols have been proposed as candidate modulators of these pathways on mechanistic and preclinical grounds, but whether this plausibility translates into measurable structural and functional benefit in clinical trials remains unresolved. A systematic review following PRISMA 2020 guidelines and the Cochrane Handbook (PROSPERO CRD420251183284) was conducted. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials evaluating polyphenol supplementation in adults aged ≥ 55 years for outcomes related to skeletal muscle mass, strength, or physical function. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool, and because a formal meta-analysis was not feasible given the small number of trials and substantial clinical heterogeneity, effect estimates and measures of uncertainty were tabulated alongside a structured direction-of-effect synthesis, following recommended practice for reviews that cannot pool data quantitatively. Six randomized controlled trials were identified; five had reported outcome data and were included in the synthesis, while a sixth remains an ongoing registered protocol with no results yet available and is reported separately. Interventions included quercetin, epicatechin-rich extracts, tea catechins, cocoa flavonoids, and marine-derived polyphenols, with durations ranging from 4 to 24 weeks among completed trials. Muscle strength improved significantly on between-group comparison in two of five completed trials; effects on muscle mass were inconsistent, with one trial showing a significant group-by-time interaction under a combined polyphenol, amino-acid, and exercise intervention, another showing an attenuated loss without a significant between-group difference, and others showing null or less clearly attributable effects; functional and balance outcomes improved in two of three trials that assessed them. Polyphenol supplementation shows biologically plausible but currently inconsistent effects on skeletal muscle outcomes in older adults; the evidence base remains too small, heterogeneous, and methodologically limited to support therapeutic recommendations. Larger, standardized randomized trials in populations with confirmed sarcopenia, incorporating direct neuromuscular assessment, are required before clinical translation.
records.authors: Diaz-Vallejo JA, Gonzalez-Correa CH, Padilla CJ.

records.title: Transcriptomic convergence and the female protective effect in autism.
records.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is highly heritable, and mutations in hundreds of genes have been implicated as individually rare causes of ASD1-3. Understanding how disruptions to these functionally diverse genes lead to the core features of ASD remains a major challenge4. Moreover, ASD is three- to four-fold more common in male than in female individuals5, and female autistic people tend to carry more autosomal risk alleles for ASD compared with their male counterparts6,7; however, the biological basis of this 'female protective effect' (FPE) has remained unknown8,9. Here we show that individual perturbations of 18 ASD genes in human neural progenitor cells converge on shared effects on gene expression, including widespread downregulation of other ASD genes. De novo reconstruction of a gene regulatory network enabled identification of central transcriptional regulators that drive this transcriptomic convergence, including prominent ASD gene CHD8 and candidates including REST. Furthermore, X-linked transcription factor ZFX, which is expressed from both the active and the inactive X chromosomes in female individuals10, emerged as a key activator of many ASD genes: we propose that the higher ZFX expression level observed in the female brain can buffer damaging mutations in diverse ASD genes, contributing to the female protective effect. Together, these results show how key gene regulatory networks can become broadly and similarly dysregulated upon disruption of individual ASD genes and provide molecular insight into the female protective effect in ASD.
records.authors: Andersen RE, Talukdar M, Sakamoto T, Exposito-Alonso D, Song JHT, Qian X, Lee S, Murugan N, Delgado RN, Zhao S, Eichfeld G, Harms J, Page DC, Walsh CA.

records.title: Recent developments in downstream processing of novel biotherapeutic modalities.
records.abstract: There is rising interest in the biopharma industry in exploring next-generation complex therapeutic modalities that offer unique advantages over their traditional counterparts. These include antibody-drug conjugates, nucleic acid-based therapeutics (plasmid DNA and messenger RNA), virus-like particles, adeno-associated virus (AAV)-based gene therapies, and monoclonal antibody (mAb) derivatives such as bispecific antibodies, nanobodies, and antibody fragments. Each of these moieties displays distinct structural, physicochemical, and functional attributes that translate to unique manufacturing challenges. This review showcases major developments over the last 5 years in downstream processing of these next-generation therapeutics, such as chromatographic and nonchromatographic separation strategies, process intensification, and automation and process control. Overall, these advancements indicate that the purification of such biotherapeutics requires an appropriate separation process tailored to modality-specific physicochemical characteristics and cannot be derived from mAb manufacturing expertise; this will be crucial for their scalability and cost-effectiveness.
records.authors: Rathore AS, Metya S, Yadav P.

records.title: Endothelial HIF-2α/TFPI signaling contributes to coagulation dysfunction and neurological deficits after traumatic brain injury.
records.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI)-associated coagulopathy is a life-threatening complication characterized by systemic coagulation dysfunction and increased mortality; however, the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated the potential role of hypoxia-inducible factor-2α (HIF-2α) in endothelial dysfunction and tissue factor pathway inhibitor (TFPI)-associated coagulation imbalance during TBI-associated coagulopathy. Building on our previous transcriptomic analysis identifying TFPI upregulation in trauma-induced coagulopathy, we further explored its upstream regulatory mechanism in a rat TBI model. Notably, integrative analysis revealed partial overlap between the transcriptomic profiles of rat injured cortex and clinical whole-blood samples, both highlighting dysregulated coagulation pathways and converging on TFPI as a key candidate. TBI-induced coagulopathy was characterized by coagulation dysfunction, accompanied by decreased endothelial HIF-2α protein stability associated with calpain activation, with concomitant upregulation of TFPI in cortical tissue. In cultured HUVECs, TNF-α combined with hypoxia/reoxygenation stress induced endothelial HIF-2α protein suppression and TFPI upregulation. Pharmacological stabilization of HIF-2α using dimethyloxalylglycine (DMOG) partially restored coagulation parameters in vivo and attenuated TFPI induction under stress conditions. Mechanistically, structural prediction analysis identified a potential interaction between HIF-2α and the HRE-containing region of the TFPI promoter. Chromatin immunoprecipitation assays further supported the association of HIF-2α with this promoter region. Moreover, AAV-mediated TFPI overexpression partially reversed the protective effects of DMOG-mediated HIF-2α stabilization on coagulation and neurological outcomes. Collectively, these findings suggest that HIF-2α may be involved in the transcriptional regulation of TFPI in endothelial cells under early TBI-associated stress conditions and may contribute to coagulation dysfunction following TBI. This pathway may provide a potential link between endothelial stress responses and trauma-induced coagulopathy.

records.title: Beyond M1/M2 dichotomy: Toward an operationally defined, modular framework for macrophage functional states.
records.abstract: Macrophages are versatile immune cells involved in tissue homeostasis, host defense, inflammation, and disease progression. Their biology has traditionally been interpreted through the M1/M2 paradigm, but single-cell and spatial profiling, lineage tracing, and multi-omics reveal substantially greater heterogeneity. This review organizes macrophage diversity around recurring functional programs: immunosuppressive/regulatory, matrix-remodeling, hypoxia-associated metabolic, IFN-responsive/antigen-presenting, and proliferative. Angiogenic/perivascular activity is treated as a putative program because its status as a distinct transcriptional entity remains uncertain. We introduce an operational framework based on three criteria-co-expression coherence, combinatorial independence, and microenvironmental inducibility-to distinguish candidate functional modules from broader programs. We also conduct an evidence-weighted assessment of these programs, examining their independent variation, contextual coupling, and co-occurrence. Furthermore, we propose a Macrophage Dominance Index (MDI) as a hypothesis-generating numerical framework, with provisional marker sets, weighting, and formula requiring independent validation. Finally, we derive falsifiable predictions and outline experimental, single-cell, spatial, and clinical strategies to test relationships among programs. Overall, available evidence suggests substantial coupling among macrophage functional programs rather than uniformly independent functional axes. Macrophage heterogeneity is therefore better understood as context-dependent combinations of programs, some of which remain unconfirmed as distinct transcriptional modules. Although the framework may inform macrophage biology broadly, most supporting evidence, particularly concerning program relationships, biomarkers, prognosis, and therapeutic implications, derives from tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs). Its applicability to non-cancer settings remains to be established. The MDI and proposed predictions are intended to facilitate testable research, not to serve as validated diagnostic, prognostic, or therapeutic tools.
records.authors: Jafari A, Vazifedust S, Harmileh KM, Karbasi F, Mazloomi E.

records.title: Decoding the role of ADAptor2 (ADA2) of HAT complex in autophagy and phospholipid metabolism to maintain ER homeostasis and triterpene regulation.
records.abstract: In yeast, transcriptional adaptor 2 (ADA2; SAGA complex subunit ADA2), a member of histone acetyltransferase (HAT) complex, regulates transcription through cell signalling, but its precise role in cellular metabolism remains unclear. In this study, genetic loss of ADA2 (ada2Δ) induces squalene (SQ) accumulation, indicating aberrant triterpene metabolism, coupled with endoplasmic reticulum (ER)/nuclear ER (nER) expansion. Lipid analyses of ada2Δ revealed elevated phosphatidic acid (PA) and phosphatidylcholine (PC) levels, indicating disrupted phospholipid metabolism. The expanded ER causes basal autophagy elevation, cellular recycling, and nER phagy, suggesting a regulatory role for ADA2 in autophagy. Downregulation of phosphatidate cytidylyltransferase (CDS1) and inositol-3-phosphate synthase (INO1), coupled with elevated PA and PC in ada2Δ, points to a significant disruption in cytidine-diphosphate-diacylglycerol and phosphatidylinositol pathway. Overexpression of CDS1 or INO1, or the inositol supplementation, in ada2Δ restores SQ, basal autophagy and ER phagy. The observed target of rapamycin Ser/Thr kinase complex (TORC1) activity in ada2Δ is due to the high PA content. Rapamycin-mediated inhibition of TORC1 reduced SQ, PA and ER expansion while increasing lipid droplets. In contrast, a rapamycin-treated ada2Δpah1Δ strain retained high PA, SQ and ER expansion, underscoring the functional role of TORC1-nuclear envelope morphology protein 1 (Nem1)/sporulation-specific protein SPO7 (Spo7)-Pah1 axis. Notably, SQ levels remained unchanged in a rapamycin-treated ada2Δatg39Δ strain, suggesting that loss of nER-phagy receptor, Atg39, impairs the effectiveness of TORC1 inhibition. In conclusion, our data unveiled a critical role for Ada2 in maintaining the intricate relationship between lipid and triterpene/sterol metabolism and connecting autophagy and ER homeostasis.
records.authors: Rathore A, Priya BG, Nawada NN, Shashank DV, Rao MJ, Anbarasu M, Manjithaya R, Tiwari AK, Ratnasekhar CH, Venkata Rao DK.

records.title: Targeting P23 by PM534 suppresses glioblastoma via disruption of SFPQ-mediated phase separation.
records.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is one of the most lethal human malignancies, with a five-year survival rate of approximately 5% and limited effective therapeutic options beyond standard-of-care regimens, underscoring an urgent need for novel therapeutic agents and druggable targets. Here, we report that PM534, a marine sponge-derived synthetic compound, potently suppresses GBM malignancy in orthotopic patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models and in vitro, with IC50 value of 1.86 nM in patient-derived GBM#P3 cells. Target identification via activity-based protein profiling (ABPP) revealed P23, a co-chaperone of HSP90, as the direct molecular target of PM534. Subsequent LC-MS/MS analysis, molecular dynamics simulation, and site-directed mutagenesis collectively demonstrated that PM534 covalently bond P23 at Cys58 and Cys75. P23 demonstrated significant upregulation in human GBM tissues and orthotopic PDX models, correlating with tumor progression. Mechanistic studies exhibited that P23 interacted with splicing factor proline- and glutamine-rich protein (SFPQ) to regulate liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS). Covalent engagement of P23 by PM534 disrupted the interaction of SFPQ with the HSP90/P23 complex, thereby triggering proteasomal degradation of SFPQ and consequently abrogating SFPQ-driven LLPS and oncogenic condensate formation. These findings establish PM534 as a promising drug candidate for clinical GBM therapy and highlight P23 as a therapeutic target in GBM.
records.authors: Lu X, Wang H, Zhang A, Zhang Q, Cao Q, Hou C, Li Z, Guo C, Li P, Fu Y, Chen A.

records.title: A Novel Drp1-Golph2 Tether Mediates Mitochondria-Golgi Spatial Association to Orchestrate Mitochondrial Function and Hepatic Lipid Catabolism Across Vertebrates.
records.abstract: Mitochondria-organelle contact sites are fundamental to cellular homeostasis; however, the molecular mechanisms and physiological significance of mitochondria-Golgi spatial communication remain elusive. To address this, we employed a cross-species approach using hepatocyte models from humans, mice, chickens, and frogs, combined with in vivo and in vitro studies in grass carp fed diets with varying lipid and chlorogenic acid (CGA). This strategy enabled us to systematically delineate the molecular machinery governing mitochondria-Golgi coupling and its role in hepatic lipid metabolism. The key findings were: (1) A candidate cross-species functional module: We identify a novel spatial association between mitochondria and the Golgi apparatus, formed by a direct protein-protein interaction between dynamin-1-like protein (Drp1) (via Leu639) and golgi membrane protein 1 (Golph2). Although Drp1 Leu639 is highly conserved across vertebrates, the corresponding Golph2 interacting site exhibits substantial sequence divergence among species, and this module exhibits functional conservation rather than sequence conservation. (2) A mechanistic link between structure and metabolism: This Drp1/Golph2-mediated mitochondria-Golgi spatial association serves as a critical regulatory node, where its disruption impairs Drp1 phosphorylation and mitochondrial fission, leading to enhanced mitochondrial β-oxidation and altered hepatic lipid metabolism. (3) A nutri-physiological regulatory axis: The nutritional compound CGA alleviates hepatic steatosis by transcriptionally downregulating Drp1 via a peroxisome proliferator activated receptor gamma (pparγ)-binding promoter element, thereby normalizing excessive mitochondria-Golgi juxtaposition. Significantly, this study reveals that Drp1/Golph2-mediated mitochondria-Golgi spatial association represents a regulatory axis with functionally conserved outputs from fish to mammals, establishing this complex as both a fundamental coordinator of mitochondrial dynamics and a promising target for treating hepatic lipid disorders.
records.authors: Feng GL, Hu NJ, Chi YJ, Zheng FF, Song YF.

records.title: Diet-independent pregravid obesity drives premature but functionally dysregulated fetal immune maturation across multiple immune compartments in rhesus macaques.
records.abstract: Pregravid obesity is associated with long-term immune alterations in offspring, but the mechanisms linking maternal metabolic state to fetal immune development remain poorly defined. To address this gap, we used a rhesus macaque model of spontaneous, diet-independent pregravid obesity to examine impact of pregravid obesity on fetal immune maturation and function. We profiled immune cell frequency, function, transcriptional programs, and inferred intercellular communication in umbilical cord blood, fetal spleen, and fetal lung using spectral flow cytometry, multiplex cytokine profiling, functional stimulation assays, and single-cell RNA sequencing. Pregravid obesity was associated with altered fetal organ growth, elevated inflammatory mediators, altered immune cell frequencies, and hyperresponsive splenic leukocyte responses to in vitro stimulation. Single-cell transcriptomic analyses revealed a conserved program of innate immune reprogramming across all three compartments, characterized by heightened inflammatory, migratory, and metabolic signatures together with reduced antigen-presentation potential. We also observed impaired T cell maturation with premature effector differentiation and evidence of B cell dysfunction. Computationally inferred cell-cell communication predicted loss of tolerogenic signaling and enhanced proinflammatory pathways across splenic and lung myeloid cells. Together, these findings indicate that diet-independent pregravid obesity drives premature but functionally dysregulated maturation of fetal circulating and tissue-resident immune cells, providing a candidate mechanism for the increased susceptibility to infection, respiratory disease, and immune dysregulation reported in offspring of mothers with obesity. This connection should be tested directly in postnatal studies.
records.authors: Doratt BM, Wagner S, Avila U, Hodge T, Martin LD, Varlamov O, Messaoudi I.

records.title: Integrative transcriptomic and single-cell analysis identifies a manganese-associated transcriptional signature and a potential JUN/HBEGF-associated endothelial signature in COPD pulmonary vascular remodeling.
records.abstract: BackgroundChronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a heterogeneous respiratory disease involving airway inflammation, emphysema, and pulmonary vascular remodeling. Manganese exposure has been linked to pulmonary inflammation and oxidative stress, but its molecular association with COPD vascular pathology remains unclear. This study explored a manganese-associated transcriptional signature in COPD and investigated its potential relationship with endothelial cell dysfunction and vascular remodeling.MethodsBulk transcriptomic datasets were used to calculate a manganese-related transcriptional score, identify differentially expressed genes, and characterize WGCNA modules. Manganese-COPD-associated genes were obtained by intersecting manganese-related genes, COPD differentially expressed genes, and manganese-associated module genes. Functional enrichment, PPI analysis, machine-learning-based feature selection, diagnostic modeling, and consensus clustering were performed. Single-cell RNA sequencing data were analyzed to characterize HBEGF expression, endothelial subpopulations, CytoTRACE2 scores, pseudotime dynamics, transcription factor activity, cell-cell communication, and NicheNet ligand-target relationships.ResultsCOPD samples showed significantly higher manganese-related transcriptional scores. A total of 43 manganese-COPD-associated candidate genes were identified and were enriched mainly in pathways related to inflammation, cytokines, immune chemotaxis, and vascular processes. Machine learning identified 14 core diagnostic genes, and the combined model showed good classification performance in the training and validation cohorts. Among these genes, HBEGF showed the highest contribution in the ElasticNet model and was prioritized for downstream analysis. Consensus clustering divided COPD samples into two molecular subtypes with distinct manganese-related scores and functional features. Single-cell analysis suggested that HBEGF was closely associated with endothelial cell alterations, especially venous endothelial cells. Pseudotime and transcription factor analyses suggested a potential JUN/HBEGF regulatory relationship. CellChat and NicheNet analyses further indicated that venous endothelial cell-derived HBEGF may participate in endothelial-smooth muscle cell communication.ConclusionThis study identified an elevated manganese-related transcriptional score in COPD and prioritized HBEGF as a key candidate associated with venous endothelial cell state changes and endothelial-smooth muscle communication. These findings suggest a potential JUN/HBEGF-associated endothelial signature relevant to COPD pulmonary vascular remodeling, which warrants further experimental validation.

records.title: Urinary oxidative DEHP metabolites and advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: Evidence from NHANES and mechanistic insights into MECPP-related macrophage inflammatory-glycolytic activation.
records.abstract: BackgroundPhthalates are ubiquitous environmental contaminants, yet their relevance to advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome remains unclear. We examined the associations between urinary phthalate metabolites and advanced CKM syndrome, and explored the potential mechanisms linking di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP)-related exposure to macrophage inflammatory-glycolytic activation.MethodsWe analyzed 4236 adults from seven cycles (2005-2018) of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). A total of ten urinary phthalate metabolites were quantified, and advanced CKM syndrome was defined as CKM stages 3-4 using an NHANES-adapted American Heart Association framework. Survey-weighted logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, and weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression were used to assess single-metabolite, dose-response, and mixture associations. Mono(2-ethyl-5-carboxypentyl) phthalate (MECPP) was further evaluated using network toxicology, molecular docking, Mendelian randomization, single-cell RNA sequencing, and macrophage reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR).ResultsAmong 4236 participants, 648 had advanced CKM syndrome. In fully adjusted models, oxidative DEHP metabolites were positively associated with advanced CKM syndrome. Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest quartile was associated with higher odds for mono(2-ethyl-5-oxohexyl) phthalate (MEOHP; odds ratio [OR], 1.64; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.12-2.42), mono(2-ethyl-5-hydroxyhexyl) phthalate (MEHHP; OR, 1.60; 95% CI, 1.05-2.42), and MECPP (OR, 1.84; 95% CI, 1.26-2.68), with significant trends. Restricted cubic spline analyses suggested non-linear associations. WQS regression indicated a positive mixture association, with MECPP receiving the highest weight. Network toxicology identified 33 overlapping genes enriched in pathways related to the renin-angiotensin system, insulin resistance, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor signaling, and diabetic cardiomyopathy. Among the candidate hub genes, tumor necrosis factor (TNF) and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARG) were further examined using molecular docking and Mendelian randomization. Single-cell analyses of public mouse heart and kidney datasets localized Tnf mainly to macrophages and Pparg to cardiac endothelial cells and renal monocytes. In RAW 264.7 macrophages, MECPP potentiated palmitic acid-induced expression of inflammatory and glycolysis-related genes.ConclusionsUrinary oxidative DEHP metabolites, particularly MECPP, were positively associated with advanced CKM syndrome in US adults. These findings support MECPP as a potential biomarker of DEHP-related exposure and generate mechanistic hypotheses involving macrophage-centered inflammatory and glycolytic transcriptional activation. Prospective and experimental studies are warranted to clarify causality and to determine whether DEHP-related exposure contributes to the development and progression of CKM syndrome.
records.authors: Liang L, Su S, Niu Q, Rao K, Zhang Y, Chen N, Wang L, Chen Y, Yao P.

records.title: Dinotefuran aggravates Alzheimer's disease-associated microglial inflammation through the CHUK/NFKB1-mediated NF-κB signaling pathway.
records.abstract: Neonicotinoid pesticides are widely used systemic insecticides with increasing evidence of neurotoxicity. However, their potential contribution to Alzheimer's disease (AD)-related neuroinflammation remains poorly understood. In this study, seven representative neonicotinoid pesticides were systematically evaluated by integrating physicochemical characterization, target prediction, pathway enrichment analysis, human AD snRNA-seq, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and experimental validation. Among the seven compounds, dinotefuran was prioritized based on its favorable blood-brain barrier permeability and enrichment in inflammation-related pathways. Integration of target prediction with AD transcriptomic analyses identified CHUK and NFKB1 as key candidate targets associated with NF-κB signaling. snRNA-seq analysis further demonstrated preferential enrichment of NF-κB signaling activity in microglia from AD brains. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations supported potential interactions between dinotefuran and IKKα (CHUK) as well as NF-κB1 (p50). In Aβ-treated BV2 microglia, dinotefuran further enhanced activation of the CHUK/NFKB1-mediated NF-κB signaling pathway, accompanied by increased expression of IKKα, phosphorylation of IκBα and p65, enhanced NF-κB1 activation, and elevated secretion of IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6, IFN-α, and IFN-β. These pro-inflammatory effects were markedly attenuated by the NF-κB inhibitor BAY11-7082. Collectively, our findings suggest that CHUK/NFKB1-associated NF-κB signaling may contribute to dinotefuran-enhanced inflammatory responses in Aβ-treated BV2 microglia, providing preliminary mechanistic insights into the potential involvement of neonicotinoid pesticides in AD-related neuroinflammation.

records.title: Migraine-driven causal genes in ischemic stroke.
records.abstract: Migraine, most notably migraine with aura, elevates the risk of ischaemic stroke, though the underlying causal molecular connections have not been fully elucidated. This study sought to uncover migraine-associated causal genes that confer susceptibility to ischaemic stroke and to dissect their cell-type-specific functional mechanisms operating within the neurovascular unit. We combined publicly available human transcriptomic resources, genetics-driven causal inference, machine-learning-assisted biomarker screening, mouse-derived single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlases, immune-cell deconvolution, and in-silico molecular docking. Twenty migraine-related genes were detected with causal associations to ischaemic-stroke risk. We prioritised three consensus hub genes: CD79A, PKN2, and PRKDC. In stroke patients, CD79A was significantly downregulated, while PKN2 and PRKDC exhibited elevated expression; their reliable diagnostic capacity was further confirmed in an independent external cohort. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic profiling mapped these hub genes to endothelial, myeloid and glial cell populations residing within a dynamic inflammatory-vascular pathological niche in mouse ischaemic brain lesions. Mechanistic analyses pointed to perturbed mitochondrial energy homeostasis and dysregulated adaptive immune responses as downstream consequences modulated by these hub genes. Molecular-docking simulations demonstrated high-affinity interactions between Tamibarotene, Dirithromycin and the three encoded hub proteins, highlighting these compounds as promising candidates for drug repurposing. Collectively, our multi-omics analysis pinpoints CD79A, PKN2 and PRKDC as migraine-derived causal targets for ischaemic stroke, delivers cell- and spatial-resolved mechanistic perspectives on neurovascular-unit injury, and puts forward lead compounds awaiting further pre-clinical validation.

records.title: Biological Signaling Pathways Associated with Late Tendon Development in Chicken Embryos and Their Dependence on Mechanical Stimulation
records.abstract: During embryonic and neonatal development, tendons exhibit rapid changes in mechanics and structure, including increases in collagen content, crosslinking, and fibril length. These functional and structural changes are partly dependent on mechanical stimulation. However, the specific mechanobiological mechanisms driving these changes remain poorly understood. The objective of this study was to identify the potential biological mechanisms and pathways driving tendon maturation into load-bearing materials using an embryonic chick model. Using bulk RNA sequencing, gene set enrichment analysis, and transcription factor analysis, we produced a transcriptomic profile of chick hindlimb tendons during late embryonic development (E16, E18, and E20) and tendons from rigid and flaccid paralysis-treated embryos. Additionally, we assessed the results from two differential expression analysis models to improve the replicability of our findings. Our results suggest that the largest transcriptomic response occurs between embryonic day 16 and 20, and that among paralysis conditions, rigid paralysis produces the greatest effect relative to controls. Across development, we found positive enrichment in processes related to mechanotransduction, extracellular matrix remodeling, cell adhesion, and contractility, and identified candidate pathways upregulated with development, including TGF-β, PI3K-AKT-mTOR, Hippo, circadian rhythm, and focal adhesion signaling. In paralysis-treated embryos, our data suggest impairment in extracellular matrix remodeling and mechanotransduction events. Specifically, we found that both modes of paralysis are associated with a cellular stress response and downregulation of WNT signaling. Together, our findings identify candidate mechanotransduction pathways that are associated with late tendon maturation and altered by paralysis, which may inform tendon tissue engineering and regenerative approaches.

records.title: Chronic Sleep Disruption Activates the Transcriptional Unfolded Protein Response and Induces Compartment-Specific Proteomic Changes in Mice
records.abstract: ABSTRACT  Sleep disruption (SD) is associated with adverse brain health and increased risk of dementia, including Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet the pathological mechanisms underlying this association are not fully understood. Preclinical studies have shown that acute SD impairs cognition by altering vulnerable synapses (molecular composition, ultrastructure, and function). However, the cumulative effects of chronic SD on the adult brain and its vulnerable synapses, that might contribute to AD risk, remain poorly defined. Here, we investigated the impact of chronic SD on brain transcriptomic signatures and subcellular compartment-specific proteomic profiles to identify genes, proteins, and signaling pathways that might confer AD risk. Chronic SD induced a modest transcriptional stress response globally, whereas alterations were more pronounced in the synaptosomal (synapse-enriched P2 fractions) and whole-brain proteomes. Remarkably, chronic SD elicited unique proteomic alterations at the synaptic compartment were distinct from whole-brain effects, including increased proteins involved in synaptic vesicle endocytosis, regulation of dendritic spine morphogenesis, and regulation of long-term synaptic depression, compared to increased proteins involved in immune/inflammatory, glial responses and neuronal function at the whole-brain level. Consistent with the chronic SD-induced molecular signatures, we observed subtle ultrastructural changes in vulnerable CA1 hippocampal synapses, including reduced pre-synapse size and decreased synaptic vesicle density, which suggest that chronic SD modifies synaptic transmission and plasticity. Together, our findings indicate that chronic SD differentially impacts the brain and the synaptic proteome, nominating candidate therapeutic targets and signaling pathways for future mechanistic studies of chronic SD and how SD contributes to increased AD risk. Highlights  Brain transcriptomics reveals chronic SD activates the unfolded protein response. Compartment-specific proteomics shows chronic SD drives unique compensatory changes. Chronic SD subtly alters the ultrastructure of vulnerable hippocampal CA1 synapses. We nominate candidate pathways that link effects of chronic SD to AD risk.

records.title: Cellular composition and the interpretation of candidate RNA readouts of trogocytosis in colorectal cancer
records.abstract: Background  RNA measurements of genes associated with trogocytosis may reflect cellular composition rather than contact-dependent membrane acquisition. We evaluated an eight-gene candidate module in colorectal cancer (CRC) using expression- and lineage-matched random modules, independent compartment analysis and patient-level inference. A separate rare-transcript definition and cancer-model fitness screens provided complementary analyses. Results  In 62 GSE178341 patients, the module correlated with T-cell fraction (ρ=0.767), but this association was typical of 10,000 matched modules (null median 0.766; one-sided empirical P=0.493; equal-tail two-sided P=0.985). A post hoc closest-10% matching sensitivity gave P=0.571. In 23 independent GSE132465 patients, the tumour-wide correlation was 0.735 (permutation P=0.00060) and the epithelial correlation was 0.376 (P=0.0892). The difference in absolute correlations was 0.359, with a 95% confidence interval of −0.041 to 0.759, leaving attenuation uncertain. Among 43,817 leukocytes, 16  CEACAM5 -positive candidates arose from four patients; 15 had expression ≤2 transcripts per million. Candidate counts were threshold-sensitive. No survival association was detected for the module in two cohorts.  SCD fitness dependency reproduced across CRC organoids and cell lines, whereas adjusted  SCD –  VPS72 and exploratory  ATF3 –  SMYD2 co-dependencies did not. Exploratory  CH25H ,  ATF3 and  FADS2 analyses yielded no Hallmark enrichment meeting the multiple-testing threshold.  Conclusions  Matched-module calibration placed the strong association with T-cell abundance within the range expected for comparable immune-lineage genes. Independent compartment analysis was consistent with a contribution from cellular composition, although attenuation remained uncertain. These results identify the comparison conditions needed to interpret the tested RNA readouts. Linking them to membrane transfer requires event-resolved protein measurements.
