records.title: GOParsimony  : parsimonious saltation across the Gene Ontology digraph for efficient functional annotation
records.abstract: Background  The Gene Ontology (GO) is standardly probed by biological researchers keen to discern the functional tendencies of their gene/protein data sets. However, lists of GO terms are often ontically overwhelming, and need to be filtered to remove redundancy. Methods for such filtering either employ predefined lists of terms that may not actually be relevant to a specific gene/protein set, or apply arbitrary thresholds, such as for semantic distance (  i .  e ., GO term dissimilarity).  Methods  Here, I introduce the tool GOParsimony, which is designed to avoid such issues and to pick out the most parsimonious (  i .  e ., simplest, most concise) explanation for the functional tendencies of any set of proteins/genes. It achieves this by saltating across the GO digraph, assigning and updating cascades of term precedence until convergence. The set of GO terms assigned precedence = 1 is the most parsimonious set. Hierarchical clustering with other GO terms with higher precedence levels can be investigated for clues about functional modules.  Results  GO term precedence graphs and two-dimensional heatmaps of GO terms and genes/proteins are output, along with other plots that can be cross-referenced for functional insights. In test analyses for five example data sets from budding yeast and human, GOParsimony consistently produces reduced GO term lists that have greater significance and low or intermediate coverage of the space of significant GO terms, when compared to other distributed methods in default mode. GOParsimony can be obtained at:  https://github.com/pmharrison/GOParsimony .

records.title: Immersion as inference: An active inference account of induced realities and its relation to the two-competitor model
records.abstract: Immersive technologies are designed for a single target: the human perceptual system. Engineers of virtual and augmented reality have long recognized that a display does not have to replicate the physical world, it only has to provide the inputs that satisfy the senses at the level at which the brain samples them. This engineering intuition is, in fact, a statement about brain function. Here we develop it into a formal account of immersion within the active inference framework. We treat an induced reality (a virtual, augmented, or mixed reality, but also a book or a daydream) as a candidate generative model that competes with the model of the actual reality for the explanation of a shared sensorium and for the control of action. Immersion is then defined as the ensuant belief that the induced reality best explains the current sensory signals and supports the current perceived reality of the winning model, despite any break in immersion by Bayesian model switching driven by a high-precision prediction error that the induced model cannot absorb. Exogenous and endogenous attention, implemented as weights governing stream selection in our earlier two-competitor model, which treated attention as necessary but not sufficient for immersion, appear as two routes of precision allocation: likelihood precision of evolutionarily entrenched sensory events, and precision that follows the expected free energy of policies. Affect and motivation enter through the pragmatic and epistemic value of remaining in the induced reality and through the rate of change of free energy. We show that the two-competitor attentional focus vector and its angle are recovered from the active inference variables, and we reproduce the two scenarios of the original model, a rewarding and a fatiguing activity interrupted by a slamming door, in a minimal simulation. The account links presence, embodiment, cybersickness, and narrative absorption to a single quantity, and it yields concrete predictions for the psychophysiological assessment and closed-loop control of immersion. We discuss implications for neuroergonomic design in which the evolutionarily entrenched core of perception is non-negotiable while its experience-dependent periphery can be trained.
records.authors: Renz L, GauthierDickey KL, Vibell J, Francis AL, Corona-Strauss FI, Strauss DJ.

records.title: Neural dynamics become significantly faster and more nonlinear at the peak of information processing
records.abstract: The temporal scale at which neural populations preserve stimulus information is often treated as fixed, even though population activity changes rapidly during sensory processing. Whether the information-optimal scale changes within a single stimulus-evoked episode, and what determines its evolution, remains unclear. We developed Integration-Split, a decoding-based framework that estimates the time-varying temporal resolution of population spike trains. Across four visual paradigms and throughout the mouse visual hierarchy, the optimal scale contracted after stimulus onset and subsequently re-expanded. This pattern persisted across stimulus temporal frequencies and was largely absent in a hippocampal control. The optimal scale varied inversely with stimulus decodability, reaching its finest resolution when stimulus identity was most accurately decoded. Beyond this association, independently estimating the signal-noise autocorrelation balance across candidate window widths identified the window that maximized the autocorrelation-based signal-to-noise ratio, and this optimal width closely followed the Integration-Split trajectory. Consistent with these findings, stronger nonlinear predictive structure coincided with finer optimal temporal resolution, consistent with the idea that shorter integration windows are needed to preserve informative nonlinear population structure that would otherwise be attenuated by temporal averaging. To test the functional relevance of this organization, we trained a Transformer solely to decode stimulus identity, without providing the optimal temporal-scale pattern or Integration-Split outputs. Its learned attention exhibited a similar contraction-and-recovery profile, and disrupting heads with stronger correspondence produced larger decoding deficits. Together, these findings reveal a dynamically changing, information-optimal temporal scale in population coding, shaped by the evolving balance of signal and noise autocorrelation and by nonlinear population structure, and independently recapitulated in the learned attention of a Transformer trained without temporal-scale supervision.

records.title: Structural Basis for Human Milk Oligosaccharides Recognition by Evolutionarily Dominant Norovirus Genogroup II Genotypes
records.abstract: ABSTRACT  Human noroviruses are a major cause of acute gastroenteritis. Human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) contain glycan motifs similar to histo-blood group antigens and may act as soluble decoys that reduce viral attachment. However, the molecular basis of HMO recognition by the P domain of the major capsid protein VP1 of different norovirus genotypes is not fully understood. Here, we combined ligand-based and protein-based NMR experiments with X-ray crystallography to study HMO binding to the P domain of the latent GII.2, dominant GII.4 and emerging GII.17 noroviruses genotypes. Screening of 12 HMOs by STD NMR showed binding of all fucosylated HMOs to GII.4 and GII.17 and none for non-fucosylated HMOs. In contrast, GII.2 showed little or no detectable binding under the same conditions. Seven crystal structures of GII.4 or GII.17 with complexed HMOs supported fucose anchoring via five conserved residues. The remaining sugar moieties formed genotype-specific secondary interactions with an extended, shallow and solvent exposed binding surface whose shape is dictated by divergent surface loops. GII.4 recognition is mainly driven by hydrogen bonds whereas GII.17 relied more strongly on water-mediated interactions. Chemical shift perturbation from NMR titrations (CSP NMR) of GII.4 corroborated the fucose interactions and gave dissociation constants of 20-33 mM, consistent with weak and rapidly exchanging interactions. IMPORTANCE  This work highlights the potential of HMOs as decoy receptors against norovirus infections. Further, it provides structural information on the broad binding profile of P domain to support the future development of HMOs derivatives or glycan-based molecules to inhibit noroviruses attachment.

records.title: AlphaFold 3 Prediction Accuracy and Reliability across RNA Structures and Protein–RNA Interfaces
records.abstract: AlphaFold 3 (AF3) models RNA and protein–RNA complexes, but when its predictions and confidence metrics can be trusted is unclear. We evaluated AF3 on more than 1,300 protein–RNA complexes and about 270 RNA-only systems, and compared post-cutoff RNAs with pre-cutoff candidates selected by sequence and fold similarity. On structurally novel RNAs, AF3 largely preserves the protein fold, while RNA-fold and interface accuracy drop sharply with little change in predicted RNA confidence score. Input ablations show that protein alignments and templates from RNA-bound proteins govern complex assembly, whereas RNA alignments matter most for single-chain and long RNAs. The most frequent failed interface retains protein-side contacts but places an often-misfolded RNA in the wrong pose. RNA interface confidence only partly distinguishes this error from correct placements. Against CLIP-seq, SELEX and RNAcompete motifs, AF3 usually places the protein against the experimentally observed motif-bearing RNA segment, even where the interface fails, but often not in the native pose. In protein–RNA complexes released in 2026, a score combining AF3 confidence with RNA familiarity and template use ranked RNA chains with accurate folds and correctly placed interfaces better than AF3’s ranking score. records.title: Disentangling Context-Specific Alzheimer’s Disease Progression Signatures through an Explainable AI Framework
records.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) progression involves stage-dependent transcriptional changes that are often masked by dominant cellular and biological variation. Here, we present  ADVISE (Alzheimer’s Disease Variational Isolation of Signal Embeddings) , an interpretable deep generative framework designed to disentangle Braak stage-associated transcriptional signals from background biological variation through separate latent representations. Using explainable AI, ADVISE prioritizes genes and pathways contributing to the disease-specific representation. Applying ADVISE to large-scale single-nucleus RNA sequencing data from the human prefrontal cortex, we identify shared and context-specific signatures of AD progression across global, sex-specific, and cell-type-specific analyses, revealing convergent molecular programs involving synaptic transmission, HSF1-associated proteostatic stress responses, and SLIT/ROBO axon guidance. Notably, ADVISE prioritizes  ROBO2 as a progression-associated candidate in excitatory neurons. Experimental validation using CRISPR activation in hiPSC-derived excitatory neurons demonstrates that  ROBO2 activation reduces the phosphorylated Tau-to-total Tau ratio. ADVISE thus reveals context-dependent molecular signatures of AD progression and bridges human single-cell discoveries with experimental validation of candidate regulators of AD pathology.
records.authors: Li AW, Qiu W, Arian C, Young JE, Lee S.

records.title: Uncovering cross-signal interactions in single-cell and spatial omics
records.abstract: Individual cells simultaneously encode multiple biological signals in their gene expression profiles, including spatial position, circadian phase, and disease state. These signals can be entangled in complex ways, including circadian patterns that vary along disease progression and cell cycle dynamics that shift along developmental trajectories. While methods to disentangle such signals have been recently developed, characterizing the interaction itself between multicellular signals along with its effects on tissue function, localizing cellular subpopulations which exhibit signal interactions, and identifying potential candidate genes which drive such interactions, all remain major challenges. We present CRISP which characterizes signal interactions in single-cell gene expression data based on the correspondence between the multiple, probabilistic signal-specific projections of the data. Across simulations with tunable couplings and four single-cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets, CRISP recovers diverse biological signal interactions and localizes them to informative cellular subpopulations and groups of associated genes; CRISP distinguishes healthy from fibrotic liver samples and localizes the loss of zonation–position coupling to individual fibrotic hepatocytes, resolves the asymmetric coupling of TGF-  β response, EMT, and cell-cycle phase to specific cell subpopulations, and flags transcriptionally delayed hepatocytes in Plasmodium liver infection. Beyond quantifying and localizing signal interactions, CRISP can refine existing labels, uncover continuous cellular transitions and reveal condition-associated genes.
records.authors: Sasson J, Niasoff B, Karin J, Ezraty Y, Nitzan M.

records.title: Comparative Transcriptomic Analysis of Gene Expression Patterns in Neutrophils from Rheumatoid Arthritis and COVID-19
records.abstract: Background  Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disorder characterised by chronic inflammation and immune dysregulation, and neutrophils play a key role in its progression. COVID-19 also involves neutrophil hyperactivation that contributes to severe immune responses. Emerging evidence links COVID-19 to increased incidence or exacerbation of RA, potentially through overlapping immune mechanisms. Objective  To compare neutrophil transcriptomic profiles in RA and COVID-19 and identify shared immune pathways and disease-specific features. Methods  Publicly available neutrophil RNA-seq count data from the Gene Expression Omnibus were analysed: RA versus healthy controls (GSE116899) and COVID-19 versus healthy controls (GSE212041). A second COVID-19 comparison (severe versus convalescent) was assembled from GSE272381 and GSE227116. Differential expression was analysed with DESeq2, pathway enrichment with fgsea (Hallmark gene sets) and topGO (Gene Ontology biological process and molecular function). Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were compared between diseases by direction of change. Results  In RA neutrophils, 11,355 DEGs were identified, of which 90 had an absolute log2 fold change of at least 2 with pConclusions  RA neutrophils show a transcriptional programme enriched for interferon and antiviral-response pathways. Part of the RA signature is shared with COVID-19 neutrophils, while a subset of genes diverges, and this divergence depended on the COVID-19 comparison used. These findings are hypothesis-generating and provide candidate genes for experimental validation.
records.authors: Nawani S, Alam M.

records.title: Evaluating the Identifiability of Temporal Delay and Response Attenuation in Endometrial Decidualization
records.abstract: Endometriosis is associated with impaired endometrial decidualization, yet conventional differential expression analyses cannot readily distinguish delayed transcriptional activation from reduced response amplitude. These mechanisms may produce similar expression differences at individual time points while implying distinct biological interpretations. Establishing when they can be distinguished is therefore a computational identifiability problem. We implement an identifiability-aware analysis of temporal displacement and amplitude attenuation in longitudinal transcriptomic responses. The approach combines reference trajectories, constrained amplitude-only and amplitude-plus-delay models, analytical examples of observational equivalence, and simulation-based assessments of mechanism distinguishability. Held-out time-point evaluation and culture-level sensitivity analyses examine the stability of model-dependent conclusions. In GSE246591, a candidate-delay-dependent dynamic-range filter excluded 30.9–38.3% of initially dynamic features under a hypothetical 24-hour shift across four endometrial stromal cultures. A two-component diagnostic separating retained dynamic range from affine shape similarity revealed that small projection residuals can arise from either loss of observable dynamics or similarity of response shapes. These findings demonstrate why a single separation statistic may be insufficient for interpreting temporal identifiability. Complementary independent in vivo analyses provided biological context. In GSE51981, an endometrial progesterone-response-associated transcriptional score was reduced in endometriosis samples (phase-model estimate 0.155, 95% CI 0.222 to 0.088). GSE6364 showed a directionally consistent but statistically inconclusive difference (0.033, 95% CI 0.068 to 0.002). Neither observation independently establishes a temporal delay. Together, these results support selection-aware evaluation of temporal transcriptomic responses, distinguishing structural ambiguity and loss of dynamic signal from evidence of a biological timing change.

records.title: Virus coinfection in plants determined by ecological responses to environmental heterogeneity
records.abstract: Community ecology is acknowledged as a relevant causative agent of epidemiological processes of plant viruses and has consequences for coinfection and virus and host evolution. Plant virus coinfection is common, but factors that promote non-random virus interactions above the population-level are unknown. Here, we analyse intrinsic and extrinsic factors in virus-host and virus-virus interactions by eighteen generalist virus species of a diverse multi-host-multi-virus system. Coinfection among viruses with broad host ranges, diverse modes of horizontal transmission, and interspecific variation in responses to environmental heterogeneity is expected to be shaped by ecological as well as evolutionary constraints. We analyse patterns of coinfection from 1,931 individual plants in 94 species from multiple plant communities of distinct habitat types and show that above 50% of plants were coinfected by 2-8 viruses. To analyse the role of environmental variables on the observed virus associations we used Markov and conditional random fields modelling. Results showed that a large majority of coinfections were random interactions, consistent with ecological fitting, and only a minor fraction being non-random associations. Random field models underscored the relevance of common responses to environmental heterogeneity driving coinfection, and strongly suggest mode of horizontal transmission as a causal agent. Results highlighted a major role of between-host, rather than within-host processes in driving coinfection. This study is a considerable addition to the understanding of drivers of virus coinfection and, hence, of virus community ecology and epidemiology.
records.authors: Zamfir Velea AD, Babalola BM, McLeish M, Garcia-Arenal Rodriguez F.

records.title: Developmental perturbation of Purkinje cell function induces male-biased core and associated autism spectrum disorder–like phenotypes in adulthood
records.abstract: Abstract  Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a prevalent neurodevelopmental condition whose etiology remains incompletely understood. Human epidemiological studies have implicated the cerebellum in ASD pathogenesis, and studies in mouse models have provided evidence for a causal contribution of cerebellar dysfunction. However, previous animal studies have largely focused on males and cerebellar manipulations at later developmental stages, with associated features of ASD remaining less explored. To address these gaps, we chemogenetically perturbed Purkinje cell function during early postnatal development in both male and female mice. Developmental Purkinje cell perturbation induced male-biased core ASD-like behavioral phenotypes, including reduced sociability and cognitive inflexibility. Phenotypes related to associated features of ASD, including impaired fine motor learning, altered sensory processing, and sleep abnormalities, were also predominantly observed in males. At the molecular level, bulk RNA sequencing following developmental Purkinje cell perturbation identified candidate sex-dependent transcriptional changes in both the hindbrain and forebrain, suggesting that altered cerebellar activity during development can influence gene expression across distant brain regions. Together, these findings demonstrate that transient early postnatal perturbation of Purkinje cell function can produce diverse core and associated ASD-like phenotypes, predominantly in males, with evidence suggesting transcriptional changes beyond the cerebellum. This study highlights developmental cerebellar dysfunction as a potential contributor to sex differences in ASD vulnerability.
records.authors: Miwa H, Kamijo S, Hori K, Hoshino M, Ikeda K.

records.title: Inverse design of chemical perturbations for desired cellular state transitions with GEMGen
records.abstract: Abstract  Perturbation biology links interventions to resulting cellular changes, providing a basis for understanding and manipulating biological processes. Recent advances in computational modelling have enabled prediction of cellular responses to diverse perturbations. However, many biomedical applications require going beyond response prediction to identify perturbations capable of inducing desired responses, an inverse design problem that remains largely underexplored compared to the forward prediction task. Here we introduce GEMGen, a large language model-based framework for the inverse design of chemical perturbations conditioned on desired cellular state transitions. GEMGen represents transitions as text-based, rank-ordered differential-gene instructions, generates molecular structures autoregressively, and uses a compound-response scorer to prioritize candidates for experimental testing. Across multiple benchmarks, GEMGen recovered small molecules structurally or mechanistically relevant to ground-truth compounds, and also generalized across perturbation modalities by generating chemical interventions from genetic perturbation signatures, outperforming existing perturbation design approaches. Beyond in silico evaluation, when conditioned on transcriptional signatures related to tissue fibrosis, GEMGen yielded eight novel antifibrotic structures from 17 de novo synthesized candidates. Notably, one lead candidate, GEMGen-010, exhibited strong antifibrotic activity in animal models of liver fibrosis without any structural optimization. Together, these results establish GEMGen as an effective approach extending perturbation modeling toward intervention design, broadening the methodology and application scope of perturbation biology.
records.authors: Shao S, Jiang Q, Ye X, Guo Z, Xia Y, Liu Z, Xu J, Jin P, Ju F, Xia H, Feng S, Liu H, Qin T, Deng P.

records.title: Matrix stiffness-related transcriptomic signatures reveal astrocyte-centered neuroimmune alterations in Alzheimer’s disease
records.abstract: Abstract    Background  Extracellular matrix remodeling and altered tissue mechanics are increasingly implicated in Alzheimer’s disease (AD), but links between matrix stiffness and AD pathology remain unclear.  Objective  To identify matrix stiffness-related transcriptomic signatures in AD and characterize their diagnostic potential, functions, cell-type specificity, and intercellular communication patterns.  Methods  Bulk transcriptomic datasets from the Gene Expression Omnibus were integrated with literature-derived matrix stiffness-related genes. Differential expression analysis, three machine-learning algorithms, and cross-dataset validation were used to identify candidate genes and construct a multigene classification model. Functional enrichment and immune-cell deconvolution analyses were performed. Single-cell RNA sequencing data were analyzed to assess cell-type-specific expression, inferred astrocyte trajectories, and predicted cell–cell communication.  Results  Eighty-one differentially expressed matrix stiffness-related genes were identified in AD brain tissue. FREM3, DUSP4, and FAM107A were selected and showed concordant differential expression across discovery and validation datasets. The three-gene model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.963 in the discovery cohort. Gene set enrichment analysis linked all three genes to oxidative phosphorylation, although FAM107A showed an enrichment direction opposite to DUSP4 and FREM3. Immune deconvolution suggested associations with immune-cell signatures. Single-cell analysis identified astrocytes as a major population expressing the three-gene signature. AD astrocytes showed altered pseudotime distributions and stronger predicted communication with immune cells, particularly T cells and macrophages.  Conclusions  FREM3, DUSP4, and FAM107A are candidate matrix stiffness-related transcriptomic signatures in AD and may connect extracellular matrix remodeling with mitochondrial metabolism, immune dysregulation, and astrocyte-associated changes. Independent clinical validation and experimental confirmation are required.
records.authors: Luo P, Qiao Y, Jin C, Wang Y, Qin Y, Wang Y, Zhang Y.

records.title: CDK4/6 inhibition exploits the radiobiology of lutetium-177 therapy to induce replication stress and durable senescence
records.abstract: Abstract    Background  Lutetium-177 (  177  Lu)-based radiopharmaceutical therapy delivers prolonged low-dose-rate irradiation, creating a radiobiological context that differs substantially from conventional external beam radiotherapy (EBRT). We hypothesised that this extended radiation exposure generates distinct therapeutic vulnerabilities and senescence states that can be exploited pharmacologically. Methods  A high-throughput clonogenic screen of 295 small-molecule inhibitors was performed in combination with  177  Lu-DOTATATE and compared with equitoxic EBRT. Candidate interactions were validated using multiple CDK4/6 inhibitors across SSTR2- and PSMA-targeted neuroendocrine and prostate cancer models, including xenografts. Cell-cycle regulation, replisome stability, DNA damage, p21 dynamics, senescence and autophagy-associated nuclear processing were interrogated mechanistically. Results  Drug interactions with  177  Lu-DOTATATE differed substantially from those observed with EBRT, identifying CDK4/6 inhibition as a preferential therapeutic vulnerability of prolonged  177  Lu exposure. Abemaciclib, palbociclib and ribociclib enhanced clonogenic suppression by  177  Lu-DOTATATE, while abemaciclib similarly potentiated  177  Lu-PSMA in human prostate cancer models and improved tumour control in vivo. Therapeutic cooperation was not associated with enhanced Rb inhibition or G1 arrest, but with replisome depletion, replication stress, genotoxicity and durable senescence. Distinct senotypes emerged between tumour models: 22Rv1 cells developed a predominantly sustained p21  high  state associated with persistent growth arrest, whereas CA20948 cells displayed a p21  low  senotype following an early p21 response, accompanied by increased autophagic and nucleophagic features. Pharmacological inhibition of autophagy differentially altered these senotypes, indicating that divergent p21-processing states can converge on durable senescence following combined CDK4/6 inhibition and  177  Lu therapy. Conclusions  CDK4/6 inhibition exploits a therapeutic vulnerability created by prolonged  177  Lu irradiation by promoting replication stress and durable senescence rather than conventional cell-cycle arrest. The emergence of distinct p21  high  and p21  low  senotypes identifies senescence heterogeneity as a previously underappreciated determinant of radiopharmaceutical response and provides a mechanistic rationale for combining clinically established CDK4/6 inhibitors with  177  Lu-based therapy.
records.authors: O'Neill E, Amoroso F, Mosley M, Genestar TH, Nonnekens J, Cornelissen B.

records.title: An Icariin-Informed Nine-Gene Transcriptomic Signature Identifies Mesenchymal–Stromal Recurrence Risk in Resected Colorectal Cancer: External Validation and Single-Cell Localization
records.abstract: Abstract    Background  Recurrence after curative resection of colorectal cancer is stratified largely by stage. Icariin, a prenylated flavonoid glycoside from  Epimedium  spp., defines a target space not yet examined as a source of recurrence-associated transcriptomes. Methods  Icariin targets intersected with tumour-versus-normal expression (TCGA-COAD, GSE39582) gave an 84-gene candidate pool; a pre-specified 100-combination screen (10 selectors × 10 models) in GSE14333 (  n   =   226  , 50 events) produced a fixed nine-gene signature. Four conditions fixed before external testing — patient-level independence, a depositor-coded disease-free-survival (DFS) event, the same platform, and the largest event count — selected GSE17536 (  n   =   145  , 36 events). Results  The signature (TIMP1/ SPARC/CLDN1 positive; PCNA/ACADM/ DPEP1/MMP3/CASP7/MMP12 negative) stratified DFS in GSE17536 (C-index 0.734; HR 2.30 per SD,  P   =   2.3  ×  10    −   8    ) and improved on stage, age and sex (  ΔC   +   0.085  , 95% CI 0.023–0.169; likelihood-ratio  P   0.001  ), but under-estimated absolute risk (observed-to-expected 1.90). Pooling the eight deduplicated cohorts (181 DFS events) gave a random-effects HR of 1.53 per SD (95% CI 1.13–2.07,  P   =   0.013  ;  I    2     =   69  %; prediction interval 0.71–3.31). High-risk tumours were mesenchymal/stromal and immune-suppressive; the signal localized mainly to fibroblasts and endothelium through SPARC and TIMP1. A protocol-matched random-pool control placed the signature at the 88th percentile (  P   =   0.118  ), and the stage-dominated TCGA-COAD transfer added no incremental value. Conclusion  The nine-gene signature is an externally validated relative-risk stratification biomarker derived from an icariin-associated candidate space; all results are in silico and await prospective and experimental validation.
records.authors: Zuo F, Yan J, Jiang M, Luo T.

records.title: CNGB3 promotes proliferation migration and metastasis in gastric cancer cells
records.abstract: Abstract    AIM: To investigate CNGB3 as a prognostic biomarker and functional driver of gastric cancer progression. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We used multi-omics approaches to comprehensively evaluate CNGB3's role in gastric cancer. Transcriptomic and clinical data were retrieved from the TCGA, GTEx, and GEO (GSE84437) databases. Analyzed methods included differential expression analysis between tumor and normal tissues, functional enrichment analysis (GO, KEGG, GSEA), immune infiltration analysis using the ssGSEA algorithm, and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with Cox regression modeling. RESULTS: CNGB3 expression levels in gastric cancer tissues were significantly elevated compared to normal tissues, and even higher in metastatic gastric cancer (p  1), from which 20 hub genes were identified through PPI network construction. Immune infiltration analysis showed substantial differences in immune cell enrichment between high and low CNGB3 expression groups (p Core tip:  Gastric cancer remains a leading cause of cancer mortality, and effective molecular biomarkers are needed to improve risk stratification. Through integrated multi-omics analysis, we identify CNGB3—a cyclic nucleotide-gated channel subunit—as a novel gastric cancer biomarker that is upregulated in tumors and linked to poor survival. records.title: Transcriptomic and machine learning analyses identify entosis-related key genes and potential regulatory networks in ischemic stroke
records.abstract: Abstract  Background  Ischemic stroke (IS) remains a major cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide, while effective therapeutic targets remain limited. Entosis is a non-apoptotic form of cell-in-cell death, but its involvement in IS is unknown. This study sought to identify entosis-related key genes and delineate their potential regulatory networks in IS. Methods  Bulk-transcriptome profiles were obtained for the training dataset GSE58294 and the validation dataset GSE122709, and entosis-related genes were compiled from previously published studies. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis and differential expression analysis were integrated with machine-learning selection and cross-dataset expression verification to determine key genes. Subsequent analyses included functional enrichment, immune infiltration, construction of molecular regulatory networks, drug prediction, and molecular docking. Results  Two key genes, NOL9 and WDR3, were identified and were significantly upregulated in both transcriptomic datasets. The nomogram incorporating these genes demonstrated favorable apparent performance in the training cohort. Eight immune cell subtypes differed significantly in the infiltration analysis. records.title: When, Where, and How Experience Becomes Structure: Mechanisms for Recursive Self-Improvement in LLM Agents
records.abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) studies how AI systems modify themselves and carry those changes into the generation of subsequent improvements. LLM agents can pursue this process by using interaction experience to revise Prompt, Memory, Skill, and Harness in some cases while keeping the task-execution model’s weights fixed. However, execution feedback does not directly specify which component should change, and a locally successful revision may not remain useful across tasks or subsequent improvement cycles. Understanding how experience becomes persistent agent structure therefore requires examining when evidence justifies a change, where that change should act, and how it is constructed, verified, and retained. This survey connects four components--Prompt, Memory, Skill, and Harness--with seven analytical functions: Collect, Evaluate, Diagnose, Abstract, Update, Verify, and Consolidate. The resulting framework supports comparisons of instruction revision, memory management, skill construction and maintenance, and Harness evolution through their update loops. These comparisons examine how mechanisms use observations to construct candidate changes, distinguishing feedback that triggers revision from evidence that supports retention. The analysis further addresses coordinated updates across components and the revision or retirement of retained components as tasks, tools, and models change. Finally, we identify cross-component attribution, long-term effectiveness, and independent validation as key challenges, and outline controlled and longitudinal evaluations of task-performance gains, the contribution of inherited state, and the effectiveness of subsequent updates.

records.title: Oxygen fugacity, temperature, and pressure of Siberian eclogitic diamonds: Implications for the Archaean convecting mantle redox state.
records.abstract: Kimberlite-borne eclogite xenoliths ultimately derive from ancient subducted oceanic crust. Some specimens still record the chemical and redox conditions of their igneous protoliths, allowing a view into contemporaneous convecting mantle sources. However, accurate reconstructions are limited because eclogites have been exposed to metasomatism in the subcontinental mantle for billions of years. Here, we investigated garnet and clinopyroxene inclusions, both touching and nontouching pairs, in 19 eclogitic diamonds from the Siberian craton, hence shielded from post-entrapment overprint. Inclusion compositions indicate average sampling depths of 180 to 280 km, temperatures of 1030° to 1540°C (±60°C), and redox conditions, for most of the samples, oxidized enough for diamonds to have originated from water(carbonate)-rich fluids. The reconstructed bulk composition points to basaltic oceanic crust formed from an Archaean convecting mantle region that was more oxygen-depleted than today, providing compelling evidence of redox heterogeneities in the source rocks of ancient oceanic crust.
records.authors: Marras G, Mikhailenko D, McCammon CA, Aulbach S, Lu Y, Tao R, Logvinova A, Zedgenizov D, Stagno V.

records.title: Local translational program at the muscle-tendon junction endows domain identity in muscle syncytia.
records.abstract: How cells establish specialized subdomains is a fundamental question in cell and tissue biology. Skeletal muscle fibers, among the largest cells in the body, are multinucleated and form distinct regions such as the neuromuscular and myotendinous junctions (MTJs), the latter forming a critical interface between muscle and tendon that transmits contractile force. While transcriptional heterogeneity among myonuclei has been described, whether local translation contributes to domain identity remains unknown, largely due to the lack of tools for domain-specific manipulation. Here, we introduce MTJ-AAV, a viral system that enables selective genetic targeting of MTJ myonuclei. This approach allowed MTJ-specific ribosome tagging and revealed extensive translational regulation underlying MTJ biology and its remodeling during exercise. Untranslated regions of these transcripts were sufficient to control regionalized translation. Notably, the Krüpper-like factor-family transcription factors emerged as translationally up-regulated targets at the MTJ, where they drive local gene expression. Our findings establish local translation as a key layer of subcellular specialization and provide a versatile toolkit for dissecting spatial molecular regulation within muscle syncytia.

records.title: Iron sourcing strategies and adaptive protein responses to iron deprivation in the intraerythrocytic parasite Babesia divergens.
records.abstract: Iron is indispensable for the survival and pathogenicity of Babesia parasites, yet the mechanisms underlying its acquisition remain largely unresolved. In contrast to other apicomplexan parasites, tick-borne Babesia species rapidly lose the parasitophorous vacuole following erythrocyte invasion and do not form hemozoin, suggesting the evolution of distinct strategies for iron metabolism. Here, we demonstrate that Babesia divergens utilizes a sequential, multi-route iron acquisition system to meet its metabolic demands within host erythrocytes. Kinetic uptake analyses reveal a pronounced preference for ferrous iron (Fe2+), which is imported through an active, energy-dependent process supported by extracellular ferric reductase activity that converts host-derived ferric iron (Fe3+) into a bioavailable form prior to uptake. Using immunogold transmission electron microscopy, we provide evidence for the active internalization of host transferrin and show that parasite proliferation is dose-dependently inhibited by apo-transferrin, establishing iron as a limiting factor for parasite growth. Quantitative proteomic profiling revealed a limited, stage-specific response to deferoxamine-induced iron deprivation. Three proteins showed statistically significant changes in abundance in free merozoites: the conserved multipass membrane protein Bdiv_019230 increased, whereas the hypothetical protein Bdiv_002300 and the putative serine hydroxymethyltransferase Bdiv_027330 decreased. No proteins reached the statistical significance threshold in intraerythrocytic parasites. These results identify a small set of statistically supported candidates for investigating the response of extracellular B. divergens merozoites to iron-restricted conditions.

records.title: Integrative analysis reveals shared biomarkers and pathways in osteoporosis and rheumatoid arthritis using machine learning and single-cell sequencing.
records.abstract: BackgroundOsteoporosis (OP) and Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) are prevalent chronic diseases characterized by bone loss and immune dysregulation. Evidence suggests that patients with RA are at increased risk of developing OP; however, the shared molecular mechanisms linking these conditions remain incompletely understood.MethodsPublicly available bulk transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets for OP and RA were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was applied to identify shared gene modules associated with both diseases. Functional enrichment and protein-protein interaction analyses were performed to characterize common biological pathways. Machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest (RF) and Support Vector Machine (SVM), were used to identify and validate shared hub genes and to construct diagnostic models. Immune cell infiltration was evaluated using CIBERSORT, and the cellular localization of hub genes was further validated using scRNA-seq analysis.ResultsWGCNA identified 329 genes shared between OP- and RA-associated modules, which were significantly enriched in muscle-related processes, cytokine signaling, and immune-inflammatory pathways. RF analysis identified three shared candidate genes: ANO5, IL27RA, and CNTN3. Among these, ANO5 and IL27RA demonstrated consistent expression evidence and literature support, whereas CNTN3 emerged as a computationally nominated candidate requiring cautious interpretation and experimental validation. An SVM-based model incorporating these genes demonstrated robust predictive accuracy in both OP and RA validation cohorts. Immune infiltration analysis revealed distinct yet coordinated immune landscapes, with hub genes showing significant correlations with T cells, macrophages, B cells, and plasma cells. ScRNA-seq analysis revealed that ANO5 was predominantly expressed in macrophages and fibroblasts, IL27RA was mainly enriched in T cells, whereas CNTN3 showed minimal enrichment at the single-cell level in both OP bone and RA synovial tissues.ConclusionThis integrative bioinformatics and machine learning study identifies shared molecular signatures and immune-related mechanisms underlying OP and RA. ANO5 and IL27RA emerge as robust candidate regulators linking immune dysregulation and bone remodeling, whereas CNTN3-although identified by machine learning-requires cautious interpretation and further investigation due to limited supporting evidence. These findings provide novel insights into the pathogenesis of RA-associated OP and highlight potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for their comorbidity.

records.title: In vivo Nupr1 regulates oxidative stress-endoplasmic reticulum stress crosstalk and mitochondria-dependent apoptosis in varicocele-related testicular injury.
records.abstract: Varicocele (VCL) is a major cause of male infertility and is closely associated with oxidative stress (OS)-induced testicular injury. Increasing evidence suggests that endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS) interacts with OS and mitochondrial dysfunction in the pathogenesis of spermatogenic impairment, but the molecular regulators linking these processes remain incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated the role of Nupr1 in VCL-related testicular stress responses. Re-analysis of transcriptomic data from VCL rat testes identified Nupr1 as a candidate gene associated with OS, ERS, and apoptosis. Nupr1 expression was significantly increased in VCL testes and was similarly upregulated in GC-2 and TM4 cells under H2O2-induced OS or tunicamycin-induced ERS. Stable knockdown of Nupr1 in GC-2 cells reduced viability under oxidative challenge, increased intracellular ROS accumulation, decreased mitochondrial membrane potential, and enhanced apoptosis, accompanied by increased cleaved caspase-3 expression and an elevated Bax/Bcl-2 ratio. Notably, Nupr1 deficiency attenuated the adaptive ERS response, as shown by reduced expression of GRP78, IRE1/p-IRE1, PERK/p-PERK, and ATF6. Pharmacological induction of ERS with tunicamycin further worsened cell injury in Nupr1-deficient cells, whereas 4-PBA failed to restore cell viability or GRP78 expression. Collectively, these findings indicate that Nupr1 is involved in the cellular stress response relevant to VCL and may help maintain adaptive UPR signaling and mitochondrial homeostasis in spermatogenic cells under oxidative stress.
records.authors: Jiang X, Tang L, Ma Z, Wu X, Zhang Z, Nian W, Li T, Liao Y.

records.title: Integrated Single-Step Duplex CRISPR-Based System for Point-of-Care Detection of Human Immunodeficiency Virus and Treponema pallidum Directly from Whole Blood.
records.abstract: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) and syphilis are two major sexually transmitted diseases that pose serious threats to public health, underscoring the urgent need for fast and sensitive diagnosis for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and Treponema pallidum (TP). Here, we developed a single-step duplex CRISPR assay that integrated reverse transcription, recombinase polymerase amplification, in vitro transcription, and CRISPR/Cas12a and Cas13a detection for simultaneous HIV and TP nucleic acid testing. We further engineered a fully integrated, low-cost microfluidic chip that consolidated whole-blood sample processing, nucleic acid release, and single-step duplex CRISPR detection. The chip featured a rapid plasma separator with a press-actuated design that removed inhibitors and extracted plasma within minutes without external equipment. The entire process was coupled with a homemade smartphone-based portable device that provided thermal incubation, dual-channel fluorescence excitation, and automated image analysis via a dedicated mobile application. This integrated system enables "sample-to-answer" detection within 30 min directly from whole blood, achieving a limit of detection of 2.5 copies/μL of both HIV and TP and demonstrating 100% sensitivity and specificity concordant with the real-time PCR in 51 cases of clinical samples. This work demonstrates a transformative point-of-care diagnostic platform that combines minimal user steps, equipment independence, and robust multiplex detection for decentralized pathogen testing.
records.authors: Xu Z, Wang Y, Wei M, Miao P, Zhang H, Li M, Wang S, Rong Z, He K.

records.title: A DPY19L2/FAM209-associated protein-Arp complex-CAPZA3 scaffold is essential for perinuclear theca assembly and fertilization.
records.abstract: Fertilization is a fundamental biological process that enables the fusion of a spermatozoon with an oocyte to initiate embryonic development. However, the underlying mechanisms leading to fertilization failure remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrated that the actin-related protein (Arp) family members ACTRT2 and ACTRT3 are essential for fertilization in both humans and mice, whereas ACTL10 is dispensable for fertility and the human-specific ACTL8 may play a role in early spermatogenesis. Ultrastructural and immunofluorescence analyses revealed that, during spermatogenesis, ACTRT2 or ACTRT3 deficiency disrupts the assembly of subacrosomal layer of the perinuclear theca (SAL-PT), leading to acrosome detachment and subsequent manchette abnormalities, which in turn impairs the formation of the postacrosomal sheath of the PT. These structural defects were accompanied by reduced abundance of the candidate sperm-borne oocyte-activating factors PAWP and PLCζ. Moreover, knockout of Actrt2 or Actrt3 severely impaired spermatozoa's ability to penetrate the zona pellucida during in vitro fertilization. Mechanistically, ACTRT2, ACTRT3, ACTL7A, ACTL7B, and ACTL9 form a testis-enriched Arp complex in the SAL-PT and maintain the stability of one another. This complex interacts with the PT protein CAPZA3, which subsequently binds and stabilizes PLCζ. Additionally, the Arp complex interacts with DPY19L2/FAM209-associated proteins to mediate acrosome anchoring to the nuclear envelope. Therefore, these findings established a sequential DPY19L2/FAM209-associated protein-Arp complex-CAPZA3 scaffold extending from the nuclear envelope to the acrosome that is indispensable for fertilization. Collectively, we defined a previously unidentified structural and molecular framework for fertilization and provided insights into the diagnosis and treatment of fertilization failure.
records.authors: Ruan T, Shen G, Zhuo L, Zhang Y, Wang X, Tian E, Tian Y, Tang X, Chen D, Jiang C, Yang X, Ma J, Zhao S, Zhao C, Cui X, Jiang X, Yang Y, Wang Y, Shen Y.

records.title: Osteoclastogenesis associated gene signatures in postmenopausal low bone mineral density: cross-dataset transcriptomics and whole-blood validation.
records.abstract: BackgroundOsteoporosis is characterized by reduced bone mass and increased fracture risk, yet minimally invasive molecular correlates of postmenopausal low bone mineral density remain limited.MethodsWe independently reanalysed two human osteoclastogenesis RNA-seq datasets, GSE225974 and GSE246769, using differential-expression, Gene Ontology, KEGG, Hallmark gene set enrichment, and cross-dataset concordance analyses. Six candidate genes, LGALSL, FAXDC2, DHCR7, MYL9, RHOC, and ITGB5, were subsequently evaluated by RT-qPCR in whole blood from 100 postmenopausal women with normal bone mineral density (n=30), osteopenia (n=30), or osteoporosis (n=40).ResultsAcross the two RNA-seq datasets, 1,782 differentially expressed genes were shared, including 1,240 concordantly upregulated and 385 concordantly downregulated genes, with strong cross-dataset effect-size correlation (r=0.74). GO and KEGG analyses identified replicated sterol/lipid, skeletal-development, adhesion/integrin, and actin-cytoskeletal programs, while Hallmark GSEA identified 22 concordantly enriched gene sets, including oxidative phosphorylation, fatty-acid metabolism, and cholesterol homeostasis. BMD was positively correlated with calcium intake and physical activity. Conversely, deteriorating bone health was positively associated with high cholesterol, low BMI, early menopause. All six candidate genes were significantly and concordantly upregulated during osteoclastogenesis in both datasets. Whole-blood RT-qPCR analysis demonstrated progressively higher relative expression across normal-BMD, osteopenia, and osteoporosis groups for all six candidates. Expression analysis from the serum validated LGALSL, RHOC, MYL9 and ITGB5 elevated expression in osteoporosis cases.ConclusionThese findings identify reproducible osteoclastogenesis-associated transcriptional programs and support the six candidate genes as candidate signature correlating with the postmenopausal BMD status.
records.authors: Anbreen N, Iqbal MJ, Wahab H, Manzoor S, Tariq A, Aruge S, Menotta M.

records.title: Quinalphos-induced chromosomal instability, DNA damage, and Bax/Bcl-2 dysregulation in mouse bone marrow: protective effects of piperine.
records.abstract: Quinalphos (QNP), an organophosphate insecticide, is known to induce genotoxic and cytotoxic effects in non-target organisms. This study evaluated the impact of subacute QNP exposure on chromosomal stability, DNA integrity, and apoptosis-related gene expression in bone marrow cells of male Swiss albino mice, and assessed the genoprotective potential of piperine (PIP), a bioactive compound from Piper nigrum. Mice were allocated into six groups: control (2% gum acacia), QNP I (0.375 mg/kg b.w.), QNP II (0.75 mg/kg b.w.), PIP alone (10 mg/kg b.w.), QNP I + PIP, and QNP II + PIP. All treatments were administered orally for 28 days. Genotoxicity was evaluated using micronucleus, chromosomal aberration, and alkaline comet assays. The expression of Bax and Bcl-2 was assessed by quantitative real-time PCR. QNP exposure produced a dose-dependent increase in micronucleated erythrocytes, chromosomal aberrations, and DNA damage, as indicated by increases in comet assay parameters. QNP upregulated pro-apoptotic Bax and downregulated anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 mRNA expression, consistent with activation of apoptosis-related signalling. Co-administration of PIP reduced several QNP-induced genotoxic alterations, although the magnitude of attenuation varied among endpoints, and did not fully restore Bax/Bcl-2 expression balance. Overall, PIP reduced QNP-induced genotoxic and apoptosis-related changes, although its protective effects were endpoint-specific. These findings suggest that PIP may have potential as a natural candidate for mitigating QNP-associated genetic damage. Clinical trial number: Not applicable.
records.authors: Singh P, Kumar V, Bagri P, Batra K, Lather D.

records.title: OsGAT2 modulates nitrogen allocation and heading date in rice through amino acid transport.
records.abstract: Heading date (or flowering time) is one of the most important agronomic traits in rice, as it determines regional adaptability and grain yield. Its regulation is influenced by multiple factors, including photoperiod, nutritional status, and endogenous phytohormones. However, the roles of amino acids and their transporters in regulating heading date remain largely unclear. In this study, we identified four haplotypes in the promoter region of the rice amino acid transporter gene OsGAT2 among diverse germplasm resources. Haplotypes associated with lower OsGAT2 expression exhibited earlier heading date, longer grain length, and reduced nitrogen content. Further analyses showed that OsGAT2 is mainly expressed in basal tissues, stems, and leaf sheaths, and is localized to the plasma membrane. Substrate assays in yeast demonstrated that OsGAT2 is capable of transporting multiple amino acids, including GABA, Ser, Leu, Glu, Val, Gly, and Ala. Functional analyses revealed that knockout of OsGAT2 promoted earlier heading date, whereas overexpression lines exhibited delayed heading date. Consistently, the contents of GABA, several amino acids, and total nitrogen in the leaves and panicles were significantly higher in OsGAT2 overexpression lines than in the wild-type, whereas OsGAT2 CRISPR knockout lines exhibited tissue-dependent changes, with increased stem nitrogen content but reduced nitrogen content in leaves and panicles. Moreover, exogenous application of these amino acids further enhanced the delayed heading date phenotype in overexpression lines, while mutants headed earlier than the wild-type. Transcriptome analysis revealed that altered expression of OsGAT2 affects the regulatory network controlling heading date. The heading repressors Ghd7 and Ghd8 were significantly upregulated in OsGAT2 overexpression lines but downregulated in mutants. In contrast, heading-promoting genes, including OsGI, Hd17, and Ehd2, were markedly upregulated in the mutants. Taken together, these results demonstrate that the amino acid transporter OsGAT2 regulates rice heading date by mediating amino acid transport and modulating the expression of key heading regulatory genes. This study provides important insights and potential targets for shortening heading time and improving regional adaptability of rice through gene editing. KEY MESSAGE : The amino acid transporter gene OsGAT2 regulates rice heading date by modulating amino acid transport and the expression of heading date-related genes, thereby improving regional adaptability.

records.title: Dual-mode biosensing featuring fluorescence and electrochemiluminescence for regional resolution of single-nucleotide variants.
records.abstract: Single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) are a critical molecular basis for antibiotic resistance in pathogenic bacteria. However, precise detection of mutant targets remains challenging because they may exist at low abundance and often coexist with wild-type sequences in complex biological matrices. Herein, we report a target-triggered strand displacement reaction that releases two functional DNA strands: one activates the trans-cleavage activity of CRISPR/Cas12a to generate a fluorescent signal, while the other competitively displaces cadmium sulfide quantum dots pre-modified on a gold electrode surface, decreasing the electrochemiluminescence (ECL) signal. The two functional strands hybridize to distinct regions of the probe, enabling the two signaling channels to respond differentially to single-base mismatches at different locations. Taking the response to wild-type targets as a reference, synchronized changes in both signals reflect target concentration. A significant decrease in the fluorescence signal alone, with the ECL signal unchanged, indicates that the mismatch occurs within the fluorescence recognition region, whereupon the unaffected ECL channel may serve for quantification. Conversely, when the ECL signal decreases while the fluorescence signal remains stable, the fluorescence channel may serve for quantification. This design enables a single probe to discriminate between wild-type and mutant targets based on the differential responses of the two signaling channels. Our strategy thus provides a new avenue for single-base nucleic acid detection.
records.authors: Yang H, Lai T, Zhang H, Zhan M, Chen S, Zhang X, Chen L, Hu S.

records.title: Development and evaluation of non-target analysis methods for characterization of cyanobacterial secondary metabolites.
records.abstract: Cyanobacteria are of global concern, impacting ecosystems and posing a public health risk from production of bioactive secondary metabolites, including several classes of potent mammalian toxins. Because of the thousands of possible metabolites, non-target analysis (NTA) using high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) is of increasing interest for studying cyanobacteria. However, performance evaluation of these NTA methods is rarely considered, potentially raising concerns over the quality and validity of results. Here, a NTA workflow was developed for cyanobacterial metabolite profiling using data-dependent LC-HRMS/MS acquisition and semi-automated data processing, including product ion, mass list, and spectral library searching using metabolomics software. Rigorous method optimization and performance evaluation at each step were carried out based on detection of cyanotoxins in a multiclass cyanobacterial matrix reference material. Deeper profiling of this material further extended its utility for evaluation of NTA performance for metabolite classes beyond traditional cyanotoxins in the future. The workflow was applied to a set of environmental benthic cyanobacterial biofilm samples associated with recent animal deaths. This led to the detection of 116 secondary metabolites from microcystin, anatoxin, cyanopeptolin, anabaenopeptin, aeruginosin, and cyanobactin classes, greatly increasing reported compound diversity for benthic cyanobacteria, which have been poorly characterized compared to planktonic bloom-forming species. Because of the association of anatoxins in these samples with animal deaths, additional structural elucidation of two newly detected analogues was carried out via analytical scale semi-synthesis. The approaches presented are broadly applicable to class-based NTA in other fields where improved confidence in detection results is increasingly important.
records.authors: Zamlynny L, Wright EJ, Jamieson RC, Beach DG.

records.title: YAP coordinates lipid and cholesterol metabolism in papillary thyroid cancer through a glucose-AMPK-gated TEAD1-SREBP1/2 axis.
records.abstract: To determine whether Yes-associated protein (YAP), a transcriptional coactivator frequently activated in cancer, coordinates lipid and cholesterol metabolism in papillary thyroid cancer (PTC), YAP was overexpressed or silenced in BCPAP and TPC-1 cells, and transcriptomic, biochemical and functional analyses were performed. Glucose deprivation and the AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) activator metformin suppressed YAP nuclear localization and lipogenic programs, whereas AMPK inhibition by Compound C or YAP overexpression (OE) restored them. Mechanistically, YAP associated with TEA domain family member 1 (TEAD1), occupied canonical TEAD-binding motifs in the SREBF1 and SREBF2 promoters, and activated their transcription in a TEAD1-dependent manner: TEAD1 knockdown abolished YAP-induced SREBF promoter activity, while eight-group genetic epistasis experiments showed that TEAD1 or SREBP1/2 depletion was required for YAP-driven proliferation, clonogenic growth, neutral-lipid and cholesterol accumulation, and expression of FASN, SCD, HMGCR and HMGCS1. Pharmacological SREBP blockade by fatostatin or AMPK activation by metformin reversed YAP-driven phenotypes in vitro and restrained xenograft growth in vivo, with comparable tumor-weight inhibition between the two treatments and no effect on body weight.Clinically, YAP1 expression correlated with lipogenic genes and with shorter disease-free survival in the TCGA-THCA cohort and with SREBP expression in 200 paired PTC specimens. These findings support a model in which glucose-AMPK signaling gates a YAP-TEAD1-SREBP1/2 axis that promotes lipid and cholesterol metabolism and PTC growth, and suggest metformin and SREBP-targeting strategies as candidate therapeutic approaches.
records.authors: Chen H, Wang J, Zhu Y, Song H, Qiu Z, Luo Q, Shen C.

records.title: Zinc promotes osteogenesis through enhanced preosteoblast proliferation, osteogenic differentiation, and bone-related transcriptomic remodeling.
records.abstract: Zinc (Zn) is an essential trace element that contributes to skeletal development, bone remodeling, and mineral homeostasis, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying its effects on osteoblast differentiation remain incompletely defined. This study investigated the effects of Zn ions on preosteoblast growth and osteogenic differentiation and characterized Zn-responsive transcriptomic changes. Under osteogenic conditions, Zn increased alkaline phosphatase activity, mineralized matrix formation, and expression of osteogenic markers, including alkaline phosphatase (ALP), osteocalcin, procollagen I, and Runx2. RNA sequencing identified over a thousand differentially expressed genes following Zn²⁺ treatment. Functional enrichment analysis revealed modulation of bone-related pathways, including Wnt, TGF-β/BMP, Hippo, and PI3K-Akt signaling, as well as extracellular matrix (ECM)-receptor interaction, focal adhesion, and osteoclast differentiation. Transcriptomic analysis highlighted osteogenesis-associated candidate genes, including Wnt16, Lrp6, Bmp6, and Tnfrsf11b. Together, these findings associate Zn-enhanced osteogenic responses with changes in bone-related gene expression and identify candidate signaling relationships for future functional investigation.

records.title: Novel 3D-printed microfluidic chip for automated real-time multi-route in vivo nanoplastics toxicity testing.
records.abstract: Plastics are one of the most pervasive pollutants in marine environments, with smaller-sized plastics, such as nanoplastics (NPLs), posing significant but understudied threats to marine organisms. Traditional bulk and end-point testing methods offer limited capability for real-time, in situ assessment of nanotoxicity. In this study, we present a fully 3D-printed, automated microfluidic chip designed for multi-route in vivo nanotoxicity testing, which addresses the limitations of conventional methods by offering automated and dynamic exposure conditions alongside real-time monitoring through fluorescence imaging and oxygen sensing. Additionally, this platform simplifies the fabrication process, avoiding the time-consuming soft-lithography typically used for microfluidic chips and increasing accessibility to users without specialized expertise. As a proof of concept, the chip was used to assess nanotoxicity in model marine organisms across different trophic levels: Artemia franciscana (instar II and III stages) and a mixture of five microalgae. Polystyrene nanoplastics, one of the most prevalent plastics in marine environments, were used as the model NPLs and tested in two exposure routes: waterborne and foodborne. The results revealed distinct uptake dynamics; in Artemia, NPL-associated fluorescence initially increased and subsequently declined during waterborne exposure, whereas it continued to increase over the measured period during foodborne exposure. Oxygen-consumption responses varied by organism and exposure route: waterborne exposure produced a higher trend in Artemia and a significant increase in algae, whereas foodborne exposure produced a response comparable to its control. Together, continuous oxygen sensing and fluorescence imaging demonstrated the capability of the chip to monitor complementary physiological and NPL-uptake responses under multiple exposure routes in real time.

records.title: Holistic integration of protein interaction datasets establishes a framework for exploring the organization and composition of Caenorhabditis elegans germ granules.
records.abstract: Spatiotemporal organization of biological molecules is a key driver of cellular processes, including many post-transcriptional epigenetic processes. The germline-specific germ granules are biomolecular condensates that act as hubs for mRNA and small RNA processing and are core regulators of germline gene expression programming. Germ granules have been studied extensively in Caenorhabditis elegans, and recent developments have led to many subdivisions of the germ granule into specialized compartments. Rapid advancements in microscopy and protein-protein interaction (PPI) screening techniques have produced a large amount of data towards characterizing the localization of proteins to specific granules. However, common methods used to probe PPIs are limited in their ability to robustly detect valid interactions, especially the multivalent and sometimes transient ones observed in granule environments. Here we perform a meta-analysis of granule protein interaction screens. While these experiments generally enrich for proteins matching the profile of granule-associated proteins, we find that when considering screens individually, reproducibility is surprisingly low, highlighting not only the variability inherent in these methods but also the dynamic nature of the PPI networks present in granules. We developed an algorithm to provide a measure of each protein's association with specific granules across various experiments (a "granule association metric" or GAM). By further clustering and investigation of the GAM matrix, we demonstrate the power of this holistic approach to provide deeper insights into germ granule organization, highlight novel candidates, and act as a resource to inform future investigations into granules and their constituent proteins.
records.authors: Wills C, Ashe A.

records.title: Overcoming platinum resistance by the disulfiram metabolite CuET in novel preclinical models of human carcinomas.
records.abstract: Overcoming resistance to standard-of-care chemotherapy represents an unmet need in oncology. To help address this challenge, here we established and characterized a panel of human cisplatin-resistant lung and breast cancer cell lines and patient-derived organoids from high-grade serous ovarian carcinomas (HGSOC), and show that platinum resistance can be overcome by treatment with diethyldithiocarbamate-copper (CuET), a metabolite of the alcohol-aversion drug disulfiram. All platinum-resistant models remained sensitive to CuET, consistent with distinct cytotoxicity mechanisms: proteotoxic stress for CuET and DNA damage for cisplatin, respectively. Platinum adduct and DNA damage response analyses suggested diverse mechanisms of cisplatin resistance among our models. Considering potential CuET-based therapies, our gene knock-down and functional assays in preclinical models, complemented with immunohistochemical analysis of tissue samples from cohorts of triple-negative breast cancer and HGSOC patients indicate that levels of metallothioneins, rather than NPL4 (the molecular target of CuET) warrant further evaluation as candidate biomarkers of CuET sensitivity. This dataset provides a resource of platinum-resistant models of common carcinomas, identifies CuET as a compound overcoming such resistance and provides leads for predictive biomarker discovery, with potential clinical implications in oncology.

records.title: Evaluation of the plant glucoside monoterpene indole alkaloid brachycerine for potential protection of human skin against ultraviolet damage.
records.abstract: Sunlight ultraviolet radiation A and B (UV-A and UV-B) affect human skin and may be a cause of cancer. Damage to skin nerve fibers and cell DNA is often observed following excessive unprotected exposure. Plants produce numerous specialized metabolites involved in stress mitigation. Brachycerine, a major leaf glucoside alkaloid from the tree Psychotria brachyceras, absorbs in the UV range and is a powerful antioxidant protecting the photosynthetic machinery against this radiation. Herein, the protective effects of new skincare formulations containing brachycerine or foliar extract were tested on ex vivo human skin exposed to UV. Nerve fibers were identified by immunofluorescence, and UV damage or neuroprotection effects were assessed by image analysis. DNA integrity of UV-B treated samples was evaluated by comet assays. UV-A and UV-B significantly reduced (circa 50%) the measured nerve endings density in the untreated or placebo-treated samples. Pre-treatment with tested skincare formulations completely blocked the effects of UV on nerve endings. UV-B-induced DNA damage was abolished by both the alkaloid and the extract. Cytotoxicity assays showed that brachycerine was not toxic to mammalian cells. Formulations with brachycerine or leaf extract effectively protected ex vivo human skin exposed to UV, indicating that these phytochemicals are potential candidate components of new broad spectrum natural sunscreens.
records.authors: do Nascimento NC, Fonseca BL, Bonorino C, Bauer ME, Matsuura HN, Ceravolo IP, Moura DJ, Saffi J, Fett JP, Fett-Neto AG.

records.title: Immunomodulatory and Antioxidant Biomimetic Hydrogel Coloaded with Glycyrrhizic Acid and Copper Gallate for Synergistic Cartilage Regeneration.
records.abstract: Articular cartilage lesions are persistently restrained by three interwoven pathological drivers: chronic inflammatory response, sustained oxidative stress, and progressive extracellular matrix (ECM) catabolism. Coupled with the inherently weak self-repair capacity of hyaline cartilage, effective therapeutic interventions for such injuries remain an unmet clinical demand owing to the inherently poor self-repair capacity of hyaline cartilage, effective therapeutic interventions remain an unmet clinical demand. Herein, we engineered a biomimetic composite hydrogel designated ECM/HAMA/GA@Cu-GA, which integrates decellularized cartilage extracellular matrix, methacrylated hyaluronic acid (HAMA), glycyrrhizic acid (GA), and copper gallate (Cu-GA). This integrated hydrogel platform simultaneously endows biomimetic mechanical support, potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidative bioactivities, as well as robust chondrogenic induction capacity. In vitro cellular evaluations verified the outstanding biocompatibility of the composite hydrogel. The biomaterial efficiently polarizes macrophages toward the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype, suppresses the secretion of pro-inflammatory mediators and matrix-degrading proteases, and facilitates the migration and chondrogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). Transcriptomic profiling suggested that its underlying molecular mechanisms may involve activation of the PI3K/Akt signaling cascade and blockade of the NF-κB-mediated inflammatory pathway. In vivo assessments using rat articular cartilage defect models demonstrated that the ECM/HAMA/GA@Cu-GA hydrogel achieves satisfactory synchronous regeneration of hyaline cartilage and subchondral bone at 4 and 8 weeks post-implantation, with superior regenerative performance relative to all control groups. Collectively, this multifunctional hydrogel enables comprehensive remodeling of the pathological joint microenvironment with favorable biosafety profiles, representing a translatable candidate strategy for clinical management of cartilage degenerative disorders.

records.title: Rethinking Pathogenesis of Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis.
records.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease characterized by progressive fibroinflammatory injury of intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts that may lead to cirrhosis, hepatobiliary malignancy, and death, with liver transplantation representing the only effective intervention in end-stage disease. Rather than a single dominant pathomechanism, the data support a model in which four axes-bile acid metabolism, the intestinal microbiome and gut barrier, biliary epithelial dysfunction, and Th17-skewed immune dysregulation-are reciprocally coupled and converge on a shared periductal fibrogenic output dominated by TGF-β signaling. This review summarizes key mechanistic advances from genetic, epigenomic, single-cell, spatial transcriptomic, and microbiome studies. These investigations implicate antigen presentation pathways, Th17-skewed immune responses, cholangiocyte senescence and profibrotic signaling, and disrupted gut-liver communication as central drivers of chronic biliary injury. Emerging spatial and multi-omics approaches further reveal complex cellular crosstalk among cholangiocytes, immune cells, macrophages, and mesenchymal populations within portal inflammatory niches. We discuss evolving biomarkers and recent clinical trial data targeting bile acid metabolism, fibrosis, the microbiome, and immune pathways. In conclusion, research data suggest viewing PSC as a network disease, which provides a unifying framework for disease pathogenesis and may enable biomarker-guided patient stratification and mechanism-based therapy development targeting distinct pathogenic pathways.

records.title: Synthesis and self-assembly of new quinuclidinolium-based surfactants: enhanced activity of cytochrome c and efficient antimicrobial activity.
records.abstract: Bio-based surfactants are a great alternative to conventional surfactants owing to their low toxicity and minimal environmental impact. Herein, four new 3-quinuclidinol-based surfactants, namely, [C16Qui][Br], [C12Qui][Br], [C12AQui][Br] and [C8Qui][Br], have been synthesized and characterized for the first time. The thermal stability of all the surfactants at higher than 250 °C makes them suitable for high-temperature applications. The self-assembly behavior of these surfactants is thoroughly characterized using various techniques. The interactions between relatively hydrophobic bulky head groups, along with other hydrophobic interactions, drive micelle formation. Small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) measurements provide insights into the micellar structures of all surfactants: [C16Qui][Br] assembles into spherical micelles, [C12Qui][Br] and [C12AQui][Br] form prolate ellipsoidal structures, and [C8Qui][Br] arranges into loosely packed, random polymer-like micelles. The micellar structure of short-chain surfactants is solely driven by interactions between head groups, while more compact micellar structures are observed for long-chain surfactants. The presence of an amide functionality near the quinuclidinolium head group further governs the characteristics and properties of the micelles. The interlocking of head groups in the self-assembled structure and distinct structural arrangement of surfactant ions are studied through 1H-NMR spectroscopy and 2D 1H-1H correlation and nuclear Overhauser effect spectroscopies (COSY and NOESY). The aqueous solutions of these surfactants are employed as a catalytic reactor to enhance the enzymatic activity of cytochrome c. The synergistic effect of hydrophobic and electrostatic interactions enhances the enzymatic activity in both monomeric and micellar forms. Interestingly, these surfactants exhibit good microbial inhibition depending upon their structural features and net charge. The present study provides additional understanding of the synthesis of bio-based surfactants and their utilization in diverse biocatalytic and medical applications.

records.title: Intergenic Spacer 1 Haplotype Genotyping Enables Efficient Dissection of Population Diversity of the Wheat Stripe Rust Fungus (Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici).
records.abstract: Wheat stripe rust caused by Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici (Pst) is a destructive disease affecting wheat production because of its capacity for long-distance dispersal. This pathogen exhibits high genetic diversity, yet the low resolving power of currently used molecular markers has restricted in-depth understanding of its migration routes. We previously detected variations among isolates in the ribosomal intergenic spacer 1 (IGS1) region of Pst. In the current study, Pst IGS1 fragments were amplified directly from DNA extracted from wheat rust lesions each bearing a single uredinium, and the intraspecific variation pattern of IGS1 was comprehensively analyzed. Thirty polymorphic loci characterized by variations in repeat units and subunits were detected, with up to 12 polymorphic loci identified within single isolates. Among the 3,050 field samples examined, 506 distinct haplotypes were identified based on combinations of these polymorphic loci, demonstrating that the IGS1 haplotypes can be effective markers for revealing genetic diversity of Pst. Furthermore, IGS1 haplotypes allowed dissection of genetic structure and gene flow among different Pst populations. The IGS1 haplotype genotyping system features several advantages: it requires no fungal isolation or culturing, relies on only one pair of specific primers, and supports high-throughput sample processing. It therefore represents a powerful tool for elucidating the gene flow and genotype flow among populations as well as for tracking long-distance dispersal of Pst both on regional and continental scales.
records.authors: Chen Y, Liang X, Zhu M, Dang H, Hao B, Ju L, Jin S, Zhan G, Yue H, Wang M, Hsiang T, Zhang R, Cai L, Kang Z, Sun G.
