records.title: Investigating the Expression and Function of PPP2R1A in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Multi-Omics Analysis with in vitro Validation.
records.abstract: BackgroundHepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains difficult to diagnose early and to treat effectively. Protein Phosphatase 2A Regulatory Subunit Aα (PPP2R1A), the scaffolding (Aα) subunit of the PP2A holoenzyme, is altered in several cancer types, but its expression pattern, functional significance, and translational relevance in HCC are incompletely understood.MethodsPublic transcriptomic, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic datasets (TCGA-LIHC, GTEx, GEO, ICGC-LIHC, HPA, TISCH2) and drug-sensitivity databases were integrated to characterize PPP2R1A expression and its associations with survival, biological pathways, and tumor immune infiltration in HCC. Functional effects of PPP2R1A knockdown were assessed in Huh7 cells by RT-qPCR, CCK-8, Transwell, flow-cytometric cell-cycle, and β-galactosidase assays.ResultsPPP2R1A was significantly overexpressed in HCC tissues relative to normal liver and was also elevated across several other cancer types. High PPP2R1A expression was associated with shorter overall and disease-specific survival in Kaplan-Meier analysis, although it was not an independent prognostic factor after multivariate adjustment (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.051, p = 0.789). PPP2R1A expression correlated positively with transcriptional programs related to cell cycle, MYC, EGFR, MAPK, and WNT signaling, and negatively with p53 pathway activity. At single-cell and spatial resolution, PPP2R1A was enriched in malignant cells and in tumor regions, and its expression correlated with the abundance of several computationally inferred immune cell populations. PPP2R1A knockdown in Huh7 cells reduced proliferation and invasion, induced G2-phase arrest, and decreased MYC, CDK1, and CCNB1 mRNA expression without inducing senescence. Drug-sensitivity screens suggested candidate agents, such as AT-7519, that warrant further investigation in PPP2R1A-high HCC.ConclusionPPP2R1A is consistently overexpressed in HCC and contributes to the malignant phenotype at least partly through cell-cycle regulation. These findings are hypothesis-generating, and the potential diagnostic, prognostic, or therapeutic value of PPP2R1A in HCC requires dedicated prospective and functional validation.
records.authors: Tan J, Zeng Y, Wu H, Liang Y, Qiu Y, Mo Q, Luo Y, He J, Wang Y, Yin H, Chen P, Li M, Lin H.

records.title: Key Genes Related to the Integrated Stress Response Identified Through Bioinformatics and Clinical Experiments in Ovarian Aging.
records.abstract: BackgroundOvarian aging (OA) compromises female fertility, but its relationship with the integrated stress response (ISR) remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify ISR-related genes associated with OA and assess their expression through experimental validation.MethodsDifferentially expressed genes from an OA-related transcriptomic dataset were intersected with ISR-related genes to identify candidates. Machine learning and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis were used to prioritize key genes. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) and immune cell enrichment analysis were performed to explore associated biological features. Gene expression was assessed using reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR).ResultsBAG2, BLVRB, PHB2, and STC1 were identified as key genes, with individual areas under the ROC curve (AUCs) ranging from 0.73 to 0.77 in the discovery dataset. All four genes were downregulated in OA samples in the transcriptomic analysis. GSEA revealed enrichment of ribosome-related pathways in gene expression profiles correlated with BAG2, BLVRB, and PHB2 (adjusted P ConclusionThese findings identify four candidate ISR-related genes associated with OA, with experimental expression support for three genes. Their biological roles and clinical relevance require further investigation in independent cohorts and functional studies before diagnostic or therapeutic applications can be considered.

records.title: Comparative foliar elicitation with yeast extract and sodium butyrate reshapes terpenoid metabolism in Salviaofficinalis.
records.abstract: The industrial utilization of Salvia officinalis L. depends on cost-effective and scalable strategies for improving the consistent production of high-value bioactive terpenoids. In this study, two non-transgenic foliar elicitation strategies, yeast extract (YE, 2 g L-1) and sodium butyrate (NaB, 25 and 50 mM), were evaluated for their ability to reprogram terpenoid metabolism in S. officinalis. Integrated GC-MS metabolite profiling and qRT-PCR analysis showed that the two elicitors induced distinct transcriptional and metabolic responses. YE promoted coordinated upregulation of MVA and MEP pathway genes, resulting in moderate enrichment of β-caryophyllene (4.28-fold) and ferruginol (2.92-fold) while largely preserving the native monoterpene-rich chemotype. In contrast, NaB induced a markedly asymmetric transcriptional response, characterized by strong upregulation of the sesquiterpene synthase SoHUMS (>15-fold), together with substantial accumulation of β-caryophyllene (>10-fold; 31% of the total extract) and ferruginol (3.55-fold; 4.60% of the total extract). NaB treatment was also associated with the appearance of α-humulene, caryophyllene oxide, α-gurjunene, and 14β-pregnane, suggesting activation of otherwise low-abundance sesquiterpene- and sterol-associated metabolic pathways. These metabolic changes were accompanied by enhanced antiproliferative activity of the extracts against MCF-7 breast cancer cells. Molecular docking and ADMET analyses provided supportive, hypothesis-generating evidence that ferruginol and other NaB-enriched terpenoids may contribute to this activity. Overall, these findings identify sodium butyrate as a non-transgenic foliar elicitor capable of redirecting isoprenoid metabolism in S. officinalis and provide a practical framework for improving the phytochemical quality of medicinal plant biomass.

records.title: Identifying potential targets in endothelial to mesenchymal transition-mediated atherosclerosis using bioinformatics and machine learning.
records.abstract: BackgroundEndothelial to mesenchymal transition (EndMT) is a key driver of atherosclerosis (AS). This study integrated multiple RNA transcriptomic and single-cell transcriptomic datasets to identify shared gene expression signatures between EndMT and AS.MethodsGEO expression profiles were analyzed via differential expression, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and functional enrichment analyses. A Random Forest model evaluated key genes, validating their expression and diagnostic performance. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) further assessed their expression patterns, and a Transcription Factor (TF)-mRNA-miRNA regulatory network.ResultsFifteen overlapping genes were identified, from which six candidates were screened through a Protein-Protein Interaction (PPI) network and validated in vitro. The application of a Random Forest model identified two key hub genes, CCL5 and IL1B, which were significantly upregulated. Their diagnostic Area Under the Curve (AUC) was >0.7 when assessed separately and increased to >0.85 in a combined model. Three shared TFs (NFKBIA, NFKB1, RELA) of the Nuclear Factor-kappa B (NF-κB) pathway were identified, highlighting its central role in disease progression.ConclusionsCCL5 and IL1B are key genes potentially regulating EndMT-mediated AS via inflammatory pathways including Nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain-like (NOD-like) receptor, Tumor Necrosis Factor (TNF), and NF-κB signaling, offering promising diagnostic and therapeutic targets for AS.
records.authors: Hou Z, Chen S, Cui Y, Ma Q, Chen J, Shu K.

records.title: Design and synthesis of butein derivatives for the treatment of liver fibrosis through modulation of the PDE4B/CREB pathway.
records.abstract: A total of 27 butein analogues, including 25 previously unreported compounds, were designed and synthesized and evaluated for their anti-fibrotic activities using a COL1A1-based screening model in TGF-β1-stimulated LX-2 cells. Among them, compound 11b exhibited potent inhibition of hepatic Stellate cell activation with a favorable cytotoxicity profile, and effectively suppressed the expression of COL1A1, TGF-β1, and α-SMA. In vivo, 11b significantly attenuated liver injury and fibrosis in a bile duct ligation (BDL)-induced mouse model. Primary mechanistic studies revealed that 11b exerted its anti-fibrotic effects through modulation of phosphodiesterase 4B (PDE4B) associated signaling, accompanied by enhanced CREB transcriptional activity and suppression of inflammatory responses. Our study provides valuable information for developing this kind of compound into a new class of candidates for the treatment of liver fibrosis, and compound 11b is worthy of further investigation as an ideal lead compound.
records.authors: Zeng Q, Fan R, Yin Z, Jia X, Zhang N, Xue H, Li F, Zhang Y, Liu Y.

records.title: SHIELD: An Argonaute-powered immobilization-free homogeneous electrochemical biosensor for ultrasensitive viable pathogen detection.
records.abstract: Accurate identification of viable foodborne pathogens is critical for preventing foodborne disease outbreaks. Herein, we developed a SHIELD platform (Sensitive Homogeneous Immobilization-free Electrochemical Live-bacteria Detection based on Argonaute). This strategy uses Argonaute-guided cleavage as the main electrochemical transduction mechanism, bypassing the reproducibility problems related to surface-fixed sensors. Crucially, the system effectively eliminates false positives from dead bacteria by incorporating Propidium Monoazide (PMA) pretreatment, which selectively blocks residual DNA from dead bacteria. Combined with the highly specific DNA cleavage capability of Argonaute, this ensures the exclusive detection of viable Salmonella typhimurium. In the detection workflow, the target DNA undergoes isothermal amplification (LAMP) to generate abundant amplicons. Subsequently, target-activated Argonaute programmatically cleaves dual methylene blue (MB)-biotin labeled electrochemical probes. Unreacted probes are removed via streptavidin magnetic separation, generating a significantly enhanced "signal-on" response. This platform achieves a remarkable limit of detection down to 1 CFU/mL within 70 min. Synergizing the specificity of PMA and Argonaute with the efficiency of an immobilization-free design, SHIELD demonstrates a reliable and innovative electrochemical biosensing paradigm, offering a promising solution for the rapid, sensitive screening of viable foodborne pathogens.
records.authors: Qiao J, Bai B, Zhang Y, Yan W, Lu W, Yang Y, Wang S.

records.title: RcbHLH79 negatively regulates 1,3,5-trimethoxybenzene biosynthesis and flower scent in roses.
records.abstract: Roses hold significant ornamental, economic, and cultural value, particularly for their diverse fragrances. Among the volatiles, 1,3,5-trimethoxybenzene (TMB), unique to ancient Chinese roses, contributes to their tea-like scent. Despite its significance, the molecular mechanisms regulating TMB synthesis remain poorly understood. This study integrates multi-omics approaches and molecular biology techniques to uncover the regulatory network of TMB biosynthesis in Rosa chinensis 'Old Blush'. We identified 18,186 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and three differentially accumulated metabolites (DAMs) across five developmental stages. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses highlighted RcbHLH79 as a critical regulator of TMB synthesis. We functionally validated the regulatory role of RcbHLH79 using RNAi, overexpression, yeast one-hybrid (Y1H), Western blot and dual-luciferase assays. The results demonstrate that RcbHLH79 directly binds to the RcOOMT1 promoter to repress its transcription, but not that of RcOOMT2, thereby negatively regulating TMB synthesis. This study elucidates the regulatory role of RcbHLH79 in TMB production and provides valuable insights for molecular breeding aimed at improving rose fragrance.
records.authors: Wu J, Xu J, Gong F, Li S, Cao Y, Jing W, Zhang Y, Zhang D.

records.title: Multi-omics and receptor-level computational analyses identify candidate bitterness-related metabolites during Musang king durian pulp ripening.
records.abstract: Musang King durian pulp develops a mild bitter aftertaste during ripening, but its metabolite basis remains unclear. Here, pulp from four ripening stages was analyzed using integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic profiling. Ripening was associated with marked shifts in amino acid metabolism, vitamin B6 metabolism, phenylpropanoid biosynthesis, and flavonoid/glycoside-related pathways. Immature pulp was enriched in pyridoxal, pyridoxamine, rutin, epicatechin, and tricetin, suggesting an early phenolic- and vitamin B6-related profile potentially linked to bitterness and defense metabolism. During ripening, bitter amino acids and bitter flavonoids, including L-phenylalanine, naringenin, and phloretin, accumulated and may contribute to the mild bitterness of ripe pulp. Co-expression analysis and qPCR supported pathway remodeling, while molecular docking and dynamics simulations predicted potential binding of the three candidates to the human bitter taste receptor TAS2R39, although receptor activation was not experimentally tested. These findings identify candidate metabolites and pathways for further sensory and functional validation.
records.authors: Yan T, Yuan S, Zhang S, Li Z, Tang Y, Wang R, Xiao Y, Fan R, Lai Y, Nan J, Zhang Y, Ao P.

records.title: Intermolecular interactions and structural evolution of candidate soy protein isolate/xylitol adhesives under heat treatment and tannic acid modulation.
records.abstract: This study investigated the effects of the soy protein isolate (SPI)/xylitol (XY) ratio, heat treatment, and tannic acid (TA) incorporation on the physicochemical and structural properties of SPI/XY. All formulations exhibited shear-thinning behavior, with composition-dependent differences in viscosity, wettability, water mobility, molecular interactions, and microstructure. The low SPI/XY ratio (6:4) produced an insufficient protein-polyol network, whereas a high ratio (12:4) promoted protein aggregation and structural heterogeneity. The 10:4 formulation exhibited the most balanced structure and greatest resistance to heat-induced rearrangement. Heating altered SPI conformation and water mobility, indicating that thermal treatment may either facilitate molecular association or destabilize poorly balanced systems. TA increased apparent viscosity, restricted water mobility, and modified the thermal and structural characteristics through multivalent non-covalent associations. These findings establish relationships among thermal processing, molecular interactions, and physicochemical stability. Further testing using standardized food-interface models is required to validate the practical performance of these systems as plant-based meat adhesives.
records.authors: Zhang Z, Li Y, Long J, Wang P, Wang S, Liu H.

records.title: Honeybee (Apis mellifera) venom and its bioactive peptides tertiapin and apamin modulate the proteome of SARS-CoV-2-infected cells.
records.abstract: The continuing emergence of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) variants highlights the need for host-directed antiviral strategies with specific molecular mechanisms. Honeybee (Apis mellifera) venom (HBV) contains bioactive peptides with immunomodulatory and membrane-active properties, yet their effects on SARS-CoV-2 infection remain insufficiently characterized. Here, we investigated the antiviral activity and proteomic impact of whole HBV and two venom-derived peptides, apamin (APA) and tertiapin (TERT), in human angiotensin-converting enzyme 2-expressing HEK293 cells infected with SARS-CoV-2 spike-pseudotyped lentiviral particles. Cell viability and membrane integrity assays showed that HBV, APA, and TERT exerted limited cytotoxicity at the tested concentrations. In pseudovirus infectivity assays, HBV displayed the strongest inhibitory effect, reducing viral infectivity to 61.3% at 2 μg/mL, whereas APA reduced it to 73.3% at 0.5 μg/mL, and TERT showed weaker inhibitory activity. Comparative nano-liquid chromatography matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization tandem mass spectrometry revealed treatment-associated remodelling of the host-cell proteome. A shared signature of 215 proteins across HBV-, APA-, and TERT-treated infected cells was enriched in binding and catalytic activity, translational proteins, metabolite interconversion enzymes, cytoskeletal proteins, and pathways linked to integrin, Wnt, interferon, and Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription signalling. Protein-protein interaction analysis highlighted functional clusters associated with cytoplasmic translation, viral mRNA translation, and the Sec61 translocon complex, with EFTUD2, EPRS1, and HSPA4 emerging as central hubs. HBV treatment additionally promoted immune-related and interferon-stimulated gene products, including factors involved in innate antiviral defence, cytoskeletal organization, ion transport, and membrane structural reinforcement. These findings suggest that HBV reduces SARS-CoV-2 pseudovirus infectivity through a multifactorial host-directed mechanism involving antiviral signalling, cellular architecture, and proteostasis, supporting further investigation of bee venom-derived compounds as antiviral agents.
records.authors: Matuszewska-Mach E, Konieczny I, Matysiak J, Rzetecka-Mańka N, Warowicka A.

records.title: Aggregate Deep Visual Proteomics reveals selective organization of α-synuclein inclusions
records.abstract: α-Synuclein inclusions, the lesions typical of Parkinson’s disease, have been interpreted as protective deposits, toxic species or failed degradation products, each predicting a different composition and correlating that enrichment with neuron dysfunction and eventual degeneration. Distinguishing them requires measuring what an inclusion concentrates relative to the cell that built it. Here we developed Aggregate Deep Visual Proteomics, which uses ultrasensitive mass spectrometry to profile laser-microdissected inclusions against the remainder of the same cell or a matched host. In HEK293 cells, iPSC-derived dopaminergic neurons and post-mortem patient brain, each inclusion concentrated a selective subset of its cell’s proteome, independent of abundance and dominated by membrane, in neurons largely presynaptic. Inclusions took up whole assemblies, with subunits moving together in 421 of 438 complexes, and the V-ATPase alone was enriched in all three systems. Degradation cargo stayed with the receptors that route it, consistent with sequestration and failed degradation acting together. Neuritic and somatic inclusions differed, the former rich in UBQLN2 and the latter in intermediate filaments. In the cell line, phosphorylated α-synuclein was tenfold higher in the inclusion than in the rest of the cell, with about one third of the rise already present before an inclusion was visible. Measured against its host, the composition of an inclusion becomes a readout of how it formed and a source of candidate markers and therapeutic targets.

records.title: GMP-Cor: Quantifying Transcriptional Dysregulation in Antibiotic Tolerance and Persistence
records.abstract: When cells are exposed to stress, they typically activate stress-response pathways and enter a regulated growth-arrest. But what if the stress overwhelms these pathways? In such cases, cells may enter a  disrupted growth-arrest - a poorly adapted, abrupt cessation of growth, characterized by a broad distribution of lag times upon stress removal [1]. This distribution underlies antibiotic persistence during stress recovery[2]. Therefore, gaining a deeper understanding of the disrupted growth-arrest is important for developing more effective antibiotic therapies. In this study, we perform single cell RNA-seq on bacteria in disrupted conditions. We develop GMP-Cor: a metric to quantify dysregulation and analyze gene-gene correlation patterns in sparse single-cell data. We find that gene-gene correlations are significantly reduced in disrupted cells compared to regulated cells, providing direct evidence that this tolerance-enhanced state, along with its increased membrane sensitivity, is associated with global-dysregulation. We demonstrate that GMP-Cor can extend to other biological systems, such as persistent cancer cells, where it separates proliferating from drug-arrested cells[3].
records.authors: Gutfreund A, Rotem A, Ronin I, Rosenthal AZ, Agam O, Balaban NQ.

records.title: Defining nutrient dependencies of intestinal  Klebsiella pneumoniae  guides rational probiotic engineering
records.abstract: Summary  Klebsiella pneumoniae is a major cause of antibiotic-resistant infections, yet the ecological determinants enabling its intestinal expansion remain poorly defined. Here, we combined  in vivo transcriptomics and metabolomics to identify carbon sources exploited by  K. pneumoniae during colonization of the antibiotic-disrupted gut across strains and dietary contexts. Despite its metabolic breadth,  K. pneumoniae consistently exploited a restricted set of substrates, including arabinose, raffinose, oligogalacturonate, arabitol, xylose, and gluconate, that contributed to intestinal fitness, with related metabolic signatures also observed in antibiotic-treated human samples. Guided by these findings, we engineered  Escherichia coli Nissle to enhance consumption of these nutrients and assembled a defined consortium, NICHE, designed to reinforce colonization resistance through nutrient competition. NICHE restricted intestinal expansion of multidrug-resistant and hypervirulent  K. pneumoniae in preventive and therapeutic settings, with efficacy influenced by dietary nutrient availability. Together, this work defines exploitable  K. pneumoniae nutrient dependencies and a framework for rational probiotic engineering.
records.authors: Zhou Y, David C, Kulkarni G, Long T, Garzón MJ, Prados J, Kloehn J, Rohr OV, Meister I, Xavier KB, Ubeda C, Yu F, Chen L, Becattini S.

records.title: GSET: Gene Signals from Embedding Trajectories select compact contexts for mechanistic GRN inference
records.abstract: Mechanistic inference of gene regulatory networks from temporal transcriptomic data can become computationally prohibitive at transcriptome scale, making gene selection an important determinant of which regulatory relationships can be recovered. However, gene selection for GRN inference commonly relies on static expression or co-expression structure, rather than prioritizing dynamically informative genes whose temporal patterns capture how transcriptional programs change and relate to one another. We introduce GSET (Gene Signals from Embedding Trajectories), an upstream retrieval framework that extracts dynamic information from temporal gene embeddings using two complementary signals: an optimal transport residual, which captures gene-specific deviations from global embedding movement, and a KL divergence, which detects changes in local co-expression neighborhoods. Temporal gene-embedding similarity identifies static transcriptional programs, whereas vectorial GSET signals represent coordinated temporal changes among genes, complementing this static structure. Lagged comparisons of these signals further prioritize temporal relationships between programs and candidate bridge genes associated with their transitions. Integrated with CardamomOT, GSET combines static program cores with dynamically retrieved bridge genes into compact, program-informed gene sets for mechanistic GRN inference. In synthetic benchmarks, at equal gene budget these sets recover more of the regulatory links between programs than static selections of the same size, and inference on the edges within the set is comparable to that of the full-gene model on the same gene pairs. On a time course of mouse fibroblasts reprogrammed into induced pluripotent stem cells, GSET traces the transition from the fibroblast program to the cell-cycle program. By providing a dynamic retrieval layer upstream of GRN inference, GSET nominates bridge genes as candidate regulators of cell-state transitions, which, once refined by a mechanistic model such as CardamomOT and confirmed by perturbation experiments, could open the way to controlling these transitions.

records.title: Resolving how genetic perturbations act through gene regulatory paths
records.abstract: Perturb-seq measures transcriptional responses to thousands of genetic perturbations, but each gene’s response mixes the contributions of many regulatory paths, so how a perturbation acts cannot be resolved from expression alone, however large the model. Here we present REGA-perturb, which supplies this missing information rather than adding model complexity: reference epigenomes define a scaffold of possible transcription factor (TF)–regulatory element–gene paths, and perturbation responses, pooled through shared latent programs, determine how each path is used, requiring only RNA measurements. Across three CRISPR interference screens totaling 2.4 million cells, REGA-perturb inferred TF–target relationships that agreed with ChIP-seq binding with a gain over random more than four times that of the best existing method, separated candidate direct from indirect targets, and predicted targets of TFs withheld from training. It also inferred perturbation-induced changes in TF activity not reflected in TF transcript levels, and resolved perturbation-specific regulatory rewiring in which opposing regulatory changes cancel at the expression level.

records.title: Integrative hdWGCNA and Machine-Learning Analysis Identifies Gastric Cancer Candidate Genes and Supports a Functional Role for KRT18.
records.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is a frequently detected malignancy worldwide. This study aimed to identify epithelial cell-associated candidate genes in GC by integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data and to explore their biological relevance using computational analyses, with in vitro functional assessment limited to KRT18. Multi-omics data were integrated to investigate the molecular mechanisms of GC. The single-cell data were processed using Seurat. Subsequently, CellChat was employed to analyze cell communication. The co-expression network of epithelial cells was constructed using high-dimensional WGCNA (hdWGCNA), and module hub genes were identified. Differential expression analysis was performed with Limma, and candidate genes were screened using LASSO and SVR-RFE. Compounds were computationally prioritized using Enrichr and DSigDB; molecular docking was not used as validation. Lastly, the biological function of KRT18 was examined in GC cells. Five candidate genes were identified: GPRC5A, KRT18, EPCAM, CLDN7, and CLDN4. These genes were associated with E2F TARGETS, GLYCOLYSIS, and OXIDATIVE PHOSPHORYLATION and correlated with multiple inferred immune-cell fractions. Drug-set enrichment nominated genistein as a computational candidate but did not establish direct binding or therapeutic efficacy. In vitro assays showed that KRT18 knockdown reduced the viability, migration, and invasion of GC cells. These findings nominate exploratory epithelial cell-associated candidate genes in GC and provide functional evidence for KRT18; further external validation is required before clinical application.
records.authors: Ran Y, He Y, Huang Y, Li T.

records.title: Identification and Validation of Autophagy- and Inflammatory-Related Genes in Childhood Asthma via Integrated Bioinformatics and Clinical Samples.
records.abstract: Childhood asthma (CA) is a prevalent chronic airway disease, yet the roles of autophagy and inflammation in its pathogenesis remain poorly understood. Transcriptomic datasets were retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). Inflammation- and autophagy-related genes were identified using weighted gene co-expression network analysis and consensus clustering and intersected with differentially expressed genes (DEGs) to identify candidate genes. Subsequently, 101 machine learning algorithm combinations were evaluated to select key genes for diagnostic model construction. Functional characterization involved immune infiltration analysis, gene set enrichment analysis, and transcription factor network construction. Mendelian randomization (MR) was used to assess potential causal relationships between key genes and CA, and gene expression was validated by quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) in clinical blood samples. The analysis identified 39 candidate genes associated with autophagy and inflammation. Machine learning identified 10 key genes, and the resulting diagnostic model achieved areas under the curve of 0.768, 0.751, and 0.710 in the training, test, and validation sets, respectively. Pathway and immune infiltration analyses revealed enrichment in signaling, metabolic, and immune-regulatory functions and significant correlations with immune cell infiltration. MR analysis suggested a potential causal association between genetically predicted STYXL1 expression and CA risk. qPCR analysis in five CA patients and five healthy controls showed expression patterns consistent with the transcriptomic findings. However, the small clinical validation cohort limits the generalizability of these results. This study identifies a 10-gene peripheral blood diagnostic signature associated with CA and highlights STYXL1 as a potential causal risk gene supported by genetic evidence. Larger clinical cohorts and functional studies are required to validate these findings.
records.authors: Huang M, Wu J, Xu D.

records.title: Network Pharmacology Identifies Stigmasterol as an Anti-Gastric Cancer Agent Targeting HSP90AA1 for Ubiquitin-Mediated Degradation.
records.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) remains a major cause of cancer mortality. We combined network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, public database analyses, and cell-based assays to investigate stigmasterol and heat shock protein 90 alpha family class A member 1 (HSP90AA1). Computational screening prioritized HSP90AA1 as a candidate target. In AGS and MKN-45 cells, stigmasterol treatment reduced cell viability and DNA synthesis, increased the proportion of Annexin V-positive cells, and decreased HSP90AA1 protein abundance. No statistically significant change in HSP90AA1 mRNA abundance was detected under the conditions tested. Increased ubiquitin signal in HSP90AA1 immunoprecipitates and attenuation of protein loss by MG-132 were consistent with proteasome involvement. Public database analyses showed higher HSP90AA1 expression in GC tissues and an association with clinical stage. These findings link stigmasterol treatment to HSP90AA1 downregulation in GC cells. Direct binding, the contribution of HSP90AA1 loss to the cellular effects, and in vivo efficacy remain to be established.
records.authors: Zhang H, Zhang Y, Ling Y, Jiang G, Wu J, Shi X, Zhao Y.

records.title: First principles study of chalcogen vacancy effect on the optoelectronic and photocatalytic properties of transition metal dichalcogenides monolayers.
records.abstract: In working conditions, chalcogen vacancies spontaneously occur in two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) monolayers, affecting their optoelectronic and photocatalytic properties. To study how chalcogen vacancies affect such properties, we use quantum mechanical calculations considering prototypical MX2 (M = Mo, W, X = S and Se) TMDCs monolayers. Band structure calculations reveal that the introduction of vacancies produce electronic states about the Fermi level, hence resulting in the reduction of the band gap. Work function and electrostatic potential calculations show that the introduction of vacancies induce an asymmetry in the electrostatic potential, which may facilitate the charge separation; such feature is absent in a pristine monolayer. All the considered defective structures are capable of performing hydrogen evolution reaction, while co-catalyst is required to perform oxygen evolution reaction when used for water splitting. WS2 and WSe2 defective monolayers can serve as promising candidates for reducing CO2 into useful chemical products. The presented results show that vacancy-containing TMDCs monolayers own photocatalytic capabilities compared to the pristine counterparts, thus showing that defective TMD monolayers have prospective applications and should not be regarded as flawed products to be discarded. Finally, the results might constitute guidelines for the experimental synthesis of vacancy-engineered MX2 monolayers for optoelectronic devices and photocatalytic applications.
records.authors: Wahab T, Cammarata A, Polcar T.

records.title: Gut-Induced Synuclein Propagation: A New Mechanism in Neurodegenerative Disease.
records.abstract: Gut-induced synuclein propagation has emerged as a potential mechanism linking gastrointestinal disturbances with the development and progression of Parkinson disease and related synucleinopathies. These disorders are characterized by progressive accumulation and spreading of misfolded α-synuclein (α-Syn), leading to selective neuronal dysfunction and degeneration. Although traditionally considered brain-centered diseases, increasing evidence indicates that gastrointestinal abnormalities, peripheral α-Syn pathology, and gut-associated immune alterations may precede neurological manifestations, suggesting that peripheral processes can influence disease evolution. Here, we review clinical, pathological, and experimental evidence supporting the role of intestinal environmental stress, microbial dysregulation, barrier dysfunction, and immune activation in promoting α-Syn misfolding, aggregation, and transmission through interconnected pathways. However, peripheral α-Syn abnormalities alone are unlikely to be sufficient to initiate neurodegeneration, indicating the presence of additional biological constraints. We propose a cumulative-threshold and biological-gates framework in which α-Syn induction, seed formation, propagation efficiency, anatomical connectivity, and neuronal vulnerability collectively determine whether gut-associated pathology progresses into a self-sustaining neurodegenerative cascade. Understanding the determinants that enable gut-induced synuclein propagation may provide new insights into disease heterogeneity and guide biomarker development and mechanism-based therapeutic strategies for synucleinopathies.
records.journal: The Neuroscientist : a review journal bringing neurobiology, neurology and psychiatry
records.authors: Sun Y, Li B, Ye K.

records.title: The Tartary Buckwheat FtMYB15 Coordinates Cadmium Uptake and Detoxification by Regulating FtZIP3 and FtGSTU19 Expression.
records.abstract: Tartary buckwheat (Fagopyrum tataricum) is a crop of significant value, yet its cultivation in cadmium (Cd)-contaminated soils poses risks to food safety. Understanding the molecular mechanisms of Cd uptake is crucial for developing strategies to minimize its accumulation. Here, we demonstrate that the Tartary buckwheat transcription factor FtMYB15 promotes Cd2+ influx and enhances Cd accumulation in transgenic hairy roots. Yeast one-hybrid (Y1H) and electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA) results indicate that FtMYB15 binds to the MYB-binding sites (MBS) of the FtZIP3 promoter, thereby upregulating the expression of FtZIP3, which encodes a zinc/iron-regulated transporter-like protein. Overexpression of FtZIP3 similarly enhances Cd2+ influx and Cd accumulation in buckwheat hairy roots. Further analysis reveals that FtMYB15 binds to the MBS in the promoter of the tau glutathione S-transferase gene FtGSTU19 and upregulates its expression in buckwheat hairy roots both before and after Cd exposure. Overexpression of FtGSTU19 in buckwheat hairy roots enhances Cd detoxification capacity via its glutathione transferase activity, thereby alleviating Cd-induced oxidative stress. Heterologous expression of FtGSTU19 increases Cd tolerance in Arabidopsis. Expression of FtMYB15, FtZIP3, and FtGSTU19 is induced by Cd stress. Together, these findings demonstrate that FtMYB15 directly regulates the expression of FtZIP3 and FtGSTU19, thereby coordinating Cd uptake and detoxification in plants.
records.authors: Zhang X, Wei J, Tang X, Wang A, Zhou Y, Mai S, Liu Y, Yang Y, Li X, Wang J.

records.title: Pediatric suprasellar primary CNS lymphoma with cavernous sinus invasion and ischemic stroke: a case report and systematic review.
records.abstract: BackgroundPrimary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL) is an exceptionally rare pediatric malignancy, accounting for less than 1% of childhood central nervous system tumors. Suprasellar involvement is particularly uncommon and frequently mimics more prevalent lesions, including germinoma and Langerhans cell histiocytosis, often resulting in delayed diagnosis.Case presentationWe report the case of a 12-year-old immunocompetent girl with a history of Epstein-Barr virus infection and a previously resected atypical smooth muscle tumor of the ileum who presented with high-grade fever, severe headache, and diplopia. She rapidly deteriorated neurologically, and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a rim-enhancing sellar-suprasellar lesion invading the cavernous sinus, causing critical internal carotid artery stenosis with bilateral watershed cerebral infarctions. Emergency endoscopic endonasal transsphenoidal decompression was performed. Histopathological examination confirmed anaplastic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) of the non-germinal center B-cell subtype. Despite prompt surgical intervention and initiation of systemic chemotherapy, the patient developed central diabetes insipidus, severe hemodynamic instability, and ultimately died within few months.MethodsA systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Ovid, and Scopus were searched from database inception to 31 May 2026 to identify published cases of pediatric suprasellar primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL).ResultsFive studies comprising seven previously reported pediatric patients met the inclusion criteria. Six of seven historical patients (85.7%) achieved complete radiological remission, Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) or large-cell B-cell lymphoma was reported in four of seven patients (57.1%). Most patients achieved complete remission following intensive CNS-directed chemotherapy, although persistent endocrine dysfunction remained common. In contrast to previously reported cases, our patient presented with fulminant cavernous sinus invasion, critical internal carotid artery stenosis, and ischemic watershed cerebral infarctions, representing an exceptionally aggressive clinical phenotype.ConclusionPediatric suprasellar PCNSL is a rare but highly aggressive disease that should be considered in children presenting with diabetes insipidus, pituitary stalk lesions, or rapidly progressive suprasellar masses. Progressive radiologic evolution or atypical vascular complications should prompt early histopathological confirmation to facilitate timely diagnosis and initiation of treatment.

records.title: TERRA: an induced responder to telomere dysfunction.
records.abstract: Telomeric repeat-containing RNA (TERRA) has long been viewed as a constitutive component of telomeres. However, accumulating experimental evidence suggests that TERRA is instead a stress-responsive signal produced specifically at dysfunctional telomeres. Across yeasts and mammals, TERRA abundance changes as telomeres shorten or become damaged, engaging the appropriate maintenance pathway through interactions with shelterin, chromatin regulators and DNA repair factors, and through the controlled formation of RNA:DNA hybrids (R-loops). In telomerase-negative cells, transient accumulation of TERRA and R-loops promotes homology-directed telomere elongation. In telomerase-positive cells, TERRA appears to direct telomerase activity selectively toward short telomeres. When telomere damage remains unresolved, sustained TERRA expression and persistent R-loops drive cells toward senescence, inflammatory signaling and crisis-associated cell death. We propose here that TERRA functions as a molecular rheostat at damaged telomeres: transient and spatially controlled induction restores chromosome-end integrity, whereas persistent accumulation results in the removal of compromised cells from the proliferative pool. Defining how cells set these switch points will be essential for elucidating how TERRA shapes ageing and disease and for harnessing its therapeutic potential.
records.authors: Bento F, Andolfato M, Luke B, Azzalin CM.

records.title: Ca<sup>2+</sup> signature gates responsiveness to exogenous auxin in Arabidopsis roots.
records.abstract: Plants must continually balance growth with arrest, especially under stress. Auxin signaling acts as a central regulatory hub in this process, yet the mechanisms that dynamically tune auxin signaling in real time remain unknown. Here, we use the light-gated, Ca2+-permeable Channelrhodopsin 2 variant XXM2.0 to optogenetically impose defined Ca2+ signatures on Arabidopsis root cells. Repetitive light activation triggers cytosolic Ca2+ signals that in turn suppress membrane depolarization and Ca2+ transients triggered by exogenous auxin. Moreover, prolonged optogenetic Ca2+ stimulation affects auxin-responsive transcriptional reprogramming. As phenotypic output, reversible inhibition of root growth by suppressing cell division and elongation is observed. We further identify a candidate CaM7-CNGC14 module that likely mediates Ca2+-dependent gating of responsiveness to exogenous auxin as well as Ca2+-dependent root growth inhibition. Our study thus introduces a synthetic biology approach to decompose calcium-auxin crosstalk in plant cells, and demonstrates that optogenetically imposed cytosolic Ca2+ signals act as dynamic regulators of auxin susceptibility in roots.
records.authors: Song H, Baudon A, Freund M, Randuch M, Pěnčík A, Novák O, He Z, Kaufmann K, Li N, Gilliham M, Friml J, Hedrich R, Huang S.

records.title: SUMOylated DDX3 Promotes HBV Replication and Tumor Growth of Hepatocellular Carcinoma via TRIM28-DDX3-KLF4α Signaling Axis.
records.abstract: DDX3 has dual biological functions of regulating cell proliferation and antiviral effects. Herein, we focus on SUMOylation-mediated DDX3 in the interplay from hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection to HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma (HBV-HCC) progression. We identified dynamic regulation of SUMOylation and DeSUMOylation of DDX3 at four key lysine (K) residues (K81/K208/K215/K564) in response to HBV infection. During the early stage of HBV acute infection, SENP1 interacts with DDX3 to keep DDX3 deSUMOylation for inhibiting HBV replication. During persistent HBV replication, as SENP1 downregulation and HBV polymerase accumulation, DDX3 disassociates with SENP1 to bind with TRIM28, which induces DDX3 SUMOylation. Meanwhile, SUMOylated DDX3 enhances alternative splicing of KLF4 mRNAs to generate KLF4α isoform that involves in Cyclin D1-mediated cell cycle progression, weakens tumor suppressor function of DDX3 and promotes HBV-HCC. Moreover, DDX3 expression is positively correlated with KLF4 mRNA, and high DDX3 level with low TRIM28 expression indicates a better overall survival for HBV-HCC patients. Our findings reveal the dynamic regulation between SUMOylation and deSUMOylation of DDX3, including mediating HBV gene transcription, virus antigen secretion, and cell proliferation. Furthermore, the TRIM28-DDX3-KLF4 axis as a novel therapeutic target for HBV-HCC, exhibiting the dual ability to inhibit tumor progression and disrupt the HBV-host interaction.
records.authors: Yang Y, Kong T, Wang B, Jin X, Huang L, Zhang N, Tang S, Syed SE, Liang S.

records.title: CA1-associated epithelial-state remodeling in colon cancer cells exposed to polystyrene nanoplastics: Integrated multi-omics and In vitro analyses.
records.abstract: Polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs) directly encounter the gastrointestinal epithelium after ingestion, yet the epithelial molecular states linking exposure to colon cancer cell behavior remain unclear. We integrated bulk transcriptomics, interpretable machine learning, WGCNA, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, structural analyses, and in vitro experiments to investigate CA1-associated epithelial responses. Intersecting 2139 colon cancer differentially expressed genes with 766 styrene-associated genes yielded 159 candidates. Among 45 classification models, LASSO + GBM ranked highest in an exploratory cross-cohort comparison, with an apparent training AUC of 1.000 and comparison-cohort AUCs of 0.999 and 0.925. CA1 had the highest SHAP importance and was located in the WGCNA module most strongly associated with tumor/normal status. Single-cell and organoid analyses showed attenuation of epithelial CA1/CA2 and carbonic anhydrase-bicarbonate-related programs, with concordant spatial trends; TCGA-COAD and Human Protein Atlas data further supported reduced CA1 expression. Low CA1 was associated with reduced metabolic and bicarbonate-related programs and enhanced inflammatory signaling. Docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics showed only weak, dynamic styrene-CA1 contacts. In HCT116 cells, PS-NPs decreased CA1, CA2, and Occludin expression, altered stress-, inflammation-, and apoptosis-related molecules, and increased scratch closure, with generally stronger changes at higher doses and after Tioxolone co-treatment. Collectively, these findings identify a CA1/CA2-low epithelial state associated with PS-NP exposure and suggest that CA1-associated epithelial-state remodeling may be part of the cellular response to PS-NPs.
records.journal: Food and chemical toxicology : an international journal published for the British Industrial Biological Research Association
records.authors: Guo B, Song Y, Qin J, Wu X, Chen Z, Guo J, Sun J, Pei L.

records.title: Rethinking inflammaging: Spatiotemporal decoupling and the failure of inflammatory regulation.
records.abstract: Chronic low-grade inflammation (inflammaging) is a central feature of aging, yet its magnitude and trajectory vary substantially among individuals and tissues. This variability is not fully explained by chronological age or cumulative inflammatory exposure. We therefore examine inflammaging through a spatiotemporal framework focused on how inflammatory responses are initiated, contained, resolved, and distributed across tissues. The framework integrates established mechanisms-including defective resolution, epigenetic drift, cellular senescence and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), cytosolic DNA sensing, inflammasome activation, cytokine dysregulation, and loss of immunometabolic flexibility. We use the term spatiotemporal decoupling to describe the observable divergence between chronological age and inflammatory state across time, tissues, and individuals. The term does not denote a newly discovered molecular pathway; its value lies in organizing existing evidence around failures of regulatory closure and in generating testable predictions about inflammatory persistence and tissue heterogeneity. This perspective suggests that systemic inflammatory markers alone are unlikely to identify the mechanism sustaining inflammation in a given patient or tissue. Therapeutic strategies should therefore be matched to the dominant process and disease context, with attention to tissue delivery, host defense, repair, and other consequences of pathway inhibition. Candidate approaches include restoration of resolution, modulation of senescent-cell burden or SASP, selective control of innate immune sensing and cytokine signaling, and improvement of metabolic flexibility. Overall, the review distinguishes established components of inflammaging from their proposed integration in a spatiotemporal model and identifies the evidence needed to test its translational relevance.
records.authors: Deng X, Wang L, Luo M, Wu J.

records.title: Ethnopharmacological basis of Huangqin Tang in colorectal cancer: Repurposing a classical formula to overcome PD-1 resistance via lactylation blockade.
records.abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevanceHuangqin Tang (HQT), documented in the Shanghan Lun, is traditionally prescribed for "dysenteric disorders" (Li Ji). Modern clinical studies confirm its efficacy against ulcerative colitis and colorectal cancer-associated inflammation, providing a verified traditional basis for investigating its immunomodulatory effects in colorectal malignancy. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.Aim of the studyThis study aimed to investigate the regulatory role of lactate-induced protein lactylation in MIF-driven PD-1 resistance and to determine if HQT can reverse this phenotype through metabolic reprogramming.Materials and methodsCT26-bearing BALB/c mice were administered HQT intragastrically combined with intraperitoneal anti-PD-1 antibodies. Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes were profiled by flow cytometry. Integrative transcriptomics and network pharmacology were utilized to screen candidate targets. LC-MS/MS-based lactylomic profiling identified specific modification sites. Lactate modulation assays, and site-directed mutagenesis (NF-κB1 K249R) coupled with rescue experiments were performed in vitro to validate the molecular cascade mechanistically.ResultsHQT synergized with anti-PD-1 to suppress tumor growth and prolong survival. This combination remodeled the immune microenvironment, increasing CD8+ T cells and M1-like macrophages while reducing M2 macrophages and MDSCs. Mechanistically, HQT inhibited tumor glycolysis and lactate production. Lactylomic analysis revealed that lactate induced NF-κB1 lysine 249 (K249) lactylation in CD4+ Tregs, driving MIF transcription. Introducing the K249R mutation abolished lactate-induced MIF expression and reversed immunosuppression. HQT effectively reduced NF-κB1 K249 lactylation, disrupting the MIF-driven feedback loop.ConclusionNF-κB1 K249 lactylation acts as a critical post-translational switch linking tumor glycolysis to Treg-mediated immunosuppression. HQT overcomes PD-1 resistance by suppressing this axis. These findings support combining metabolic intervention with immunotherapy and highlight K249 lactylation as a potential biomarker for treatment response.

records.title: Cycloastragenol suppresses LPS-induced macrophage inflammation and promotes M2 polarization via TLR4/NF-κB signaling and SIRT1-related regulation.
records.abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevanceAstragalus has long been used in traditional Chinese medicine for tonifying qi and supporting defensive functions. Cycloastragenol (CAG), a characteristic triterpenoid aglycone derived from Astragalus saponins, has emerging pharmacological relevance in immune and inflammatory regulation, but its role in macrophage inflammatory regulation and phenotypic remodeling remains insufficiently defined.Aim of the studyTo investigate the effects of CAG on lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced macrophage inflammation and phenotypic remodeling, focusing on Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) signaling and the involvement of sirtuin 1 (SIRT1).Materials and methodsRAW 264.7 macrophages were pretreated with CAG before LPS stimulation. Cytokine secretion, phenotype markers, and inflammatory signaling were evaluated by ELISA, immunofluorescence, reverse transcription quantitative PCR, and Western blotting. SIRT1-targeting small interfering RNA was used for functional evaluation. Network pharmacology prioritized candidate targets, while two acute inflammatory tissue transcriptomes and a normal human immune atlas provided expression context. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations explored candidate CAG-protein interactions.ResultsCompared with LPS alone, CAG at 20 μmol/L reduced TNF-α from 56.15 ± 2.17 to 25.80 ± 1.87 pg/mL and IL-1β from 93.55 ± 2.66 to 44.49 ± 2.85 pg/mL (mean ± standard deviation; both Tukey-adjusted P ConclusionsCAG attenuated LPS-induced macrophage inflammation and favored M2-associated phenotypic remodeling, with SIRT1 contributing to these effects. These findings support CAG as a promising Astragalus-derived immunomodulatory candidate and provide a basis for further exploration of its clinical translational potential.
records.authors: Zhou X, Qin S, Guo Y, Niu W, Chang X, Wang S, Wang J, Xu C.

records.title: Pharmacological characterization of clinical candidate CORT118335 (miricorilant), a selective glucocorticoid receptor modulator, in short-term preclinical models for MASLD.
records.abstract: CORT118335 (miricorilant) is a selective glucocorticoid receptor (GR) modulator (SGRM) that is currently being evaluated in clinical trials for the treatment of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), based on strong efficacy in mouse models. We reveal gene-specific GR modulation by CORT118335 in the mouse liver. In cell-based models, we evaluated the biological activity of CORT118335 metabolites. Metabolite CORT118335-P9a showed potent GR agonism, while metabolite CORT118335-P9b was largely inactive. CORT118335-P9a concentrations in the mouse liver were very low, and therefore neither metabolite is likely to contribute to the beneficial effects of CORT118335 in vivo. We investigated various aspects of CORT118335 activity in reducing lipid levels in the mouse liver using a model of short-term high-fat diet feeding. Daily administration of CORT118335 appeared to lower hepatic triglyceride rapidly within several days after treatment initiation, specifically in male mice, and these effects were reversed after 7 days of treatment discontinuation. No synergy was observed between the lipid-lowering effects of CORT118335 and the TRβ agonist VK2809 or the PPARγ agonist pioglitazone. At a dose of 6 mg/kg/day, CORT118335 induced evident transcriptional effects with modest lowering of hepatic triglyceride levels, while higher doses induced a more pronounced lipid lowering but less ongoing transcriptional activity for hepatic lipid metabolism genes. Altogether we substantiate the potential of selective GR modulation using CORT118335 as a lipid-lowering strategy in MASLD and highlight the complexity of SGRM-mediated hepatic lipid lowering.
records.authors: Moll TJA, Gentenaar M, Viho EM, Hoekstra AT, Afkir S, Deurloo JN, Laman PV, Schonk AW, Henst MW, Hunt HJ, Meijer OC, Kroon J.

records.title: Diagnostic performance of serum P85-Ab versus routine laboratory indicators for nasopharyngeal carcinoma: specificity assessment of P85-Ab in multiple control cohorts and its correlation with EBV DNA load.
records.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the diagnostic value of serum anti-BNLF2b total antibody (P85-Ab) for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) compared with routine laboratory indicators, validate its specificity across control cohorts, and explore the correlation between P85-Ab level and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) DNA load.MethodsWe retrospectively enrolled 331 participants from Xiangya Hospital of Central South University, comprising 115 patients with NPC, 46 patients with benign nasopharyngeal diseases, 118 healthy controls, and 52 EBV DNA-positive non-NPC individuals. Serum P85-Ab levels were detected. Routine blood parameters, biochemical indicators, and EBV DNA load were collected. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to assess diagnostic performance. The DeLong test was employed to compare differences in area under the curve (AUC), and Spearman's rank correlation analysis was performed to explore the association between P85-Ab level and EBV DNA load.ResultsThe P85-Ab positivity rate in the NPC group was 90.4% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 83.5%-95.1%), whereas all non-NPC controls were negative, yielding a specificity of 100% (95% CI: 92.3%-100.0%). The AUC for P85-Ab (0.949) significantly exceeded those for lymphocyte count (0.749), platelet count (0.668), globulin level (0.777) (all P ConclusionP85-Ab demonstrated 90.4% (95% CI: 83.5%-95.1%) sensitivity and 100% (95% CI: 92.3%-100.0%) specificity for NPC diagnosis, with diagnostic efficacy significantly surpassing both individual and combined routine laboratory indicators. No significant within-group monotonic association was detected between P85-Ab level and EBV DNA load. P85-Ab represents a convenient and reliable serological diagnostic marker for NPC.
records.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
records.authors: Tao Y, Wu Q, Liang Y, Wang K, Huang K, Yi B, Long L.

records.title: Tilianin counteracts doxorubicin-induced myocardial injury by downregulating mitophagy-dependent ferroptosis.
records.abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX)-induced cardiotoxicity (DIC) remains a major clinical limitation of this widely used chemotherapeutic agent. Dracocephalum moldavica L., a traditional Uyghur medicinal herb used for cardiovascular disorders, contains the flavonoid Tilianin (Til). Although Til exhibits reported cardioprotective properties, whether and how it mitigates DIC remains incompletely understood. In this study, we established DIC models in H9c2 cardiomyocytes and C57BL/6N mice and performed transcriptomic profiling to identify underlying mechanisms. Pharmacological interrogation using mitochondrial modulators (carbonyl cyanide m-chlorophenylhydrazone and cyclosporin A) and a ferroptosis inhibitor (ferrostatin-1) revealed that DOX triggers excessive mitophagy, leading to mitochondrial iron release and lipid peroxidation, ultimately driving mitophagy-dependent ferroptosis in cardiomyocytes. Til intervention attenuated DOX-induced cardiac dysfunction and myocardial injury in vivo and protected H9c2 cells from cytotoxicity in vitro by suppressing overactivated mitophagy and partially restoring iron homeostasis. These findings demonstrate that Til confers cardioprotection against DIC through modulation of the mitophagy-ferroptosis axis, supporting its potential as a candidate agent for managing chemotherapy-related cardiac injury.
records.authors: Yan M, Yuan Y, Huang C, Liu R, Ruan X, Chen Y, Hong Y, Ma X, Wang L, Guo X, Wang X, Cao W.

records.title: A TORC1-regulated H3K4me reader preserves promoter chromatin stability, and its degradation promotes meiotic remodeling.
records.abstract: Histone H3 lysine 4 methylation (H3K4me) is enriched at active promoters and promotes the recruitment of chromatin regulators, yet how cells protect H3K4-methylated promoter chromatin from inappropriate remodeling remains unknown. Here, we show that proteins encoded by the essential genes jmj3 and lid2 in fission yeast function coordinately to preserve promoter chromatin stability by limiting inappropriate H3K4me-dependent NuA4 acetyltransferase chromatin engagement. Decreased NuA4 at the chromatin restricts excessive histone H4 acetylation, SWI/SNF-mediated remodeling, and promoter-associated nucleosome-sized fragile particle (NSFP) destabilization, thereby maintaining transcriptional programs that support vegetative growth. Upon nutrient limitation, TOR complex 1 (TORC1) inactivation triggers Ubc14-Dbl4-dependent degradation of Jmj3 and Lid2, which results in programmed promoter remodeling. Moreover, loss of Jmj3/Lid2 couples meiotic transcriptional reprogramming with Rec12-dependent recombination hotspot activation, ensuring efficient meiotic differentiation. Together, our findings identify a nutrient-responsive mechanism that safeguards H3K4-methylated promoter chromatin while permitting regulated chromatin remodeling during developmental transition.
records.authors: Yun L, Zhang PC, Zhou K, Wang WT, Zhang KY, Wu YL, Zhu M, Ge HQ, Min T, Suo F, Du LL, Guo W, Sun LL, Wei Y.

records.title: Metal enrichment and downstream concentration gradients in an agricultural ditch draining a long-term fertilisation experiment.
records.abstract: Agricultural sediment surveys seldom quantify the downstream extent of metal enrichment. We measured Cd, Co, Cr, Cu, Ni, Pb and Zn in 24 surface sediment samples below the Palace Leas long-term fertilisation experiment at Cockle Park, UK. Eighteen samples formed a 452.5 m ditch transect, with three samples each from the receiving stream and an adjacent diffuse runoff line. Concentrations declined downstream, with the strongest enrichment near the ditch head. Metal-specific segmented-fit breakpoints were 104 m for Cd (5-95% resampling interval, 78-129 m), 159 m for Co (129-185 m) and 159 m for Cu (104-236 m). These do not establish a shared boundary. Cr and Ni breakpoint positions were poorly constrained. The first 150 m contained 66.3-96.7% of the distance-integrated excess concentration for six metals, an index of profile shape rather than stored metal mass. Cd contributed 73.9% of a partial seven-metal risk index, while Ni exceeded its freshwater probable effect level in one third of samples. As and Hg were not measured, so the screening may underestimate multi-element hazard and cannot establish the overall priority contaminant. Missing grain-size and organic-carbon measurements leave sediment sorting and carrier mixing unresolved. Uniform concentration scaling preserves within-metal spatial contrasts, but absolute concentrations and screening classifications remain conditional on unmeasured digestion recovery. Detection-limit-aware uncertainty was therefore used for risk-score scenarios. The upper reach is a candidate for follow-up monitoring; a 150 m mitigation zone requires validation with sediment-flux and repeated sampling data.

records.title: Changes in self-reported Long COVID in different variant-dominant phases of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic: the influence of vaccination on a diverse Israeli cohort study.
records.abstract: Purpose of researchLong COVID (LC) risk varies across SARS-CoV-2 variants, but causal inference is complicated by rising vaccine coverage coinciding with viral evolution. We examined how pre-infection vaccination status modified LC risk across different pandemic periods dominated by different variants, to disentangle the contributions of viral evolution and vaccine-induced immunity. In this prospective cohort study of Israeli adults with SARS-CoV-2 infections from July 2021-March 2023, participants completed baseline and follow-up online surveys ≥60 days post-infection. LC was defined as ≥3 symptoms within validated symptom clusters. Infections were assigned to an infection period corresponding to the predominant circulating variant (Wild type, Alpha, Delta, Omicron) at onset time. Pre-infection vaccination was categorized as unvaccinated (0-1 doses), partially vaccinated (2 doses), or fully vaccinated (≥3 doses). Generalized estimating equations estimated multivariable risk ratios, adjusted for age, sex, and follow-up time. Among 1715 participants reporting 2018 infections, LC was reported following 30·4% of infections. In models adjusted for vaccination, LC risk did not differ between the Delta and Omicron-dominant periods (aRR 1·01, 95% CI 0·80-1·26). Among partially vaccinated individuals, infections during the Omicron-dominant period carried lower LC risk than during Delta (aRR 0·62, 95% CI 0·40-0·98). LC risk did not differ by variant-dominant periods among unvaccinated or fully vaccinated individuals.Major conclusionsObserved differences in LC risk at various periods of the pandemic dominated by different variants may be largely explained by concurrent increases in vaccine coverage rather than intrinsic changes in variant pathogenicity. Full pre-infection vaccination conferred consistent protection against LC regardless of the period of variant dominance.

records.title: Composition and bioavailability of dissolved organic matter in a semi-enclosed mariculture bay: Insights from spectral and stable carbon isotope analyses.
records.abstract: Characterizing the composition, sources, and apparent bioavailability of coastal dissolved organic matter (DOM) is essential for understanding carbon cycling in semi-enclosed mariculture systems. In this study, field observations and laboratory incubation experiments were conducted in the Haizhou Bay (HZB), South Yellow Sea, during July 2024. Using measurements of dissolved organic carbon (DOC) concentration, DOM absorption and three-dimensional excitation-emission matrix fluorescence spectroscopy, stable carbon isotope (δ13C) analysis, and a Bayesian mixing model, the composition, sources, and microbial transformation of DOM were assessed. Three fluorescent components were identified, including microbial humic-like (C1), tryptophan-like (C2), and terrestrial humic-like (C3) substances. The DOM pool exhibited strong terrestrial characteristics, with the Bayesian model estimating a terrestrial contribution of 73.05 ± 15.55%, mainly associated with riverine inputs. Among fluorescent components, protein-like C2 appeared to represent an apparent bioavailable fraction and was preferentially removed during microbial degradation. Dark incubation experiments revealed a two-phase degradation pattern, with an average short-term microbial degradability of 24.53 ± 9.85%. Microbial processing selectively depleted labile DOM components while increasing the relative contribution of humic-like fluorescence, aromaticity, and humification degree. Higher apparent BDOC values near aquaculture zones suggested potential local modulation by aquaculture activities, although terrestrial inputs and microbial community differences may also contribute. This study highlights terrestrial dominance, selective microbial transformation, and the complex regulation of DOM cycling in semi-enclosed mariculture bays.
records.authors: Yan R, Xie L, Zhang G, Yang B, Yang B, Lu D, Kang Z, Zhou J, Yan Y, Xia J.

records.title: CDH3-directed immunotherapy targets basal-like hormone receptor negative prostate cancer and breast cancer.
records.abstract: Basal-like double-negative prostate cancer (DNPC) and triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) are aggressive tumors with few targeted treatment options, raising the question of whether a shared, druggable cell-surface antigen can be leveraged for effective immunotherapy. Here, we integrated analyses of independent bulk and single-cell transcriptomic datasets with mechanistic and preclinical therapeutic studies to evaluate CDH3 (P-cadherin) as a candidate target in basal-like disease. CDH3 expression was consistently enriched in basal-like subtypes across prostate and breast cancer cohorts and was preferentially expressed in basal epithelial tumor compartments. Mechanistically, CDH3 expression was governed by a YAP1-WNT5A/ROR2 signaling axis, linking basal subtype gene expression to non-canonical Wnt signaling. To exploit this target, we evaluated both a CDH3-directed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) and CDH3-specific chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells. The ADC exhibited antigen-dependent internalization and cytotoxicity in vitro and reduced metastatic tumor burden in vivo. CDH3 CAR-T cells showed antigen-specific activation and tumor cell killing in vitro and improved tumor control and survival in metastatic prostate and breast cancer xenograft models, with additional benefit when combined with PD-1 blockade (nivolumab). Together, these findings establish CDH3 as a clinically relevant and therapeutically actionable target and support CDH3-directed ADC and CAR-T strategies for aggressive, basal-like DNPC and TNBC.

records.title: Rhamnoside from Aquilaria sinensis leaves ameliorates chronic atrophic gastritis via immunomodulation and apoptosis regulation.
records.abstract: ObjectiveChronic atrophic gastritis (CAG) is a precancerous inflammatory‑atrophic gastric disorder with limited effective therapies. Although Traditional Chinese medicine shows multi‑target benefits for CAG, the bioactivity of rare medicinal plant Aquilaria sinensis remains poorly understood. This study aimed to identify anti‑inflammatory components from Aquilaria sinensis leaf extract and clarify the compound's anti‑CAG effects and mechanism.MethodsAnti‑inflammatory constituents were screened. Macrophages stimulated by LPS and MNNG‑injured GES‑1 cells were used to assess cell viability, inflammation, cell‑cycle, proliferation and apoptosis. Transcriptomic‑proteomic profiling predicted candidate pathways. An MNNG‑combined rat CAG model was established; gross gastric observation, H&E, AB‑PAS, Masson staining, immunofluorescence, immunohistochemistry and qPCR were performed.Resultsrhamnoside exhibited the strongest anti‑inflammatory activity. It reduced IL‑1β, IL‑6 and TNF‑α secretion and suppressed apoptosis in LPS‑treated macrophages, and triggered S‑phase cell‑cycle arrest in MNNG‑damaged GES‑1 cells. Omics analyses pinpointed PI3K/Akt as the core regulatory pathway. In vivo animal experiments demonstrated that rhamnoside dose‑dependently alleviated gastric gland atrophy, intestinal metaplasia and lamina propria fibrosis; it elevated PI3K/Akt signals, down‑regulated pro‑apoptotic BAX/caspase‑3, up‑regulated anti‑apoptotic BCL‑2, and normalized CAG‑associated gene transcription in gastric mucosa.ConclusionRhamnoside from Aquilaria sinensis leaves protects against CAG by regulating immunity and inhibiting apoptosis via PI3K/Akt signaling, which provides a potential candidate for CAG experimental therapy.

records.title: Bcl11a preserves hematopoietic stem cell function in culture by restraining Ncf1-dependent ROS.
records.abstract: Ex vivo expansion of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) is limited by culture-induced oxidative stress, yet the upstream transcriptional drivers remain poorly defined. Here, we show that the transcription factor Bcl11a is rapidly and persistently downregulated during HSC culture and that this decline drives functional deterioration. Bcl11a was both required and sufficient to maintain quiescence, clonogenic activity, and serially transplantable HSC function. Mechanistically, Bcl11a directly represses a Nox2 NADPH oxidase gene module, including Ncf1, encoding the p47phox organizer subunit; Ncf1 deletion reduced ROS and partially rescued the defects of Bcl11a-deficient HSCs. Rapamycin-but not the ROS scavenger N-acetylcysteine-restored Bcl11a expression, suppressed Ncf1 and ROS, and improved HSC function, identifying Bcl11a as a candidate effector linking mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 inhibition to redox control. This axis was conserved in human hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, revealing a druggable transcriptional vulnerability of cultured HSCs and a framework for improving ex vivo-expanded grafts.
records.authors: Xu X, Zhang L, An Y, Wang J, Ding X, Xie J, Yu Y.

records.title: miR-8485 by Targeting ITGAM Expression Alleviates Cognitive Impairment Induced by Ischemic Stroke.
records.abstract: ObjectivePost-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is a major complication of ischemic stroke (IS). This study aims to explore the role of miR-8485 in PSCI and its underlying molecular mechanism.Methods84 PSCI patients and 90 post-stroke cognitively normal (PSCN) patients were included. Serum miR-8485 and ITGAM expression were examined via reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction. The diagnostic efficacy of miR-8485 was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve. Risk factors of PSCI were determined via logistic regression analysis. An in vitro PSCI cell model was constructed through oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R). Cell viability, apoptosis and inflammatory factor levels were determined by Cell Counting Kit-8 assay, flow cytometry and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. The oxidative stress was evaluated by measuring superoxide dismutase (SOD), malondialdehyde (MDA) and catalase (CAT) levels. The interaction between miR-8485 and ITGAM was verified by dual-luciferase reporter assay.ResultsmiR-8485 was downregulated in PSCI patients, and ROC analysis showed that it could differentiate PSCI patients from PSCN patients. Downregulated miR-8485 expression was associated with PSCI disease severity. In OGD/R-treated human microglial cells (HMC3), upregulation of miR-8485 increased cell viability, suppressed inflammatory responses and oxidative stress, and inhibited apoptosis. ITGAM was the target of miR-8485. Overexpression of ITGAM partially reversed the protective effect of miR-8485 upregulation in OGD/R-induced HMC3 cells.ConclusionmiR-8485 alleviates OGD/R-induced inflammatoty responses and oxidative stress via targeted inhibition of ITGAM expression. The miR-8485/ITGAM axis may serve as a key regulatory pathway and a potential therapeutic candidate for further investigation in PSCI.

records.authors: Shen W, Gao L, Liu G, Li Z, Li J.

records.title: Physiological and Transcriptomic Responses of Armillaria gallica to Selenium: Bioaccumulation, Biotransformation, and Growth Promotion.
records.abstract: AimsArmillaria gallica is a medicinal fungus and key symbiont for Gastrodia elata cultivation. This study aimed to investigate the dose-dependent effects of exogenous selenium (Se) on mycelial growth, Se accumulation and biotransformation, antioxidant regulation, and transcriptional responses in A. gallica.Methods and resultsDose-response experiments showed that 20 mg L-1 Na2SeO3 optimally promoted mycelial biomass (47% increase) and Se accumulation (837.53 mg kg-1), with 99.71% of Se in organic forms, predominantly associated with polysaccharides and proteins. Physiological assays revealed enhanced SOD, POD, CAT, and GPx activities and reduced MDA content under Se treatment. Transcriptomic profiling identified extensive gene remodeling in ion transport, redox metabolism, carbohydrate metabolism, glutathione metabolism, and MAPK signaling pathways, with qRT-PCR validating key DEG expression patterns.ConclusionsAppropriate Se concentration promotes A. gallica growth and enhances antioxidant capacity through coordinated transcriptional and metabolic regulation. The strong Se accumulation and biotransformation capacity position A. gallica as a promising candidate for Se biofortification and for developing Se-enriched Gastrodia elata via the Armillaria-Gastrodia symbiotic system.
records.authors: Liu J, Du J, Zhang X, Gao M, Ai L, Song Y, Qiao Y, Xie X.

records.title: Transformer-Guided Co-Optimization of Mutation Prioritization and Thermodynamic Probe Design for Mutation Detection.
records.abstract: The design of sequence-selective DNA probes has long been limited by a decoupled workflow in which target selection proceeds without considering the physicochemical determinants of probe performance, such as thermodynamic stability and mismatch discrimination. Here, we establish an iterative computational design strategy that unifies mutation prioritization with chemical probe design. A custom transformer model extracts diagnostic attribution scores of mutations from 1,782 samples, generating semantic maps to guide probe placement. Candidate designs undergo in silico thermodynamic screening based on differential binding free energy. Probes failing to satisfy the integrated criteria of thermodynamic discrimination, diagnostic attribution, and population frequency are further evaluated by refining their spatial configuration to co-optimize thermodynamic discriminability and clinical relevance. This iterative process converges on an 8-plex targeted panel. Wet laboratory validation confirms 0.03% variant allele frequency detection with low assay cost and short turnaround time. Clinical testing on 375 samples achieves AUROC values of 0.96 for tissue and 0.90 for plasma. This work provides a potential chemical framework for nucleic acid probe design that could be explored in other molecular diagnostic systems.
records.authors: Zhang Y, Xue B, Zhang L, Zhao L, Su X, Song H, Zuo X, Yang X, Jin C, Wang Y, Fan C, Song P.

records.title: Transcriptional Regulatory Crosstalk Between Heat Stress and Nitrogen-Sulfur Nutrition in Plants.
records.abstract: Plant responses to high temperature depend on the nutritional state in which the stress occurs. Nitrogen and sulfur shape this state through photosynthetic capacity, protein synthesis, nitric oxide production, and thiol redox buffering, while heat alters nutrient uptake and assimilation. We review how nitrate and sulfate nutrition interact with heat responses through direct transcriptional cross-regulation, metabolite- or redox-mediated regulation, and convergence on shared processes. Nitrate provides the clearest transcriptional link: in Arabidopsis, the nitrate-responsive transcription factor NLP7 regulates HSFA2 and HSFA3, encoding heat stress transcription factors that sustain chaperone expression and acquired thermotolerance, and rice NLP3 binds the HsfA3 and HsfA7 promoters under heat. Nitrate reductase-derived nitric oxide modulates HSF activity, and warm temperature represses the nitrate transporter and sensor NRT1.1 through the transcription factor HY5. For sulfur, evidence comes mainly from glutathione-deficient mutants, glutathione application and hydrogen sulfide donors, which alter heat-responsive transcription factors and antioxidant genes; whether sulfate supply acts through these routes, and how sulfate sensing and the sulfate-limitation regulator SLIM1 contribute, remain unresolved. Comparing published Arabidopsis transcriptomic meta-analyses, we identify genes responding to heat and to nitrate or sulfate and propose candidate regulators. In crops, nitrogen maintains photosynthesis under heat but does not consistently protect yield.
records.authors: Soto-Rauch G, Saez AR, Salvo A, Canales J.
