records.title: Targeting ALDOA Lactylation Reverses Vascular Remodeling in Pulmonary Hypertension by Disrupting Actin Polymerization and YAP Activation.
records.abstract: BackgroundMaladaptive vascular remodeling is a hallmark of pulmonary hypertension (PH), and therapeutic strategies directly targeting the pathological activity of smooth muscle cells remain limited. Metabolic and epigenetic dysregulation are established drivers of PH, and lysine lactylation has emerged as a novel posttranslational modification implicated in diverse diseases; however, its direct contribution to PH progression remains undefined.MethodsIntegrated lactylomic and proteomic profiling was performed in hypoxic human pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells. The functional role of ALDOA (aldolase A) lactylation at lysine 42 (K42) was assessed using site-specific mutant virus and smooth muscle cell-specific inducible ALDOA knockout mice in 2 established PH models: SU5416+hypoxia in mice and monocrotaline in rats.ResultsWe identified ALDOA as a prominent lactylation target in hypoxic pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells, with K42 lactylation consistently elevated in primary pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells derived from PH rodent models and human PH tissues. Mechanistically, AARS1 (alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1)-mediated ALDOA K42 lactylation enhanced its binding to γ-actin, independent of glycolytic activity. This lactylation-enhanced interaction promoted F-actin polymerization and activated YAP (Yes-associated protein) signaling via LATS1 (large tumor suppressor kinase 1) inhibition, thereby driving pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cell proliferation and phenotypic switching. Moreover, YAP/TEAD4 (TEA domain transcription factor 4)-mediated transcriptional upregulation of AARS1 established a positive feedback loop reinforcing ALDOA K42 lactylation under hypoxia. In vivo, ALDOA inducible knockout or reconstitution with the lactylation-deficient K42R (lysine 42 mutant to arginine) mutant attenuated experimental PH progression, with suppressed F-actin/YAP activation and reduced vascular remodeling. Furthermore, competitive inhibition of lactylation through β‑alanine reduced ALDOA K42 lactylation and ameliorated vascular remodeling in ALDOA-overexpressing rodent PH models. Translationally, pharmacological disruption of the ALDOA/γ-actin interaction by raltegravir suppressed cytoskeletal reorganization and YAP signaling, mitigating PH progression in both mouse and rat models.ConclusionsAARS1-mediated ALDOA K42 lactylation drives pulmonary vascular remodeling through a mechanism independent of ALDOA's catalytic activity, promoting F-actin polymerization and YAP activation. Precision targeting of this modification selectively inhibits pathological signaling while preserving metabolic homeostasis, highlighting a translational potential for precision intervention in PH.

records.title: 2D and 3D antiproliferative properties of Schiff base and reduced Schiff base palladium(II) complexes in doxorubicin-resistant colorectal cancer cells.
records.abstract: To further investigate the structural features and antiproliferative properties of Pd(II) complexes containing halogenated ligands, one Schiff base and two reduced Schiff base complexes, I2PyPd, Cl2Pic(R)Pd, and BrClPic(R)Pd (Pic = 2-picolylamine; Py = 2-(2-pyridyl)ethylamine), were synthesized and characterized spectroscopically. The molecular structure of Cl2Pic(R)Pd was confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, revealing a distorted square-planar Pd(II) center coordinated by a bidentate N,N-chelating ligand and two chloride ions. DFT calculations supported the experimental structure. Electronic absorption spectra, corroborated by TD-DFT analysis, indicated low-energy transitions assigned to 1LC for I2PyPd and 1MLCT for Cl2Pic(R)Pd and BrClPic(R)Pd. Biological evaluation showed that I2PyPd was inactive, whereas Cl2Pic(R)Pd and BrClPic(R)Pd exhibited significant antiproliferative activity. Cl2Pic(R)Pd displayed broad cytotoxicity across all tested cancer cell lines, while BrClPic(R)Pd demonstrated pronounced activity against doxorubicin-resistant HCT116-DoxR cells with limited toxicity toward other cancer cells and normal fibroblasts, indicating enhanced selectivity. Consistent results were obtained in 3D HCT116-DoxR spheroids, where BrClPic(R)Pd remained the more promising candidate despite higher IC50 values. Mechanistic studies revealed that both active complexes induced apoptosis and autophagy, with minimal necrosis. Cl2Pic(R)Pd increased intracellular ROS levels, suggesting an oxidative stress-mediated mechanism, whereas BrClPic(R)Pd reduced ROS while maintaining strong cytotoxicity, indicating a ROS-independent mode of action. Molecular docking studies showed that both complexes interact with the drug-binding cavity of ABCB1/P-gp and the DNA minor groove, supporting a dual mechanism involving modulation of multidrug resistance and DNA targeting. BrClPic(R)Pd exhibited slightly stronger binding, consistent with its superior activity against resistant cancer cells.

records.title: dsRNA: mechanisms of gene expression regulation, disease pathogenesis, and therapeutic potential.
records.abstract: Double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) has long been recognized as a viral pathogen-associated molecular pattern that activates innate immunity. However, dsRNA is increasingly recognized as a regulatory RNA species involved in RNA homeostasis, gene expression, and cell fate determination. In this review, we discuss canonical dsRNA-dependent mechanisms, including RNA interference (RNAi), with particular emphasis on nuclear RNAi, and dsRNA-sensing networks, together with broader RNA-RNA duplex-associated regulatory processes. We also consider structurally distinct RNA-DNA hybrids that functionally converge with dsRNA-responsive innate immune pathways. We further examine how dysregulation of dsRNA production, processing, sensing, and clearance contributes to cancer, autoimmune disorders, and neurodegenerative diseases, and how these mechanisms can be therapeutically exploited. Collectively, these insights establish a conceptual framework for understanding the roles of dsRNA in physiological regulation, disease pathogenesis, and therapeutic applications.
records.authors: Liu S, Zhe C, Hou J, Fang Y, Yang H, Chen Y, Wu S, Xiang Q, Zhang Y, Fang J, Zhou Y, Li L, Xiao B.

records.title: Bromeliad Brocchinia reducta, a rare carnivorous monocot, is a holocarnivorous plant secreting its own digestive enzymes.
records.abstract: Carnivorous bromeliad Brocchinia reducta is a rare carnivorous plant. As a monocot, it is the youngest and most distantly related to the remaining ∼800 dicot carnivorous plant species. Although considered carnivorous for more than 40 years, it is believed that it does not secrete digestive enzymes and relies on microorganism-mediated digestion. Here we investigated the digestive physiology of B. reducta by measuring enzyme activity and using LC-ESI-MS/MS in response to feeding. We found prey-induced pH regulation and digestive capacity with secreted hydrolytic enzymes (e.g., aspartic protease, type I and III chitinase, GDSL hydrolase) similar to those found in other carnivorous lineages. Although the enzyme activity is rather low and comparable to the members of the carnivorous Sarraceniaceae family, the active prey response and presence of secreted enzymes placed B. reducta among truly holocarnivorous plants. Our results showed that a nutrient-poor environment exerts the same selective pressures on even distantly related plants and, through the process of convergent evolution, leads to the co-option of the same proteins for digestive function.
records.authors: Pavlovič A, Rotreklová M, Chamrád I, Lenobel R.

records.title: Integrative transcriptome meta-analysis distinguishes compatibility and incompatibility in rice-Xanthomonas interaction.
records.abstract: Diseases caused by the Xanthomonas oryzae pathovars are important constraints for global rice productivity. Despite being a well-studied pathosystem, the transcriptional mechanisms distinguishing resistance from susceptibility remain incompletely understood. Here, we present a systems-level meta-analysis of more than a hundred publicly available rice-Xanthomonas transcriptome datasets. Using appropriate analysis pipelines, stringent filtering criteria and metadata integration, we identified rice functions that distinguish disease resistance and susceptibility with temporal resolution. Compatible interactions were characterized by early activation of abscisic-acid biosynthetic and signaling genes, and extensive transcriptional plasticity associated with susceptibility gene activation. In contrast, incompatible interactions displayed a restrained transcriptome reprogramming, enrichment of phenylpropanoid and aromatic-amino-acid biosynthetic pathways, and enrichment of an AP2/ERF-GCC-box regulatory module. Transient over-expression of three conserved infection-responsive genes, OsJAZ11, OsSYP131b, and OsMYB45, modestly enhanced defense gene expression and reduced lesion length caused by X. oryzae pv. oryzae in rice leaves, thus providing a proof-of-concept relevance of the candidates to rice-Xoo interaction. We also developed RiceXtra, an openly available database hosting the analyzed data (http://tdb.ccmb.res.in/RiceXtra), for exploring gene expression patterns during rice-Xanthomonas interactions. Overall, our study proposes a mechanistic framework connecting hormonal signalling and transcriptional plasticity with disease outcome, offering a foundation for engineering durable disease resistance.
records.authors: Cg G, Malukani KK, Gaur N, M S, Patel HK, Sonti RV.

records.title: Concrete waste as a source of calcium and alkalinity for coccolithophore cultivation: an experimental test of carbon dioxide removal and sequestration
records.abstract: ABSTRACT  Cultivation of calcifying microalgae has been proposed as a route to carbon dioxide removal (CDR), but biogenic calcification releases CO  2 unless the calcium supplied also adds alkalinity. We used cultures of the coccolithophore  Chrysotila sp to test whether hydrated lime (Ca(OH)  2 ), supplied as a reagent or within ground waste concrete, can provide both calcium and alkalinity. In a 26-day factorial batch experiment, we monitored pH, nitrate and dissolved calcium. Calcite was quantified by thermogravimetric analysis. Nitrate concentration decreased and calcite accumulated in all algal treatments, indicating that lime or concrete did not inhibit growth or calcification. Lime and concrete raised culture pH significantly whereas the algal growth rate inferred from nitrate drawdown did not differ among treatments. Calcite production was 3.6-fold higher with lime than in seawater (4.5 vs. 1.2 mg L  −1 d  −1 ) and highly variable with concrete; lime and concrete cultures remained supersaturated with respect to calcite (Ω ≈ 7-10 vs. 0.2). Carbonate-system calculations indicate that the added alkalinity raises the equilibrium CO  2 uptake capacity of the medium by  ca. 3.4 mmol kg  −1 , offsetting CO  2 released by calcification. These results provide proof of concept for coupling coccolithophore cultivation with concrete waste reuse for CDR.
records.authors: Ferriere M, Affholder A, Welchert J, Katterman M, Zeng H, Kim H, Apai D, Cuello J.

records.title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Protein Language Models for Dual-Target Antimicrobial Peptide Discovery Under Strict Homology Constraints
records.abstract: The global escalation of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a severe challenge to modern public health, necessitating novel classes of therapeutic agents. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) represent highly promising alternatives to small-molecule antibiotics due to their co-evolutionary resilience and rapid membrane disruption dynamics. However, translating computational AMP leads into clinical drug candidates remains bottlenecked by off-target cytotoxicity, predominantly hemolytic activity against mammalian erythrocytes. Although pretrained foundational protein language models (PLMs) have rapidly advanced molecular property prediction, current architectures frequently isolate antibacterial potency and cytotoxicity into disconnected single-task pipelines or succumb to catastrophic performance drops under strict homology-controlled evaluations. Recently, the Quantitative Mapping of Antimicrobial Peptides (QMAP) benchmark proposed that frozen PLM embeddings shows weak linearly accessible features for hemolytic activity (HC  50 ), resulting in poor rank correlation (  ρ < 0.25) on out-of-distribution sequence splits. In this work, we introduce an end-to-end multi-task parameter-efficient transfer learning framework designed to simultaneously optimize antibacterial potency and minimize mammalian cytotoxicity without sequence leakage. Built upon ESM-2 (150M), our architecture incorporates Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) into self-attention projections, fine-tuning approx 0.70% of model weights. To restore gradient interference originating from disparate membrane lysis mechanisms, we implement an adaptive multi-task loss guided by Kendall homoscedastic uncertainty weighting. Evaluated across predefined QMAP benchmark splits enforcing a 60% maximal sequence identity threshold, our joint architecture remarkably outperforms conventional linear probes, tree-based regressors, and frozen foundational models. The framework achieves an  E. coli potency rank correlation of  ρ = 0.6132 (  r = 0.6816) and successfully elevates hemolytic toxicity correlation to  ρ = 0.5374 (  r = 0.5541). To establish real world utility, we deploy the optimized joint network to screen a curated in silico library of 749 de-novo designed peptides, successfully isolating selective cationic-amphipathic candidates possessing Therapeutic Indices (TI = HC  50 /MIC) up to 144.03 while effectively deprioritizing broadly lytic motifs (TI < 2.0). These findings demonstrate that parameter-efficient adaptation unlocks fine-grained bioactive structural semantics in foundational PLMs, providing an accurate, scalable framework for therapeutic peptide engineering.
records.authors: Jat R, Ejaz SR.

records.title: Lac1-dependent ceramide synthesis couples septum assembly to cell separation in  Schizosaccharomyces pombe
records.abstract: ABSTRACT  Ceramides are precursors of complex sphingolipids and bioactive membrane lipids. In the fission yeast  Schizosaccharomyces pombe , they are produced by a ceramide synthase with two catalytic subunits, Lac1 and Lag1, which are redundant but not functionally equivalent: only Lac1 is required for normal growth and cell size. Why Lac1 has this unique role, and how ceramide synthesis contributes to cell morphogenesis, remain unknown. Here, we show that Lac1 couples septum assembly to cell separation. Cells lacking Lac1 die predominantly during cell separation and build septa with a thinner primary layer and markedly thicker secondary layers, accompanied by altered deposition of β-(1,3)-glucans and galactomannan. These defects are not rescued by osmotic stabilization. The essential glucan synthase Bgs4 is mislocalized to cytoplasmic granules, and total β-(1,3)-glucan synthase activity is partially reduced. Nevertheless, Ags1, Bgs1 and Bgs4 accumulate to higher levels and persist almost twice as long at the division site, indicating defective clearance rather than delivery of the septum-synthesis machinery. Plasma membrane sterol distribution remains unaffected. To accurately impair ceramide synthesis, we isolated thermosensitive  lac1-ts alleles in a  lag1 Δ background. Their substitutions cluster in the conserved TRAM/LAG1 domain. Metabolic labeling showed that these alleles reduce ceramide synthesis at the restrictive temperature. Molecular dynamics simulations indicated that two substitutions perturb distinct contacts with C26-CoA, while Lac1-M167T loses its endoplasmic reticulum localization. Acute inactivation recapitulates the deletion phenotype, causing septum accumulation and cell death. Together, our findings establish that Lac1-dependent ceramide synthesis is required for the orderly completion of septum assembly and cell separation.

records.title: A respiratory microdomain links ubiquinone biosynthesis to succinate dehydrogenase in an apicomplexan mitochondrion lacking Complex I
records.abstract: Mitochondrial complex I (CI) is a major entry point for NADH-derived electrons and an important site of redox regulation in most eukaryotes. However, apicomplexan parasites, including  Toxoplasma gondii , lack CI, raising a fundamental question of how mitochondrial respiration is organized in these parasites. Here, we identify a parasite-specific mitochondrial microdomain that physically and functionally couples ubiquinone (UQ) biosynthesis to succinate dehydrogenase (SDH). Using proximity labeling, membrane-based yeast two-hybrid analyses, reciprocal co-immunoprecipitations, and blue native PAGE, we show that UQ biosynthesis proteins associate with parasite-specific SDH subunits and co-migrate as a high-molecular-weight assembly. Knockdown of TgCoq4, a component of the UQ biosynthesis pathway, reduced SDH activity, and adding exogenous UQ to the assay did not restore it, indicating that UQ availability is not sufficient for efficient succinate oxidation. FCCP stimulates malate- and TMPD/ascorbate-supported respiration to maximal capacity but fails to do so with succinate as the substrate. This result, combined with reactive oxygen species (ROS) data, suggests that succinate causes over-reduction of the UQ pool, limiting further electron flow. We also find that CIII associates with the UQ synthesis machinery, suggesting a larger protein assembly. Together, these findings reveal that UQ biosynthesis and electron transport are physically and functionally integrated in  T. gondii , defining a previously unrecognized organization of mitochondrial respiration in an organism lacking CI.
records.authors: Baierna B, Moreno SN.

records.title: ANABOLIC FAILURE, NOT CATABOLIC ACTIVATION, UNDERLIES GLYCOGEN DEPLETION IN CERVICAL CARCINOGENESIS: A MULTI-COHORT TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS
records.abstract: Background  Cervical epithelium loses its glycogen as disease grade rises, an observation old enough to underpin iodine-based visual screening, but which arm of glycogen metabolism accounts for the loss has not been established. The expectation from cancer metabolism is catabolic: that stored glycogen is mobilised and glycolysis activated. Methods  We analyzed 238 specimens from four publicly available cohorts across three sample types: 128 laser-capture-microdissected epithelial samples, 35 bulk-tissue samples, and 75 exfoliated cytology samples in two sets (44 and 31; GSE27678). We prespecified a 33-gene panel comprising four modules: glycogen synthesis, glycogen degradation, glycolysis, and squamous differentiation. For each specimen, we calculated module scores using single-sample gene set enrichment. Differential expression was assessed with limma, pathway enrichment with fgsea, and classification performance with bootstrap confidence intervals for ROC curves. We documented all analytical decisions and their rationale. Results  Synthesis and differentiation fell with grade in all four cohorts, while degradation and glycolysis stayed at their normal-tissue baseline. All seven differentiation genes were reduced in carcinoma and all seven occupied the top 5.1% of the ranked transcriptome, with CRNN the most down-regulated of 21,755 genes. Synthesis failed selectively, through GYS2 and PPP1R3C only, with the ubiquitous synthase GYS1 unchanged. The glycolytic module separated from normal epithelium at no grade (p 0.45 to 0.62), classified CIN3 or worse at an area under the curve of 0.569 with an interval spanning chance, and showed no enrichment in carcinoma. Synthesis separated from normal first, at CIN2, and differentiation at CIN3. The composite index tracked grade in the discovery cohort (Spearman rho 0.652,  p 7.9×10  -17 ), but offered no discriminatory advantage over its differentiation component alone (0.832 against 0.832).  Conclusions  Glycogen depletion in cervical carcinogenesis reflects failure of a tissue-restricted synthetic axis, GYS2 and PPP1R3C, within a collapsing squamous differentiation programme, not catabolic activation. Measuring all four candidate mechanisms on one scale in the same specimen is what allows the catabolic explanation to be excluded rather than merely left untested. The pattern holds across two array chemistries and three specimen preparations, including the exfoliated cytology that screening already collects, and the synthesis and differentiation modules together are the molecular counterpart of what iodine staining reports. These are transcript-level findings and define no clinical threshold.
records.authors: Ajayi OO, Odigie EB, Adesite SO, Erameh TO, Archibong AM, Eziagu UB.

records.title: Endogenous PROM1 activation redistributes liver cancer cells along a preexisting differentiation axis
records.abstract: Summary  CD133 is widely used as a marker of stem-like cells in hepatocellular carcinoma, yet its functional contribution remains incompletely defined. In PLC/PRF/5 cells, acute CRISPR activation of endogenous PROM1 suppresses hepatic programs, whereas PROM1 knockdown elicits an opposing hepatocyte-identity response, together defining a PROM1-responsive transcriptional axis. Single-cell profiling shows that this axis is preexisting and tracks endogenous PROM1 heterogeneity, separating a hepatocyte-like, PROM1-low compartment from a PROM1-enriched, less hepatocyte-like compartment. Sustained PROM1 activation reduces the hepatocyte-like compartment and shifts the population toward intermediate positions along this axis. Related transcriptional patterns are detectable in an independent HuH-7 dataset and a human HCC case. Endogenous ALFA tagging identifies candidate CD133-associated proteins. Together, these findings support CD133 as an active contributor to tumor-cell state redistribution, extending its role beyond a mere marker of stem-like populations.
records.authors: Schneider T, Kaneko K, Vogl M, Utpatel K, Immel A, Hirsch D, Raggi C, Spinola Lasso E, Evert M, Feng G, Calvisi DF, Scheiter A.

records.title: Apelin signaling controls neuroendocrine homeostasis via Atoh8-dependent transcriptional regulation
records.abstract: ABSTRACT  Apelin is a pleiotropic peptide hormone with established roles in cardiovascular function, angiogenesis, and metabolism, but its contribution to neuroendocrine development and function remains poorly understood. Here, using genetic loss-of-function and inducible gain-of-function approaches in zebrafish, we show that Apelin signaling is dosage-sensitive and required for normal development, reproductive capacity, and physiological homeostasis. Both  apelin deficiency and  apelin overexpression disrupted embryonic development and reduced adult lifespan, while exhibiting markedly reduced fertility in both sexes. Transcriptomic profiling revealed broad changes in neuroendocrine, hormonal, stress-response, and inflammatory genes with young adult mutant expression profiles resembling those of aged wild-type fish. Both loss and excess of Apelin also disrupted hypothalamic–pituitary–thyroid (HPT) axis development, reducing hypothalamic thyrotropin-releasing hormone-expressing cells, pituitary gonadotropic cell populations, and thyroid gland volume. Transcriptomic analyses identified  atoh8 , encoding a basic helix–loop–helix transcription factor, as a candidate effector of Apelin signaling. Apelin expression increased  atoh8 expression during early embryogenesis, whereas atoh8 mRNA partially rescued developmental defects in apelin mutants, including hypothalamic and pituitary markers, and thyroid volume. Conversely,  atoh8 crispants displayed thyroid and pituitary abnormalities, supporting a role for Atoh8 in neuroendocrine development. Together, these findings establish Apelin signaling as a dosage-sensitive regulator of zebrafish development and tissue homeostasis and identify Atoh8 as a functional downstream effector that partially mediates Apelin-dependent HPT axis formation. This work links peptide hormone signaling to neuroendocrine development and provides a framework for investigating its broader contributions to vertebrate physiology, reproduction and aging.
records.authors: Menard R, Neog A, Halluin C, Bonnet F, Madelaine R.

records.title: CrJAMs are transcriptional repressors of the monoterpenoid indole alkaloid pathway in  Catharanthus roseus
records.abstract: Catharanthus roseus produces monoterpenoid indole alkaloids (MIAs) in response to the defense hormone jasmonate (JA). In  Arabidopsis , JA regulates defense processes through MYC2 and JA-Associated MYC2a-like transcription factors (JAMs). Here we characterize two previously identified  C. roseus JAMs, CrJAM2 and CrJAM3, as regulators of MIA biosynthesis.  Functional screens using viral-induced gene silencing and transient promoter activity assays showed that CrJAMs repress the MIA pathway; silencing both  CrJAM2 and  CrJAM3 increased expression of MIA pathway genes and MIA levels while their individual overexpression repressed promoter activity. To assess their activity broadly across MIA regulatory and biosynthetic genes, we generated  C. roseus hairy root cultures either constitutively overexpressing individual  CrJAMs or  CRISPR-Cas9 creating mutations in multiple  CrJAMs , and profiled their expression by RNA-Seq.  CrJAM2 overexpression decreased expression of most MIA biosynthetic genes relative to the  GUS control, while double mutant lines showed increased basal expression of these genes relative to non-targeting controls. Notably, methyl JA treatment perturbs this equilibrium, reversing these trends at 24 hrs in both  CrJAM overexpression and mutant lines relative to basal conditions.  In summary, CrJAMs broadly repress MIA regulatory and biosynthetic gene expression and together with CrJAZ and CrMYC2a regulates MIA biosynthesis. Summary sentence  We characterize two previously identified  Catharanthus roseus JAMs; CrJAM2 and CrJAM3 regulate overlapping and unique genes and broadly repress the expression of monoterpenoid indole alkaloid regulatory and biosynthetic genes.
records.authors: Breselge S, Traverse KKF, Cole-Osborn LF, Sathitloetsakun S, Dürr K, Wang J, Childs KL, Cram EJ, Lee-Parsons CW.

records.title: Hmox1/CO regulates retina regeneration via modulation of Wnt/β-catenin signalling and induction of  vaspb  in zebrafish
records.abstract: Müller glia (MG) in the zebrafish retina retain a latent stem cell capacity that is absent in mammals, yet the injury responsive signals that drive this reprogramming remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify heme oxygenase-1 (Hmox1), the stress-inducible, rate-limiting enzyme of heme catabolism, as a previously unrecognized regulator of this process. Following injury,  hmox1a is selectively and rapidly induced among the heme oxygenase gene family, localizing to photoreceptors with expression peaking during the MG proliferation window. Pharmacological inhibition and morpholino mediated knockdown of Hmox1 dysregulate the acute inflammatory response, impair Müller glia-derived progenitor cell (MGPC) proliferation, and produce lasting deficits in retinal lamination, establishing Hmox1 as a potentially non-redundant, early-acting node required for structural recovery. Exogenous delivery of carbon monoxide (CO), a bioactive Hmox1 metabolite, partially rescues each of these phenotypes, functionally implicating CO as a key downstream effector. Mechanistically, Hmox1/CO signalling stabilizes β-catenin likely via transcriptional repression of the Wnt antagonist  dkk1b . This stabilized β-catenin is enriched at a predicted Tcf7l2 site in the promoter of  vaspb , which encodes an actin binding protein and is newly identified here as an injury-induced Wnt target gene. Bioinformatic and functional analyses further implicate Nfe2l2a (Nrf2) as a candidate intermediary bridging Hmox1/CO to Wnt regulation, with putative antioxidant response elements identified within the  dkk1b locus. Together, these findings outline a putative Hmox1→CO→Nrf2⊣  dkk1b →β-catenin→  vaspb relay coupling redox biology to Wnt-dependent glial reprogramming. Notably, HO-1 is similarly induced in stressed mammalian retina, yet Wnt/β-catenin activation fails to sustain regeneration, positioning the Hmox1/CO axis as a candidate target for future investigation in mammalian retina regeneration.
records.authors: Sherpa RD, Sen A, Chaudhuri AG, Hui SP.

records.title: Transcriptomic Analysis of Innate Immune Responses to  Toxoplasma gondii  in Bat Cells
records.abstract: Bats exhibit remarkable tolerance to numerous viral infections, a phenotype associated with distinctive adaptations in innate immune and inflammatory pathways. Whether these adaptations also shape responses to nonviral intracellular pathogens remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the interaction between the protozoan parasite  Toxoplasma gondii and epithelial cell lines derived from the black flying fox (Pteropus alecto). We found that both type I and type II strains of  T. gondii readily invaded and replicated in bat cells, demonstrating a high degree of cellular permissiveness to infection. Surprisingly, transcriptomic analysis revealed remarkably limited early host responses despite progressive intracellular parasite replication. A pronounced transcriptional response emerged only at later stages of infection, coinciding with extensive parasite replication and cellular damage, and was characterized by changes in genes associated with inflammatory signaling, metabolic adaptation, and tissue remodeling. Together, these findings reveal an unusual interaction between bat cells and an intracellular protozoan pathogen, characterized by efficient parasite replication and markedly delayed host transcriptional activation. Our results suggest that distinctive regulation of cellular responses to intracellular infection may extend beyond viral pathogens and represent a broader feature of bat immune biology.
records.authors: Yarovinsky P, Kwok SF.

records.title: CTLA-4 checkpoint signalling modulates germinal centre dynamics and antibody avidity during  Borrelia burgdorferi  infection in mice
records.abstract: Borrelia burgdorferi , the causative agent of Lyme borreliosis, persists in mammalian hosts despite robust activation of innate and adaptive immunity. A hallmark of murine infection is the production of low-avidity antibodies, yet the immunological mechanisms underlying this defective humoral response remain poorly understood.  Here, we used single-cell RNA sequencing of draining lymph node cells from Borrelia-infected mice at days 7 and 14 post-infection, comparing transcriptional profiles with those from mice immunised with heat-killed Borrelia or with a potent germinal centre-inducing protein immunisation. Borrelia infection induced a rapid germinal centre response, however, light zone B cells displayed diminished expression of co-stimulatory and T-B cell interaction molecules while maintaining core germinal centre identity markers, suggesting impaired positive selection. T follicular helper cells upregulated multiple inhibitory checkpoint receptor genes, most prominently Ctla4, alongside an active germinal centre engagement programme. Foxp3⁺ regulatory T cells upregulated genes associated with follicular-homing and suppressive function, including those implicated in CTLA-4-mediated trans-endocytosis. To test whether inhibitory signalling contributes to the impaired humoral response, infected mice were treated with anti-CTLA-4 blocking antibody. CTLA-4 blockade significantly increased plasma cell numbers and enhanced both the magnitude and avidity of  Borrelia - specific IgG responses, including the induction of complement-fixing IgG2a. These findings reveal that CTLA-4-dependent inhibitory signalling contributes to defective antibody quality during  Borrelia infection, identifying a mechanism by which dysregulated T cell responses may facilitate impaired humoral control of a persistent spirochaetal pathogen.  Authors summary  Borrelia burgdorferi , the bacteria that cause Lyme borreliosis, can persist in the body for long periods despite triggering a strong immune response. One puzzling feature of this infection is that the antibodies produced are often of poor quality and do not bind the bacteria effectively.  To investigate why, we examined individual immune cells in lymph nodes of  Borrelia -infected mice and compared them with cells from mice that received non-living  Borrelia or a vaccine- like immunisation known to generate strong antibody responses. Although  Borrelia infection rapidly triggered the formation of structures that normally help the immune system refine and improve antibodies, key communication signals between immune cells were reduced. At the same time, both helper and regulatory T cells showed increased activity of molecular pathways that act as brakes on immune responses. One such brake, controlled by a molecule called CTLA-4, appeared particularly important. When we blocked CTLA-4 during infection, mice produced more antibody-secreting cells and generated antibodies that had improved functional properties.  Our findings identify a mechanism that limits antibody quality during  Borrelia infection and help explain how the bacteria can evade effective immune control and persist in the host.
records.authors: Mäkinen V, Alinikula J, Fair-Mäkelä R, Sundqvist P, Salmi M, Mattila P, Pietikäinen A, Hytönen J.

records.title: Microbial Consortia from Chilean Salt Flats Drive Coupled Gypsum Dissolution and Mineralization in the Absence of Evaporation: Experimental Evidence
records.abstract: Microbial consortia actively modulate mineralogical processes in polyextreme environments, yet biological mechanisms are often excluded from evaporite evolution models. Here, we investigated gypsum surface dissolution and secondary mineral nucleation driven by microbial mats and natural brines from three Andean salt flats (Salar de Llamara, Salar de Pajonales, and Salar de Gorbea) across 90-day incubation experiments. Synthesized gypsum crystals were exposed to inoculated media and sterile brines (abiotic controls) under controlled conditions, and analyzed using SEM-EDS and epifluorescence microscopy. Results demonstrate that microbial colonization dual-modulates gypsum dynamics: while apparent microbially-mediated boring formed rounded cavities, extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrices acted as diffusion barriers that buffered abiotic dissolution. Furthermore, EPS promoted localized supersaturation and authigenic mineral nucleation, yielding fibrous eugsterite and globular Mg-silicates across all sites, alongside site-specific phases such as dumbbell-shaped calcite, allotriomorphic halite (Pajonales), and lenticular alunite (Gorbea). Abiotic controls exhibited simpler parageneses and angular dissolution along cleavage planes without filling. Specific bio-induced textures, including EPS-infilled pores, dumbbell calcite, Mg-Si globules, and alveolar eugsterite, represent potential morphological biosignatures relevant to astrobiology. Our findings demonstrate that purely abiotic geochemical models are insufficient to describe brine evolution, underscoring the critical necessity of integrating geomicrobiological interactions into evaporite formation frameworks.
records.authors: Orellana I, Tebes C, Demergasso C, Cabestrero Ó.

records.title: Analysis of HPV Genotype Distribution, Viral Load Profiles, and Their Relationship With Cervical Pathology Among Women in Samarkand Region (2023-2025)
records.abstract: Abstract  Introduction:  Persistent infection with high-risk oncogenic human papillomavirus (HPV) is the primary cause of cervical cancer development. Objective  To evaluate the prevalence of various HPV genotypes, describe genotype-specific viral load patterns, and determine their relationship with patient age and cervical cytological changes among women in the Samarkand region. Methods  In a cross-sectional study (2023–2025), cervical epithelial samples from 535 women (aged 19–56 years) were analyzed. Genotyping of 21 HPV types and quantification of viral load (expressed in \(\:\text{l}\text{g}\) copies of DNA/10⁵ cells) were performed using real-time PCR. Cytological status was classified according to The Bethesda System (TBS, 2014) in cohorts with monoinfection (n = 73) and mixed infection (n = 20). Results  Out of 116 HPV-positive cases, HPV 16 was unconditionally dominant (24%). An atypically low prevalence of HPV 18 (3%) was observed alongside a high detection rate of non-vaccine types: HPV 56 (6%), 51 (5%), and 58 (4%). No statistically significant correlation was found between patient age and viral load (p > 0.05). A significant overall association was revealed between HPV genotype and cytological status (χ²=97.06; df = 68; p = 0.012). HPV 58 demonstrated the highest pathogenetic potential (OR = 12.11; 80% of cases were ASC-US, 20% were ASC-H) and was never detected in normal cytology (NILM). No direct linear correlation was found between viral load level and lesion severity: peak loads were recorded in NILM cases, whereas the only severe case (HSIL, associated with HPV 68) presented with a low viral load (2.7 lg copies/10⁵ cells). Conclusion  The regional epidemiological profile is determined by the dominance of HPV 16 and a high circulation of high-risk non-vaccine strains (56, 51, 58). Viral load exhibits immense genotype-specific variability and does not directly correlate with the severity of cytological changes, highlighting the necessity of integrating multi-genotype PCR testing and cytological screening.
records.authors: Yarmukhamedova GK, Kan SV, Dushanova GA, Ziyadullayeva GZ, Khalilova SA, Yarmukhamedova MK.

records.title: Neuroscience Research: Before and After the Evolution of Optogenetics
records.abstract: Abstract  In an article titled “Thinking about the Brain,” published in a special issue of Scientific American devoted to the Brain in September 1979, Francis H.C. Crick wrote: “Reflecting on itself, the human brain has uncovered some marvelous facts. What appears to be needed for understanding how it works is new techniques for examining it and new ways of thinking about it.” He made several important observations about the technological limitations of the time, noting that electrodes cannot readily distinguish different types of neurons. Light could be an ideal signal to turn firing on and off in an alert animal (Crick 1999; Crick 1979). This conceptual blueprint was eventually realized experimentally through the groundbreaking work of Hegemann, Nagel, Deisseroth, and their colleagues, who harnessed the microbial channelrhodopsins to achieve fast, genetically targeted, light-driven control of neuronal activity (Boyden et al. 2005; Nagel et al. 2002; Nagel et al. 2003). Over the past two decades, optogenetics has become a mainstay of circuit neuroscience and is now emerging as a potential therapeutic approach. In light of the 2026 Nobel Prize awarded to optogenetics, this perspective narrates the evolution of neuroscience research before and after the advent of optogenetics, and summarizes how this technology has transformed our approaches to studying the brain.
records.authors: Pandey S, Abraham NM.

records.title: Sustained HBsAg Loss and Marked Reversal of Liver Cirrhosis in a Patient with Antiviral-Resistant Chronic Hepatitis B: A Case Report with 13-Year Follow-up
records.abstract: Abstract    Background  Achieving sustained hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) loss and reversing established cirrhosis is considered extremely challenging, especially in patients with prior antiviral resistance. We report a case of marked reversal of liver cirrhosis and sustained HBsAg loss in a patient with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) who previously failed standard antiviral therapy.  Case Presentation  A 60-year-old male patient was diagnosed with CHB in 2006 and developed cirrhosis after 6 years of standard antiviral therapy at a top-tier hospital. In February 2012, his liver stiffness (FibroScan) was 19.9 kPa, with HBV DNA at 1.47×10^7 IU/ml. He subsequently received combined Chinese-Western medicine ("Neo-Chinese Medicine") treatment. After 7 years and 2 months of treatment, his liver function normalized, HBV DNA became undetectable, and FibroScan decreased to 5.1 kPa. Notably, the patient achieved HBsAg loss and Pre-S1 antigen negativity. All medications were discontinued in April 2019. By November 2020, despite the patient developing hyperlipidemia and steatohepatitis due to lifestyle factors, imaging and elastography confirmed a marked reversal of cirrhosis (FibroScan: 6.2 kPa, normal portal vein diameter of 12 mm) without disease progression. Long-term follow-up up to 2025 consistently showed sustained HBsAg negativity (Conclusion  This case demonstrates that Neo-Chinese Medicine can achieve marked reversal of cirrhosis and sustained functional cure in patients with antiviral-resistant CHB. The durability of these outcomes after treatment discontinuation suggests a fundamental restoration of the hepatic microenvironment and the depletion of the viral reservoir.

records.title: Native-to-fibril structural remodelling reveals an amyloid-selective transthyretin epitope for AI-guided binder design
records.abstract: Abstract  Transthyretin (TTR) amyloidosis involves conversion of the native tetramer into cross-$\beta$ fibrils, creating potential targets for conformation-selective binders. Full-assembly solvent-accessibility analysis of 30 patient-derived fibril structures, spanning wild-type TTR and ten hereditary variants, identifies increased exposure of an N-terminal region adjacent to Cys10. Using a common normalisation reference, mean relative solvent accessibility for residues 11--15 is 0.089 in native TTR and at least 0.168 in fibrils. Modification mapping, saturation-mutagenesis stability predictions and steric PTM models provide molecular context. BoltzGen and RFAntibody generate candidate binders, and sequence-only Boltz-2 counter-predictions place selected nanobodies at the Pro11/Met13/Lys15 region in fibril-derived constructs but at distal surfaces in native-state constructs. Vitreous-fibril designs also engage cardiac-fibril constructs, suggesting cross-tissue epitope recognition. These results support structure-guided candidate prioritisation, while fibril geometry, binding affinity and disease-state selectivity require experimental validation.
records.authors: Lomoio U, Carbonari V, Roncada P, Urbani A, Lio' P, Veltri P, Guzzi PH.

records.title: Verifiable Deep Learning: Smart Contract--Enabled Model Integrity and Provenance on Distributed Ledgers
records.abstract: Abstract  Deep learning artifacts undergo long and mutable lifecycles in which datasets, preprocessing pipelines, checkpoints, evaluation configurations, and deployed versions may be controlled by different actors. Hash anchoring makes individual bytes tamper-evident but does not establish that a checkpoint was derived from authorized data or that its alleged computation actually occurred. We present ProofWeave, a provenance-coupled verification specification that treats model evolution as a typed, policy-constrained transition system. Each transition binds content commitments, authenticated parent references, version rules, and explicit evidence obligations; the proposed contract state machine admits only policy-valid transitions. We distinguish full computational proofs, conditioned on a sound external proving backend, from probabilistic committed-step audits with a finite-population detection bound. For transparent evaluation we implement a local integrity prototype, not a live blockchain or zero-knowledge proof service. Seven deterministic integrity fault types are assessed across three public datasets; four nested validators cover 2, 4, 6, and 7 of the nine broader threat classes discussed. To expose an essential security boundary, we additionally perform 105 real MLP training runs over seven random seeds and five controlled training-label corruption rates. Hash/signature microbenchmarks and Merkle trees of up to 65,536 leaves characterize local scaling. A controlled Monte Carlo audit study quantifies probabilistic detection under committed-step sampling, separately from the local measurements. The evidence supports preliminary provenance-check correctness and quantifies its limits; it does not establish on-chain costs or end-to-end verifiable neural training.
records.authors: Wu F, Yuan B, Wang Y.

records.title: Experimental Synthesis, Characterization, and Numerical Device Simulation of Hydrazinium–Methylammonium Mixed Lead Bromide Perovskites for Solar Cell Applications
records.abstract: Abstract  Mixed-cation lead bromide perovskite thin films and powders with composition HA(1−x)MAxPbBr3 (x = 0.0, 0.20, 0.40) were synthesised via solution-processed spin-coating and comprehensively characterised to elucidate the role of methylammonium (MA+) incorporation in hydrazinium (HA+) lead bromide perovskites. XRD analysis revealed a progressive hexagonal-to-tetragonal phase transition with increasing MA+ content, accompanied by crystallite size reduction from 86.68 ± 5.99 nm to 61.26 ± 11.59 nm and concurrent increases in dislocation density and microstrain. SEM confirmed morphological evolution from agglomerated nanoparti cles (88.61 ± 23.43 nm) in pristine HAPbBr3 to a refined homogeneous nanostructure (72.41 ± 16.40 nm) in HA0.6MA0.4PbBr3, while EDX confirmed stoichiometric compositions and successful A-site cation mixing. FTIR and Raman spectroscopy verified co incorporation of both cations within the intact PbBr4− 6 octahedral framework. UV–Vis spectrophotometry revealed direct bandgaps of 2.9565, 2.9339, and 2.3075 eV for x = 0, 0.20, and 0.40, respectively, demonstrating continuous bandgap tunability via a two-stage mechanism of chemical A-site perturbation and phase-transition-driven bandgap collapse. Urbach energy decreased monotonically from 0.2112 to 0.1902 eV, indicating progressive band-edge quality improvement. Hall effect measurements showed carrier mobility increasing from 71.86 to 143.2 cm2 V−1 s−1 and conductivity from 1.078×10−5 to 2.278×10−5 Ω−1 cm−1 for HA0.6MA0.4PbBr3. Using experimentally determined parameters, seventeen solar-cell architectures (SC1–SC17) were evaluated by SCAPS-1D simu lation, employing HAPbBr3 and HA0.8MA0.2PbBr3 as electron transport layers and HA0.6MA0.4PbBr3 as the absorber layer. The highest PCE of 32.18% was achieved by Cs2InSbCl6-based devices (SC3 and SC8) with NiO hole transport layers, while HA0.6MA0.4PbBr3 single-absorber cells (SC11–SC13) attained the highest fill factors (>82%) among all architectures. Temperature (300–420 K) and back-contact work function (4.8–6.0 eV) analyses confirmed the thermal robustness and contact tolerance of the devices, establishing HA(1−x)MAxPbBr3 as a promising candidate for next-generation tandem photovoltaic applications.
records.authors: Alam S, Bhuiyan MMR, Bashar MS, Neher B, Ahmed F.

records.title: LINC00641 Expression and a Predicted LINC00641-Associated RNA Network in Multiple Sclerosis
records.abstract: Abstract  Background  Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neuroinflammatory disease characterized by demyelination and neurodegeneration. Long non-coding RNAs may contribute to gene-regulatory changes in MS, but the involvement of LINC00641 has not been investigated. Methods and Results  LINC00641 expression was measured by quantitative real-time PCR in peripheral blood samples from 48 patients with MS and 48 healthy controls. LINC00641-associated mRNAs were retrieved from ENCORI and integrated with differential-expression analysis of the GSE137143 RNA-seq dataset. Protein-interaction analysis, functional enrichment, miRNA-target prediction, and receiver operating characteristic analyses were then performed. LINC00641 was significantly upregulated in MS and showed case-control discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.74). Six LINC00641-associated genes—DDX5, HNRNPC, THRAP3, YY1, SUPT16H, and HP1BP3—were significantly upregulated in the RNA-seq dataset, with individual AUC values of 0.64–0.71. A logistic-regression model combining the six genes showed an AUC of 0.806. Eleven predicted miRNAs were shared among the six genes, and enrichment analysis linked the gene set mainly to RNA splicing, mRNA processing, and chromatin organization. Conclusions  LINC00641 is upregulated in MS, and integration of experimental expression data with transcriptomic and network analyses identifies a LINC00641-associated RNA signature linked to RNA-processing pathways. These findings support independent validation and functional investigation of LINC00641 and the associated network as candidate molecular biomarkers and regulators in MS.
records.authors: Sadeghi¹˒³ N, Salehi² Z, Hojati³ Z, Salehi Z.

records.title: Integrative Pan-Cancer Multi-Omics Analysis Reveals POLQ as a Prognostic Biomarker and Immunotherapeutic Target in Uterine Corpus Endometrial Carcinoma
records.abstract: Abstract  DNA polymerase theta (POLQ) mediates microhomology-mediated end joining and represents a synthetic lethal target for homologous recombination deficient cancers, yet its pan-cancer clinical, immunoregulatory and predictive functions are poorly defined. Multi-omics data from TCGA, GTEx, cBioPortal, TIMER2.0 and GSCA were used for pan-cancer profiling of POLQ expression, mutations, prognosis, immune signatures. Drug sensitivity correlation analysis together with in silico molecular docking simulations were applied to predict potential binding between POLQ and candidate therapeutic agents. Differential gene expression analysis and functional enrichment were further investigated in uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC). POLQ was overexpressed in most malignancies, associated with advanced stages and poor survival. Gene amplification drove its upregulation. POLQ expression showed significant correlations with immune cell infiltration, tumor mutation burden, and microsatellite instability. The strong negative correlations between POLQ expression and responses to multiple chemotherapeutic agents, with molecular docking predicted potential direct interactions between vincristine, paclitaxel, docetaxel and the POLQ protein. In UCEC, high POLQ activated DNA replication, cell cycle and ATR-dependent DNA damage pathways. POLQ is a pan-cancer prognostic and therapeutic biomarker. In UCEC, it accelerates tumor progression via DNA damage and cell cycle dysregulation and reshapes immune microenvironment, supporting POLQ-targeted precision immunotherapy especially for endometrial cancer.
records.authors: Du B, Wang C, Lv Y, Wang Q, Wang F, Li J, Gao H, Chang R, Li H.

records.title: Increased Zoonotic Risk Posed by Emerging Haemagglutinin Variants of Clade 2.3.4.4b A(H5Nx) High Pathogenicity Avian Influenza Virus
records.abstract: Abstract  High pathogenicity avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs) remain a major threat to animal and human health. The clade 2.3.4.4b H5Nx panzootic has been marked by increasing cross-species adaptation, including outbreaks in dairy cattle. The surge in mammalian infections in both wild and captive populations heighten concerns about zoonotic and pandemic potential. Here, we analyse haemagglutinin (HA) evolution in clade 2.3.4.4b H5Nx viruses from 2020 to 2025, focusing on key residues within the receptor-binding domain. We identify HA E185K (mature H5 HA numbering; E189K in H3 numbering) as a novel immune escape mutation that confers increased binding to avian- and human-type sialic acid receptors. Strikingly, this mutation is increasingly prevalent in cattle-derived H5N1 viruses and enhances binding to human-like receptors. However, ferret studies demonstrated that whilst pathogenicity of the E185K virus was comparable to the cattle derived isolate, the E185K mutation did not confer transmission to direct or indirect contact ferrets. Our results reveal a mechanism linking immune escape with expanded receptor specificity, highlighting a potential pathway for mammalian adaptation. These findings underscore the need for continued surveillance of evolving H5Nx viruses to mitigate emerging zoonotic threats.

records.title: Fucosyltransferase 4 as a candidate diagnostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target in osteosarcoma: a multi-dataset transcriptomic and structural bioinformatics analysis
records.abstract: Abstract    Background  Osteosarcoma, the most common primary malignant bone tumor in children and young adults, has a poor prognosis in metastatic or recurrent disease. Fucosyltransferase 4 (  FUT4  ) mediates fucosylation and has been implicated in several cancers, but its role in osteosarcoma remains unclear. Methods  Using two public Gene Expression Omnibus microarray cohorts (GSE36001, GSE16088), we assessed  FUT4  expression and diagnostic performance by limma-based differential analysis and ROC curves with AUC estimation, and profiled function through GO, KEGG, GSEA and GSVA. We further constructed protein-protein interaction and transcription factor/microRNA/drug regulatory networks, characterized immune-cell signatures by ssGSEA, and prioritized candidate binding compounds by DrugCLIP virtual screening followed by AutoDock Vina docking. Results  FUT4  transcripts were significantly down-regulated in osteosarcoma in both cohorts (GSE36001, p FUT4  -associated genes were enriched in ossification, osteoblast differentiation and extracellular matrix-related terms. GSEA linked high  FUT4  to epithelial-mesenchymal transition and inflammatory-response signatures, and exploratory GSVA suggested differences in cytoskeletal, apoptotic and Wnt/beta-catenin signalling between  FUT4  -low and  FUT4  -high subgroups, which also showed distinct immune-cell correlation patterns. Structure-based screening prioritized ST50926609 as the lead candidate  FUT4  -binding compound (Vina score = − 7.35 kcal/mol). Conclusions  Collectively, these computational findings support  FUT4  as a candidate diagnostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target in osteosarcoma, but they remain hypothesis-generating and require validation in clinical cohorts, cell and animal models.

records.title: Circular RNA in Lipid Nanoparticles: From Molecular Engineering to First-in-Human Testing
records.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) were, until a decade ago, a by-product of transcriptome profiling. They are now drug candidates. A covalently closed backbone removes the termini that exonucleases and cap-dependent decay require, and lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) turn that molecular property into a pharmacological one by carrying the RNA into the cytoplasm of a chosen cell. Between 2021 and 2026 the field moved from reporter-gene proof of concept to nine first-in-human programmes, five of which encode a CD19 chimeric antigen receptor and one of which has completed. We argue that the central question is no longer whether circRNA can be made and delivered, but which of its claimed advantages survive in vivo, and at what cost in manufacturing complexity. We examine performance determinants at three coupled levels, the molecule, the particle and the biological context, and set out the manufacturing, analytical and regulatory problems that will decide whether circularity becomes a general platform property or a niche solution.
records.authors: Zhao Y, Cheng H, Zhou S, He L, Xiu C, Huang B, Lu X.

records.title: Isoform Remodeling Along the Human Monocyte-to-Macrophage Differentiation Axis
records.abstract: Tissue-resident macrophage diversity has been mapped at the gene-expression level, and alternative splicing has been catalogued across immune lineages [1,2]; isoform behavior along the monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation axis remains unexamined. Analyzing a 17-gene immune panel across BLUEPRINT differentiation series and GTEx v8, we identify an MSR1 isoform switch with complete donor-level separation (short-isoform fraction 0.844–0.914 in monocytes versus 0.291–0.541 in six macrophage samples; exact permutation p = 0.024) — a switch from the dominant-negative SR-AIII scavenger-receptor isoform to functional SR-AI/II receptors — with equally supported PTPRC, MYD88, and IRAK1 remodeling, whereas an IL1B canonical-fraction rise is donor-heterogeneous (p = 0.114). LY96 (MD-2) is induced ~17-fold during differentiation, yet the functionally decisive antagonist/agonist isoform ratio is not resolved by standard short-read annotation — a methodological gap for immune isoform studies. CD14/CD163 show dosage regulation without isoform switching: CD163 peaks in LPS-driven M1 macrophages and, in human brain, marks border-associated macrophages rather than microglia. A 62-gene cytoskeletal panel nominates septin-family isoform divergence as a candidate mechanism of the ramified-to-amoeboid morphology spectrum, with PTBP1/hnRNP/SRSF programs as candidate executors of immune-side switching. Differentiation-coupled isoform remodeling is thus a component of macrophage identity.
records.authors: Wang X, Chen H, Li D, Shen C.

records.title: Polysaccharides in modern therapeutics: structural diversity, delivery platforms, and antitumor applications.
records.abstract: Polysaccharides, as structurally diverse and biologically versatile natural macromolecules, have long been recognised for their indispensable roles in immune regulation, intercellular communication, and tissue architecture. Their intrinsic biocompatibility, biodegradability, and chemical modifiability position them at the interface between small-molecule drugs, biologics, and functional biomaterials. This review provides a systematic overview of the biological characteristics, historical evolution, and clinical applications of polysaccharide-based drugs, with an emphasis on marketed products and advanced clinical candidates. We critically discuss recent progress in polysaccharide-based delivery platforms, including nanoparticles, hydrogels, and polysaccharide-drug conjugates, highlighting how molecular design - such as molecular weight control, glycosidic linkage configuration, and functional group substitution - governs pharmacological activity and targeting performance. Particular attention is given to antitumor applications, where natural and chemically modified polysaccharides (e.g. selenized, phosphorylated, and sulphated derivatives) exert multitarget effects through cell cycle arrest, apoptosis induction, tumour microenvironment remodelling, and immunomodulation. Despite significant advances, challenges related to structural heterogeneity, batch-to-batch variability, and incomplete structure-activity relationship elucidation continue to hinder clinical translation. By integrating structural precision with mechanistic clarity, polysaccharide-based drugs are poised to evolve from supportive agents into rationally designed, next-generation therapeutic platforms.
records.authors: Wang X, Li Y, Li X, Zhang Y, Yu C, Guo J, Li K, Wang H.

records.title: Integrated multi-omics analysis of sulfadiazine-induced oxidative stress and its impact on catechin biosynthesis and tea quality in Camellia sinensis.
records.abstract: Sulfadiazine (SDZ), a sulfonamide antibiotic and soil contaminant, poses risks to tea metabolism. Integrated analyses revealed that SDZ (>5 mg/kg) markedly inhibited root elongation, disrupted mesophyll architecture, accompanied by elevated malondialdehyde and ascorbate peroxidase but reduced peroxidase activity, indicating oxidative stress and membrane lipid peroxidation damage. HPLC analyses revealed a significant increase in total catechin content. Metabolomic profiling revealed 616 DAMs, mainly phenylpropanoids, flavonoids, and lipids. Multi-omics analysis indicated activation of the pentose phosphate and oxidative phosphorylation pathways to sustain redox balance and energy supply. Transcriptomic and dual-luciferase evidence supported CsMYB1 as a candidate negative regulator of catechin biosynthesis. Reduced CsMYB1 expression under high SDZ exposure may relieve repression of CsANR, CsSCPL, and CsF3'H, potentially promoting esterified catechin accumulation, particularly epigallocatechin gallate and epicatechin gallate. These findings reveal metabolic and transcriptional reprogramming under high SDZ exposure and highlight a trade-off between bioactive catechin accumulation and growth or structural impairment.
records.authors: Xue Y, He B, Li S, Deng H, Zhang S, Hu X, Yao X, Luo C, Lu L.

records.title: Dynamic CD4⁺ T-Cell eQTLs Reveal Gene Regulatory Networks Associated with Atopic Dermatitis.
records.abstract: Background and objectiveAtopic dermatitis (AD) is a complex immune-mediated disorder in which aberrant activation of CD4⁺ T cells plays a critical pathogenic role. We integrated dynamic CD4⁺ T cell expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) data with Mendelian randomization (MR) to dissect the causal effect of transcriptional changes on AD risk.MethodsThis study integrated dynamic CD4⁺ T-cell eQTL analysis, two-sample MR, colocalization analysis, single-cell transcriptomic, pseudotime, cell-cell communication and protein-protein interaction (PPI) analyses, with virtual single-cell knockout further used to evaluate gene regulatory effects in AD. We systematically analyzed gene expression and genetic variation in CD4⁺ T cells from 119 individuals of European ancestry across multiple activation time points (0 h, 16 h, 40 h, and 5 days).ResultsWe performed two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) integrating dynamic CD4⁺ T-cell eQTL, OneK1K, eQTLGen, and FinnGen R12 AD cohort data. The analysis identified 298 genes significantly associated with AD (FDR ConclusionWe demonstrate that understanding the dynamic characteristics of CD4⁺ T cells is crucial for AD, and prioritize genes for future research into its pathogenesis.

records.title: A rare co-infection of Colletotrichum truncatum and Nocardia cyriacigeorgica in a renal transplant recipient.
records.abstract: Opportunistic infections caused by uncommon pathogens are increasingly reported in renal transplant recipients receiving prolonged immunosuppressive therapy. We report the first case of co-infection with Colletotrichum truncatum and disseminated Nocardia cyriacigeorgica in a renal transplant recipient. A 52-year-old woman presented with right arm and thigh swellings. Microbiological examination of the pus from thigh lesion demonstrated Colletotrichum truncatum, confirmed by sequencing of internal transcribed spacer (ITS) region of ribosomal DNA, whereas aspirate from the arm swelling revealed partially acid-fast branching filamentous bacilli, identified as Nocardia cyriacigeorgica by MALDI-TOF MS. Chest imaging showed pulmonary nodules which yielded N. cyriacigeorgica from fine-needle aspirate, confirming disseminated nocardiosis. The patient was treated with a successive combination of antibiotic therapy (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and ceftriaxone followed by amoxicillin-clavulanate, meropenem, linezolid, minocycline and tedizolid) for Nocardia species and itraconazole for C. truncatum. Complete resolution of pulmonary lesions was achieved after a year of therapy, but persistence of cutaneous lesions required surgical removal. This case highlights the importance of prompt microbiological diagnosis, and individualized treatment strategies in managing rare opportunistic co-infections in renal transplant recipients.
records.authors: Kaur H, Kumar D, Ahmad H, Sharma A, Kaur R, Kundu R, Singh H, Muthu V, Agnihotri S, Rudramurthy SM.

records.title: Identification and validation of an ion homeostasis-related diagnostic gene signature for tuberculosis and exploratory analysis of SLC24A2.
records.abstract: BackgroundTuberculosis (TB) remains a major global public health problem. Ion homeostasis is involved in the regulation of host anti-infection immunity, but the potential value of ion homeostasis-related genes (IHRGs) in the molecular diagnosis of TB has not been fully evaluated.MethodsDifferentially expressed IHRGs were screened based on GEO transcriptomic datasets; candidate diagnostic genes were identified by combining the LASSO and Boruta algorithms; a multivariable logistic regression model was constructed; and its discriminative performance and stability were evaluated through internal cross-validation, penalized regression, and independent external cohorts. In addition, ssGSEA, GeneMANIA, GSVA, and molecular docking analyses were performed to explore the potential biological implications of the representative candidate gene SLC24A2.ResultsA total of 8 candidate diagnostic genes were screened out: CCL28, CCR2, CCR6, CD52, FAM20A, KEL, SLC24A2, and XCL1. The model showed an apparent AUC of 0.997 in the training set, a nested cross-validation AUC of 0.862 for the combined LASSO and Boruta screening strategy, and an AUC of 0.986 in the GSE34608 external validation cohort. Further analysis indicated that the original model suffered from unstable parameter estimation and numerical saturation of predicted probabilities in part of the external validation data. SLC24A2 was upregulated in the three datasets and was associated with some immune-related gene sets and signaling pathway scores. Molecular docking analysis suggested a potential interaction between Calcitriol and SLC24A2.ConclusionIn this study, 8 ion homeostasis-related candidate diagnostic genes were identified, and exploratory analyses of the potential biological role of SLC24A2 and its interaction with candidate compounds were performed. These findings provide a preliminary basis for further validation of molecular diagnostic markers for TB and subsequent research on potential therapeutic targets.
records.authors: Li M, Sun C, Chen L, Wu C, Liu Q.

records.title: Identification of Endoplasmic reticulum Homeostasis-associated diagnostic biomarkers for Sarcopenia through integrated Bioinformatics and Experimental Validation.
records.abstract: Sarcopenia is an age-related skeletal muscle disorder characterized by progressive loss of muscle mass and function, yet reliable biomarkers for early diagnosis remain limited. Emerging evidence suggests that disruption of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) homeostasis contributes to skeletal muscle aging, however, the diagnostic relevance of ER stress- and reticulophagy-related alterations in sarcopenia remains poorly understood. In this study, three skeletal muscle transcriptomic datasets (GSE25941, GSE28422, and GSE38718) were integrated following batch-effect correction to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between sarcopenic and control samples. DEGs were intersected with ER stress and reticulophagy related gene sets to obtain sarcopenia-associated candidate genes. Subsequently, three machine-learning algorithms, including least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), random forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM), were applied to identify key hub genes. Functional enrichment analyses, transcription factor (TF)-miRNA regulatory network construction, protein-chemical interaction analyses, external validation, nomogram development, and quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) verification were performed. A total of 236 DEGs were identified, comprising 34 upregulated and 202 downregulated genes. Intersection analysis with 1,772 ER stress and reticulophagy related genes yielded 10 candidate genes, from which five hub genes (ACTC1, NPY, CDKN2B, GADD45G, and GRIA1) were consistently identified by machine-learning analyses. Functional enrichment analysis indicated significant involvement in extracellular matrix organization, cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction, mitochondrial translation, and respiratory electron transport pathways. Regulatory network analyses further revealed potential interactions with multiple transcription factors, miRNAs, and chemical compounds. In the independent validation cohort (GSE1428), ACTC1 showed strong individual discriminative performance, NPY and GADD45G showed moderate performance, whereas GRIA1 showed limited discrimination and CDKN2B showed near-chance individual performance, whereas the combined gene signature exhibited improved discriminative ability. A predictive nomogram was established. Moreover, qRT-PCR analysis of human skeletal muscle biopsy specimens confirmed significantly increased expression of ACTC1, NPY, CDKN2B, and GRIA1, together with decreased expression of GADD45G in sarcopenic muscle tissues compared with controls (all p < 0.05). Collectively, our findings identified a five-gene signature associated with ER stress and reticulophagy related molecular networks in sarcopenia. Although these genes are not established core regulators of ER stress or reticulophagy, they exhibited promising diagnostic value and may reflect ER homeostasis-related molecular alterations during skeletal muscle aging, providing novel biomarkers and potential insights into the molecular basis of sarcopenia.

records.title: Polystyrene microplastic and bisphenol A Co-exposure drives oxidative collapse, neuroendocrine disruption, apoptotic activation, and hepatopancreatic pathology in Pontogammarus maeoticus.
records.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) and bisphenol A (BPA) are widespread emerging aquatic pollutants that may pose ecological risks to sensitive invertebrates; however, their combined chronic effects on neuroendocrine regulation, apoptotic signaling, and hepatopancreatic integrity in endemic Caspian crustaceans remain uncharacterized. This study assessed the 30-day chronic toxicity of polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs, 7.26 µm; 0.05 and 5 mg L⁻¹), BPA (50% LC₅₀), and their combination (5 mg L⁻¹ PS-MPs + 50% LC₅₀ BPA) in Pontogammarus maeoticus using a multi-biomarker approach. Combined exposure produced the highest mean CYP450 level, although it did not differ significantly from MP2 or BPA alone, and the highest cleaved/pro-caspase-3 ratio. Heat shock protein 70 (HSP70) increased in all exposed groups, peaking under combined exposure at a level not significantly different from BPA alone. SOD activity increased, whereas catalase and total antioxidant capacity were lowest under co-exposure. Crustacean hyperglycemic hormone (CHH), measured as a relative immunoreactive value, was highest in the combined group, and acetylcholinesterase (AChE) activity was significantly reduced under the higher PS-MP concentration, BPA, and co-exposure. Reproductive hormones (17β-estradiol and testosterone) decreased in exposed groups, with the lowest values under co-exposure, and hepatopancreatic lesions were most severe in the combined treatment. Overall, co-exposure was empirically associated with stronger oxidative, apoptotic, endocrine, and histological responses than most single exposures. Because BPA adsorption onto PS-MPs and tissue residues were not measured, a carrier-mediated interaction remains a plausible but unproven hypothesis. These findings support further evaluation of P. maeoticus as a candidate bioindicator of plastic-associated pollution in the Caspian Sea.

records.title: A time-resolved single-nucleus atlas of cochlear aging reveals biphasic inflammaging and Tbx2-dependent inner hair cell maintenance.
records.abstract: BackgroundAge-related hearing loss (ARHL) is the most prevalent sensory deficit in older adults, yet its molecular progression remains poorly resolved. Few cochlear single-cell studies have integrated cell-cell communication, gene regulatory network (GRN) reconstruction, and cross-cohort bulk validation into one temporal framework.MethodsWe reanalyzed publicly available single-nucleus RNA sequencing data from C57BL/6 J mouse cochleae at 3, 12, and 24 months and cross-validated against two independent bulk microarray cohorts. Ligand-receptor interactions were inferred and validated at the ligand-expression level. GRNs were reconstructed and perturbed in silico; and feature selection extracted cross-scale inflammatory features.ResultsARHL did not follow a linear decline. A cochlea-wide type I interferon response peaked at 12 months and resolved by 24. Apolipoprotein E followed a three-phase trajectory, baseline, compensatory upregulation, collapse, across spiral ganglion neurons, inner hair cells (IHCs), macrophages, and fibrocytes. SLIT-ROBO axon-guidance signaling shut down in these cells, alongside neurotrophic and Notch withdrawal. In silico perturbation identified T-box transcription factor 2 (Tbx2) as a protective GRN node: knockout drove 81.2% of IHCs toward aging and overexpression 74.6% toward youth. A 13-gene inflammatory panel showed midlife activation and end-stage exhaustion in macrophages, mirroring the interferon peak.ConclusionThese findings support a two-stage ARHL model, midlife immune activation followed by end-stage synaptic, lipid, and axon-guidance collapse, positioning the midlife window and Tbx2-dependent IHC maintenance as candidate intervention targets, pending in vivo validation.
records.authors: Zhao H, Wang Y, Wang Q, Ma X, Zhao K, Zhai X, Wang R, Han M, Cui L, Sun Y.

records.title: Low-Titre ANA Late-Onset Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Presenting With Pleural Effusion and Markedly Elevated Pleural Adenosine Deaminase Mimicking Tuberculous Pleuritis.
records.abstract: Pleural effusion with markedly elevated adenosine deaminase (ADA) levels is commonly associated with tuberculous pleuritis but may occur in other conditions. We report a case of low-titre ANA late-onset systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) presenting with pleural effusion and markedly elevated ADA levels mimicking tuberculosis. A 78-year-old man with pneumoconiosis presented with fever, cough, and progressive pleural effusion. Pleural fluid analysis revealed lymphocyte-predominant exudative effusion with markedly elevated ADA levels. Tuberculous pleuritis was initially suspected, but microbiological tests were negative. The patient developed thrombocytopenia, renal dysfunction, and altered consciousness. Immunological findings showed hypocomplementemia and elevated anti-double-stranded DNA antibodies despite low-titre ANA. Corticosteroid therapy led to rapid improvement, confirming the diagnosis of late-onset SLE. Clinicians should consider autoimmune diseases when tuberculosis is not microbiologically confirmed.
records.authors: Inoue S, Tatsuta M, Tatsutani T, Ueda S, Wakamatsu K, Kawasaki M.

records.title: Global Trends and Burden of HIV Coinfection With Extensively Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis From 1990 to 2021: The Global Burden of Disease Study 2021.
records.abstract: BackgroundTuberculosis (TB) and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) remain global health threats. Extensively drug-resistant TB with HIV co-infection is associated with substantial mortality worldwide. This study aimed to estimate the global burden and temporal trends of extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis and human immunodeficiency virus co-infection (HIV/XDR-TB) from 1990 to 2021.MethodsWe used the Global Burden of Diseases Study 2021 data to estimate the global burden of HIV/XDR-TB from 1990 to 2021. We employed a Disease Modeling-Meta-Regression model to estimate incidence, prevalence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life years. Mortality was calculated using population attributable fraction methods, accounting for HIV/XDR-TB overlap. Results were stratified by Socio-demographic Index (SDI) and reported with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs).ResultsIn 2021, global HIV/XDR-TB incidence was 1,606.42 cases (95% UI, 1,163.94-2,182.83), with an age-standardized incidence rate of 1.94 per 10 million and a -15.59% change (95% UI, -36.38 to +10.26) since 2010. Mortality estimates indicated 840 deaths (95% UI, 385.44-1,491.72) in 2021, with an age-standardized death rate of 1.01 per 10 million (95% UI, 0.47-1.80), representing a 35.85% decline from 2010 (95% UI, -50.45% to -17.75%). The burden was highest among those aged 35-39 and consistently higher in males. Regionally, Eastern Europe and Southern Sub-Saharan Africa showed the highest burden, while Oceania had the greatest increase. Substantial heterogeneity was observed across regions and SDI levels.ConclusionDespite declines in HIV/XDR-TB burden, significant regional and demographic disparities persist, highlighting the need for targeted public health strategies in high-burden regions.
records.authors: Lee EH, Kim YS, Kim MS, Ravindran R, Yon DK, Kang YA, Shin JI, Smith L.

records.title: A molecular networking-guided strategy for identifying anti-osteoporotic sterols from the soft coral Sclerophytum humesi.
records.abstract: Marine soft corals represent a rich source of structurally diverse secondary metabolites; however, their potential effects on bone metabolism remain poorly explored. In this study, an integrated molecular networking- and bioactivity-guided strategy was employed to identify potential anti-osteoporotic constituents from the soft coral Sclerophytum humesi. LC-MS/MS-based molecular networking was integrated with biological activity data to prioritize bioactivity-associated molecular families for targeted isolation. In a glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis zebrafish model, fraction SH-E3 exhibited a pronounced ability to restore impaired skeletal mineralization and was therefore prioritized for further chemical investigation. Targeted isolation of SH-E3 afforded one previously undescribed compound (1) together with eight known metabolites (3-10), including six sterols: ergosta-5,24(28)-dien-3-ol (5), ergosta-5,22-dien-3-ol (6), cholesterol (7), gorgosterol (8), (3β)-33-norgorgost-5-en-3-ol (9), and ergost-5-en-3-ol (10). Parallel investigation of SH-E7 yielded a second previously undescribed compound (2), structurally related to 1. Evaluation of compounds 1-10 in MG-63 cells revealed that sterols 5-10 enhanced alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity to varying degrees, whereas compounds 1-4 exhibited relatively weak or negligible effects. These findings indicate that the osteogenic activity of SH-E3 is primarily associated with its sterol-enriched chemical profile. Collectively, this study demonstrates the utility of integrating molecular networking with biological activity for the efficient prioritization of bioactive constituents from chemically complex marine extracts and highlights soft-coral-derived sterols as promising candidates for further investigation of their potential roles in glucocorticoid-induced bone loss.
