records.title: Effects of locust bean gum on cholesterol gallstones and the gut microbiota in lithogenic diet-fed C57BL/6J mice.
records.abstract: Locust bean gum (LBG) is widely used as a thickener, stabilizer, emulsifier, and gelling agent in the food industry. In this study, a lithogenic diet-induced mouse model of cholesterol gallstones was employed to examine the effects of dietary supplementation with 2% and 5% LBG. Compared to the 5% dose, the 2% dose demonstrated superior efficacy. Gut microbiota analysis revealed that the lithogenic diet disrupted the network formed by Bacillota and Bacteroidota. Intervention with 2% LBG increased the abundance of Bacillota and established a network dominated by this phylum, accompanied by the enrichment of functional genes related to two-component systems, quorum sensing and biofilm formation. In contrast, 5% LBG failed to restore the intestinal network and only elevated the abundance of certain specific members. Furthermore, 2% LBG significantly reduced the abundance of Desulfovibrio and the expression of genes involved in H2S synthesis, while also promoting a more pronounced increase in butyrate levels. Both 2% and 5% LBG suppressed HMGCR gene expression. Additionally, 2% LBG significantly downregulated the transcription of ABCG5/G8 genes and upregulated that of CYP7A1 and CYP8B1 genes, thereby decreasing cholesterol synthesis and secretion and enhancing its conversion into bile acids. Collectively, these results led to marked alterations in bile acid profiles across the groups, and consequently influenced the degree of gallstone formation. This study demonstrates for the first time that LBG dose-dependently protects mice against lithogenic diet-induced cholesterol gallstones and provides mechanistic insights into its protective effects.
records.authors: Liu X, Zhang J, Zhou S, Luo X, Song Y.

records.title: Single-cell and spatial analysis of inflammation-associated resistance in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
records.abstract: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) is frequently associated with chronic inflammation and a complex stromal microenvironment, yet the cellular and molecular features underlying heterogeneous responses to neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy remain unclear. Here, using Flex-based single-cell transcriptomic profiling of post-treatment ICC specimens from responders and non-responders, together with multiplex immunohistochemistry and animal model validation, we delineate a coordinated, inflammation-associated multicellular state linked to treatment non-response. Non-response tumors showed enrichment of SPINK1⁺ epithelial cells, inflammatory cancer-associated fibroblasts, SPP1⁺ and inflammatory macrophage states, and immunosuppressive or inflammation-associated CD4⁺ T-cell programs. Across epithelial, stromal, and immune compartments, IL6-JAK-STAT3-related inflammatory signaling emerged as a recurrent feature of resistance. Computational cell-cell communication analysis predicted increased communication probabilities between iCAFs and SPINK1⁺ epithelial cells and between InfMp and CD4Tem cells in non-response tumors, nominating TNF-TLR2, HMGB1-TLR2, AGT-CYBB, and TNF-ICAM1 as candidate ligand-receptor associations. Tissue-level validation confirmed increased SPINK1 expression, inflammatory macrophage features, and elevated p-STAT3 signals in non-response tumors. Combined PD-1 blockade and JAK1/2 inhibition showed enhanced antitumor activity in both a hydrodynamic injection-based cholangiocarcinoma-like mouse model and a humanized huPBMC-NOG-dKO mouse model bearing ICC-X1 xenografts. In the hydrodynamic model, the combination was also accompanied by reduced p-STAT3 activity and enhanced T-cell infiltration and granzyme B expression. Together, these findings identify a coordinated, multicellular inflammatory state associated with non-response to neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy in ICC and nominate JAK-STAT signaling as a convergent, therapeutically actionable vulnerability. The antitumor activity observed with combined JAK1/2 inhibition and PD-1 blockade further supports evaluating this inflammatory signaling axis as a therapeutic target to improve immunotherapy responsiveness in ICC.
records.journal: Drug resistance updates : reviews and commentaries in antimicrobial and anticancer chemotherapy
records.authors: Tang X, Huang H, Shen X, Kong G, Zhang W, Yu J, Wu C, Wu J.

records.title: Integrated Molecular Detection and Epidemiological Investigation of Brucella abortus in Dairy Cattle and Farm Workers During a Brucellosis Outbreak.
records.abstract: BackgroundBrucellosis is a highly contagious zoonotic disease caused by bacteria belonging to the genus Brucella that can infect a wide range of domestic and wild animals. A recent brucellosis outbreak was reported at a dairy farm in the peri-urban region of Khanewal District, Punjab, Pakistan.ObjectiveIn response, this study aimed to improve understanding of the dynamics of Brucella abortus infection in cattle and dairy farm workers in the local context.MethodsIn November 2024, a total of 83 cattle, representing six different breeds, along with blood samples from 11 farm workers directly involved in handling these animals, were sampled. Relevant epidemiological data were also collected to support the investigation. To detect Brucella infection in cattle, both the Rose Bengal Plate Test (RBPT) and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) targeting the IS711 gene were employed.ResultsAll sampled cattle tested seropositive for Brucella antibodies by RBPT, indicating widespread exposure to Brucella. Molecular detection through partial IS711 sequence amplification revealed that 48% of the cattle and 45% of the farm workers (5 out of 11) tested positive for Brucella spp.InfectionSubsequent DNA sequencing and BLAST analysis confirmed the presence of B. abortus in both cattle and humans. The obtained IS711 sequences closely matched those previously reported in ruminants and humans in China. Data analysis further showed that cows were more susceptible to B. abortus infection compared to bulls (p = 0.01). However, no significant association was observed between infection status and cattle breed, age, presence or absence of ectoparasites, or history of abortion (for all p > 0.05).ConclusionThe present study provides evidence of B. abortus detection among cattle at the investigated dairy farm in Khanewal. The findings should be interpreted within the context of the studied farm, as the purposive sampling of a single dairy farm does not permit extrapolation to the wider cattle population of Khanewal District or Pakistan. Further multi-farm studies involving geographically diverse cattle populations are warranted to determine the broader occurrence and epidemiological pattern of B. abortus.
records.authors: Asif M, Obaid MK, Naeem M, Muqaddas H, Ullah S, Khan A, Mahmood N, Ren Q, Alqahtani FM, Said MA, Dabiellil F, Iqbal F.

records.title: Circadian Rhythm-Associated Diagnostic Biomarkers Reveal Immune Dysregulation and Molecular Subtypes in Recurrent Pregnancy Loss.
records.abstract: BackgroundRecurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) is a clinically complex reproductive disorder involving impaired maternal-fetal communication and immune imbalance. Circadian rhythm disturbance has recently attracted attention in reproductive failure, but its diagnostic relevance and possible connection with immune dysregulation in RPL remain insufficiently defined.MethodsGSE165004 was used as the discovery cohort, and GSE26787 was used as an independent small cohort for preliminary evaluation. Circadian rhythm-associated genes were collected from GeneCards. Differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and ssGSEA-based circadian rhythm scoring were integrated to identify RPL-associated circadian transcriptional alterations. Candidate genes were further evaluated by protein-protein interaction analysis, functional enrichment, receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, nomogram construction, immune infiltration assessment, molecular subtype identification, and ceRNA regulatory network prediction.ResultsRPL samples showed a significantly lower circadian rhythm-associated gene score than control samples, indicating reduced circadian-associated transcriptional activity. Three genes, GJA1, UCP2, and GSN, were identified as circadian rhythm-associated candidate diagnostic biomarkers for RPL. In the discovery cohort, the AUC values of GJA1, UCP2, and GSN were 0.80, 0.77, and 0.81, respectively. Their diagnostic performance was further evaluated in an independent small cohort, where the AUC values were 0.72, 0.80, and 0.92, respectively. GSN showed a significant expression difference between RPL and control samples in the independent cohort, whereas GJA1 and UCP2 did not reach statistical significance. Immune infiltration analysis revealed changes in fibroblast, neutrophil, macrophage, Treg, T helper cell, and interferon-related signatures. Consensus clustering based on the three biomarkers classified RPL samples into two molecular subtypes with different immune-stromal characteristics, coagulation-related activity, and metabolic features. The ceRNA network contained 3 diagnostic mRNAs, 43 predicted miRNAs, and 61 upstream lncRNAs.ConclusionGJA1, UCP2, and GSN may represent circadian rhythm-associated candidate biomarkers for RPL. Their expression patterns may reflect circadian-immune dysregulation and molecular heterogeneity. These findings provide a circadian rhythm-based perspective for understanding RPL pathogenesis and nominate candidate molecules for future diagnostic and mechanistic validation.
records.journal: American journal of reproductive immunology (New York, N.Y. : 1989)
records.authors: Chen Y, Li Y, Wang S, Wang Y, Feng X.

records.title: Hypoxia Signatures in Renal Cell Carcinoma: From HIF-Mediated Omics Remodeling to Precision Diagnostics.
records.abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC), particularly clear cell RCC (ccRCC), exhibits extensive metabolic, signaling, and microenvironmental remodeling associated with dysregulated VHL-HIF signaling. HIF activation in RCC may arise from VHL loss under normoxic conditions and from genuine tumor hypoxia due to inadequate oxygen availability; these states can converge on overlapping downstream programs but are biologically distinct. This review examines proteomic, phosphoproteomic, metabolomic, and emerging spatial and single-cell studies that characterize hypoxia- and VHL-HIF-associated molecular alterations in RCC. Particular emphasis is placed on protein-level changes in metabolism, angiogenesis, extracellular matrix remodeling, signaling, and immune regulation, as well as on how these measurements complement transcriptomic data. The review further distinguishes mechanistic molecular signatures from candidate diagnostic, prognostic, predictive, pharmacodynamic, and treatment-selection biomarkers. Evidence for circulating proteins and metabolites is discussed together with available measures of diagnostic performance, analytical validation, and clinical validation. Finally, the potential of integrated discovery and targeted mass-spectrometry approaches to support clinically useful multianalyte biomarker panel development is considered, while highlighting the challenges of tumor heterogeneity, assay reproducibility, cohort validation, and clinical utility.
records.authors: Mahalinga M, Rai AB, Prasad TSK.

records.title: Proximity Labeling: An Empowering Tool for Deciphering Molecular Mechanisms.
records.abstract: Proximity labeling (PL) has become a widely used approach for studying protein-protein interactions (PPIs) and addressing limitations of conventional techniques in capturing transient, weak interactions, and physiological protein networks within living systems. Over the past decade, core PL enzymes, notably APEX2, BirA* (BioID), and TurboID, have been iteratively engineered, with reported improvements in temporal resolution, targeting specificity, and biocompatibility. This review summarizes how PL technologies have developed and describes the enzymatic properties, catalytic mechanisms, and reported performance trade-offs of the commonly used tools. We then survey applications of PL in neuroscience, cardiology, oncology, and infectious disease, where it has been used to map compartment-specific proteomes and spatiotemporally regulated networks, including neural activity-driven PPIs, tumor microenvironment cross-talk, and host-pathogen interfaces. Many of the resulting candidates await orthogonal validation. We also describe recently reported conditional PL systems with optical, calcium- or oxygen-dependent control. Finally, we discuss open questions and possible directions for PL development, including enzyme-directed evolution, multisignal responsive regulation, cross-omics integration, and translational applications. This review is intended as a practical reference for researchers to support the selection and application of PL platforms in specific experimental contexts from mechanistic studies to the identification of candidate therapeutic targets.
records.authors: Liang H, Chen S, Gan K, Chai R, Bi Z.

records.title: From Mechanical Perturbation to Pathological Locking: Temporal-Mechanical Evolution of the Postsynaptic Density After Traumatic Brain Injury.
records.abstract: BackgroundTraumatic brain injury (TBI) induces persistent cognitive deficits, yet conventional biochemical and structural models often fail to explain synaptic signal collapse in the absence of overt tissue rupture.ResultsHere, we present a hypothesis-generating mechanobiological framework that positions postsynaptic density (PSD)-a multivalent protein condensate governed by liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS)-as a primary locus of synaptic mechanovulnerability. We argue that TBI-induced synaptic pathology is not merely a quantitative loss of molecular components, but a progressive, staged material state transition of the PSD network. This pathological evolution initiates with hyperacute mechanical deconstruction, leading to physical scaffold decoupling and nanoscale receptor misalignment. It then advances through an acute mechano-metabolic crisis characterized by enzymatic scaffold cleavage and impaired re-condensation, ultimately culminating in a chronically locked, low-dynamic "solidified" state. Furthermore, post-injury extracellular matrix stiffening and the mechanical exposure of cryptic epitopes trigger aberrant microglial pruning via mechanosensors such as Piezo1, permanently dismantling neural circuits. Because the supporting evidence is heterogeneous, we explicitly grade each element of this model as established directly in TBI, supported in non-TBI synaptic systems, extrapolated from reconstituted condensates, or hypothetical.ConclusionsBy bridging macroscopic biomechanics with nanoscale molecular pathology, this review highlights a critical conceptual gap and proposes "mechano-therapeutics" as a hypothesis-generating concept rather than an established treatment avenue. We suggest that strategies targeting the physical properties of the synapse, such as stabilizing scaffold oligomerization, modulating mechanotransduction pathways, and restoring physiological tissue stiffness, are candidate directions whose feasibility, delivery, cell-type specificity, timing, and safety must first be established in preclinical models before any clinical translation to rescue synaptic homeostasis and cognitive function after TBI.
records.authors: Jia Y, Cao Z, Xue H, Feng Z, Ma Z, Tian Z, Li X, Luo P.

records.title: Revealing the Action Mechanism of WISP2 in Miscarriage Based Multi-Omic Analysis and Experimental Validation.
records.abstract: Recurrent miscarriage (RM) is a major unresolved issue in reproductive medicine. Although WISP2 is known to participate in multiple cellular processes, its function in trophoblast biology and pregnancy maintenance remains unknown. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing on chorionic villus tissues from RM patients and normal controls to identify cell-type-specific transcriptional alterations, which led to the identification of WISP2 as a candidate gene in the SCT/EVT subpopulation. Fetal membrane samples (chorion) were obtained from Qingdao Women and Children's Hospital's Surgical Outpatient Department: 20 RM patients and 20 healthy controls. Using qRT-PCR, Western blot, and immunohistochemistry to detect gene and protein expression. HTR-8 cells were used to construct WISP2 overexpressing cells, and MTT, wound healing and Transwell experiments were performed for functional experiments. Eleven cell classes in the sample were demonstrated by single-cell analysis. Among these cells were DSCs and SCT/extravillous trophoblasts (EVT). The level of WISP2 is low in SCT/EVT cells from RM patients. In chorionic villus tissues, both WISP2 and E-cadherin were significantly upregulated in the RM group relative to the control group (all p  0.05), suggesting that WISP2 promotes an epithelial-like phenotype accompanied by ERK pathway activation. In summary, WISP2 is dysregulated in RM and suppresses trophoblast invasion and EMT in vitro, suggesting a potential role in RM pathogenesis, though in vivo validation is required.
records.authors: Leng Z, Yan B, Wang F, Bian X, Huang Y, Lv H, Jiang Z, Sun X.

records.title: Analysis and Identification of Candidate Genes Associated with M1 Macrophage Infiltration and Glycolysis in Breast Cancer.
records.abstract: Macrophage polarization and glycolytic reprogramming contribute to the breast cancer microenvironment. However, the genes associated with these features and their clinical relevance remain poorly defined. Breast cancer transcriptomic datasets were analyzed using immune deconvolution, single-sample gene set enrichment analysis, and weighted gene coexpression network analysis. We identified 101 genes shared by the M1 macrophage-associated, glycolysis-related, and differentially expressed gene sets. Eight genes showed suggestive genetically predicted associations with BC risk. Machine learning selected seven consensus genes. In TCGA-BRCA, six genes differed significantly between tumor and normal tissue, but only five changed in the same direction as in GSE65194. In the 56 paired clinical tissues, ADAM15, PPP1R14B, and XPO5 were upregulated in tumors, whereas FAM172A and PPM1M were downregulated. ADAM15, PPP1R14B, and XPO5 were preferentially expressed in M1-like TAMs, whereas FAM172A and PPM1M showed higher expression in M2-like TAMs. In BMDMs, overexpression of ADAM15, XPO5, or PPP1R14B, as well as knockdown of PPM1M or FAM172A, increased the proportion of CD80-positive cells and ATP, glucose uptake, and lactate production. Five genes showed significant associations with overall survival. Functional enrichment analyses implicated immune regulation, extracellular matrix organization, and metabolic pathways.
records.authors: Zhang L, Wu L, Xu C, Fang C, Tian X, Zhu K.

records.title: Machine-Learning-Guided Identification of CCT245737 as a Functional Pan-G-Quadruplex Ligand for the Treatment of Multiple Myeloma.
records.abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) still lacks curative therapies, creating an urgent demand for innovative agents targeting unique molecular vulnerabilities. G-quadruplex (G4) stabilization modulates oncogenic regulatory regions and displays potent preclinical antitumor effects. Nevertheless, most existing G4 ligands act on single G4 motifs. Pan-G4 agents capable of perturbing multiple oncogenic pathways are scarce, while conventional high-throughput screening is costly and labor-intensive. Herein, we constructed a repurposing-driven screening pipeline combining curated fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET)-derived melting-temperature shift (ΔTm) data sets, 1024-bit Chemistry Development Kit (CDK) molecular fingerprints, three machine-learning classifiers, and multi-G4 molecular docking. In nested cross-validation, our Random Forest (RF) classifier yielded a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC AUC) of 0.840 and a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.708, superior to label-randomized controls. Consensus screening of 4270 compounds from the TargetMol Anticancer Library yielded 812 high-confidence hits; the top-ranked 487 candidates underwent docking against four structurally diverse oncogenic G4s (c-Myc, c-KIT, Bcl-2, k-RAS). CCT245737 ranked in the top ten across all four independent docking analyses. Functional assays revealed that CCT245737 suppressed the viability of U266 and RPMI-8226 MM cells (IC50 = 0.58 ± 0.06 and 0.68 ± 0.04 μM) and enhanced nuclear BG4 signals. FRET-melting and NMM-displacement assays verified its concentration-dependent stabilization of the four G4s with minimal duplex-DNA interference. qPCR and immunoblotting confirmed downregulation of c-Myc, c-KIT, Bcl-2, and k-RAS at both mRNA and protein levels. In summary, CCT245737 is validated as a promising pan-G4 ligand, and our FRET-guided workflow offers a feasible repurposing strategy for discovering anti-MM G4-targeted therapeutics.

records.title: Revealing the Widespread Bias of Extinction Risk in the Antarctic and the Southern Ocean.
records.abstract: Accelerating environmental change in the Antarctic and Southern Ocean (ASO) necessitates robust extinction risk assessments to inform conservation priorities. Nevertheless, no systematic, region-wide baseline of extinction risk currently exists for tracking ASO biodiversity responses to ongoing change, a significant barrier to global biodiversity monitoring. Here, we conducted the first ASO-wide synthesis of current extinction risk knowledge for plants, animals and Fungi. This included examining biases in current assessments, the distribution of Threatened species and their associated threats. Using a data-inclusive workflow, we compiled 8908 assessments representing 4970 species, more than doubling the number of ASO species assessed compared with any single source. As expected, assessments were heavily biased towards vertebrates (58% assessed), while invertebrates, despite their ecological prevalence, were markedly underrepresented (6% assessed). Among vertebrates, mammals had the highest proportion of Threatened species (26%). Birds within the ASO were disproportionately Threatened (25%) compared to the global average (11%), with the greatest threat for ASO species being 'Biological Resource Use'. The sub-Antarctic Islands had the highest density of both Threatened species and assessment effort, whereas many Antarctic species remain unassessed. Additionally, Threatened species have the lowest protected area coverage of any conservation status. These pronounced assessment biases highlight the need for more balanced, representative and data-inclusive extinction risk assessments to be able to effectively detect conservation status change. This work represents an important step in ensuring ASO representation in global biodiversity monitoring frameworks, strengthening the capacity of these frameworks to detect, attribute and respond to future biodiversity changes.
records.authors: Farrant MG, Liu WPA, McGeoch MA.

records.title: Thiol-Mediated Hydrazide Installation from Diazo in the Biosynthesis of Spinamycin.
records.abstract: Natural products featuring nitrogen-nitrogen (N-N) bonds often possess potent bioactivities, and their architectures frequently reveal novel enzymatic mechanisms. Current understanding for acylhydrazide installation is limited to a "hydrazine-first" strategy, wherein an activated acyl donor is nucleophilically attacked by a preassembled hydrazine intermediate. Spinamycin, an antifungal hydrazide-containing aryl polyene from Streptomyces albospinus, challenges this convention. Its biosynthetic machinery utilizes SpiA7, an ATP-dependent, nitrite-utilizing N-nitrosylase, to synthesize a highly transient diazo intermediate rather than a hydrazine core. How this unstable diazo compound is converted into a stable hydrazide has remained a long-standing biosynthetic mystery. Herein, we report the in vitro reconstitution of the activity of SpiA7 in conversion of the amine substrate into its mature succinylhydrazide form. Mechanistic characterization revealed that the electrophilic diazo intermediate is initially captured by thiol reagents to generate a covalent azo-sulfide intermediate (R-N═N-S-R'). This species likely undergoes a noncanonical four-electron reduction driven cooperatively by disulfide bond formation and the oxidative decarboxylation of α-ketoglutarate (αKG), which serves as the succinyl donor. Furthermore, site-directed mutagenesis identifies Cys453 of SpiA7 as a likely active-site thiol donor orchestrating this transformation. Collectively, our findings unveil an unprecedented chemical strategy for hydrazide assembly that completely bypasses a free hydrazine intermediate, expanding nature's known catalytic repertoire for building complex N-N linkages.

records.title: PEGylated Chrysin: In Vitro Biological Activity and Mechanistic Insights in HepG2 Cells.
records.abstract: PEGylated chrysin, a natural flavonoid conjugated with methoxypolyethylene glycol, exhibits in vitro cytotoxic properties, likely through apoptosis induction. In this study, we investigated its biological effects on HepG2 hepatocellular carcinoma cells, comparing its activity with the chemotherapeutic agent paclitaxel. We evaluated reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, membrane integrity, DNA damage, and wound closure using the scratch assay. At equivalent concentrations, PEGylated chrysin induced higher cell membrane damage but generated lower ROS levels compared to paclitaxel. Both compounds exhibited similar efficacy to reduce wound closure under the evaluated experimental conditions. Additionally, PEGylated chrysin significantly increased the frequency of micronuclei in binucleated cells, indicating genotoxic potential. To assess cellular uptake, a novel fluorescein-tagged conjugate (fluorescein-PEG-chrysin) was synthesized which demonstrated that the PEGylated drug is accumulated in the cytoplasm of HepG2 cells. These results highlight PEGylated chrysin as a promising candidate with antiproliferative potential, capable of inducing diverse cellular damage pathways in liver cancer cells while showing a distinct cytotoxic profile compared with Paclitaxel.
records.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
records.authors: Gasser FB, Oggero J, Renna MS, Beltramino MF, Simonetto C, Dominguez L, Ortega HH, Vaillard SE, Vaillard VA, Baravalle ME.

records.title: In Situ Mechanistic Insights into the Divergent Electrochemical Behaviors of Li, Na, and K in Metal Sulfur Batteries.
records.abstract: Metal-sulfur batteries are promising candidates for next-generation energy storage, yet the origins of their distinct reaction behaviors remain elusive. Here, we employ a noncatalytic vapor-grown carbon fibers/sulfur (VGCF/S) interface to regulate sulfur electrochemistry. In situ TEM reveals highly reversible two-step redox reactions and rapid reaction-front propagation in Li-S nanobatteries. Coin-cell measurements further show reversible cycling and rate capability for Li-S under specific testing conditions. DFT calculations in idealized graphitic and sulfur-carbon environments provide a qualitative comparison of alkali-species-dependent migration. The observed divergence may reflect coupled contributions from alkali-species transport, interfacial processes, electrolyte-dependent sulfur-redox pathways, and product evolution. This work highlights noncatalytic interfaces as a platform for probing sulfur electrochemistry.
records.authors: Cao X, Sun G, Hua Z, Zhou L, Gao P, Yan L, Bao L, Chang X, Zhang L, Tan G, Wang L, Zuo X, Shao R.

records.title: Design, Synthesis, and Antifungal Activity of Benzoxazole Amides: Focusing on Target Research against Verticillium Dahliae.
records.abstract: A series of benzoxazole amide derivatives were synthesized, and their antifungal activities against phytopathogens were tested by mycelial growth inhibition method. Compound L9 exhibited potent activity against Verticillium dahliae with an EC50 of 0.18 μM. In vivo experiments revealed its curative efficacy on eggplant verticillium wilt was 80.00%. Phenotypic results indicated that L9 damaged the integrity of fungal cell wall and membrane. Transcriptome and RT-qPCR screening identified β-N-acetylhexosaminidase as the core gene. Molecular docking predicted stable binding of L9 to this protein, which was further verified by time-series enzyme activity assays showing obvious inhibition of enzyme activity. This study constructs a complete phenotype-pathway-target evidence chain, offering lead compounds for novel antifungal agrochemicals.

records.title: SlABCB13 Regulates Hexose and Sucrose Homeostasis during Tomato Fruit Development.
records.abstract: Sugar accumulation in fleshy fruits is largely dependent on membrane-localized sugar transporters, among which SWEET proteins play important roles. Although ABCB transporters, a subclass of the ATP-binding cassette (ABC) superfamily, mediate the transport of diverse substrates and participate in various physiological processes in plants, their direct involvement in fruit sugar accumulation remains unclear. In this study, SlABCB13, an ABCB transporter in tomato, was characterized. Multiple in vitro and in vivo assays demonstrated that SlABCB13 physically interacts with SlSWEET14. SlABCB13 was predominantly expressed in fruits and localized to the plasma membrane. Heterologous expression in yeast showed that SlABCB13 transported fructose and glucose, but not sucrose. Genetic analysis revealed that CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of SlABCB13 significantly increased fruit hexose, sucrose, and total sugar contents while reducing fruit weight. SlABCB13-overexpressing lines also demonstrated reduced fruit weight, accompanied by stage-specific alterations in sugar levels. Transcriptome analysis revealed distinct transcriptional reprogramming in SlABCB13 knockout and overexpression lines, characterized by downregulation of sugar transporter genes in the overexpression lines, consistent with feedback inhibition, and upregulation in the knockout lines, indicative of compensatory activation. These results identify SlABCB13 as a plant ABCB transporter that mediates hexose transport in yeast and as an important regulator of sugar homeostasis in tomato fruits through coordinated feedback and compensatory mechanisms. This study broadens the functional spectrum of ABCB transporters and highlights SlABCB13 as a potential target for molecular breeding to improve fruit quality.
records.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
records.authors: Xie X, Xie N, Qi T, Liu P, Li Q, Qiao H, Wang W, Zhang X.

records.title: Synergistic Pairwise Residues Identification for Efficient Evolution of Candida antarctica Lipase B for Synthesis of γ- and δ-Lactones.
records.abstract: The lipase enzyme shows great potential for catalyzing the synthesis of valuable food flavor compounds, such as γ- and δ-lactones, but natural lipases are limited by low conversion rates. In this study, we developed a computational-guided strategy named Synergistic Pairwise Residues Evolution for the efficient directed evolution of Candida antarctica lipase B (CalB). This approach identifies synergistic hotspot residues by combining substrate-contact information with evolutionarily coupled functional sectors. E188Q/I189F, the top-performing mutant with 2.75-fold improved activity, achieved over 99.5% conversion within 5 h at 37 °C, compared with only 49% for wild-type CalB in the synthesis of δ-dodecalactone. This study presents an efficient strategy for building functional enzyme toolkits and demonstrates their high catalytic performance in lactone synthesis.

records.authors: Zhang Q, Tang L, Zhao Y, Li Z, Ran Y, Tan Z, Chen H, Feng Y, Cui L.

records.title: Posttranslational Modifications of Unconventional Autoantigens: Shaping Immunogenicity and Inflammatory Activity.
records.abstract: Posttranslational modifications (PTMs) of self-antigens precipitate autoimmunity by generating neo-epitopes that breach tolerance and activate autoreactive T and B cells. This review spotlights cathelicidin LL37 and chemokine CXCL4 (PF4) in psoriatic disease (psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis, PSO and PSA), systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), and systemic sclerosis (SSc), drawing on key studies including our own. Uniquely, unlike most autoantigens, LL37 and CXCL4 exert a dual role: they are immunogenic targets for T and B cells while directly fueling innate inflammation. Through chaperone-like binding to self- and microbial DNA/RNA, they form complexes that potently stimulate plasmacytoid and myeloid dendritic cells (pDCs/mDCs) via DNA/RNA sensors, such as TLR7-9 and cGAS/STING, driving Type I interferon and cytokines storms. Strikingly, these complexes also induce B cells to become antibody-producing plasma cells, amplifying adaptive responses and likely suppressing regulation. Here, we detail the role of PTM-modified LL37 in PSO, PSA, and SLE-forming autoantigenic neutrophil extracellular traps-and CXCL4 in SSc, where it acts as biomarker and autoantibody target. Our work underscores how this dual functionality as "bifunctional autoantigens" exacerbates disease, and how PTMs modification influence these phenomena. These molecules and their PTM can be targeted to halt inflammatory cascades and restore tolerance.
records.authors: Lande R, Mennella A, Palazzo R, Frasca L.

records.title: From data-driven differential equations to mechanistic forecasting with machine learning.
records.abstract: The equations of complex dynamical systems may not be identified by expert knowledge, especially if the underlying mechanisms are unknown. Data-driven discovery methods address this challenge by inferring governing equations from time-series data using a library of functions constructed from the measured variables. However, these methods typically assume time-invariant coefficients, which limits their ability to capture evolving system dynamics. To overcome this limitation, we allow some of the parameters to vary over time, learn their temporal evolution directly from data and infer a system of equations that incorporates both constant and time-varying parameters. We then transform this framework into a forecasting model by predicting the time-varying parameters and substituting these predictions into the learned equations. The model is validated on simulated susceptible-infected-recovered and consumer-resource systems, as well as on real-world greenhouse gas concentration and cyanobacteria cell count datasets. By dynamically adapting to temporal shifts, our proposed model achieved a mean absolute error below 3% for learning a time series and below 6% for forecasting up to a month ahead. We additionally compare forecasting performance against convolutional neural network-long short-term memory and gradient boosting machine, and show that our model outperforms these methods across most datasets. Our findings demonstrate that integrating time-varying parameters into data-driven discovery of differential equations improves both modelling accuracy and forecasting performance.
records.journal: Journal of the Royal Society, Interface
records.authors: Chakraborty AK, Wang H, Ramazi P.

records.title: Monotonic additive modeling reveals candidate biomarkers of cardio-renal-metabolic disorder susceptibility.
records.abstract: Cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus form an interconnected disease continuum driven by shared risk factors, overlapping molecular pathways and reciprocal progression. This convergence has led to the recognition of cardio-renal-metabolic disorder (CRMD) as a unified systemic condition in which dysregulation of metabolic, vascular, inflammatory and renal pathways precedes organ-specific pathology. Despite this understanding, current diagnostic strategies remain disease-centric and are typically initiated after substantial tissue damage, limiting opportunities for early intervention. Identification of early non-invasive biomarkers capturing shared CRMD susceptibility is therefore of utmost clinical importance. In this study, we developed an explainable monotonic additive machine learning framework to identify blood-based molecular biomarkers associated with CRMD susceptibility. Transcriptomic profiles representing cardiovascular, renal and metabolic disease states were analysed within a unified CRMD paradigm. Following transcriptomic harmonization and batch correction, a monotonic additive XGBoost model combined with integrated biomarker score, gene-response analysis and differential expression analysis was implemented to identify biologically interpretable and directionally consistent biomarkers reflective of shared CRMD-associated dysregulation. Six biomarkers, including EEF1D, RPL27A, ERO1LB, JUN, POSTN and SERPINE2, were identified as potential CRMD susceptibility biomarkers spanning translational regulation, proteostasis, endoplasmic-reticulum function, systemic inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, vascular dysfunction, extracellular remodeling and fibrosis. Importantly, these biomarkers have potential for blood-based detection using established assays such as ELISA, multiplex immunoassays and quantitative PCR, underscoring their translational potential for early CRMD screening, susceptibility assessment and risk stratification.

records.title: Voltage-Dependent Metabolic Shifts Regulate the Fouling Behavior of the Anaerobic-Anodic Membrane.
records.abstract: Fouling remains the key barrier to durable membrane operation, against which electrochemical processes offer a promising fouling control strategy. However, the performance of an anodic membrane under anaerobic conditions exhibits significant instability, the mechanism of which remains unclear and represents a critical knowledge gap. This study systematically investigated the response of membrane fouling evolution to gradient electric fields within anodic membranes. A distinct threshold behavior of electric field strength on membrane fouling was observed, with a system-dependent threshold occurring between 0.7 and 1.0 V. Following an initial fouling layer, subthreshold fields (≤0.7 V) exacerbated fouling accumulation, whereas supra-threshold fields (≥1.0 V) slowed down membrane fouling development. Comprehensive analysis revealed that surpassing critical field strength enhanced anodic electron-accepting capacity, likely facilitating microbial extracellular electron release and alleviating reductive pressure. This triggered a nonlinear, threshold-dependent metabolic switch from biosynthesis-dominated to catabolism-enhanced pathways, coupled with quorum quenching that inhibited biofilm maturation. These synergistic transitions underpinned the fouling reversal. This work advances the understanding of anaerobic-anodic membrane fouling from an empirical observation into a threshold-governed electrochemical-microbial switching process, thereby providing the scientific foundation for harnessing this interplay to achieve durable and efficient operation in anaerobic wastewater treatment and resource recovery systems.
records.authors: Sun X, Chen M, Yan W, Wang J, Wu Q, Li N, Wang X, Wang Z.

records.title: Nitrogen-Centered Persistent Free Radicals from Roxarsone Phototransformation on Soil Minerals: Magnetic Coupling Mechanism and PFR-Driven Ecological Risks.
records.abstract: Roxarsone (ROX) degradation in soil environments is a recognized source of arsenic contamination, but the concurrent evolution of persistent free radicals (PFRs) presents an overlooked hazard. Here, we report the generation of unique nitrogen-centered PFRs during ROX phototransformation on soil mineral surfaces. Unlike typical environmental PFRs, these species exhibit a distinct triple-peak EPR signature, which is proposed to arise from the magnetic coupling between •NO and •NHR radicals following C-As bond cleavage. Mineral composition strongly governs radical evolution, with MnO2 enhancing and Fe2O3 suppressing PFR stability. These nitrogen-centered radicals act as efficient electron shuttles, sustaining the production of reactive oxygen species (•OH, •O2-, H2O2). Multitrophic toxicity tests (bacteria-plant-earthworm) combined with rigorous arsenic-controlled conditions (As(V)≤150 ppb, As(III)≤20 ppb) reveal that the observed growth inhibition, oxidative damage, and histopathological effects are predominantly driven by PFR-mediated processes rather than by released inorganic arsenic. These findings uncover a previously unrecognized pathway for nitrogen-centered radical formation and highlight the necessity of incorporating radical-driven toxicity into environmental risk assessments of organoarsenic contaminants.
records.authors: Feng H, Li Y, Ren F, Jin X, Zhang X, Yang Y, Chen H, Cai P, Ding X.

records.title: Quinone Reductase 2 Dimerization is Dynamically Driven by Ligand Binding.
records.abstract: Human quinone reductase 2 is a cytosolic flavoprotein involved in cell physiology and metabolism, and implicated in several diseases. However, the mechanisms that govern its oligomeric assembly and diverse functional outcomes remain incompletely understood. Here, we employ native mass spectrometry to directly resolve the dynamic oligomeric landscape of recombinant human quinone reductase 2 expressed in Escherichia coli, preserving noncovalent interactions and enabling analysis of assembly behavior under native conditions. Quinone reductase 2 is predominantly observed as a dimer stabilized by multiple noncovalently bound ligands, giving rise to discrete species. Top-down native mass spectrometry reveals a single intact proteoform, excluding covalent modification or covalently bound flavins as drivers of oligomerization. Binding of flavin adenine dinucleotide robustly stabilizes the dimer, while unexpectedly, flavin mononucleotide also promotes dimer formation. As flavin mononucleotide and flavin adenine dinucleotide differ structurally by the presence of an adenine dinucleotide moiety, we hypothesized that purine nucleotide binding itself may modulate quinone reductase 2 assembly. Consistent with this, we identify a new concentration-dependent effect of guanosine triphosphate on quinone reductase 2 dimerization. Functional reductase assays show that flavin-stabilized dimers exhibit the highest catalytic activity, whereas guanosine triphosphate-induced dimers retain reduced activity. Binding of the inhibitor YB537 abolishes activity despite promoting dimer formation. Together, these findings reveal ligand-dependent structural plasticity in quinone reductase 2 oligomerization that is decoupled from reductase activity. This supports a model in which dimerization is shaped by the local ligand environment, enabling distinct functional states and suggesting a broader regulatory role beyond reductase catalysis.
records.authors: Miller M, Loewenthal D, Kukura P, Gould N.

records.title: TP-Ring and ZN-Ring Systems Allow Efficient Protein Clamping, Solubilization and Stabilization.
records.abstract: Improving recombinant protein stability remains a central challenge in biotechnology, as many proteins exhibit limited robustness during production and use. Here, we introduce two intramolecular "clamping" systems, termed ZN-ring and TP-ring, that exploit ultrastable noncovalent protein-protein interactions to constrain the N- and C-termini of a target protein. These systems are derived from the high-affinity complexes formed by ZNHIT3/NUFIP1 and TAH1/PIH1, respectively, whose interactions are driven by extensive hydrophobic interfaces. Proof-of-concept constructs demonstrate that intrachain clamping preserves native-like interactions and yields highly stable assemblies with melting temperatures exceeding 95 °C. When applied to a model protein, the TP-ring significantly enhances thermal stability, consistent with structural predictions suggesting additional stabilizing contacts. Furthermore, clamping markedly improves the soluble expression of a challenging polyethylene terephthalate hydrolase (PETase) in Escherichia coli, without compromising its catalytically active fold. These results establish protein clamping as a versatile strategy to enhance stability, solubility, and expression. Given their intrinsic robustness and broad compatibility with diverse targets, ZN- and TP-ring systems provide a promising platform for protein engineering, with potential applications in biotechnology and structural biology.
records.authors: Wenzel J, Kriznik A, Chagot ME, Quinternet M.

records.title: Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia Starts in Utero: MicroRNA Dysregulation Across the Fetal-Neonatal Continuum in the Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia Development.
records.abstract: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is a heterogeneous developmental lung disorder resulting from the interaction between antenatal susceptibility and postnatal injury. Increasing evidence suggests that its biological origins may precede preterm birth, with placental dysfunction, fetal growth restriction, inflammation and oxidative stress influencing pulmonary developmental trajectories before exposure to the extrauterine environment. MicroRNAs (miRNAs), small non-coding RNAs that regulate gene expression at the post-transcriptional level, are emerging as potential molecular mediators linking these fetal and neonatal processes. This educational review examines miRNA dysregulation across the fetal-neonatal continuum of BPD. We first discuss the role of miRNAs in physiological lung development and their disruption following premature birth. We then explore how placental dysfunction and fetal growth restriction may influence miRNA networks, including placenta-enriched C19MC miRNAs, thereby contributing to antenatal susceptibility to BPD. Particular attention is given to miRNA-mediated regulation of pulmonary angiogenesis and VEGF signaling and to the bidirectional relationship between miRNAs and oxidative stress, including modulation of NRF2-dependent antioxidant responses. Beyond their mechanistic relevance, miRNAs offer potential translational opportunities. Their stability and detectability across different biological compartments-including placenta, cord blood, peripheral blood, respiratory samples and extracellular vesicles-make them attractive candidates for longitudinal biomarker profiling, while experimental modulation using miRNA mimics and inhibitors provides proof of concept for future therapeutic approaches. However, heterogeneity in biological sampling, analytical methods, developmental timing and BPD phenotypes, together with challenges in tissue-specific delivery and off-target effects, currently limit clinical translation. Rather than identifying a single 'BPD miRNA', future research should focus on dynamic, multi-compartment miRNA networks integrating antenatal programming with postnatal exposures. Such an approach may improve molecular endotyping, early risk stratification and ultimately the development of individualized preventive and therapeutic strategies for BPD.

records.title: Hypothalamic cell-type differences associated with selection for tameness in the silver fox.
records.abstract: The hypothalamus is a highly heterogeneous brain region that regulates fundamental physiological processes and behaviors, including innate social behaviors such as aggression, mating, and parenting1. Distinct cell types within hypothalamic nuclei have been linked to social behaviors, a principle established most clearly in mice, where manipulation of defined hypothalamic neuronal subtypes can initiate or suppress behaviors including attack, mounting, and parenting1,2,3,4. Whether hypothalamic cell types are modified as a result of selection during the evolution of social behavior remains unknown. Silver foxes (Vulpes vulpes) have been selectively bred for tame or aggressive behaviors and we have studied whether there are differences relating to these behaviors in the cellular makeup of the hypothalamus. We report here that tame foxes have fewer estrogen receptor-expressing neurons in the ventrolateral subdivision of the ventromedial hypothalamus (VMHvl) than aggressive foxes, and that this reduction is specific to a neuronal subtype linked to aggressive states in mice5. We have thus identified a candidate hypothalamic neuronal subtype associated with selection on social behavior during animal domestication.
records.authors: Klein JL, Shepeleva DV, Vladimirova AV, Kharlamova AV, Miller AD, Kukekova AV, Markenscoff-Papadimitriou E.

records.title: Novel recombinant bovine papular stomatitis virus expressing foot-and-mouth disease virus-like particles elicits neutralizing antibodies in cattle.
records.abstract: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) remains a major burden in endemic regions, where inactivated vaccines are constrained by cost, short duration of immunity, cold-chain dependence and high-containment manufacturing. Here, we engineered a recombinant bovine papular stomatitis virus (rBPSV) expressing the FMD virus (FMDV) A24 Cruzeiro capsid precursor P1-2A together with an attenuated 3C protease (3CproL127P). Infection of ovine foetal turbinate cells resulted in FMDV capsid protein expression and assembly of 25-30 nm icosahedral virus-like particles (VLPs). Intramuscular immunization of two BPSV-seropositive calves with rBPSV (107 TCID50 on days 0, 21 and 35) induced anti-FMDV humoral responses. By day 28, liquid-phase blocking ELISA titres exceeded laboratory-defined protective threshold (≥1.9 log10), and homologous neutralizing titres against A24 Cruzeiro surpassed the threshold associated with protection (≥1.36 log10). Intra-serotypic cross-neutralization was observed against A/Argentina/2001, whereas no neutralization was detected against heterologous serotype O1 Campos. Pre-existing anti-BPSV antibodies did not prevent induction of neutralizing responses. These findings establish the first proof of concept that BPSV can serve as a cattle-adapted vector platform for delivery of FMDV VLPs.

records.title: Single-cell transcriptome-wide association analysis reveals epithelial cell-specific genetic susceptibility to colorectal cancer
records.abstract: Bulk-tissue transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) have identified colorectal cancer (CRC) susceptibility genes, but cell-type-specific regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we performed single-cell TWAS integrating matched germline genotypes and single-cell transcriptomes from normal colorectal mucosa (381 donors) and polyps (84 donors), cell-type-specific chromatin accessibility, and GWAS from 132,261 cases and 1,752,398 controls. We identified 546 gene-cell-type associations implicating 347 candidate susceptibility genes across seven normal and nine polyp epithelial populations, including 213 previously unreported genes, with 74% exhibiting cell-type-specific associations. Integrated co-expression and ChIP-seq analyses revealed distinct TF-risk gene networks, highlighting GATA6, MAX and RAD21 in normal mucosa, and TFAP4- and CEBPB-associated networks in premalignant polyp populations. Further multi-omics analyses supported dysregulation of 233 genes (67%), while drug-target analyses identified 63 potentially druggable genes. DepMap and CRISPR–Cas9 analyses implicated 35 genes in CRC cell viability. These findings reveal cell-type-specific susceptibility mechanisms and prioritize candidate therapeutic targets for CRC prevention.

records.title: A network of bZIP transcription factors and inhibitors enforces differentially proliferative and cytotoxic states in T cells
records.abstract: The bZIP family of transcription factors (TFs) plays a central role in regulating T-cell exhaustion. Their complex dimeric interactions obscure the roles of individual members, which genetic knockout or overexpression alone poorly resolve. Here, we use overexpression of full-length bZIP family TFs alongside genetically encoded, protein-based inhibitors to probe the effect of increased or decreased bZIP TF activity on CAR T-cell expansion under exhausting conditions. Enrichment of inhibitors of pro-exhaustion TFs (CREM, NFIL3) illustrated the utility of this approach. The screen enriched full-length TFs of established anti-exhaustion relevance and identified underappreciated bZIP TFs such as BATF2. Detailed comparison of several bZIP TFs and inhibitors revealed distinct effects on proliferation, persistence, and cytotoxicity. We investigated combinations of pro-cytotoxic JUN, pro-proliferative BATF2, and a novel inhibitor (AEL-CREM) of pro-dysfunction CREM. Distinct pairs were more advantageous for maintenance of cytotoxicity or proliferation, revealing relationships between BATF2, JUN-, and CREB1-family bZIPs. Using a combination of epistasis, transcriptome, proteome, and AP-MS interactome analyses of BATF2 and AEL-CREM, we discovered functional overlap in their inhibition of pro-dysfunction CREB1-family activity, potentially driven by unexpected binding of CREB1-family members by overexpressed BATF2. Their function diverged in BATF2’s early promotion of pro-proliferation AP-1 activity and later physical and functional interactions with BACH2, contributing to persistence. These findings were mirrored in murine chronic viral infection and syngeneic tumor models, where BATF2 or AEL-CREM overexpression were notably pro-proliferative and anti-exhaustion. Together, these results illuminate new connections and functional roles enabled by bZIP family perturbations, with implications for modulating T-cell state. One sentence summary  Overexpression and protein-based inhibition of bZIP-family transcription factors in T cells reveal a network of BATF-, JUN-, CREB1-, and BACH2-family bZIPs regulating T cell exhaustion.

records.title: Combined siRNA Targeting IκBα and Stat6 Promotes Macrophage Reprogramming toward Cancer Immunotherapy.
records.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are central regulators of the tumor microenvironment (TME). Their polarization state can critically influence tumor development and treatment resistance. In the TME, the pro-tumor M2-like phenotype is the most prevalent among TAMs and contributes to tumor progression by promoting immunosuppression, angiogenesis, and metastasis. Thus, reprogramming TAMs from an M2 to an antitumor M1-like phenotype is a promising strategy to enhance cancer immunotherapy by inhibiting these processes, stimulating inflammatory responses, and activating cytotoxic immune cells. In this study, an array of small interfering RNA (siRNA) targeting candidate genes to repolarize macrophages, i.e., the inhibitor of nuclear factor kappa B alpha (IκBα), the colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor (Csf-1r), and the signal transducer and activator of transcription 6 (Stat6), was delivered by lipid nanoparticles (LNPs). While knockdown of all targeted genes was successful, silencing IκBα or Stat6 altered M1/M2 marker expression toward an M1-like polarization. Furthermore, combining IκBα and Stat6 produced the most effective macrophage reprogramming, achieving simultaneous downregulation of M2 markers and upregulation of M1 markers. Our data demonstrates that this dual-targeting strategy strongly induced potent reprogramming of M2-polarized macrophages, establishing it as a superior immunotherapeutic framework.

records.title: Prospective Evaluation of Hepatitis B Virus Reactivation in Cancer Patients Receiving Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors.
records.abstract: Data on hepatitis B virus reactivation (HBVr) during tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy remain limited. We prospectively enrolled patients with chronic or resolved HBV receiving TKIs for lung cancer or chronic myeloid leukemia at one Taiwanese center (January 2023-March 2025). HBV DNA and liver enzymes were monitored 12-weekly and HBsAg 24-weekly. HBVr was defined by AASLD criteria, with APASL and EASL definitions applied secondarily. Among 79 patients (20 HBsAg-positive, 59 resolved HBV), none received antiviral prophylaxis. Median follow-up was 42 weeks (IQR, 19-65). HBVr occurred in 7 (8.9%; 95% CI, 4.4%-17.2%): 5 HBsAg-positive (25.0%; 95% CI, 11.2%-46.9%), and 2 with resolved HBV (3.4%; 95% CI, 0.9%-11.5%). APASL and EASL definitions yielded 30.0% and 35.0% in HBsAg-positive patients, with no additional events in resolved HBV. No HBVr-associated hepatitis flare meeting the study definition was observed, although transient flares between assessments could not be excluded and deterioration in one fatal case was attributed clinically to sepsis. Median HBVr detection time was 19 weeks (IQR, 14-30). Week-48 Kaplan-Meier HBVr incidence was 37.5% (95% CI, 17.0%-69.5%) in HBsAg-positive and 5.6% (95% CI, 1.4%-21.2%) in resolved HBV (log-rank p < 0.001); Aalen-Johansen estimates were 28.3% (95% CI, 9.5%-50.9%) and 4.3% (95% CI, 0.8%-13.2%), respectively. In exploratory Firth-corrected regression, HBsAg positivity was associated with HBVr (HR, 6.95; 95% CI, 1.60-40.19), while osimertinib exposure was not. HBVr was common among HBsAg-positive patients and less common but not negligible among those with resolved HBV receiving TKIs.

records.title: Ataxia Telangiectasia and Rad3-Related Kinase as a Drug Target and Its Inhibitors: Synthetic Aspects, Current Research and Potential Perspectives.
records.abstract: ATR kinase is a key regulator of the DNA damage response and replication stress, with two decades of homology model-based drug design now validated by cryo-EM structures of full-length human ATR-ATRIP. This review treats ATR drug discovery as both a synthetic chemistry and structural challenge, outlining reagent-level pathways from initial hits to drug substances for clinical candidates. It includes multi-kilogram biocatalytic and photoredox-flow routes for ceralasertib, analysing the strategic logic behind each scheme, a focus absent in recent SAR-based reviews. We analyse the binding modes observed in the recent ~3 Å ATR-ATRIP inhibitor co-structures and compare them with previous PI3K homology model predictions. Additionally, we expand the discussion on selectivity to include not only the (R)-3-methylmorpholine pocket but also the aminopyrazine and macrocyclic chemotypes. The section on PROTACs is reoriented around degrading the ATR-CHK1-ATM pathway, highlighting a CHK1 degrader and ATM degrader that synergise with ATR inhibition. Finally, ATR's roles beyond oncology are considered, including neurodevelopment, mitochondrial homoeostasis, gametogenesis, and in parasitic DDR. Overall, in the current scenario, ATR inhibitors are positioned as promising candidates for repurposing in biomarker-guided therapies, balancing potency, selectivity, toxicity and resistance.
records.authors: Bhagwat P, Kirubakaran S.

records.title: Resveratrol Modulates Bone Metabolism Through SIRT1-Mediated NF-κB Inhibition: Molecular Mechanisms and Therapeutic Implications.
records.abstract: Osteoporosis and associated skeletal pathologies impose a staggering global health burden, disproportionately impacting elderly populations and postmenopausal women. At the root of excessive bone resorption and stalled osteogenesis lie persistent oxidative stress and chronic inflammation. Enter resveratrol, a naturally occurring polyphenol derived from red wine and grapes, which has surfaced as a compelling therapeutic candidate for skeletal preservation owing to its robust antioxidant and anti-inflammatory capacities. Herein, we evaluate the molecular pathways through which resveratrol governs bone metabolism, focusing sharply on SIRT1-driven suppression of NF-κB signaling. Integrating findings across cell cultures, animal models, and clinical trials yields a unified perspective on these osteoprotective mechanisms. Dual benefits define resveratrol's impact on skeletal architecture: it stimulates osteoblast differentiation and mineralization while suppressing osteoclastogenesis and bone resorption. Primarily, these outcomes stem from the activation of SIRT1, a NAD + -dependent deacetylase acting as a negative regulator of NF-κB transcription. Through SIRT1-mediated deacetylation of the NF-κB p65 subunit, the transcription of pro-inflammatory cytokines including IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-6 diminishes, subsequently dampening RANKL-driven osteoclastogenesis. Simultaneously, through the SIRT1-dependent engagement of Nrf2/ARE pathways, antioxidant defenses are bolstered, sparing bone cells from oxidative stress-induced apoptosis. Substantial preclinical promise notwithstanding, hurdles persist regarding both systemic bioavailability and the standardization of ideal dosing protocols for bone preservation. This review provides a mechanistic framework to evaluate resveratrol as a viable nutraceutical modality for the prevention and management of osteoporosis.

records.title: Interfacial Electronic Coupling and Surface Reconstruction in Co(OH)<sub>2</sub>@NiFe-btz for Durable Alkaline Oxygen Evolution.
records.abstract: Coupling metal hydroxides with coordination frameworks offers a route to active and durable oxygen evolution reaction (OER) electrodes. A binder-free Co(OH)2@NiFe-btz heterostructure, where btz is 1,4-bis(4H-1,2,4-triazol-4-yl)benzene, is constructed on nickel foam through solvothermal growth followed by electrodeposition. Microscopy reveals close contact between Co(OH)2 nanosheets and the framework. Ultraviolet and x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy indicate interfacial charge redistribution consistent with the work-function difference, while electron paramagnetic resonance detects paramagnetic states. In 1.0 M KOH, the electrode delivers 10 mA cm-2 at an overpotential of 219 mV, exhibits a Tafel slope of 57.1 mV dec-1, and operates at 100 mA cm-2 for 1000 h. Operando Raman spectroscopy reveals potential-dependent formation of a cobalt/nickel oxyhydroxide-like surface phase. Isotope-labeling mass spectrometry and infrared spectroscopy of the target electrode, considered alongside electrochemical probes, are consistent with possible lattice-oxygen participation, without establishing its fraction of the oxygen-evolution flux. Density functional theory calculations on idealized precursor structures show that interfacial coupling and an imposed oxygen vacancy modify metal d and O 2p states and reduce the largest uphill free-energy step in a candidate lattice-oxygen pathway. Together, these results connect framework-hydroxide coupling with enhanced electrode performance and the evolution of its catalytic surface.

records.title: UHPLC-DAD-HRMS<sup>2</sup> Characterization of Novel Dihydrochalcone Conjugates From the Antiviral Mansoa hirsuta Extracts: Diagnostic Fragmentation Pathways and Dereplication of Oligomeric Polyphenols.
records.abstract: High-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) coupled with ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography (UHPLC) enables rapid characterization of complex polyphenolic constituents in medicinal plants. Mansoa hirsuta (Bignoniaceae), a neotropical liana traditionally used to treat infectious diseases, remains poorly characterized chemically. This study reports the comprehensive UHPLC-DAD-HRMS/MS profiling of ethanolic extracts from leaves, stems, and fruits, leading to the identification of 57 phenolic compounds, including 40 previously unreported flavonoid conjugates. Accurate mass measurements and diagnostic MS/MS fragmentation patterns enabled the structural characterization of five classes of dihydrochalcone-derived metabolites: dihydrochalcone-tyramine, -flavanone (mansoin-type), -flavan-3-ol, and -flavonol conjugates. Characteristic fragment ions, particularly those corresponding to the dihydrochalcone core and tyramine moiety, supported the annotation of novel oligomeric flavonoids. Organ-specific metabolite distribution revealed leaves enriched in Mansoin A-type heterotrimers, stems containing phenylethanoid glycosides and cinnamoyl-mangiferins, and fruits predominated by simpler dihydrochalcone-tyramine conjugates. All extracts exhibited low cytotoxicity (CC50 > 400 μg mL-1) and selective antiviral activity against Zika (ZIKV), chikungunya (CHIKV), Mayaro (MAYV), and dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV-2). The stem extract showed the highest selectivity against ZIKV (SI > 25.5), whereas the fruit extract displayed the greatest potency against DENV-2 (EC50 = 25.4 ± 1.2 μg mL-1; SI > 19.7). These findings expand the phytochemical knowledge of M. hirsuta, demonstrate the utility of HRMS-based metabolite profiling for dereplication of complex flavonoids, and provide diagnostic MS/MS fragmentation patterns applicable to the characterization of related oligomeric flavonoids in other plant species.
records.authors: Reis ACC, de Mello Silva B, de Brito Magalhães CL, Kroon EG, da Costa Gontijo D, Kohlhoff M, Brandão GC.

records.title: From fast-follower to emerging innovator: a critical review of 68 ISO-approved pesticides developed in China (2002-2025), resistance-management potential and translational barriers.
records.abstract: BackgroundChina has emerged as a major source of innovative crop-protection chemistry, yet the international applicability of its domestically developed agrochemical pipeline has not been critically evaluated. We systematically identified and analyzed 68 China-developed insecticides, acaricides, nematicides, fungicides and herbicides that received ISO common names between 2002 and 2025, and assessed their structural evolution, resistance-management potential and translational progress.ResultsThe portfolio comprises 18 insecticides, 6 acaricides, 3 nematicides, 20 fungicides and 21 herbicides, showing a shift from early pyrethroid and strobilurin modifications to heterocyclic scaffolds such as meta-diamides, pyrazolecarboxamides and benzoylpyrazoles. On the basis of publicly available data, no compound has a confirmed first-in-class binding site. As of 30 April 2026, none had achieved Codex maximum residue limit (MRL) establishment, EU active-substance approval, or Japan registration; only 11 (16.2%) had been listed/classified by Resistance Action Committee (RAC). The China Translational Attainment Index (TAI) (0.040) was therefore driven solely by RAC listing, versus 0.444 for the non-China comparator (P ConclusionThese 68 compounds are a valuable resource for global resistance management, but their international use is constrained by translational deficits. Absence of Codex MRLs, limited baseline-sensitivity data, and incomplete resistance and environmental fate data are core barriers to registration and stewardship. Prioritized data generation is needed to bridge this gap and support international registration and stewardship. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

records.title: Brain Transcriptomic Changes Associated With the Socially Regulated Behavioural Specialisation of Ant Queens.
records.abstract: Insect societies are characterised by a reproductive division of labour between queens that monopolise egg production and workers that perform all non-reproductive tasks. The queen specialisation in egg laying is typically considered to be constitutive and independent of environmental conditions, but this common assumption was recently challenged by the finding that the presence of workers both induces and maintains the queen specialisation in several species of ants. However, the molecular changes that translate worker presence into queen behavioural specialisation remain unknown. To investigate the transcriptomic basis of the socially regulated specialisation of ant queens, we produced 93 individual brain transcriptomes from queens of the black garden ant Lasius niger that were experimentally maintained in different social environments. Our transcriptomic analyses revealed that 123 genes were differentially expressed between the brains of queens maintained with and without workers. These genes were enriched for processes related to brain energy metabolism and neuronal plasticity and signalling. By investigating the response of selected genes of interest to further manipulations of the social environment, we identified four candidate genes that fully mirrored the queen behavioural changes. Specifically, their expression changes in response to worker presence were reversible and they did not respond to mere cues of the worker presence. These candidate genes included the transcription factor Krüppel-homologue 1 and other genes in the juvenile hormone and insulin signalling pathways, both known to regulate multiple aspects of division of labour in social insects. By producing a robust, well-replicated and well-controlled investigation of the transcriptomic basis of the behavioural specialisation of ant queens, this study provides a better understanding of the emergence and maintenance of reproductive division of labour in insect societies.
records.authors: Le Lay HE, Bolder MF, Colgan TJ, Libbrecht R.

records.title: Targeting Ninjurin-1-Mediated Microglial Pyroptosis Attenuates Neuroinflammation and Neuronal Injury Following Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
records.abstract: ObjectiveThis study aims to delineate the pathophysiological contribution of Ninjurin-1 (Ninj1) to secondary neural injury following intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), specifically elucidating its function in microglial pyroptosis and its upstream transcriptional governance by nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB).MethodsCandidate targets were initially identified via in silico transcriptomic profiling. We subsequently employed a collagenase-induced murine ICH paradigm alongside hemin-challenged microglia. Mechanistic pathways were interrogated utilizing targeted genetic silencing (in vivo siRNA and in vitro shRNA) and pharmacological blockade. Disease phenotypes-encompassing pyroptotic execution, neuroinflammation, and collateral neuronal death-were quantified via immunoblotting, molecular assays, and histopathology. The upstream regulatory architecture was validated through ChIP-qPCR, EMSA, and dual-luciferase reporter assays.ResultsBioinformatic screening highlighted Ninj1 as a prominently upregulated candidate transcript post-ICH, a finding corroborated by robust induction in both in vivo and in vitro hemorrhagic models. Through prophylactic in vivo target validation, Ninj1 depletion restricted perihematomal edema and preserved sensorimotor function. Mechanistically, suppressing Ninj1 abrogated the microglial pyroptotic cascade and mitigated collateral neurotoxicity. Furthermore, NF-κB was shown to transcriptionally activate NLRP3 and Ninj1, although direct promoter enrichment in the ChIP-qPCR assay was statistically significant only for the Nlrp3 locus.ConclusionsNinj1 functions as a terminal executioner of microglial pyroptosis and a critical amplifier of post-ICH neuroinflammation. Governed by a coordinated NF-κB-dependent transcriptional program alongside NLRP3, this signaling axis exacerbates secondary brain injury, positioning Ninj1 as a viable molecular candidate for neuroprotective target validation.
records.authors: Peng L, Peng A, Zhu H, Sun T, Liu P, Qi T.

records.title: Integrated clinical and transcriptomic analysis reveals miRNA-mediated mechanisms linking hearing loss to cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease.
records.abstract: BackgroundHearing loss (HL) is a potent, modifiable risk factor for Alzheimer's disease (AD), but the underlying molecular mechanisms remain elusive. microRNAs (miRNAs) are potential key mediators given their roles in both neurodegeneration and auditory function.ObjectiveTo investigate whether peripheral blood miRNA profiles differ between AD patients with and without HL, and whether hsa-miR-6875-5p serves as a candidate molecular link.MethodsIn a case-control study of 41 AD patients (AD-HL n = 24, AD-non-HL n = 17), we performed neuropsychological assessments, plasma miRNA sequencing, target gene prediction, and external validation using public transcriptomic datasets.ResultsAD-HL patients showed significantly worse Montreal Cognitive Assessment and Auditory Verbal Learning Test delayed recall scores (p < 0.05). We identified 9 differentially expressed miRNAs, with hsa-miR-6875-5p being the most upregulated (3.29-fold, p = 0.041). Its predicted targets were enriched in synaptic plasticity-related pathways. External validation in AD brain datasets supported consistent upregulation of hsa-miR-6875-5p and downregulation of SYN1/PSD95. Validation in mouse cochlear datasets showed concordant expression trends for homologous miRNA and target genes. The absence of healthy control groups precludes determination of whether this miRNA signature is specific to AD-HL or a general feature of HL or AD.ConclusionsThis preliminary study identifies hsa-miR-6875-5p as a potential circulating biomarker linking HL to cognitive decline in AD. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger cohorts, including healthy controls, and functional experiments.
records.authors: Wang X, Zhang B, Ma H, Shan A, Lian Q, Han X, Xu C, Yao Q, Wen B, Luan H, Li S, Cui T, Lv S, Sun Q, Guo J, Chen R, Wei C.

records.title: [Construction and internal validation of a prognostic prediction model for R0 resection after conversion therapy in colorectal cancer liver metastases based on clinicopathological features combined with ctDNA].
records.abstract: Objective: To construct and validate an overall survival (OS) prediction model for patients with colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRLM) undergoing R0 resection after conversion therapy. Methods: A total of 364 patients with CRLM who were evaluated by a multidisciplinary team as initially unresectable and underwent R0 resection of both the primary tumor and liver metastases after conversion therapy between January 2018 and December 2023 were retrospectively included with 226 male, 138 female and a median age [M(Q1, Q3)] of 58.0(51.0,66.0) years and randomly divided by computer software at a 7∶3 ratio into a training set (n=255) and a validation set (n=109). Follow-up was conducted through February 2026, with OS as the primary endpoint. For model 1, all modelable baseline variables were included in the candidate pool; variable selection was performed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-Cox regression, and an OS prediction model was constructed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and presented as a nomogram. Model 2 additionally included the adjuvant chemotherapy regimen variable on the basis of model 1 for sensitivity analysis. Model performance was evaluated using the concordance index (C-index), area under the time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results: The median follow-up was 36.2 months, and 198 deaths (54.4%) occurred. After LASSO selection from the full candidate pool, model 1 included N stage, number of liver metastases, maximum liver metastasis diameter, preoperative carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9) level, KRAS mutation status, BRAF V600E mutation status, postoperative 1-month circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) status, body mass index (BMI), number of conversion therapy cycles, and intraoperative blood loss. Multivariable Cox regression analysis showed that negative postoperative 1-month ctDNA (HR=0.134, 95%CI: 0.088-0.202, PBRAF V600E wild type (HR=0.200, 95%CI: 0.106-0.379, PHR=2.564, 95%CI: 1.518-4.332, PHR=1.593, 95%CI: 1.082-2.345, P=0.018) were factors associated with OS after R0 resection following conversion therapy in CRLM. The C-index values of model 1 were 0.759 and 0.773 in the training and validation sets, respectively; the 1-, 3-, and 5-year AUC were 0.808, 0.851, and 0.862 in the training set and 0.850, 0.835, and 0.832 in the validation set, respectively. records.title: Ultrasound as a Multifunctional Physical Platform for Whole-Grape Valorization: From Field Management to Green Extraction, Quality Modulation, and Intelligent Scale-Up.
records.abstract: The grape and wine industry faces prolonged barrel aging, microbial spoilage, protein haze, chemical additives, and inefficient by-product valorization. These challenges motivate nonthermal technologies that reduce chemical inputs. Ultrasound operates in two mechanistically distinct regimes: sensing, based on acoustic propagation, reflection, and echo detection, and processing, driven mainly by acoustic cavitation and its physical and chemical effects, including microjets, shock waves, localized hotspots, and reactive radicals. These complementary modes provide a versatile physical platform. This review covers ultrasound across the grape-wine continuum: acoustic imaging for precision viticulture; postharvest preservation with green activated water; green extraction enhanced by natural deep eutectic solvents; grape protein modification for ingredient assembly; modulation of wine color, aroma, and colloidal stability; selected aging-associated reactions involving 1-hydroxyethyl radicals; selective microbial inactivation and fermentation modulation; and scale-up based on energy characterization, continuous-flow reactors, and data-driven modeling. Current evidence indicates that ultrasound is evolving from an empirically optimized unit operation toward a mechanistically informed and quantitatively characterized physical-field platform. Reported effects include accelerated aging-related transformations, modified protein structure and stability, and selective microbial responses, although they depend on treatment conditions and matrix properties. Absorbed energy density supports quantitative comparison of treatments, but reliable scale-up also requires acoustic-field distribution, residence time, temperature, and reactor geometry. Future progress will require standardized energy reporting, pilot- and continuous-flow validation, physics-informed data-driven modeling, and integration of process analytical technologies with closed-loop control. These advances would support more reproducible, scalable, and sustainable ultrasound processing in the grape and wine sector.
