records.title: HOXC9 promotes gastric cancer cell proliferation, invasion, and migration via regulating HIF-1 pathway.
records.abstract: BackgroundGastric cancer (GC) remains a major malignancy associated with rapid progression and poor clinical outcomes. Elucidating the molecular events responsible for GC advancement, and the identification of key regulatory targets, is of critical importance for improving patient prognosis.MethodsIntegrated bioinformatics analyses of public datasets identified HOXC9 as a candidate gene. Its expression was validated using independent database analyses, and mRNA/protein expression assessment. Functional assays following HOXC9 overexpression or knockdown were performed to evaluate malignant phenotypes and metabolic changes in GC cells. We employed RNA-seq to profile transcriptomic alterations upon HOXC9 modulation, and their functional relevance was further validated.ResultsDatabase analyses identified HOXC9 as an unfavorable prognostic factor in GC, and its increased expression was subsequently verified in HGC-27 and MKN-45. Functional assays demonstrated that overexpression of HOXC9 markedly enhanced the proliferative, invasive, and migratory capacities, whereas silencing of HOXC9 produced the opposite effects. Transcriptomic profiling suggested that HOXC9 regulates the HIF-1 pathway, and an inverse association between HOXC9 and HIF1A was observed. Mechanistically, overexpression of HOXC9 accelerated malignant characteristics via modulation of the HIF-1 pathway, accompanied by increased ATP and lactate production and reduced glucose levels. In contrast, knockdown of HOXC9 exerted opposing effects.ConclusionsHOXC9 drives GC progression through activating the HIF-1 pathway, highlighting a novel regulatory axis with potential implications for GC intervention.

records.title: TaMYB39 positively regulates salt tolerance in wheat seedlings.
records.abstract: Salt stress severely restricts wheat growth and productivity, yet the regulatory mechanisms governing the abundance and activity of stress-responsive transcription factors remain incompletely understood. In this study, we characterized the wheat MYB transcription factor TaMYB39 and investigated its role in salt tolerance and protein stability. TaMYB39 expression was rapidly induced by NaCl treatment, and the protein was predominantly localized in the nucleus. Transgenic wheat lines overexpressing TaMYB39 exhibited improved growth and greater dry weight under salt stress, whereas RNAi lines showed increased sensitivity. TaMYB39 overexpression was associated with reduced Na⁺ accumulation, enhanced K⁺ retention, a lower Na⁺/K⁺ ratio, increased proline accumulation, and reduced membrane damage. The overexpression lines also accumulated less H2O2 and O2- and exhibited higher SOD, POD, and CAT activities, consistent with enhanced antioxidant capacity. Yeast two-hybrid screening identified the bZIP transcription factor TabZIP27 as a TaMYB39-interacting protein, and this interaction was confirmed by pairwise Y2H, BiFC, GST pull-down, and Co-IP assays. Salt treatment enhanced the TaMYB39-TabZIP27 interaction. Cell-free degradation and CHX chase assays further showed that TabZIP27 delayed TaMYB39 degradation, whereas MG132 treatment attenuated the decline in TaMYB39 abundance, supporting the involvement of the 26S proteasome pathway in TaMYB39 turnover. Collectively, these findings identify TaMYB39 as a positive regulator of salt tolerance in wheat and suggest that its protein stability is modulated through interaction with TabZIP27 under salt stress.

records.title: Trichoderma reesei-driven aerobic fermentation of bamboo leaf-stem residues: lignocellulose deconstruction, fungal community succession, and feed properties improvement.
records.abstract: Leaf-stem residues of Dendrocalamus brandisii are abundant lignocellulosic byproducts, but their compact cell-wall matrix limits direct conversion and feed use. This study developed an aerobic solid-state bioconversion process with Trichoderma reesei and linked process control, enzyme secretion, fungal community assembly, and product chemistry. Sterilization markedly enhanced fungal establishment and fiber degradation. Under selected conditions (4% ammonium sulfate, a 1:4 solid-to-liquid ratio, 15% inoculum, and 9 days), cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin degradation reached 24.5, 21.9, and 5.9%, respectively. Rising cellulase and xylanase activities accompanied hyphal penetration and matrix disruption. Soluble sugars accumulated while glucose-equivalent recovery declined, indicating greater assimilation or respiration of cellulose-derived carbon. Internal transcribed spacer profiling indicated predominantly deterministic assembly: sterilized fermentation remained Trichoderma-dominated, whereas unsterilized communities underwent competitive succession and unique amplicon sequence variants declined from 143 to 63. Fermentation decreased neutral detergent fiber (NDF) and acid detergent fiber (ADF) from 65.04 and 39.53% to 53.32 and 28.18%, increased total antioxidant capacity by 39.9%, and raised in vitro dry-matter and crude-protein digestibility from 22.3 and 55.0% to 40.7 and 70.8%, respectively. These findings link fungal establishment and community succession to cell-wall deconstruction and support upgrading bamboo residues into a more accessible feed resource.

records.title: SALL4 drives gastric cancer progression through PI3K/Akt-mediated regulation of glycolysis, EMT, stemness, and adhesion remodeling.
records.abstract: SALL4 has emerged as an oncogenic driver in multiple malignancies; however, its role in gastric cancer (GC) is insufficiently defined. This paper was conceived to elucidate the functional significance as well as to uncover the downstream mechanisms of SALL4 in GC progression. SALL4 expression in GC tissues and its prognostic significance were processed via bioinformatics datasets, RT-qPCR, western blot, and IHC staining. Functional assays, including CCK-8, colony formation, migration, invasion, adhesion, and spheroid formation, were performed in GC cell lines following SALL4 knockdown or overexpression. Glycolytic activity was evaluated by ECAR, OCR, glucose uptake, and lactate production. The involvement of the PI3K/Akt pathway and its downstream effectors, including β-catenin, FAK-YAP and HIF-1α was examined using pathway inhibitors and rescue experiments. HIF-1 transcriptional activity and downstream target gene expression were further assessed using an HRE-driven dual-luciferase reporter assay and RT-qPCR, respectively. Elevated SALL4 expression was observed in GC samples and was positively associated with advanced TNM classification, nodal metastasis, and poor clinical outcomes. Silencing of SALL4 suppressed GC cell growth, motility, invasiveness, EMT progression, stemness maintenance, adhesive capacity, cytoskeletal dynamics, and glycolysis, while overexpression produced the opposite effects. Mechanistically, SALL4 activated the PI3K/Akt pathway, resulting in β-catenin upregulation that promoted EMT and stemness, FAK-YAP activation that enhanced adhesion and cytoskeleton, and HIF-1α induction that facilitated glycolytic reprogramming. Pathway inhibition and rescue experiments supported the involvement of PI3K/Akt and its downstream effectors in selected SALL4-associated phenotypes. Our findings support a potential role for SALL4 in regulating GC cell phenotypic plasticity and metabolic reprogramming through the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway. The SALL4/PI3K/Akt axis represents a candidate molecular pathway warranting further investigation, while its therapeutic applicability remains to be established through dedicated preclinical intervention studies and validation in appropriate in vivo and patient-derived models.

records.title: Ubiquitination of retinoic acid receptor alpha promotes severe acute pancreatitis-associated acute lung injury by releasing hexokinase 3 transcriptional repression.
records.abstract: Lung macrophages constitute the first line of defense against environmental attack and participate in the pathogenesis of acute lung injury (ALI). In this study, we sought to elucidate the impact of HK3 on the regulation of macrophage phenotype in severe acute pancreatitis (SAP)-associated acute lung injury (PALI). HK3 expression was enhanced in lung macrophages of mice with SAP, and overexpression of HK3 in macrophages using adeno-associated viral vectors exacerbated PALI progression and increased macrophage M1 polarization in lung tissues. Overexpression of HK3 enhanced the glycolytic activity of macrophages, thereby polarizing macrophages toward the M1 phenotype. Retinoic acid receptor alpha (RARA) repressed HK3 transcription by binding to the promoter of HK3. Knockdown of HK3 inhibited the macrophage glycolysis induced by RARA knockdown and alleviated PALI development. NEDD4L mediated ubiquitination and degradation of RARA, and NEDD4L overexpression promoted macrophage glycolysis-induced increase in M1 polarization and inhibited M2 polarization. In peripheral blood CD14+ monocytes, NEDD4L and HK3 mRNA expression correlated positively with APACHE II scores and negatively with PaO₂/FiO₂, whereas RARA mRNA expression showed the opposite associations. In conclusion, NEDD4L-mediated degradation of RARA hinders its transcriptional repression of HK3 to activate macrophage glycolysis and M1 polarization in PALI development.

records.title: Mapping the evolution of spatially fractionated radiation therapy: A comprehensive bibliometric analysis of research trends and future directions.
records.abstract: PurposeSpatially fractionated radiation therapy (SFRT) has emerged as a research hotspot in radiation oncology, characterized by its unique dose distribution pattern that effectively spares normal tissues while treating tumors. Compared to conventional radiotherapy, SFRT demonstrates particular advantages in bulky and radioresistant tumors. This study aims to analyze the developmental trends of SFRT through bibliometric analysis and identify future research directions.Methods865 SFRT-related publications were retrieved and screened systematically from the Web of Science Core Collection (WOSCC) and Scopus databases. Extracted metadata including titles, authors, publication years, abstracts, affiliations, cited references, keywords, citation counts, and country/region information were analyzed using VOSviewer and Bibliometrix.ResultsOur analysis reveals that SFRT's evolution has been heavily driven by collaborations across large-scale multidisciplinary facilities. While pioneering institutions in Europe and North America historically drove the field, the Asia-Pacific region demonstrates rapidly increasing engagement. Prezado emerged as the most prolific author. Keyword clustering maps the converging landscape of primary modalities into three main domains: microbeam (MRT), minibeam (MBRT), and GRID/lattice radiotherapy (LRT). While MRT remains the most extensively studied yet facility-dependent technique, LRT and MBRT have received increasing attention in recent years due to their greater clinical feasibility.ConclusionsThe independent historical origins of SFRT modalities are now converging into a unified domain. Advancing accessible dosimetry systems, elucidating underlying biological mechanisms, standardizing clinical protocols, and integrating with emerging FLASH radiotherapy are critical priorities. Overcoming these challenges will enable SFRT to fulfill its potential as a highly valuable complementary therapeutic option in comprehensive cancer care.

records.title: Cross-modal transfer enables zero-shot prediction of drug responses across cell types
records.abstract: Genetic perturbation responses capture the functional consequences of gene-level interventions, providing functional information for drug-response prediction beyond baseline gene expression. Within the same cellular context, genetic and chemical perturbations engage shared regulatory networks, providing a biological basis for transferring response information between perturbation modalities. Here we introduce  GRAFT , a framework that combines genetic-to-chemical transfer with cross-context prediction to infer drug-induced transcriptional responses without drug measurements in the target context. Across benchmarked LINCS and external contexts, GRAFT improved response correlation, directional agreement and magnitude reconstruction over competing methods, particularly for drugs with context-dependent responses.  GRAFT-Adapt further refines predictions of unmeasured responses using a small number of drug measurements from the target context.  GRAFT-Atlas spans 13 cellular contexts and 7,856 drug catalog entries, comprising 102,128 predictions for drug–context combinations. The atlas captured recognizable pharmacological neighborhoods, shared functional programs, context-dependent transcriptional changes and structural–functional associations supported by molecular docking. Across ten iPSC lines from distinct donors, GRAFT identified candidate inter-donor differences, with functional support for selected candidates from measured genetic perturbation responses. Together, GRAFT enables perturbation-informed prediction and comparison of drug responses across cellular contexts.

records.title: Phenotypic screening in Parkinson’s iPSC-dopamine neurons identifies the FASN-SREBP1 axis as a potential therapeutic target
records.abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) remains highly challenging to model in vitro, particularly when seeking robust functional phenotypes for target discovery. Patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell dopaminergic neurons (iPSC-DANs) offer a promising platform to address this challenge. Because calcium dyshomeostasis is well-described in PD pathophysiology, it offers a platform for phenotypic screening. We have previously shown that  GBA-N370S iPSC-DANs display impaired intracellular calcium release. Here, we used this disease-relevant phenotype to undertake a 4,108-compound phenotypic screen in  GBA-N370S (  GBA-NS ) iPSC-DANs. This screen identified fatty acid synthase (FASN) as the most enriched protein target. The ability of compounds to rescue calcium release correlated with biochemical potency against FASN across multiple chemical series. We confirmed that FASN knockdown increased intracellular calcium release, supporting an on-target effect. Untargeted lipidomics demonstrated broad remodelling of the neuronal lipidome after FASN inhibition, confirming target engagement. FASN inhibition also increased active β-glucocerebrosidase (GCase), reduced extracellular α-synuclein release and ER stress, and altered RASGRF1 expression. Mechanistically, FASN inhibition activated sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1 (SREBP1), and SREBP1 overexpression alone was sufficient to increase intracellular calcium release, identifying a FASN-SREBP1-calcium homeostasis axis in human neurons. Finally, the FASN inhibitor BI 99179 achieved brain exposure and reduced brain fatty acid levels while inducing an SRE-associated transcriptional response in a Parkinson’s mouse model, providing evidence of in vivo target engagement. These findings establish patient iPSC-neuron functional screening as a tractable discovery platform to identify targets which can be taken in vivo and nominate the FASN-SREBP1 axis as a candidate therapeutic pathway in PD.  One Sentence Summary  We applied a disease-relevant phenotypic screen in patient neurons to uncover a lipid-calcium regulatory axis that rescues multiple pathogenic pathways in Parkinson’s.

records.title: FateDriver: Weakly supervised dual-view graph learning for transition-specific prioritization of candidate regulators in cellular reprogramming
records.abstract: SUMMARY  Cellular reprogramming supports regenerative medicine, yet the endogenous regulators of a specified source-to-target transition remain incompletely defined. Existing computational methods rank candidate regulators from network topology, trajectory dynamics, or cell-state labels, leaving unused the factors experimentally delivered to induce the transition. We present Fat-eDriver, a weakly supervised dual-view graph neural network that jointly represents cells and genes from single-cell transcriptomes, treats the delivered factors as sparse gene-level labels, and ranks the remaining genes for a specified transition under a positive–unlabeled formulation. Across two OSKM datasets and one GMT dataset, FateDriver ranked first or second among six methods in recovering externally curated reference genes, exceeded a supervision-matched non-graph model despite weaker co-expression with the delivered factors, and achieved the highest recovery of protein targets of pluripotency-inducing chemical cocktails in both OSKM datasets. Holding either the source or the endpoint fixed yielded distinct candidate programs, including a  DDX58 –interferon axis associated with cells lacking endogenous pluripotency markers. Applying the same framework to candidate source–target pairs prioritized distinct candidate origins for two  in vivo partially reprogrammed intestinal populations. FateDriver converts sparse experimental knowledge into transition-specific hypotheses for regulator prioritization from single-cell trajectories.

records.title: miR-195-3p alleviates atherosclerosis by regulating VSMC functions through JNK2/NF-κB pathway
records.abstract: Abstract  Background and Aim:  Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammatory vascular disease and the primary pathological driver of life-threatening cardiovascular diseases. Vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) contribute critically to vascular remodeling; their aberrant proliferation, migration, phenotypic switching and inflammatory activation promote atherosclerotic lesion development. miR-195-3p is a potential vasculo-protective microRNA, yet its exact functions and downstream mechanisms in VSMC-related atherosclerosis remain poorly defined. This study investigated the biological role of miR-195-3p in VSMCs and its molecular regulatory axis. Methods and Results  miR-195-3p expression was measured in plasma from patients with coronary artery disease, atherosclerotic aortas from high-fat diet-fed ApoE⁻/⁻ mice, and pathologically stimulated VSMCs. miR-195-3p was significantly downregulated under atherosclerotic conditions. Gain- and loss-of-function assays showed that miR-195-3p overexpression suppressed VSMC proliferation, migration and inflammation while preserving the contractile phenotype, whereas miR-195-3p inhibition induced pathological VSMC dysfunction. Transcriptomic, bioinformatic and dual-luciferase assays identified JNK2 as a direct target of miR-195-3p. Rescue experiments confirmed JNK2 mediates miR-195-3p’s protective effects, and JNK2 aggravates VSMC dysfunction partly through activating the NF-κB inflammatory cascade. In ApoE⁻/⁻ mice, AAV-mediated miR-195-3p overexpression reduced plaque burden, repressed JNK2/NF-κB signaling, restored VSMC homeostasis and mitigated vascular inflammation. Conclusions  miR-195-3p maintains VSMC homeostasis and alleviates atherosclerosis by directly targeting JNK2 and inhibiting the NF-κB cascade. The miR-195-3p/JNK2/NF-κB axis enriches our understanding of atherosclerosis pathogenesis and offers candidate molecular targets for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease therapy.

records.title: Senescence-associated KRAS upregulation in peripheral T cells links to premature coronary artery disease
records.abstract: Abstract    Aims  Premature coronary artery disease (PCAD) lacks specific molecular drivers, and the role of immunosenescence is unclear. We investigated whether aging-related gene dysregulation in T cells contributes to PCAD. Methods  We combined bulk transcriptomics of PBMCs from 12 PCAD patients and 21 controls, single-cell RNA sequencing of PBMCs and human atherosclerotic plaques, weighted gene co‑expression network analysis, gene perturbation network analysis, and molecular docking. Results  KRAS was identified as a hub gene intersecting PCAD-associated genes and aging-related genes. Single-cell analysis showed KRAS upregulation predominantly in effector CD8  +  T cells, which exhibited the highest senescence scores that were further elevated in disease. Network perturbation of KRAS strongly impacted the cell killing pathway. KRAS-high effector CD8  +  T cells were detected in coronary and carotid plaques, displaying enhanced cytotoxicity, exhaustion, and senescence features. Additionally, a candidate small molecule was computationally predicted to bind inactive KRAS. Conclusions  Elevated KRAS expression in senescent, cytotoxic CD8  +  T cells is associated with PCAD, bridging immunosenescence and premature atherosclerosis. This finding provides a novel biomarker candidate and potential therapeutic entry point, awaiting further functional validation.
records.authors: Sun Z, Yang Z, Wang X, Zhang M, Gao R, Yang M, Li Y, Liu Q, Hou J.

records.title: The Construction and Validation of KCP-Based Chemoresistance Predictive Model for Cervical Cancer
records.abstract: Abstract  Objective:  This study aimed to determine the diagnostic threshold of serum KCP for predicting chemoresistance in cervical cancer and to establish and externally validate a relevant prediction model. Additionally, computational drug virtual screening was performed to identify candidate compounds that may reverse KCP-mediated chemoresistance. Methods: This ambispective cohort study enrolled patients with FIGO 2018 stage IB3–IVA cervical cancer who received paclitaxel–platinum neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The retrospective cohort (January 2013–January 2023; n = 158) served as the training set, and the prospective cohort (January 2023–November 2025; n = 130) served as the external validation set. Serum KCP levels were measured by ELISA. Predictive performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, Kaplan–Meier survival analysis, Cox proportional hazards regression, and nomogram construction with decision curve analysis (DCA). Computational drug screening was performed using DrugReflector based on transcriptomic signatures of chemoresistant versus chemosensitive cervical cancer states from the TISCH single-cell database. Results: A total of 288 patients were enrolled (185 chemosensitive, 103 chemoresistant). The optimal diagnostic threshold of serum KCP for predicting chemoresistance was 24.59 ng/L (sensitivity 88.9%, specificity 77.8%, AUC = 0.707) in the training cohort. Independent risk factors for recurrence after neoadjuvant chemotherapy included serum KCP levels, SCCA, tumor shrinkage, depth of stromal infiltration, lymph node metastasis, and degree of tumor differentiation. A predictive nomogram integrating these variables achieved an AUC of 0.762 in the training cohort but showed substantially reduced performance in the validation cohort (AUC = 0.535, 95% CI: 0.414–0.656), indicating limited external validity. Drug virtual screening identified 9,597 candidate compounds, with the top-ranked drugs exhibiting high logit scores and predicted probabilities, providing a foundation for future experimental validation. Conclusion: KCP was identified as a promising serum biomarker for paclitaxel resistance in cervical cancer with an optimal cutoff of 24.59 ng/L. However, the KCP-integrated nomogram demonstrated insufficient external validity, highlighting the necessity of prospective validation and consideration of population heterogeneity in predictive model development. Computational drug screening identified candidate compounds that may inform future therapeutic strategies for KCP-mediated chemoresistance.
records.authors: Ji C, Wang Y, Li Y, Xia M, Li C, Wu Y, He Y.

records.title: Association of Unsaturated Fatty Acid–Related Immunometabolic Features with Differential Responses to Erenumab in Patients with Migraine: An Exploratory Multi-Omics Study
records.abstract: Abstract  Background  Erenumab, the first calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) receptor-targeting monoclonal antibody approved for migraine prevention in China, has shown substantial clinical benefit in Chinese patients with migraine. However, the degree of improvement varies among individuals. We therefore investigated pretreatment metabolic and transcriptional features associated with differences in erenumab response. Methods  In this prospective study, 40 patients with migraine received erenumab 70 mg every 4 weeks for 3 months. Pretreatment whole-blood samples underwent untargeted metabolomics and RNA sequencing. Super-response was defined as a ≥ 75% reduction in monthly headache days at month three; patients not meeting this criterion were classified as non-super-responders. Analyses integrated differential feature screening, metabolite-set enrichment, a UFA-related principal component score, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and response-group-adjusted gene–metabolite correlations. Molecular docking was exploratory. Results  26 patients (65%) achieved super-response. We identified 52 differential metabolomic features and 297 candidate differentially expressed genes. UFA biosynthesis was enriched toward non-super-responders (normalized enrichment score 2.12; P = 0.00118). Four transcriptional modules were associated with the metabolic score, and 14 genes overlapped these modules and the differential expression set. Across 84 gene–metabolite correlations, the feature annotated as strophanthidin was inversely associated with PREX1, MYADM, BCL3, and KDM6B (partial rho − 0.52 to − 0.48; P = 0.0418 for each). These four genes showed higher expression in non-super-responders than in super-responders. Gene-centered enrichment identified overlapping pathways related to immune function, and exploratory docking characterized potential interactions between erenumab and proteins encoded by the four candidate genes. Conclusions  We identified UFA-related metabolic variation associated with non-super-responder versus super-responder status in erenumab-treated migraine patients. Four candidate genes were inversely associated with a shared mass-spectrometry feature. These findings provide new molecular insights into response heterogeneity and potential directions for further investigation.
records.authors: Wu R, Fu J, Yan Q, Zeng Y, Wu T, Liu X, Gong L.

records.title: FGFR4 Enhances Extracellular Vesicle-Associated Output and Promotes STAT1-Dependent LGALS3BP Enrichment in Colorectal Cancer.
records.abstract: Background/aimFibroblast growth factor receptor 4 (FGFR4) contributes to colorectal cancer (CRC) progression, but its effects on extracellular vesicle (EV)-associated proteins remain unclear. In the present study, we examined FGFR4-associated changes in EV-enriched extracellular fractions and the role of STAT1 in LGALS3BP regulation.Materials and methodsEV-enriched fractions from conditioned media of CT26-vector and CT26-FGFR4 cells were analyzed by nanoparticle tracking analysis and liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Proteomic findings were integrated with RNA-sequencing and STAT1-related chromatin immunoprecipitation-sequencing and perturbation datasets. STAT1 dependence was examined using siRNA knockdown, quantitative real-time PCR, and immunoblotting. Associations among FGFR4, STAT1, and LGALS3BP were assessed in the CNUHH CRC cohort and TCGA COAD/READ datasets.ResultsParticle concentration and size did not differ significantly between CT26-vector and CT26-FGFR4 preparations. Proteomic analysis detected 736 proteins, including 36 previously annotated in EV/exosome databases. LGALS3BP, MFGE8, and AXL were selected as extracellular candidates, and LGALS3BP was also identified in the filtered STAT1-associated transcriptional signature. FGFR4 overexpression increased the expression of interferon-responsive genes, including Lgals3bp, and was accompanied by higher LGALS3BP, TSG101, and ALIX abundance in EV-enriched fractions. STAT1 knockdown attenuated Lgals3bp mRNA induction and reduced LGALS3BP abundance in these fractions without comparable reductions in TSG101 or ALIX. In the CNUHH and TCGA cohorts, LGALS3BP expression was positively correlated with FGFR4 and STAT1, although stage-specific patterns differed.ConclusionFGFR4 overexpression was associated with altered protein composition in EV-enriched extracellular fractions and STAT1-dependent LGALS3BP induction. These findings identify the FGFR4-STAT1-LGALS3BP relationship as a component of extracellular remodeling in CRC.
records.authors: Kim DH, Choi JN, Hwang JE, Shim HJ, Bang HJ, Kim HJ, Chung IJ, Cho SH.

records.title: Route-aware Therapeutic Target Atlas for Desmoplastic Small Round Cell Tumor.
records.abstract: Background/aimDesmoplastic small round cell tumor (DSRCT) is an EWSR1::WT1-driven sarcoma with limited disease-specific options. We assembled an 80-gene candidate-and-control panel and evaluated bulk tumor RNA prevalence, cellular source, fusion-associated expression change, normal-tissue expression, and treatment-specific validation requirements to construct a DSRCT target atlas.Materials and methodsThe panel was examined in two bulk RNA-sequencing cohorts comprising 61 patients and 86 tumor specimens. Technical libraries were collapsed to specimens and specimens to patients on each cohort's native counts per million (CPM) or transcripts per million (TPM) scale; threshold and collapse-rule sensitivity analyses were performed. Exploratory supporting data comprised single-cell RNA sequencing (two distinct specimens analyzed separately, 9,520 cells total; both sharing one anonymized patient label), spatial transcriptomics (five patients, six specimens), three fusion-suppression cohorts, one cell-state cohort, and Human Protein Atlas (HPA)/Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) normal-tissue references.ResultsCD276, CD200, ERBB2, ALCAM, IGF2, TFRC, and the established diagnostic marker CACNA2D2 were detected in 61/61 patients. CLDN6 was detected in 33/61 patients [54%; Wilson 95% confidence interval (CI)=42-66%] and SSTR3 in 59/61 (97%; 95% CI=89-99%). CACNA2D2, FGFR4, and MSLN expression decreased after EWSR1::WT1 suppression in all three cohorts, whereas results for several other candidates differed among cohorts.ConclusionThe atlas identifies the next validation study required for each target; RNA detection alone does not establish protein abundance, therapeutic accessibility, efficacy, or safety.

records.title: A Role for Janus Cyclohexyl Ring Motifs in Medicinal Chemistry. Incorporation Into G-Quadruplex Ligands and Anti-Trypanosoma brucei Activity.
records.abstract: The naphthalene diimide (NDI) ring system is recognized as a privileged motif for binding to G-quadruplex DNA. Accordingly, compounds with peripheral groups attached to the NDI core are being explored as antiparasitic and anticancer candidates. In this study, we have synthesized and explored a series of NDIs with peripheral all-cis ring fluorinated cyclohexyl rings to assess their relative stabilization potential for G-quadruplex and double-stranded DNA. This was explored through FRET melting experiments and measuring changes in melting temperatures (ΔTm). Compounds were also assayed against Trypanosoma brucei to assess their in vitro potency (EC50) against the causative parasite of human African trypanosomiasis or African Sleeping Sickness. The study revealed significant differences in activity when changing the nature of fluorine substitutions on the cyclohexane ring and also the length and nature (ether (O) or methylene (CH2)) of the linker to the core aromatic motif. The most active compound of the series was ether 12a which displayed nanomolar activity (EC50 = 40 nM) against T. brucei although with a modest selectivity (14-fold) for the parasite over HeLa (human model) cells. The study reveals good prospects for exploring fluorinated Janus cyclohexanes in a medicinal chemistry context.

records.title: Deciphering the molecular basis of maize cold tolerance via integrative regulatory network analysis.
records.abstract: Maize (Zea mays L.) is a globally critical but cold-sensitive crop. Understanding the temporal organization of cold-responsive, circadian-associated, and hormone-associated transcriptional programs is essential for deciphering how plants balance growth and survival under cold stress to ensure food security. We performed high-resolution time-series RNA-seq on 108 maize seedling samples across 14 time points (0-36 h cold stress and 24 h recovery). Coronatine (COR) was utilized as a defined JA-associated chemical perturbation to probe hormone-associated transcriptional responses during cold stress. We identified 12 986 cold-responsive and 2259 recovery-responsive genes, revealing a recovery-associated transcriptional transition characterized by suppressed photosynthesis-related processes and enrichment of genes associated with lipid catabolism, accompanied by transient physiological stress during early recovery. Cold stress induced widespread phase shifts and reduced oscillation amplitudes among circadian-associated transcripts, while COR identified distinct hormone-associated transcriptional modules and candidate network-associated genes, including ZmWRKY71 and ZmHSP28, whose roles were further supported by molecular and genetic analyses. This study establishes a temporally resolved transcriptional framework for maize cold stress and recovery, integrating transcriptional dynamics, physiological responses, and experimentally supported regulatory nodes.

records.title: Towards Greener Pastures in Alzheimer's Therapy: Synthesis and XRD/HSA/DFT Mechanistic Investigation of Novel Trifluoromethylated Compounds.
records.abstract: A concise, high-yield one-pot protocol afforded two novel trifluoromethylated Schiff base hybrids, (E)-2,2,2-trifluoro-N-(2-((2-hydroxybenzylidene)amino)-2-methylpropyl)acetamide (1) and its 2-hydroxynaphthyl analogue (2). Both combine a branched diamine core, a phenolic/naphtholic imine, and a trifluoroacetamide fragment, giving fluorinated frameworks distinct from reported donepezil and galantamine analogues, which typically use extended benzyl-piperidine architectures. Both compounds were characterised by multinuclear NMR, IR, MS and elemental analysis; their purity was established by reverse-phase HPLC (98.8% for 1 and > 99% for 2 after recrystallisation), and their structures were determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Crystal structure and Hirshfeld surface analyses reveal a tautomerism-controlled switch in supramolecular assembly: compound 1 adopts an enol-imine form, generating discrete amide-phenol dimers via a robust heterosynthon, while 2 exists as a keto-enamine, forming infinite N-H···O hydrogen-bonded chains reinforced by π-π stacking of naphthalene rings. DFT calculations (B3LYP/6-311 + G(d,p)) support these findings, showing distinct charge distributions and a reduced HOMO-LUMO gap for 2, consistent with enhanced electronic polarizability. Molecular docking against acetylcholinesterase (PDB: 1EVE) predicted that both compounds adopt binding modes within the catalytic gorge, with 2 showing particularly favourable interactions within the catalytic gorge. These predictions were tested experimentally. In a colorimetric AChE inhibitor screening assay both compounds inhibit the enzyme in a concentration-dependent manner, with IC50 values of 22.5 µM (1) and 55.0 µM (2) against 15.0 µM for the galantamine reference measured alongside. Compound 1 is the more potent of the pair, by a factor of 2.4, and comes within 1.5-fold of the reference inhibitor, identifying the compact phenolic scaffold rather than the extended naphthalenic one as the better lead for further development. Computational ADME/Tox profiling tentatively predicts compliance with Lipinski and Veber criteria, oral bioavailability, blood-brain barrier permeation, and acceptable toxicity classes, pending experimental confirmation. Overall, this work establishes a synthetically accessible, structurally tunable family of trifluoromethylated scaffolds whose solid-state behaviour and preliminary computational pharmacology indicate potential as crystallography-guided AChE inhibitor candidates warranting further investigation.
records.authors: Said MA, Al-Kaff NS, Hughes DL, Sarkar B.

records.title: Stemonine Alleviates UVB-Induced Keratinocyte Senescence by Activating SIRT3.
records.abstract: Ultraviolet B (UVB) radiation is the primary environmental factor contributing to skin damage, largely by accelerating cellular senescence, which leads to impaired skin function and premature aging. Recent studies have indicated that Stemonine, a natural alkaloid, has therapeutic potential owing to its documented biological activities. In this study, we investigated the protective effects of Stemonine on immortalized human keratinocyte cell line HaCaT against UVB-induced cellular senescence and elucidated the underlying mechanisms. Our results demonstrated that Stemonine significantly improved cell viability, attenuated oxidative stress, and ameliorated mitochondrial dysfunction in UVB-irradiated HaCaT cells. Furthermore, Stemonine treatment reduced DNA damage signaling, downregulated key senescence executors such as acetylated p53 and p21, and decreased SA-β-Gal activity. Importantly, Stemonine upregulated both the expression and activity of SIRT3. Crucially, the protective effects of Stemonine were largely abolished upon SIRT3 knockdown, indicating that its actions are mediated via the SIRT3 pathway. These findings suggest that Stemonine is a promising candidate for mitigating UVB-induced skin aging.
records.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
records.authors: Chen K, Yan X, You G, Li M, Chen C, Yu X, Xia J.

records.title: Dapagliflozin Inhibits BK Polyomavirus Replication via AMPK Signaling.
records.abstract: BK polyomavirus (BKPyV) infection is a significant contributor of graft loss in kidney transplant recipients, yet no effective antiviral therapy is currently approved. This study investigated whether the SGLT2 inhibitor dapagliflozin could suppress BKPyV replication. BKPyV-infected HK-2 cells were treated with dapagliflozin, and viral load, protein expression, and noncoding control region (NCCR) transcriptional activity were analyzed. siRNA-mediated knockdown of AMPK was used to verify its role in dapagliflozin-mediated response. Dapagliflozin treatment at 10 and 20 μM resulted in a dose-dependent suppression of BKPyV progeny release into the supernatant and a concomitant reduction in large T-antigen (TAg) and VP1 protein expressions. These antiviral effects were achieved without compromising host cell viability, as no significant cytotoxicity was observed at the doses utilized. Luciferase reporter assays revealed that dapagliflozin markedly attenuated TAg-driven NCCR transcriptional activity in both early and late orientations, effectively disrupting viral autoregulation. While high-glucose conditions (25 mM) enhanced BKPyV replication and reduced baseline AMPK phosphorylation, the inhibitory efficacy of dapagliflozin remained consistent. Mechanistically, dapagliflozin increased AMPK phosphorylation even under hyperglycemic stress. The suppression of viral progeny and NCCR activity was significantly reversed upon AMPK knockdown, demonstrating that AMPK activation is required for dapagliflozin-mediated viral suppression regardless of the glucose environment. Dapagliflozin inhibits BKPyV replication through an AMPK-dependent pathway. These results provide a strong rationale for evaluating SGLT2 inhibitors as a novel strategy to reduce the severity of BKPyV infection in transplant recipients.

records.title: The Vitamin D Receptor-AADAC Signaling Axis Mediates Epidermal Inflammation and Dermal Fibrosis in Prurigo Nodularis via Regulation of Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress.
records.abstract: Prurigo nodularis (PN) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease, but the role of vitamin D receptor (VDR) in its pathogenesis remains unclear. VDR expression in clinical PN skin samples was assessed by qRT-PCR, Western blot, IHC, and IF staining. RNA sequencing combined with GO, KEGG, and PPI analyses was used to identify arylacetamide deacetylase (AADAC) as a VDR-associated candidate molecule. The mechanistic role of VDR-associated AADAC regulation was then investigated using an H2O2-induced oxidative stress model in HaCaT cells, vitamin D (VD) intervention, VDR knockdown, and a Transwell-based indirect HaCaT-fibroblast co-culture system. VDR and AADAC were significantly downregulated in PN lesions, accompanied by increased fibrosis-related proteins. Transcriptomic analysis identified AADAC as a VDR-associated candidate. In vitro, H2O2 activated the endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS) pathway, increased inflammatory cytokines, and suppressed VDR/AADAC expression. VD restored AADAC expression, attenuated ERS and inflammation, and inhibited the profibrotic paracrine effect of stressed HaCaT cells on fibroblasts. These protective effects were abolished after VDR knockdown, and VD intervention failed to restore AADAC expression. VDR-AADAC signaling deficiency promotes PN-related inflammation and fibrosis through ERS activation and paracrine fibroblast activation, suggesting this axis as a potential therapeutic target.

records.title: Transcriptional Profiling Links LNC_501 to Cucumber Responses to Fusarium Wilt and Reveals Fatty-Acid-Metabolism Changes in Host and Pathogen.
records.abstract: Fusarium wilt is a devastating soil-borne disease that severely limits cucumber production. However, the roles of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in cucumber resistance and the transcriptional interplay between cucumber roots and Foc during infection remain poorly understood. Here, we employed dual RNA-seq to simultaneously profile cucumber mRNAs, lncRNAs, and Foc transcripts in the roots of resistant and susceptible cucumber lines during the early stages of infection. Comparative transcriptome analysis revealed extensive transcriptional reprogramming in both host and pathogen and highlighted cell wall-related and fatty acid metabolism-related processes among the major responses associated with the cucumber-Foc interaction. Functional analyses in transgenic cucumber lines further supported LNC_501 as a putative negative regulator associated with resistance to Fusarium wilt. LNC_501 expression was inversely associated with that of a nearby glycine-rich cell wall structural protein gene, CsGRP1.8, and altered LNC_501 expression in transgenic plants was accompanied by opposite changes in CsGRP1.8 transcript abundance, suggesting a possible role for lncRNA-associated cell wall regulation in cucumber defense. In addition, fatty acid metabolism-related genes in both cucumber and Foc exhibited dynamic and host genotype-dependent expression patterns during infection, suggesting that fatty acid metabolism may be an important shared component of the cucumber-Foc interaction. Together, these findings identify LNC_501 as a candidate lncRNA associated with cucumber responses to Fusarium wilt and suggest a possible link between LNC_501, CsGRP1.8, and cell wall-related defense. They also highlight coordinated fatty acid metabolism changes in both cucumber and Foc during infection, providing a framework for future mechanistic studies of host-pathogen interaction.

records.title: Unraveling the Chemical Dialogue: The Impact of Volatiles on the Interaction Between PGPR and Verticillium dahliae in Pepper Plants.
records.abstract: Plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) have attracted increasing scientific interest due to their potential to enhance crop productivity and alleviate plant stress. An important trait of PGPR is the production of volatile organic compounds (VOCs), which can play crucial roles in plant-microbe and interspecies communication. This study investigates the volatilome composition of a novel PGP strain, Chryseobacterium sp. SAESo14, and its impact during interactions with the soilborne pathogen Verticillium dahliae and pepper plants. First, volatiles from SAESo14 and V. dahliae co-inoculated in dual cultures were analyzed by Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). A diverse set of VOCs, including alcohols, ketones, esters, and sulfur-containing compounds, was detected. Among these, VOCs with known antifungal activity, such as 2-heptanone, ethyl propionate, and ethyl acetate, were identified. To further investigate the role of VOCs in tripartite interactions, volatilomes of a pepper-V. dahliae pathosystem treated with SAESo14 were analyzed. Seedlings treated with SAESo14 showed viable root cells and enhanced terpenoid metabolism, leading to the emission of 1,8-cineole, β-elemene, and sclarene, whereas V. dahliae-inoculated seedlings released 4,5-di-epi-aristolochene. When tested in planta, pepper plants treated with SAESo14 exhibited increased net photosynthesis and improved growth, along with a 25% reduction in disease index compared to pathogen-inoculated plants, in which distinct metabolic and transcriptomic reprogramming was observed. Collectively, these findings highlight the importance of VOC-mediated signaling in plant-microbe-pathogen interactions in a tripartite system and support the potential of a novel Chryseobacterium strain and its derived VOCs as sustainable alternatives for improving plant performance and disease management.

records.title: Renal Safety and Antiviral Effectiveness of Tenofovir Alafenamide Versus Entecavir in Patients With Chronic Hepatitis B and Chronic Kidney Disease: A Real-World Cohort Study.
records.abstract: Real-world data on tenofovir alafenamide (TAF), especially in patients with advanced renal impairment, are scarce. We evaluated its renal safety and antiviral effectiveness versus entecavir (ETV) in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and pre-existing chronic kidney disease (CKD). In this retrospective single-centre study, CHB patients with pre-existing CKD treated with TAF or ETV were included. The primary outcome was change in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) over 48 weeks. Secondary outcomes included virological, biochemical and metabolic responses. Exploratory subgroup analyses were performed by CKD stage and dialysis status. Among 54 patients (35 TAF, 19 ETV), renal function remained stable in both groups. eGFR change from baseline to week 48 was not significantly different between the TAF and ETV groups (1.56 ± 8.14 vs. -0.53 ± 9.78 mL/min/1.73 m2; Δchange, 2.09; 95% CI, -0.35 to 7.68; p = 0.46). Both groups achieved sustained viral suppression, with no significant difference in undetectable HBV DNA in week-48. HBsAg reduction was greater with TAF than with ETV (-0.36 ± 0.42 vs. 0.02 ± 0.34 log10 IU/mL; p = 0.01). Exploratory analyses in patients with eGFR 2, TAF showed effective viral suppression and renal safety regardless of dialysis status. Metabolic parameters remained stable, without complex dose adjustments. TAF was safe and effective in CHB patients with CKD, including those with advanced renal impairment. Its renal safety and antiviral effectiveness did not differ significantly from those of ETV, with the practical advantage of fixed dosing without complex adjustment.

records.title: Fatal Rickettsia parkeri Rickettsiosis in Immunocompromised Pediatric Patient, Georgia, USA, 2025.
records.abstract: We describe a fatal Rickettsia parkeri rickettsiosis case in a 3-year-old boy in Georgia, USA, receiving chemotherapy for B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, hospitalized with febrile neutropenia. Plasma microbial cell-free DNA sequencing confirmed the diagnosis. This report highlights the need to maintain suspicion for tickborne diseases in immunocompromised hosts in some settings.

records.title: Differentiating Avian and Seasonal Influenza Viruses in Wastewater by Digital PCR.
records.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5Nx) viruses, particularly clade 2.3.4.4b, pose substantial global health risks. We combined and piloted 2 duplex reverse transcription digital PCRs to discriminate between avian and seasonal influenza viruses in wastewater. This approach enabled rapid, strain-specific detection to reduce ambiguity in environmental surveillance for influenza viruses.

records.title: Advancements of Emerging Thiazole-Based CDKs Inhibitors for Cancer Therapy: From Hits to Clinical Candidates.
records.abstract: Cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) represent highly attractive anticancer targets and several inhibitors have been approved for cancer therapy. However, drug resistance and dose-dependent toxicity have limited clinical application. Therefore, discovering new CDKs inhibitors featuring novel scaffolds and high selectivity for disease treatment and target research remains to attract significant interest from both academics and industry. Recently, thiazole has emerged as a privileged heterocyclic scaffold for design and synthesis of antitumor drugs targeting CDKs. Currently, although there are no FDA-approved thiazole-based CDKs inhibitors, this review systematically summarizes the evolution of inhibitors from early hits to clinical-stage candidates including GFH009, SNS-032, and JSH-150, with particular emphasis on structure-based drug design strategies. Furthermore, we highlight the challenges and future prospects in development of thiazole derivatives targeting CDKs, with particular emphasis on discovery of next-generation, highly selective inhibitors.
records.authors: Luo M, Jiang S, Ma Y, Zhao P.

records.title: Oral Protein Fibril Microgels with Gastric Stability and Intestinal Targeting Enhance Capsaicin Bioavailability for Effective Obesity Prevention.
records.abstract: To address the susceptibility of protein fibrils to pepsin degradation, this study proposed a fibril-to-microgel hierarchical assembly strategy, where flexible whey protein isolate fibrils (WPIF) and rigid flaxseed protein isolate fibrils (FPIF) were in situ self-cross-linked into microgels via a W/O emulsion template, followed by capsaicin (Cap) loading. Both microgels exhibited high gastric stability and intestinal response release properties. Compared with WPIF-based microgels (WPIFM), FPIF-based microgels (FPIFM) exhibited a more sustained intestinal digestion profile, leading to a higher Cap bioavailability. In high-fat-diet-induced obese mice, Cap-loaded microgels (WPIFM/Cap and FPIFM/Cap) effectively prevented metabolic disorders, as evidenced by reduced lipid accumulation, hepatic steatosis, and pro-inflammatory cytokines, with FPIFM/Cap demonstrating the highest protective efficacy. Both microgels modulated gut microbiota homeostasis, with FPIFM/Cap uniquely enriching Akkermansia, potentially due to its high arginine content and its stable fibrillar structure. This work provides a proof of concept for upcycling agricultural processing byproduct proteins into high-performance biomaterials for mitigating metabolic diseases.

records.title: FLASH effect on the liver and spleen of mice-a transcriptional perspective.
records.abstract: BackgroundFLASH radiotherapy (FLASH-RT), delivered at an ultra-high dose rate (typically ≥ 40 Gy/s), has been shown to reduce normal tissue toxicity compared with conventional dose-rate radiotherapy (CONV-RT). However, the transcriptomic mechanisms underlying FLASH-mediated protection remain incompletely understood.PurposeThis study aimed to compare the biological effects of FLASH and CONV irradiation on mouse liver and spleen tissues and to identify molecular pathways associated with the FLASH effect from a transcriptional perspective.MethodsC57BL/6J male mice received a single 12 Gy abdominal dose delivered at either 2 Gy/min (CONV) or 100 Gy/s (FLASH). Twelve days after irradiation, spleen and liver tissues were harvested for histological section analysis and RNA-seq. Inflammatory responses in the spleen and liver were assessed by hematoxylin-eosin staining (H&E staining) and immunohistochemical quantification. A series of bioinformatic analyses, such as gene enrichment, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, and transcription factor prediction, were performed to explore the effect of FLASH irradiation. Subsequently, reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR), western blot analysis, and immunohistochemical quantification were used to verify the bioinformatic results.ResultsHistological and immunohistochemical analyses showed less prominent inflammatory changes and lower immune-cell marker staining in mouse spleen and liver after FLASH than after CONV irradiation at 12 days post-irradiation. Bioinformatic analysis and corresponding experimental results revealed that compared to CONV irradiation, FLASH irradiation induced down-regulation of oxidative phosphorylation and cytoplasmic translation pathways in both mouse liver and spleen. Meanwhile, immune-related pathways, especially interferon β (IFNβ) signaling pathways, were significantly activated in both tissues after FLASH than after CONV irradiation. For these three pathways, key transcription factors were further identified and verified. Notably, STAT1 was found to play a potentially critical role in the upregulation of the IFNβ-related pathway under FLASH irradiation conditions in both liver and spleen.ConclusionsFLASH irradiation induces distinct metabolic and immune adaptations in normal mouse liver and spleen tissues compared with CONV irradiation. The coordinated suppression of metabolic and translational pathways, together with activation of IFNβ-STAT1 signaling program, provides transcriptomic evidence for potential mechanisms underlying FLASH-mediated normal tissue sparing. These findings offer candidate pathways and molecular markers for future functional validation and support the clinical translation of FLASH-RT.
records.authors: Ma Y, Zhu X, Yang T, Lv J, Yan X, Yang G, Lin X, Cao Z.

records.title: Circular RNAs in Drug-Induced Cardiotoxicity: Roles, Mechanisms, and Therapeutic Potential.
records.abstract: Drug-induced cardiotoxicity (DIC) remains a major challenge in drug development and clinical practice, often resulting in treatment interruption, drug attrition, and adverse cardiovascular outcomes. DIC has been associated with a wide range of therapeutic agents, including anthracyclines, HER2-targeted therapies, tyrosine kinase inhibitors, immune checkpoint inhibitors, and other cardiotoxic drugs. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have attracted increasing attention as stable and versatile regulatory RNAs involved in cardiovascular injury. This review summarizes the biogenesis and functional mechanisms of circRNAs, their pathological roles in DIC, biomarker potential, therapeutic implications, and translational challenges. CircRNAs regulate gene expression through diverse mechanisms, including miRNA sequestration, interactions with RNA-binding proteins, transcriptional regulation, modulation of alternative splicing, and, in some cases, peptide translation. These regulatory functions have been implicated in apoptosis, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammatory signaling, pyroptosis, and cardiac remodeling during DIC. Emerging evidence suggests that circRNAs may serve as candidate molecular markers and potential therapeutic targets for DIC. However, the current evidence is derived predominantly from cellular and animal models, with doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity accounting for a substantial proportion of available studies. Clinical validation, particularly in well-characterized patient cohorts and across different drug classes, remains limited. Overall, further efforts are needed to establish standardized circRNA detection and quantification methods, validate their functional roles, conduct prospective clinical studies, and determine their incremental value in combination with established cardiac biomarkers before circRNA-based approaches can be translated into clinical management of DIC.
records.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
records.authors: Leng K, Yang Z, Shi L, Sun Z, Gu M, Tang N.

records.title: Hepatic Progenitor Cells and the Ductular Reaction: Pathophysiological Role in the Progression of Liver Disease.
records.abstract: Ductular reaction (DR), a defining histological hallmark of diverse acute and chronic liver injuries, is fundamentally driven by the activation of hepatic progenitor cells (HPCs) and their complex, spatiotemporal bidirectional crosstalk within the hepatic niche. As bipotent precursor cells, HPCs initiate compensatory regeneration when mature hepatocyte proliferation is compromised. However, DR is not a uniform process but a multiphase dynamic reaction: transient early activation facilitates parenchymal restoration, whereas persistent, dysregulated HPC expansion fuels progressive fibrogenesis. The convergence of conserved developmental signalling cascades-including Hippo-YAP, Hedgehog, Notch and TGF-β-strictly governs HPC fate commitment and biliary epithelial proliferation. Concurrently, DR orchestrates intricate inflammatory circuitries by recruiting innate and adaptive immune cells, activating hepatic stellate cells and remodelling the extracellular matrix, thereby establishing a pro-fibrotic niche that perpetuates chronic injury. This review systematically categorizes the disease-specific morphological and molecular subtypes of DR across heterogeneous liver disorders, including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), viral hepatitis and cholestatic liver diseases, highlighting its robust value as an independent histological and serological prognostic biomarker. Leveraging recent mechanistic breakthroughs from single-cell transcriptomics, lineage tracing and spatial imaging, we comprehensively evaluate widely adopted preclinical models and summarise emerging therapeutic strategies targeting the HPC-DR axis, such as small-molecule compounds, phytochemicals and cytokine modulators. Despite substantial advances in deciphering the HPC-DR axis, critical translational bottlenecks impede its clinical application. Collectively, this review integrates state-of-the-art multidimensional evidence to reconstruct the pathogenic network of HPC-DR interactions, providing mechanistic insights to facilitate precise prognostic evaluation and the development of novel targeted interventions for chronic liver diseases.

records.title: PDBe-SIFTS: An open-source tool for Structure Integration with Function, Taxonomy, and Sequences, featuring improved alignment, scoring scheme, and accelerated search.
records.abstract: Structure integration with function, taxonomy and sequences (SIFTS) provides residue-level mappings between UniProt Knowledgebase sequences and Protein Data Bank structures and has historically been generated through internal Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe) pipelines. Here, PDBe-SIFTS is presented as a fully open-source, locally deployable implementation of this mapping framework. The pipeline combines fast, scalable sequence search using MMseqs2, an improved bounded scoring scheme for ranking candidate mappings, and residue-level mapping refinement based on backbone connectivity. PDBe-SIFTS is distributed as a Python package with command-line tools for (1) building a sequence search database, (2) identifying the best sequence-structure match, (3) one-to-one mapping at the residue level, and (4) generating SIFTS annotations in PDBx/mmCIF format. Benchmarking on the complete Protein Data Bank archive showed that MMseqs2 reduced archive-scale UniProtKB searches from hours with BLASTP to minutes, approximately 22-36 times faster, while curated mappings were recovered at top rank in 93.1% of cases. The remaining discrepancies mainly involved biologically ambiguous cases such as highly conserved proteins, chimeric constructs, or closely related orthologs. These results show that PDBe-SIFTS enables fast mapping, improving structural coherence in residue-level alignments while delivering the most up-to-date and accurate mappings, comparable to expert curation. Tool: https://github.com/PDBeurope/SIFTS. Quick start notebook with example: https://github.com/PDBeurope/SIFTS/tree/master/notebooks.

records.title: Safety, Tolerability and Antiviral Activity of GST-HG131 in Chronic Hepatitis B: A Randomized, Double-Blind Phase IIa Study.
records.abstract: Background and aimsChronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major global health burden. Current therapies rarely achieve a functional cure due to low rates of HBsAg clearance, the persistence of the viral replication template-covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA)-and the need for lifelong treatment. GST-HG131 is a first-in-class, orally bioavailable small-molecule inhibitor of PAPD5/7, key host factors involved in HBV mRNA stabilization and HBsAg production. We evaluated the safety, tolerability and antiviral activity of GST-HG131 in patients with CHB receiving nucleos(t)ide analogue (NUC) therapy in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase IIa study.MethodsThis double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled Phase IIa study evaluated the efficacy and safety of GST-HG131 in 45 CHB patients. Cohorts 1 and 2 (n = 10 each; 8 active, 2 placebo) received 30 mg or 60 mg BID for 28 days, respectively. Cohort 3 (n = 25; 20 active, five placebo) received 30 mg BID for 12 weeks. All participants were on nucleos(t)ide analog monotherapy for more than 6 months, with HBsAg between 100 and 1500 IU/mL, and serum ALT below 1× ULN.ResultsAt Day 28, HBsAg reductions were -0.65 log10 IU/mL in the 30 mg BID 28-day group and -0.53 log10 IU/mL in the 60 mg BID 28-day group. The 30 mg BID 12-week group showed a greater reduction of -0.89 log10 IU/mL at the end of treatment versus placebo (p  50% reduction in HBsAg with a maximum decrease of 1.64 log10 IU/mL. Notably, 76.5% of patients in the 12-week group achieved HBsAg below 100 IU/mL. Rebounds in HBsAg were observed following treatment discontinuation. GST-HG131 was well tolerated, with no dose-related toxicity or emerging safety concerns across all cohorts.ConclusionGST-HG131, a first-in-class oral PAPD5/7 inhibitor, demonstrated favourable safety and significant HBsAg reduction in patients with CHB. The greatest antiviral activity was observed after 12 weeks of treatment, supporting further clinical development of GST-HG131 as a component of functional cure strategies for CHB.Trial registrationClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06263959.

records.title: Identification of immune-related hub genes as candidate biomarkers for preeclampsia: integrative transcriptomic and machine learning approaches.
records.abstract: In brief: This study integrated placental transcriptomic datasets, multiple machine learning approaches, single-cell analyses, and immunohistochemical validation to identify six immune-related candidate genes associated with pre-eclampsia. The resulting six-gene signature showed apparent discrimination in placental data and exploratory cross-tissue performance in a small peripheral-blood cohort but requires validation in larger prospective studies. Abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a major cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and is increasingly recognized as a disorder involving immune dysregulation. However, reliable candidate biomarkers and key molecular alterations associated with PE remain unclear. We integrated multiple public placental transcriptomic datasets from patients with PE and normotensive controls. Weighted gene coexpression network analysis and eight machine learning algorithms were used to identify stable immune-related candidate genes, followed by immune infiltration analysis, single-cell analysis, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) interpretation, and in-silico gene knockout analysis. A six-gene logistic regression model was evaluated in the same merged placental dataset used for feature selection and explored in a small independent peripheral-blood cohort. Frequency-based integration across the eight algorithms identified a six-gene signature comprising ACSS3, F13A1, MCTP1, PTGFR, SLC16A10, and TNFRSF11A. The model showed apparent discrimination in the merged placental dataset (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.869, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.820-0.919) and exploratory cross-tissue discrimination in the peripheral-blood cohort (AUC = 0.860, 95% CI: 0.691-1.000). Immunohistochemical analysis of placental tissues from five women with PE and five normotensive controls showed lower protein abundance of all six candidates in PE, consistent with the bulk transcriptomic findings. Single-cell analysis indicated heterogeneous cell-type-dependent expression patterns, while in-silico knockout analysis suggested potential macrophage-associated regulatory effects. Collectively, these exploratory findings identify a six-gene immune-related candidate signature associated with PE that requires validation in larger, prospectively collected cohorts before clinical application.

records.title: Identifying biomarkers for methotrexate efficacy in rheumatoid arthritis: a machine learning approach to whole-blood transcriptomic analysis.
records.abstract: ObjectivesMethotrexate (MTX) is the first-line treatment for rheumatoid arthritis (RA), yet inadequate response is reported in 30-40% of patients. Predicting MTX response early could enable more personalized and effective treatment. This study aimed to identify biomarkers predictive of MTX response at 6 months through whole-blood transcriptomic signatures using machine learning.MethodsRNA sequencing data were generated in whole-blood samples taken from 100 MTX-naive RA patients at baseline (pre-treatment) and following 4 weeks post treatment with MTX. Machine learning models were trained to classify MTX response following 6 months of treatment using gradient boosted trees and interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values to identify predictive genes.ResultsMachine learning models trained on baseline and 4-weeks data achieved AUCs of 0.89 and 0.90, respectively. Stability of SHAP values showed that the baseline model was generally more stable, and therefore potentially more generalizable. Key predictive genes at baseline, which were downregulated in responders, included CAV1, LCN12 and GLB1L.ConclusionBlood-based gene expression profiling at baseline and after 4 weeks of MTX treatment can predict treatment response with high confidence revealing relevant gene pathways and candidate gene targets but requires independent validation. These findings highlight the potential for transcriptomic biomarkers to inform early treatment decision in RA, supporting precision medicine approaches.

records.title: Non-Invasive Visualization of Cells Expressing Unmodified Target mRNA Using a Programmable RNA-Mediated BiFC Platform.
records.abstract: Real-time visualization of specific mRNA expression in living cells is essential for understanding diverse biological processes; however, many existing approaches require modifications to target genes. In this study, we developed a programmable RNA-mediated bimolecular fluorescence complementation (RmBiFC) system by fusing split Venus fluorescent protein fragments with the Pumilio homology domain as a modular RNA-binding domain. Using murine leukemia virus mRNA as a model target, we systematically optimized the orientation of the probes and demonstrated robust detection of cells expressing target mRNA. This system enables live-cell imaging of target mRNA-expressing cells without modifying the target gene. This provides a valuable means of tracking cells expressing wild-type genes, which is challenging to achieve using conventional reporter-based approaches. The RmBiFC system represents a versatile and non-invasive platform with broad potential for identifying specific cell populations based on their transcriptomic profiles at the cellular level.

records.title: Identification of Quality Markers for Tongmai Qiangshen Medicinal Liquor in the Treatment of Heart Failure Based on Multicomponent Qualitative-Quantitative Analysis and Integrated Bioinformatics.
records.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is an end stage of cardiovascular diseases. Tongmai Qiangshen Medicinal Liquor (TMQSJ) is an over-the-counter traditional Chinese medicinal liquor, but its efficacy-related material basis and mechanisms in HF remain unclear. In this study, UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS was used to characterize TMQSJ constituents and prototype compounds in rat plasma. HPLC fingerprinting, spectrum-effect relationship analysis, single-compound activity evaluation, and integrative bioinformatics were combined to screen efficacy-related candidate quality markers and HF-associated candidate genes. A total of 223 compounds were characterized, including 33 prototype plasma components. Chemometric analysis identified caffeic acid, Epimedin A, Epimedin B, Epimedin C, and icariin as characteristic constituents. Spectrum-effect analysis based on 10 batches of TMQSJ and validation in DOX-injured AC16 cells highlighted Epimedin A, Epimedin B, and Epimedin C. Among them, Epimedin A and Epimedin C showed prototype plasma exposure and were prioritized as efficacy-related candidate quality markers. Integration of predicted targets of prototype plasma components with HF transcriptomic data and machine-learning analysis identified BCL2L1, STAT3, HIF1A, MAPK8, and ESR1 as five candidate core genes. Immune cell estimation and molecular docking provided computational clues. Overall, this study establishes an integrated framework linking chemical quality, pharmacological association, in vivo exposure, and mechanistic prediction for TMQSJ quality evaluation.
records.authors: Li Y, Huo J, Zhang Q, Li T, Wang S, Bao Y, Meng X.

records.title: Evolutionary drivers of vocal amplitude in birds.
records.abstract: Vocal amplitude is crucial for acoustic communication because it determines how far a sound travels and can convey valuable information about signal senders to signal receivers. Yet, until recently, amplitude had received limited attention in the literature mainly because of operational challenges in its measurement. As a result, fundamental questions about amplitude remain largely unanswered even in one of the most extensively studied group of singers-birds. Here, we set out to answer two such questions: to what degree do birds vary in how loud they can vocalize, and what evolutionary factors drive this variation? Using original amplitude data from 123 bird species, we show that maximum measured amplitudes vary broadly across species-from 64 dB LAeq,20ms at 1 m in a species of hummingbird to 122 dB in a species of cotinga-, with two new species emerging as candidates for the world's loudest bird (as yet identified). Regarding evolutionary drivers of amplitude, we found that species with larger body sizes and larger beak gape widths tend to achieve higher maximum amplitudes. By contrast, ecological predictors assessed-aerial mobility, habitat density, and mating system-had no unequivocal effect on maximum amplitude. By establishing connections between morphology and vocal amplitude, our results represent a step forward in uncovering what enables birds to produce the loudest acoustic signals of all terrestrial fauna.

records.title: Investigating the role of phosphodiesterase Pde2 in coordinating resource reallocation through the environmental stress response.
records.abstract: Yeast responding to acute stress reallocates cellular resources, in part via the environmental stress response (ESR) that induces stress-defense genes while repressing ribosome biogenesis and growth genes. The purpose and regulation of coordinated induction and repression are incompletely understood, but both responses are influenced by ESR transcription factors Msn2 and Msn4 (Msn2/4). Here, we used single-cell microscopy and transcriptomic analysis to investigate the role of the upstream regulator Pde2 in ESR regulation and poststress fitness. Loss of PDE2 weakened and shortened Msn2 activation following salt stress and produced muted induction of Msn2/4 targets, similar to a msn2Δmsn4Δ strain. In contrast, Pde2 had at most a minor impact on the ESR repressor Dot6, yet was important for repression of its targets beyond Msn2/4 influence. Consistent with our recent resource-reallocation model, pde2Δ cells had normal or faster poststress growth rates, despite weaker activation of the ESR. We discuss implications for ESR regulation and function.
records.authors: Kocik RA, Ahrens J, Gasch AP.

records.title: Discovery of a small peptide that increases yeast lifespan by enhancing the function of APCCdh1 in nondividing quiescent cells.
records.abstract: Aging is characterized by molecular hallmarks conserved from yeast to humans. One such hallmark, senescence, is an irreversible nondividing state that promotes aging. We previously reported that mutants of the yeast anaphase-promoting complex (APC) shorten the lifespan of both dividing and nondividing cells. Here, we propose that activation of the APC will promote the maintenance of quiescent yeast cells, thereby delaying senescence and aging. We observed that APC activity in aging quiescent cells becomes increasingly impaired, as the APC substrates Clb1 and Mps1 accumulated within aging cells reintroduced back into the cell cycle. To identify peptide activators of the APC, we used a yeast 2-hybrid screen to recover peptides that interacted with the APC subunit Apc10. Recovered peptides were tested for their effects on the replicative lifespan (RLS) of dividing cells and the chronological lifespan (CLS) of nondividing cells. Several peptides increased the RLS of wild-type cells, but only one peptide (C43-4) increased CLS, which requires the APC Cdh1 coactivator but not the Cdc20 coactivator. In cells expressing C43-4, Clb1 and Mps1 levels remained low when aging quiescent cells were reintroduced back into the cell cycle. The addition of a synthetic C43-4 to aging quiescent cells increased CLS even when added at late stages of aging. Mutations to APC subunits and coactivators blocked the ability of C43-4 to extend CLS. Htz1, which shares sequence homology with C43-4, was found to suppress APC mutant phenotypes and stabilize Apc10. We individually mutated the 6 amino acids in C43-4 that were shared with Htz1; one of the mutants disrupted the C43-4-Apc10 2-hybrid interaction and abolished the C43-4-dependent increase in CLS. C43-4 action is evolutionarily conserved, as C43-4 increased Caenorhabditis elegans lifespan in a daf-16- and aak-2-dependent manner. Our results describe the discovery of an evolutionarily conserved translational peptide that is the first of its kind to specifically activate the anti-aging APCCdh1 complex.
records.authors: Harris RE, Postnikoff SD, Shukla NK, Harkness AH, Brooks HM, Khawaja AA, Malo ME, Zapien-Verdugo C, Waddell BM, Wu CW, Harkness TAA.

records.title: Transcriptomic signatures of carotenoid-based color polytypism in Oophaga granulifera (Anura: Dendrobatidae).
records.abstract: Aposematic phenotypes advertise their unprofitability to predators with colorful warning signals. The family Dendrobatidae is the prime example of aposematism in amphibians but with pronounced intraspecific variation in some species, particularly in the genus Oophaga. We herein compare the skin spectral reflectance, pigment composition, and gene expression of individuals with aposematic (red) and cryptic (green) phenotypes of Oophaga granulifera from Costa Rica. The accumulation of ketocarotenoids, xanthophylls, and β-carotene in the skin is responsible for the red phenotype. Differentially expressed pigmentation genes, particularly some in the carotenoid metabolism pathway, are strongly associated with the distinction between red and green skin phenotypes. Among these the bco1 gene represents a strong candidate for additional enzymatic studies. We found no clear candidate ketolase gene, but the ketolation enhancer ttc39b was upregulated in the liver of red O. granulifera. Along with the carotenoid metabolism genes, red frogs upregulate the metabolism of amino acids, lipids, and the mitochondrial energy production, markedly in the liver but also in the skin. This suggest a close association between increased ketocarotenoid accumulation and a higher metabolic rate in the red frogs, which is congruent with macroevolutionary patterns in the family and behavioral observations in this species.
records.journal: Evolution; international journal of organic evolution
records.authors: Rodríguez A, Vasquez V, Mantzana Oikonomaki V, Twomey E, Mora-Machado A, Freire Espin D, Mundy NI, Tamayo-Castillo G, Pröhl H.

records.title: Entorhinal cortex astrocytes in early Alzheimer disease: Human evidence, cross-species circuit rationale, and translational boundaries.
records.abstract: Alzheimer disease (AD) pathology affects the transentorhinal/entorhinal region early but whether entorhinal cortex (EC) astrocytes are causal drivers or therapeutic targets remains unresolved. This narrative review evaluates EC astrocytes through an explicit evidence hierarchy. We distinguish: (1) human EC-specific neuropathology, imaging, and transcriptomic findings, (2) human AD astrocyte data lacking EC-cell resolution, (3) mechanistic evidence from animal and cellular models, and (4) translational hypotheses. Human data support early EC vulnerability and region- and stage-dependent astrocyte remodeling, whereas the most direct functional evidence comes from rodent medial EC layer II and should be interpreted as circuit plausibility rather than anatomical equivalence to the human EC. We therefore prioritize candidate astrocyte modules according to astrocyte specificity, relevance to EC or medial temporal pathology, mechanistic links to circuit dysfunction, and the availability of measurable target-engagement readouts. These modules include inflammatory-complement signaling, EAAT2/GLT-1-mediated glutamate clearance, MAO-B/GABA metabolism, AQP4-related gliovascular regulation, astrocytic calcium signaling, and APOE-related lipid handling. Cell transplantation, glial reprogramming, and engineered extracellular vesicles remain experimental platforms. EC astrocytes should therefore be viewed as candidate circuit-glial vulnerability nodes requiring human validation, not as established clinical targets.
records.journal: Journal of neuropathology and experimental neurology
records.authors: Wu F, Wang M.
